name: MonarchDisclosureGroupStyle
title: Accordion
wrapsNative: DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) and isExpanded: bindings, separated by MonarchDivider
summary: Stacked sections whose content opens under each header: standard DisclosureGroups with the Monarch style, one shared binding for one-at-a-time or a Set for any number.
whenToUse: For reference content where people look for one item: FAQs, policy sections, help topics, optional detail under a summary.
whenNotToUse: For switching between views of one object, use Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) or a TabView. Do not hide content everyone must read, and do not use it for form steps. Inside a List, the system disclosure style fits better.
api: DisclosureGroup(_ titleKey: StringProtocol, isExpanded: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> Content).disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch)
init(expandedLabel: String? = nil, collapsedLabel: String? = nil)  // MonarchDisclosureGroupStyle

options.name: expandedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Expanded" spoken value of every header.

options.name: collapsedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Collapsed" spoken value of every header.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the headers are shown; chevrons point down.

states.name: expanded
states.description: A section's content is shown under its header and its chevron points up. With one String? binding, opening a section closes the open one; with a Set<String> binding any number stay open.

states.name: disabled
states.description: A section with disabled(_:) uses the disabled text colour and does not open.

appearance: Headers use the label type role in the default text colour with a muted chevron; MonarchDivider draws a hairline in the subtle border colour between sections. No boxes or fills, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web Accordion is Radix Accordion with type single or multiple, collapsible and headingAs. On iOS each section is a standard DisclosureGroup with the Monarch style; single or multiple is decided by the binding the app passes (an optional id or a Set of ids), so no accordion type is shipped. Arrow-key movement between headers is not offered; VoiceOver moves between them as separate elements. Android ships a MonarchAccordion type.
accessibility: Each header is a button labelled with the section title, with the value "Expanded" or "Collapsed".
The recipe adds the header trait to each section, so VoiceOver's headings rotor reaches them.
Collapsed content is removed, so VoiceOver does not reach it.
Every header is at least 44 points high; content appears without animation when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: Long titles wrap before the chevron.
With a single optional binding, opening a section closes the open one in the same change.
State held inside a section's content is lost when it collapses.
Whether the header trait added to a DisclosureGroup is read together with the button by VoiceOver was not checked on a device.

title: AccountMenu
wrapsNative: A Button with MonarchAvatar as the trigger and, open, a card of rows: the signed-in name and address, Profile and Settings, the workspace and theme choices under their own titles with a dot on the current one, and Sign out. (MonarchElevation, MonarchDivider, MonarchIcon)
summary: A recipe, not a component: the signed-in person's menu, an avatar button that opens a system menu with who is signed in, Profile and Settings, a workspace switcher, the colour scheme and Sign out.
whenToUse: In the toolbar or header of an app with accounts, as the one place for the person's own settings and signing out.
whenNotToUse: For a full account screen with many settings, push a Form from a toolbar button instead. For switching workspaces as the main navigation, use a dedicated switcher in the sidebar.
api: Menu { Section("Signed in as …") { Button("Profile", systemImage:) {}; Button("Settings", systemImage:) {} }; Picker("Switch workspace", selection:) { … }.pickerStyle(.menu); Picker("Theme", selection: $scheme) { … }.pickerStyle(.menu); Divider(); Button("Sign out", systemImage:, role: .destructive) {} } label: { MonarchAvatar(image:name:size:status:isDecorative:) }

states.name: closed
states.description: The avatar, with a presence dot when given, as the menu's button.

states.name: open
states.description: The system menu: the signed-in address as the section title, Profile and Settings, the workspace and theme pickers as submenus that show the current choice, and Sign out in the destructive colour.

states.name: with name
states.description: The label can be the avatar and the name in an HStack, for wide toolbars.

appearance: The avatar keeps its Monarch colours; the menu is the system menu in every theme, with the destructive role drawing Sign out in the system red.
platformNotes: The web ships AccountMenu as one component with user, workspaces, theme and callback props, and renderLink for router links. On iOS it is a recipe: Menu already gives the trigger, focus, keyboard and VoiceOver behaviour, and on a phone the system menu is the expected surface, so no Monarch type is added. The theme picker binds the same MonarchSchemePreference that MonarchThemeToggle uses; apply it with .monarchTheme(scheme:) and keep it with @AppStorage through MonarchThemeToggle.storageValue(for:). The web's workspaceSlot and items props are the app's own Menu items. The web's "sheet on phones" option is not needed: the system menu fits phone screens; push a Form if the account options grow.
accessibility: The menu's button is named "Account menu for <name>" with accessibilityLabel; the avatar inside is decorative.
The pickers are read as menus with their current value; each choice is read with a selected state.
Sign out uses the destructive role, which VoiceOver announces.
The avatar label keeps a 44-point touch target with monarchMinimumHitTarget().
edgeCases: With one workspace, leave the workspace picker out.
Long names and addresses in the section title are truncated by the system menu.
Signing out usually needs a confirmation only when there is unsaved work; use confirmationDialog then.

name: MonarchActionEditor
title: ActionEditor
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchCard per action, with a Picker(.menu) sectioned by group for the type, inputs from MonarchTextField, MonarchNumberInput, MonarchTagInput, MonarchFormField with Picker(.menu), Menu of Toggles with menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled), and Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox); reorder through a Menu and accessibilityActions
summary: Edits the ordered list of actions a rule runs; each action has a type and the labelled inputs that type defines, with validation and accessible reordering.
whenToUse: In routing rules, automations and macros, where the same editor serves many kinds of action defined as data (set team, set priority, add tags, send a message).
whenNotToUse: For the conditions of a rule use MonarchQueryBuilder; for a plain reorderable list use List with onMove (see reorderable-list); for a fixed form use MonarchFormField fields directly.

var MonarchActionParameter.blankValue: MonarchActionValue

options.name: actions
options.description: The actions in the order they run, each an id, a type id and parameter values by key.

options.name: types
options.description: The kinds of action: a name, description, menu group, inputs, defaults, a disabled state with a reason and an optional extra check.

options.name: isOrdered
options.description: Whether actions run in order; adds a reorder menu and Move up / Move down accessibility actions.

options.name: maxActions
options.description: The most actions; the add button is replaced by a note at this count.

options.name: showsErrors
options.description: Shows "Fill in “Team”." under empty required inputs, "“Delay” is out of range." under a number outside its range, and the type's own check, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: defaultType
options.description: The type new actions start as; the first type that is not disabled when nil or unknown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the action titles, the required and out-of-range messages, the reorder items and the move announcement.

options.name: makeID
options.description: Makes the id of a new action.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No actions yet." above Add action.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each action is a card titled "Action 1" with a reorder menu, a remove button, the type menu with the type's description, and its inputs.

states.name: conditional input
states.description: An input with visibleWhen appears only while its condition holds, such as Message after Notify is checked.

states.name: errors shown
states.description: Empty required inputs show "Fill in “Message”." with an icon; the type's own check shows under the card.

states.name: unavailable type
states.description: An action of a disabled type shows a warning banner with the reason; the type is disabled in the menu for other actions.

states.name: unknown type
states.description: A stored type no longer offered reads "escalate (not available)" in the menu and shows no inputs.

states.name: full
states.description: At maxActions, "You can add up to 20 actions." replaces Add action.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the editor disables every menu, input and button.

appearance: Each action is a MonarchCard on the surface role with its title in the default text role; inputs are Monarch fields; errors use the danger strong role with an icon; the unavailable warning is a warning MonarchBanner. All roles adapt to the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ActionEditor uses a ReorderableList with drag handles and move buttons and supports a custom render function per type. On iOS each action is a card in a stacked list for the phone; moving is a reorder Menu (Move up, Move down) and the same two accessibility actions, announced after the move, instead of drag. A custom parameter editor is not offered: compose MonarchActionEditor's model with your own view for types the input kinds cannot express. Multi-select is a Menu of Toggles that stays open while choosing; multi-line text is a vertical TextField. Focus after removing an action is left to the system. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Actions"; each card is a container named "Action 1, Set team" and its visible title has the header trait.
When ordered, each card has Move up and Move down accessibility actions, and "Moved to position 2." is announced after a move.
The reorder menu and the remove button are icon-only with spoken names ("Reorder action 1", "Remove action 1").
Every input is labelled; required inputs add "Required" to the hint and their error is spoken as a hint and announced by the field.
A multi-select menu reads the chosen labels as its value; disabled types and options are disabled menu items, not only grey.
Every control has a touch target of at least 44 points and the text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Changing an action's type replaces its parameters with the new type's defaults.
Required inputs that are hidden by visibleWhen are not reported as missing.
Multi-select keeps the options' order and keeps stored ids that are no longer options.
A number outside the minimum and maximum is reported by MonarchNumberInput.
Actions of an unknown type are kept and can be changed to a known type or removed.

name: MonarchActivityTimeline
title: ActivityTimeline
wrapsNative: VStack of day sections (a header Text per day) and event rows with a drawn line; DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) for details; TimelineView(.everyMinute) for relative times; MonarchAvatar, MonarchTag, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchInlineErrorRetry
summary: A vertical feed of events (actor, verb, object, time and a marker) grouped by day, with expandable details and Load more.
whenToUse: For a record's history, an audit trail in context, or project activity: who did what, to what, and when, newest first.
whenNotToUse: For a conversation people reply in, use a comment thread. For a searchable, filterable audit log of a whole workspace, use a table. For the steps of a process, use MonarchStepper or MonarchStageJourney.
api: MonarchActivityTimeline.init(_ events: [MonarchActivityTimelineEvent], isGroupedByDay: Bool = true, marker: MonarchActivityTimelineMarker = .dot, density: MonarchActivityTimelineDensity = .regular, expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isLoading: Bool = false, isFailed: Bool = false, hasMore: Bool = false, isLoadingMore: Bool = false, isLoadMoreFailed: Bool = false, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchActivityTimelineLabels = MonarchActivityTimelineLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onLoadMore: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchActivityTimelineEvent.init(id: String, actor: MonarchActivityTimelineActor? = nil, verb: String, object: String?, link: String?, time: Date, systemImage: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, tags: [String] = [], body: String? = nil, details: String? = nil)
MonarchActivityTimelineActor.init(_ name: String, avatarURL: URL? = nil, kind: MonarchActivityTimelineActorKind = .person, seed: String? = nil)
enum MonarchActivityTimelineActorKind { case person, automation, system }
enum MonarchActivityTimelineMarker { case dot, avatar }
enum MonarchActivityTimelineDensity { case regular, compact }

MonarchActivityTimelineLabels.init(list: String? = nil, today: String? = nil, yesterday: String? = nil, automated: String? = nil, details: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil, error: String? = nil)

options.name: events
options.description: The events, newest first or oldest first; the order is kept. The app filters them; put filter controls above the timeline.

options.name: isGroupedByDay
options.description: Groups events under Today, Yesterday and dates, in the environment's calendar and time zone.

options.name: marker
options.description: A dot in the event's tone, or the actor's avatar. An event's systemImage always wins.

options.name: density
options.description: Regular, or compact for side panels.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The ids of events whose details are open. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows three placeholder rows for the first page.

options.name: isFailed
options.description: Shows the error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Shows Load more after the feed when onLoadMore is given.

options.name: isLoadingMore
options.description: Load more shows that the next page is loading.

options.name: isLoadMoreFailed
options.description: Load more shows that the next page failed, with a retry.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times and day headings. The current time when nil, refreshed every minute.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries the first page after a failure.

options.name: onLoadMore
options.description: Loads the next page.

states.name: default
states.description: Day headings, then each event: marker on a line, the sentence with the actor and object in bold, the relative time and tags, the body.

states.name: automated
states.description: Automation and system actors get an "Automated" tag after the time.

states.name: details open
states.description: The Details disclosure shows the event's details under it.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholder rows, redacted.

states.name: empty
states.description: The Monarch empty state "No activity yet".

states.name: failed
states.description: An inline error with Try again, or the error text alone without onRetry.

states.name: more
states.description: Load more after the feed, with its loading and failed states.

appearance: Sentences are default body text with the actor and object in bold; times and day headings are muted. Dots use the solid colour of their tone (neutral is the strong border colour); icon markers are the tone's symbol colour on its subtle background. The line between markers is the subtle border colour. Light, dark and high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: The web takes rich content (links, nodes) for the verb, object, meta, body and details; here they are strings and tags, and a link to the record belongs in the app's navigation. The web accent tone is not offered, because MonarchTone has no accent case yet. The filters slot is not offered: put the controls above the timeline. The web day heading level option has no meaning here: headings are headers. The web locale and timeZone options are the environment's locale, calendar and time zone. The parity map named a List with a Section per day; a VStack is used so the line can join the markers and the timeline can sit inside a ScrollView with other content. Details use the Monarch disclosure group, which says Expanded or Collapsed, instead of Show and Hide titles. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: Day headings are headers; each day is a container.

Each event is one element read as its sentence, its absolute date and time, "Automated" for rules, its tags and its body, such as "Ana Ruiz moved Acme renewal, Mar 4, 2026 at 2:00 PM, Negotiation". The relative time is visual.
Markers, avatars and the line are decorative and hidden.
Details are a standard disclosure group after the event: a button named "Details" with the value Expanded or Collapsed, at least 44 points high.
Loading is one element read as "Loading activity".
The ungrouped feed is a container named "Activity".
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type; the marker column scales with it.
edgeCases: Days appear in the order of their first event, so an oldest-first feed reads oldest day first.
Day boundaries follow the environment's time zone; an event near midnight can move to the other day in another zone.
Events from another year get the year in their day heading.
An event without an actor reads as its verb and object only.
Load more is hidden while loading or failed, and without onLoadMore.
Relative times refresh every minute when now is nil; pass now for a fixed time, as tests and screenshots do.

title: ActivityWidget
wrapsNative: MonarchWidget (a VStack card with a Menu and a View all Button) holding a compact MonarchActivityTimeline (a VStack of event rows)
summary: A recipe, not a component: the recent-activity card of a dashboard, a MonarchWidget around a compact MonarchActivityTimeline of the latest few events, with View all leading to the full log.
whenToUse: On a dashboard or a Space home screen that shows what changed recently, when the full activity log is another screen.
whenNotToUse: For the full log or an audit trail, push a screen with MonarchActivityTimeline on its own. For the person's own notifications, use the notification center pattern.
api: MonarchWidget(_:systemImage:state:onRetry:onViewAll:content:) { MonarchActivityTimeline(_:isGroupedByDay:marker:density:isLoading:now:labels:) }

states.name: ready
states.description: The first events, newest first. Pass only the latest few (the web default is 6); View all opens the rest.

states.name: loading
states.description: Pass isLoading to the timeline so the card shows the timeline's own redacted placeholder rows.

states.name: empty
states.description: The timeline shows its empty text; set labels.empty to "No activity yet" or the product's wording.

states.name: failed
states.description: Set the widget's state to .failed with onRetry: the card shows the error with Try again instead of the timeline.

appearance: The widget's surface and subtle border with its title row, then the compact timeline: tone-coloured dots or avatars, the sentence in the default text colour and the time in the muted text colour. The same roles change with dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ActivityWidget is a component with a limit prop and its own "Recent activity" and "No activity yet" strings. On iOS it composes MonarchWidget and MonarchActivityTimeline: the app passes the first events (events.prefix(6)) and its own title, which it has already localised, so Monarch ships no strings for the recipe. The web view-all link is an href; on iOS onViewAll pushes the full log in the navigation stack. The web time zone prop has no counterpart: the timeline formats in the device time zone. Android uses the same recipe.
accessibility: The widget title is read as a header, then each event as one sentence: actor, verb, object and time.
Automated actors carry the visible "Automated" tag from the timeline, so people and rules are told apart without colour.
View all and the retry button are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: Keep the list short: the card does not scroll on its own, so pass five or six events and lead to the full log.
Pass now from a fixed clock in tests and previews so relative times do not change between runs.
Ungrouped (isGroupedByDay: false) reads better in a short card; grouped by day suits a taller widget.

name: MonarchAddressAutocomplete
title: AddressAutocomplete
wrapsNative: Button field that presents a .sheet with a NavigationStack, a List and .searchable(text:placement:prompt:), a debounced search in .task(id:), and a form of MonarchTextField with textContentType(.streetAddressLine1 …) and MonarchCombobox over Locale.Region.isoRegions
summary: An address field with suggestions from the app's own provider: search, pick a suggestion, and the street, city, region, postal code and country fill in for review, with manual entry one step away.
whenToUse: For a postal address in checkout, billing, shipping or a profile, when the app has an address provider (its own endpoint, or MKLocalSearchCompleter behind a closure).
whenNotToUse: Not for a place or point of interest on a map (use a map search), and not when no provider is available (use the address form of MonarchTextField fields with address text content types).
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, address: Binding<MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress>, mode: Binding<MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode>? = nil, helper: String? = nil, initialQuery: String = "", error: String? = nil, fieldErrors: [MonarchAddressAutocompleteField: String] = [:], isRequired: Bool = false, allowsManualEntry: Bool = true, minQueryLength: Int = 3, debounce: Duration = .milliseconds(300), labels: MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels = MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels(), search: @escaping @Sendable (String) async throws -> [MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion], resolve: (@Sendable (MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion) async throws -> MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress)? = nil, onSuggestionSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion, MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress: Hashable, Sendable { var line1: String; var line2: String; var city: String; var region: String; var postalCode: String; var countryCode: String?; var isEmpty: Bool { get }; init(line1: String = "", line2: String = "", city: String = "", region: String = "", postalCode: String = "", countryCode: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchAddressAutocompleteSuggestion: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, address: MonarchAddressAutocompleteAddress? = nil) }
enum MonarchAddressAutocompleteMode { case search, manual }
enum MonarchAddressAutocompleteField { case line1, line2, city, region, postalCode, country }

struct MonarchAddressAutocompleteLabels: Sendable { init(placeholder:searching:resolving:empty:searchFailed:resolveFailed:enterManually:backToSearch:filled:cancel:line1:line2:city:region:postalCode:country:optional:noAddress: String? = nil, tooShort: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, results: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: The search field's label and the sheet's title. "Address" when nil.

options.name: address
options.description: The address. A picked suggestion replaces it; the form edits its parts.

options.name: mode
options.description: The search field only, or the form, when the app owns it. Kept inside when nil, starting on the form when the address has a street line.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the search field, also read as the hint.

options.name: error
options.description: An error under the search field; the field takes the danger border.

options.name: fieldErrors
options.description: Errors of the form's fields, shown under each field.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Marks the search field and the country as required.

options.name: allowsManualEntry
options.description: Offers "Enter the address manually" under the field and at the end of the list.

options.name: minQueryLength
options.description: The characters needed before search runs.

options.name: debounce
options.description: How long to wait after typing before search runs. A newer text cancels the wait and the older search.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: search
options.description: Returns the suggestions for the trimmed text. Throw to show "Couldn’t search addresses." with Try again.

options.name: resolve
options.description: Turns a picked suggestion without an address into one. Throw to show the resolve error. Without it, such a suggestion fills only the street line.

options.name: onSuggestionSelect
options.description: Receives the picked suggestion and the address it gave.

options.name: initialQuery
options.description: Text to search for when the view appears; when it is not empty the search opens with it typed in.

states.name: search, empty
states.description: The search field shows the placeholder in the subtle text colour, with "Enter the address manually" under it.

states.name: searching
states.description: The sheet shows a progress row with "Searching…".

states.name: too short
states.description: The sheet asks for more characters and does not search.

states.name: search failed
states.description: The sheet shows the error with Try again, which reruns the same text.

states.name: no results
states.description: The sheet shows "No addresses found" and the manual entry row.

states.name: resolving
states.description: A progress row with "Getting the address details…" shows under the field and the field is disabled.

states.name: resolve failed
states.description: The resolve error shows under the field with an icon and is announced.

states.name: manual
states.description: The form shows street, apartment (optional), city, region, postal code and country, then "Search for an address".

states.name: disabled
states.description: Text takes the disabled colours and nothing responds.

appearance: The search field has the input background and border of a text field with a search symbol; it shows the address on one line once filled. Suggestions are list rows with a pin symbol, the label in the default text colour and the description in the muted colour. Dark and high-contrast themes resolve the same roles.
platformNotes: The web shows a combobox with a listbox popup under an input; on iPhone the search opens in a sheet with the system search field, as in Maps and checkout forms. The manual form uses the system address text content types so AutoFill offers the person's addresses, and the country list comes from Locale.Region.isoRegions named in the current locale. The web's LocationFields adapter (region and city pickers from data) and idPrefix are not offered: region and city are typed. Search and resolve are async closures cancelled through Swift task cancellation instead of an AbortSignal. Android uses the same name. Several closures are optional (resolve, onSuggestionSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is resolve.
accessibility: The search field is one button labelled with the label ("Address"), whose value is the address on one line or "None" and whose hint is the error, the help text and "Required".
The number of suggestions ("3 addresses found") or "No addresses found" is announced when a search finishes.
"Address filled in. Check the details." is announced after a pick, and the resolve error is announced when it fails.
Each suggestion is a button read as its label and description; the pin symbol is decorative.
The form fields are standard text fields and a country combobox, each named by its label; the optional apartment line has "Optional" as help text.
Rows and buttons are at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: An answer that arrives after the text changed is dropped, because the task that asked for it was cancelled.
A suggestion without an address and without resolve fills only the street line, for review.
Leaving the search for manual entry keeps an existing street line; otherwise the typed text becomes the street line.
Long street lines wrap in the search field and in the form.

name: MonarchAgendaList
title: AgendaList
wrapsNative: List with listStyle(.plain) and a Section per day (pinned headers), MonarchEventChip(variant: .bar) rows, MonarchEmptyState when empty
summary: Events grouped by day in a plain list: a heading per day with a count and a Today marker, all-day events first, multi-day events on each day they touch, and an empty state.
whenToUse: For a list of upcoming events or bookings by day: the agenda view of a calendar, a person's schedule, the next week's appointments.
whenNotToUse: For a month grid use MonarchMiniMonth; for a single event use MonarchEventChip. Do not put the agenda inside another ScrollView: it is a List and scrolls itself.
api: MonarchAgendaList.init(_ events: [MonarchAgendaEvent], from: Date? = nil, days: Int? = nil, today: Date? = Date(), showsEmptyDays: Bool = false, calendar: Calendar = .current, labels: MonarchAgendaListLabels = MonarchAgendaListLabels(), dayNotes: [Date: [String]] = [:], onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchAgendaEvent) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchAgendaEvent.init(_ title: String, id: String, start: Date, end: Date? = nil, isAllDay: Bool = false, detail: String? = nil, color: Color? = nil, status: MonarchEventChipStatus = .confirmed)

MonarchAgendaListLabels.init(today: String? = nil, allDay: String? = nil, count: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, emptyTitle: String? = nil, until: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, range: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: events
options.description: The events in any order. A timed event's end is exclusive; an all-day event's end is any time on its last day.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day listed. By default the first day with an event. Events that started earlier and still run appear on it.

options.name: days
options.description: How many days from from to cover. By default through the last event.

options.name: today
options.description: The day marked Today, or nil for no marker.

options.name: showsEmptyDays
options.description: Whether days in the range without events are listed.

options.name: calendar
options.description: The calendar and time zone events are grouped and formatted in. The web's timeZone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Today", "All day", the count, "Nothing scheduled" and the spoken "until" and "to".

options.name: dayNotes
options.description: Informational lines shown first in a day, such as time off or a holiday, keyed by any time on that day. A day with notes is listed even without events.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens an event. Without it the events are labels, not buttons.

states.name: days
states.description: Each day has a pinned heading with the date, the Today badge when it is today, and the count; rows are bar event chips.

states.name: multi-day
states.description: A timed event shows its start and end on its first day, "All day" on days it covers whole, and "– 02:00" on its last day.

states.name: notes
states.description: Muted lines with an info icon before the day's events.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "Nothing scheduled" and a calendar symbol.

states.name: event status
states.description: Tentative, cancelled and declined events use the event chip's hollow, struck-through and muted forms, and say their status.

appearance: Day dates use the default text colour in a semibold label style, counts and notes the muted text colour, and the Today marker is an info badge. Rows are MonarchEventChip bars in the event's colour or the theme's accent. List rows have no separators or background of their own; the pinned headers use the system list header background. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from the roles.
platformNotes: The web AgendaList reads ISO days in an IANA time zone, takes a renderEvent wrapper and moves focus between events with the arrow keys. On iOS events use Date and the given Calendar, the list's rows are the system's for VoiceOver and keyboard navigation, and a wrapper is not needed because the app handles onSelect (or adds swipe actions in its own List). The web's headingLevel has no meaning in SwiftUI; headings have the header trait. The web's hourCycle and locale are the environment's locale. The web's empty slot is not offered; the built-in empty state takes labels.emptyTitle. The web's accent Today marker is the info tone, because MonarchTone has no accent. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: Each day heading is one element with the header trait, read as "Wednesday 4 November, Today, 3 events", so the headings rotor moves from day to day.
Each event is a MonarchEventChip read as one element: title, spoken time ("9:30 to 10:15", "until 02:00" or "All day"), status and detail.
With onSelect each event is a button with a touch target of at least 44 points.
Today is a word in a badge, not only a colour; statuses are spoken by the event chip.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; rows grow instead of truncating.
edgeCases: An event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day.
An end before the start is treated as no end.
Ids must be unique; one event appears on several days with the same id, inside different sections.
Give the agenda a height (it fills its container), for example as a screen's content or with frame(height:).
Formatting and grouping use calendar.timeZone, so pass the calendar of the place the events happen when it differs from the device.
dayNotes is a dictionary rather than a closure so that a trailing closure after the events is always onSelect.

name: MonarchAiActionLog
title: AiActionLog
wrapsNative: VStack of rows (MonarchAiAgentAvatar, MonarchBadge, Text(AttributedString) with a link, RelativeDateTimeFormatter in a TimelineView(.everyMinute)), MonarchButton for Undo and Show more, accessibilityAction(named:), AccessibilityNotification.Announcement, MonarchEmptyState
summary: An audit list of what AI agents did: the agent, marked as an AI agent, what it did and to what, when, and Undo for actions that can be reversed.
whenToUse: When an agent acts on records, documents or schedules and people need a record of it, for example on an agent's settings screen or in an assistant panel that shows recent agent activity with Undo.
whenNotToUse: For activity by people, or people and automations together, use an activity timeline. For Undo right after one AI edit use MonarchAiUndoBanner. For the steps of a run in progress use MonarchAiChainOfSteps or MonarchAiTaskProgress.
api: init(_ entries: [MonarchAiActionLogEntry], now: Date? = nil, pageSize: Int = 200, labels: MonarchAiActionLogLabels = MonarchAiActionLogLabels(), onUndo: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchAiActionLogEntry { init(id: String, date: Date, agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, action: String, target: String? = nil, url: URL? = nil, isUndoable: Bool = false, isUndone: Bool = false) }
struct MonarchAiActionLogLabels { init(label:, actorKind:, undo:, undoLabel:, undone:, undoneAnnouncement:, undoFailed:, openTarget:, empty:, showMore:) }

options.name: entries
options.description: The actions, in the order to show them, usually newest first.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times. Without it they follow the clock, updated every minute.

options.name: pageSize
options.description: How many entries are shown at first and how many Show more adds; at least one.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onUndo
options.description: Reverses an action, given its entry id. Shows Undo on entries with isUndoable. Throwing shows and announces the failure.

states.name: entry
states.description: The decorative agent avatar, the agent's name in the strong body style with an "AI agent" badge, the action and target, and the relative time.

states.name: link
states.description: A target with an http or https URL is a link in the accent colour; other URLs show as plain text.

states.name: undoing
states.description: The entry's Undo button shows its spinner; pressing again does nothing.

states.name: undone
states.description: The action text turns muted, the meta line adds "Undone" and Undo goes away; announced.

states.name: undo failed
states.description: "Could not undo: …" under the entry in the strong danger colour with an icon; Undo stays; announced.

states.name: paged
states.description: A secondary Show more button says how many entries it adds.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState, "No AI activity yet.".

appearance: Rows separated by dividers: a small agent avatar, the name in the default text colour with a subtle neutral badge, the action in the default text colour (muted once undone), the target link in the strong accent colour and a caption time in the muted text colour; Undo is a ghost button. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names List rows with Undo; the rows are a VStack so the log can sit inside an agent screen or assistant panel that scrolls, as on the web. The web's per-entry onUndo closure is one onUndo handler that receives the entry id, so entries stay plain values. The web's visibleEntries is pageSize; the web moves focus to the first revealed row after Show more, which iOS leaves to VoiceOver. The web marks the actor kind with visually hidden brackets; here the badge shows "AI agent" and VoiceOver reads it in brackets. A target link opens with the environment's openURL and is also a named VoiceOver action. A failed undo shows text in the entry as well as the announcement, where the web only announces it. The locale comes from the SwiftUI environment. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: Each entry is one element read as "Research agent (AI agent) added a summary to Quarterly report", built by a tested pure function, so the actor is never mistaken for a person.
The time, "Undone" and a failure are the entry's value.
A target link is a named accessibility action, "Open Quarterly report".
The agent avatar is decorative.
Undo buttons are named per entry ("Undo: Research agent added a summary to Quarterly report") and keep a 44-point touch target.
A successful undo and a failed undo are posted as announcements.
The list is a container named "AI activity".
edgeCases: A blank target is left out of the sentence and the spoken text.
Only http and https target URLs become links; others, such as javascript: or file:, show as text.
An entry with isUndone has no Undo even when isUndoable.
The log keeps the undone state of entries it reversed until the app passes entries with isUndone; it does not remove them.
A pageSize below one shows one entry at a time.

name: MonarchAiAgentAvatar
title: AiAgentAvatar
wrapsNative: MonarchAvatar with the square shape, a RoundedRectangle strokeBorder ring (AngularGradient turned by TimelineView(.animation) while working) and a Circle badge with an SF Symbol
summary: The picture of an AI agent: a rounded square with a bot badge, so it is never taken for a person's round avatar, and a ring that shows whether the agent is working, waiting for someone or stopped with an error.
whenToUse: Wherever an agent appears as an actor: beside its messages, in a list of agents, on a task it owns.
whenNotToUse: Not for people, workspaces or apps (use MonarchAvatar). Not to show that a single answer is AI-generated (use MonarchAiGeneratedBadge).
api: init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, showsState: Bool = false, isDecorative: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels = MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels())

init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, image: Image?, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, size: MonarchAvatarSize = .md, showsState: Bool = false, isDecorative: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels = MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels())

struct MonarchAiAgentAvatarLabels { init(kind: String? = nil, state: (@Sendable (MonarchAiAgentState) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent from the conversation model: name names the avatar, codename feeds the initials, avatar is the picture's http or https address (other schemes are ignored), id picks the fallback colour.

options.name: image
options.description: A picture the app already has, instead of loading agent.avatar. nil shows the initials.

options.name: state
options.description: What the agent is doing: idle, working, waiting (needs a person) or error.

options.name: size
options.description: The picture's side before Dynamic Type: sm 24, md 32, lg 40 points, as MonarchAvatar.

options.name: showsState
options.description: Writes the state beside the picture.

options.name: isDecorative
options.description: Hides the avatar from VoiceOver when the agent's name is written beside it; a state other than idle is still read.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in kind ("AI agent") and state names.

states.name: idle
states.description: No ring; the AI badge.

states.name: working
states.description: A ring in the AI strong and AI subtle colours that turns once every 1.6 seconds; a still AI strong ring with Reduce Motion.

states.name: waiting
states.description: A dashed ring in the warning strong colour.

states.name: error
states.description: A ring in the danger strong colour and a danger badge.

states.name: no picture
states.description: Initials of the codename, else the name, on a colour picked from the agent id; a chip symbol when there are no letters or digits.

appearance: A rounded square picture with a small round badge at the bottom trailing corner, filled with the AI solid colour (danger solid on error) and ringed with the surface colour. Rings use the AI, warning and danger strong roles. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Sizes are MonarchAvatar's three touch sizes; the web's xs, xl and numeric sizes are not offered. The web draws a bot glyph; SF Symbols has no robot before iOS 18, so the badge uses the cpu symbol. The web hides a failed image with an error handler; on iOS MonarchAvatar shows the initials while loading and on failure. The two initialisers follow MonarchAvatar's image convention, except that the URL comes from the agent's avatar field rather than a url parameter. Android has the same states.
accessibility: The avatar is one element with the image trait, read as "Research agent, AI agent" plus the state when it is not idle, such as ", Working".
The state is always in words, so it never depends on the ring's colour, dash or motion.
With isDecorative the avatar is hidden, except that a state other than idle is read on its own.
The visible state text is not read a second time.
With Reduce Motion the working ring stands still.
The picture, the ring and the badge scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A name of emoji or symbols only shows the chip symbol.
An avatar address that is not http or https is ignored.
A long state text wraps beside the picture.

title: AiAgentBuilder
wrapsNative: NavigationStack; a segmented Picker (.pickerStyle(.segmented)) for Configure and Test in a compact width and an HStack of the two panes in a regular width (horizontalSizeClass); a Form of MonarchTextField, TextField(axis: .vertical), a row that opens MonarchAiConnectorPicker in a .sheet, and MonarchAiKnowledgeScope; a test pane of MonarchAiThread with MonarchAiPromptInput in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom)
summary: A recipe, not a component: a screen to define an AI agent (persona, instructions, tools and knowledge) and try the unsaved definition in a test chat.
whenToUse: Admin or builder screens where people create or edit an agent and want to test it before saving.
whenNotToUse: Picking an existing agent: use MonarchAiAgentPicker. Only choosing tools or knowledge for a conversation: use MonarchAiConnectorPicker or MonarchAiKnowledgeScope on their own.
api: if horizontalSizeClass == .regular { HStack(spacing: 0) { form; Divider(); test } } else { VStack { Picker("View", selection: $pane) { Text("Configure"); Text("Test") }.pickerStyle(.segmented); if pane == .configure { form } else { test } } }

form: Form { Section("Persona") { MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent, size: .lg, isDecorative: true); MonarchTextField("Name", text:, error:); MonarchTextField("Role", text:, helper:) }; Section { TextField("Instructions", text:, axis: .vertical) } footer: { "n / 8000 characters" }; Section("Tools") { Button → .sheet { MonarchAiConnectorPicker("Tools", connectors: $connectors, isSearchable: false) } }; Section("Knowledge") { MonarchAiKnowledgeScope(sources, selection: $knowledge) }; Section { Button("Save agent") } }

test: VStack { MonarchAiAgentAvatar(agent, state: conversation.isBusy ? .working : .idle); Button("Restart test") { conversation.stop(); conversation.reset() }; MonarchAiThread(conversation.messages, showsDaySeparators: false, empty:).safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { MonarchAiPromptInput("Message the agent", text:) { conversation.send($0, body: ["agent": definition]) } } }

options.name: definition
options.type: App state: name, role, instructions, tool permissions ([MonarchAiConnector]), knowledge ids
options.description: Held by the app and saved on Save agent; every edit clears the saved message, as the web's onChange does.

options.name: connectors
options.description: The tools the agent may use, grouped by connector with a permission per tool (allow, ask, never), edited in MonarchAiConnectorPicker in a sheet from the Tools row. Destructive tools cannot be set to allow unless the app passes allowsDestructiveAutoApprove.

options.name: sources
options.description: Knowledge the agent can read, as a MonarchAiKnowledgeScope tree. Leave the section out without sources.

options.name: conversation
options.description: The test chat. Each test message is sent with the current definition in body under "agent", so the transport runs the unsaved agent. Leave the Test pane out without it.

options.name: maxInstructions
options.description: Longest instructions; the field is cut to it and its section footer counts characters.

options.name: save
options.description: Save agent checks the name, then the app saves; the section footer reads Agent saved and VoiceOver announces it.

states.name: iPhone
states.description: Configure and Test are a system segmented control under the navigation bar; the form scrolls in Configure and the test chat fills Test.

states.name: regular width
states.description: On iPad the form and the test chat show side by side with a system divider.

states.name: name missing
states.description: After Save agent with an empty name, the name field shows "Give the agent a name." as its error and nothing is saved.

states.name: saved
states.description: The Save section's footer reads Agent saved until the next edit.

states.name: testing
states.description: The avatar reads working while the reply runs; Restart test stops and clears the test conversation.

states.name: empty test
states.description: The thread shows "Send a message to try the agent."

appearance: Every part is an existing component or system control: a system Form with section headers and footers, MonarchTextField, the system multi-line TextField, MonarchAiConnectorPicker, MonarchAiKnowledgeScope, MonarchAiAgentAvatar, MonarchAiThread, MonarchAiPromptInput, a Monarch ghost button and the system segmented control and divider. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components and the system controls.
platformNotes: The web ships AiAgentBuilder as one component with the form and the test chat side by side, stacked on narrow screens. On iOS it is a recipe drawn as the web draws it on a narrow screen: one column, the form and then the Test panel below it. Android uses Material 3 primary tabs and switches at 840dp. The fields are a system Form, so section headers and footers carry the headings and the character count. The web's tool checkbox list is MonarchAiConnectorPicker, opened in a sheet from a Tools row because it is itself a searchable List in a NavigationStack and cannot be nested in the Form; the definition sends the allowed and asked tool ids. Instructions use the system TextField with axis: .vertical because MonarchTextField is single line. The web's avatar URL field is the app's own picker beside MonarchAiAgentAvatar, since Monarch loads no images. The web's save promise with progress and error is the app's own call; this recipe shows the saved state as a section footer with a VoiceOver announcement and the missing name as the field's error. The web moves focus to the name field when the name is missing; this recipe does not move focus.
accessibility: Persona, Instructions, Tools and Knowledge are Form section headers; Test is a header in the test pane.
The name field shows its error as text and reports it through MonarchTextField.
The character count is the Instructions section footer.
Agent saved is written in the Save section footer and announced without moving focus.
Configure and Test are a system segmented control with the selected state.
The avatars are decorative; the agent's name is in the name field and the navigation title.
edgeCases: Keep the test thread out of the scrolling Form: on iPhone it is its own segment, on iPad its own pane.
A test send while a tool call waits for approval is refused and the text comes back into the prompt input.
Edits after a save clear the saved message, so it never claims an unsaved edit was saved.
Long instructions are cut to the limit, including pasted text.
Switching segments keeps the test conversation and the draft, because both are state above the panes.

name: MonarchAiAgentCard
title: AiAgentCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with MonarchAiAgentAvatar, Text, MonarchBadge tags in a MonarchFlowLayout and MonarchIcon list rows
summary: What an AI agent is and what it may do: its name and role, a description, capabilities, the tools it can call, the data it can see and who owns it, with optional actions; a compact variant summarises it for lists.
whenToUse: In an agent directory, an "About this agent" screen or the confirmation before enabling an agent; the compact variant for a row of agents in a list.
whenNotToUse: For just the agent's picture next to a message use MonarchAiAgentAvatar. To edit what an agent may access use MonarchAiPermissionScope. To list several agents working together use MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster.
api: init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, description: String? = nil, capabilities: [String] = [], tools: [MonarchAiAgentTool] = [], dataAccess: [String] = [], owner: String? = nil, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, variant: MonarchAiAgentCardVariant = .full, labels: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels(), @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, description: String? = nil, capabilities: [String] = [], tools: [MonarchAiAgentTool] = [], dataAccess: [String] = [], owner: String? = nil, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, variant: MonarchAiAgentCardVariant = .full, labels: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels()) where Actions == EmptyView
struct MonarchAiAgentTool { init(_ name: String, description: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiAgentCardVariant { case full, compact }
struct MonarchAiAgentCardLabels { init(kind:, capabilities:, tools:, dataAccess:, owner:, toolCount:) }

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent: name, role, codename and avatar URL.

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on what the agent is for.

options.name: capabilities
options.description: Short capability phrases, shown as badges, such as "Drafts replies".

options.name: tools
options.description: The tools the agent can call, each with what it does. The compact card shows only their count.

options.name: dataAccess
options.description: What data the agent can read, such as "Documents in this space". Full card only.

options.name: owner
options.description: Who owns or maintains the agent. Full card only.

options.name: state
options.description: What the agent is doing now, shown on its avatar.

options.name: variant
options.description: Every section, or the compact summary for lists and pickers.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons or links at the end of the full card, such as "Start a chat".

states.name: full
states.description: Large avatar, name and role line, description, then the sections that have content: What it can do, Tools, Data it can see, Owner, and the actions.

states.name: compact
states.description: Medium avatar, name, role line and a tool count, the description and the capability badges; no other section and no actions.

states.name: idle, working, waiting, error
states.description: The agent avatar's ring and, for a state other than idle, its spoken state.

appearance: A MonarchCard on the raised surface. The name uses the subheading style in the default text colour; the role line, section headings, icons and the tool descriptions use the muted text colour; capabilities are subtle neutral badges. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's headingLevel, as, nameId and descriptionId exist for HTML structure and for the web AiAgentPicker; on iOS the name has the header trait and a picker builds its own rows. The web's owner can be any node, such as an avatar with a name; here it is text. The description is text rather than any node. The web's capability tags are MonarchBadge views. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The name and the role line are one element with the header trait; the role line always says "AI agent".
Section headings have the header trait.
Each tool is one element read as its name and what it does, built by a tested pure function.
The owner is read as "Owner, <name>".
The avatar is decorative; it reads only a state other than idle ("Working").
In the compact card the capability badges are a container named "What it can do".
Actions stay separate elements.
edgeCases: A blank role leaves only "AI agent" on the role line.
Sections with no content are left out; a card with only an agent shows the header alone.
Long names, roles and descriptions wrap; badges flow onto new lines.
The compact card ignores dataAccess, owner and actions.

name: MonarchAiAgentPicker
title: AiAgentPicker
wrapsNative: Button with a ButtonStyle over each compact MonarchAiAgentCard, in a VStack or a LazyVGrid, with the selected accessibility trait
summary: A single choice of AI agent, each shown as a compact agent card with its role, description, capabilities and tool count.
whenToUse: When a person starts a conversation or a task with one of a few agents, or sets the default agent of a space, and should see what each agent is for before choosing.
whenNotToUse: For a model rather than an agent, use MonarchAiModelPicker. For dozens of agents that need searching, use MonarchCombobox with the agents' names. For several agents at once, use MonarchCheckboxGroup.
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, selection: Binding<String?>, agents: [MonarchAiAgentPickerOption], layout: MonarchAiAgentPickerLayout = .list, labels: MonarchAiAgentPickerLabels = MonarchAiAgentPickerLabels())
static func key(for agent: MonarchAiAgentRef) -> String

struct MonarchAiAgentPickerOption: Identifiable, Sendable { init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, description: String? = nil, capabilities: [String] = [], tools: [MonarchAiAgentTool] = [], state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, isDisabled: Bool = false); var id: String }
enum MonarchAiAgentPickerLayout { case list, grid }
struct MonarchAiAgentPickerLabels: Sendable { init(label: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, unavailable: String? = nil, card: MonarchAiAgentCardLabels = MonarchAiAgentCardLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: A visible label over the agents, already localised. It also names the group; without it the group is named Choose an agent.

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen agent's key: its id, or its name when it has no id (key(for:)). nil for none.

options.name: agents
options.description: The agents in display order, each with a description, capabilities, tools, a state and whether it can be chosen.

options.name: layout
options.description: list stacks the agents; grid uses two columns on a regular width and one on a compact width or at the accessibility text sizes.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces Choose an agent, No agents are available., the Unavailable tag and the agent card's strings.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The card has the accent strong border, heavier than the others, and a filled check mark before it.

states.name: not chosen
states.description: The default border and an empty circle in the input border role.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The border of an unchosen card takes the strong border role.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: The mark uses the disabled text role, an Unavailable tag is shown under the card and tapping does nothing.

states.name: busy agent
states.description: The agent card's avatar shows the agent's state (working, waiting, error).

states.name: empty
states.description: No agents are available. in the muted text role.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every mark and border uses the disabled roles and nothing can be chosen.

appearance: Each agent is a compact MonarchAiAgentCard on the card surface; the chosen one has the accent strong border and check mark, the same roles as MonarchRadioCardGroup. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web AiAgentPicker is a radiogroup with arrow-key navigation and a check in the card's corner; on iOS each agent is a button with the selected trait, the mark sits before the card (where the card's tool count would otherwise collide with it), and VoiceOver swipes move between agents. The web's disabled prop is SwiftUI's disabled(_:), and onChange is the selection binding. The web shows disabled agents dimmed; iOS adds an Unavailable tag so the state is not colour alone. Marked experimental, as AI composites are, until a Rook app adopts it. Android plans the same component.
accessibility: The group is a container named by the label or Choose an agent.

Each agent is one button: its label is the name and role line (ending in AI agent), its value is the state when busy, the description, the capabilities, the tool count and Unavailable when it cannot be chosen.
The chosen agent has the selected trait, and its mark is a filled check instead of an empty circle, so the choice is not shown by colour alone.
Unavailable agents are disabled buttons, read as dimmed, with a visible Unavailable tag.
Every card is at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: Agents without an id are keyed by name, so two agents with the same name and no id cannot be told apart.
A selection that matches no agent shows nothing as chosen.
Tapping the chosen agent again keeps it chosen; there is no way to clear the choice from the picker.
Long names, roles and descriptions wrap at every text size; the grid becomes one column at the accessibility sizes.

name: MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline
title: AiAgentRunTimeline
wrapsNative: VStack of DisclosureGroup rows with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch), each with a RoundedRectangle bar placed by leading padding in a GeometryReader track; Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) for the view; Grid in a ScrollView(.horizontal) for the table, with accessibilityChildren
summary: The trace of one agent run: every model call, tool call and hand-off as a bar on a shared time axis, totals for time, tokens and cost, and details that open per event, with a table view of the same data.
whenToUse: In a developer or operator view of an agent: to see where a run spent its time, tokens and money, and to jump from an event to the conversation part it produced.
whenNotToUse: For the steps an assistant shows the person while it works, use MonarchAiChainOfSteps. For usage over a period, use MonarchAiUsageMeter or a chart.
api: init(_ events: [MonarchAiRunEvent], currency: String = "USD", now: Date? = nil, mode: Binding<MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode>? = nil, initialMode: MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode = .timeline, labels: MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineLabels = MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineLabels(), onOpenPart: (@MainActor (MonarchAiRunEvent) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAiRunEvent { init(id: String, kind: MonarchAiRunEventKind, name: String, startedAt: Date, endedAt: Date? = nil, inputTokens: Int? = nil, outputTokens: Int? = nil, costMicros: Int? = nil, detail: String? = nil, partId: String? = nil, messageId: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiRunEventKind: String { case model, tool, handoff, error }
enum MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineMode: String { case timeline, table }

struct MonarchAiAgentRunTimelineLabels { init(label:modeLabel:mode:kind:events:totalDuration:inputTokens:outputTokens:cost:start:duration:eventColumn:kindColumn:running:empty:notAvailable:openPart:formatDuration:formatOffset:), every parameter optional }

options.name: events
options.description: The run's events in any order: kind, name, start and end (nil while running), tokens, cost in micros, a detail text, and the conversation part or message it belongs to.

options.name: currency
options.description: The ISO 4217 currency of costMicros.

options.name: now
options.description: The end of events that are still running. Without it they end at the latest known time, so the trace never reads the clock.

options.name: mode
options.description: The view, timeline or table. Without it the component keeps the state.

options.name: initialMode
options.description: The first view when the component keeps the state.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, and duration and offset formatters.

options.name: onOpenPart
options.description: Adds "Show in conversation" to an open event that has a partId or a messageId.

states.name: timeline
states.description: A time axis (start, middle, end), then one disclosure per event with its kind label, name, duration and bar.

states.name: open event
states.description: Start offset, duration, the known tokens and cost, the detail in the code style, and Show in conversation.

states.name: running
states.description: "Running" instead of a duration, and a bar that fades into the AI thinking colour.

states.name: error
states.description: The kind label on the danger subtle fill with danger text, and a danger bar.

states.name: table
states.description: Event, kind, start, duration, input and output tokens and, when any event has one, cost; unknown values show "–". Scrolls sideways.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No events yet" under the totals.

appearance: Bars use the AI solid colour for model calls, the AI tool colour for tools, info solid for hand-offs and danger solid for errors, on a subtle track. Totals are strong body text with muted captions. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map named Swift Charts; the bars are drawn with shapes instead, because each bar sits inside its event's disclosure so the bar, the header and the details form one row for touch and VoiceOver, which a Chart cannot hold. The web draws a moving shimmer on running bars; iOS draws a still gradient, so Reduce Motion needs no special case. The web's detail is any React node; on iOS it is text. Times are Date values and durations are formatted with the locale; the web also accepts ISO strings and epoch milliseconds. The axis shows three ticks instead of five, for phone widths. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The trace is a container named "Agent run"; the heading has the header trait.
Each total is one element, such as "Total time, 4.2 s".
Each event is a disclosure button read as its kind, name and duration, such as "Tool, search_invoices, 1.6 s", with an expanded or collapsed value; a running event says "Running".
Bars and the axis are hidden, so nothing depends on their colour or length.
Each fact of an open event is one element; Show in conversation is a button with a 44-point touch target.
In the table each row is one element with every known value; the grid is not read cell by cell.
The view switch is a standard segmented Picker named "View".
edgeCases: Events are sorted by start; equal starts keep their order.
An event that ends before it starts is drawn with no length.
An instant event keeps a 2-point bar.
Long names wrap in the timeline and widen the table, which scrolls.

options.name: artifact
options.description: The artifact version to show: kind, title, version, content and an optional code language.

options.name: versions
options.description: Every version, for the MonarchAiArtifactVersions stepper, which shows with two or more versions and onVersionChange.

options.name: onCopy

options.name: onSave

options.name: onClose
options.description: Shows the close button; dismiss the sheet here.

options.name: preview(for:_:)
options.description: Replaces the preview of the given kinds, for example charts drawn with Swift Charts.

states.name: preview: document or table
states.description: The Markdown rendered by MonarchAiMarkdown in a scroll view.

states.name: preview: web page
states.description: The HTML in a sandboxed web view with the note "Sandboxed preview: scripts, forms and network requests are blocked.".

states.name: preview: image
states.description: The image loaded with AsyncImage, fitted to the width, with a spinner while it loads.

states.name: unsafe image
states.description: A warning MonarchCalloutBanner, "This image address is not allowed, so it is not shown.".

states.name: code
states.description: The content in a MonarchAiCodeBlock with line numbers; the only view, without the segmented control, for kinds with no preview.

states.name: versions
states.description: The version stepper with Compare above the actions.

states.name: saving

states.name: copied

appearance: A surface-coloured panel: the kind icon in the strong AI colour on a subtle AI tile, the title in the subheading style, the kind and version in the muted caption style, ghost Copy and Share buttons and a primary Save, the system segmented control, a divider and the content. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows the canvas as a pane beside the thread on wide screens and a full-screen sheet below 640px; on iOS the app presents it with .sheet (and can place it beside the conversation in a regular-width layout), so there is no placement option and no Escape key handling. The web's tab list is the system segmented control here. The web's Download button is Share, the system share sheet, which also offers Save to Files. The web previews HTML in an iframe with an empty sandbox and a Content Security Policy; iOS uses a WKWebView with JavaScript turned off, a non-persistent data store, the same Content Security Policy and every navigation except its own document cancelled; the web also strips meta refresh and base tags, which here cannot act because navigations are cancelled. renderPreview is the preview(for:_:) modifier. The web's allowImages for Markdown follows MonarchAiMarkdown's own image handling. onSave is async rather than returning a promise. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android has no artifact canvas yet.
accessibility: The canvas is a container named "Artifact: Q3 summary".
The header is one element with the header trait, read as "Q3 summary, Document, version 3", built by a tested pure function; the kind icon is decorative.
Preview and Code are a system segmented picker named "View", so the selected segment is read as selected.
The close button is named "Close artifact"; Copy announces that it copied (MonarchCopyButton).
The web preview is named "Preview of Event landing page" and is followed by the sandbox note in text.
An image preview is read as the artifact's title.
Every button has a 44-point touch target, and the text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Model output is never rendered as HTML outside the sandboxed web view; scripts in it do not run.
Links, redirects and refreshes inside the web preview are cancelled; new windows are refused.
Image content that is not an http or https address is refused with a warning.
A requested Preview tab falls back to Code for kinds with no preview.
A long title wraps; the panel keeps a minimum height so a web preview always has room.

name: MonarchAiArtifactCard
title: AiArtifactCard
wrapsNative: Button with a private ButtonStyle
summary: The compact card a reply shows for an artifact it made: one button with the title, kind and version that opens the artifact.
whenToUse: In an AI conversation, where a reply produced a document, code, a table, a chart, an image or a web page.
whenNotToUse: For a file the person attached use a file component. For a general tappable card put a MonarchCard in a Button.
api: init(_ title: String, kind: MonarchAiArtifactKind, version: Int, description: String? = nil, isActive: Bool = false, kindLabel: String? = nil, versionLabel: String? = nil, actionLabel: String? = nil, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)
enum MonarchAiArtifactKind { case document, code, table, chart, image, html }

options.name: title
options.description: The title of the artifact.

options.name: kind
options.description: What the artifact is, which selects the icon and the kind name.

options.name: version
options.description: The version number.

options.name: description
options.description: Secondary text under the title.

options.name: isActive
options.description: Whether the artifact is the one currently on show.

options.name: kindLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the kind.

options.name: versionLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "v3", and "version 3" for VoiceOver.

options.name: actionLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Open" or "Showing".

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when the card is activated.

states.name: resting
states.description: A surface-coloured card with the default border; the icon tile and the action use the AI colours.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The subtle background and the AI border.

states.name: active
states.description: The AI-subtle fill, a 2-point AI border, and "Showing" in place of "Open".

states.name: disabled

appearance: A card with 12-point corners, at most 448 points wide. The icon tile is AI-subtle with the strong AI colour; the action text and chevron are the strong AI colour.
platformNotes: The web takes the artifact part of the conversation model; MonarchAiConversation is not built yet, so the card takes the title, kind and version directly. The parity map names MonarchCard as the base, but a card has no pressed or active state, so the surface is drawn by a button style with the card's radius. The web's hover state has no counterpart on touch.
accessibility: One button whose label reads the title, the kind, the version in words, the description and the action.
The artifact on show has the selected trait, reads "Showing" and has a heavier border, not colour alone.
The icon and chevron are hidden from VoiceOver; the chevron mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
The card is at least 44 points high.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; at the accessibility text sizes the action moves under the text.
edgeCases: A long title wraps; nothing is truncated.
An empty versionLabel removes the version from the visible line.
The card does not open anything itself; the action does.

name: MonarchAiArtifactVersions
title: AiArtifactVersions
wrapsNative: MonarchAiMessageBranch (previous and next buttons), Menu with .menuStyle(.button) and an inline Picker, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.button), MonarchDiffViewer, Date.FormatStyle(date: .abbreviated, time: .shortened)
summary: Steps through the versions of an AI artifact with previous and next buttons, the position, a menu to jump to any version and Compare with previous, which shows a diff of what changed.
whenToUse: When an AI-made document, plan or snippet has more than one version and people need to go back to an earlier one, jump to any version or see what changed since the version before.
whenNotToUse: For alternative replies to the same prompt use MonarchAiMessageBranch. For an audit history with authors and comments use a version history list. For one proposed edit with Accept and Reject use MonarchAiEditProposal.
api: init(selection: Binding<Int>, versions: [MonarchAiArtifactVersion], isComparing: Binding<Bool>? = nil, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = .word, showsCompare: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiArtifactVersionsLabels = MonarchAiArtifactVersionsLabels())
struct MonarchAiArtifactVersion { init(_ version: Int, createdAt: Date, label: String? = nil, content: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchAiArtifactVersionsLabels { init(label:, position:, previous:, next:, select:, versionTag:, versionName:, compare:, announce:) }

options.name: selection
options.description: The version number shown. A number not in versions shows the newest.

options.name: versions
options.description: Every version, in any order; shown oldest to newest, one per number.

options.name: isComparing
options.description: Whether the diff with the previous version shows. Without it the stepper keeps the state itself.

options.name: granularity
options.description: Whether the diff marks changed words (prose) or whole lines (code).

options.name: showsCompare
options.description: Whether Compare with previous is offered.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

states.name: middle version
states.description: Previous and next are enabled; the position reads "Version 2 of 4".

states.name: first or last
states.description: Previous (first) or next (last) is disabled.

states.name: single version
states.description: Both buttons are disabled; the position reads "Version 1 of 1"; there is no Compare.

states.name: comparing
states.description: Compare is on (filled in the accent colour) and a MonarchDiffViewer from the previous version to this one shows under the controls.

states.name: compare unavailable
states.description: No Compare when there is no previous version or either version has no content.

states.name: no versions
states.description: Nothing is shown.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Through disabled(_:), every control is disabled and the position uses the disabled text colour.

appearance: Ghost buttons with mirrored chevrons, a caption position in the muted text colour, a ghost menu button with a clock symbol and a system button-style toggle tinted with the strong accent colour; the diff has MonarchDiffViewer's added and removed colours. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names a version stepper and a diff; the stepper reuses MonarchAiMessageBranch for previous and next, the web's native select is a system Menu with an inline Picker, and the diff is MonarchDiffViewer, which this component shows itself when Compare is on, where the web calls onCompare for the app to render an AiArtifactDiff. So each version carries its content. The web's aria-pressed compare button is a system button-style Toggle. Dates in the menu use the environment's locale, calendar and time zone. The web's separate AiArtifactDiff export is not a separate type: MonarchDiffViewer covers it. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The controls are a group named "Versions".
Previous and next are named "Previous version" and "Next version", keep 44-point touch targets and their chevrons mirror in right-to-left layouts.
The position is read as text, "Version 3 of 5", built by a tested pure function.
The menu button is named "Choose a version"; its items are a system Picker, so the chosen version is read as selected.
Compare is a toggle, read with its on or off state.
Every change of version, from the buttons or the menu, is announced: "Showing version 3 of 5".
The diff is MonarchDiffViewer, named "Changes from Version 2 to Version 3"; changes are marked with signs as well as colour.
edgeCases: Duplicate version numbers keep the first one given.
A selection that is not in versions shows the newest version; moving from there changes the selection.
Version numbers with gaps (1, 2, 5) are stepped in order and the position counts versions, not numbers.
A version without content cannot be compared.

name: MonarchAiAssistantPanel
title: AiAssistantPanel
wrapsNative: .sheet with .presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) and a NavigationStack (Close as ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction)) in a compact width, .inspector in a regular width (View.monarchAiAssistantPanel(isPresented:panel:) picks one), with MonarchAiThread over MonarchAiPromptInput and MonarchAiContextChips in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom), MonarchAiWelcome with MonarchAiStarterPrompts when empty, and MonarchAiAgentAvatar
summary: The assistant surface any app mounts: the title with the agent and Close, a thread over a prompt input with chips for what the assistant can see, and a welcome with starter prompts while empty, as a sheet on iPhone or an inspector pane on iPad.
whenToUse: A product adds a general assistant beside its screens. Hold the MonarchAiConversation above the navigation so it survives moving between screens, open the panel from MonarchAiLauncher, and present it with .monarchAiAssistantPanel(isPresented:panel:).
whenNotToUse: A full-screen chat product: use the ai-chat-page recipe. A single AI action on a record: use the action's own button and show the result with MonarchAiSummaryCard or MonarchAiInlinePrompt.
api: public struct MonarchAiAssistantPanel<HeaderActions: View, Toolbar: View, Footer: View, Empty: View>: View
