extension MonarchAiAssistantPanel where HeaderActions == EmptyView, Toolbar == EmptyView, Footer == EmptyView, Empty == EmptyView { the same two initialisers without headerActions, toolbar and footer }
public func emptyState<NewEmpty: View>(@ViewBuilder _ content: () -> NewEmpty) -> MonarchAiAssistantPanel<HeaderActions, Toolbar, Footer, NewEmpty>
public enum MonarchAiAssistantPanelPlacement: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case automatic, inline, sheet }

public struct MonarchAiAssistantPanelLabels: Sendable { public init(close: String? = nil, inputLabel: String? = nil, context: String? = nil, welcome: String? = nil, starters: String? = nil, assistant: String? = nil) }
extension View { public func monarchAiAssistantPanel<Panel: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, @ViewBuilder panel: () -> Panel) -> some View }

options.name: title
options.description: The heading, such as "Assistant": the navigation title in a sheet, a heading in a pane, and the name of the pane for VoiceOver.

options.name: conversation
options.description: The conversation the panel shows and sends to. Its messages, status, error, connection, queue, slowness and agent are read; sending calls send, and a refused send gives the text back to the prompt input; Stop calls stop.

options.name: messages
options.description: The conversation, oldest first, shown by MonarchAiThread.

options.name: isPresented
options.description: Whether the panel shows. Close sets it to false; a sheet also clears it when swiped down.

options.name: prompt
options.description: The draft. Without it the panel keeps a draft only while it stays on screen; a sheet's content is rebuilt each time it opens, so hoist it to keep drafts.

options.name: placement
options.description: sheet draws a NavigationStack with the title and Close in the navigation bar and the medium and large detents; inline draws its own header row for an inspector or a split view column; automatic follows .monarchAiAssistantPanel, otherwise sheet in a compact width and inline in a regular one.

options.name: status / error / isOffline / queuedCount / isSlow
options.description: Second initialiser only. Passed to MonarchAiThread. While submitted or streaming the avatar reads working and Send becomes Stop; while a reply runs or a tool call awaits approval the starters are disabled.

options.name: agent
options.description: The agent in the header (name · role under the title) and in the welcome. With a conversation, its agent is used when this is nil. Without one the avatar is named "Assistant" and no line is shown under the title.

options.name: agentImage
options.description: The agent's picture, loaded by the app; initials are shown without it.

options.name: context
options.description: What the assistant can see on the current screen, shown as MonarchAiContextChips above the thread (web and Android parity).

options.name: starters
options.description: Suggested first prompts under the welcome while the conversation is empty, as MonarchAiStarterPrompts in its list layout. Choosing one sends its prompt.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: close, inputLabel, context, welcome, starters, assistant.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Second initialiser only. Stops the running reply, from the prompt input's Stop, the Escape key and the Magic Tap.

options.name: onRemoveContext
options.description: Lets the person remove a context chip by id.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Buttons beside Close, such as New conversation: the primary action of the navigation bar in a sheet, the header row in a pane.

options.name: toolbar / footer
options.description: Passed to MonarchAiPromptInput: controls in its bar (a model picker) and content under it (MonarchAiDisclaimer).

options.name: onSend
options.description: Sends the typed prompt or a chosen starter's prompt. Throw to give the typed text back to the prompt input.

options.name: emptyState(_:)
options.description: Replaces the whole empty state.

options.name: monarchAiAssistantPanel(isPresented:panel:)
options.description: Presents the panel as a .sheet in a compact width and as an .inspector in a regular width, and tells an automatic panel which chrome to draw.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is shown. A hoisted prompt keeps the draft; the conversation keeps the messages.

states.name: sheet
states.description: A system sheet at the medium detent, which the person can drag to large. The navigation bar shows the avatar, the title and the agent line, Close as the cancellation action and the header actions as the primary action. Swiping down closes it.

states.name: pane
states.description: A column on the surface colour with a header row (avatar, title, agent line, header actions, Close) and a divider under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchAiWelcome with "How can I help?", the agent and the starters, scrolling when the panel is short; or the emptyState content.

states.name: running
states.description: The avatar reads working, Send becomes Stop, the starters are disabled, and Escape stops the reply instead of closing.

states.name: awaiting approval
states.description: The starters are disabled; a typed prompt that the conversation refuses comes back into the prompt input.

states.name: offline / slow / error
states.description: MonarchAiThread shows and announces its notice or the error.

appearance: Every part is an existing component: the small decorative agent avatar, the title in the subheading style in the default text colour with the agent line in the muted text colour, a ghost close button, and the thread, chips and prompt input on the surface colour. A sheet uses the system sheet and navigation bar; a pane has a system divider under its header. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those roles and components.
platformNotes: The web panel docks to the right or left edge and becomes a full-screen modal sheet under 640px. On iOS the phone form is a system sheet with the medium and large detents and a NavigationStack, and the regular-width form is an .inspector column (or a column the app places), so the web's side option is not offered: the system puts the inspector at the trailing edge. Android shows a full-height ModalBottomSheet and a SupportingPaneScaffold pane. iOS has no minimize: a sheet already drags between detents and closes with a swipe, and an inspector is shown or hidden by isPresented, so Android's minimized and onMinimizedChange and the minimize and expand strings are not offered. The context chips sit above the thread, as on Android and the web (decision D6). The web moves focus to the input on open; iOS does not focus it, as Android, so the keyboard does not cover the conversation. Escape closes the panel while no reply runs (Close carries the cancel keyboard shortcut) and stops a running reply, as the web. Swift idiom: isPresented is a Binding instead of open and onOpenChange; the prompt is a Binding<String> instead of TextFieldState; the empty slot is the emptyState(_:) modifier; closeIcon and minimizeIcon are not offered because SF Symbols are available. The thread's scroll position is MonarchAiThread's own and is not exposed (Android's threadState). The web's messageProps, threadProps and promptProps pass-throughs are not offered; compose MonarchAiThread and MonarchAiPromptInput directly for that.
accessibility: The title is a header: the navigation title of the sheet, or a heading in the pane, which is a container named by the title.
Close is a button named "Close assistant" with a 44-point touch target and the cancel keyboard shortcut (Escape) while no reply runs.
While a reply runs, Escape and the Magic Tap stop it through MonarchAiThread and MonarchAiPromptInput.
The avatar is decorative; the agent's name and role are text under the title.
The prompt input is named "Message the assistant"; Send becomes Stop while a reply runs.
The thread announces new replies, errors and the offline notice.
The context chips are a group named "Context" and the starters a group named "Suggested prompts".
Starters are disabled, not hidden, while a reply runs or a tool call waits for approval.
The input is not focused when the panel opens.
The header row mirrors right to left: Close sits at the leading edge.
edgeCases: Give an inline panel a bounded height: the thread is a scroll view and cannot sit in a vertically scrolling parent.
A sheet's content is rebuilt every time it opens: hoist the prompt binding and the conversation to keep the draft and the messages.
A starter that the conversation refuses (while a tool call waits for approval) is not sent and shows no error; the starters are disabled then anyway.
A long title and a long agent line wrap at the largest text size; Close keeps its size.
With no agent and no role, no line is shown under the title and the avatar is named Assistant.
How the medium detent and the keyboard interact (the system moves the sheet to make room) was not checked on a device for this entry.

The progress bar is a standard ProgressView named "Uploading" and the file name.

accessibility: The control keeps its own label, value and traits.
The status line is one element, such as "AI suggested, High confidence, From invoice.pdf", read after the control.
Accept and Clear are buttons named with the field, such as "Accept suggested Company", with 44-point touch targets.
After Accept or Clear, "Suggestion accepted" or "Suggestion cleared" is announced.
The suggested state is in words (the badge), so the marker bar's colour is not the only signal.
edgeCases: A long source wraps onto its own line.
With no confidence and no source, the status line is the badge and the actions.
If the app never sets edited, the field keeps saying "AI suggested" after the person types.

whenToUse: When agents run long tasks that the person starts and leaves: show the button in the toolbar and the tray in a sheet, so the work stays visible after the conversation is closed.
whenNotToUse: For one task in the conversation itself, use MonarchAiTaskProgress. For work that must be followed outside the app, post a local notification or start a Live Activity from onStatusChange; the tray only reports while the app is open.

MonarchAiBackgroundTasksButton.init(tasks: [MonarchAiBackgroundTask], labels: MonarchAiBackgroundTasksLabels = MonarchAiBackgroundTasksLabels(), action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)

struct MonarchAiBackgroundTask: Identifiable, Hashable { init(_ title: String, id: String, status: MonarchAiBackgroundTaskStatus, agent: String? = nil, progress: Double? = nil, isIndeterminate: Bool = false, step: String? = nil, startedAt: Date? = nil, endedAt: Date? = nil, result: String? = nil, error: String? = nil) }

struct MonarchAiBackgroundTasksLabels { init(title:, runningCount:, queuedCount:, needsInputCount:, needsInputGroup:, runningGroup:, finishedGroup:, groupHeading:, status:, elapsed:, ended:, progressLabel:, open:, cancel:, retry:, respond:, dismiss:, clearFinished:, actionLabel:, empty:, announce:)  // every parameter optional, nil by default

options.name: tasks
options.description: Every background task, in any order; the tray groups and sorts them.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for elapsed and end times. Without it the clock is read: every second while a task runs, every minute with Reduce Motion.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Shows Open on every task.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows Cancel, and a Cancel swipe action, on queued, running and waiting tasks.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Retry on failed tasks.

options.name: onRespond
options.description: Shows Respond on tasks that need input.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a Dismiss icon button, and a Dismiss swipe action, on finished tasks.

options.name: onClearFinished
options.description: Shows Clear finished in the Finished heading; receives the finished tasks.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Runs once when a task succeeds, fails or starts needing input, for example to post a local notification.

options.name: action (button)
options.description: MonarchAiBackgroundTasksButton: opens the tray, usually in a sheet.

states.name: needs you
states.description: Tasks waiting on the person come first under Needs you, with a bell icon in the warning colour and Respond as the primary action.

states.name: running
states.description: A spinner, the step, a linear bar (indeterminate when the amount is unknown) and Running for 3 min 12 sec.

states.name: queued
states.description: A clock icon, listed after running tasks; a bar only when the amount is known.

states.name: succeeded
states.description: A check in the success colour, the result line and Ended 5 minutes ago.

states.name: failed
states.description: An octagon in the danger colour, the error in the danger colour, Retry.

states.name: cancelled
states.description: A minus icon in the muted colour; no detail.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with No background tasks.

states.name: button
states.description: A small secondary button with a bot (cpu) icon, the title, a count of running (or queued) tasks and a warning count of tasks that need the person.

appearance: A system grouped list in the theme: titles in the default text colour, status lines and steps muted, icons in the success, danger, warning or accent strong roles, bars in the accent. Buttons are Monarch small buttons: primary for Respond, secondary for Retry and Open, ghost for Cancel. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows the tray in a popover from a trigger button, or inline in a sidebar. On iPhone a popover is the wrong surface for a long list, so the tray is a List that the app presents in a sheet with detents (or pushes); the trigger is a separate MonarchAiBackgroundTasksButton. Dismiss and Cancel are also swipe actions. The web's notify hook and useAiRunNotifications become onStatusChange, where the app posts a UserNotifications request or updates a Live Activity; Monarch posts no notifications itself. headingLevel, align and the controlled open state have no meaning here; the sheet's isPresented is the app's. The web's accent tone for the running count is the info tone, because MonarchTone has no accent. Android has no tray yet. Marked experimental as a domain composite until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: Section headings have the header trait and include the count, for example "Running (2)".
Each row's title, status line and detail are one element; actions are separate buttons named with the task, such as "Open: Weekly report".
The Dismiss icon button has a spoken name and a 44-point touch target; Cancel and Dismiss are also swipe actions, which VoiceOver offers as actions.
A task that succeeds, fails or starts needing input is announced once ("Weekly report: Done"); progress and step changes are not announced.
Status is an icon and a word, never colour alone; the spinner of a running task is hidden from VoiceOver because the status word is read.
The progress bar is named "<title> progress" and reads its percentage.
The button is one element read as "Background tasks, 2 running, 1 needs you".
edgeCases: Tasks without a start or end time sort last in their section; ties keep the given order.
Progress outside 0 to 1 is clamped; isIndeterminate forces the animated bar.
A task that first appears already failed or done is not announced.
Action buttons wrap under each other when they do not fit, at the largest text sizes.
Without now, a running task's elapsed time ticks every second; with Reduce Motion it updates once a minute.

whenToUse: Inside an assistant reply, to show the steps of a plan part (MonarchAiPlanPart) while an agent works through them.
whenNotToUse: Not for a person's own multi-step form (use MonarchStepper) and not for a single long task (use a ProgressView).

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, in order, from MonarchAiPlanPart. Update each state (todo, active, done, skipped, failed) as the assistant works.

options.name: details
options.description: Optional detail under a step, such as a result or an error, by step id. Already localised.

options.name: isCollapsible
options.description: Whether the list folds under a summary once every step has finished.

options.name: startsExpanded
options.description: Whether the folded list starts open.

options.name: announces
options.description: Whether starts, failures and completion are announced to VoiceOver. Turn it off when the thread announces progress itself.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: todo
states.description: Dotted circle in the subtle text colour; muted label.

states.name: active
states.description: A small ProgressView in the AI strong colour, or a still filled circle with Reduce Motion.

states.name: done
states.description: Filled check in the success strong colour.

states.name: failed
states.description: Filled octagon in the danger strong colour and the word "Failed" under the label.

states.name: skipped
states.description: Minus circle, struck-through muted label and the word "Skipped".

states.name: folded
states.description: Once every step has finished, a disclosure with the summary ("3 steps, 1 failed", with a failure icon when any failed).

appearance: Icons take the AI strong, success strong, danger strong or subtle text roles by state; labels the default or muted text role. The summary uses the Monarch disclosure group style. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The step model is the shared MonarchAiPlanStep, whose not-started state is called todo (pending on the web). The web's detail is part of each step; on iOS it is a details dictionary by step id because the shared step model has no detail field. The web draws a shimmer on the running label; iOS shows the system spinner instead. The web announces through a live region; iOS posts an accessibility announcement.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Steps".
Each step is one element: its label is the step label, its value the state name and the detail, so the state does not depend on the icon or colour.
Failed and skipped steps also show their state in words.
A step that starts or fails, and the end of the run, are announced once; the state at first appearance is not.
The folded summary is a disclosure button with an expanded or collapsed value and a 44-point touch target.
With Reduce Motion the running step shows a still icon instead of a spinner.
edgeCases: Long labels wrap at every text size.
An empty list shows nothing and never folds.
Several changes in one update are announced together, joined by full stops.

title: AiChatPage
wrapsNative: NavigationSplitView(preferredCompactColumn:) with MonarchAiConversationList in the sidebar and, in the detail, MonarchAiThread with MonarchAiPromptInput in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) and MonarchAiConversationHeader in ToolbarItem(placement: .principal); on iPhone the split view collapses to a navigation stack
summary: A recipe, not a component: the full chat screen of an assistant app, with the conversation history in a sidebar beside the open conversation on iPad and as the previous screen of a navigation stack on iPhone.
whenToUse: An app whose main screen is a chat with an assistant and a history of conversations.
whenNotToUse: An assistant beside other screens: use MonarchAiAssistantPanel. A single conversation without history: put MonarchAiPromptInput in the bottom safe area inset of MonarchAiThread.

open(id): activeID = id; conversation.reset(stored messages of id); column = .detail

MonarchAiThread(conversation.messages, status:, error:, isOffline:, queuedCount:, isSlow:, onStop:, empty: { MonarchAiWelcome("How can I help?") { MonarchAiStarterPrompts(starters, layout: .list) { conversation.send($0.prompt) } } })
.safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) { MonarchAiPromptInput("Message the assistant", text: $prompt, isBusy:, onStop:, footer: { MonarchAiDisclaimer() }) { guard conversation.send($0) else { throw … } } }
.toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) { MonarchAiConversationHeader(title, agent: conversation.agent, onRename:) } }
.inspector(isPresented:) or .sheet { MonarchAiArtifactCanvas(artifact, onClose:) } for an artifact a reply produced

options.name: conversations

options.name: activeID
options.description: The open conversation's id, marked selected in the list.

options.name: column
options.description: The column shown on iPhone. The page opens on the history, as on Android and the web; opening a conversation sets it to detail and the back button returns to the sidebar.

options.name: onNew
options.description: Adds New conversation at the top of the list; the recipe adds an untitled entry, resets the conversation and opens it.

options.name: title
options.description: Shown by MonarchAiConversationHeader in the navigation bar, which renames through its title menu.

options.name: empty
options.description: The thread's empty content while the conversation has no messages, in a ScrollView so it fits at every text size.

options.name: toolbar / footer
options.description: MonarchAiPromptInput's toolbar (a model picker) and footer.

states.name: two columns
states.description: On iPad the history sidebar and the conversation show side by side; the system sidebar button hides and shows the history.

states.name: one column
states.description: On iPhone the split view collapses to a stack: the conversation shows with a back button to the history, and choosing or starting a conversation opens it. The system back swipe returns to the history.

states.name: empty
states.description: The thread shows MonarchAiWelcome with starters; choosing one sends it.

states.name: running
states.description: Send becomes Stop; the thread shows thinking, streams the reply and announces it; the starters are disabled.

states.name: error / offline
states.description: MonarchAiThread shows and announces the error or the offline notice.

appearance: Every part is an existing component or system container: the system split view and navigation bar, MonarchAiConversationList, MonarchAiConversationHeader, MonarchAiThread, MonarchAiPromptInput and MonarchAiDisclaimer in the Monarch theme. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiChatPage as one component: a history rail beside the chat from 768px, the history in a start-edge sheet below it, and the artifact canvas as a third column. On iOS it is a recipe on NavigationSplitView: a sidebar and a detail on iPad, collapsed to a navigation stack with the system back button and back swipe on iPhone, instead of a drawer-like sheet. Android uses NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold and starts on the history; this recipe does the same (preferredCompactColumn .sidebar, decision D6), and opening a conversation shows it with a back button to the history. MonarchAiConversationList reports taps through onSelect rather than a List selection, so the recipe sets preferredCompactColumn to push the conversation on iPhone. The conversation title is MonarchAiConversationHeader in the principal toolbar item (the system title menu with Rename), not a row above the thread. The artifact canvas is MonarchAiArtifactCanvas in an .inspector on iPad or a sheet on iPhone, not a third column. The web's messageProps wiring (regenerate, feedback, branches, tool approval) is the default MonarchAiMessage of MonarchAiThread plus the app's own calls on MonarchAiConversation. The web focuses the prompt after New conversation; this recipe does not move focus, so the keyboard does not open by itself.
accessibility: MonarchAiConversationList is named "Conversation history" and marks the open conversation with the selected trait.
The conversation title is a header in MonarchAiConversationHeader, with the assistant as its value; the system back button returns to the history on iPhone.
MonarchAiThread announces replies, errors and the offline notice.
MonarchAiPromptInput is named "Message the assistant"; Send becomes Stop while a reply runs, and Escape and the Magic Tap stop it.
The split view follows the system back gesture and sidebar button.
edgeCases: The history list and the thread scroll themselves: give the split view the screen, never a vertically scrolling parent.
A new conversation has an empty title until the app names it; MonarchAiConversationList and MonarchAiConversationHeader show their untitled text.
Deleting the open conversation: pick another active id or start a new one, and reset the conversation.
A send that the conversation refuses (while a tool call waits for approval) throws in onSubmit, so the prompt input gives the text back.

states.description: A source without a handler and without a safe address has no button or link in the card.

appearance: The marker uses the link text colour. The card uses the raised background, muted caption text for the heading and meta line, the strong body style for the title and the subtle background with a strong border colour bar for the quote. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web opens the card on hover and focus after a delay and pins it on click; iOS has no hover on a phone, so a tap opens and closes it, and openDelay and closeDelay are not offered. The card stays a popover on iPhone (presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover)) rather than becoming a sheet. SwiftUI Text cannot contain a button, so the marker sits after the sentence in an HStack or MonarchFlowLayout instead of inside the text run. Relative addresses, which the web resolves against the page, are not opened. The web's shared AiSourceGlyph and aiSourceMeta helpers are internal here. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The marker is a button named "Source <n>: <title>" by a tested pure function; the brackets are not read.
The marker has a 44-point touch target although it draws as small text.
The card's heading has the header trait; the favicon or kind symbol is decorative.
The card's Visit page is a standard Link marked as external; Open source is a MonarchButton.
The popover is the system's, so VoiceOver moves into it and the escape gesture closes it.
edgeCases: A source repeated in a message keeps its first number.
A javascript:, file: or relative address is neither opened nor shown as the host.
A favicon address that is not http or https is ignored and the kind symbol is shown.
Long titles and quotes wrap; the card is at most 320 points wide, scaled with Dynamic Type.

name: MonarchAiClaimSources
title: AiClaimSources
wrapsNative: VStack of DisclosureGroup(isExpanded:content:label:) with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch), Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) for the filter, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchBadge, MonarchButton, MonarchCopyButton and Environment(\.openURL) for the source
summary: The claims of an AI answer with the passages that back or contradict them: a summary, a filter for the claims that need checking, and one expandable row per claim with its support level, a note, and each passage with its source, stance and actions.
whenToUse: Under or beside an AI answer, so people can check each statement against the passages it rests on before they rely on it.
whenNotToUse: For a plain list of the sources an answer used use MonarchAiSourceList; for one inline citation use MonarchAiCitation.
api: init(_ claims: [MonarchAiClaim], sources: [MonarchAiClaimSource], filter: Binding<MonarchAiClaimSourcesFilter>? = nil, expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, locale: Locale? = nil, calendar: Calendar? = nil, labels: MonarchAiClaimSourcesLabels = MonarchAiClaimSourcesLabels(), onOpenSource: (@MainActor (MonarchAiClaimSource, MonarchAiClaimEvidence) -> Void)? = nil, onFlag: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onVerify: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onCopyQuote: (@MainActor (MonarchAiClaimEvidence) -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchAiClaim { init(id: String, text: String, support: MonarchAiClaimSupport, evidence: [MonarchAiClaimEvidence] = []); var needsChecking: Bool }
struct MonarchAiClaimEvidence { init(id: String, sourceID: String, quote: String, location: String? = nil, stance: MonarchAiClaimEvidenceStance? = nil) }

struct MonarchAiClaimSource { init(id: String, title: String, url: String? = nil, kind: MonarchAiSourceKind? = nil, published: Date? = nil); init(_ part: MonarchAiSourcePart, published: Date? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiClaimSupport { case supported, partial, unsupported, conflicting, unchecked }
enum MonarchAiClaimEvidenceStance { case supports, contradicts }
enum MonarchAiClaimSourcesFilter { case all, needsChecking }

struct MonarchAiClaimCounts { static func of(_ claims: [MonarchAiClaim]) -> MonarchAiClaimCounts; func count(_ support: MonarchAiClaimSupport) -> Int; let total, needsChecking, supported, partial, unsupported, conflicting, unchecked: Int }

struct MonarchAiClaimSourcesLabels { init(heading:, summary:, filterLabel:, all:, needsChecking:, support:, note:, passages:, evidenceLabel:, stance:, unknownSource:, published:, kind:, openSource:, fromSource:, copyQuote:, copied:, copiedAnnouncement:, flag:, verify:, empty:, noneNeedChecking:, noEvidence:, showing:) }

options.name: claims
options.description: The claims of the answer, in the order the answer makes them.

options.name: sources
options.description: The sources the passages point at. MonarchAiClaimSource(_:) takes an MonarchAiSourcePart as it is.

options.name: filter
options.description: Which claims are shown: all, or the ones that need checking. Internal when nil.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The ids of the open claims. Internal when nil, all closed at first.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of dates and counts. Default: the environment's.

options.name: calendar
options.description: The calendar and time zone of publication dates. Default: the environment's.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onOpenSource
options.description: Opens a passage's source, for example at the passage. Without it a safe http, https or mailto address opens through openURL.

options.name: onFlag
options.description: Reports a problem with a claim, given its id. Shows Report a problem in each open claim.

options.name: onVerify
options.description: Checks an unchecked claim, given its id. Shows Check again in unchecked claims.

options.name: onCopyQuote
options.description: Runs after a passage is copied to the pasteboard.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Each claim shows its support icon, the claim and a caption with the support level and passage count in the level's colour.

states.name: expanded
states.description: A note for a claim that is not fully supported, then each passage on a subtle surface with a quote bar, the source and its detail, a stance badge, Open source and Copy quote.

states.name: needs checking
states.description: The filter shows only claims that are not supported; a sentence says when none need checking.

states.name: unknown source
states.description: A passage whose source is missing reads Unknown source and has no Open source.

states.name: empty
states.description: "There are no claims to check."

appearance: A heading in the subheading style with a muted caption summary, a segmented picker, and claims separated by dividers. Support levels use the strong success, warning and danger colours or the muted text colour, each with its own icon. Passages sit on the subtle background with a border-coloured bar before the italic quote. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web lays the claims out as a list of collapsible rows with a filter of two toggle buttons; iOS uses the standard DisclosureGroup in the Monarch style and a segmented Picker. The web's selectedClaimId and onSelectClaim, which highlight the claim in the answer text beside the list, are not offered: on a phone the answer and the claims are not side by side. The web's expandIcon and supportIcon slots are not offered; the icons are Monarch's. Copy uses MonarchCopyButton (the system pasteboard, a success haptic and an announcement), so the web's copyFailed strings have no use. Open source without a handler goes through the system openURL. Android builds the same component, also experimental.
accessibility: The heading has the header trait and the summary follows it.
Each claim header is the DisclosureGroup's button: label the claim, value the support level and passage count (a tested pure function), plus Expanded or Collapsed from the Monarch style.
Every support level has its own icon and words, so partial and conflicting differ without colour.
Each passage is one element read as its stance, quote, source and detail; its buttons are separate and named after the source ("Open source from Q3 report").
Changing the filter posts "Showing <n> of <total> claims".
Buttons are MonarchButtons and MonarchCopyButton with 44-point targets.
edgeCases: A claim with no passages shows only its note, or "No passages were provided for this claim." when it is supported.
A source address that is not http, https or mailto (such as javascript:) is never opened.
Check again appears only on unchecked claims.
The summary lists only the levels that have claims.

name: MonarchAiCodeBlock
title: AiCodeBlock
wrapsNative: MonarchCodeBlock (ScrollView(.horizontal) of monospaced Text, Toggle for wrap, MonarchCopyButton) with a MonarchFlowLayout row of MonarchButton for Insert and Apply
summary: Code written by an assistant: MonarchCodeBlock with copy, wrap, diffs and line numbers, plus optional Apply and Insert actions that hand the code back to the app.
whenToUse: In an assistant's answer, for code the person may copy, apply to a file or insert into an editor, including a diff that is still streaming.
whenNotToUse: For code samples in documentation or settings, with nothing to apply, use MonarchCodeBlock. For a side-by-side or full-file comparison, use a diff viewer.
api: init(_ code: String, language: String? = nil, title: String? = nil, isDiff: Bool? = nil, isHighlighted: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = false, showsWrapToggle: Bool = true, isCopyable: Bool = true, isIncomplete: Bool = false, isWrapped: Binding<Bool>? = nil, labels: MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels = MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onInsert: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onApply: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(_ code: String, language: String? = nil, title: String? = nil, isDiff: Bool? = nil, isHighlighted: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = false, showsWrapToggle: Bool = true, isCopyable: Bool = true, isIncomplete: Bool = false, isWrapped: Binding<Bool>? = nil, labels: MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels = MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onInsert: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onApply: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil) where Actions == EmptyView

struct MonarchAiCodeBlockLabels { init(apply: String? = nil, insert: String? = nil, actionLabel: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, incompleteHint: String? = nil, codeBlock: MonarchCodeBlockLabels = MonarchCodeBlockLabels()) }

options.name: code
options.description: The code, exactly as it should be copied, applied and inserted.

options.name: language
options.description: A language id that picks the highlighter and the header text; "diff" or "patch" turns on the diff mode.

options.name: title
options.description: The header text, such as a file name (the web's filename). It also names the code for VoiceOver and the action buttons.

options.name: isDiff
options.description: Forces the diff mode on or off.

options.name: isHighlighted
options.description: Syntax colouring.

options.name: showsLineNumbers
options.description: Line numbers before the lines, not read by VoiceOver.

options.name: showsWrapToggle
options.description: The wrap toggle in the header.

options.name: isCopyable
options.description: The copy button in the header.

options.name: isIncomplete
options.description: The code is still arriving: Apply and Insert are disabled, with a hint saying why. Copy stays available.

options.name: isWrapped
options.description: Controls wrapping; without it the block keeps the state itself, starting unwrapped.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Apply, Insert, the spoken action names, the incomplete hint and the code block's own strings.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied code after each copy.

options.name: onInsert
options.description: Adds a secondary Insert button that hands over the code.

options.name: onApply
options.description: Adds a primary Apply button that hands over the code.

options.name: actions
options.description: App controls placed in the action row before Insert and Apply.

states.name: ready
states.description: The code block, then a trailing row with the app's controls, Insert (secondary) and Apply (primary).

states.name: incomplete
states.description: Insert and Apply are disabled while the code streams in; Copy works on what has arrived.

states.name: diff
states.description: Added and removed lines with markers and the AI diff colours of MonarchCodeBlock.

states.name: no actions
states.description: Without onApply, onInsert or actions there is no action row: the block is a plain MonarchCodeBlock.

appearance: The code block's muted surface, border and header, then Monarch buttons in the secondary and primary variants. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: On the web Apply and Insert sit in the block's header. MonarchCodeBlock has no slot for extra header controls, so on iOS they are in a row under the code; a header slot on MonarchCodeBlock would let them move up. The web re-tokenises streaming code incrementally; iOS re-tokenises the whole code on each update. The web names the header text filename; iOS calls it title, as MonarchCodeBlock does. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The code is read as MonarchCodeBlock reads it: a container named after the title or language, one element per line, added and removed lines named.
Apply and Insert are buttons named with the code, such as "Apply server.ts".
While the code is incomplete they are disabled and their hint is "Available when the code is complete".
Every button has a 44-point touch target; the row wraps at large text sizes.
edgeCases: Empty code still shows the header and one empty line.
Apply and Insert receive the code as given, including a trailing newline.
With several blocks in one answer, give each a title so the actions are told apart.

name: MonarchAiComputerView
title: AiComputerView
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchCalloutBanner, a screenshot box (MonarchRemoteImage/AsyncImage at the screenshot's aspectRatio with GeometryReader markers), MonarchLightbox for pinch zoom, MonarchButton controls in MonarchFlowLayout, confirmationDialog for Stop, DisclosureGroup for the compact log, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: A live view of an AI agent operating a browser or a computer: the latest screenshot with the agent's pointer and actions marked, the status in words, who is in control, a log of every action, and Pause, Take over, Hand back and Stop.
whenToUse: When an agent operates a website or a computer on the person's behalf and they need to watch it, see what it did, and pause, take control or stop it.
whenNotToUse: For an agent's actions on records without a screen use MonarchAiActionLog. For the steps of a plan use MonarchAiChainOfSteps or MonarchAiTaskProgress. For a plain screenshot use MonarchLightbox.
api: init(status: MonarchAiComputerViewStatus, frame: MonarchAiComputerFrame? = nil, actions: [MonarchAiComputerAction] = [], currentURL: String? = nil, windowTitle: String? = nil, pointer: MonarchAiComputerPoint? = nil, surface: MonarchAiComputerViewSurface = .browser, waitingReason: String? = nil, selection: Binding<String?>? = nil, showsTypedText: Bool = false, isCompact: Bool = false, visibleActions: Int = 200, announceInterval: Duration = .seconds(4), labels: MonarchAiComputerViewLabels = MonarchAiComputerViewLabels(), onPauseChange: (@MainActor (Bool) -> Void)? = nil, onTakeOver: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onHandBack: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onStop: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiComputerViewStatus: String { case starting, working, paused, waitingForYou, takenOver, done, failed, stopped }
enum MonarchAiComputerActionKind: String { case click, type, scroll, navigate, key, wait, read, other }
enum MonarchAiComputerViewSurface: String { case browser, computer }
struct MonarchAiComputerPoint { init(x: Double, y: Double) }

struct MonarchAiComputerFrame { init(image: Image?, width: Double, height: Double, capturedAt: Date, alt: String? = nil, isSensitive: Bool = false); init(url: URL?, width: Double, height: Double, capturedAt: Date, alt: String? = nil, isSensitive: Bool = false) }

struct MonarchAiComputerAction: Identifiable { init(id: String, kind: MonarchAiComputerActionKind, label: String, date: Date, point: MonarchAiComputerPoint? = nil, detail: String? = nil, isSensitive: Bool = false) }

struct MonarchAiComputerViewLabels { init(label:, status:, kind:, agentInControl:, youInControl:, waitingTitle:, waitingFallback:, pause:, resume:, takeOver:, handBack:, stop:, stopQuestion:, stopConfirm:, stopCancel:, logLabel:, logToggle:, empty:, hidden:, sensitiveLabel:, noFrame:, frameUnavailable:, frameHidden:, frameAlt:, latestAction:, capturedAt:, address:, zoom:, showEarlier:, announceActions:, announceStatus:, announceTakenOver:, announceReleased:) }

options.name: status
options.description: Where the session is. Each change is announced once.

options.name: frame
options.description: The latest screenshot, as an Image or an http or https URL, with its pixel size and capture time.

options.name: actions
options.description: What the agent did, oldest first. New entries are announced, throttled.

options.name: currentURL
options.description: The address of the page, shown as text without any user:password part.

options.name: windowTitle
options.description: The title of the window or page.

options.name: pointer
options.description: Where the agent's pointer is, in screenshot pixels.

options.name: surface
options.description: What is operated; only changes the wording.

options.name: waitingReason
options.description: Why the agent waits, shown while the status is waitingForYou.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the highlighted action, whose point is marked on the screenshot. Without it the view keeps the selection.

options.name: showsTypedText
options.description: Shows the detail of typing actions. Sensitive actions stay hidden.

options.name: isCompact
options.description: Puts the log behind a disclosure, "Actions (12)".

options.name: visibleActions
options.description: How many of the newest actions the log shows before "Show earlier"; at least one.

options.name: announceInterval
options.description: The shortest time between two action announcements.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onPauseChange
options.description: Shows Pause while starting or working and Resume while paused; receives the wanted paused state.

options.name: onTakeOver
options.description: Shows Take over while the agent holds control (primary while it waits for the person).

options.name: onHandBack
options.description: Shows Hand back while the person holds control.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Shows Stop until the session is finished; runs after the confirmation dialog.

states.name: starting
states.description: A small spinner beside "Starting"; the agent-in-control banner.

states.name: working
states.description: The CPU icon and "Working"; the agent-in-control banner in the info tone; Pause, Take over and Stop.

states.name: paused
states.description: "Paused" with Resume in place of Pause.

states.name: waiting for you
states.description: A warning notice with the reason; Take over is the primary button.

states.name: taken over
states.description: "You are in control" and a warning-tone banner; Hand back is the primary button.

states.name: done, failed, stopped
states.description: A success, danger or neutral icon and the word; no banner and no buttons.

states.name: no screenshot
states.description: The box keeps a 16:10 shape and reads "No screenshot yet".

states.name: screenshot hidden
states.description: A crossed-out eye and "Screenshot hidden: it may show private information", for a sensitive screenshot or one right after a sensitive action.

states.name: screenshot unavailable
states.description: "Screenshot unavailable" for an address that is not http or https.

states.name: selected action
states.description: The row has the accent background and border and a check mark; its point gets an accent ring on the screenshot.

states.name: windowed log
states.description: A ghost "Show 3 earlier actions" button above the newest actions.

appearance: The screenshot sits in a rounded box on the muted background with the default border. The latest action's point has a ring in the strong AI colour, the selected action's a thicker ring in the strong accent colour, and the pointer is an arrow glyph in the default text colour; each has a light halo in the surface colour so it reads on any screenshot. Log rows are rounded surface tiles with the subtle border, the selected one on the subtle accent background. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows the log beside the screenshot on wide screens; on iPhone the log is under the screenshot, and isCompact puts it in a system DisclosureGroup. Zoom opens the screenshot in MonarchLightbox, where it can be pinched and panned, instead of a wheel-zoomed frame. Stop confirms in the system confirmation dialog rather than inline buttons. The web can show a live MediaStream and forward the person's pointer and keys to the remote screen while in control (onPointer, onKey, onRelease); a native app owns its own streaming and input, so this view shows screenshots only and has no input forwarding. onSelectAction and selectedActionId are one selection binding. The parity map names MonarchAiActionLog as a dependency; its rows describe agent actions on records with Undo, which does not fit screen actions with points and private details, so the log here is its own list of row buttons. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android has no computer view yet.
accessibility: The view is a container named "Assistant browser view" or "Assistant computer view".

The screenshot is one image element read as its description and the latest action ("The sign-in page. Latest action: Clicked Continue"), built by a tested pure function, with a named Zoom action; the markers are hidden.
A hidden or missing screenshot reads why it is not shown.
The status is an icon and a word, never colour alone.
Each status change is announced once; taking over and handing back have their own sentences.
New actions are announced no more often than announceInterval; several are summed up as "3 new actions. Latest: …". A sensitive action is announced as "Private action".
Log rows are buttons read as "Click: Clicked Continue" with the detail (or "Hidden") and the time as the value; the selected row has the selected trait and a check mark.
Every button has a 44-point touch target; the address is read after "Address".
edgeCases: A sensitive action's label and detail are never shown or announced, and the screenshot after it is hidden even if showsTypedText is true.
Typed text shows only with showsTypedText.
Credentials in currentURL (user:password@) are removed before it is shown.
Points outside the screenshot are clamped to its edges; a screenshot with no usable size draws no markers.
When the selected action is also the latest action with a point, only the selection ring is drawn.
A visibleActions below one shows one action before Show earlier.
The stop confirmation closes by itself when the session finishes.

            label: {{actions.1.label}},
            date: {{actions.1.at|date}}
        ),
    ],
    currentURL: {{currentUrl}},

name: MonarchAiConfidenceMeter
title: AiConfidenceMeter
wrapsNative: HStack in a Capsule (badge), or Capsule track and fill in a GeometryReader (bar)
summary: How sure the AI is about a value, as low, medium or high, always in words: a compact badge or a labelled bar.
whenToUse: Beside a value the AI extracted or generated, so people know when to check it.
whenNotToUse: For task progress use ProgressView with the monarchLinear style. For a status that is not a confidence use MonarchBadge.
api: init(value: Double, explanation: String? = nil, variant: MonarchAiConfidenceMeterVariant = .badge, size: MonarchAiConfidenceMeterSize = .md, lowThreshold: Double = 0.6, highThreshold: Double = 0.85, showsValue: Bool? = nil, levelLabel: String? = nil, meterLabel: String? = nil, valueText: ((String, String) -> String)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiConfidenceLevel { case low, medium, high; static func level(for value: Double, lowThreshold: Double = 0.6, highThreshold: Double = 0.85) -> MonarchAiConfidenceLevel }
enum MonarchAiConfidenceMeterVariant { case badge, bar }
enum MonarchAiConfidenceMeterSize { case sm, md }

options.name: value
options.description: The confidence from 0 to 1. Values outside the range are clamped; not-a-number counts as 0.

options.name: explanation
options.description: Why the model is or is not confident. Shown under the bar; for the badge it is only the VoiceOver hint.

options.name: variant
options.description: A compact pill, or a labelled bar.

options.name: size
options.description: sm has tighter padding, a thinner track and caption text in the bar.

options.name: lowThreshold
options.description: The edge under which confidence is low.

options.name: highThreshold
options.description: The edge from which confidence is high.

options.name: showsValue
options.description: Whether to show the percentage. By default only the bar shows it.

options.name: levelLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in label of the band.

options.name: meterLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Confidence" spoken name of the bar.

options.name: valueText
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken value. Receives the band label and the percentage.

states.name: low
states.description: "Needs check" with a warning triangle, in the low-confidence colour on a danger-subtle pill.

states.name: medium
states.description: "Medium confidence" with a half-filled circle, in the medium-confidence colour on a warning-subtle pill.

states.name: high
states.description: "High confidence" with a check symbol, in the high-confidence colour on a success-subtle pill.

appearance: The badge is a capsule with a subtle status fill and border and the confidence colour for the icon and label. The bar is a muted capsule track filled with the confidence colour of the band.
platformNotes: The web shows the badge's explanation in a tooltip on hover and focus; iOS has no tooltip on touch, so for the badge the explanation reaches only VoiceOver. Use the bar when sighted people must read it. The web's small badge uses an 11-point size; iOS uses the caption role at both sizes and tightens the padding.
accessibility: The meter is one element. The badge reads "Needs check, 42% confidence"; the bar has the label "Confidence" and that text as its value.
The explanation is the accessibility hint.
The band is always in words and has its own icon, not colour alone.
The percentage is formatted in the user's locale.
Text scales with Dynamic Type. The meter is not interactive.
The fill of the bar starts at the leading edge, so it mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A value exactly on the low threshold is medium; exactly on the high threshold is high.
If lowThreshold is above highThreshold there is no medium band.
A change of value animates the fill unless Reduce Motion is on.

name: MonarchAiConnectorPicker
title: AiConnectorPicker
wrapsNative: Content for sheet(isPresented:content:): NavigationStack with a List, searchable(text:prompt:), a Toggle (switch) per connector, DisclosureGroup of tools, Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) per tool, ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) Done
summary: A searchable sheet where a person chooses which connected apps and data sources an assistant may use in this conversation, and whether each tool runs, asks first or never runs.
whenToUse: From the composer of an assistant that can call outside apps, so people can turn connectors on and off and decide which tools need their approval.
whenNotToUse: To show the access an assistant already has to apps as read, write or admin levels, use MonarchAiPermissionScope. To approve one tool call in the conversation, use the tool call's own approval.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, connectors: Binding<[MonarchAiConnector]>, allowsDestructiveAutoApprove: Bool = false, isSearchable: Bool = true, expandedIDs: Set<String> = [], labels: MonarchAiConnectorPickerLabels = MonarchAiConnectorPickerLabels(), onConnect: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onManage: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAiConnector { init(id: String, name: String, description: String? = nil, iconURL: URL? = nil, status: MonarchAiConnectorStatus, account: String? = nil, isEnabled: Bool, tools: [MonarchAiConnectorTool] = []) }
struct MonarchAiConnectorTool { init(id: String, name: String, description: String? = nil, risk: MonarchAiConnectorToolRisk, permission: MonarchAiConnectorToolPermission) }
enum MonarchAiConnectorStatus: String { case connected, needsSignIn, error, unavailable }
enum MonarchAiConnectorToolRisk: String { case read, write, destructive }
enum MonarchAiConnectorToolPermission: String { case allow, ask, never }

struct MonarchAiConnectorPickerLabels { init(title:, searchPrompt:, done:, summary:, results:, noResults:, clearSearch:, empty:, status:, account:, enable:, disabledReason:, signIn:, reconnect:, manage:, actionLabel:, tools:, permissionLabel:, permission:, risk:, destructiveLocked:) }

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the navigation title "Connectors".

options.name: connectors
options.description: The connectors with their state. The switches change isEnabled and the pickers change each tool's permission; store and enforce them in the app.

options.name: allowsDestructiveAutoApprove
options.description: Lets a tool that can delete data be set to Allow. By default Allow is not offered for such a tool and a line says why.

options.name: isSearchable
options.description: Adds the system search field, which filters connectors by name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the summary, counts, statuses, reasons, permissions and risks.

options.name: onConnect
options.description: Runs the sign-in for a connector that needs it, or reconnects one with a problem, given its id. Shows Sign in or Reconnect on those rows.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Opens a connector's settings, given its id. Shows Manage on every row.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The ids of the connectors whose tools are open when the picker appears.

states.name: connected
states.description: The switch can be used; a filled check in the strong success colour and "Connected as <account>".

states.name: sign-in needed
states.description: The switch is disabled; a lock in the strong warning colour, "Sign-in needed", the reason, and Sign in with onConnect.

states.name: connection problem
states.description: The switch is disabled; an exclamation mark in the strong danger colour, "Connection problem", the reason, and Reconnect with onConnect.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: The switch is disabled with a muted no-connection symbol and the reason.

states.name: tools
states.description: A disclosure group "4 tools"; each tool has its name, a risk badge (neutral Reads data, warning Changes data, danger Can delete data) and a menu picker. The pickers are disabled while the connector is off.

states.name: destructive locked
states.description: Allow is not offered and "Tools that can delete data can’t run without asking." is shown under the picker.

states.name: no results
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState naming the search, with Clear search.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState: "No connectors are available."

appearance: A system List in the sheet with Monarch text styles: connector names in the strong body style, descriptions, statuses and reasons in the muted caption style, the summary as the section header. Status symbols use the strong success, warning and danger colours and risk badges the matching tones. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names a List in a sheet: the component is the sheet's content, with its own NavigationStack, search field and Done button, because the web panel sits beside the conversation where a phone has no room. The web reports changes through onEnabledChange and onPermissionChange; iOS binds the connectors, the SwiftUI convention, so the picker writes the new values and the app watches the binding. The web's radio group of Allow, Ask first and Never becomes a menu Picker, which stays readable at large text sizes; a disabled Allow radio becomes Allow left out of the menu, unless it is already the stored value. The web's controlled query and expandedIds are internal state here. Connector icons are an address loaded with MonarchFavicon (letter tile otherwise) instead of any view. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: Each switch is a standard toggle named "Use <name> in this conversation" by a tested string; its hint is the status and, when it cannot be turned on, the reason.
Status and risk are always words next to the icons and colours.
Sign in, Reconnect, Manage and the tools disclosure are named with the action and the connector, such as "Sign in: Drive".
Each tool's picker is a standard menu Picker named "Permission for <tool>", so VoiceOver reads the current choice.
The number of connectors found is announced when the search text changes.
Done is a standard toolbar button in the confirmation placement when the picker is presented.
edgeCases: The summary counts every connector, whatever the search.
Search ignores case, accents and spaces around the text.
A connector stored as enabled while not connected shows its switch on but disabled and does not count as on.
Turning a connector on that is not connected is refused by the binding logic, not only by the disabled switch.
Setting Allow on a locked destructive tool is refused even if a stored value tries to.

name: MonarchAiContextChips
title: AiContextChips
wrapsNative: MonarchFlowLayout (a SwiftUI Layout) of capsule chips with a Button for removal; Int.formatted(.number.notation(.compactName)) for counts
summary: What the AI will see with the next prompt, as removable chips with a kind, a name, a token count with a weight mark, and a total.
whenToUse: Above or inside a prompt composer, to show and trim the files, selection, page, records, apps and people that go with the next prompt.
whenNotToUse: Not for general tags or filters (use MonarchTag) and not for attachments that are uploaded as files in a message (show them as file parts).
api: init(_ items: [MonarchAiContextItem], budget: Int? = nil, showsTotal: Bool? = nil, emptyText: String? = nil, locale: Locale = .current, labels: MonarchAiContextChipsLabels = MonarchAiContextChipsLabels(), onRemove: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchAiContextItem { init(id: String, kind: MonarchAiContextKind, label: String, tokens: Int? = nil, description: String? = nil, isRemovable: Bool = true, group: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiContextKind: String { case file, selection, page, record, app, person }
enum MonarchAiContextWeight { case light, medium, heavy; init(tokens: Int, reference: Int) }

struct MonarchAiContextChipsLabels { init(label: String? = nil, kind: ((MonarchAiContextKind) -> String)? = nil, tokens: ((String, Int) -> String)? = nil, total: ((String, Int) -> String)? = nil, remove: ((String) -> String)? = nil, removed: ((String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: items
options.description: What the AI will see, in the order it was added.

options.name: budget
options.description: Tokens the context may use. When set, each weight is the item's share of the budget instead of the total.

options.name: showsTotal
options.description: Whether the total is shown after the chips. By default when any item has a token count; never with no items.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Shown when items is empty. Without it nothing is shown.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of the compact numbers.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: list name, kind names, count and total texts, remove name and removal announcement.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Runs with the id of the item to remove; take it out of items. No remove buttons without it. Items with isRemovable false never get one.

states.name: weight
states.description: Light, medium or heavy fill one, two or three bars of the mark; heavy also draws the count in the default text colour.

states.name: empty
states.description: Shows emptyText in the subtle text colour, or nothing.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Apply disabled(_:): muted fill, subtle border, disabled text, and the remove buttons stop responding.

appearance: Capsules in the AI subtle fill with the AI border; the kind icon and the filled bars in the AI strong role, empty bars in the default border role, counts in the muted text role. All are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same kinds, weights, compact counts and strings as the web. The web shows the description as a tooltip; on iOS it is the VoiceOver hint and a pointer tooltip through help(_:). The web moves keyboard focus to the next remove button or a fallback element; on iOS VoiceOver focus moves to the next chip (or the previous one) and there is no fallback element parameter. The kind icons are SF Symbols rather than the web's drawn glyphs.
accessibility: The chips are a container named "Context".
Each chip is one element read as kind, name and count, "File: contract.pdf, 1.2K tokens"; the full name is read even when it is truncated on screen.
The description is the hint of the chip.
The weight is shown by the number of filled bars and by the count, not by colour alone.
Each remove button is a separate button named "Remove contract.pdf from context" with a 44-point touch target.
After a removal VoiceOver announces "contract.pdf removed from context" and moves to the next chip, or the previous one.
edgeCases: A long name truncates in the middle at 192 points, scaled with Dynamic Type.
Chips wrap onto new rows; a chip wider than the row gets a row of its own.
Exactly one token reads "1 token"; negative counts are shown as 0.

name: MonarchAiContextDivider
title: AiContextDivider
wrapsNative: Text, a stroked Shape for the lines, DisclosureGroup, Button with MonarchButtonStyle
summary: A labelled rule between messages in a thread: a calendar day, a context reset, or a point where earlier messages were summarized.
whenToUse: Between messages of an AI thread, to start a new day, to mark where the assistant's memory starts again, or to mark messages that were condensed.
whenNotToUse: Not as a general separator: use MonarchDivider. Not for a handoff to another agent or person, which is AiHandoff.
api: init(_ kind: MonarchAiContextDividerKind, date: Date? = nil, summary: String? = nil, now: Date? = nil, label: String? = nil, detail: String? = nil, summaryTitle: String? = nil, summaryPrefix: String? = nil, expandTitle: String? = nil, onExpand: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiContextDividerKind { case day, contextReset, summarized }

options.name: kind
options.description: day, contextReset or summarized.

options.name: date
options.description: The day of a day divider. Without it a day divider has an empty label.

options.name: summary
options.description: For summarized: the summary the assistant now works from, shown behind a disclosure.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for Today and Yesterday. nil is the current time.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in label of the kind.

options.name: detail
options.description: Replaces the built-in description of a context reset.

options.name: summaryTitle
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Show summary".

options.name: summaryPrefix
options.description: Replaces the built-in "AI-generated summary:" that VoiceOver reads before the summary.

options.name: expandTitle
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Show earlier messages".

options.name: onExpand
options.description: For summarized: shows a button that runs this to reveal the original messages.

states.name: day
states.description: The label is Today, Yesterday, a weekday and date for this year, or a full date. Solid lines.

states.name: contextReset
states.description: The label, dashed lines and one line of description under them.

states.name: summarized
states.description: The label and the lines in the AI colours. With a summary, a disclosure; with onExpand, a button.

states.name: summary expanded
states.description: The summary is shown in a tinted box under the disclosure.

appearance: A centred caption between two hairlines. The lines use the subtle border role for a day, the default border role, dashed, for a reset, and the AI border role for a summary; the label is muted text, or the strong AI role for a summary. The summary box is the subtle AI fill with the AI border. All roles come from the theme, so the four themes differ only in their values.
platformNotes: The web takes locale, timeZone and now as props; here the locale, calendar and time zone come from the SwiftUI environment and only now is a parameter. Today and Yesterday come from the system's relative date formatter in the environment locale, so Monarch ships no strings for them and they cannot be overridden separately (use label). The summary is a String, not arbitrary content. The disclosure is the standard DisclosureGroup, so its chevron is at the trailing edge rather than after the centred title as on the web. The web gives the divider the separator role; SwiftUI has no separator trait, so it is read as text.
accessibility: Without controls the divider is one element, read as the label and then the description.
A context reset has dashed lines as well as its own colour and text, so it does not depend on colour.
With controls, the label, the disclosure and the button are separate elements in reading order.
The summary is read after "AI-generated summary:", which is not shown.
The disclosure title and the button each have a touch target at least 44 points high.
The lines are hidden from VoiceOver. Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps.
edgeCases: A day divider without a date has an empty label and shows only the lines.
A long label wraps and stays centred; the lines keep a least length of 16 points.
summary and onExpand are ignored for day and contextReset.
Tomorrow and later days are shown as a date, not as a relative name.
The day is counted in the time zone of the environment, so the same moment can be Today in one zone and Yesterday in another.

appearance: A muted track with segments in the theme's data colours (the sixth part and Other in the subtle text colour), a label in default text and the summary in muted text. Without a breakdown the fill is accent, warning or danger solid. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web cycles the five data colours for a sixth part; iOS follows MonarchChartLegend and draws the sixth part and later in neutral. The web's useAiContextUsage hook and its token estimator are not offered: pass used and isApproximate, or the usage the latest message reported. accessibility: The bar is one element named "Context window" whose value is the summary, for example "45,000 of 128,000 tokens (35%)", with the updates-frequently trait.
The legend is a container named "What fills the context window"; each entry is read as its label and amount, and the swatches are decorative.
The notice is written text with an icon, so the state does not depend on colour, and VoiceOver announces it when the state changes while the meter is on screen.
The compact meter is a button with the same name and value, a hint that it shows the details, and a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: Negative counts are drawn as zero; a limit of zero or less is always ok and shows 0%.
When the parts add up to more than the window, the bar is scaled to the total so every part stays visible.
Parts that cover more than used produce no Other entry.
The heading and summary sit on one line when they fit and stack at large text sizes.

The web's model slot takes any view, such as an AiModelPicker; here model is text, and the model is changed with a Picker in the menu or a MonarchAiModelPicker in a toolbar item, because a menu cannot hold a sheet-presenting picker. name: MonarchAiConversation
title: useAiConversation
wrapsNative: Observation (@Observable, on the main actor) over an injected transport that returns AsyncThrowingStream; Codable for the message model
summary: Headless state for an AI conversation: it sends prompts through an injected transport, streams the reply into the vendor-neutral message model, and handles stop, regenerate, retry, edit and resend as branches, tool approval, client-side tools, an offline queue and feedback.
whenToUse: As the model behind any chat surface. Keep it in @State or in your own model, read messages, status and error in views, and implement MonarchAiTransport for your backend.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single completion in a text field, which is MonarchAiCompletion with AiGhostText. It draws nothing: use the AI components to show the messages.

options.name: transport
options.description: Connects the conversation to your backend. Monarch does no networking.

options.name: initialMessages
options.description: Messages to start with, for example a stored conversation. Shown as one branch.

options.name: conversationId
options.description: The id from an earlier session, sent with every request. A done event replaces it.

options.name: body
options.description: Request fields sent on every turn, merged under the fields given to send. Also a settable property.

options.name: queuesWhileOffline
options.description: While offline, send keeps the message in queued and sends it, in order, once setOnline(true) is called.

options.name: slowAfter
options.description: The time without any event from a running reply before isSlow becomes true. nil turns it off.

options.name: connectionLostMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in "The connection was lost." of the error raised when the stream throws.

options.name: toolResultFailedMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in "The tool result could not be sent." recorded when a client-side tool throws without a message.

options.name: generateId
options.description: Custom message ids. The default is a UUID.

states.name: idle
states.description: Nothing is running.

states.name: submitted
states.description: Sent, waiting for the first event. isBusy is true.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Events are arriving and messages changes with each one. isBusy is true.

states.name: awaitingApproval
states.description: A tool call waits for approveTool or denyTool. canSend is false and send returns false.

states.name: awaitingToolResult
states.description: The model called a tool the client runs: onToolCall runs it, or call submitToolResult.

states.name: error
states.description: The last turn failed. error holds the code, the message and whether it can be retried or resumed; the reply ends with an error part.

states.name: stopped
states.description: stop() ended the reply. What arrived stays, streaming parts are closed and running tool calls are cancelled.

states.name: offline
states.description: After setOnline(false), sent messages wait in queued and appear at the end of messages with isQueued.

states.name: slow
states.description: isSlow is true while a running reply has sent nothing for slowAfter.

appearance: None: it is a model and draws nothing.
platformNotes: The web is the useAiConversation hook; here it is an @Observable class. The message model has the web's fields and reads and writes the web's JSON (kebab-case raw values, a type field per part); the model type is MonarchAiConversationMessage because MonarchAiMessage is the message view. Times stay ISO 8601 strings, with createdDate and timestamp(_:) for Date. Fields the web types as unknown are MonarchAiJSON. Not offered, because they belong to the browser or to a transport: File uploads (uploadFile, inlineFiles, uploads, onUploadProgress; send takes file parts the app has already uploaded), the SSE, provider, AG-UI and Rook transports and their mappers, the testing kit, and submit as a promise (send returns whether the message was accepted). There is no AbortSignal: the stream is read in a task that is cancelled on stop. The network source is setOnline(_:), fed by the app, for example from NWPathMonitor. Updates are not batched per frame; SwiftUI coalesces observation changes itself. With a tool policy, every waiting call is put to the policy before the status is decided; the web stops at the first decided call.
accessibility: It draws nothing and announces nothing; the components that show the messages do.
isSlow, isQueued, the error message and the tool call states are plain values, so a view can speak them.
edgeCases: Sending while a reply streams ends that reply, keeping what arrived, and starts the next.
A done or error event ends the reply even if the transport keeps the stream open; a stream that ends without done leaves the status idle and does not call onFinish.
A stream that throws ends the reply with the retryable code network. With a run id and a transport that resumes runs, the error is resumable.
retry rewrites the same message; regenerate and editAndResend add a branch, and messages then carry branch with the index and count.
A queued message that fails holds the rest of the queue until the connection comes back again.
Sending a new message cancels tool calls that still waited for a client-side result.
Releasing the conversation cancels the task that reads the stream.
Decoding a part with an unknown type throws.

whenToUse: An app screen where the assistant should act on the rows, text or records the person has selected, and the content should make room for the assistant on a wide window instead of being covered.
whenNotToUse: A full-screen chat with history: use the ai-chat-page recipe. An assistant that never needs page context: MonarchAiAssistantPanel opened from MonarchAiLauncher with .monarchAiAssistantPanel(isPresented:panel:) is enough.
