options.description: The conversation the assistant shows and sends to, held above the navigation so it survives moving between screens.

options.name: title
options.description: The assistant's heading, such as "Assistant", passed to MonarchAiAssistantPanel.

options.name: isAssistantOpen
options.description: Whether the assistant is shown; set by MonarchAiLauncher (and its Command-J shortcut), the panel's Close (and Escape), and a swipe down on the sheet.

options.name: draft
options.description: The prompt draft, hoisted because a sheet's content is rebuilt each time it opens and the panel moves between sheet and inspector when the width class changes.

options.name: content
options.description: The app screen. It writes the selection; the inspector sits beside it in a regular width and the sheet covers it in a compact width.

options.name: selected
options.description: What the person selected on the page. Shown as a Selection chip after the always-present chips and sent under the selection request field as label and text objects, as the web's body.selection is.

options.name: context
options.description: Chips that always show, such as the current page (isRemovable: false); the selection chip follows them.

options.name: onRemoveContext
options.description: Removing the selection chip clears the selection, so nothing is sent.

options.name: launcher
options.description: Leave it out when the app opens the assistant from its own toolbar button (a subtle MonarchAiLauncher in a ToolbarItem).

options.name: starters / headerActions / toolbar / footer
options.description: Passed straight to the panel, as the web's panelProps are.

states.name: closed
states.description: The content uses the full width; the launcher shows at the bottom trailing corner.

states.name: docked open
states.description: In a regular width (iPad full screen and wide split views) the assistant is a system inspector column at the trailing edge and the content reflows beside it; the launcher hides; Close or Escape closes it.

states.name: sheet open
states.description: In a compact width the assistant is a system sheet at the medium detent over the content, which the person can drag to large; a swipe down, Close or Escape closes it. The launcher stays under the sheet.

states.name: with selection
states.description: A Selection chip with the count of selected rows shows above the prompt input, and the selection goes in the request body of the next prompt; removing the chip clears it.

appearance: Every part is an existing component or system container: the system inspector or sheet, MonarchAiAssistantPanel on the surface colour, MonarchAiLauncher in its solid accent form, a system List with Monarch checkbox toggles, and the app's content in the Monarch theme. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiCopilotLayout as one component with a React selection context (useAiSelectionContext), a side option, a 24rem rail of at most 45%, a full-screen sheet under 640px and a launcher with Cmd+J or Ctrl+J. On iOS it is a recipe, as on Android: the selection is ordinary app state the screen writes, shown as a MonarchAiContextItem chip and sent by setting MonarchAiConversation.body, so no context object is needed. Android docks the assistant in the supporting pane of SupportingPaneScaffold from the expanded width class; iOS uses the system .inspector through .monarchAiAssistantPanel(isPresented:panel:), which is what Apple's apps use for supporting content: it sits at the trailing edge with a system width, so there is no side option, and it follows the regular horizontal size class rather than a width breakpoint (iPad full screen and wide split views dock; iPhone and narrow Slide Over or split views use the sheet). The phone form is the panel's sheet with the medium and large detents, where Android uses a full-height ModalBottomSheet. Android's BackHandler is not needed: the sheet closes with a swipe and the inspector with Close. The keyboard shortcut is offered because MonarchAiLauncher carries Command-J by default, so a hardware keyboard opens the assistant; while the inspector shows the launcher is hidden and Escape (Close's cancel shortcut) closes it, so Command-J does not toggle it closed as the web's does. The web moves focus to the input on open and back to the launcher on close; here the input is not focused on open (the panel's choice, as Android) and the system sheet and inspector manage focus on close. The web's clearSelectionOnSend and panelProps.onSend become app code: clear the selection after send, or use the panel initialiser that takes messages and onSend. The selection on the page uses Toggle with .monarchCheckbox in a List, as Android's MonarchCheckboxRow; a table with many rows can use List(selection:) with EditMode instead.
accessibility: MonarchAiLauncher is a button named by its label that states whether the assistant is open, with Command-J as its keyboard shortcut.

MonarchAiAssistantPanel's title is a header (the navigation title of the sheet, or a heading of the inspector pane); its Close button is named "Close assistant" and carries the Escape shortcut while no reply runs.
What the assistant will receive is visible before sending: the Selection chip names the number of selected rows, reads the selected rows as its hint, and can be removed; the page chip cannot.
The selection on the page is made with Toggle and .monarchCheckbox, whose whole row toggles and reads its checked state.
The sheet closes with the system swipe down; the inspector closes with Close.
Replies, errors and the offline notice are announced by the panel's MonarchAiThread.
edgeCases: The panel's thread scrolls itself: give the layout a bounded height (the screen, or a fixed height in a scrolling page) and never put it in a vertically scrolling parent. The content may scroll itself.
Setting conversation.body replaces the conversation's own request fields; an app that uses them merges its fields with the selection.
A prompt queued while offline is sent with the body at the moment it leaves the queue, so a selection changed in between goes with it.

Crossing the width class while open (rotating an iPad in a split view, resizing a window) moves the panel between the inspector and the sheet; the hoisted draft and the conversation keep the text and the messages.
An empty selection sends no selection field and shows no chip.
Hiding the launcher reads the environment's horizontal size class, which is the same signal .monarchAiAssistantPanel uses, so the two always agree.

accessibility: The queue is a container named by its title, or "Drafts to review"; the progress bar reads "2 of 5 reviewed".
Each draft's title is a header; its status is a badge with an icon and a name, so it does not depend on colour.
The body is read after "AI draft", so it is identified as AI-written; the visible AI badge is hidden from VoiceOver to avoid repeating it.
After Approve, Send or Skip, VoiceOver moves to the next draft that needs review, wrapping to the top, or stays on the same draft when none is left.
Every status change is announced, for example "Approved: Reply to Alex Morgan" or "New draft ready: …".
The editor is named "Edit draft:" and the title, and focus returns to the draft after Save or Cancel.
Buttons have 44-point touch targets and wrap onto new rows.
edgeCases: Drafts that appear for the first time are not announced; only status changes are.
The body is plain text and is never rendered as markup.
A long title moves the status badge under it when they do not fit on one line.

The web's word tokens keep inner apostrophes as one word; this component reuses MonarchDiffViewer's tokens, which split them, so a changed contraction can show a smaller change. The part keeps the conversation model's MonarchAiEditProposalPart.
accessibility: The card is a container named by its title; the title is a header.
Each change is one element read as its name, its decision, then the diff with "Deleted:" and "Inserted:" before removed and added words.
Per-change buttons are named with the change, for example "Accept, Change 2 of 3".
After a decision the result is announced ("Change accepted. 2 left.") and VoiceOver focus moves to the next undecided change's Accept button, else the title.

A change's own status wins over a remembered decision.
Accept all and Reject all only decide undecided changes and hide when none are left.
An addition has an empty before; a removal an empty after.
Very long texts fall back to one removal and one insertion above two million word pairs.

states.description: The retry action is disabled and reads "Try again in 12s". Without onRetry the same text is shown as a caption.

states.name: retrying
states.description: The retry action shows a progress indicator and does not run.

states.name: details expanded
states.description: The technical details are shown in a bordered box.

appearance: The same surface as MonarchBanner: the subtle fill and the border of the tone, the strong role of the tone for the icon, default text for the title and muted text for the description. The first action is a primary button, the others secondary.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner, but the banner takes one action and no custom icon or content, so the card is composed from the banner's tokens and the tone palette and looks the same. The web's code prop is MonarchAiErrorKind(code:). title and message are Strings, and details is a String shown as code. The many built-in strings are replaced through one labels value instead of one parameter each. The actions sit side by side where they fit and one under the other where they do not (ViewThatFits), instead of wrapping one by one. The countdown starts when the card appears and is checked every half second.
accessibility: The icon, title and message are one element, read as "Warning" or "Error", then the title, then the message.
Each action is a separate button with a 44-point touch target; the disclosure title is 44 points high.
The title and message are announced once, at high priority, when the card appears, unless announces is false.
"You can try again now." is announced when a countdown ends.
The tone is an icon and a spoken name as well as a colour. The raw error code is never shown or spoken.
While retrying, the retry button reads "Loading" as its value.
edgeCases: Without handlers and without extra actions there is no action row.
onSummarize is ignored unless the kind is contextOverflow.
A non-positive or infinite retryAfter is no countdown.
A code that matches several rules takes the first: rate limit, then context, safety, tool, network.
Long titles, messages and details wrap; details keep their line breaks.

title: AiEvalReview
wrapsNative: NavigationSplitView(sidebar:detail:) with List(selection:) for the queue and a ScrollView for the item (a navigation stack on iPhone); Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) for the verdict; ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear); TextField(axis: .vertical) in MonarchFormField for notes
summary: A recipe, not a component: a review queue for AI outputs, with each output's prompt, output and expected answer, a 1 to 5 rubric per criterion, notes and a pass or fail verdict.
whenToUse: Human evaluation of model or prompt changes, or spot-checking AI outputs before a feature launches or a model is switched.
whenNotToUse: For end-user feedback on one reply use MonarchAiFeedback. For reviewing AI drafts before they are sent use MonarchAiDraftQueue.

MonarchAiMarkdown(item.output) after MonarchAiGeneratedBadge(size: .sm)
MonarchRatingPicker(criterion.label, value: score(item.id, criterion.id), in: 1...criterion.scale, isClearable: true)
MonarchFormField("Notes") { TextField("Notes", text: note(item.id), axis: .vertical).lineLimit(3...8) }
Picker("Verdict", selection: verdict(item.id)) { Text("Pass").tag("pass" as String?); Text("Fail").tag("fail" as String?) }.pickerStyle(.segmented)

states.name: pending
states.description: A queue row reads "Not reviewed" under its title.

states.name: pass / fail
states.description: The row reads "Pass" or "Fail", and the segmented picker shows the selected segment.

states.name: current
states.description: The queue row of the item shown is the List selection, highlighted by the system and read as selected.

states.name: scored
states.description: "Score 9 / 13" sums the scores given; each picker reads its value.

states.name: first / last
states.description: Previous is disabled on the first item, Next on the last.

states.name: done

states.name: empty

appearance: Every part is an existing control: the system list and segmented picker in the Monarch theme, the linear MonarchProgressViewStyle, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge on the AI roles, MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchRatingPicker, MonarchFormField and small MonarchButtons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AiEvalReview as one component with a sticky queue column beside the item from 768px and the queue stacked above it below. On iOS it is a recipe on the list-detail pattern, as on Android (NavigableListDetailPaneScaffold): NavigationSplitView shows the queue and the item side by side on iPad and in landscape on large iPhones, and collapses to a navigation stack on iPhone, where selecting a row pushes the item and the system back gesture returns to the queue. The web's radio choices per criterion are MonarchRatingPicker; its pass and fail radios are a segmented Picker (Android: a single-choice segmented button row). The web's J / K and P / F shortcuts and the visible shortcut hint are left out: the web hides the hint on touch screens, and an app that wants them for hardware keyboards adds .keyboardShortcut to Previous and Next or .onKeyPress on the detail. The web moves focus to the new item's heading after Previous and Next; this recipe does not move focus. The web's check, cross and dot glyphs in the queue are left out; the verdict is the row's second line of text, as on Android.
accessibility: Each queue row is one element (title and verdict combined) in a List with selection, so VoiceOver reads its title, its verdict as text and whether it is selected.
The Prompt, Output, Expected, Rubric and Verdict labels are headers, so the VoiceOver rotor moves between them; the item's title is the navigation title.
The output carries MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, read as AI-generated.
Each MonarchRatingPicker is named by its criterion and reads its value, for example "3 of 5".
Pass and Fail are a system segmented Picker: VoiceOver reads the picker's label, each segment and the selected state, not colour alone.
Previous, Next and Submit reviews are MonarchButtons with 44-point targets, read as dimmed when disabled.
edgeCases: Keep each criterion at five points or fewer, as the web does.
Persist every change; nothing in the recipe saves reviews by itself.
Do not show which model produced an output when reviewers should judge blind.
A long output scrolls in the detail; the queue scrolls on its own, so do not put the split view in a scrolling parent.
Clearing a score (isClearable) removes it from the total.

summary: Thumbs up and down for an AI answer, then reasons and an optional comment in a sheet, then a thank-you.
whenToUse: Under an AI answer, summary or generated draft when the product wants structured feedback to improve prompts, retrieval or models.
whenNotToUse: When a plain rating is enough, put thumbs in the message's own actions. For rating a person's work or a product, use MonarchRatingPicker or a survey.

options.name: reasons

options.description: Which ratings open the sheet. down: a thumbs up is sent at once. none: every rating is sent at once.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Sends the rating, the chosen reason ids in listed order and the trimmed comment. Throw to show the error.

states.name: unrated
states.description: Two outlined thumbs, neither pressed.

states.name: rated
states.description: The chosen thumb is pressed: filled glyph and the toggle button's on fill.

states.name: details
states.description: A sheet with the question and reasons as checkboxes, the comment, Send feedback and Cancel.

states.name: sending
states.description: The send button shows progress; the sheet cannot be swiped away and the thumbs are disabled.

states.name: thanks
states.description: "Thanks for your feedback." with a check under the thumbs, announced.

states.name: error
states.description: onSubmit threw: the error is shown with an icon and announced; the sheet stays filled in, or the error shows under the thumbs after a direct send.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The thumbs use the disabled colours and do nothing.

appearance: The thumbs are ghost toggle buttons: no fill while off, the accent subtle fill and accent border while on. The sheet uses the surface background, the checkbox group and the text field look; the error is strong danger text, the thank-you muted text. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web shows the reasons as chips and the form inline under the thumbs; on iOS the form is a sheet, as the plan names, and the reasons are a MonarchCheckboxGroup, which is the platform's way to pick several items. Pressed thumbs use the shared toggle button style, so they take the accent colours where the web uses the AI colours. The rating type is MonarchAiMessageFeedback, the same one the conversation model uses. The web returns focus to the thank-you; iOS announces it instead because the sheet closes. onSubmit is an async throwing closure in place of a promise.
accessibility: Each thumb is a standard Toggle (through accessibilityRepresentation) named "Good response" or "Bad response", with on and off as its value; the thumbs are a container named "Rate this response".
A pressed thumb has a filled glyph, so the state is never colour alone.
In the sheet the reasons are labelled checkboxes under the question, the comment has a visible label and reads the error as its hint, and Cancel is the sheet's cancellation action.
The thank-you and the error are announced when they appear.
Thumbs, checkboxes and buttons have touch targets of at least 44 points; text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Pressing the pressed thumb clears the rating and closes nothing else; no submission is sent.
Cancel or a swipe down keeps the rating and sends nothing.
Reason ids that are not listed are dropped from the submission; reasons keep the listed order whatever order they were picked in.
Without onSubmit the thank-you shows at once.
A comment of only spaces is sent as an empty string.

name: MonarchAiGenerativeUi
title: AiGenerativeUi
wrapsNative: A name-to-view-builder registry (MonarchAiUiRegistry) with JSONDecoder into each component's Decodable props type; MonarchInlineNotice for refused parts; ProgressView while props stream
summary: Renders a component the model asked for in a ui part, only when its name is in the app's allow-listed registry, with props treated as untrusted data and decoded into typed models.
whenToUse: When an assistant answers with interactive UI (a slot picker, a chart, a form) that the app has built and registered in advance.
whenNotToUse: Not to render arbitrary markup or code from a model (never do that) and not for documents the assistant produced (use MonarchAiArtifactCard).
api: init(_ part: MonarchAiUiPart, registry: MonarchAiUiRegistry, labels: MonarchAiGenerativeUiLabels = MonarchAiGenerativeUiLabels(), onReject: (@MainActor (MonarchAiUiRejection, MonarchAiUiPart) -> Void)? = nil, onAction: (@MainActor (MonarchAiUiAction) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAiUiRegistry { init(); mutating func register<Props: Decodable & Sendable, Content: View>(_ name: String, props: Props.Type, description: String? = nil, streaming: MonarchAiUiStreaming = .progressive, validate: (@Sendable (Props) -> Bool)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping @MainActor @Sendable (Props, MonarchAiUiEmit) throws -> Content); var names: [String]; func contains(_ name: String) -> Bool; func manifest() -> String }
struct MonarchAiUiEmit { init(_ handler: (@MainActor @Sendable (String, MonarchAiJSON?) -> Void)? = nil); var isConnected: Bool; func callAsFunction(_ type: String, payload: MonarchAiJSON? = nil) }
struct MonarchAiUiAction { init(type: String, payload: MonarchAiJSON? = nil, component: String, partId: String? = nil, toolCallId: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiUiRejection: String, Error { case unknownComponent, invalidProps, renderError }
enum MonarchAiUiStreaming { case progressive, onComplete }
struct MonarchAiGenerativeUiLabels { init(unknown: String? = nil, invalid: String? = nil, failed: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil) }

options.name: part
options.description: The ui part of the message: a component name and its props. While state is streaming, props may be JSON text that is still arriving.

options.name: registry
options.description: The allow-list. Only names registered here render, matched exactly.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the three notices and the spoken name of the progress indicator.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Runs once per refused outcome of a part, for logging. Not called while a streaming part waits for more props.

options.name: onAction
options.description: Receives actions the component sends through its emit channel, with the payload sanitised and the part id and tool call id attached. Without it the channel is not connected.

states.name: rendered
states.description: The registered component, built from its decoded props.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Progressive components render as soon as the partial props decode; others, and props that do not decode yet, show a ProgressView named "Loading".

states.name: unknown component
states.description: A neutral notice: "This part of the answer can’t be shown here."

states.name: invalid props
states.description: A neutral notice: "This part of the answer had data that couldn’t be shown."

states.name: render error
states.description: A neutral notice: "This part of the answer couldn’t be displayed."

appearance: Rendered components draw themselves. The notice is a subtle neutral MonarchInlineNotice with an information icon, using the theme's neutral roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Same allow-list model, notices, streaming policies and action channel as the web. Differences: props decode into a Decodable Swift type instead of a JSON Schema, so the schema check is the type itself plus an optional validate; Swift has no runtime props spreading, so blocked prop names (style, className, on… handlers) have no meaning and are not filtered, while unsafe URLs and the size, depth and number limits are applied as on the web. SwiftUI cannot catch a view that fails while rendering; a builder that throws is the render error instead. The manifest lists names and descriptions without a schema summary, and there is no JSON format. A custom fallback view is not offered; replace the notice text with labels.
accessibility: The rendered component brings its own accessibility.
The notice is static text with a decorative icon; the neutral tone adds no spoken tone name.
The progress indicator while props stream is named "Loading".
Model output is never rendered as markup, so nothing unexpected becomes focusable.
edgeCases: A streaming part is never refused for its props, because they may still become valid; once complete, props given as text instead of data are refused.
Registering a name twice replaces the earlier component; an empty name is ignored.
Strings longer than 20,000 characters are cut, arrays and objects keep 500 members, nesting stops at 8 levels, and numbers that are not finite are dropped.

appearance: The box of MonarchTextField: the surface fill, the input border and the control radius, with the focus ring while editing. Typed text is the default text role and the suggestion the muted text role, both in the body type role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web wraps any textarea or input; on iOS the component is the field, because the suggestion must be drawn inside a UITextView. SwiftUI's TextField cannot report the caret or marked text on iOS 17, draw after the caret, turn off the system's inline predictions or take Tab from the focus system. The web's accept hint (a "Tab" key that is also a button) is here a tap on the suggestion itself plus an "Accept suggestion" button with a full touch target, since a key cap means nothing on touch. The keys are the web's: Tab or the forward arrow accepts, Control or Option with the forward arrow accepts a word, Escape dismisses; they need a hardware keyboard. The cursor is a UTF-16 offset, as on the web. Accepting sets the text through the binding, so it is not a step in the text view's undo history. The web's useAiRewrite and applyAiRewrite (rewriting a selection), exported from the same web folder, are not part of this entry. On the macOS host, which only exists to build and test the package, the field is a SwiftUI TextField with the suggestion laid over it.
accessibility: The field is one element whose label is the label and whose value is the typed text. The suggestion is not part of the value.
While a suggestion shows, the hint says how to accept it; otherwise the hint is the helper text.
A new suggestion is announced. The rest of one being typed through, or taken word by word, is not announced again.
VoiceOver has "Accept suggestion" and "Dismiss suggestion" actions on the field while a suggestion shows.

The accept button has a touch target at least 44 points high. The tap area on the suggestion itself is the suggestion's text with a 4-point margin, which is smaller than 44 points; the button is the full-size alternative.
"Suggestion accepted." and "Suggestion dismissed." are announced.
The suggestion differs from typed text by its position after the caret as well as its colour.
Nothing is suggested while an input method is composing. The system's inline predictions are off in this field; the QuickType bar stays.
The text follows Dynamic Type and the layout direction; in a right-to-left layout the forward arrow is the left arrow.
edgeCases: A suggestion is only shown with the caret at the end of the text (white space may follow), never in the middle or with a selection.
The field grows with the typed text, not with the suggestion: a suggestion that wraps past the last typed line is cut off at the bottom of the field and still inserted whole.
Changing the text from outside, losing focus or disabling the field dismisses the suggestion.
A request whose text has since changed is cancelled and its answer ignored.
With a custom font family in the theme the field uses it; if the family is not registered it falls back to the system font.

The UIKit text view is compiled for iOS and has its own tests, but when this entry was written those tests had only been compiled, not run: the tap on the suggestion, the hardware keys and the alignment of the suggestion with the typed text still need a simulator or a device.
Experimental: the UIKit text view used on iOS has been compiled for iOS but not yet run on a simulator or device. It becomes available after the simulator tests and a VoiceOver check pass.

Lines and border use the AI border role for an agent target and the default border role for a person; the sentence is default text, the reason muted text and the time subtle text. All roles come from the theme, so the four themes differ only in their values.
platformNotes: The web takes reason as any node and a locale prop; here the reason is a String and the locale, calendar and time zone come from the SwiftUI environment. The web drops the side lines below 30rem; iOS drops them at accessibility text sizes. The web marks the root with the note role; SwiftUI has no note trait, so the marker is one static element whose label starts with "Handoff". The arrow is the SF Symbol arrow.forward, which flips right to left.
accessibility: The marker is one element read as "Handoff", the sentence, "Reason:" and the reason, then the time.
Agent names are read with "(AI agent)" after them; a person's name is not, so the direction is clear without the pictures.
The avatars, the arrow and the lines are hidden from VoiceOver.
The sentence is built by a function of both names, so a translation can reorder it.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; nothing is interactive.
edgeCases: An empty reason is treated as no reason.
Long names and reasons wrap inside the border; the side lines keep a least length of 16 points.
Without date no time is shown; now only matters with date.
Future dates read as "in 3 minutes".

platformNotes: The web filters unsafe src values; iOS loads only http, https and file URLs, or an Image the app passes. onSelect becomes a selection binding and onAltChange the images binding. The web shows previews refining with a soft filter; iOS blurs them. Columns are at least 160 points at the default text size and widen with Dynamic Type, so large text gives one column. accessibility: The group is a container named "AI generated images".
The status line is text; the progress bar is hidden because the line carries the percentage.
Completion is announced once, on the change into done.
Each image is read by its alt text with the image trait, or "Generated image n" while the alt text is empty.
Each alt field is a MonarchTextField with its own label ("Alt text for image n") and error text.

"Use image" and "More like this" are named with the image's position; "Use image" has the selected trait on the chosen image, which is also marked by a ring and a "Selected" label, not by colour alone.
Placeholders stop pulsing under Reduce Motion.
edgeCases: Ids must be unique; they identify the grid cells.
Whitespace-only alt text counts as empty.
Progress outside 0...1 is clamped; a non-finite value is ignored.
Images may stay listed in the error state; they keep their slots.

name: MonarchAiInlineDiff
title: AiInlineDiff
wrapsNative: Text(AttributedString) with strikethroughStyle, underlineStyle, backgroundColor and a link per change handled by the openURL environment action, MonarchAiMessageBranch for previous and next, MonarchButton for Accept and Reject, accessibilityActions, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: AI-suggested edits marked inside read-only text, deletions struck through and insertions underlined, with the position, previous and next, and Accept and Reject for the change on show.
whenToUse: When an assistant suggests rewording a paragraph, a description or a message draft and the changes are small enough to read in context, one at a time.
whenNotToUse: For edits that span several labelled fields or sections use MonarchAiEditProposal. For code use MonarchAiCodeBlock with isDiff. For two whole versions side by side use MonarchDiffViewer. Wait until streamed text is complete.
api: init(_ segments: [MonarchAiDiffSegment], showsNavigation: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiInlineDiffLabels = MonarchAiInlineDiffLabels(), onAccept: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onReject: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

static func resolve(_ segments: [MonarchAiDiffSegment], change id: String, decision: MonarchAiInlineDiffDecision) -> [MonarchAiDiffSegment]

enum MonarchAiDiffSegmentKind: String { case equal, insert, delete }
struct MonarchAiInlineDiffChange: Identifiable { let id: String; let segmentIndexes: [Int]; let deleted: String; let inserted: String }
enum MonarchAiInlineDiffDecision: String { case accept, reject }
struct MonarchAiInlineDiffLabels { init(label:, deleted:, inserted:, position:, none:, previous:, next:, acceptTitle:, rejectTitle:, accept:, reject:, announce:) }

options.name: segments
options.description: The text as unchanged, inserted and deleted runs, for example from MonarchAiDiffSegment.words(from:to:). Controlled: update it after a decision.

options.name: showsNavigation
options.description: Shows the position ("Change 2 of 5", or "No suggested changes") with previous and next buttons. Hide it for one short suggestion.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onAccept
options.description: Accepts the change with this id. Shows Accept under the text and as an accessibility action.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Rejects the change with this id. Shows Reject under the text and as an accessibility action.

states.name: active change
states.description: The change on show is bold and has the stronger danger or success background; Accept and Reject act on it.

states.name: other changes
states.description: Struck through on the subtle danger background (deleted) or underlined on the subtle success background (inserted).

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onAccept and onReject there are no decision buttons; previous and next still work.

states.name: no changes
states.description: The position reads "No suggested changes" and the text is plain.

appearance: Body text in the default text colour. Deletions are struck through on the subtle danger background, insertions underlined on the subtle success background, and the change on show is bold on the hover shade of those backgrounds. Accept is a primary button and Reject a secondary one. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web places small Accept and Reject icon buttons right after the active change inside the text; SwiftUI Text cannot hold buttons, so iOS puts full-size Accept and Reject buttons under the text and makes each change a link in the text that selects it. The web wraps from the last change to the first with the buttons; the buttons here (MonarchAiMessageBranch) stop at the ends, and the VoiceOver Next and Previous actions wrap. Arrow-key navigation and roving focus are web keyboard patterns; iOS uses the buttons and the named accessibility actions. Marks inside an editable text view wait for a later wave, as on the web, where no editor adapter ships yet. MonarchAiDiffSegment.words(from:to:) is the same word diff as MonarchAiEditProposal. Marked experimental as an AI product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android has no inline diff yet.
accessibility: The diff is a group named "AI suggested changes", which says the suggestions come from AI.
The text is one element that reads unchanged text as it is and every removal and addition after "Deleted:" or "Inserted:", built by a tested pure function.
The text's value is the position, "Change 2 of 5".
The text has the named actions Next change and Previous change (wrapping) and Accept change 2 of 5 and Reject change 2 of 5, so every decision works without a precise tap.
Accept and Reject are buttons named "Accept change 2 of 5" and "Reject change 2 of 5" with 44-point touch targets.
Every decision is announced: "Change accepted. 3 left." or "Change rejected. No changes left.".
Changes are never marked by colour alone: deletions are struck through, insertions underlined, and the change on show is bold.
edgeCases: Adjacent deleted and inserted runs with different ids are separate changes.
After the app applies a decision, the change in the same position becomes the one on show; after the last one, the previous change is shown.
An unknown id in resolve returns the segments unchanged.
Long text wraps at every text size; there is no horizontal scrolling.
Tapping a change link selects it; other links in the environment keep their system action.

name: MonarchAiInlinePrompt
title: AiInlinePrompt

summary: A prompt about selected text: an "Ask AI" item in the text selection menu (or a context menu) that opens a sheet with an excerpt of the selection, a prompt field and quick prompts.
whenToUse: In documents, emails or notes where AI rewrites what the person selected, opened from the text menu, a long press, or a visible button such as "Edit paragraph with AI".
whenNotToUse: For an open-ended conversation, use MonarchAiPromptInput in an assistant screen. For suggesting the value of one form field, use MonarchAiAutofillField. For completing text as it is typed, use MonarchAiGhostText.
api: public struct MonarchAiInlinePrompt: View { public init(context: String? = nil, suggestions: [String] = [], initialValue: String = "", closesOnSubmit: Bool = true, isPending: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels = MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels(), onSubmit: @escaping @MainActor (String) -> Void) }

public struct MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView: View { public init(_ title: String, text: Binding<String>, isEditable: Bool = true, isEnabled: Bool = true, label: String? = nil, onAskAi: @escaping @MainActor (String) -> Void) }

public struct MonarchAiInlinePromptArea<Content: View>: View { public init(isEnabled: Bool = true, label: String? = nil, onAskAi: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) }

public struct MonarchAiInlinePromptLabels: Sendable, Hashable { public init(label: String? = nil, placeholder: String? = nil, inputLabel: String? = nil, submit: String? = nil, context: String? = nil, suggestions: String? = nil, pending: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil) }

options.name: context
options.description: What the prompt acts on, usually the selected text. Shown as an excerpt of at most 140 characters under the label "Selection".

options.name: suggestions
options.description: Quick prompts such as "Shorten". Tapping one sends it at once.

options.name: initialValue
options.description: The text the field starts with each time the sheet is shown.

options.name: closesOnSubmit
options.description: Dismisses the sheet after sending. Off, the sheet stays and the field is cleared.

options.name: isPending
options.description: A request is being sent: the field, Send and the quick prompts are disabled and "Sending…" is shown and announced.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: label, placeholder, inputLabel, submit, context, suggestions, pending, cancel.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the trimmed prompt or the tapped quick prompt. Never called with blank text or while pending.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView title, text
options.description: The spoken name and the text of a UITextView whose text menu gets "Ask AI" while text is selected.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView isEditable
options.description: Off, the text can be selected but not edited.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView / Area isEnabled
options.description: Off, the menu item and the VoiceOver action are not added.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView / Area label
options.description: The menu item's title; the built-in "Ask AI" without it.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView onAskAi
options.description: Receives the selected text when "Ask AI" is chosen. Present the sheet.

options.name: MonarchAiInlinePromptArea onAskAi, content
options.description: Adds "Ask AI" to the context menu of the content; the app passes the context itself.

states.name: open
states.description: The sheet opens at the medium detent with the drag indicator and can be pulled to large; the keyboard raises it.

states.name: empty
states.description: Send is disabled until the field holds text (MonarchAiPromptInput).

states.name: with context
states.description: An excerpt box with the subtle AI fill and AI border shows "Selection" and the first 140 characters of the context, cut with an ellipsis.

states.name: pending
states.description: The field, Send and the quick prompts are disabled and "Sending…" with a spinner appears under them.

states.name: closed
states.description: After sending (with closesOnSubmit), Cancel, a swipe down or the VoiceOver escape gesture, the sheet is dismissed.

states.name: text menu
states.description: In MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView, "Ask AI" follows the system's items in the edit menu only while text is selected; the caret menu is unchanged.

appearance: The sheet uses the surface fill. The excerpt sits in a box with the subtle AI fill and the AI border role, its label in the strong AI colour and the excerpt in muted text. The prompt box and Send come from MonarchAiPromptInput; quick prompts and Cancel are small ghost MonarchButtons. The text view draws its text in the default text role (disabled role when disabled). Dark and both high-contrast themes swap the same roles.
platformNotes: The web shows a floating popover anchored to the selection rectangle. iOS, like Android, has no floating panel for a selection; the platform pattern is an item in the system text edit menu plus a sheet. SwiftUI on iOS 17 has no public hook for the text edit menu and does not report the selection of TextEditor or of Text with textSelection, so MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView is a UITextView whose delegate adds the item through textView(_:editMenuForTextIn:suggestedActions:) and passes the selected text (Android's TextFieldState overload). For other content MonarchAiInlinePromptArea uses the SwiftUI context menu (a long press), and the app passes the context, as Android's SelectionContainer overload does. The sheet is MonarchAiInlinePrompt, presented by the app with .sheet(isPresented:) or .sheet(item:); Android's onDismissRequest is SwiftUI's dismiss and the sheet's binding, and Android's closeOnSubmit and pending are closesOnSubmit and isPending. iOS opens at the medium detent, which suits a short prompt, where Android opens fully expanded. A Cancel button is added because iOS sheets offer a visible way out. There is no anchor, side, align or returnFocusTo: the system returns focus when the sheet closes. The keyboard hint line of the web is left out; a hardware keyboard sends with Return as in MonarchAiPromptInput. Android's sendIcon is not needed: MonarchAiPromptInput shows its own SF Symbol. The prompt field does not take focus when the sheet opens, because MonarchAiPromptInput keeps its focus state private; the web and Android focus it.
accessibility: The sheet's title "Ask AI" is a header.
The prompt field is named "Prompt" (labels.inputLabel).
The excerpt is one VoiceOver element read as "Selection, " followed by the excerpt.
The quick prompts are a container named "Suggestions"; each is a button with a 44-point touch target.
While pending, "Sending…" is announced once, and the field, Send and the quick prompts are disabled.

In MonarchAiInlinePromptTextView, "Ask AI" is a regular item of the system edit menu, built from the same suggested actions as Cut, Copy and Paste; the text view is named by its title and, while its text is not blank, has an "Ask AI" VoiceOver action that passes the selection or, without one, the whole text.
In MonarchAiInlinePromptArea, the context menu is reached from the VoiceOver actions, and "Ask AI" is also a named accessibility action of the content.
The sheet keeps the system's VoiceOver escape gesture and drag indicator.
edgeCases: A blank prompt or quick prompt is never sent; the prompt is trimmed before onSubmit.
Context longer than 140 characters is cut at a character boundary with trailing spaces removed and an ellipsis added; blank context shows no excerpt.
The edit menu may move "Ask AI" behind its forward arrow when there is no room after the system's items.
The text view adds nothing while only a caret is placed, so the caret menu (Paste, Select) is unchanged; a selection of only spaces adds nothing.
Do not combine MonarchAiInlinePromptArea with .textSelection(.enabled) on the same text: both use the long press.
Long prompts grow the field up to eight lines and then scroll inside it.
On the macOS host build, which exists only for tests, the text view is a TextEditor whose context menu passes the whole text.

appearance: Each row is a Monarch checkbox with the label in the default text role and the description and kind in the muted text role; the chevron uses the subtle text role. Levels are indented by a spacing token. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web builds an ARIA tree with a roving focus and arrow keys; iOS uses standard toggles in a column, so VoiceOver, Switch Control and a hardware keyboard move through them like any controls, and a group's disclosure is a separate button. Level, set size and position are not spoken on iOS. The web's Space and Enter shortcuts are the toggle's own activation. The web announces the summary politely; iOS shows it as text and lets each checkbox speak its new value. The web's controlled expanded and onExpandedChange are not offered; startsExpanded sets the first state. disabled is SwiftUI's .disabled(_:).
accessibility: The tree is a container named "Knowledge sources".
Each source is a checkbox (a standard Toggle through the Monarch checkbox style) named "Handbook, Space", whose value is on, off or mixed; the description is its hint.
A partly selected group is a standard mixed toggle, so its state is spoken, not only drawn as a dash.
Each group has a disclosure button named "Show contents of Handbook" or "Hide contents of Handbook".
Every checkbox and disclosure button has a 44-point touch target; labels and descriptions wrap at every text size.
The chevron uses forward and down symbols, so it points the right way in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: Checking a group selects every descendant; checking the last unchecked child of a group selects the group.
Selecting a group's id alone checks everything under it.
Ids in the selection that are not in the tree are kept, at the end.
A group whose parent is closed stays hidden even if it is in startsExpanded.
An empty tree shows the empty state and no summary.

name: MonarchAiLauncher
title: AiLauncher
wrapsNative: Button with a custom ButtonStyle and keyboardShortcut(_:); placed by the app with safeAreaInset or overlay
summary: The button that opens and closes an AI assistant: a round floating button or a quieter toolbar button, with an unread dot, a working ring or a count, and a hardware keyboard shortcut.
whenToUse: As the one way into the assistant on a screen: the solid variant in a safeAreaInset or overlay at the bottom trailing corner, the subtle variant in a toolbar or rail.
whenNotToUse: Not for sending a prompt or stopping a reply. Not more than one launcher with a shortcut on a screen.
api: init(isOpen: Binding<Bool>, systemImage: String? = nil, variant: MonarchAiLauncherVariant = .solid, badge: MonarchAiLauncherBadge? = nil, showsLabel: Bool? = nil, shortcut: KeyboardShortcut? = KeyboardShortcut("j", modifiers: .command), label: String? = nil, badgeLabel: String? = nil, openLabel: String? = nil)
enum MonarchAiLauncherVariant { case solid, subtle }
enum MonarchAiLauncherBadge { case unread, working, count(Int) }

options.name: isOpen
options.description: Whether the assistant the launcher controls is open. The button toggles it.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: An SF Symbol that replaces the AI glyph.

options.name: variant
options.description: solid is the round, filled, raised floating button; subtle is a tinted button with its label for a toolbar.

options.name: badge
options.description: unread (a dot), working (a ring) or count.

options.name: showsLabel
options.description: Shows the label beside the glyph. nil shows it for the subtle variant only.

options.name: shortcut
options.description: The hardware keyboard shortcut that toggles isOpen. nil for none.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in name "Assistant".

options.name: badgeLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text of the badge.

options.name: openLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Open" spoken while the assistant is open.

states.name: open
states.description: The solid variant shows a close mark instead of the glyph; the subtle variant gets a stronger border.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A darker fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true): a muted fill and the disabled text role, no AI colour.

states.name: unread
states.description: A dot at the top trailing corner.

states.name: working
states.description: A part of the outline travels around the button. Under Reduce Motion the whole outline is drawn and still.

states.name: count
states.description: The number at the top trailing corner, "99+" above 99, nothing for zero or less.

appearance: solid is filled with the solid AI role with the on-solid role for the glyph and a medium shadow; subtle is the subtle AI fill with the AI border and the strong AI role. The dot and the count are the solid danger role ringed in the surface role; the working ring is the AI thinking role. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web positions the launcher itself (bottom-end, bottom-start, inline) and moves it above other floating elements with avoidSelector. On iOS the app places it with safeAreaInset or overlay, which is how the system keeps it clear of bars, the keyboard and other insets, so there are no position or avoid parameters; the two looks are the solid and subtle variants. The shortcut is the standard keyboardShortcut, so it works with a hardware keyboard only, is listed by the system when Command is held on iPad, and is not drawn beside the label. It also works while a text field has focus; the web's shortcutInEditable switch has no equivalent. The web puts the badge text in the accessible name; here it is the accessibility value.
accessibility: A button named "Assistant", or the label parameter.
The value is "Open" while the assistant is open, followed by the badge: "New messages", "Working" or the count of unread messages.
The touch target is at least 48 by 48 points for the solid variant and 44 by 44 for the subtle one.
The badge is also spoken, so it does not depend on colour or on the dot alone.
The working ring is still under Reduce Motion. The glyph and the badge are hidden from VoiceOver as separate elements.
The dot and the count sit at the top trailing corner, which mirrors in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A long label wraps; the solid variant then becomes a pill.
The count has one built-in string for one message and one for more; languages with more plural forms need badgeLabel.
The badge stands 4 points outside the button, so leave that much room at the corner.

name: MonarchAiMarkdown
title: AiMarkdown
wrapsNative: Text with AttributedString (link, inlinePresentationIntent, strikethrough and baselineOffset attributes) for inline content; VStack and HStack(alignment: .firstTextBaseline) for blocks and lists; ScrollView(.horizontal) of a Grid for tables; MonarchCodeBlock for code; the openURL environment action for links
summary: Renders GitHub-flavoured Markdown written by a model (headings, emphasis, links, lists, task lists, quotations, code, tables, rules and footnotes) as SwiftUI text and layout, never as HTML.
whenToUse: For the text of an assistant's answer, a model-written summary or any Markdown that comes from a model and may contain block structure. It reads untrusted input safely and can be re-rendered on every streamed chunk.
whenNotToUse: For Markdown you write yourself in the app, use MonarchProse with MonarchProseStyle.markdown(_:in:), or Text with AttributedString(markdown:) for one line. For code alone use MonarchCodeBlock.
api: init(_ text: String, isStreaming: Bool = false, showsLinkHosts: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiMarkdownLabels = MonarchAiMarkdownLabels(), onOpenLink: (@MainActor (URL) -> Void)? = nil)
func image<Content: View>(@ViewBuilder _ content: @escaping @MainActor (_ url: URL, _ alt: String) -> Content) -> MonarchAiMarkdown
func codeBlock<Content: View>(@ViewBuilder _ content: @escaping @MainActor (_ language: String, _ code: String, _ isComplete: Bool) -> Content) -> MonarchAiMarkdown

struct MonarchAiMarkdownLabels { init(table: String? = nil, tableSize: (@Sendable (_ rows: Int, _ columns: Int) -> String)? = nil, footnotes: String? = nil, task: String? = nil, linkHost: (@Sendable (_ host: String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: text
options.description: The Markdown source, treated as untrusted. While it grows, only the last block is parsed again.

options.name: isStreaming
options.description: The text is still arriving: an unclosed code block is incomplete, so MonarchCodeBlock hides its copy button and codeBlock(_:) receives isComplete false.

options.name: showsLinkHosts
options.description: Shows the host after a link whose text does not name it, such as "paypal.com (evil.example)".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces "Table", the spoken table size, "Footnotes", "Task" and the "(host)" text after links.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens links in the app instead of the environment's openURL action. With it, relative links are links too.

options.name: image(_:)
options.description: Renders a paragraph that is only an image with an http or https source and alt text. Monarch loads no images; without it the alt text is shown.

options.name: codeBlock(_:)
options.description: Renders every code block instead of MonarchCodeBlock, for example a diagram for mermaid or typeset maths for math. Receives the lower-cased language (empty when none), the code and whether it is complete.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every block is rendered; footnotes are numbered by first reference and listed at the end under "Footnotes".

states.name: streaming
states.description: The last block is parsed again on every update; an unclosed code block renders as code without its copy button.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty text renders nothing.

appearance: Running text uses the body type in the default text colour; # headings use the subheading type and deeper ones the strong body type. Quotations are muted text beside a bar in the default border colour. Links take the link colour with an underline, and the host after them is muted. Inline code uses the subtle inline code look. Tables have a subtle border, a muted header fill and subtle row lines; rules use the subtle border. A checked task mark uses the accent fill, an open one the strong border. Every role resolves to its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parser is a port of the web parser through the Android port (same block and inline rules, same incremental re-parse while streaming) and is internal: iOS takes the text and keeps the parse state itself, as Android does, instead of exposing parseMarkdownBlocks and a blocks prop. The image and code block slots are modifiers (image(_:), codeBlock(_:)) instead of optional closures, so the view stays one type. Links open through the openURL environment action, which the app can also replace, or through onOpenLink; there is no new-tab option. Protocol-relative links are never links, and relative links are links only when onOpenLink handles them, because a native app has no base URL. Inline maths shows as inline code; display maths reaches codeBlock(_:) with language math. Footnote references are raised numbers and the footnotes are listed at the end under a header; there are no in-page anchors or back links. Headings follow the iOS body sizes rather than the web's small answer size, and VoiceOver gets heading levels. A table is one element named "Table" with its size, since SwiftUI has no table semantics for a Grid; the web reads a real table. The web's trailing slot (the streaming caret) is not offered. Android uses the same names, with streaming and showLinkHosts as isStreaming and showsLinkHosts.
accessibility: Headings have the header trait and their Markdown level, so the VoiceOver rotor moves between them.
Links are underlined, so they are not told apart by colour alone, and are reachable through the rotor; an unsafe link is plain text.
Numbers of ordered lists are read before each item; bullets are hidden.
A task's check mark is represented to VoiceOver as a dimmed toggle named "Task" with its checked state.
A table is an element named "Table" with the value "3 rows, 2 columns"; its header cells have the header trait.
Rules and the quotation bar are hidden; quoted text is muted but keeps its words.
Paragraphs allow text selection.
Every length that holds text grows with Dynamic Type; table columns cap at a width that grows with the text size and then wrap.
edgeCases: Raw HTML is never interpreted: it stays visible text.
javascript:, data:, other schemes and //host links keep their text without a link, even with control characters hidden inside the scheme.
A link whose text names another site, such as [paypal.com](https://evil.example), shows the real host after it.
A reference to a footnote that is not defined stays as its text, [^label]; a definition that is never referenced is not listed.
A wide table scrolls sideways inside its border instead of widening the answer.
A single $ is never maths, so prices stay text.
Very long text renders every block at once: the column does not scroll and is not lazy; put long answers in a scrolling list.

title: AiMemoryChip
wrapsNative: HStack of Text in a Capsule like MonarchTag, Menu for Edit and Forget, alert(_:isPresented:actions:) with a TextField for editing
summary: One thing the assistant remembers, from a MonarchAiMemoryPart, shown as "Remembered: …" with a menu to edit or forget it.
whenToUse: In a thread when the assistant used, saved or forgot a memory (chip), or as a row in a list of memories (row).
whenNotToUse: For what the assistant can see in this turn only use MonarchAiContextChips. For a plain removable label use MonarchTag.
api: MonarchAiMemoryChip.init(_ memory: MonarchAiMemoryPart, variant: MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant = .chip, showsScope: Bool? = nil, labels: MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels = MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels(), onEdit: (@MainActor (_ id: String, _ text: String) -> Void)? = nil, onForget: (@MainActor (_ id: String) -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiMemoryChipVariant { case chip, row }

MonarchAiMemoryChipLabels.init(prefix: (@Sendable (_ action: MonarchAiMemoryAction) -> String)? = nil, options: (@Sendable (_ text: String) -> String)? = nil, edit: String? = nil, forget: String? = nil, editTitle: String? = nil, editField: String? = nil, save: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil)

options.name: memory
options.description: The memory from the conversation model: its id, action (read, write, forget), text and scope.

options.name: variant
options.description: chip: an inline pill in the AI colours with the AI glyph and a prefix. row: a full-width row without the prefix.

options.name: showsScope
options.description: Whether the scope is shown under the text. By default on the chip and not on the row.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the prefixes, the menu name and the edit dialog strings.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Adds Edit. Receives the id and the trimmed new text; never called with empty or unchanged text.

options.name: onForget
options.description: Adds Forget. Runs straight away, without confirmation.

states.name: read
states.description: Prefix "Used memory:".

states.name: write
states.description: Prefix "Remembered:".

states.name: forget
states.description: Prefix "Forgotten:", muted struck-through text and no commands.

states.name: read only
states.description: No callbacks: no menu.

states.name: editable
states.description: A menu button with Edit and Forget, as given.

states.name: editing
states.description: A dialog with a text field, Save and Cancel. Save is disabled while the text is empty or unchanged.

appearance: The chip uses the AI subtle background, the AI border and the AI strong colour on the glyph, prefix and menu button, with default text. The row has no fill or border and a muted prefix. A forgotten memory's text is muted. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: Built on the shared MonarchAiMemoryPart, so the web's separate entity becomes the part's scope and the prefix follows the part's action (the web always says "Remembered:"). Editing happens in a system alert with a text field instead of inline, so there are no Enter and Escape hints; the web's Edit and Forget buttons are a Menu, as the iOS plan asks. The web's leading and meta slots for the row are not offered. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The prefix, the text and the scope are one element.
That element carries Edit and Forget as accessibility actions when they are offered.
The menu button is a separate element named "Options for memory:" and a shortened copy of the text, so each name is unique in a list, with a 44-point touch target.
The AI glyph is decorative; the prefix says that the assistant kept the memory.
A forgotten memory is struck through and also says "Forgotten:", so the state does not depend on the line.
edgeCases: Long text wraps; the spoken menu name uses at most 48 characters of it, with an ellipsis.
An empty or white-space scope is never shown.
A forgotten memory offers no commands even when callbacks are given.

options.name: memories
options.description: Everything remembered: id, text, the entity it is about and when it was last updated. The app's state: change it in the callbacks. MonarchAiMemoryItem.apply keeps it in step with a conversation's memory events.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces every built-in string, the row strings (chip) and the bulk bar strings.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Saves an edited memory with the trimmed new text, from the row's Edit dialog.

options.name: onForget
options.description: Forgets one memory straight away, from the row's menu or a swipe.

options.name: onForgetMany
options.description: Forgets the selected memories after the person confirms. With one selected, onForget is called instead.

options.name: environment locale and timeZone
options.description: The search's case folding, the order of names and the updated dates follow the environment's locale and time zone.

options.name: startsSelecting
options.description: Opens in selection mode with select-all and forget showing.

states.name: listing
states.description: One section per entity: people, then organizations, projects and other, each by name; newest memory first, each with "Updated" and its date.

states.name: searching
states.description: Only memories whose text or entity name contains the search are shown; the count is announced 300 ms after typing stops.

states.name: selecting
states.description: Select in the toolbar puts the list in edit mode with selection circles, a Select all (n) or Deselect all button, and MonarchBulkActionBar with the count and Forget once something is selected. Row menus are hidden meanwhile.

states.name: confirming
states.description: A confirmation dialog asks "Forget 2 memories?" with Forget (destructive) and Cancel.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Nothing is remembered yet." as a first-run empty state, and no Select button.

states.name: no matches
states.description: "No memories match “…”." as a filtered empty state with a way to clear the search.

appearance: A standard inset grouped list: group names in the default text colour with the strong body type, kinds, counts and dates muted, rows from MonarchAiMemoryChip's row variant. Swipe and confirmation use the system destructive red. The list follows the system's dark and high-contrast appearance; Monarch roles resolve in each theme.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it; plain public API with status experimental, like the other experimental iOS entries, because the compiled examples import MonarchUI without SPI. On a phone the web's toolbar (search, select-all checkbox and a Forget selected button) becomes the system pattern: searchable in the navigation bar, a Select button that turns on the list's edit mode, Select all in the toolbar and MonarchBulkActionBar at the bottom, as Mail and Files do; so the panel needs a NavigationStack around it. There are no group checkboxes (the web's and Android's select-a-group): iOS edit mode selects rows, and Select all covers what the search shows. Each row reuses MonarchAiMemoryChip's row variant, so Edit and Forget are in its menu and VoiceOver actions; a trailing swipe also forgets. The web's AiMemoryItem entity kind org is organization here, and updatedAt is a Date. Locale and time zone come from the environment instead of parameters (Android takes locale and timeZone). The web's onForgetMany may return a promise that keeps the dialog pending; here the dialog closes on confirm and the app updates memories. The web moves focus to the next row after a forget; iOS leaves focus to the system. Android uses the same type names.
accessibility: The list is named "Memories"; each group name has the header trait and is followed by its kind and count.
Each row is the MonarchAiMemoryChip row: the memory is one element with Edit and Forget as actions, and the menu button is named after the memory.
Selection uses the system edit mode, so VoiceOver reads each row's selected state and the toolbar buttons by name.
The number of matches is announced after the search settles; "Memory updated", "Memory forgotten" or "2 memories forgotten" are announced after a change.
Forgetting several memories always asks for confirmation first.
edgeCases: A selected memory that the search hides is not forgotten; only shown selected memories count.
Selecting one memory and confirming calls onForget, not onForgetMany.
Long memories wrap; the menu's spoken name uses a shortened copy.
With no memories the Select button is hidden.

name: MonarchAiMentionContext
title: AiMentionContext
wrapsNative: VStack of plain Buttons in an optional ScrollView, shown above the keyboard in a safeAreaInset; MonarchMentionQuery, MonarchAvatar, MonarchInlineErrorRetry, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: The @ context menu of an AI prompt: documents, people, records and apps that can be added to what the AI sees, grouped by kind, with loading, empty and error states.
whenToUse: In an AI composer, when typing @ should add a document, a person, a record or an app to the context the AI sees, shown afterwards with MonarchAiContextChips.
whenNotToUse: For mentioning people or channels in a message to people, use MonarchMentionPicker. For browsing sources without typing, use MonarchAiKnowledgeScope or MonarchAiConnectorPicker.
api: init(_ query: MonarchMentionQuery?, items: [MonarchAiMentionItem], status: MonarchMentionPickerStatus = .ready, labels: MonarchAiMentionContextLabels = MonarchAiMentionContextLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchAiMentionItem) -> Void)

struct MonarchAiMentionItem: Identifiable { var id: String; var kind: MonarchAiMentionKind; var label: String; var description: String?; var tokens: Int?; var avatarURL: URL?; var isDisabled: Bool; var contextItem: MonarchAiContextItem }
enum MonarchAiMentionKind: String { case doc, person, record, app; var contextKind: MonarchAiContextKind }

struct MonarchAiMentionContextLabels { var label: String?; var group: (@Sendable (MonarchAiMentionKind) -> String)?; var loading: String?; var empty: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var error, retry: String?; var tokens: (@Sendable (String, Int) -> String)?; var count: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? }

options.name: query
options.description: The @ query found with MonarchMentionQuery.find(in:caret:triggers:). Nothing is drawn while it is nil.

options.name: items
options.description: The results of the product's search, without ids already in the context.

options.name: status
options.description: loading shows placeholder rows, failed an error, ready the results or the empty text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats a failed search; adds a retry button to the error.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Receives the chosen result. Add item.contextItem to the context and remove the query from the prompt.

states.name: results
states.description: Rows with an icon or avatar, the label, the description and the token estimate; headings when more than one kind is present.

states.name: searching
states.description: Three redacted placeholder rows; "Searching…" is announced.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Type to search" for an empty query, else "Nothing matches “q3”".

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn’t load results.", with a retry button when onRetry is given.

states.name: disabled result
states.description: Dimmed text; the row cannot be chosen.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is drawn while query is nil, or after a query with a space found nothing.

appearance: A full-width strip on the surface colour with a subtle border line above it, like MonarchMentionPicker. Labels are default text, descriptions and token estimates muted, disabled rows the disabled text role. Documents, records and apps show their context-chip symbol on a square tile; people show a round avatar.
platformNotes: The web is a listbox under the caret driven by aria-activedescendant and a hook that wires it into the prompt input. iOS gives no caret position, so this is a strip above the keyboard (the same layout as MonarchMentionPicker) and results are buttons; the product finds the query with MonarchMentionQuery and runs its search in .task(id:). There is no highlighted result or arrow-key navigation. The status reuses MonarchMentionPickerStatus. The parity map called it a mention picker preset; MonarchMentionPicker's items are people and channels only, so this component has its own item type and reuses the picker's query, open rule and layout.
accessibility: Each result is a button read as its label, description and token estimate; a disabled result is dimmed and cannot be activated.
The list is a container named "Add context", with headings marked as headers when more than one kind is present.
"Searching…", the number of results, the empty text and the error are announced as they change, so focus stays in the prompt.
Rows are at least 44 points high and grow with Dynamic Type; icons and avatars are decorative.
edgeCases: More than four results scroll in a height of four and a half rows.
One kind of result shows no heading.
Token counts use the context chips' compact form, for example 12.4K tokens; 1 reads "1 token".
A query with a space that found nothing closes the menu, because the person has moved on.

    items: [],
    status: .failed,
    onRetry: {},
    onSelect: { _ in }
)

name: MonarchAiMessageActions
title: AiMessageActions
wrapsNative: HStack of Button with .buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost, size: .sm)), Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton(.ghost, size: .sm)) for the thumbs, ShareLink(item:) for Share, MonarchCopyButton for Copy, Menu for More, inside ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal)
summary: The row of actions under a chat message: copy, regenerate, edit, thumbs up and down, share, read aloud and a More menu; each action appears only when it is turned on.
whenToUse: Under each assistant message in a conversation, and under the person's own messages with Copy and Edit.
whenNotToUse: For rating with reasons and a comment use MonarchAiFeedback. For actions on any chat message (reply, react, delete) use the actions slot of MonarchMessageRow or a .contextMenu.
api: init(_ messageText: String, feedback: Binding<MonarchAiMessageFeedback?>? = nil, isReadingAloud: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isCopyable: Bool = true, isShareable: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels = MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onRegenerate: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onEdit: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder more: () -> More)

init(_ messageText: String, feedback: Binding<MonarchAiMessageFeedback?>? = nil, isReadingAloud: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isCopyable: Bool = true, isShareable: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels = MonarchAiMessageActionsLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onRegenerate: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onEdit: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) where More == EmptyView

options.name: messageText
options.description: The message's plain text: what Copy copies and Share shares.

options.name: feedback
options.description: The rating. Shows the thumbs when set; pressing the pressed thumb sets it to nil.

options.name: isReadingAloud
options.description: Whether the app is reading the message aloud. Shows Read aloud when set; the button only flips the value, the app speaks.

options.name: isCopyable
options.description: Shows Copy (MonarchCopyButton).

options.name: isShareable
options.description: Shows Share, the system share sheet with the message text.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the row name and every button title.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied text after each copy, for analytics. Copy writes to the pasteboard itself.

options.name: onRegenerate
options.description: Shows Regenerate and runs when it is pressed.

options.name: onEdit
options.description: Shows Edit and runs when it is pressed.

options.name: more
options.description: Extra menu items at the end of the More menu. Without them, More appears only when actions do not fit.

states.name: rated
states.description: The pressed thumb is filled and selected; the other is an outline.

states.name: copied
states.description: Copy shows a checkmark and is named "Copied" for two seconds (MonarchCopyButton).

states.name: reading aloud
states.description: Read aloud shows a stop symbol and is named "Stop reading".

states.name: narrow
states.description: When the full row does not fit, Copy and the thumbs stay and Regenerate, Edit, Share and Read aloud move into the More menu.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every button takes the disabled colours with .disabled(true).

appearance: Ghost icon buttons in the small size: the icons use the default text colour, the pressed thumb uses the selected toggle colours and a filled symbol. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web row appears on hover by default; phones have no hover, so the iOS row is always visible. The web speaks the text with the browser's speech synthesis; on iOS the app owns speech (AVSpeechSynthesizer) and the row only flips isReadingAloud, because Monarch adds no audio session handling. The web's onShare callback becomes the system ShareLink with the message text. The web moves between buttons with the arrow keys as one tab stop; on iOS each button is its own VoiceOver element in a container named "Message actions". When the row does not fit the width the iOS row moves the less common actions into a More menu, which the web does not do. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The row is a container named "Message actions".
Every action is a standard button named by its title; icons are not read separately.
The thumbs are toggles named "Good response" and "Bad response" with the selected state; a pressed thumb is filled, so the state is a shape as well as a colour.
Read aloud is named "Stop reading" while reading.
Copy announces "Copied to clipboard" and plays the success haptic; a rating plays the selection haptic.
Every button is at least 44 by 44 points.
edgeCases: With no callbacks and isCopyable false the row is empty.
An empty message text still copies and shares an empty string; hide the row while the answer streams.
At the accessibility text sizes the buttons grow and the less common actions move into More.
The app must set isReadingAloud back to false when speech ends or is interrupted.

summary: The previous, position, next switcher between alternative versions of a message, made when a reply is regenerated or a prompt is edited and resent.
whenToUse: Under a message that has more than one version, bound to the version that is shown.
whenNotToUse: Not for paging through a list: use the system page controls. Not for a number a person sets: use the standard Stepper.
api: init(selection: Binding<Int>, count: Int, showsSingle: Bool = false, label: String? = nil, previousLabel: String? = nil, nextLabel: String? = nil, formatPosition: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, formatAnnouncement: ((Int, Int) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: selection
options.description: The version shown, counted from 0.

options.name: count
options.description: How many versions exist.

options.name: showsSingle
options.description: Shows the switcher when there is only one version.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Versions".

options.name: previousLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Previous version".

options.name: nextLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Next version".

options.name: formatPosition
options.description: Replaces the built-in visible position "2 / 3". Receives the version, counted from 1, and the count.

options.name: formatAnnouncement
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken position "Version 2 of 3".

states.name: first version
states.description: The previous button is disabled.

states.name: last version
states.description: The next button is disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true) both buttons are disabled and the position uses the disabled text role.

states.name: hidden
states.description: With fewer than two versions nothing is shown, unless showsSingle is true.

appearance: Two ghost buttons with chevrons and a muted caption between them, in tabular digits so the buttons do not move. Colours are the ghost button roles and the muted text role of the theme.
platformNotes: The web is controlled with index and onChange; here it is a Binding, the SwiftUI convention. The web's disabled prop is the standard disabled(_:) modifier. The web moves keyboard focus to the other button when one becomes disabled at an end; this is not done here, because VoiceOver keeps its focus on a button that becomes dimmed.
accessibility: A group named "Versions" that contains the two buttons and the position.
The buttons are named "Previous version" and "Next version"; each has a 44-point touch target.
The position is read as "Version 2 of 3", not as "2 / 3".
After a button changes the version, the new position is announced. A change made elsewhere is not announced.
The chevrons are the backward and forward symbols, so they mirror in right-to-left layouts.
edgeCases: A selection outside the range is shown as the nearest version; a step then starts from the version shown.
A count below 1 is treated as 1.
Large counts widen the position; the buttons keep their size.
