states.description: The bubble is replaced by MonarchAiUserMessageEdit with Save and Cancel; the actions row is hidden.

states.name: queued
states.description: Under the person's message a clock and "Queued. It will send when you are back online." with Cancel; no actions.

states.name: cut short
states.description: A finished reply whose finish reason is length, content filter or refusal ends with a warning symbol and a notice.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchAiErrorMessage with the tone and actions of its kind, Retry when the error can be retried and Resume when the run can be resumed.

states.name: branches
states.description: With two or more alternatives MonarchAiMessageBranch shows the position and previous and next buttons.

appearance: The person's bubble uses the muted background role with an extra-large radius and a small bottom trailing corner; the name uses the default text colour in the strong body style, the role and time the muted text colour in the caption style; the finish notice symbol uses the strong warning colour. Each part keeps its component's colours, all theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web AiMessageView renders the same parts in the same order. On iOS callbacks capture the message, so they do not receive it again; the web's editing, onEdit and onEditCancel become the isEditing binding, and onEditSubmit receives the text. The web's renderPart, which can replace any part, becomes part, which draws only generative UI and edit proposals: on iOS the app supplies the registry or diff view through it (AiGenerativeUi's registry and AiEditProposal's hunks have no iOS equivalent in this component). The web shows its actions on hover by default; phones have no hover, so the row is always shown (actionsVisibility is not offered). Citations cannot sit inside SwiftUI text, so consecutive citation markers form a row after the text they follow. The web caps the person's bubble at 85% of the width; iOS keeps a 48-point leading inset instead, which reads the same on a phone and needs no width measurement. The time uses the environment's locale and time zone instead of a locale prop. Experimental: a product composite (the message row of an AI chat) that waits for a Rook app to adopt it. Android ships the same component, also experimental, with the same name and callbacks (onRegenerate, onBranch, onRetry, onResume, onCancelQueued, onApproveTool, onDenyTool, onAlwaysAllowTool, onEditSubmit, onEditMemory, onForgetMemory, onOpenArtifact, onOpenSource, onOpenLink). Differences in Swift idiom: Android's editing, onEdit and onEditCancel are the isEditing binding; Android's onFeedback and speaking/onReadAloud are the feedback and isReadingAloud bindings; Android's onShare callback is isShareable with the system ShareLink; Android's showTimestamp, showActions and copyable are showsTimestamp, showsActions and isCopyable; Android's timeZone and is24Hour come from the SwiftUI environment; Android's onOpenFile is not offered (a file chip with a web address opens it); Android's uiRegistry, onUiAction and editHunks are the part slot; onOpenSource receives a MonarchAiSourceListItem instead of the source part.
accessibility: The message is a container named by who said it: "You said", "Assistant said" or "System message".
The assistant header is one element with the header trait, read as the name, the agent's role and the time; the avatar is decorative.
Streaming text announces new sentences and the last text part announces the end of the reply, through MonarchAiStreamingText; announces turns both off.
A tool call's state changes and an error are announced by MonarchAiToolCall and MonarchAiErrorMessage.
Each citation is a button read as "Source 1: Ledger, March"; the source list has numbered, named sources.
The finish notice is text with a decorative warning symbol, so it does not rely on colour.
The actions, branch buttons, Resume and Cancel are standard buttons of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A message with no visible parts shows only its header or footer.
Empty finished text parts are left out; an empty streaming text part shows the caret.
Citations that point at a source the message does not have are left out.
Sources are listed once, where the first source part stands, however many source parts follow.
Artifacts are left out without onOpenArtifact, and generative UI and edit proposals without part.
At the largest text sizes the header and footer wrap onto more lines.
An invalid createdAt hides the time.

name: MonarchAiModeSwitcher
title: AiModeSwitcher
wrapsNative: Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) and controlSize(_:), a description Text, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Switches how the assistant works (Ask, Edit, Agent by default) with a segmented control and shows what the selected mode may change.
whenToUse: When an assistant has 2 to 5 modes with different permissions or behaviour, for example in a prompt toolbar to set the mode of the next messages.
whenNotToUse: To choose a model or a writing style use the model or tone picker (see ai-tone-picker). For more than five modes or long names use a Picker with the menu style.
api: MonarchAiModeSwitcher.init(selection: Binding<String>, modes: [MonarchAiMode] = MonarchAiMode.defaults, size: MonarchAiModeSwitcherSize = .sm, showsDescription: Bool = true, label: String? = nil)
MonarchAiMode.init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, isIconOnly: Bool = false, isDisabled: Bool = false)
static var MonarchAiMode.defaults: [MonarchAiMode]
enum MonarchAiModeSwitcherSize { case sm, md }

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected mode. A disabled or unknown id is never written.

options.name: modes
options.description: The modes, 2 to 5: each with an id, a label, an optional description, an optional symbol for an icon-only segment, and a disabled flag.

options.name: size
options.description: sm: the small control size, for a prompt toolbar. md: the regular control size.

options.name: showsDescription
options.description: Whether the selected mode's description is shown under the control. Turn it off when it is shown elsewhere.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the choice, "Mode".

states.name: selected
states.description: The system segmented control marks the selected segment; its description is shown underneath.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With the standard disabled(_:) modifier the control is dimmed and the description uses the disabled text role.

states.name: mode disabled
states.description: The segment is dimmed where the system supports it, and selecting it does not change the selection.

states.name: no description
states.description: When no mode has a description, or showsDescription is false, there is no description line.

appearance: The system segmented control, tinted by the app's accent. The description is caption text in the muted text role. No status colours: a mode is a setting, not a status. High contrast follows the system control.
platformNotes: The web builds on Monarch's SegmentedControl; iOS uses the system segmented Picker. UISegmentedControl shows a symbol or text in a segment, not both, so a symbol appears only on icon-only modes. iOS ships built-in Ask, Edit and Agent modes with descriptions; the web has no defaults. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The control is the system segmented Picker named by label ("Mode"); VoiceOver reads each segment and the selected one.
The selected mode's description is the control's hint; the visible line is not read twice.
When the selection changes and a description is shown, the new description is announced.
An icon-only segment is read as the mode's label.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no mode leaves no segment selected and shows an empty description line.
A mode with an empty description shows an empty line, so the layout does not jump.
Long descriptions wrap; long labels are truncated by the system control, so keep them to one word.

name: MonarchAiModelPicker
title: AiModelPicker
wrapsNative: Button with MonarchButtonStyle that presents a .sheet with a NavigationStack and a List of Sections, MonarchBadge, MonarchFlowLayout
summary: A button showing the current AI model that opens a list of models grouped by provider, with capabilities, context size, speed, cost and provider key state.
whenToUse: When people may choose which model answers, for example in a prompt toolbar or a conversation's settings.
whenNotToUse: For a short list of plain choices without details use a Picker with the menu style. For the assistant's mode (chat, research, agent) use MonarchAiModeSwitcher.
api: init(selection: Binding<String?>, models: [MonarchAiModelOption], size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, startsOpen: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiModelPickerLabels = MonarchAiModelPickerLabels(), onConfigureKey: (@MainActor (MonarchAiModelOption) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAiModelOption: Identifiable { var id, provider, name: String; var description: String?; var capabilities: [MonarchAiModelCapability]; var contextTokens: Int?; var speed: MonarchAiModelSpeed?; var costTier: Int?; var requiresKey, isKeyConfigured, isDisabled: Bool }
enum MonarchAiModelCapability: String { case vision, tools, reasoning, web }
enum MonarchAiModelSpeed: String { case fast, balanced, slow }

struct MonarchAiModelPickerLabels { var label, placeholder: String?; var capability: (@Sendable (MonarchAiModelCapability) -> String)?; var context: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var speed: (@Sendable (MonarchAiModelSpeed) -> String)?; var cost: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)?; var ownKey, keyNeeded, addKeyHint, unavailable, done: String? }

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected model, nil for none. Set when a model is chosen.

options.name: models
options.description: The models in display order, grouped by provider in first-seen order.

options.name: size
options.description: The height and padding of the button.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onConfigureKey
options.description: Runs when a model whose key is missing is chosen, to add the key. Without it such models cannot be chosen.

options.name: startsOpen
options.description: Presents the model list when the view appears.

states.name: placeholder
states.description: No model selected: the button reads "Choose a model" in muted text.

states.name: selected
states.description: The button shows the model and its provider; the row has a check mark and the selected trait.

states.name: your key
states.description: A model on a configured workspace key shows a success "Your key" badge with a key.

states.name: key needed
states.description: A model whose key is missing shows a warning "Key needed" badge with a lock; choosing it calls onConfigureKey.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A disabled model, or one whose key cannot be added, is dimmed and cannot be chosen.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The button uses the disabled colours and does not open.

appearance: The button is the secondary Monarch button with the name in default text and the provider in muted text. In the list, names are default text, details muted, capabilities info badges, key badges success or warning; unavailable rows use the disabled text role. The selected check uses the strong accent role.
platformNotes: The web opens a popover listbox with arrow-key navigation and typeahead; iOS opens a List in a sheet, because a Menu cannot show badges and several lines per model. The web's controlled open state is not offered; the button owns the sheet. The selection is a Binding<String?> instead of value and onChange. A cost tier outside 1 to 3 is clamped.
accessibility: The button is named "Model" and its value is the selected model and provider, or "Choose a model".
Each model is one button named by the model and its key badge; its value lists the description, capabilities, context, speed and the cost in words ("Cost: high"), never the dollar signs.
The selected model has the selected trait and a check mark, so selection is not colour alone.
A model whose key is missing has the hint "Select to add an API key."; one that cannot be chosen is disabled and reads "Unavailable".
Rows are at least 44 points high; badges wrap and text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A selection id that matches no model shows the placeholder.
Without onConfigureKey a model needing a key is shown but disabled.
Context sizes are formatted in the environment locale with at most one decimal: 32 768 tokens is "32.8K".
Empty models give an empty list.

name: MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster
title: AiMultiAgentRoster
wrapsNative: VStack of rows with MonarchAiAgentAvatar, MonarchAvatarGroup for the stack, ViewThatFits, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Every agent taking part in a task and what each is doing now, as a list of rows or a compact stack of pictures.
whenToUse: When several agents work on one request and the person should see who is involved, what each is doing and which one needs them. Use the stack in headers and toolbars and the list in a side panel.
whenNotToUse: Not for one agent working through steps: use MonarchAiChainOfSteps or MonarchAiTaskProgress. Not for people in a workspace: use MonarchPresenceAvatars or MonarchAvatarGroup.
api: init(_ members: [MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterMember], variant: MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterVariant = .list, maxVisible: Int = 4, showsSummary: Bool = true, announcesChanges: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterLabels = MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterLabels())

struct MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterMember: Identifiable { var agent: MonarchAiAgentRef; var state: MonarchAiAgentState; var task: String?; var id: String; init(_ agent: MonarchAiAgentRef, state: MonarchAiAgentState = .idle, task: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterVariant { case list, stack }

struct MonarchAiMultiAgentRosterLabels { var label: String?; var agentKind: String?; var state: (@Sendable (MonarchAiAgentState) -> String)?; var summary: (@Sendable (Int, [MonarchAiAgentState: Int]) -> String)?; var changed: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)?; var empty: String? }

options.name: members
options.description: The agents, each with a state and an optional task. Keep agent ids stable between updates.

options.name: variant
options.description: list: a row per agent. stack: overlapping pictures beside the summary.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: In the stack, the pictures shown before "+N". At least one is shown.

options.name: showsSummary
options.description: Shows the "3 agents · 2 working" line.

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Announces state changes to VoiceOver. Never the first state.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list name, "AI agent", the state names, the summary, the change announcement and the empty text.

states.name: idle
states.description: No ring; the state text is muted.

states.name: working
states.description: A turning ring (still with Reduce Motion); the state text uses the strong AI colour.

states.name: waiting
states.description: The row is tinted warning, the state text is strong warning, the avatar has a dashed warning ring. First in the stack after errors.

states.name: error
states.description: The row is tinted danger and the state text is strong danger. First in the stack.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No agents are working on this." in muted text, without a summary.

appearance: Rows on the surface, with the warning subtle fill for waiting and the danger subtle fill for errors. Names are default text, roles muted, tasks default; the state is caption text in the AI, warning, danger or muted strong role. The stack uses the avatar group's ring on the surface colour. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web's task is any node; here it is a String. The web uses a polite live region; iOS posts an accessibility announcement when a state changes. The stack reuses MonarchAvatarGroup, so a "+1" tile is never shown: with one agent too many all are shown, as everywhere else in Monarch. When the stack and the summary do not fit on one line the summary moves under the pictures. The parity map listed presence-avatars and status-badge; the stack is the avatar group that presence-avatars also builds on, and the state is plain coloured text as on the web, so neither is used directly.
accessibility: A list row is one element read as the name with "(AI agent)", the role, the task and the state; the picture is hidden because the text says the same.
In the stack each picture is an image named by the agent, "AI agent" and its state unless idle; "+N" reads every hidden agent with its state.
Every state is written text as well as a ring and a tint, so it never depends on colour or motion.
A state change is announced, for example "Research agent: Error"; several changes are joined. The first state is not announced, and announcesChanges false turns announcements off.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; names, roles and tasks wrap, and the state stays on one line at the trailing edge.
edgeCases: Agents are matched by agent.id, else by name; changing ids makes every update read as new.
An agent that joins is announced with its state.
maxVisible below 1 shows one picture.
Empty roles and tasks are not shown or read.

summary: A short, step-by-step introduction to AI in a product (what it can see, what it can do, how to turn it off) with Back, Next and Turn off AI on every step.
whenToUse: The first time people meet AI features in a product, in a sheet or at the top of a screen, to explain what the assistant sees and does and how to switch it off.
whenNotToUse: To point at one control use TipKit's popoverTip(_:arrowEdge:). For a general setup checklist use MonarchOnboardingChecklist.

appearance: The AI strong colour on the glyph and the "AI" eyebrow, headings in default text and bodies in muted text, the stepper's colours, a primary Next button, a secondary Back button and a ghost Turn off AI button. No surface of its own: the sheet or a MonarchCard provides it. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web's target option, which outlines an element on the page, has no equivalent: use TipKit's popoverTip to point at a control. The web's floating placement becomes a sheet presented by the app. Steps are swiped as pages as well as moved with Back and Next. On the macOS host build, which is not a supported product, the current step is shown without paging. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: Each step's heading has the header trait, and VoiceOver focus moves to it when the step changes.
The stepper reads the position and the name of the step.
The close button is named "Skip introduction".
Turn off AI is on every step, so the opt-out is always reachable.
Every button has a 44-point touch target; the buttons stack when they do not fit on one line.
edgeCases: The tour takes the height of its tallest step, so pages do not jump in height and long text at large sizes is not clipped.
A step outside the range is clamped to the first or the last step.
Step ids default to the title; the stepper gets unique ids even when titles repeat.

name: MonarchAiPermissionScope
title: AiPermissionScope
wrapsNative: VStack of rows with MonarchFavicon; Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) per row when editable; ViewThatFits to stack a row when narrow
summary: What an AI agent may see and change, app by app: each row names the app and the resources it covers and shows No access, Can read or Can read and edit, or a None / Read / Write control when editable.
whenToUse: In agent settings or before an agent runs, to show or change what it may read or edit in each connected app.
whenNotToUse: For one yes-or-no permission use a Toggle (see switch). For system permissions (camera, location) use the system prompt. For per-action approval use the tool-call approval in the conversation.

options.name: scopes
options.description: One row per app, each with a unique app name, optional resources, the access level and an optional icon URL. An array gives a read-only list; a binding gives a segmented control per row that writes the access.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the list name, the level descriptions, the short option names, the control name, the manage title and the empty text.

options.name: onManage
options.description: Adds a "Manage permissions" button in the Monarch link style.

states.name: read only
states.description: Each row shows the level with a symbol: lock for No access (muted text), eye for Can read, pencil for Can read and edit.

states.name: editable
states.description: Each row has a None / Read / Write segmented control.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When the row does not fit on one line, the access or the control moves under the app name.

states.name: empty
states.description: "The AI has no access to any app." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With the standard disabled(_:) modifier the controls are dimmed by the system.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers; app names in the default text role and resources in muted text; a favicon or letter tile per app; the system segmented control when editable. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web's manageHref link becomes an onManage closure, since a native app opens its own settings screen. The web's onChange(scopes, changed) becomes a binding. iOS adds an optional app icon through MonarchFavicon. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The list is a container named "What the AI can access".
A read-only row is one element read as the app and its resources, with the access ("Can read") as its value.
Each level has its own symbol as well as its text, so it never depends on colour.
An editable row's control is the system segmented Picker named "Access to <app>".
The favicon is decorative and hidden.
Rows wrap and stack at large text sizes.
edgeCases: App names must be unique: they are the rows' identity.
An empty resources string is not shown or read.
Long app names and resources wrap; the control moves under them.

name: MonarchAiPlan
title: AiPlan
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with a VStack of rows (MonarchDragHandle with draggable(_:) and dropDestination(for:action:isTargeted:), MonarchInlineEditText, an icon Button) and MonarchButton for Add, Reject and Approve; MonarchAiChainOfSteps once decided
summary: The plan an agent proposes before it acts, which a person edits, reorders, approves or rejects, and which then shows the steps as the agent works through them.
whenToUse: When an agent should not act until a person agrees: show the plan part (MonarchAiPlanPart) from the message model and run the approved steps.
whenNotToUse: Not to show steps the agent is already running with no approval (use MonarchAiChainOfSteps) and not for a single risky tool call (use MonarchAiToolResultCard or a confirmation dialog).
api: init(_ part: MonarchAiPlanPart, decision: MonarchAiPlanDecision? = nil, isEditable: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiPlanLabels = MonarchAiPlanLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor ([MonarchAiPlanStep]) -> Void)? = nil, onReject: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onApprove: (@MainActor ([MonarchAiPlanStep]) -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiPlanDecision { case pending, approved, rejected }

struct MonarchAiPlanLabels { init(title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, editHint: String? = nil, approvedNotice: String? = nil, rejectedNotice: String? = nil, stepLabel: ((Int) -> String)? = nil, stepPlaceholder: String? = nil, untitledStep: ((Int) -> String)? = nil, reorder: ((String) -> String)? = nil, moved: ((String, Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, remove: ((String) -> String)? = nil, removed: ((String) -> String)? = nil, addStep: String? = nil, approve: String? = nil, reject: String? = nil, emptyPlan: String? = nil) }

options.name: part
options.description: The plan part the agent proposed. Its steps seed the draft; a new part from the model (not an echo of the draft) replaces it.

options.name: decision
options.description: The decision, when the app owns it. When nil the view keeps its own after Approve or Reject.

options.name: isEditable
options.description: Whether the person can change the steps before deciding. Once decided the plan is always read-only.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the title.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Called with the draft after every edit, move, addition and removal.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Called when the person rejects the plan.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Called with the approved steps, labels trimmed and empty steps left out.

states.name: pending, editable
states.description: Each step is a numbered row with a drag handle, the step text as an inline editor and a remove button; Add step, Reject and Approve plan follow.

states.name: pending, read-only
states.description: isEditable false: the steps as a MonarchAiChainOfSteps with Reject and Approve plan.

states.name: empty
states.description: Every step empty: Approve plan is disabled and a note says to add a step.

states.name: approved
states.description: The description reads the approved notice; the cleaned steps show as a MonarchAiChainOfSteps whose states follow the part and are announced.

states.name: rejected
states.description: The description reads the rejected notice; the steps show read-only with no buttons.

states.name: drop target
states.description: While a dragged step is over a row, the row takes the AI subtle background.

appearance: A Monarch card: the title in the subheading style and default text role, the description and step numbers in the muted text role, a drop target in the AI subtle role. Buttons are Monarch ghost, secondary and primary buttons. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Planned as a List with onMove; built as a VStack instead, because the plan sits inside a scrolling conversation where a List cannot size itself, and onMove only works inside a List. Steps move by dragging the handle onto another step, or with the handle's Move up and Move down actions; the web also shows visible move buttons and keyboard reordering. The web's text inputs are always open with Enter adding a step and Backspace removing an empty one; iOS uses MonarchInlineEditText, which opens on tap and saves on Return or when focus leaves. The web's title prop is labels.title. The web announces through a live region; iOS posts accessibility announcements.
accessibility: The plan is a container named by its title; the title has the header trait.
Each step's text is a button named "Step 2" whose value is the step text, with the Edit hint of MonarchInlineEditText.
Each drag handle is named "Reorder <step>" and offers Move up and Move down actions; a move is announced as "<step>, position 2 of 3".
Each remove button is named "Remove <step>"; a removal is announced as "Removed <step>".
An empty step is named "step 2" in these names.
Approving or rejecting announces the approved or rejected notice; once approved the chain of steps announces starts and failures.
The step number is hidden from VoiceOver because the step label carries it.
Every control has a 44-point touch target; the footer buttons stack when they do not fit.
edgeCases: A step whose text is only spaces counts as empty and is left out of the approved steps.
A new step opens its editor at once.
When the app passes a decision and neither onApprove nor onReject, no buttons are shown.
Long steps wrap at every text size.

name: MonarchAiPromptInput
title: AiPromptInput
wrapsNative: TextField(_:text:prompt:axis: .vertical) with lineLimit(min...max), onKeyPress for Return and Escape, keyboardShortcut(.return, modifiers: .command) on Send, PasteButton(supportedContentTypes:payloadAction:) and onDrop(of:isTargeted:perform:) for files, inside a bordered box with MonarchAiAttachmentTray, Button with .buttonStyle(.monarch(.primary, size: .sm)) for Send and MonarchAiStopButton
summary: The prompt box of an AI chat: a growing text field with attachments, a slot for the slash command or mention menu, a toolbar, a character and token count, and Send, which becomes Stop while a response runs.
whenToUse: At the bottom of an assistant conversation, in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom), where the person writes prompts and attaches files.
whenNotToUse: For person-to-person chat and ticket replies use MonarchMessageComposer, which has mentions, emoji, reply context and modes. For a single AI-assisted field in a form use MonarchAiAutofillField.

public enum MonarchAiPromptInputSubmitOn: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case returnKey, commandReturn }

options.name: label
options.description: The accessible name of the field, such as "Message the assistant". Shown above the box with showsLabel.

options.name: text
options.description: The prompt. The app owns it, so it can keep and restore a draft.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Shown while the text is empty; the built-in "Send a message…" without it.

options.name: attachments
options.description: The attached files, shown by MonarchAiAttachmentTray inside the box. They allow sending without text.

options.name: acceptedContentTypes
options.description: The types the Paste button and drops hand to onReceiveFiles; other items are ignored.

options.name: submitOn
options.description: Which hardware-keyboard key sends: Return (Shift-Return adds a line) or only Command-Return. Command-Return sends with either.

options.name: minLines
options.description: The fewest visible lines.

options.name: maxLines
options.description: The lines the text grows to before it scrolls.

options.name: maxLength
options.description: The most characters. Shows the counter; over the limit sending is off and the box border turns to danger. The text is never cut.

options.name: warnAt
options.description: The share of maxLength at which the counter turns to the warning colour and the characters left are announced.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: A response is running: Send is replaced by MonarchAiStopButton and Escape on a hardware keyboard calls onStop.

options.name: showsLabel
options.description: Shows the label above the box.

options.name: disabledReason
options.description: Why the input is disabled, shown under it while .disabled(true) is applied.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the attachment tray's.

options.name: countTokens
options.description: Estimates tokens for the "≈ N tokens" readout. Called on every change, so keep it cheap.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Stops the running response, from Stop and Escape. Without it Stop is disabled.

options.name: onAttach
options.description: Adds the attach button. Present the app's PhotosPicker or fileImporter.

options.name: onReceiveFiles
options.description: Adds the system Paste button and accepts files dropped on the box, filtered by acceptedContentTypes. Load each provider and add it to attachments.

options.name: onRemoveAttachment
options.description: Removes an attachment by id. Without it the tray is disabled.

options.name: onRetryAttachment
options.description: Retries a failed upload by id.

options.name: triggerMenu
options.description: A menu above the box that reads and writes the same text, such as MonarchAiSlashCommands, or MonarchAiMentionContext with MonarchMentionQuery.find.

options.name: toolbar
options.description: Controls in the bar under the text, after the attach and paste buttons, such as MonarchAiPromptToolbar or MonarchAiModelPicker.

options.name: footer
options.description: Under the box, such as MonarchAiDisclaimer.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the text as typed. The field clears at once; if onSubmit throws, the text comes back unless something new was typed.

states.name: empty
states.description: The placeholder shows and Send is disabled.

states.name: typing
states.description: The text grows to maxLines and then scrolls; Send is enabled.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: The counter turns to the strong warning colour and the characters left are announced once.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: The counter and the box border turn to the danger colours, the counter is read as how many characters are over, and Send is disabled.

states.name: busy
states.description: Send is replaced by MonarchAiStopButton; Escape on a hardware keyboard stops.

states.name: dragging
states.description: While files are dragged over the box it takes the accent fill and border and shows "Drop files to attach".

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the subtle fill and border, disabled text and buttons, and the reason under the box.

appearance: A box in the surface background with the input border and the container radius, the focus ring while the field has focus, the subtle placeholder colour, and the primary Monarch button for Send. Dragging uses the accent subtle fill and accent border (the accent roles directly, because MonarchTone has no accent case); over the limit the border uses the danger border role. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web component keeps its own attachments and opens its own file input; on iOS, as on Android, the attachments are hoisted (attachments, onRemoveAttachment) because the app picks and uploads files with PhotosPicker or fileImporter. The web's paste of images into the text area becomes the system PasteButton, which reads the pasteboard without the paste permission prompt, and the web's drop becomes onDrop on the box; both hand NSItemProviders to onReceiveFiles (Android uses content URIs). SwiftUI's TextField cannot receive pasted images itself. The web's triggers and renderTriggerMenu become one triggerMenu slot; MonarchAiSlashCommands and MonarchAiMentionContext bind to the same text, so the slot needs no arguments (Android passes a TextFieldValue). Keyboard avoidance needs no option: SwiftUI keeps a view in the bottom safe-area inset above the keyboard (Android's keyboardPadding). Enabled is SwiftUI's .disabled(_:) instead of a parameter. The web's screen reader hints for Enter and Escape are not added: on a phone the on-screen Return adds a line and Send sends. The send and attach icons are fixed SF Symbols with their spoken names, instead of Android's icon slots. usePromptDraft has no counterpart: the app keeps the text binding.
accessibility: The text field is named by label; the visible label is hidden from VoiceOver so it is not read twice.
Send, Stop, Attach and Paste are standard buttons with spoken names ("Send", "Stop", "Attach files", the system's "Paste") and touch targets of at least 44 points.
The counter is read as "120 of 4000 characters", or as "3 characters over the limit" when over.
Reaching the warning share announces the characters left once; going over the limit is announced; returning is silent.
Dragging files shows "Drop files to attach" as text, not only the accent colours.
Dropping files has equivalents VoiceOver can reach: the Paste button and the Attach button.
Disabled: the reason is shown as text under the box.
edgeCases: White space alone does not enable Send; attachments without text do.
Text over maxLength is kept, not cut; only sending is blocked.
maxLines smaller than minLines is raised to minLines; minLines under 1 is 1.
If onSubmit throws after the person typed something new, the new text is kept and the failed text is not restored.
Dropped or pasted items of other types are ignored, and nothing is received while disabled.
At the largest text sizes the text grows taller and the counter and buttons stay in the bar.

states.name: empty

appearance: The system list and navigation bar with Monarch text: titles in default text, descriptions in muted text and an AI strong symbol on each row; fields are MonarchTextField or a multi-line field with the same colours; the template and the preview sit on the subtle background; Use template is a full-width primary button. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web shows the gallery and a preview side by side, then a form step; iOS pushes a page per template in its own NavigationStack, so it belongs in a sheet. Categories are a Picker instead of filter chips. A multi-line blank uses a text field drawn with MonarchTextField's tokens until a shared multi-line field exists. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: Each template is one button read as its title and description.
Each field is read with its label, "Optional" when it may be empty, and its error or help as the hint.
When Use template finds an empty required field, the first error is announced and every error is written with an icon, not shown by colour alone.
The Template and Prompt preview headings have the header trait; the preview text can be selected.
Rows and buttons have 44-point touch targets and all text wraps at every size.
edgeCases: A blank used twice is one field and is filled everywhere.
A blank without a value stays as {{name}} in fill(_:values:); an empty value removes it, so an empty optional blank disappears from the used prompt.
Without variables every blank is required and labelled from its name: customer_name becomes "Customer name".
Search ignores case and diacritics and looks at the title, description, body and keywords.

name: MonarchAiPromptToolbar
title: AiPromptToolbar
wrapsNative: MonarchFlowLayout of standard Button and Toggle, with buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost, size: .sm)) and a compact ToggleStyle applied to the content
summary: The row of controls under an assistant prompt (web search, templates, mode, model, tone) that gives standard buttons and toggles one compact, quiet style and wraps when they do not fit.
whenToUse: Under a prompt field, for a few options that change how the next message is answered.
whenNotToUse: For text formatting use a formatting toolbar. For actions on a finished answer use the message actions. To choose one of several modes put MonarchAiModeSwitcher in the toolbar rather than several toggles.
api: MonarchAiPromptToolbar.init(label: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the group, "Prompt options".

options.name: content
options.description: The controls in order: standard Buttons, Toggles and pickers. Buttons get the small ghost Monarch button style and Toggles a compact toggle-button style, unless you apply your own.

states.name: toggle on
states.description: Assistant subtle fill, assistant border and assistant strong text; a check mark is added when the person asks for differentiation without colour.

states.name: toggle off
states.description: A ghost button in muted text with no border.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Off: the emphasis background. On: the assistant subtle hover fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With the standard disabled(_:) modifier the controls use the disabled text role; a toggle that is on keeps a muted fill and border.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Controls that do not fit move to a new line.

appearance: Buttons are the small ghost Monarch button. Toggles are transparent with muted text when off and take the assistant (ai) subtle fill, border and strong text when on. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web ships AiPromptToolbarButton and AiPromptToolbarToggle; on iOS the standard Button and Toggle are styled by the toolbar, and icon-only controls use .labelStyle(.iconOnly) instead of hideLabel. The web's uncontrolled defaultPressed is not offered: a Toggle takes a binding. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The toolbar is a container named by label ("Prompt options"); controls are read in order.
A toggle keeps the system Toggle as its accessibility representation, so VoiceOver reads it as a switch with its on or off value; its label does not change with its state.
An icon-only control keeps its title as its spoken name.
Every control is at least 44 by 44 points.
A toggle that is on also differs by its border, and by a check mark when Differentiate Without Colour is on.
Press and state changes are not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: Controls wider than the row get a line of their own and their text wraps.
A control with its own buttonStyle or toggleStyle keeps it.
An empty toolbar takes no height.

name: MonarchAiReasoning
title: AiReasoning
wrapsNative: DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch); MonarchAiThinkingIndicator (TimelineView) as the live timer in the header
summary: The model's reasoning for one answer, as a disclosure that reads "Thinking…" with a live timer while it streams and "Thought for 12s" once it finishes.
whenToUse: Inside an assistant reply, to show a reasoning part (MonarchAiReasoningPart) from the message model without letting it crowd the answer.
whenNotToUse: Not for the wait before the first token when there is no reasoning to show (use MonarchAiThinkingIndicator) and not for the steps of an agent (use MonarchAiChainOfSteps).
api: init(_ part: MonarchAiReasoningPart, startedAt: Date? = nil, startsExpanded: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiReasoningLabels = MonarchAiReasoningLabels(), onExpandedChange: (@MainActor (Bool) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAiReasoningLabels { init(prefix: String? = nil, thinking: String? = nil, thoughtFor: ((String) -> String)? = nil, thought: String? = nil, reasoningHidden: String? = nil, duration: ((Int) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: part
options.description: The reasoning part from the message model: its text, whether it streams, its durationMs and whether it is redacted.

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the reasoning started. Pass it when the view can be rebuilt while the part streams, so the timer does not restart. The moment the view appears when nil.

options.name: startsExpanded
options.description: Whether finished reasoning starts open. Streaming reasoning always starts open.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the duration format.

options.name: onExpandedChange
options.description: Called when the disclosure opens or closes, by the person or automatically when the reasoning finishes or starts again.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Open; the header is a MonarchAiThinkingIndicator with the pulsing assistant mark, "Thinking…" and the elapsed time after 3 seconds; the text grows live. With no text yet it is a still row with the same header.

states.name: finished
states.description: Closed; the header reads "Thought for" the part's durationMs, or the time this view measured, or "Thought" when neither is known.

states.name: touched
states.description: If the person opens or closes it while it streams, it stays as they left it when the reasoning finishes.

states.name: restarted
states.description: When a finished part streams again (a regeneration), it opens and measures again.

states.name: redacted
states.description: A still row with the assistant mark and "Reasoning hidden"; no disclosure and no text.

appearance: The header uses the Monarch disclosure group style; the thinking mark and the still-row glyph take the AI strong role; the reasoning text takes the muted text role beside a thin rule in the AI border role. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web wraps a details element and renders the text with AiStreamingText; iOS uses the standard DisclosureGroup and plain selectable Text, because iOS has no streaming text component yet. The web chevron leads; the Monarch disclosure style puts it at the trailing edge. The web's onOpenChange is onExpandedChange; its locale prop is the SwiftUI locale environment. The web prefixes the summary with hidden text; iOS puts the prefix in the header's accessibility label.
accessibility: The header is the disclosure button of MonarchDisclosureGroupStyle, labelled "Assistant reasoning: Thought for 12s" (or "Thinking…") with an Expanded or Collapsed value.
Redacted or empty reasoning is one element with the same label and no button.
The live timer is not read on every tick and the reasoning is not announced; VoiceOver reads the current header when it reaches it.
With Reduce Motion the thinking mark stops pulsing (the timer still ticks once a second) and the content opens without animation.
The header and the still row are at least 44 points high; text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A part that streams with no text yet shows the live header without a disclosure, then becomes a disclosure when text arrives.
A durationMs on the part wins over the time this view measured.
Durations round to whole seconds and are at least 1 second.
Long reasoning wraps; the disclosure has no height limit.

name: MonarchAiRelatedEntities
title: AiRelatedEntities
wrapsNative: VStack of rows (MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, a Capsule relevance bar), Button when selectable; a custom Layout (radial placement) with a Shape for relation lines for the graph variant
summary: People, organisations, projects and records the assistant found related to the current content, ranked by relevance with their relations, as a list or a radial graph.
whenToUse: Beside an answer or a record, to show what the assistant connected it to and let the person open one.
whenNotToUse: Not for the sources an answer cites (use MonarchAiSourceList) and not for a full network chart (use MonarchForceGraph).
api: init(_ entities: [MonarchAiRelatedEntity], relations: [MonarchAiEntityRelation] = [], variant: MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesVariant = .list, centerID: String? = nil, maxGraphNodes: Int = 12, labels: MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesLabels = MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchAiRelatedEntity) -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchAiRelatedEntity { init(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchAiRelatedEntityKind, weight: Double? = nil, imageURL: URL? = nil) }
struct MonarchAiRelatedEntityKind: RawRepresentable, ExpressibleByStringLiteral { static let person, org, project, document, record, place, other }
struct MonarchAiEntityRelation { init(from: String, to: String, label: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesVariant { case list, graph }

struct MonarchAiRelatedEntitiesLabels { init(label: String? = nil, kind: ((MonarchAiRelatedEntityKind) -> String)? = nil, weight: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, relation: ((String, String?) -> String)? = nil, relatedTo: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil) }

options.name: entities
options.description: The entities: id, label, kind, optional weight from 0 to 1 and optional imageURL. The list is sorted by weight, highest first; unweighted entities keep their order after them.

options.name: relations
options.description: Links between entities by id, with an optional label such as "works at". Shown under each entity and as lines in the graph.

options.name: variant
options.description: A ranked list, or a radial graph.

options.name: centerID
options.description: The graph's middle entity. The one with the highest weight when nil or unknown.

options.name: maxGraphNodes
options.description: Above this many entities the graph variant shows the list.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes every entity a button that calls this with the entity.

states.name: list
states.description: Bordered rows with the avatar, the name, the relations line, the kind badge and a relevance bar.

states.name: graph
states.description: A square up to four node widths across: the centre entity with a large avatar in the middle, the others on a ring from the top, clockwise, with medium or small avatars by weight, and a line for each relation.

states.name: graph fallback
states.description: More than maxGraphNodes entities, or an accessibility text size: the list is shown instead.

states.name: selectable
states.description: With onSelect each row or node is a plain button.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState reading "No related entities".

appearance: Names use the default text role, relations and ring labels the muted role; the relevance bar fills with the AI solid role on the muted background; relation lines and row borders use the default and subtle border roles. Avatars and badges use their own Monarch colours. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web draws the graph in SVG with circles; iOS places MonarchAvatar nodes with a custom Layout and draws relation lines with a Shape. The diagram is drawn left to right in both layout directions, because a radial diagram has no reading direction and the lines must meet the nodes. iOS also falls back to the list at accessibility text sizes, where node labels would overlap. Entities can carry an imageURL for the avatar; the web shows no pictures. The web's kind is any string; iOS uses a string-backed kind with static members, so custom kinds still work.
accessibility: The list or the diagram is a container named "Related entities".
Each entity is one element read as "Jordan Lee. Person. Relevance 90%. Related to: works at Acme"; with onSelect it is a button.
Avatars are decorative; relevance bars and relation lines are hidden because the spoken name carries them.
The kind is written in a badge, so it does not depend on the avatar symbol.
Rows and nodes are at least 44 points high; text scales with Dynamic Type, and the graph becomes the list at accessibility sizes.
edgeCases: Weights outside 0 to 1 are limited; missing or infinite weights count as unweighted.
Relations that name an entity not in the list are left out.
Graph node labels are cut to two lines; the full name is spoken.
A single entity in the graph sits alone in the middle.

name: MonarchAiResponseSkeleton
title: AiResponseSkeleton
wrapsNative: Capsule bars in VStack/HStack, TimelineView(.animation) for the pulse
summary: A placeholder shaped like the coming answer (lines of text, cards or a table) shown between sending a prompt and the first streamed token.
whenToUse: When an assistant answer has been requested and nothing has arrived yet, especially for a generated card, table or summary that loads in place.
whenNotToUse: Once text streams, show the text. For a short wait inside a chat bubble use MonarchAiThinkingIndicator or MonarchAiTypingDots. For loading that is not the assistant, use redacted(reason: .placeholder) (see skeleton).
api: MonarchAiResponseSkeleton.init(shape: MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape = .text, lines: Int? = nil, columns: Int = 3, label: String? = nil)
enum MonarchAiResponseSkeletonShape { case text, cards, table }

options.name: shape
options.description: text: paragraph lines with a short last line. cards: a column of card outlines. table: a header row and body rows.

options.name: lines
options.description: The number of text lines, cards or table body rows. nil gives 3 for text and cards and 4 for a table. Values below 1 draw 1.

options.name: columns
options.description: The number of table columns. Values below 1 draw 1.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text, "Generating response…".

states.name: waiting
states.description: The bars pulse with the assistant subtle tint over one shimmer duration.

states.name: Reduce Motion
states.description: The bars stay still with no tint.

appearance: Bars use the muted background, title and header bars the emphasis background; cards and the table sit on the surface colour with a subtle border and a subtle header row. The pulse is the assistant (ai) subtle colour. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web lays cards out in a responsive grid; on iOS they are one column, which holds at every text size. The web sweeps a gradient band across the bars from the start edge; iOS pulses the tint over the whole bar, which needs no direction. Bar heights scale with Dynamic Type. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The placeholder is one element read as "Generating response…" or the label given, with the updates-frequently trait.
The bars are not read.
It posts no announcement; the conversation announces its own progress.
Under Reduce Motion the pulse stops and the bars stay.
edgeCases: lines and columns below 1 draw one line, card, row or column.
A single text line is full width; with several, the last one is shorter.
Many table columns get narrow bars; widths are fractions of each cell.

name: MonarchAiSafetyNotice
title: AiSafetyNotice
wrapsNative: VStack of Text with MonarchBanner's tokens and colours, MonarchButton for Edit prompt, Link with MonarchLinkStyle for the guidelines
summary: Says, calmly and specifically, that a safety system blocked a request, changed an answer or removed parts of it, with an optional reason, next steps, an Edit prompt button and a link to the content guidelines.
whenToUse: In place of an answer a safety system blocked (blocked), or above an answer that was changed (modified) or had parts removed (filtered).
whenNotToUse: For technical failures such as timeouts or rate limits use MonarchAiErrorMessage. For a general reminder that AI can be wrong use MonarchAiDisclaimer.
api: MonarchAiSafetyNotice.init(_ kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind, title: String? = nil, message: String? = nil, reason: String? = nil, nextSteps: String? = nil, learnMoreURL: URL? = nil, labels: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels = MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels(), onEditPrompt: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind: String { case blocked, modified, filtered }

MonarchAiSafetyNoticeLabels.init(title: (@Sendable (_ kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind) -> String)? = nil, message: (@Sendable (_ kind: MonarchAiSafetyNoticeKind) -> String)? = nil, reason: String? = nil, editPrompt: String? = nil, learnMore: String? = nil)

options.name: kind
options.description: What the safety system did. Sets the tone, the symbol and the default title and explanation.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the title of the kind for this notice.

options.name: message
options.description: Replaces the explanation of the kind for this notice.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why, in plain words, shown after a bold "Reason:" label. Empty text is not shown.

options.name: nextSteps
options.description: What the person can do next, as a sentence.

options.name: learnMoreURL
options.description: Adds a "Content guidelines" link. Only http, https and mailto links are shown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the built-in titles, explanations, "Reason:", "Edit prompt" and "Content guidelines".

options.name: onEditPrompt
options.description: Adds an "Edit prompt" button, usually to put the prompt back in the composer.

states.name: blocked
states.description: Warning colours and a lock symbol: "This request wasn’t answered".

states.name: modified
states.description: Info colours and a pencil symbol: "This response was adjusted".

states.name: filtered
states.description: Info colours and a filter symbol: "Some content was hidden".

states.name: static
states.description: Without onEditPrompt and learnMoreURL the notice has no actions.

appearance: Drawn like MonarchBanner: the tone's subtle background, the tone's border and the tone's strong colour on the symbol, with default text. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web takes rich content for the reason and next steps; iOS takes plain strings, and an app that needs more places its own views after the notice. The link opens through the environment's openURL action (the browser by default) instead of the same tab. The web uses the accent edge only through logical CSS; iOS mirrors the whole layout in right to left. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The title, the explanation, the reason with its "Reason:" label and the next steps are one element, read in that order.
The symbol is decorative; each kind has its own title, so the kind does not depend on colour or on the symbol.
"Edit prompt" is a button and the guidelines link keeps the link trait and is read with "opens in the browser"; both are separate elements with 44-point touch targets.
The notice does not announce itself; place it where the answer would have been.
edgeCases: A reason or next steps that are empty or only spaces are not shown.
A javascript:, file: or custom-scheme URL is dropped and no link is shown.
The actions sit on one line when they fit and stack when they do not, at large text sizes.

name: MonarchAiScore
title: AiScore
wrapsNative: MonarchScoreRing (ProgressView with a ring style) or a Capsule bar, MonarchBadge for the band, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge, and a DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) for the band legend
summary: A 0 to 100 score produced by a model, as a ring or a bar, with its band, the rationale and the factors that raised or lowered it.
whenToUse: To show a model's score for a record, such as a lead, churn or fit score, with the reasons behind it.
whenNotToUse: Not for a score a person or a rule computed (use MonarchScoreRing) and not for how sure the model is of an answer (use MonarchAiConfidenceMeter).
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, value: Double?, bands: [MonarchAiScoreBand] = MonarchAiScoreBand.defaults, rationale: String? = nil, factors: [MonarchAiScoreFactor] = [], variant: MonarchAiScoreVariant = .ring, size: MonarchAiScoreSize = .md, showsBands: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiScoreLabels = MonarchAiScoreLabels())
struct MonarchAiScoreBand { init(minimum: Double, label: String, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral); static var defaults: [MonarchAiScoreBand] }
struct MonarchAiScoreFactor { init(_ label: String, impact: Double, detail: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiScoreVariant { case ring, bar }
enum MonarchAiScoreSize { case sm, md }

struct MonarchAiScoreLabels { init(label: String? = nil, aiGenerated: String? = nil, valueText: ((String, String) -> String)? = nil, unavailable: String? = nil, factors: String? = nil, impact: ((String, Bool) -> String)? = nil, noImpact: String? = nil, bands: String? = nil, currentBand: String? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: What is scored, such as "Lead score". "Score" when nil.

options.name: value
options.description: The score from 0 to 100; values outside are limited. nil while there is no score.

options.name: bands
options.description: Named ranges with a minimum, a label and a MonarchTone. Low (0, danger), Medium (40, warning) and High (70, success) by default.

options.name: rationale
options.description: Why the model gave this score, in plain words.

options.name: factors
options.description: The inputs that moved the score, each with a label, a signed impact and an optional detail.

options.name: variant
options.description: A ring with the number in its centre, or a bar with the number above it.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the ring: sm or md.

options.name: showsBands
options.description: Whether the band legend disclosure is offered.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.name: scored
states.description: The ring or bar fills to the score in the band's tone; the band badge shows the tone's icon and the band's name.

states.name: no score
states.description: An empty ring with a dash, or "No score yet" above an empty bar; no band badge.

states.name: factors
states.description: Each factor shows its label, detail, a signed impact with an up or down arrow and a small bar sized against the largest impact.

states.name: legend
states.description: A collapsed disclosure, "How to read this score", listing each band with a swatch and its range; the current band is marked "(this score)" in bold.

appearance: The ring is a MonarchScoreRing in the band's tone; the bar fill and the legend swatches use the tone's solid role on the muted background track; raised and lowered impacts use the success and danger strong roles; text uses the default and muted text roles. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web lists factors and bands in tables; iOS shows rows, each read as one element. The web's tones include ai and info; MonarchTone has no ai case, so a band cannot take the AI colour on iOS. The web's locale prop is the SwiftUI locale environment. label, rationale and factor text are plain strings on iOS, not arbitrary content.
accessibility: The ring is one element named by the label, with the value "72 out of 100" or "No score yet"; the band badge is read after it.
The bar is one element named by the label, with the value "72 out of 100, High".
The band is always written and shown with the tone's icon, so it never depends on colour.
Each factor is one element: its label, then "Raised the score by 18" or "Lowered the score by 9" and its detail.
The legend is the Monarch disclosure button; each band row is read as one element and the current band is marked in words.
Headings (the label and the factors heading) have the header trait; text scales with Dynamic Type and the header stacks when it does not fit.
edgeCases: Scores above 100 or below 0 are limited; NaN counts as no score.
A score below the lowest band's minimum takes the lowest band.
Band upper bounds are the next band's minimum minus one, and 100 for the last.
Impacts are compared with the largest impact, and never with less than 1 point.

title: AiScrollAnchor
wrapsNative: ScrollView with .defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom); .scrollPosition(id:anchor:) to jump to the latest message (ScrollPosition and onScrollGeometryChange from iOS 18)
summary: Bottom-pinned scrolling for a growing thread is a property of the standard ScrollView. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a chat thread or log that should open at its newest entry and stay there while content arrives: put the messages in a ScrollView with defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom).
whenNotToUse: Not for content read from the top. For the full thread with Jump to latest and Load earlier, use AiThread when it is available.
api: func defaultScrollAnchor(_ anchor: UnitPoint?) -> some View
func scrollPosition(id: Binding<(some Hashable)?>, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil) -> some View
func scrollTargetLayout(isEnabled: Bool = true) -> some View

states.name: at the bottom
states.description: The scroll view opens at the bottom anchor, and keeps that anchor when the content or the container changes size.

states.name: scrolled up
states.description: The person's position is kept. Setting the scrollPosition binding to the last id scrolls back to the newest entry.

appearance: System scrolling in every theme. The content inside uses the theme.
platformNotes: The web ships a hook and a headless container that measure the scroller, pin it while the person is within 48 pixels of the bottom and report atBottom. In SwiftUI the anchor is declared on the ScrollView and the system does the pinning, so there is no Monarch type. iOS 17 has no public reading of the scroll offset: to show a Jump to latest button only when the person has scrolled up, compare the scrollPosition id with the last id, or on iOS 18 and later use onScrollGeometryChange. iOS 18 also adds ScrollPosition and defaultScrollAnchor(_:for:), which separates the initial offset from size changes. Android uses a reversed LazyColumn.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver scrolls the ScrollView with three-finger swipes and announces the page.
Scrolling to the newest entry does not move VoiceOver focus.
Scrolling with withAnimation follows the system's Reduce Motion handling only if the app checks accessibilityReduceMotion; the example does.
edgeCases: scrollPosition(id:) needs scrollTargetLayout() on the stack that holds the entries, and each entry needs a stable id.
Content shorter than the scroll view is laid out from the bottom with a bottom anchor.
How firmly iOS 17 keeps the bottom while text streams in was not measured on a device for this entry.

title: AiSettingsSection
wrapsNative: Form with Section(content:header:footer:), Toggle rows, Picker rows, MonarchSecretField for the provider key, and toolbar ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) and .confirmationAction for Discard and Save; MonarchSectionCard with the buttons in its footer on a scrolling page
summary: A recipe, not a component: workspace AI settings (AI on or off per app, data sharing, conversation retention and a bring-your-own provider key) as Form sections kept as a draft until Save.
whenToUse: On a workspace settings screen where admins decide where AI is available and how it handles data.
whenNotToUse: For switches that save one by one as they change, use MonarchSwitchSettingsList. For a spending limit use MonarchAiSpendCap; for the model choice, MonarchAiModelPicker.
api: Form { Section { Toggle(appName, isOn: …) } header: { Text("Use AI in") } }
Section { Toggle("Share data to improve AI", isOn: …); Picker("Conversation history", selection: …) { … } } header: { Text("Data") } footer: { Text(…) }
Section { Picker("AI provider", selection: …) { … }; MonarchSecretField("<Provider> API key", text: …, helper: …, isSet: keyIsSaved) } header: { Text("Provider") }
.toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) { Button("Discard") }; ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) { Button("Save") } }
MonarchSectionCard("AI", description: …) { rows } actions: { EmptyView() } footer: { MonarchButton("Discard") ; MonarchButton("Save changes", variant: .primary) }

options.name: apps
options.type: list of app ids and names (app state)
options.description: One Toggle per app under a Use AI in header; leave the section out when there are no apps.

options.name: isDirty
options.description: The draft differs from the saved settings, or a new key was typed: Discard and Save are enabled.

options.name: isSaving
options.description: Disable the form and show a ProgressView in place of Save while the app saves.

options.name: read only
options.description: Every row disabled, the reason in the first section's footer, and no Save or Discard.

states.name: ready
states.description: The saved settings, Discard and Save disabled.

states.name: dirty
states.description: Discard and Save enabled in the toolbar.

states.name: provider chosen
states.description: A MonarchSecretField for the provider's key; a saved key shows as set and is never sent back to the screen.

states.name: saving
states.description: The form is disabled while the app saves.

states.name: read only
states.description: Rows disabled and the reason shown in a footer.

states.name: save failed
states.description: Keep the draft and show the error in an alert or a MonarchInlineErrorRetry above the form.

appearance: The system grouped form: section headers and footers in the system's secondary styles, toggles and pickers tinted with the accent fill, the secret field in Monarch's field style. The card form uses the MonarchSectionCard surface and Monarch buttons. Both follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships AiSettingsSection as one component with a value, a draft and onSave. As for settings-section, iOS makes it a recipe on Form sections: the Form gives the titled groups, headers, footers, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver order of iOS settings, and the app keeps the draft and the saved value. Save and Discard are toolbar buttons, the iOS pattern for editing screens, instead of the web's footer; the card form with the footer is offered for a scrolling page. The web lists apps with SwitchSettingsList, which saves each switch as it changes; this recipe uses plain Toggle rows so the apps stay in the same draft as the other rows (Android does the same with MonarchSwitchRow). The web's NativeSelect is a Picker; its SecretField with isSet is MonarchSecretField with isSet. The web's bot icon in the heading is left out: a Form header is text. Experimental, as a product composite, until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: Section headers are read as headings in a Form, and footers after their rows.
Each app is a system Toggle with its name as the label and its state as the value.
Pickers are system pickers, read with their label and selected value.
The provider key is a MonarchSecretField: hidden by default with a Show button, and a saved key read as set.
Discard and Save are toolbar buttons with text labels, read as dimmed while disabled.
edgeCases: Apps missing from the saved settings count as off.
Changing the provider clears a typed key; leaving the key blank keeps the saved one.
Send the key only when one was typed, and never show a saved key.
Leaving the screen with unsaved changes should ask first: pair it with the unsaved-changes-guard recipe.

summary: The presence and turn-taking bar of an AI conversation shared by several people and agents: who is here, who is typing, whose request is being answered, what waits, and whether you may send.
whenToUse: Above a shared AI conversation where several people send requests to the same assistant and take turns.
whenNotToUse: For presence alone in a document or page use MonarchPresenceAvatars. For agents working on one task use MonarchAiMultiAgentRoster.
api: init(_ participants: [MonarchAiSharedSessionParticipant], answering: MonarchAiSharedSessionAnswering? = nil, queue: [MonarchAiSharedSessionRequest] = [], maxVisible: Int = 4, following: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isQueueExpanded: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isAccessRequested: Bool = false, announcesChanges: Bool = true, labels: MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels = MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels(), onWithdraw: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onReorder: (@MainActor ([String], MonarchAiSharedSessionMove) -> Void)? = nil, onRemove: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onInvite: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRequestAccess: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchAiSharedSessionParticipant: Identifiable { var id, name: String; var avatarURL: URL?; var kind: MonarchAiSharedSessionKind; var role: MonarchAiSharedSessionRole; var presence: MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence; var activity: MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity?; var isYou: Bool }
enum MonarchAiSharedSessionKind: String { case person, agent }
enum MonarchAiSharedSessionRole: String { case owner, editor, viewer }
enum MonarchAiSharedSessionPresence: String { case active, idle, away }
enum MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity: String { case typing, speaking, reviewing }
struct MonarchAiSharedSessionAnswering { var participantID, forParticipantID: String; var label: String? }
struct MonarchAiSharedSessionRequest: Identifiable { var id, participantID, preview: String }
struct MonarchAiSharedSessionMove { var id: String; var from, to: Int }

struct MonarchAiSharedSessionLabels { var label, listTitle, people, agents, agentKind, assistant, someone, quiet, queueTitle, withdraw, remove, moveUp, moveDown, invite, follow, viewerNotice, requestAccess, accessRequested, done: String?; var here: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)?; var showAll, several, queueCount, queueToggle: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)?; var nameWithYou, followLabel: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var role, presence, activity: per-enum (@Sendable (…) -> String)?; var activityLine: (@Sendable (MonarchAiSharedSessionActivity, String, Int) -> String)?; var answering: (@Sendable (String, String, String?) -> String)?; var answeringYou: (@Sendable (String, String?) -> String)?; var requestAction, moved: three-argument closures }

options.name: participants
options.description: Everyone in the session, people and agents, in display order. Mark one person isYou; their role decides what they can do.

options.name: answering
options.description: The answer in progress: which agent, whose request and an optional short label.

options.name: queue
options.description: Requests waiting for their turn, first in line first.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: The avatars shown before "+N". At least one.

options.name: following
options.description: The ids of the people you follow. Shows a Follow toggle beside every other person in the list.

options.name: isQueueExpanded
options.description: Whether the queue is shown, when the app owns it. nil lets the Queue button own it.

options.name: isAccessRequested
options.description: Replaces a viewer's Request access button with "Access requested".

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Announces status changes and queue moves to VoiceOver.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onWithdraw
options.description: Shows Withdraw on your own requests.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Shows Move up and Move down to an owner; receives the request ids in their new order and the move.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Shows Remove on other people's requests to an owner.

options.name: onInvite
options.description: Shows an Invite button; the product opens its own invite flow.

options.name: onRequestAccess
options.description: Shows Request access in a viewer's notice.

states.name: quiet
states.description: "No requests in progress" in subtle text.

states.name: answering
states.description: The answering agent's avatar turns (still with Reduce Motion) and the status starts with whose request it answers, "your request" when it is yours.

states.name: activity
states.description: Other people typing, speaking or reviewing are named, two at most, else counted.

states.name: queue
states.description: "Queue (2)" shows or hides the waiting requests; your own requests are tinted with the subtle AI fill.

states.name: owner
states.description: Move up, Move down and Remove on requests when the closures are given; the ends' moves are disabled.

states.name: viewer
states.description: A notice "You can watch but not send" with Request access, or "Access requested".

states.name: empty
states.description: No avatars; only the status line.

appearance: A plain bar: overlapping avatars with presence dots, the status line in muted text, ghost and secondary small buttons, the viewer notice and requests on the subtle background. Agents use the square AI agent avatar. All roles come from the theme.
platformNotes: The web opens the participant list in a popover; iOS presents it in a sheet, and the whole stack is one button because single overlapping avatars are too small to tap. The web throttles announcements with announceInterval; iOS announces each change of the announced clauses, and typing and speaking are never announced, so there is no interval. The open state of the participant list is not controllable. Follows are a Binding<Set<String>> instead of following, defaultFollowing and onFollowChange. Presence is drawn with the avatar's presence dot (active online, idle away, away offline) and always written as a word in the list. The queue toggle has the selected trait while open, because SwiftUI has no expanded trait. The parity map listed presence-avatars; its stack is MonarchAvatarGroup, which this bar uses directly because it mixes people and agents.
accessibility: The bar is a container named "Shared session".
The avatar stack is one button named "3 people and 1 agent here"; its value names each visible participant with role or "AI agent", presence and activity, and its hint is "Shows all 5 participants."
In the list each participant is one element with name, "(you)", role, presence and what they are doing; Follow toggles are named "Follow Sam Lee".
Changes of who is being answered, of who is reviewing and of the queue length are announced; typing and speaking are not, and the first status is not.
Queue buttons are named with the request, for example "Move up: request 2, from Sam Lee", and a move is announced.
Presence is always a word as well as a dot; every button has a 44-point touch target and text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: An answering agent or requester that is not a participant reads as "Assistant" or "Someone".
Your own activity is left out of the status line.
A "+1" tile is never shown: with one participant too many all are shown.
Without a person marked isYou there is no role, so no owner actions and no viewer notice.
Request previews are cut to one line.

whenToUse: Above an assistant prompt or composer that offers commands such as /summarize, /translate or /search.
whenNotToUse: For inserting blocks in a document editor use MonarchSlashMenu. For @ mentions use the mentions of MonarchMessageComposer (MonarchMentionPicker). For starting suggestions in an empty conversation use MonarchAiStarterPrompts.

states.name: open

platformNotes: The web hook wires a listbox beside the caret of AiPromptInput, with focus kept in the textarea and Arrow keys, Enter and Tab to choose; iOS gives no caret position, so the menu is the MonarchSlashMenu strip above the prompt and each command is a button. Each command is a button read as its /name and its description; disabled commands are not activatable.
The number of commands, or the empty text, is announced as it changes, so focus can stay in the prompt.
Rows are at least 44 points high and grow with Dynamic Type; icons are decorative.
edgeCases: A slash inside a word (and/or) does not open the menu; a space after the command closes it.
Queries longer than 24 characters close the menu (MonarchSlashMenuQuery's maxLength).
Return text ending in a space, such as "/summarize ", so the menu closes after the choice.

The group headings count every source, also the ones hidden while collapsed.
collapseAfter 0 hides every source until the list is expanded.

An empty list shows only the heading; leave the view out when a reply has no sources.

name: MonarchAiSpendCap
title: AiSpendCap
wrapsNative: VStack card with ProgressView(value:total:) in a private tone-aware ProgressViewStyle, and an inline form of MonarchCurrencyInput, Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu), MonarchRadioCardGroup and confirmationDialog
summary: A spending limit for AI usage: what has been spent against the limit this period, whether that is fine, close or reached, and a form to change the limit, when to warn and what happens at the limit.
whenToUse: In workspace or account settings where an admin sets how much AI may spend per day, week or month, and where people check how much is left.
whenNotToUse: Not for token or credit usage without money, which is MonarchAiUsageMeter. Not for plan quotas of a subscription, which is MonarchUsageMeter.

enum MonarchAiSpendCapBehavior: String { case pause, notify }
enum MonarchAiSpendCapState: String { case ok, warning, reached, noLimit }
enum MonarchAiSpendCapUnit: String { case minor, micros }
