options.description: Spent so far this period, as an integer in unit. Negative values count as zero.

options.name: limit
options.description: The limit as an integer in unit, or nil when none is set.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of every amount.

options.name: period
options.description: The window the limit applies to: day, week or month.

options.name: unit
options.description: What the integers count: the currency's minor unit, or micros (millionths of the major unit).

options.name: warnAt
options.description: The share of the limit at which the state becomes warning.

options.name: behavior
options.description: What happens at the limit: pause and ask, or keep going and tell.

options.name: resetsAt
options.description: When the period starts again; shown with the day and month, and the time for a daily limit, in the environment's time zone.

options.name: breakdown
options.description: Spending per agent or feature, shown as a list under the bar.

options.name: maxLimit
options.description: The highest limit this person may set.

options.name: warnAtOptions
options.description: The warn-at choices; the current value is always offered, values outside 0 to 1 are left out.

options.name: isEditing
options.description: Whether the form is open. Kept inside, closed at first, when nil.

options.name: canEdit
options.description: Whether this person may change the limit. false shows a read-only note and no form.

options.name: isSaving
options.description: Shows Save as busy and disables the form while the app saves.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Runs with the new settings on Save, or with a nil limit once removal is confirmed. Nothing is applied by the component.

options.name: onRequestIncrease
options.description: For people who cannot edit: adds "Request a higher limit".

states.name: ok
states.description: "Within limit" with a check, an accent bar.

states.name: warning
states.description: "Close to the limit" with a triangle, a warning bar.

states.name: reached
states.description: "Limit reached" with an octagon, a full danger bar; with pause, a danger notice says AI is paused and offers Raise limit or Request a higher limit.

states.name: no limit
states.description: "No limit set", no bar, and Set a limit instead of Edit limit.

states.name: editing
states.description: The amount field, the warn-at menu, the behaviour choice, Save, Cancel and Remove limit.

states.name: below spent
states.description: A limit below what is spent shows a warning notice and Save becomes Save anyway; saving the same amount again confirms.

states.name: invalid
states.description: An empty, zero, negative or too-high amount shows an error under the field.

states.name: saving
states.description: Save shows its loading state and the form is disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: A lock and "Only a workspace admin can change this limit.", with Request a higher limit when given.

appearance: A card on the surface background with the subtle border; the state is a small status badge in its tone, the amount line is strong default text, the bar's track is the muted background and its fill the accent, warning or danger solid role, facts are muted text. Every colour is a theme role, so it follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds the form with a native select and a radio group and confirms removal inline; on iOS the warn-at choice is a menu Picker, the behaviour is MonarchRadioCardGroup and removal is a system confirmationDialog. The amount field is MonarchCurrencyInput, which accepts only numbers, so the web's "not an amount" error does not arise. The web's children slot for extra content is left out; place content beside the card. The bar uses a private tone-aware ProgressViewStyle because MonarchProgressViewStyle has a single fill colour. Times use the environment's locale and time zone instead of locale and timeZone props.
accessibility: The card is a container named by its title; the title has the header trait.
The state is a word and an icon in a status badge, never colour alone.
The bar is a ProgressView named "Spent against the limit" with the amount line as its value.
A change of state after the card appears is announced once, such as "AI spending limit: Limit reached. £50.00 of £50.00 this month".
Errors are read by MonarchCurrencyInput with the field; the below-spent warning is announced when it appears.
Removing the limit asks in a confirmation dialog with a destructive Remove limit and Keep limit.
Every button is a MonarchButton with a 44-point target.
edgeCases: A limit of zero is always reached and draws no bar.
Spending over the limit reads "£2.10 over the limit"; the bar stays full.
Amounts in micros are rounded to the currency's digits when shown and when typed.
Currencies without minor units, such as JPY, show whole amounts.
Long breakdown labels wrap.

options.name: announces
options.description: Announce new sentences and finished blocks, then Response complete. Turn it off when the surrounding thread announces messages itself.

options.name: announceInterval
options.description: The minimum time between announcements; values below one second are raised to one second.

options.name: announcesCompletion
options.description: Whether Response complete may be announced when this text stops streaming. Pass false while the reply goes on after this text (a tool runs), then true once it ends: the announcement is owed until then.

options.name: showsCaret
options.description: Whether a caret follows the last character while streaming.

options.name: showsLinkHosts
options.description: Whether the host follows a link whose text does not name it, as in MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces Response complete, Code block and Table.

options.name: markdownLabels
options.description: Replaces the strings of the Markdown rendering (table name and size, Footnotes, Task, link host).

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens links in the app instead of the environment's openURL action; with it, relative links are links too.

options.name: image(_:)
options.description: Renders paragraphs that are a single http or https image; without it the alt text shows.

options.name: codeBlock(_:)
options.description: Renders code blocks instead of MonarchCodeBlock; isComplete is false until the closing fence arrives.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Finished blocks are drawn once and skipped while later ones arrive; the last block is completed for display (open emphasis and code spans closed, a link whose target is still arriving shown as its text, a lone trailing delimiter hidden, table rows held back until the delimiter row) and a caret follows its last character.

states.name: streaming code
states.description: An unclosed code block renders as code without its copy button and with no caret, since the code itself grows.

states.name: complete
states.description: The caret goes; the text renders as MonarchAiMarkdown would, and Response complete is announced once.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty text renders nothing.

appearance: The same as MonarchAiMarkdown: running text in the default text role, headings, lists, quotations, code and tables in their roles. The caret is a thin block glyph in the text colour, so it follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web streams into AiMarkdown with a live region; iOS uses the same incremental parser as MonarchAiMarkdown and the same completion rules, ported from the web's completeStreamingMarkdown, and announces through AccessibilityNotification.Announcement with the web's throttle: sentences and finished blocks, at most once per interval, never below one second, then Response complete, and nothing for text that never streamed. The web's caret is a blinking block in the AI solid colour placed after the text with zero width; SwiftUI text has no zero-width inline slot and MonarchAiMarkdown has no trailing slot, so the caret is a text glyph at the end of the last paragraph, heading or list item, in the text colour, and it does not blink (a blinking glyph would redraw the last paragraph twice a second, and the static form is what Reduce Motion asks for anyway). It is not drawn after code, tables or rules, and not drawn while VoiceOver runs, so it is never read. The web's headingLevelOffset, allowImageHosts, resolveImageUrl, externalLinksInNewTab and renderMath are not offered, as for MonarchAiMarkdown; image(_:) and codeBlock(_:) are the slots. Android has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: Complete sentences and finished blocks are announced at most once per interval, never single tokens; a code block is announced as Code block and a table as Table instead of being read out.
Response complete is announced once when streaming ends, or later, when announcesCompletion becomes true.
Text that never streamed in this view (history) is not announced, and a different answer starts the announcements over.
The caret is not drawn while VoiceOver runs, so it is never read.
Headings, links, lists, task check marks and tables keep the accessibility of MonarchAiMarkdown.
edgeCases: If the text is replaced rather than extended (regenerate), it is parsed again in full and the announcements start over.
A link whose target is still arriving shows its text without a link until the closing parenthesis arrives, so a half URL is never tappable.
A table header is held back until its delimiter row arrives, so pipes never flash as text.
A footnote definition arriving later turns earlier references into numbers; finished blocks are drawn again once when that happens.
Very long answers render every block: put the view in the message list, which scrolls.

name: MonarchAiStructuredAnswer
title: AiStructuredAnswer
wrapsNative: VStack of LabeledContent with MonarchLabeledContentStyle, Grid with GridRow and gridCellColumns for the grid layout, MonarchBadge in MonarchFlowLayout, MonarchAiMarkdown, MonarchAiGeneratedBadge and redacted(reason: .placeholder)
summary: A model's structured output shown as labelled fields (text, lists, numbers, badges or Markdown) instead of prose, filling in as it streams with placeholders for the fields still to come.
whenToUse: When the model returns structured data that follows a schema, such as an interview brief, a lead summary or fields extracted from a document, and people compare such answers.
whenNotToUse: For free-form answers use MonarchAiMarkdown or MonarchAiStreamingText. For many rows of the same shape use MonarchAiTableAnswer. For facts the app already knows, not generated, use LabeledContent with the Monarch style.
api: init(_ schema: [MonarchAiStructuredField], data: [String: MonarchAiJSON], title: String? = nil, layout: MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLayout = .list, isStreaming: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels = MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels(), onOpenLink: (@MainActor (URL) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)
init(_ schema:, data:, title:, layout:, isStreaming:, labels:, onOpenLink:)  // Actions == EmptyView

struct MonarchAiStructuredField { init(_ key: String, label: String, type: MonarchAiStructuredFieldType = .text, format: MonarchMetricFormat = .number, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, toneForValue: (@Sendable (String) -> MonarchTone)? = nil, isWide: Bool? = nil) }
enum MonarchAiStructuredFieldType { case text, list, number, badge, markdown }
enum MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLayout { case list, grid }
struct MonarchAiStructuredAnswerLabels { init(aiAnswer: String? = nil, pending: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, complete: String? = nil) }

options.name: schema
options.description: The fields in order: key, label, type, number format, badge tone and width. Values whose key is not in the schema are ignored.

options.name: data
options.description: The values by key, usually parsed from the model's structured output. Treated as untrusted.

options.name: title
options.description: A title under the AI answer label, such as Interview brief.

options.name: layout
options.description: .list: one field per row, the label beside a short value and above a long one. .grid: each field as a small card, two to a row, one to a row at accessibility text sizes; wide fields span the row.

options.name: isStreaming
options.description: The answer is still arriving: missing fields show placeholders read as Still generating.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces AI answer, Still generating, Not provided and Response complete.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens links of Markdown fields in the app.

options.name: actions
options.description: Views after the fields, such as a copy button or feedback buttons; they wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.type
options.description: text: plain text. list: an array as a bulleted list. number: written with format in the reader's locale. badge: one MonarchBadge per value. markdown: rendered by MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.format
options.description: How a number field is written: a number, a percentage of a ratio or a currency, as MonarchMetric writes it.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.tone / toneForValue
options.description: The tone of a badge field's badges, fixed or from each value.

options.name: MonarchAiStructuredField.isWide
options.description: Spans the full width; nil makes list and markdown fields wide.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every field shows its value; a field without one shows a dash read as Not provided.

states.name: streaming
states.description: Fields that have not arrived show a static placeholder bar read as Still generating, so the layout does not jump as they arrive.

states.name: streaming ended
states.description: Response complete. is announced once.

appearance: A card on the surface role with the default border and a large radius. The AI answer label is MonarchAiGeneratedBadge in the AI roles; the title is strong body text. Labels are muted captions, values default body text, empty values a dash in the subtle role, bullets muted. In the grid layout each field is a card on the subtle background with a subtle border. Every role follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web builds on DescriptionList; iOS uses LabeledContent with MonarchLabeledContentStyle, the iOS description list. The web's Intl.NumberFormat options become MonarchMetricFormat (number, percent, currency), the format MonarchMetric uses; numeric text such as 1,200 is read as a number and text ending in % stays as written. The web's grid layout uses responsive auto columns; on iPhone it is a SwiftUI Grid of two columns, one at accessibility text sizes. The web's shimmer placeholder is a static redacted placeholder here, so there is nothing to stop for Reduce Motion. The web's headingLevel and locale props are not offered: VoiceOver gives the title the header trait, and the locale comes from the environment. Values are MonarchAiJSON, the conversation model's JSON type. Android has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The AI answer label and the title are one element with the header trait, so the provenance is spoken with the title.
Each field is one element read as its label and then its value; list and badge items are read separated by commas.
A field still to come is read as Still generating, and an empty one as Not provided, not as a dash.
A Markdown field keeps its own elements, so its headings and links stay reachable.
Response complete. is announced once when streaming ends, never per field.
Badges carry their value as text, so their tone is never the only signal.
edgeCases: HTML in a value is shown as text; Markdown fields go through MonarchAiMarkdown, which never renders HTML.
Empty text, null and empty arrays count as missing; a single value in a list field is a one-item list.
Objects and arrays in a text field are shown as compact JSON.
An odd number of narrow fields in the grid leaves the last row half filled.
Long values wrap; nothing scrolls sideways.

name: MonarchAiSubagentTree
title: AiSubagentTree
wrapsNative: Recursive VStack of rows: a chevron Button that shows or hides sub-agents and a row Button that selects the agent, with MonarchAiAgentAvatar and MonarchStatusBadge for the status and MonarchButton actions
summary: A lead AI agent and the sub-agents it handed work to, as a tree with each agent's status, activity, progress and result, and actions for the selected agent.
whenToUse: Beside a conversation or in a run screen when one request fans out to several agents and people need to follow the run, answer an agent or stop one.
whenNotToUse: Not for the timing of model and tool calls in one run, which is MonarchAiTraceView or MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline. Not for one agent's plan, which is MonarchAiPlan.
api: init(_ agents: [MonarchAiSubagent], label: String? = nil, selection: Binding<String?>? = nil, expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, labels: MonarchAiSubagentTreeLabels = MonarchAiSubagentTreeLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchAiSubagent) -> Void)? = nil, onRespond: (@MainActor (MonarchAiSubagent) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchAiSubagent) -> Void)? = nil, onOpenPart: (@MainActor (MonarchAiSubagent) -> Void)? = nil, onStop: (@MainActor (MonarchAiSubagent) -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchAiSubagent.init(id: String, name: String, role: String? = nil, status: MonarchAiSubagentStatus, activity: String? = nil, stepsDone: Int? = nil, stepsTotal: Int? = nil, toolCalls: Int? = nil, startedAt: Date? = nil, endedAt: Date? = nil, summary: String? = nil, children: [MonarchAiSubagent] = [], partId: String? = nil, messageId: String? = nil)
enum MonarchAiSubagentStatus: String { case working, needsInput, waiting, done, failed, stopped }
MonarchAiSubagentTreeLabels.init(label:status:agentCount:statusCount:empty:steps:toolCalls:started:ran:actionsFor:stop:open:respond:openPart:announce:expand:collapse:)

options.name: agents
options.description: The top-level agents, usually one lead, each with the agents it handed work to, nested to any depth. Ids are unique across the tree.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Agents".

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected agent. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The ids of open agents. Kept inside when nil: active branches open at first, and a branch that becomes active opens once unless the person closed it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the count, step and time phrases.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs when the person selects an agent.

options.name: onRespond
options.description: Adds Respond for a selected agent that needs input.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Adds Open for the selected agent, for example to show its transcript.

options.name: onOpenPart
options.description: Adds Show in conversation for a selected agent with a partId or messageId.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Adds Stop for a selected agent that is waiting or working. The tree does not stop anything itself.

states.name: working
states.description: Info tone, circling arrows and "Working"; the activity line is shown.

states.name: needs input
states.description: Warning tone, a question mark and "Needs input"; Respond is offered when selected.

states.name: waiting
states.description: Neutral tone, a clock and "Waiting".

states.name: done, failed, stopped
states.description: Success, danger or neutral tone with a check, an octagon or a minus; the summary line is shown.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row takes the subtle AI fill and a bar in the strong AI role at its leading edge, and the action bar appears under the tree.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: The chevron points forward and the sub-agents are hidden.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no agents the header reads "No agents yet" and no tree is shown.

appearance: Rows on the page background with a small agent avatar whose ring follows the status, the name in default text, a small status badge in the status's tone, the role and facts in muted text and the activity and summary in default text. The selected row uses the subtle AI fill with a strong AI bar; the action bar sits on the subtle background. All colours are theme roles.
platformNotes: The web builds on TreeView with a tree role, arrow-key navigation and typeahead. iOS has no tree role; each agent is a button with the selected trait and a separate chevron button, which is what VoiceOver users navigate on iOS. The parity map named OutlineGroup, but OutlineGroup's rows toggle on tap and cannot select, so the rows are drawn as a recursive stack in the same way as MonarchGoalTree. Times are Dates formatted with the environment's locale and time zone; the web takes ISO strings and a timeZone prop. Callbacks receive the agent; the web passes the id and the agent.
accessibility: The tree is a container named "Agents" (or label).
Each row is a button read as name, status, role, activity (while working), steps, tool calls, times and summary (once ended).
The selected row has the selected trait and a visible bar, not only a fill.
The chevron is a separate 44-point button named "Show agents under <name>" or "Hide agents under <name>".
A status change after the tree appears is announced as "<name>: <status>"; a new agent that already needs input or failed is announced too; the first statuses are not.
The action bar is a container named "Actions for <name>"; its buttons are MonarchButton with 44-point targets.
Status icons are decorative; the status is always a word.
edgeCases: An unknown selection id shows no action bar.
Steps without a total read "3 steps"; one step and one tool call use the singular.
Long names, roles and activities wrap; nothing is cut.
Agents nested deeply are indented one step per level; very deep trees get narrow on a phone.

name: MonarchAiSuggestedActions
title: AiSuggestedActions
wrapsNative: VStack of rows with MonarchButton (Run, with isLoading), MonarchBadge tags and a ghost icon Button (dismiss), alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:) for approval, sensoryFeedback(.success/.error, trigger:) and AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: The next best actions for a record, each with Run, an optional approval step and dismiss, and where the suggestions came from.
whenToUse: On a record screen (a customer, a ticket, a deal) to offer a few next steps an AI model or product rules suggest, which the person runs with one tap.
whenNotToUse: For approving a tool call an agent wants to make, with its arguments, use MonarchAiToolApproval. For follow-up prompts in a chat use MonarchAiFollowUpSuggestions. For a fixed set of record actions use the toolbar or a Menu.
api: init(_ actions: [MonarchAiSuggestedAction], title: String? = nil, origin: MonarchAiSuggestedActionsOrigin = .ai, labels: MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels = MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels(), onDismiss: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onRun: @escaping @MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)

public struct MonarchAiSuggestedAction: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, requiresApproval: Bool = false, risk: MonarchAiToolCallRisk = .low, consequences: [String] = [], confirmLabel: String? = nil, status: MonarchAiSuggestedActionStatus? = nil); var needsApproval: Bool { get } }
public enum MonarchAiSuggestedActionStatus: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case ready, running, done, failed }
public enum MonarchAiSuggestedActionsOrigin: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case ai, rule }

MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels.init(originAi:originRule:run:runAction:running:done:failed:dismiss:needsApproval:risk:approvalTitle:approvalDescription:approve:cancel:doneAnnouncement:empty:), every string String? = nil and every function (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, risk (@Sendable (MonarchAiToolCallRisk) -> String?)? = nil

options.name: actions
options.description: The suggestions, most useful first: id, label, description, requiresApproval, risk, consequences, confirmLabel and an optional status.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading; "Suggested actions" without it.

options.name: origin
options.description: Where the suggestions came from, always shown: "Suggested by AI" in the assistant colour or "Rule-based" in the muted colour.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button to each action. Remove the action from actions.

options.name: onRun
options.description: Runs an action by id, after approval when it needs it. Running… while it runs, Done when it returns, Failed when it throws.

states.name: ready
states.description: Run is available.

states.name: running
states.description: Run shows a progress indicator, reads "Running…" and ignores taps.

states.name: done
states.description: Run is replaced by "Done" with a check mark in the strong success colour, the label turns muted, "“…” done." is announced and the success haptic plays.

states.name: failed
states.description: A line in the strong danger colour says "That didn’t work. Try again.", it is announced, the error haptic plays and Run is available again.

states.name: needs approval
states.description: A "Needs approval" tag with a lock; Run opens a system alert titled "Run “…”?" with the description (or the built-in text) and the consequences, a confirm button and Cancel.

states.name: risk
states.description: Medium and high show a warning tag, destructive a danger tag and a confirm button with the destructive role; low shows no tag.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No suggestions right now." under the heading.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers. Labels use the default text colour in the strong body style (muted once done), descriptions the muted caption style; tags are MonarchBadge in the neutral, warning and danger tones; the origin uses the strong assistant colour for AI and the muted text colour for rules; Run is the small secondary Monarch button. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web lays each action out as a row with Run and dismiss at the end; on a phone the buttons go under the text so long labels wrap at the largest text sizes, as on Android. The web's approval is its ConfirmDialog; iOS uses the system alert, which closes when a button is pressed, so a failed run shows its failure line on the row instead of inside the dialog (the web and Android keep the dialog open). The parity map names MonarchAiToolApproval as a dependency, but that component reviews an agent's tool call and its arguments, which a suggested action does not have, so it is not used. The parity map names a list of action rows; the rows are a VStack, not a List, because the list is short and sits on a scrolling record screen, where a List cannot be nested. The risk vocabulary is MonarchAiToolCallRisk, shared with the conversation model. onRun is async throws instead of a returned promise; description and consequences are strings. The origin and dismiss icons are fixed SF Symbols with spoken names, instead of Android's icon slots. The web moves focus to the Done text; on iOS VoiceOver hears the announcement and focus is not moved. The heading level is not offered: VoiceOver has the header trait only. Success and error haptics are added, as iOS apps do for a completed action. Experimental: a product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the origin is a label with text, not only a colour.
Each action's label, description and tags are read as one element.
Run is named "Run “…”" with the action's label; while running it shows a progress indicator and reads "Running…" (MonarchButton's loading state).
Dismiss is an icon button named "Dismiss “…”".
"“…” done." is announced after a run; the failure text is announced after a failed run.
Done and failed are text with a symbol, not only a colour.
Every button is at least 44 points; the approval is the system alert, which VoiceOver focuses.
edgeCases: A controlled status on an action wins over the status the list tracks.
Pressing Run while the action runs or after it is done does nothing.
An empty description falls back to the built-in approval text in the dialog.
Long labels and descriptions wrap; the buttons stay under them.
An empty list shows the empty text under the heading; the origin is still shown.

MonarchAiSuggestedActions(

        ),

            id: "task",

            risk: .medium
        ),
        MonarchAiSuggestedAction(
            id: "email",

            description: "Goes to 3 people.",

            confirmLabel: "Send email"

            id: "close",
            label: "Close 4 stale tickets",
            description: "No reply in 60 days.",
            risk: .destructive,
            consequences: ["4 tickets will be closed", "Requesters are notified"],
            confirmLabel: "Close tickets"
        ),
    ],
    onDismiss: { _ in },
    onRun: { _ in }
)

whenToUse: At the top of a record or a long page, to give a short model-written overview that people can refresh and check against its sources.
whenNotToUse: For an answer in a conversation use the assistant message with MonarchAiMarkdown. For one insight with an action use MonarchAiInsightCallout. For text a person wrote use MonarchCard.

struct MonarchAiSummaryCardLabels { init(aiSummary: String? = nil, refresh: String? = nil, generated: (@Sendable (_ time: String) -> String)? = nil, generating: String? = nil, updated: String? = nil, stale: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, sources: String? = nil) }

options.name: title
options.description: What is summarised, for example "Account summary". A header.

options.name: summary
options.description: The summary as Markdown, rendered by MonarchAiMarkdown as untrusted model output. Empty while there is none.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, generating (placeholder, or a busy Refresh when a summary exists), stale (a warning banner) or error (a danger banner and no body).

options.name: isRefreshing
options.description: A refresh is running: Refresh shows a spinner and the start and the end are announced.

options.name: generatedAt
options.description: When the summary was written. Shown as "Generated 3 hours ago"; VoiceOver reads the date and time.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for generatedAt. The current time when nil.

options.name: sources
options.description: The documents or records the summary was written from, listed by MonarchAiSourceList under "Sources".

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: A detail shown under the error title when status is error.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces every built-in string.

options.name: onRefresh
options.description: Adds Refresh, which asks for a new summary.

options.name: onOpenSource
options.description: Opens a source, for example in a preview sheet; without it MonarchAiSourceList opens a safe URL through the system.

options.name: onOpenLink
options.description: Opens a link in the summary in the app; passed to MonarchAiMarkdown.

options.name: actions
options.description: More buttons in the footer, after the age.

states.name: ready
states.description: The summary, its sources and its age.

states.name: generating
states.description: Without a summary: "Generating summary…" and three redacted placeholder lines. With one: the summary stays and Refresh shows a spinner.

states.name: stale
states.description: A warning banner above the summary asks for a refresh.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger banner with "The summary couldn’t be generated." and the detail; the body is empty.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No summary yet." in muted text.

appearance: The card surface with its border and shadow; the AI generated badge in the AI colours; the title in the default text colour with the subheading type; the age, the empty text and the generating text muted. Banners use the warning and danger tones. Every role resolves to its own value in the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A product pattern, experimental until a Rook app adopts it, built only from Monarch parts. It is plain public API with status experimental, like the other experimental iOS entries, not @_spi(Experimental), because the compiled examples import MonarchUI without SPI. The web marks the summary with a bot glyph and an eyebrow; iOS uses MonarchAiGeneratedBadge labelled "AI summary". The web's heading levels are not offered; the title has the header trait. The web dims the previous summary while refreshing; iOS keeps it and shows the spinner on Refresh with an announcement. The web's sources are a plain list of links; iOS reuses MonarchAiSourceList (numbered, collapsible). The age comes from RelativeDateTimeFormatter in the environment's locale and is not updated live: render again with a new now. The header stacks Refresh under the title when they do not fit side by side. Android uses the same names, with refreshing, error and Long times as isRefreshing, errorMessage and Date.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the "AI summary" badge is read before it, so the summary is never presented as human-written.
Refresh is a button that shows a spinner and the generating text as its loading label while busy.
"Generating summary…" is announced when work starts and "Summary updated." when it ends; nothing is announced when the card first appears or after an error.
The age is read as the full date and time instead of the relative text.
The redacted placeholder lines are hidden from VoiceOver; the generating text is read instead.
Stale and error notices are MonarchBanner, with an icon and a tone name, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A summary of only white space counts as none.
An error without a detail shows the error title as the banner message.
A long title wraps; at large text sizes Refresh moves under the title.
Without generatedAt and actions there is no footer.

options.name: isCopyable

states.name: unsorted
states.description: Rows in the order the model gave; every header shows a neutral up and down chevron.

states.name: sorted
states.description: The active header shows an up or down chevron and reads Sorted ascending or Sorted descending. Blanks stay last.

states.name: streaming
states.description: A placeholder bar row under the rows; Open as artifact is disabled.

states.name: empty

appearance: The AI table label and bot glyph in the AI strong role, the title in default text, the row count in muted text. The table sits on the surface with a subtle border and rules between rows; headers are muted, cells default text, empty cells a dash in the subtle text role. Numbers use tabular digits.
platformNotes: The web renders an HTML table with aria-sort; SwiftUI has no table semantics on iOS 17, so headers are buttons with the header trait and the sort as their value, and each row is read as one element of header and value pairs. Rows are dictionaries of MonarchAiJSON, which have no key order, so inferred columns are alphabetical; pass columns for the model's order. The web's per-column render closure is not offered; cells are text. Dates in the data are ISO strings and are shown as given, not reformatted. Long cells stay on one line and the table scrolls sideways. Copy as CSV uses MonarchCopyButton, which writes to the general pasteboard.
accessibility: The AI table label, title and row count are one header element.
Each sortable header is a button with the header trait, read as its name with Sorted ascending or Sorted descending as its value, at least 44 points high.
A sort is announced, for example "Sorted by Revenue, ascending.".
Each row is one element read as "Region: North, Revenue: 1,200"; an empty cell is read as Empty.
The streaming placeholder is read as "More rows are being generated", and the end of streaming is announced as "Table complete.".
The sort chevrons are decorative; the direction is the spoken value.
edgeCases: Text a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, +, -, @) is prefixed with ' in the CSV; numbers such as -3 are kept.
Numeric text such as "1,200", "12%" and "−3" sorts by value; mixed columns are text.
A date or time without a zone is read as UTC for sorting.
JSON numbers in a number column are formatted for the locale; numeric text is shown as given.
Arrays and objects in a cell are shown as compact JSON.
The CSV is built on every render while copyable; very large tables should set isCopyable false and offer an export.

name: MonarchAiTaskProgress
title: AiTaskProgress
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with ProgressView (.progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear)), MonarchBadge, MonarchAiChainOfSteps, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton(.ghost, size: .sm)), MonarchButton, RelativeDateTimeFormatter in a TimelineView(.everyMinute)
summary: A long-running assistant task in a card, with its status, a progress bar, when it started and how long is left, its steps, and controls to cancel, minimize or be notified.
whenToUse: For agent work that takes minutes, such as summarising many documents or an export, so the person can follow it, leave it, or stop it.
whenNotToUse: Not for a short wait inside a reply (use MonarchAiThinkingIndicator) and not for steps the person approves first (use MonarchAiPlan).
api: init(_ title: String, status: MonarchAiTaskStatus, startedAt: Date, steps: [MonarchAiPlanStep] = [], progress: Double? = nil, eta: TimeInterval? = nil, isNotifying: Binding<Bool>? = nil, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchAiTaskProgressLabels = MonarchAiTaskProgressLabels(), onMinimize: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onCancel: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiTaskStatus: String { case running, paused, done, failed, cancelled }

struct MonarchAiTaskProgressLabels { init(status: ((MonarchAiTaskStatus) -> String)? = nil, progressLabel: ((String) -> String)? = nil, progressValue: ((Int) -> String)? = nil, started: ((String) -> String)? = nil, eta: ((TimeInterval) -> String)? = nil, cancel: String? = nil, minimize: String? = nil, notify: String? = nil, announce: ((String, String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: title
options.description: What the task is, such as "Summarising 40 documents". Names the card.

options.name: status
options.description: running, paused, done, failed or cancelled. Changes are announced.

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the task started, shown as "Started 5 minutes ago".

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, shown as a MonarchAiChainOfSteps. A task may have only a bar.

options.name: progress
options.description: Completion from 0 to 1. By default the share of finished (done, failed or skipped) steps; with no steps the bar is indeterminate while running.

options.name: eta
options.description: Estimated seconds left, shown while running.

options.name: isNotifying
options.description: Whether "Notify me when done" is on. The toggle is shown while running or paused when given.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for the start text, for previews, tests and identical renders. The current minute, updated every minute, when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onMinimize
options.description: Shows a Minimize icon button, for example to dock the task in a tray.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Shows a Cancel button while the task runs or is paused.

states.name: running
states.description: Info badge with a circular-arrows icon; the bar fills, or is indeterminate without progress; the time left is shown; Notify and Cancel are offered.

states.name: paused
states.description: Warning badge with a pause icon; no time left; Notify and Cancel are still offered.

states.name: done
states.description: Success badge with a check; the bar is full; no controls but Minimize.

states.name: failed
states.description: Danger badge with an octagon; the failure is announced with high priority.

states.name: cancelled
states.description: Neutral badge with a slashed circle; no controls but Minimize.

appearance: A Monarch card: the title in the subheading style and default text role, the meta line in the muted text role, the Monarch linear progress bar, and the status as a subtle Monarch badge in its tone. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web colours the bar by status (accent while running); the Monarch linear progress style has one accent fill, so on iOS the status is carried by the badge. MonarchTone has no accent case, so the running badge uses the info tone. The web's etaMs is eta in seconds; startedAt is a Date, not an ISO string or epoch. The web's children slot and stepsProps are not offered: put extra content after the card, and pass ready steps. The web announces through live regions; iOS posts accessibility announcements, with high priority for a failure.
accessibility: The card is a container named by the title; the title has the header trait.
The status is a badge with an icon and its name, never colour alone.
The progress bar is named "<title> progress" with "40% complete" as its value, or the status name when indeterminate.
A status change is announced as "<title>: <status>"; a failure is announced with high priority; the first status is not announced.
The steps announce their own starts and failures (MonarchAiChainOfSteps).
The minimize button is an icon button named "Minimize"; the notify control is a standard Toggle in the Monarch toggle-button style, so it reads its on or off state.
Every control has a 44-point touch target; the controls stack when they do not fit.
edgeCases: Progress outside 0 to 1 is limited; NaN is ignored.
Without now, the start text updates every minute.
Estimates under a minute read "Less than a minute left"; an hour or more reads in hours to one decimal.
Long titles wrap at every text size.

whenToUse: After a message is sent and before the reply streams its first token, or while a named tool or retrieval step runs ("Searching your files…").
whenNotToUse: Once text streams, show the text. In a dock or row with no room for a label, use MonarchAiTypingDots. For loading that is not the assistant, use the standard ProgressView (see spinner).

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Thinking…", for example "Searching your files…".

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the assistant started working. The moment the indicator first appeared when nil. Pass it when the view can be rebuilt during one turn.

states.name: long wait
states.description: After showsElapsedAfter seconds the elapsed time follows the label and updates every second.

states.name: Reduce Motion

appearance: The label is muted text; the shimmer band and the mark use the assistant (ai) strong colour; the elapsed time is subtle text with tabular figures. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web shimmers a band of the thinking tint behind the label; iOS sweeps the assistant colour through the label's own text, which keeps contrast in every theme. The web announces through a hidden live region; iOS posts an announcement. Android uses the same names. The parity map named ai-typing-dots as the mark; the web component uses the assistant bot mark, so iOS reuses MonarchAiBotGlyph (from ai-generated-badge) and leaves the dots to MonarchAiTypingDots for places without a label.
accessibility: One element read as the label, with the elapsed time as its value and the updates-frequently trait.
The label is announced when the indicator appears and again when the label changes; the elapsed time is never announced.
The mark is decorative and hidden.
Under Reduce Motion the shimmer and the pulse stop.
The label wraps at large text sizes; nothing has a fixed height.
edgeCases: A startedAt in the future counts as 0 seconds.
The clock restarts if the view is recreated without startedAt.
Long labels wrap and the elapsed time stays after them on the same baseline where it fits.

whenNotToUse: For person-to-person chat use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For one answer without a conversation use MonarchAiMessage or MonarchAiStructuredAnswer on their own.

public struct MonarchAiThreadMessageContext: Sendable, Hashable { public let index: Int; public let isLast: Bool; public let announces: Bool; public init(index: Int, isLast: Bool, announces: Bool) }

public struct MonarchAiThreadLabels: Sendable { public init(label: String? = nil, jumpToLatest: String? = nil, newMessages: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, loadEarlier: String? = nil, loadingEarlier: String? = nil, thinking: String? = nil, responseComplete: String? = nil, responseStopped: String? = nil, error: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, codeBlock: String? = nil, table: String? = nil, today: String? = nil, yesterday: String? = nil, offline: String? = nil, offlineQueued: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, sendingQueued: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, slow: String? = nil, stop: String? = nil) }

options.name: messages
options.description: The visible conversation, oldest first: MonarchAiConversation.messages. Ids must be unique and stable: they are the row identities.

options.name: status
options.description: submitted shows the thinking indicator; submitted and streaming let Escape and the Magic Tap call onStop; stopped ends the announcement with "Response stopped".

options.name: error
options.description: Announced with high priority as "Error: <message>" when the newest message has no error part of its own. Nothing is drawn for it.

options.name: isOffline
options.description: Shows the offline notice under the messages.

options.name: queuedCount
options.description: How many messages wait for the connection: named in the offline notice, and once online shows "Back online. Sending N queued messages…".

options.name: isSlow
options.description: Shows "This is taking longer than usual. Still working…" while a reply is submitted or streaming.

options.name: hasEarlier
options.description: Older messages exist. With onLoadEarlier, "Load earlier messages" (MonarchLoadMore) is the top row.

options.name: isLoadingEarlier
options.description: The load row shows progress and "Loading earlier messages…".

options.name: showsDaySeparators
options.description: A MonarchAiContextDivider day label above the first message of each calendar day.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for Today and Yesterday. nil reads the clock.

options.name: announces
options.description: The thread announces for the whole conversation and tells each message not to; false lets each message announce itself.

options.name: announceInterval
options.description: The least time between two announcements while a reply streams.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Called by the Escape key and the VoiceOver Magic Tap while a reply is submitted or streaming.

options.name: onLoadEarlier
options.description: Loads older messages; prepend them to messages.

options.name: empty
options.description: Shown instead of the list when there are no messages, nothing to load and no submitted reply, for example a MonarchAiWelcome.

options.name: message
options.description: Draws one message, given its index, whether it is the newest and whether it should announce itself.

states.name: pinned
states.description: While the invisible row under the newest message is on screen, a new message scrolls into view (animated unless Reduce Motion is on) and a growing reply, a new indicator or a notice keeps the bottom in view.

states.name: scrolled up
states.description: New messages do not scroll the view; a small secondary "Jump to latest" button over the bottom trailing corner counts them ("2 new messages") and scrolls back.

states.name: submitted
states.description: A MonarchAiThinkingIndicator is the bottom row, and "Thinking…" is announced once.

states.name: streaming
states.description: The reply is read out in whole sentences, then "Response complete" or "Response stopped" when it ends.

states.name: earlier
states.description: "Load earlier messages" (MonarchLoadMore) is the top row; while loading it shows progress.

states.name: offline / sending / slow
states.description: One MonarchInlineNotice under the list, offline first: warning tone with a no-connection or upload symbol for the connection, neutral with a clock for a slow reply.

states.name: error
states.description: An error no message shows is announced with high priority; nothing is drawn for it.

states.name: empty
states.description: The empty content replaces the list.

appearance: The thread has no surface of its own: it shows on the screen's background. Messages, day labels, the thinking indicator and the load row keep their own roles; the notice uses the warning or neutral tone of MonarchInlineNotice, and the jump button is a small secondary MonarchButton. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web renders a scrolling div with role=log, measures rows and windows them itself after 200 messages (virtualizeAfter, keepLast, estimatedMessageHeight). On iOS the LazyVStack builds only the rows near the screen, so those parameters do not exist; .defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom) opens on the newest message and ScrollViewReader follows new rows while the bottom is on screen, the same approach as MonarchVirtualMessageList. Android uses a reversed LazyColumn; the parameters match Android's in Swift form: offline, slow and loadingEarlier are isOffline, isSlow and isLoadingEarlier, daySeparators is showsDaySeparators, announceIntervalMillis is a Duration, and nowMillis is a Date. Android's timeZone parameter and the web's locale and timeZone are the SwiftUI environment here (\.timeZone, \.calendar, \.locale), which MonarchAiContextDivider and MonarchAiMessage already read. Android's contentPadding and LazyListState are not offered: the thread pads its rows by the space-4 token, an app adds margins with .contentMargins, and scrolling is the system's. The web's renderMessage and messageProps are the message closure; pass MonarchAiMessage's parameters there. Android's jumpIcon is not needed: the jump button uses the arrow.down SF Symbol. The web's Escape key is .onKeyPress(.escape) for hardware keyboards, and the VoiceOver Magic Tap is added on iOS for the same stop. The announcer names code blocks and tables ("Code block", "Table") as the web does, through MonarchAiStreamingText's speech rules. The web draws warning and clock glyphs in the notice; iOS uses SF Symbols through MonarchInlineNotice. The composer is not part of the thread on any platform. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The list is a VoiceOver container named "Conversation" (labels.label).
Day labels are MonarchAiContextDividers, read as one element: "Today", "Yesterday" or the date.

With announces, the thread posts one stream of announcements: "Thinking…" when a reply is submitted, a reply that arrives while the thread is shown in whole sentences at most once per announceInterval, then "Response complete" or "Response stopped"; replies that were already finished are not read.
The messages get announces == false from the context, so streamed text is not read token by token.
A conversation error that no message shows is announced with the high announcement priority.
The offline, sending and slow notices are announced when their text changes.
"Jump to latest" and "Load earlier messages" are standard buttons of at least 44 points; the jump button is named "Jump to latest, 2 new messages" when messages arrived.
The Magic Tap (two-finger double tap) and the Escape key call onStop while a reply is submitted or streaming.
Jumping scrolls without animation when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: Give the thread a bounded height; it cannot sit in a vertically scrolling parent.
Message ids must be unique and stable: they are the row identities and the scroll targets.
A message whose createdAt is not an ISO 8601 time gets no day label, and the next message starts a new day, as on the web.
Without onLoadEarlier, hasEarlier shows nothing.
The empty content shows only when there are no messages, nothing to load and no submitted reply.
Offline wins over the sending and slow notices; slow shows only while a reply is running.
Whether prepending older messages keeps the visible rows still depends on SwiftUI's bottom anchoring of the scroll view, as for MonarchVirtualMessageList; it has not been checked on a device.

whenToUse: In assistant settings or a compose screen where the person picks how generated text should read. Use the compact variant in toolbars and dense forms.
whenNotToUse: For any other single choice use the standard Picker (see radio-group). Inside a Form or List where plain rows are expected, a Picker with the inline style fits better.

static var MonarchAiTone.defaults: [MonarchAiTone]
static let MonarchAiTone.customID: String
enum MonarchAiTonePickerVariant { case cards, compact }

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected tone, or MonarchAiTone.customID for the Custom option.

options.name: customText

options.name: tones
options.description: The tones to offer, each with an id, a label and a one-line detail.

options.name: variant
options.description: cards: one row per tone with its description. compact: a menu Picker.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the choice, "Tone".

options.name: customLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the Custom option.

options.name: customDetail
options.description: Replaces the built-in description of the Custom option.

options.name: customFieldLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in label of the custom text field.

options.name: customPrompt
options.description: Replaces the built-in placeholder of the custom text field.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row has the assistant subtle fill, a 2-point assistant border and a filled radio mark.

states.name: not selected
states.description: A surface row with a 1-point border and an empty radio mark.

states.name: custom selected
states.description: A MonarchTextField for the custom tone appears under the options.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Rows use the disabled text role and do not respond, with the standard disabled(_:) modifier. The selected row keeps a stronger border and the filled mark.

states.name: compact
states.description: A label and the system menu picker on one line.

appearance: Rows sit on the surface colour with the default border. The selected row uses the assistant (ai) subtle fill, border and strong mark colour in every theme; the high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The web lays the cards out in a grid of columns at least 176px wide; on iOS they are one column, which holds at every text size. The web's compact variant is a native select, here the system menu Picker. The web's uncontrolled custom text (defaultCustomText) is not offered: pass a binding. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: In cards each row is a button read as the tone name, with the description as its hint and the selected trait on the current tone.
The selected row is also marked by a filled radio symbol and a thicker border, not by colour alone.
The rows are one container labelled with the name of the choice; the visible legend is not read twice.
Every row is at least 44 points high, and its text wraps at large text sizes.
The compact variant is the system Picker, labelled with the name of the choice.
The custom field is a MonarchTextField with its own label.
The selection change is not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no tone shows no row as selected.
A tone whose id is "custom" is dropped while the Custom option is shown, so ids stay unique.
A tone with an empty detail shows only its label.
The custom text is kept when another tone is selected; the app decides whether to use it.

name: MonarchAiToolApproval
title: AiToolApproval
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with a VStack of Text, MonarchBadge for the risk, MonarchFormField around a vertical TextField for the JSON and the reason, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) for Always allow, and Buttons with .buttonStyle(.monarch(…)) in a MonarchFlowLayout; @AccessibilityFocusState for the first focus
summary: The approval card for a tool call the assistant wants to run: what it will do, its arguments as readable pairs, the risk, and Approve and Deny, with editable arguments, an optional reason and an optional Always allow.
whenToUse: In an assistant conversation, for each tool-call part in the pending-approval state, before the app runs the tool.
whenNotToUse: After the decision, to show what ran, use MonarchAiToolCall. To grant an assistant standing permissions use MonarchAiPermissionScope. For a confirmation that is not about a tool call use a confirmationDialog.
api: init(_ part: MonarchAiToolCallPart, summary: String? = nil, consequence: String? = nil, risk: MonarchAiToolCallRisk? = nil, toolLabels: [String: String] = [:], argumentLabels: [String: String] = [:], argumentOrder: [String] = [], isEditable: Bool = true, focusesOnAppear: Bool = false, labels: MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels = MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels(), onAlwaysAllow: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onDeny: @escaping @MainActor (String?) -> Void, onApprove: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchAiJSON?) -> Void)

MonarchAiToolApprovalLabels.init(eyebrow:risk:consequence:arguments:noArguments:approve:deny:editArguments:discardEdits:argumentsJSON:invalidJSON:addReason:reason:alwaysAllow:approved:denied:cancelled:announce:), every parameter optional

options.name: part
options.description: The tool call waiting for a decision (state .pendingApproval). A new id starts the card over.

options.name: summary
options.description: The title in plain words, such as "Delete 12 records". The tool's label by default.

options.name: consequence
options.description: What happens if this is approved. Destructive calls say "This can’t be undone once it runs." by default.

options.name: risk
options.description: How much harm approving can do: low, medium, high or destructive. The call's own risk, else medium.

options.name: toolLabels
options.description: Display names by tool name. Unlisted tools get a humanized name.

options.name: argumentLabels
options.description: Labels for argument keys, such as ["to": "Recipients"]. Unlisted keys are humanized.

options.name: isEditable
options.description: Offers Edit arguments, a JSON editor.

options.name: focusesOnAppear
options.description: Moves VoiceOver focus to Deny (high and destructive) or Approve when the card appears.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the risk names, the consequence and the announcement.

options.name: onAlwaysAllow
options.description: Shows "Always allow this tool". When ticked, called with the tool name just before onApprove. Never offered for destructive calls.

options.name: onDeny
options.description: Called when the person denies, with the trimmed reason, or nil.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Called when the person approves, with the edited input, or nil when the arguments were not changed.

states.name: pending
states.description: The header (warning icon, "Approval needed", title, risk badge), the arguments and the buttons.

states.name: low, medium, high
states.description: Neutral, warning and warning badge tones; Approve is the primary button.

states.name: destructive
states.description: Danger tone, the consequence line, no Always allow, and Approve is the danger button.

states.name: editing
states.description: A JSON editor with the pretty-printed input; Edit arguments becomes Discard edits.

states.name: invalid JSON
states.description: Approve does nothing and "Fix the JSON before approving." shows under the editor with an icon.

states.name: reason
states.description: Add a reason opens a reason field; its text is passed to onDeny.

states.name: approved, denied, cancelled
states.description: The buttons give way to the outcome with a check, a cross or a minus, also when the call's state is no longer pending.

states.name: no arguments
states.description: "No arguments." in muted text.

appearance: A Monarch card on the surface colour with an extra-small elevation. The header icon and consequence use the strong warning or danger roles by risk, the eyebrow and keys are muted text, the risk is a subtle badge in its tone, and the outcome uses the strong success or danger role or muted text. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web renders a group with a description list and an assertive live region; iOS uses a MonarchCard, a VStack of label and value pairs (sorted by key, because MonarchAiJSON objects have no order) and an AccessibilityNotification announcement. The web's focusOnMount moves keyboard focus; iOS's focusesOnAppear moves VoiceOver focus. The web's describe returns any content; iOS takes a summary String. The JSON editor is a vertical TextField that reuses the action editor's bordered field until a shared multi-line field exists. The web keeps the card focusable after the decision; on iOS the outcome line is a plain element. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The header is one element read as "Approval needed", the title and the risk, with the header trait.
"Approval needed: <title>" is announced when a pending card appears.
With focusesOnAppear, VoiceOver focus moves to Deny for high and destructive calls and to Approve otherwise.
Each argument is one element read as its label and value.
The JSON and reason fields are labelled through MonarchFormField; the JSON error is text with an icon and is announced.
The risk and the outcome are words with icons, not only colours.
Every button and the checkbox are at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A string input that is not an object is shown as code; a nested value is shown as pretty JSON.
Approving with the editor open but unchanged passes nil, like the web.
A part whose state is not pendingApproval shows its outcome at once and is not announced.
Long titles and values wrap; the buttons wrap onto more rows at large text sizes.

name: MonarchAiToolCall
title: AiToolCall
wrapsNative: DisclosureGroup(isExpanded:content:label:) with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch), MonarchStatusBadge for the state and MonarchAiCodeBlock for the input and output
summary: One tool call of an assistant turn as a card that opens: what was done in plain words, the state as an icon and a word, how long it took and, on demand, the exact input and output.
whenToUse: For each tool-call part of an assistant message, when people should see what the assistant did; and in audit or debugging views where the raw arguments and results must be inspectable.
whenNotToUse: Not while the call waits for a decision: show an approval (MonarchAiPermissionScope or the app's approval card) instead. Not to show the result as a thing, such as a created record, which is MonarchAiToolResultCard.
api: init(_ part: MonarchAiToolCallPart, summary: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, toolLabels: [String: String] = [:], isExpanded: Binding<Bool>? = nil, announcesChanges: Bool = true, maxValueLength: Int = 4000, labels: MonarchAiToolCallLabels = MonarchAiToolCallLabels(), describeTool: (@MainActor (MonarchAiToolCallPart) -> String?)? = nil)
MonarchAiToolCallLabels.init(state:formatDuration:input:output:error:tool:empty:stateChanged:showMore:truncated:)

options.name: part
options.description: The call from the conversation model: name, input, state, output, error, start and end times, streamed input text.

options.name: summary
options.description: The one-line summary in words. Wins over describeTool.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the wrench symbol before the title. Decorative.

options.name: toolLabels
options.description: Display names by tool name. Unlisted tools get a humanized name.

options.name: isExpanded
options.description: Whether the details are open. Kept inside, closed at first, when nil.

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: Whether a change of state is announced. Turn it off when the thread already announces it.

options.name: maxValueLength
options.description: The longest input or output shown before Show all, in characters. 0 shows everything.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the state names, the duration format, the headings, the empty and truncation notes, the announcement and Show all.

options.name: describeTool
options.description: Builds the summary from the call. Return nil to fall back to the tool's label.

states.name: pending approval
states.description: Warning tone, a triangle and "Waiting for approval".

states.name: awaiting result
states.description: Neutral tone, a clock and "Waiting for result".

states.name: running
states.description: Info tone, circling arrows and "Running". No duration until it ends.

states.name: succeeded
states.description: Success tone, a check mark, "Done" and the duration.

states.name: failed
states.description: Danger tone, an octagon, "Failed", and the error under the card without opening it.

states.name: denied
states.description: Neutral tone, a crossed circle and "Denied".

states.name: cancelled
states.description: Neutral tone, a minus and "Cancelled".

states.name: expanded
states.description: The tool's name, the input and the output in code blocks, or "No details yet.".

states.name: truncated
states.description: A value longer than maxValueLength is cut at a line end with "Showing 4,000 of 52,113 characters" and a Show all button.

appearance: A card on the subtle background with the subtle border; the tool icon uses the AI tool role, the state is a small status badge in its tone, the duration and notes are muted text and the error is the strong danger role. Every colour is a theme role, so it follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web uses <details>/<summary>; iOS uses the standard DisclosureGroup in the Monarch style, so the header is a button with an expanded or collapsed value. The running state shows a symbol instead of the web's spinner. Values are MonarchAiJSON, pretty-printed with sorted keys; the web keeps the key order of the object. The web renders input and output only while open; SwiftUI also builds the content only when the group is open. The summary is a String, not arbitrary content.
accessibility: The summary row is one button read as the title, the state and the duration, with the value Expanded or Collapsed.
State icons are decorative; the state is always a word as well as a tone.
A change of state after the card appears is announced as "<tool>: <state>"; the first state is not announced, and announcesChanges turns announcements off.
The error line is read as "Error: message".
The input and output blocks are named Input and Output through MonarchAiCodeBlock, with a Copy button.
The header and Show all are at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: A call without input and output shows "No details yet." when open.
While arguments stream, inputText stands in for an empty input.
A string that holds JSON is re-indented; text that only starts with a brace is shown as it is.
Times that cannot be read, or an end before the start, show no duration.
A long title wraps; the state badge and duration move under it.

examples.title: Humanized summary with details
examples.template:
MonarchAiToolCall(
    MonarchAiToolCallPart(
        id: {{id}},
        name: {{name}},

Without url and onUndo there is no action row.
Long titles and descriptions wrap.
The undo state lives in the view; give the card a new id to show a new result in the same place.

name: MonarchAiTraceView

summary: The technical trace of one agent run: every model call, tool call, retrieval and sub-agent as a row in a tree with its duration, tokens, cost and a bar on a shared time scale, and its details in a sheet.
whenToUse: In developer, audit or support screens where someone needs to see exactly what one agent run did, how long each step took, what it cost and where it failed.
whenNotToUse: Not for people using the assistant, who need the plain-language story of the run: use MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline or MonarchAiChainOfSteps. Not for agents handing work to each other, which is MonarchAiSubagentTree.
api: init(_ spans: [MonarchAiTraceSpan], currency: String = "USD", now: TimeInterval? = nil, selection: Binding<String?>? = nil, filter: Binding<MonarchAiTraceFilter>? = nil, expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, labels: MonarchAiTraceViewLabels = MonarchAiTraceViewLabels(), onOpenPart: (@MainActor (MonarchAiTraceSpan) -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchAiTraceSpan.init(id: String, parentId: String? = nil, kind: MonarchAiTraceSpanKind, name: String, status: MonarchAiTraceSpanStatus, start: TimeInterval, end: TimeInterval? = nil, inputTokens: Int? = nil, outputTokens: Int? = nil, costMicros: Int? = nil, currency: String? = nil, model: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, attributes: [String: String] = [:], input: String? = nil, output: String? = nil, partId: String? = nil, messageId: String? = nil)
enum MonarchAiTraceSpanKind: String { case model, tool, retrieval, agent, guardrail, other }
enum MonarchAiTraceSpanStatus: String { case ok, error, cancelled, running }
enum MonarchAiTraceFilter: String { case all, errors, slowest }

MonarchAiTraceViewLabels.init(label:filterLabel:filter:kind:status:totalDuration:totalTokens:totalCost:errors:notAvailable:empty:noErrors:formatDuration:timing:closeDetails:openPart:start:end:duration:inputTokens:outputTokens:model:statusName:kindName:error:attributes:input:output:expand:collapse:)

options.name: spans
options.description: The spans of one run in any order; children are found through parentId and shown in start order. Times are seconds from the start of the run.

options.name: currency
options.description: The ISO 4217 currency of spans that do not name one.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time in seconds from the run start, where the bars of running spans end. Without it they end at the latest known time, so rendering is deterministic.

options.name: selection
options.description: The span whose details are open in the sheet. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: filter
options.description: All spans, failed spans with their parents, or siblings slowest first. Kept inside, starting at all, when nil.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The open spans. Kept inside when nil: top-level spans, failed spans and their parents start open.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, the duration format and the spoken timing.

options.name: onOpenPart
options.description: Adds Show in conversation to the details of a span with a partId or messageId.

states.name: ok
states.description: The bar takes the colour of the kind: model, tool, retrieval, agent, guardrail or other.

states.name: error
states.description: An error icon, the word Error in the strong danger role, a danger bar; the span and its parents start open.

states.name: running
states.description: The word Running instead of a duration and an AI thinking bar that ends at now.

states.name: cancelled
states.description: The word Cancelled and a strong border coloured bar.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row takes the subtle AI fill and a strong AI bar at its leading edge, and the details open in a sheet.

states.name: filtered
states.description: Errors only shows failed spans and their parents, or "No errors in this run"; Slowest first sorts siblings by duration.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No spans recorded".

appearance: Rows on the page background with the name in default text, facts in muted text and a bar on the subtle track; bar colours come from the AI, info, accent, warning and danger roles. The totals use the Monarch labelled-content style. Every colour is a theme role, so it follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a six-column tree grid with arrow-key navigation, typeahead-free windowing and an inline details panel. A phone cannot fit six columns, so each row shows the name with a facts line and the bar under it, and the details open in a sheet with a NavigationStack, as the plan describes. The parity map named OutlineGroup; its rows toggle on tap and cannot select, so the rows are a LazyVStack with separate chevron and row buttons. LazyVStack replaces the web's manual windowing. Times are seconds (TimeInterval) rather than milliseconds, and attributes are strings. Durations and costs use the same formatting as MonarchAiAgentRunTimeline.
accessibility: The trace is a container named "Run trace", and the title has the header trait.
Each row is a button read as name, status unless OK or running, kind, duration or Running, tokens, cost and "Starts at +1.2 s, takes 850 ms".
The selected row has the selected trait and a visible bar, not only a fill.
Spans with children have a separate 44-point chevron button, "Show spans inside <name>".
Failures have an icon and the word Error, not colour alone; bars are hidden from VoiceOver because the timing is in the row's label.
The filter is a standard segmented Picker named "Show".
The details are a sheet with a Close button, labelled facts, and input and output in MonarchAiCodeBlock with Copy.
edgeCases: A span whose parent is missing, itself, or in a loop is shown at the top level; a repeated id keeps the first span.
Token and cost totals add every span, so a parent should carry only its own usage.
Costs in several currencies are listed per currency, joined with +.
A trace of zero length still draws bars, at least the minimum width.
A very deep tree is indented one step per level and gets narrow on a phone.

name: MonarchAiTypingDots
title: AiTypingDots
wrapsNative: TimelineView(.animation) drawing Circle shapes; AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Three dots that rise and brighten in turn to show the assistant is writing, for places with no room for a label.
whenToUse: In a chat dock, a conversation row or a small message bubble that waits for the first words of a reply.
whenNotToUse: Where there is room for text, say what is happening in words. For a wait that is not the assistant writing, use the standard ProgressView (see spinner).
api: MonarchAiTypingDots.init(label: String? = nil, size: MonarchAiTypingDotsSize = .md, isAnnounced: Bool = true)
enum MonarchAiTypingDotsSize { case sm, md }

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken label "Assistant is typing".

options.name: size
options.description: sm: 4-point dots for docks and dense rows. md: 6-point dots for a message bubble.

options.name: isAnnounced
options.description: Whether the label is announced when the dots appear. Pass false when something else already announces the state.

states.name: animating
states.description: Each dot rises by 0.6 of its size and goes from 40% to full opacity, one after another, in a 1.2-second cycle.

states.name: Reduce Motion
states.description: The dots are still, at 70% opacity.

appearance: The dots use the assistant (ai) strong colour role in every theme, which the high-contrast themes resolve to a stronger colour.
platformNotes: The timing follows the web: a cycle of 0.75 of the shimmer duration and 0.125 of it between dots. The web eases between keyframes with its standard curve; iOS uses a smooth step, so the motion is close but not identical. The web also stops the animation in forced-colours mode, which iOS does not have; the high-contrast themes keep the animation.
accessibility: The dots are one element whose label is the label parameter or "Assistant is typing".
When the dots appear and isAnnounced is true, the label is posted as a VoiceOver announcement.
With Reduce Motion on the dots do not move or change opacity.
The dots scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: The announcement is posted every time the view appears, so remove and insert it once per reply, not per token.
A rising dot draws slightly above the view's bounds, as on the web; leave the default spacing around it.

name: MonarchAiUndoBanner
title: AiUndoBanner

summary: An inline banner after the AI changed something on the person's behalf: what changed, before and after, an Undo and a link to the audit log, optionally for a limited time.
whenToUse: On the screen the AI changed, right after it applied the change, so the person can review and revert it.
whenNotToUse: Not for a change that is only proposed: show the proposal with accept and reject. For a short timed message that floats over the screen, use the undo toast recipe with MonarchToast.
