options.name: title
options.description: What the AI did, in the past tense: "AI changed 3 fields".

options.name: description
options.description: One line of detail.

options.name: changes
options.description: The fields that changed, before and after. More than three collapse into a disclosure.

options.name: auditURL
options.description: The audit log entry. Only http and https are shown.

options.name: duration
options.description: How long Undo stays available. nil keeps it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the spoken form of a change.

options.name: onUndo
options.description: Reverts the change. Throw to report a failure.

options.name: onExpire
options.description: Runs once when duration runs out without an undo.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a dismiss button.

states.name: active
states.description: AI subtle fill and AI border, with Undo.

states.name: undoing
states.description: Undo shows a progress indicator; the time limit is paused.

states.name: undone
states.description: Neutral fill and border; Changes undone is shown and announced; Undo goes away.

states.name: failed
states.description: Couldn’t undo. Try again. in the danger strong role, announced; Undo stays.

states.name: expired
states.description: Neutral fill; Undo is no longer available. is shown and announced; onExpire runs.

appearance: The AI subtle fill and AI border with the bot glyph in the AI strong role while the change can be undone; the subtle background and subtle border afterwards. The title is strong body text, the description muted; each change is caption text with the field muted, the old value muted and struck through, an arrow and the new value in default text.
platformNotes: The parity map names MonarchBanner, but the banner has one action and a tone icon, so this banner is drawn from the same layout with the AI roles, Undo, an audit link and dismiss. On the web the time limit pauses while the pointer is over the banner or focus is inside it; iOS has neither, so it pauses while the app is in the background and while the changes disclosure is open, and does not run at all with VoiceOver or Switch Control on. The web's useAiUndoToast hook is the undo toast recipe on iOS. MonarchTone has no accent or AI tone, so the AI colour roles are used directly.
accessibility: The title is read as "AI change: " followed by the title.
Each change is one element read as "Status changed from Open to Closed"; the old value is struck through as well as muted, and the arrow is decorative.
Undo, the audit link and Dismiss are separate controls with 44-point touch targets.
Changes undone, the failure and the end of the time limit are shown as text and announced.
The time limit does not run while VoiceOver or Switch Control is on.
The bot glyph is decorative.
edgeCases: A finished undo wins over the timer: an undo that completes as the time runs out stays undone.
The time left is kept while paused and resumes from there.
Unsafe audit links are dropped.
The undo state lives in the view; give the banner a new id for a new change.

name: MonarchAiUsageMeter
title: AiUsageMeter
wrapsNative: MonarchUsageMeter (ProgressView with a ProgressViewStyle per item)
summary: How much AI the person has used against their quotas: one meter per scope (this turn, this conversation, this month) in tokens or credits, with a written warning near the limit and over it.
whenToUse: In an assistant panel, settings or billing screen where people need to see how close they are to their AI quotas.
whenNotToUse: For quotas that are not AI tokens or credits (seats, storage, requests) use MonarchUsageMeter. For the cost of one message use the message metadata.
api: MonarchAiUsageMeter.init(_ title: String? = nil, scopes: [MonarchAiUsageScope], period: String? = nil, resetsAt: Date? = nil, warningAt: Double = 0.8, isLoading: Bool = false, error: String? = nil, labels: MonarchAiUsageMeterLabels = MonarchAiUsageMeterLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchAiUsageScope.init(_ label: String, id: String? = nil, used: Double, limit: Double? = nil, unit: MonarchAiUsageUnit = .tokens)
enum MonarchAiUsageUnit { case tokens, credits }
MonarchAiUsageMeterLabels.init(label: String? = nil, unit: (@Sendable (_ unit: MonarchAiUsageUnit, _ count: Double) -> String)? = nil, meter: MonarchUsageMeterLabels = MonarchUsageMeterLabels())

options.name: title
options.description: A visible heading. Without it the group is named "AI usage" for VoiceOver.

options.name: scopes
options.description: The quotas in order, each with a label, the amount used, an optional limit and a unit (tokens or credits).

options.name: period
options.description: The period measured, shown under the title.

options.name: resetsAt
options.description: When the quotas reset, shown under the title.

options.name: warningAt
options.description: The share of a limit at which a scope is near the limit.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows a spinner instead of the scopes.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message shown instead of the scopes.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the group name, the unit names and the strings of the underlying usage meter.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry button under the error.

states.name: normal
states.description: Below the warning share: the meter uses the accent fill and the share in muted text.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: At or above warningAt: warning fill, a warning icon and "Near the limit".

states.name: over the limit
states.description: Above the limit: danger fill, a danger icon and "Over the limit".

states.name: no limit
states.description: The amount alone, with no meter.

states.name: loading
states.description: A spinner and "Loading usage".

states.name: error
states.description: The message with an icon, and a retry button with onRetry.

appearance: The look of MonarchUsageMeter: muted labels, strong figures, a muted track with the accent, warning or danger fill, and warning or danger status text. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: A preset of MonarchUsageMeter, so it also offers a title, a period, a reset date, loading and error, which the web does not. The web calls a scope exceeded when it reaches its limit; the shared iOS meter calls a scope over the limit only above it and near the limit at exactly 100%. The web's number and percent formatters are replaced by the meter's locale-aware formatting. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The meter is a group named by the title, or by "AI usage".
Each scope is one element read as its label, with the figures, the level and the percentage as its value.
Near and over the limit are written and have an icon, so they do not depend on colour.
When a scope reaches near or over the limit while the view is on screen, VoiceOver announces it once.
edgeCases: A negative amount counts as zero; a limit of zero or less is no limit.
Scopes are identified by position unless they have an id, so labels may repeat.
The unit is singular only for exactly one (the limit, or the amount when there is no limit).

The visible note and its icon are hidden from VoiceOver, so the note is not read twice.

whenToUse: Beside an AI prompt field, so people can speak a request instead of typing it.
whenNotToUse: For a spoken, two-way conversation with the assistant, use MonarchAiVoiceMode. For dictation in any text field, the system keyboard's dictation key already works and needs nothing.
api: init(locale: Locale? = nil, mode: MonarchAiVoiceInputMode = .toggle, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, showsLevel: Bool = true, showsTranscript: Bool = true, recognizer: any MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer = MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer(), labels: MonarchAiVoiceInputLabels = MonarchAiVoiceInputLabels(), onStateChange: (@MainActor (MonarchAiVoiceInputState) -> Void)? = nil, onTranscript: @escaping @MainActor (_ text: String, _ isFinal: Bool) -> Void)
enum MonarchAiVoiceInputMode { case toggle, pushToTalk }
enum MonarchAiVoiceInputState { case idle, starting, listening, denied, error }

@MainActor protocol MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer: AnyObject { func isAvailable(for locale: Locale?) -> Bool; func start(locale: Locale?, continuous: Bool) -> AsyncThrowingStream<MonarchAiSpeechEvent, any Error>; func stop() }
enum MonarchAiSpeechEvent { case started, level(Double), partial(String), final(String) }
enum MonarchAiSpeechError: Error { case denied, noSpeech, noMicrophone, unavailable, failed }
@MainActor final class MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer: MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer { init(prefersOnDeviceRecognition: Bool = false) }
struct MonarchAiVoiceInputLabels { var dictate, holdToTalk, holdHint, starting, listening, stopped, denied, noSpeech, noMicrophone, unavailable, error, transcript, openSettings: String? }

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the speech. The device language by default.

options.name: mode
options.description: toggle: press to start and again to stop. pushToTalk: listen while held.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the button: sm, md or lg.

options.name: showsLevel
options.description: Show a five-segment level meter while listening.

options.name: showsTranscript
options.description: Show the words under the button as they are recognised.

options.name: recognizer
options.description: The speech engine. Conform your own type to use SpeechAnalyzer, a server recogniser or a scripted one.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStateChange
options.description: Called with every change of state.

options.name: onTranscript
options.description: Recognised text. Guesses have isFinal false and may change; each settled phrase arrives once with isFinal true.

states.name: idle
states.description: The button with a microphone symbol, off.

states.name: starting
states.description: The button is on and the status reads Starting microphone… while permission and the microphone are requested.

states.name: listening
states.description: The button is on with a filled microphone, the level meter moves, the status reads Listening… and the transcript grows.

states.name: denied
states.description: A warning notice explains that access is off, with an Open Settings action on iOS.

states.name: error
states.description: A notice with the reason: nothing heard (info), no microphone or recognition unavailable (warning), or an unexpected failure (danger).

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) the button uses the disabled roles and does not start; a running session is stopped.

appearance: The button is the outline toggle button: bordered surface while off, subtle accent fill with an accent border and accent text while listening. The status is a muted caption, the transcript default body text, and the level meter uses the meter's accent and muted roles. The notice uses the tone roles of MonarchInlineNotice.
platformNotes: The web uses the browser's Web Speech API and getUserMedia; iOS uses the Speech framework and AVAudioEngine through MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer, and the app must add NSMicrophoneUsageDescription and NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription to its Info.plist. Languages, length limits and on-device support differ: SFSpeechRecognizer's supported languages apply, server recognition is limited in length per request and needs a network, and prefersOnDeviceRecognition keeps audio on the device where the language supports it. SpeechAnalyzer (iOS 26) is not built in; an app can conform its own recogniser to MonarchAiSpeechRecognizer. The web's createRecognition hook is the recognizer parameter here. The web's Escape key maps to the VoiceOver escape gesture. With SFSpeechRecognizer, partial results are the whole utterance so far and the final phrase arrives when listening stops.
accessibility: In toggle mode the button is a standard Toggle styled as a button, so VoiceOver reads it as on while listening and off otherwise.
In push-to-talk mode, which cannot be held with VoiceOver, Switch Control or Full Keyboard Access, the button's default action starts and a second activation stops; its hint says so.
The VoiceOver escape gesture stops listening.
"Listening…" is announced on start, "Stopped listening." when it ends, and the failure message when it fails.
The level meter is decorative; with Reduce Motion it shows full or empty instead of following the level.
The transcript is read as "Transcript:" followed by the words.
The notice has an icon and the tone's spoken name, so the failure is not conveyed by colour alone.
The button keeps a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points; all text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: When the recogniser is not available for the language the component draws nothing.
Releasing push-to-talk before the microphone opens stops the session as soon as it starts.
Leaving the screen cancels the session and discards pending words without an announcement.
A second start while a session runs is ignored.
The Open Settings action is shown only on iOS, where the system Settings URL exists.

Experimental: the default recogniser (MonarchAiSystemSpeechRecognizer: SFSpeechRecognizer, AVAudioEngine and the audio session) compiles but has not yet been run against a real microphone, and its error-code mapping is based on observed codes, not documented API. The component itself is tested with scripted recognisers. It becomes available after a device check.

name: MonarchAiVoiceMode

summary: The surface for a live, two-way spoken conversation with an AI assistant: a calm central visual, always-visible state text, live captions from the conversation's messages, and explicit Mute, Interrupt, Captions and End controls. UI only; the app owns the audio.
whenToUse: When the person talks with the assistant by voice, presented with .fullScreenCover (md) or inside an assistant panel (compact).
whenNotToUse: For dictating a prompt that the person then sends, use MonarchAiVoiceInput. For a call between people, use the call components.
api: init(state: MonarchAiVoiceModeState, level: Double = 0, agent: MonarchAiAgentRef? = nil, captions: [MonarchAiConversationMessage] = [], captionsVisible: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isMuted: Bool? = nil, elapsedSeconds: Int? = nil, error: String? = nil, size: MonarchAiVoiceModeSize = .md, labels: MonarchAiVoiceModeLabels = MonarchAiVoiceModeLabels(), onMuteChange: (@MainActor (Bool) -> Void)? = nil, onInterrupt: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onEnd: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRestart: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAiVoiceModeState { case connecting, listening, thinking, speaking, muted, reconnecting, ended, error }
enum MonarchAiVoiceModeSize { case md, compact }

struct MonarchAiVoiceModeLabels { var label: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var assistant, you: String?; var states: [MonarchAiVoiceModeState: String]; var microphoneMuted, mute, interrupt, captions, end, restart, retry, captionsEmpty, elapsed: String?; var lasted: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var errorFallback: String? }

options.name: state
options.description: Where the call is, reported by the app.

options.name: level
options.description: The live audio level, 0 through 1, of whoever is talking. Drives the halo and bars while listening or speaking.

options.name: agent
options.description: The assistant; its name labels the surface and its captions, its avatar URL is shown beside the name.

options.name: captions
options.description: The conversation's messages, oldest first. User and assistant text is shown; a message with streaming text is an interim caption.

options.name: captionsVisible
options.description: Whether captions show. Without a binding the surface keeps its own value, on at first.

options.name: isMuted
options.description: Whether the microphone is muted. By default only in the muted state; pass it when the microphone stays muted while the assistant thinks or speaks.

options.name: elapsedSeconds
options.description: How long the call has run, shown as a clock and as the duration once ended.

options.name: error
options.description: What went wrong, shown on the error state.

options.name: size
options.description: md fills the space on the canvas background; compact is a bordered card with small buttons.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the state texts.

options.name: onMuteChange
options.description: Called with the wanted value from Mute or Magic Tap. Shows Mute while the call is live.

options.name: onInterrupt
options.description: Shows Interrupt while the assistant thinks or speaks.

options.name: onEnd
options.description: Shows End while the call is live. Only this button ends the call.

options.name: onRestart
options.description: Shows Start again on the ended state.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Retry on the error state.

states.name: connecting, thinking, reconnecting
states.description: The orb shows the AI typing dots; the state text says which.

states.name: listening, speaking
states.description: The orb shows five bars and the halo grows with the level.

states.name: muted
states.description: A neutral orb with a crossed-out microphone; Mute is on. Muted in another state adds the note Your microphone is muted.

states.name: ended
states.description: A neutral orb, Conversation ended, the duration, and Start again when onRestart is given.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger orb with an exclamation mark, the error text, and Retry when onRetry is given.

appearance: md fills the space on the canvas background; compact is a surface card with a subtle border. The halo uses the AI subtle role and the orb the AI solid role with AI on-solid bars; error uses the danger roles, muted and ended the neutral emphasis roles. The state is heading text, the name and clock labels, captions body text with the speaker in bold (AI strong for the assistant, muted for the person).
platformNotes: The web component reports state through props in the same way and also ships browser and realtime session helpers (Web Speech, WebRTC, PCM players); iOS ships only the surface, and the app owns AVAudioSession, interruptions and route changes as described in the component's documentation. Captions use the shared MonarchAiConversationMessage model instead of the web's separate caption type: a message with streaming text is interim. Space toggles mute on the web; on iOS Magic Tap (two-finger double-tap) does. The web shows an AiAgentAvatar; iOS shows the agent's avatar image when it has a URL, and nothing otherwise, as there is no agent avatar component on iOS yet. Present it with .fullScreenCover; macOS, used only to build, has no full-screen cover. The web keeps the captions scrolled to the newest unless the person scrolled up; iOS anchors the captions to the bottom with defaultScrollAnchor.
accessibility: The surface is a container named "Voice conversation with" and the assistant's name.
The state is always written; each change is announced, except the first state and turns into listening or speaking, which the audio already makes clear. An error is announced with its text.
Final captions are announced once each as "You:" or the assistant's name followed by the words; interim captions are hidden from VoiceOver until they are final.
Mute and Captions are toggles with on and off values; Magic Tap toggles mute while the call is live.
When Interrupt goes away while VoiceOver focus is on it, focus moves to Mute.
The visual is decorative and holds still with Reduce Motion; the state text and the glyph carry the meaning, not colour.
Buttons keep 44 by 44 point touch targets; text scales with Dynamic Type and the captions scroll.
edgeCases: System and tool messages, and messages with no text, are not captions.
Captions show while the call is live even when there are none yet (with a hint), and after it only when there are some.
A level outside 0 through 1 is limited; not-a-number is 0.
Times of an hour or more show hours: 1:02:09.
Captions announced while hidden are still marked as announced, so turning captions on does not replay them.

summary: One API key in a list: name and status, the visible prefix with the rest masked, created, last used and expiry times, scopes, and Rotate and Revoke actions that ask for confirmation before calling the app.

options.description: Scopes shown before a +N badge.

options.name: status
options.description: Active, expiring, expired or revoked; expired and revoked keys have no actions.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times; without it they follow the clock, updated every minute.

options.name: revokeConfirmPhrase
options.description: A phrase, usually the name, that must be typed in the revoke alert before Revoke key works.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string; strings that name something take %@.

options.name: onRotate
options.description: Rotates the key after confirmation. A thrown error is shown in the row with a retry.

options.name: onRevoke
options.description: Revokes the key after confirmation, like onRotate.

options.description: More menu items after Rotate and Revoke, such as Edit.

states.name: active, expiring
states.description: A success or warning status badge and the actions menu.

states.name: expired, revoked
states.description: A neutral or danger status badge and no actions.

states.name: confirming
states.description: Rotate shows a confirmation dialog; Revoke shows an alert, with a field when a phrase is required.

states.name: running
states.description: A small spinner with Rotating… or Revoking…; the menu is disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with the error's description or the built-in sentence; Retry runs the action again.

appearance: The name in the default text role, the prefix in the code style and muted role, the times in the muted caption, outline scope badges, and status badges in their tone's subtle colours, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web row shows Rotate and Revoke as buttons and keeps its ConfirmDialog open while the promise runs, showing a rejection inside it. On iOS the actions sit in a trailing menu, as in list rows; the system confirmation dialog and alert close when a button is tapped, so progress and failures are shown in the row instead. The web's rotateConfirmOptions and revokeConfirmOptions are replaced by labels. The web's `as` and link-name options have no meaning on iOS. Android has the same parameters. Several closures are optional (onRotate, onRevoke). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRotate.
accessibility: The name and the status badge are combined into one element; the status is a word, not only a colour.
The prefix is read as "Key starting with sk_live_4f2a"; the mask is not read.
Scopes are one element read as "Scopes" and every scope, including those behind +N.
The menu is a button named "Actions for Reporting job" with a 44-point touch target; Revoke has the destructive role.
Rotating… or Revoking… is announced when an action starts, and the failure message when it fails.
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type; the name and status stack when they do not fit on one line.
edgeCases: A long prefix is truncated in the middle, so the start and the mask stay visible.
Only one action runs at a time; the menu is disabled while it runs.
The Revoke button in the alert is disabled until the phrase matches (case-sensitive, ignoring surrounding spaces), and the action checks the phrase again.
A negative maxScopes shows only the +N badge.

appearance: Row labels in the default text role and descriptions in the muted text role, rows divided by the subtle border role. The controls are system segmented and menu pickers tinted with the accent through the theme's tint, and look like the system controls in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web panel writes the rook_theme and mn_contrast cookies and applies all four choices to the html element. On iOS the panel only changes its binding: the app applies scheme, contrast and accent with .monarchTheme(preferences.appearance) and stores the choices itself (for example with @AppStorage). SwiftUI does not let an app turn on Reduce Motion for other views, so motion is applied by the app's own animations through reducesMotion(systemReducesMotion:); Monarch components keep following the device setting. Density has no Monarch-wide meaning on iOS yet; the app reads preferences.density (for example to choose a smaller controlSize). The accent row is native-only, because the note for this entry asks for the accent as a theme input; the web panel has no accent row. The default theme is System, where the web default is Light, because iOS apps follow the device. Android has the same rows.
accessibility: Each row's label and description are combined into one element, read before the row's control.

The theme row is MonarchThemeToggle, named by the row label.
The accent row is a standard menu Picker named by the row label, whose value is the current accent's name; accents are chosen by name, not by colour.
The title has the header trait.
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type; the accent menu has a touch target of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: Long translated choice names are truncated by the system segmented control; keep them short.
An accent that is not in accents is added to the end of the menu, so the current choice is always visible.
A row listed twice is shown once; an empty rows list shows only the title.
Accent names come from the tokens' MonarchAccent.label (English); an app that translates them passes its own MonarchAccent values or leaves the accent row out.

Each step is a container read as "Step 1, Finance check (Role: Finance team)" with Move up and Move down accessibility actions; each move is announced ("Moved to position 2.").
The remove button is named "Remove step 1" and the reorder menu "Reorder step 1".
The approver and target menus are labelled through MonarchFormField; the target is marked Required and its error is text with an icon.
Touch targets are at least 44 points.
edgeCases: Changing the approver drops a target the new type does not offer, as the web does.
Labels longer than 60 characters are cut; an emptied label becomes nil.
With no approver types the add button is disabled.
validate returns ids, so the app can scroll to the first incomplete step.

name: MonarchApprovalQueue
title: ApprovalQueue
wrapsNative: List with .listStyle(.plain) and .swipeActions on each row, searchable(text:prompt:), Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) (Toggle(sources:isOn:) for Select all), .sheet for the reason, .alert for confirmations; MonarchAvatar, MonarchButton, MonarchBadge, MonarchBulkActionBar in safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom), MonarchTextField, MonarchEmptyState
summary: Requests waiting on the viewer, with Approve, Send back with a reason and Review on each, swipe actions, search and bulk approval.
whenToUse: When a manager or admin has requests (expenses, leave, timesheets, access) that need their decision, on an approvals screen or, with limit and a footer, in a dashboard card.
whenNotToUse: For the steps of one request, use MonarchApprovalTimeline. For requests with many columns, sorting and paging, use MonarchDataTable with row actions.
api: MonarchApprovalQueue.init(_ items: [MonarchApprovalQueueItem], rejectReason: MonarchApprovalQueueRejectReason = .required, isSearchable: Bool = false, limit: Int? = nil, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchApprovalQueueLabels = MonarchApprovalQueueLabels(), onApprove: (@MainActor (MonarchApprovalQueueItem) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onReject: (@MainActor (MonarchApprovalQueueItem, String?) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onReview: (@MainActor (MonarchApprovalQueueItem) -> Void)? = nil, onApproveMany: (@MainActor ([MonarchApprovalQueueItem]) async throws -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder footer: () -> Footer)

MonarchApprovalPerson.init(_ name: String, avatarURL: URL? = nil, seed: String? = nil)
enum MonarchApprovalQueueRejectReason { case required, optional, none }

MonarchApprovalQueueLabels.init(label: String? = nil, approve: String? = nil, reject: String? = nil, review: String? = nil, approveItem: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, rejectItem: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, reviewItem: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, selectItem: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, selectAll: String? = nil, approveSelected: String? = nil, overdue: String? = nil, search: String? = nil, emptyTitle: String? = nil, emptyDescription: String? = nil, noMatchesTitle: String? = nil, rejectTitle: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, rejectDescription: String? = nil, rejectReason: String? = nil, rejectReasonPrompt: String? = nil, bulkDescription: String? = nil, bulkConfirm: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil, approved: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, rejected: (@Sendable (_ requester: String) -> String)? = nil, failed: String? = nil, bulkTitle: (@Sendable (_ count: Int) -> String)? = nil, bulkApproved: (@Sendable (_ count: Int) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: items
options.description: The requests, in the order to show them. The app removes a request once it is decided.

options.name: rejectReason
options.description: required and optional open a dialog with a reason field (Send back is disabled while a required reason is empty); none asks for confirmation only.

options.name: isSearchable
options.description: Adds a searchable field that filters by requester and title, or by each item's searchText. Needs a NavigationStack.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many requests, for a dashboard card.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for "2 hours ago". The current time, refreshed every minute, when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the announcements and the per-request button names.

options.name: onApprove
options.description: Adds Approve (button and full trailing swipe). The button shows progress until it returns; a thrown error marks the row as failed.

options.name: onReject
options.description: Adds Send back. Receives the trimmed reason or nil. The dialog stays open with a progress button until it returns and shows the failure if it throws.

options.name: onReview
options.description: Adds Review (button and leading swipe), which opens the full request.

options.name: onApproveMany
options.description: Adds checkboxes, Select all and a bulk action bar with Approve selected, confirmed by an alert.

options.name: footer
options.description: Content after the requests, such as a See all requests link.

states.name: pending
states.description: While onApprove runs, the row's Approve shows a spinner and Send back and the swipe actions are unavailable.

states.name: failed
states.description: The row shows "That did not work. Try again." in the strong danger colour with a warning symbol, and it is announced.

states.name: selected
states.description: With onApproveMany, checked rows are counted in the bulk action bar at the bottom.

states.name: read-only request
states.description: canDecide false: no Approve, no Send back, a disabled checkbox; Review stays.

states.name: overdue
states.description: A danger Past due badge after the title.

states.name: empty
states.description: A success empty state, Nothing to review.

states.name: no matches
states.description: A filtered empty state with Clear filters, which empties the search.

appearance: A plain list. Names use the strong body role, details, times and summaries the muted caption text. Approve is a primary button, Send back secondary and Review ghost. Swipe actions are tinted with the solid success, danger and accent roles. The same roles adapt to dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ApprovalQueue is a list of rows with buttons; iOS adds swipe actions and uses the system search field, alerts and a sheet for the reason. The web uses a success button for Approve; MonarchButton has no success variant, so Approve is primary. Titles, summaries and badges are strings and MonarchStatusDefinition values rather than rich content. The web keeps the bulk confirmation open while it runs; here the alert closes and the bulk bar shows progress and the failure. Android uses the same name and API shape. Several closures are optional (onApprove, onReject, onReview, onApproveMany). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onApprove.
accessibility: The list is named "Requests waiting for you".
Each request is one element read as requester, detail, title, absolute submission time, Past due, badges, summary and, after a failure, the error.
Approve, Send back, Review and each checkbox name the request they act on, such as "Approve request from Sam Lee".
Approving, sending back, bulk approval and failures are announced.
Swipe actions repeat the row's buttons, so every action is reachable without swiping.
Select all is a standard Toggle over the row checkboxes, read as on, off or mixed.
Overdue is a badge with a word and failures have a symbol and text, so nothing relies on colour.
edgeCases: Decided requests stay until the app removes them from items; the queue does not hide them itself.
Selections of requests that are no longer in items are ignored.
limit applies after the search.
Give the queue a height or a screen: as a List it does not size itself to its rows inside a ScrollView.

name: MonarchApprovalTimeline
title: ApprovalTimeline
wrapsNative: VStack of step rows with a drawn marker (Circle, SF Symbol) and a Capsule rail; MonarchFlowLayout, MonarchAvatar; TimelineView(.everyMinute) and RelativeDateTimeFormatter for relative times
summary: The history and outlook of one approval: who submitted it, each step with its decision, who is deciding now and what comes next.
whenToUse: On the detail screen of a request (expense, leave, purchase, access) to show where it is in its approval chain and who decided what.
whenNotToUse: For the list of requests waiting on the viewer, use MonarchApprovalQueue. For a general feed of events on a record, use MonarchActivityTimeline. For the steps of a form, use MonarchStepper.
api: MonarchApprovalTimeline.init(_ steps: [MonarchApprovalTimelineStep], now: Date? = nil, absoluteAfter: TimeInterval = 7 * 86_400, showsAvatars: Bool = true, labels: MonarchApprovalTimelineLabels = MonarchApprovalTimelineLabels())

MonarchApprovalTimelineStep.init(id: String, label: String, status: MonarchApprovalStepStatus, actor: MonarchApprovalPerson? = nil, approvers: [MonarchApprovalPerson] = [], delegatedFrom: MonarchApprovalPerson? = nil, date: Date? = nil, comment: String? = nil, note: String? = nil)
MonarchApprovalPerson.init(_ name: String, avatarURL: URL? = nil, seed: String? = nil)
enum MonarchApprovalStepStatus { case submitted, approved, rejected, pending, waiting, skipped, cancelled }

MonarchApprovalTimelineLabels.init(label: String? = nil, status: (@Sendable (MonarchApprovalStepStatus) -> String)? = nil, approvers: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, delegatedFrom: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, current: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil)

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps in order, from submission to the outcome.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times. The current time, refreshed every minute, when nil.

options.name: absoluteAfter
options.description: How far from now, in seconds, a time is shown as a date and time instead of "2 hours ago".

options.name: showsAvatars
options.description: Shows a small avatar before the name of whoever decided or submitted.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the status names, the approvers and delegation phrases, the spoken names and the empty text.

states.name: submitted / approved
states.description: A filled success marker with a check; the rail below it is the success border.

states.name: rejected
states.description: A filled danger marker with a cross; the status text is bold in the strong danger colour.

states.name: pending
states.description: A warning-outlined marker with a dot; the status is bold in the strong warning colour, the approvers are listed and VoiceOver adds "Current step".

states.name: waiting
states.description: An empty outlined marker and a muted label; the approvers are listed.

states.name: skipped / cancelled
states.description: A dashed outlined marker with a dash or a cross, and the note.

states.name: empty
states.description: No steps: the text "Not submitted yet".

appearance: Markers use the solid success and danger roles with their on-solid glyph colour, the subtle warning fill with the solid warning border, or the surface fill with the strong border. Labels use the default text, meta lines the muted text in the caption role, and comments sit in a rounded box on the muted background. The same roles adapt to dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Matches the web ApprovalTimeline. Labels, comments and notes are plain strings rather than rich content, and the time zone and locale come from the environment rather than parameters. Android uses the same name and API shape.
accessibility: The timeline is a container named "Approval timeline".
Each step is one element read as its label, status, actor, absolute date and time, approvers, delegation, comment and note.
The step waiting for a decision adds "Current step".
Markers differ by shape (check, cross, dot, dash, empty, dashed border) and the status is written, so nothing relies on colour.
Markers, rails and avatars are hidden from VoiceOver; markers and text scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Long labels and comments wrap; the rail stretches with the step.
A decided step without an actor or a date has no meta line.
Approvers are only shown on pending and waiting steps; a delegation on a decided step gets its own line.
Times in the future are relative too ("in 2 hours").

name: MonarchAreaChart
title: AreaChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts: Chart with AreaMark(x:yStart:yEnd:series:) per run of each series between edges Monarch computes (overlap, stacked, 100% stacked), LineMark on each upper edge, PointMark for lone and inspected points, RuleMark for reference lines and the crosshair, chartXSelection(value:) for touch inspection, inside MonarchChartFrame (accessibilityChartDescriptor and View as table)
summary: An area chart for volumes over time: several series overlapping, stacked so the top edge is the total, or stacked to 100% to show shares, with touch inspection, legend toggles and a data table.
whenToUse: To show a total over time made of parts (traffic by platform, revenue by plan) with stacked, how the mix changes when the total does not matter with expand, or one or two volumes where the filled area helps read magnitude with overlap.
whenNotToUse: To compare trends of independent measures, use MonarchLineChart: overlapping fills hide each other beyond two series. For values that go negative, use a bar chart. For parts of one whole at a single moment, use MonarchDonutChart or MonarchStackedProportionBar.
api: MonarchAreaChart.init(_ title: String, dates: [Date], series: [MonarchLineChartSeries], description: String? = nil, xTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, stacking: MonarchAreaChartStacking = .overlap, referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine] = [], curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = .linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, includesZero: Bool = true, valueDomain: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, isLegendInteractive: Bool = true, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, dateFormat: Date.FormatStyle = .dateTime.month(.abbreviated).day(), emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), totalLabel: String? = nil, shareLabel: (@Sendable (_ value: String, _ share: String) -> String)? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchAreaChart.init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchLineChartSeries], description: String? = nil, xTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, stacking: MonarchAreaChartStacking = .overlap, referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine] = [], curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = .linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, includesZero: Bool = true, valueDomain: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, isLegendInteractive: Bool = true, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), totalLabel: String? = nil, shareLabel: (@Sendable (_ value: String, _ share: String) -> String)? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchAreaChartStacking { case overlap, stacked, expand }

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, a heading in the frame and the name VoiceOver reads.

options.name: dates
options.description: The x values, in order. Points are spaced by time.

options.name: categories
options.description: The x values, in order, already localised. Points are spaced evenly.

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, bottom of the stack first: key, label, one value per x value (nil is a gap), optional colour slot and isDashed. The same type as MonarchLineChart.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: xTitle
options.description: The heading of the x column of the data table. Built in: "Date" or "Category".

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure, for the data table and VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: stacking
options.description: overlap: each area from the baseline; stacked: piled so the top edge is the total; expand: piled as shares of 100%.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed horizontal lines with a label and value. Not drawn in expand, whose axis is shares.

options.name: curve
options.description: linear, or monotone: smooth edges that never overshoot.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error, drawn by the frame. A ready chart with no x values is empty.

options.name: includesZero
options.description: Whether the value axis keeps zero when the areas overlap. Stacks always start at zero.

options.name: valueDomain
options.description: Fixes the value axis. Ignored in expand, which is always 0 to 100%.

options.name: isLegendInteractive
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend shows for two or more series.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected index, to share a crosshair between charts. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: dateFormat
options.description: How dates are written in the popover and the data table (dates initialiser only).

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The empty-state message.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The height of the plot; 240 points by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the frame's built-in strings.

options.name: totalLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Total" of a stack, in the popover and the table.

options.name: shareLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "value (share)" text of the expand popover.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value in the popover, the table and for VoiceOver. Default: a number in the locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: overlap
states.description: Each visible series is a translucent area from the baseline (zero, or the lowest value without includesZero) with a solid top line.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Series are piled in order, first at the bottom; the top edge of the last is the total. Bands are more opaque because they touch. A negative value counts as zero in the stack.

states.name: expand
states.description: Series are piled as shares of each x value's total; the value axis reads 0% to 100% and reference lines are not drawn.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: While the plot is touched, or activeIndex is set: a crosshair, a point on each upper edge and a popover listing the series top of the stack first, with each share in expand and the total under a stack of two or more.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The series leaves the plot and the stack; its legend entry is struck through; it stays in the data table and the table's total.

states.name: gap
states.description: A missing value breaks that series' band; in a stack the series above keep their place. A lone value between gaps is a dot.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: Drawn by MonarchChartFrame at the chart's height.

appearance: Series use the theme's data colours 1 to 5 in order (later series are neutral). Overlapping fills are the series colour at low strength, stacked bands a little stronger, dashed series fainter; each top edge is a solid line in the series colour. Reference lines are the muted text colour, dashed; the crosshair is the strong border colour; the popover is the raised surface with a medium shadow. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts, which draws the axes and grid; the stack itself is computed by Monarch (not MarkStackingMethod) so gaps break a band and negatives count as zero exactly as on the web. Series, reference lines and the curve reuse the MonarchLineChart types rather than new ones. Touch inspection uses chartXSelection and clears when the finger lifts; there is no keyboard inspection, live region or generated summary: VoiceOver gets the data through the frame's chart descriptor. The legend keeps one series visible, where the web lets every series be hidden. onPointSelect, xScale, valueFormat and formatTick are not offered (the initialiser chooses dates or categories, formatValue writes values, the expand axis is whole percentages). Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (shareLabel, formatValue, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is shareLabel.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one element named by the title, with the data as an accessibility chart descriptor (Audio Graphs and the data table in the rotor).
"View as table" shows the data table, where each row is read as the x value followed by every series and, in a stack of two or more series, the total. Values are the real values, not shares.
Values are read with formatValue.
The inspection popover is hidden from VoiceOver.
Series differ by name in the legend and the popover and, where isDashed is set, by a dashed edge and marker, never by colour alone.
Legend toggles are switches with a 44-point target.
edgeCases: Missing, nil and non-finite values are gaps, never zero; extra values are dropped.
In stacked and expand, a negative value counts as zero in the stack; the popover and the table still show the real value.
An x value whose visible total is zero has every share at 0% in expand.
A ready chart with no x values shows the empty state.
A single series has no legend and no total.
Hiding series changes the stack and the expand shares but not the table's total, which is the sum of every series.

Once uploaded with a URL, the name is a link.
The progress bar is a standard ProgressView named "Uploading" and the file name.
Retry and remove are separate buttons named with the file name ("Remove Q3 report.pdf"), with 44-point touch targets.
A change to failed is announced.
The type icon is decorative; the chip is at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: A long name is shortened in the middle so the extension stays visible.
Progress outside 0 through 1 is limited; not-a-number counts as unknown.
Without a size the done state shows only the name.

wrapsNative: Canvas
summary: Shows how loud a microphone is, as rising segments or a thin bar, from a level the app measures.
whenToUse: In a call tile, a pre-call check or a recorder, to show that the microphone picks up sound.
whenNotToUse: For the progress of a recording or an upload, use ProgressView. For a waveform over time, draw one from the samples.
api: MonarchAudioLevelMeter.init(_ level: Double, label: String? = nil, variant: MonarchAudioLevelMeterVariant = .segments, size: MonarchAudioLevelMeterSize = .md, segments: Int = 5, isMuted: Bool = false, mutedLabel: String? = nil, isDecorative: Bool = false)

options.name: level
options.description: The loudness, 0 through 1. Values outside are limited to that range.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Microphone level".

options.name: variant
options.description: segments are rising bars the size of a word; bar is one thin bar that fills the width.

options.name: size
options.description: sm (12 points high) or md (16). Segments only.

options.name: segments
options.description: The number of segments. At least one.

options.name: isMuted
options.description: The microphone is off: the meter is empty and reads "Muted".

options.name: mutedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken value "Muted".

options.name: isDecorative
options.description: Hides the meter from assistive technology.

states.name: silent
states.description: Every segment is a dot in the strong border colour; the bar is an empty track.

states.name: sound
states.description: Segments up to the level are tall and in the success colour; the bar is filled to the level.

states.name: muted
states.description: Empty, in the disabled colours, and read as "Muted".

states.name: reduce motion
states.description: The meter does not follow the level: it is full at or above a level of 0.08 and empty below.

appearance: Segments that are on use the success solid colour and those that are off the strong border colour; the bar's track is the muted background. A muted meter uses the disabled text colour and the muted background, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web component can measure a MediaStream itself with the Web Audio API; on iOS capturing audio needs the microphone permission and an audio session, which belong to the app, so the meter only takes a level. On the web a segment that is off keeps its height and changes colour; here it is drawn as a dot, so the level can be read without colour. The web variants bars and bar are named segments and bar. The meter scales with Dynamic Type. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The meter is one element named "Microphone level" (or label) whose value is the level as a whole percentage in the user's locale, or "Muted".
It has the updates-frequently trait, so VoiceOver does not read every change.
With Reduce Motion the meter shows only whether there is sound; the spoken value is still the real level.
Segments that are on are tall and segments that are off are dots, so the level does not depend on colour.
isDecorative hides it when the same information is given elsewhere.
The segments rise towards the trailing side and the bar fills from the leading edge, in both layout directions.
edgeCases: A level that is not finite is treated as silence.
A segment count below one draws one segment.
The level changes without animation; pass a smoothed level for a calmer meter.
The meter is not interactive and has no touch target.

states.name: loading

states.name: failed

states.name: no access

states.name: details open
states.description: A sheet at medium height that can be pulled to large, with Close in the confirmation slot.

Columns and density have no meaning in a list. The web's auditLogToCsv helper is the app's: the recipe shares a simple CSV with ShareLink, and large exports belong on the server. Absolute times in the list and a relative time in the details follow the web; in tests and screenshots give the relative formatter a fixed reference time. Actor kinds are text, never colour alone. Rows are at least 44 points high.
MonarchCursorList announces new pages and its end, and Load more is a standard button.
In the sheet each fact is one element read as the term and the value; the relative time is spoken as the full date and time.
People, automations, systems and API keys are told apart by text in a badge, not by colour.
Close is in the standard place, and the escape gesture closes the sheet.

Long targets and origins wrap; IP addresses and ids stay on one line where they fit.
Deep links to an event set selected to open its sheet.
At the largest text sizes the rows grow taller and the sheet content scrolls.

name: MonarchAutosaveIndicator

wrapsNative: An @Observable MonarchAutosave that runs saves in Tasks and waits on an injectable Clock, shown by MonarchSaveStatusIndicator
summary: Saves a value automatically after the person stops changing it (MonarchAutosave) and shows where saving stands (MonarchAutosaveIndicator).
whenToUse: For editors and settings forms that save without a Save button: debounced, one save at a time, retried on failure, and flushed before leaving.
whenNotToUse: Not when the app already tracks its own save status (use MonarchSaveStatusIndicator directly), and not for forms with an explicit Save button.
api: MonarchAutosaveIndicator.init(_ autosave: MonarchAutosave<Value>, errorMessage: ((any Error) -> String)? = nil, announcesSaving: Bool = false, labels: MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels = MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels())

@MainActor @Observable final class MonarchAutosave<Value: Equatable & Sendable> { init(_ value: Value, delay: Duration = .seconds(1), retries: Int = 2, retryDelay: Duration = .seconds(2), savedAt: Date? = nil, clock: any Clock<Duration> = ContinuousClock(), now: @escaping @Sendable () -> Date = { Date() }, save: @escaping @MainActor (Value) async throws -> Void) }

MonarchAutosave: var status: MonarchSaveStatus { get }; var savedAt: Date? { get }; var value: Value { get }; var error: (any Error)? { get }; var isDirty: Bool { get }; var isEnabled: Bool { get set }
MonarchAutosave: func update(_ value: Value); func retry(); @discardableResult func flush() async -> Bool

options.name: autosave
options.description: The autosave to show. Keep it in @State and call update(_:) from onChange of the edited value.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Turns the save error into the visible message, such as "You are offline". Without it, "Couldn't save".

options.name: announcesSaving
options.description: Whether "Saving…" is announced too. Off so frequent autosaves stay quiet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Unsaved changes", "Saving…", "Saved", "Couldn't save" and "Retry".

options.name: MonarchAutosave value
options.description: The current value, taken as saved.

options.name: MonarchAutosave delay
options.description: How long to wait after the last change before saving.

options.name: MonarchAutosave retries
options.description: Automatic retries after a failed save before the status becomes error.

options.name: MonarchAutosave retryDelay
options.description: The wait before the first automatic retry; it doubles each time.

options.name: MonarchAutosave savedAt
options.description: When the value was last saved, if known; the status then starts as saved.

options.name: MonarchAutosave clock
options.description: The clock the waits are measured on. Tests pass a clock they advance by hand.

options.name: MonarchAutosave now
options.description: The current date, recorded as savedAt when a save finishes.

options.name: MonarchAutosave save
options.description: Saves a value. Throwing reports a failure.

states.name: idle
states.description: Nothing edited and no save time known: nothing is drawn.

states.name: unsaved
states.description: A change is waiting for the delay, or saving is paused with isEnabled false.

states.name: saving
states.description: A save is in flight, or an automatic retry is waiting.

states.name: saved
states.description: The last save finished: "Saved · 2 minutes ago".

states.name: error
states.description: The retries are used up: "Couldn't save" or the app's message, with a Retry button that saves at once.

appearance: As MonarchSaveStatusIndicator: caption text in the muted role, the success role for saved and the danger role for error, each with an icon. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's useAutosave hook becomes the MonarchAutosave class, because SwiftUI keeps long-lived state in an @Observable object rather than a hook. The app reports changes with update(_:) (usually from onChange). Values are compared with Equatable rather than JSON equality. The clock and the date source are parameters so tests and previews never wait for real time. Saves run on the main actor; an app that saves on another actor awaits it inside save.
accessibility: The status is one element: the words and the relative time; the icon is decorative.
Saved and error outcomes are announced; "Saving…" is announced only with announcesSaving.
The Retry button is a separate standard button with a 44-point touch target.
Each status has words and an icon, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A change back to the saved value cancels the wait and returns to saved (or idle).
Edits during a save are saved after it; flush() during a save waits for it and then saves the newest value at once.
flush() returns true at once when nothing is unsaved, and false when the save fails even if an automatic retry is scheduled.
While an automatic retry waits the status stays saving; after the last retry it becomes error.
An edit after an error keeps the error shown until the next save starts.

summary: A standard switch for whether automatic assignment may give someone new work, with a status word ("Available" or "Away"), a mark and an optional explanation.
whenToUse: Where work is assigned automatically and a person must be able to step out of it: an account menu, a settings screen, a home screen.
whenNotToUse: For any other setting use the standard Toggle (see switch). For presence with custom statuses use a status picker.

options.name: isAvailable
options.description: Whether the person is available for new work.

options.name: isPending
options.description: Whether a change is being saved. The switch is disabled and a progress indicator is shown.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name "Available for new work".

options.name: availableLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in status word "Available".

options.name: awayLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in status word "Away".

options.name: availableHint
options.description: Replaces the built-in explanation shown when available.

options.name: awayHint
options.description: Replaces the built-in explanation shown when away.

options.name: pendingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken word "Saving".

options.name: showsHint
options.description: Whether the explanation is shown under the status word and read as the hint.

states.name: available
states.description: The switch is on, the status word is "Available" and the mark is a filled dot in the success colour.

states.name: away
states.description: The switch is off, the status word is "Away" and the mark is a ring in the warning colour.

states.name: pending
states.description: The switch is disabled, a small progress indicator follows the text, and the spoken hint starts with "Saving".

states.name: disabled
states.description: The text and mark use the disabled text role and the switch is dimmed by the system, with the standard disabled(_:) modifier.

appearance: The switch is the system one, tinted with the theme's accent. The status word uses the default text role and the explanation the muted role; the mark uses the success solid role when available and the warning solid role when away, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web renders nothing while the value is null; on iOS do not show the view until the value is known. The web's inMenu flag handles menu key events and has no meaning here. The mark's filled and ring shapes, used on the web only in forced-colours mode, are always used on iOS. A progress indicator is shown while pending; the web only disables the switch.
accessibility: It stays a standard Toggle: VoiceOver reads the switch role and the system's on and off values.
The spoken name is "Available for new work" (or label), not the visible status word.
With showsHint the explanation is the hint; while pending the hint starts with "Saving".
The mark is decorative and differs in shape as well as colour; the status word carries the meaning.
The row is at least 44 points high and its text wraps at large text sizes.
edgeCases: The component does not save anything. Set isPending while saving and set the binding back if saving fails.
A long status word or explanation wraps beside the switch.
Inside a List or Form the row takes the system's row insets.

whenNotToUse: Not for attaching files in general (use PhotosPicker or fileImporter with MonarchUploadQueue) and not for only showing a picture (use MonarchAvatar).

options.name: name
options.description: The person's or workspace's name, for the initials fallback and what VoiceOver reads for the avatar.

options.name: image / url
options.description: The current picture, as an image the app loaded or an address loaded with AsyncImage; nil for none.

options.name: shape
options.description: circle for people, square for workspaces and organisations; also the crop mask.

options.name: maxFileSize
options.description: The largest picked file accepted, in bytes; larger files show "Choose a photo smaller than 5 MB."

options.name: outputSize
options.description: The width and height of the saved picture in pixels.

options.name: outputFormat
options.description: png, or jpeg with a quality from 0 to 1.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes the picture. Without it, or without a picture, there is no remove button.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Receives the encoded square picture, its size, the crop in the picked picture's pixels and the original file. While it runs Save shows progress; when it throws the editor stays open with an error.

states.name: no picture
states.description: The avatar shows initials; the picker button reads "Upload photo".

states.name: picture
states.description: The avatar shows the picture; the picker button reads "Change photo" and Remove photo appears when onRemove is set.

states.name: editing
states.description: A sheet with the picture in a square crop area, the cut-away part dimmed outside a circle or rounded square with a ring, a hint, the zoom slider, Save photo and Cancel.

states.name: saving
states.description: Save shows progress, Cancel and the slider are disabled, gestures and keys do nothing and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: error
states.description: A refused file (too large, not a picture) shows an error under the buttons; a failed save shows an error in the editor. Both have an icon and are announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every button is disabled.

appearance: The current picture is MonarchAvatar at the large size. In the editor the crop area has the muted fill behind the picture, the cut-away part is covered by the inverse background colour at a fixed fraction, and the kept area has a ring in the surface colour. Errors use the strong danger colour with an icon.
platformNotes: The picker is the system PhotosPicker, which needs no photo library permission; the web uses a file input with accept and size checks. The crop editor opens in a sheet instead of in place. The web draws the result with a canvas and offers WebP; on iOS Core Graphics renders it and Image I/O encodes PNG or JPEG (iOS cannot write WebP). Picked pictures are turned upright from their orientation data and decoded at no more than 2,048 pixels on the long side, so the crop is in the pixels of that upright picture. The editor area keeps left-to-right coordinates in right-to-left layouts because a photo is not mirrored. Disabled state comes from .disabled() rather than a parameter. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The avatar is read by name (MonarchAvatar); the picker, remove, save and cancel controls are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets.
The editor's title is a header.

The crop area is one element named "Photo position" with the zoom as its value ("150%") and the hint as its hint; swiping up or down zooms (adjustable action), and the actions rotor offers Move left, Move right, Move up, Move down and Reset position.
With a hardware keyboard the crop area takes focus: arrow keys move (four times as far with Shift), + and − zoom, Home resets, Return saves and Escape cancels.
The zoom slider is labelled "Zoom" and reads the zoom in percent.
Errors are announced and drawn with an icon and text, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A file that cannot be decoded as a picture, or that the picker cannot load, shows "This file can't be used as a photo."
A file exactly at maxFileSize is accepted.
The picture always covers the crop area: zoom stays between 100% and 400% and the picture cannot be moved past its edges.
Saving is ignored while a save is running, so a second tap or Return does not save twice.
The picture shown after saving is the app's: pass the new image or URL when onSave has stored it.

summary: A picture of a person or an entity, with initials or a symbol as the fallback, an optional presence dot, and an overlapping group with a "+N" tile.

whenNotToUse: For a website or app icon, use MonarchFavicon. For a presence without a picture, use MonarchPresenceDot. For uploading a new picture, use an avatar upload control.

options.name: image / url
options.description: The picture, from the app or loaded with AsyncImage. nil shows the fallback, which also shows while loading and after a failure.

options.name: name
options.description: The person or entity. Read by VoiceOver and used for the initials.

options.name: seed
options.description: Picks the fallback colour; the name by default. Pass a stable id so a renamed person keeps their colour.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: An SF Symbol shown instead of the initials, for entities without a logo.

options.name: shape
options.description: circle for people, square (rounded) for workspaces, organisations and brands.

options.name: size
options.description: xs (20), sm (24), md (32), lg (40) or xl (56) points before Dynamic Type.

options.name: status
options.description: A MonarchPresenceDot at the bottom trailing corner; its name is added to the spoken name.

options.name: isDecorative
options.description: Hides the avatar from VoiceOver when the name is written next to it.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the presence.

options.name: label (group)
options.description: Names the group for VoiceOver. Optional: without it the group is read as the number of people ("4 people").

options.name: maxVisible (group)
options.description: Show at most this many avatars, then a "+N" tile. With exactly one too many, all are shown.

options.name: overflowLabel (group)
options.description: Replaces the spoken "N more" of the tile.

states.name: image
states.description: The picture fills the shape.

states.name: initials
states.description: No picture, loading or failed: one or two initials on a subtle colour picked from the seed, in the strong colour of the same family.

states.name: symbol
states.description: With systemImage, or when the name has no letter or digit: the symbol (a person by default) on the same colours.

states.name: presence
states.description: A presence dot with a surface-coloured ring at the bottom trailing corner.

states.name: group overflow
states.description: A "+N" tile in the muted colours after the shown avatars, each ringed in the surface colour.

appearance: Fallback colours are five subtle-and-strong pairs of theme roles (accent, info, success, warning, AI), so they follow dark and both high-contrast themes; danger is left out so no face reads as an error. The square shape uses 6-point corners at sm and 8-point corners above. In a group each avatar is ringed with the surface colour and covers a quarter of the previous one.
platformNotes: The web derives a soft colour from a hue per name (or one of five data colours with palette="tokens"); iOS has no data colour roles, so it always uses five theme role pairs, picked with the same hash as the web so a seed lands on the same index. The web's xs and xl sizes and any number of pixels are not offered: Monarch's touch vocabulary is sm, md and lg, and a larger picture in a profile header can be an Image clipped by the app. The presence uses MonarchPresenceStatus, which adds do not disturb to the web's four. AvatarGroup on the web counts its children; SwiftUI cannot count view builder children on iOS 17, so the group takes the data and a content closure. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The avatar is one element with the image trait, named by the name, and by the presence when there is one ("Ana Silva, Online"); the name is built by a tested pure function.
The presence dot is not read on its own, and its form (bar, ring, half, square) keeps presence distinct without colour.
isDecorative hides the avatar from VoiceOver when the name is written beside it.
The group is a container named by its label; each avatar is read by its own name, then the tile as "2 more".
The avatar and its initials scale with Dynamic Type; initials shrink to fit rather than being cut.
edgeCases: An empty name or one made only of emoji shows the person symbol; the spoken name is the name as given.
Initials keep whole characters, so an emoji or an accented letter is never cut in half.
A URL that fails to load shows the fallback; a failure is not an error state.
In a group, give each avatar the same size and shape as the group; the group uses them for the overlap, the ring and the tile.

summary: Going one level up is the back button that NavigationStack adds to every pushed screen. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Push detail screens with NavigationLink or navigationDestination inside a NavigationStack. The back button, its label, the edge swipe and the long-press history are the system's.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a back link in the content of a screen, and do not hide the system back button to replace it with one. To close a sheet use a Cancel or Done button in its toolbar.

@Environment(\.dismiss) var dismiss: DismissAction

states.name: pushed
states.description: The navigation bar shows a back chevron with the title of the previous screen.

states.name: long previous title
states.description: The system shortens the label to "Back" when the title does not fit.

appearance: The system draws the back button in the tint of the navigation stack. monarchTheme sets the tint to the theme's accent, so apply it outside the NavigationStack. The chevron mirrors in a right-to-left layout.
platformNotes: The web BackLink is a link in the page content with a leading arrow, a variant and its own text ("Back to domains"). On iOS the label is the previous screen's navigation title, so name screens well instead of writing a back label. The web's variant has no equivalent: the bar is the system's. Android uses the navigation icon of the top app bar and the system back gesture.
accessibility: System behaviour: the back button is read as the previous screen's title with "Back button".
System behaviour: the VoiceOver escape gesture (a two-finger Z) and the edge swipe go back.
System behaviour: with a hardware keyboard, Command and the left bracket go back.
edgeCases: navigationBarBackButtonHidden(true) also turns off the edge swipe; use it only to guard unsaved changes, with a visible way out.
dismiss() pops the current screen from the stack; in a sheet it closes the sheet.
The root screen of a stack has no back button.

name: MonarchBacklogPlanner
title: BacklogPlanner
wrapsNative: List with Section(isExpanded:content:header:) per bucket, ForEach.onMove(perform:), draggable(_:) rows with DynamicViewContent.dropDestination(for:action:), a Menu with the other buckets and Move up and Move down, accessibilityActions, ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear) for capacity, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Plans work into buckets (iterations, sprints, releases and the backlog) with totals and capacity per bucket, and moves items by drag, a Move menu or VoiceOver actions.
whenToUse: For sprint or release planning: moving prioritised items between the backlog and upcoming iterations while watching each iteration's capacity.
whenNotToUse: For reordering one list use a List with onMove (the reorderable-list entry). For columns of work by status use a board. For a single item's details use MonarchIssueCard.
api: init(buckets: Binding<[MonarchBacklogBucket<Item>]>, itemLabel: @escaping (Item) -> String, points: ((Item) -> Int?)? = nil, canMove: ((_ item: Item, _ toBucketID: String, _ fromBucketID: String) -> Bool)? = nil, collapsed: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isReadOnly: Bool = false, labels: MonarchBacklogPlannerLabels = MonarchBacklogPlannerLabels(), onMove: (@MainActor (MonarchBacklogMove<Item.ID>) -> Void)? = nil, onBucketAction: (@MainActor (_ bucketID: String) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder row: @escaping (Item) -> Row)

struct MonarchBacklogBucket<Item: Identifiable> { init(id: String, title: String, subtitle: String? = nil, badge: String? = nil, badgeTone: MonarchTone = .info, capacity: Int? = nil, actionTitle: String? = nil, items: [Item], emptyMessage: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchBacklogMove<ItemID: Hashable> { let itemID: ItemID; let fromBucketID: String; let fromIndex: Int; let toBucketID: String; let toIndex: Int }

struct MonarchBacklogPlannerLabels { var capacityLabel, rowUnestimated, notEstimated, moveTo, moveUp, moveDown, empty, expanded, collapsed: String?; var summary: (@Sendable (Int, Int?, Int) -> String)?; var capacity: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)?; var overCapacity, rowPoints: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)?; var moveMenu, moveToBucket: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var moved: (@Sendable (String, String, Int, Int) -> String)? }

options.name: buckets
options.description: The buckets top to bottom, each with a title, optional subtitle, badge and capacity, and its items in priority order. Updated at once on every move.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: A short plain name of an item, such as its key, for the move menu and announcements.

options.name: points
options.description: The points of an item, nil when it has no estimate. Turns on totals, row points and capacity.

options.name: canMove
options.description: Whether an item may go to a bucket (item, to, from). Refused buckets are disabled in the menu, skipped by Move up and Move down, and refuse drops.

options.name: collapsed
options.description: The ids of closed buckets, when the app keeps them. Kept inside otherwise.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Turns off dragging, reordering and the move menu.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onMove
options.description: Runs after each finished move with the item, the buckets and the places, to save it.

options.name: row
options.description: The content of an item's row, such as a title, a MonarchIssueCard or pickers.

states.name: default
states.description: A section per bucket: a header with a disclosure chevron, the title, badge, subtitle and "5 items · 13 points", then the rows with their points and a Move menu.

states.name: capacity
states.description: With a capacity and points, a linear meter labelled "18 of 20 points".

states.name: over capacity
states.description: A warning icon and "Planned work is over capacity by 3 points." in the warning role; the meter stays full.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: The bucket shows only its header, with a forward chevron.

states.name: empty bucket
states.description: "Nothing here yet." or the bucket's own message in muted text.

states.name: dragging
states.description: The system drag preview of the row while it is dragged to a place in a bucket.

states.name: read only
states.description: No drag, no reorder and no Move menu.

appearance: The system list with Monarch type: headings in the default text role, counts, subtitles and row points in the muted role, the badge in the info tone, the capacity meter in the Monarch linear progress style and the over-capacity note in the warning strong role. All follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web draws its own drag handles with a keyboard pick-up mode and an optimistic save that a rejected promise undoes. On iOS the system drag and drop, onMove and VoiceOver actions do that work: the binding updates at once and onMove reports the move; the app sets the buckets back if the save fails. Bucket badges and actions are a text badge only; put bucket actions in the app's toolbar or the row content. Headings are header buttons rather than a heading level. Android has no entry yet. Several closures are optional (points, canMove, onMove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is points.
accessibility: Each bucket heading is a button with the header trait, read with "Expanded" or "Collapsed" as its value and the hint "Shows or hides the items."
Each row's Move menu is named "Move ENG-101 to…" and lists the other buckets, Move up and Move down; buckets that refuse the item are disabled.
The Move menu also carries Move up, Move down and "Move to Sprint 15" as VoiceOver actions.
Every move is announced: "ENG-101 moved to Sprint 15, position 1 of 3."
Row points are read as "5 points" or "Not estimated" instead of the abbreviations.
Over capacity is text with an icon, not only a colour; the capacity meter reads its label and value.
edgeCases: An empty bucket has no rows to drop between; use the Move menu or Move up and Move down to fill it.
Move up from the first item of a bucket goes to the end of the previous bucket that accepts it; Move down from the last goes to the start of the next.
Moving to a bucket from the menu puts the item at its end.
Drag payloads are item ids as text; ids must be unique across buckets.
Long bucket titles and rows wrap at the largest text sizes.
