name: MonarchBarChart
title: BarChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts Chart with BarMark (position(by:) for groups, yStart/yEnd for stacks), RuleMark for the zero and reference lines, RectangleMark for the inspected band, chartXSelection(value:) / chartYSelection(value:) for inspection; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and an AXChartDescriptor
summary: A bar or column chart of one or more series per category, grouped or stacked, vertical or horizontal, with value labels, a highlighted category, reference lines, touch inspection, legend toggles, drill-in and the data as a table.
whenToUse: To compare amounts across a handful of categories or periods, or to show how a few series make up each category's total.
whenNotToUse: For a ranked list of labelled values with no axis, use MonarchBarList. For a trend over many points, use a Swift Charts LineMark in MonarchChartFrame or MonarchSparkline. For parts of one whole, use MonarchDonutChart.
api: init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchBarChartSeries], description: String? = nil, categoryTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, orientation: MonarchBarChartOrientation = .vertical, layout: MonarchBarChartLayout = .grouped, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, highlightedIndex: Int? = nil, referenceLines: [MonarchBarChartReferenceLine] = [], valueRange: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, showsValueLabels: Bool = false, segmentSeparator: Bool = false, isLegendToggleable: Bool = true, isTableToggleShown: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchBarChartLabels = MonarchBarChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (Int) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchBarChartSeries.init(_ key: String, label: String, values: [Double?], color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
MonarchBarChartReferenceLine.init(_ value: Double, label: String? = nil)

MonarchBarChartLabels.init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), category: String? = nil, total: String? = nil, noData: String? = nil, details: String? = nil, clearSelection: String? = nil)
enum MonarchBarChartOrientation { case vertical, horizontal }
enum MonarchBarChartLayout { case grouped, stacked }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's accessibility label.

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in display order, already formatted by the app (dates, months, names).

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, each with a key, a label, one value per category and an optional colour slot.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: categoryTitle
options.description: The heading of the category column of the table and the name of VoiceOver's category axis.

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure; the name of VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: orientation
options.description: vertical columns or horizontal bars.

options.name: layout
options.description: With several series, grouped side by side or stacked.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready with no categories or no series shows empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Without it the chart keeps its own set, changed by the legend.

options.name: highlightedIndex
options.description: A category to emphasise; the bars of the others are dimmed.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines across the bars at a value, with an optional label.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. Swift Charts fits the values, zero and the reference lines when nil.

options.name: showsValueLabels
options.description: Writes each bar's value at its end; a stack shows its total once.

options.name: isLegendToggleable
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: isTableToggleShown
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height: 240 points for columns; 32 points per category, at least 120, for bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values on the value axis, in value labels, the inspection row, the table and the summary. A number in the current locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the category index from Details in the inspection row or from the VoiceOver action of that category.

options.name: segmentSeparator
options.description: Sets the parts of a stacked bar apart with a thin gap, so neighbouring series stay distinct without relying on colour. Stacked layout only.

states.name: ready
states.description: The plot, the legend (two or more series) and "View as table".

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a touch or drag on the plot: the category's band is shaded with the muted background and a row under the plot reads its values (and the stack total), with Details (when onSelect is set) and Clear. It stays until Clear or another category is touched.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: With highlightedIndex, the other categories' bars are drawn at reduced opacity.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: A hidden series is not drawn and its legend entry is struck through; the others keep their colours. The table still lists it.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" replaces the plot with every category and series as text, plus a Total column when stacked.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's muted placeholder of the plot's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: Bars take the theme's data slots 1 to 5 in series order, then the subtle text colour. The value grid uses the subtle border colour, the zero line the strong border colour, and axis and value labels the muted text colour. Reference lines are dashed in the subtle text colour. The inspected band uses the muted background. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts instead of the web's hand-drawn SVG. Touch inspection uses chartXSelection / chartYSelection; the values show in a row under the plot rather than a floating tooltip, so they are never clipped and wrap at large text sizes. There is no keyboard arrow navigation; VoiceOver gets the chart descriptor (Audio Graphs) and one action per category for drill-in instead. Categories are strings the app has formatted (the web formats dates and numbers itself). Series have no dashed style: Swift Charts bars cannot be outlined with a dash; use the neutral colour slot for a comparison series. hiddenSeries is a Binding (controlled) or internal state, not separate default and change callbacks. The inspected category is internal, not a controlled activeIndex. Android ships the same MonarchBarChart. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The plot is one accessibility element labelled with the title. Its value is the generated summary (number and range of categories, each shown series' total and highest category, each reference line) or the summary parameter.

The plot carries an AXChartDescriptor built from the table: a categorical axis of the categories, a numeric axis named by valueTitle, and one series per table column with the app's formatted values, for Audio Graphs and the chart data rotor.
With onSelect, the plot has one VoiceOver custom action per category, named "Details, <category>".
The inspection row is ordinary text followed by MonarchButton controls with 44-point targets.
The legend is MonarchChartLegend: each entry is a switch that is on while its series is shown; the last visible series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value as text; each table row is read as the category, then each series and its value.
Series are told apart by the legend's names and the table, not by colour alone; a highlighted category is also reported by nothing but opacity, so the highlight is decorative.
edgeCases: Gaps (nil) and values that are not finite draw no bar, are written "No value" in the inspection row and "–" in the table, and are left out of the summary and the chart descriptor.
Negative values draw below (or before) the zero line; in a stack they stack down from zero separately from the positive values, and the stack's label shows the net total at the end with its sign.
Categories with the same text are one category to Swift Charts; give each a distinct label.
More than five series: the sixth and later are neutral, as in the legend.
Long category names in horizontal bars wrap or are truncated by Swift Charts' axis; the full names are in the table and the inspection row.
A highlightedIndex outside the categories dims every bar.
chartXSelection and Audio Graphs were not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; the descriptor, summary, inspection text and action names are unit-tested.

name: MonarchBarList
title: BarList
wrapsNative: VStack of rows, each with a bar drawn in background(_:); Button for tappable rows
summary: A ranked list with a bar behind each row's label: top pages, top referrers, rivals by score.
whenToUse: To compare up to a dozen named values where the names matter as much as the sizes.
whenNotToUse: For values over time, use a sparkline or a chart. For a scrolling list of many rows with swipe actions, use a List and draw the bar in the row yourself.
api: MonarchBarList.init(_ label: String? = nil, items: [MonarchBarListItem], sort: MonarchBarListSort = .descending, maximum: Double? = nil, limit: Int? = nil, isRanked: Bool = false, isLoading: Bool = false, loadingRows: Int = 5, error: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, missingLabel: String? = nil, emptyLabel: String? = nil, loadingLabel: String? = nil, overflowLabel: String? = nil, retryLabel: String? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchBarListItem) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchBarListItem.init(_ label: String, id: String? = nil, value: Double?, description: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, displayValue: String? = nil, isHighlighted: Bool = false)

options.name: label
options.description: Names the list for VoiceOver, such as "Top pages".

options.name: items
options.description: The rows.

options.name: sort
options.description: descending, ascending or none. Rows without a value go last.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The value of a full bar. The largest value when nil. Pass 1 for ratios of a whole.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows only the first rows, with a "Top 5 of 12" footer.

options.name: isRanked
options.description: Numbers the rows.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows redacted placeholder rows instead of the rows. VoiceOver reads Loading.

options.name: loadingRows
options.description: How many placeholder rows to show while loading, from 1 to 12.

options.name: error
options.description: A message shown instead of the rows when they could not be loaded. With onRetry it is a MonarchInlineErrorRetry.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Whether a retry is running. The retry button waits and reads Retrying.

options.name: retryLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in title Try again of the retry button.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry button to the error. Pass it with its label, onRetry:.

options.name: missingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text "No value".

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No data yet".

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "Loading".

options.name: overflowLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in footer "Top 5 of 12".

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the current locale.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes every row a button.

states.name: default
states.description: Rows sorted by value, each with a bar as long as its share of the largest value.

states.name: highlighted row
states.description: A stronger bar and a heavier label and value.

states.name: missing value
states.description: A dash instead of the value and no bar.

states.name: empty
states.description: The text "No data yet".

states.name: loading
states.description: Redacted placeholder rows, read as one Loading element.

appearance: Bars use the accent subtle colour behind default text; a highlighted row uses the stronger accent subtle colour and semibold text. Ranks, descriptions and the footer are muted text, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web draws the bar on a track under the label or inline; here the bar is behind the label, the usual form on a narrow screen, so there is no layout option. The web formats numbers, percentages and currencies from options; here formatValue takes a closure, so an app writes $0.formatted(.percent) or a currency style itself. Row links (href) become onSelect, because navigation in an app is not a URL. Like the web, loading draws skeleton rows and a failed load shows MonarchInlineErrorRetry. Row icons are SF Symbols. The bar grows from the leading edge, so it is mirrored in right-to-left layouts. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The list is an accessibility container with the given label.
Each row is one element: its label and description, then its value. A row without a value reads "No value".
Bars and rank numbers are not read; the order of the rows carries the rank.
With onSelect each row is a button with a touch target at least 44 points high.
A highlighted row is heavier as well as stronger in colour. The emphasis is not spoken, so say why in the label.
Labels scale with Dynamic Type and wrap.
edgeCases: Equal values keep the order they were given in.
Values that are not finite are treated as missing.
Negative values and an all-zero list draw no bars.
A value above maximum draws a full bar.
limit hides rows but the scale still uses the largest value of all items.
Item ids default to the label, so give an id when two rows have the same label.

summary: A block document editor: paragraphs, headings, lists, checklists, quotes, code, callouts, toggles, tables and embeds as rows of a List, with a slash menu, block actions, reordering, multiple selection and undo.
whenToUse: For a document that people build from blocks on the phone: notes, briefs, wiki pages, launch plans. Make it the main content of a screen.

api: init(_ label: String, blocks: Binding<[MonarchBlock]>, prompt: String? = nil, kinds: [MonarchBlockKind] = MonarchBlockKind.defaultKinds, embedProviders: [MonarchEmbedProvider] = MonarchEmbedProvider.defaults, isReadOnly: Bool = false, showsToolbar: Bool = true, slashItems: [MonarchSlashMenuItem] = [], labels: MonarchBlockEditorLabels = MonarchBlockEditorLabels(), onSlashItem: (@MainActor (MonarchSlashMenuItem, String) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchBlock: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable { var id: String; var kind: MonarchBlockKind; var text: String; var detail: String; var isChecked: Bool; var isExpanded: Bool; var table: MonarchTableBlockData?; init(id: String = UUID().uuidString, kind: MonarchBlockKind = .paragraph, text: String = "", detail: String = "", isChecked: Bool = false, isExpanded: Bool = true, table: MonarchTableBlockData? = nil) }

enum MonarchBlockKind: Sendable, Hashable { case paragraph, heading(Int), bulletList, orderedList, taskList, blockquote, codeBlock, callout(MonarchTone), toggle, table, embed; static let defaultKinds: [MonarchBlockKind]; var isText: Bool }

struct MonarchBlockEditorLabels: Sendable { init(handle: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, handleHint: String? = nil, moveUp: String? = nil, moveDown: String? = nil, duplicate: String? = nil, deleteBlock: String? = nil, deleteSelected: String? = nil, turnInto: String? = nil, tone: String? = nil, toneNames: [MonarchTone: String] = [:], select: String? = nil, done: String? = nil, selectedCount: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, listItem: (@Sendable (String, Int) -> String)? = nil, blockNames: [MonarchBlockKind: String] = [:], blockDescriptions: [MonarchBlockKind: String] = [:], groupText: String? = nil, groupLists: String? = nil, groupBlocks: String? = nil, summaryPrompt: String? = nil, detailPrompt: String? = nil, embedPrompt: String? = nil, addBlock: String? = nil, toolbar: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), slashMenu: MonarchSlashMenuLabels = MonarchSlashMenuLabels(), table: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels(), embed: MonarchEmbedBlockLabels = MonarchEmbedBlockLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The editor's name for VoiceOver, already localised, such as the document's title.

options.name: blocks
options.description: The document. The editor never leaves it empty: deleting every block leaves one empty paragraph.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder of an empty paragraph with the caret, and of a one-block empty document. Built in: Write, or type / for blocks.

options.name: kinds
options.description: The kinds offered by the slash menu, the toolbar and Turn into, in order. .callout(tone) sets the tone a new callout starts with. Kinds already in the document are always shown.

options.name: embedProviders
options.description: The sites that embed blocks may frame; other links show as link cards.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the blocks as text, without the toolbar, action buttons, swipes, dragging or the slash menu.

options.name: showsToolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar with undo, redo, text styles, lists and Select blocks above the document.

options.name: slashItems
options.description: Product items added to the slash menu after the block kinds.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the toolbar's, the slash menu's, tables' and embeds'.

options.name: onSlashItem
options.description: Receives a product slash item and the id of the block it was typed in, after the typed command is removed from the text.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each block is a field in its kind's style, with an action button before it; the toolbar shows the kind of the block with the caret as on.

states.name: slash menu
states.description: While a / command is typed at the start of a word, the slash menu shows above the keyboard and filters as people type.

states.name: selecting
states.description: Select blocks puts the list in multiple selection; a bar shows how many are selected with Duplicate, Delete and Done.

states.name: dragging
states.description: Touching and holding a block lifts it with the system list reordering.

states.name: empty
states.description: One empty paragraph shows the prompt.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Blocks are text; tables and embeds are read-only; no toolbar, buttons, swipes or dragging.

states.name: disabled
states.description: As read-only, with the disabled text colour.

appearance: A borderless document on the surface colour. Text uses the default text colour by kind (title, heading and subheading styles for headings 1 to 3, code style on the subtle fill for code); list markers are muted, ticked checklist items are muted and struck through, quotes have a strong border bar. Callouts, toggles, tables and embeds keep their own components' roles, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web BlockEditor is one Tiptap document with rich inline text. iOS has no shared engine, so each block is its own field and block text is plain: inline bold, italic, code and links are not stored (use MonarchRichTextEditor for rich text in one field). Selecting text across several blocks is replaced by the iPhone pattern, multiple selection of whole blocks. The web's columns and image blocks are not offered: columns do not fit beside each other on a phone and images need the app's upload. There is no selection bubble menu (see bubble-menu: the system edit menu is used), and keyboard shortcuts (Alt+Shift+arrows, Cmd+Z) are replaced by the action button, accessibility actions and the toolbar's undo and redo. Backspace in an empty block does not delete it; use the swipe or the action button. The value is an array of MonarchBlock, not HTML or JSON. Android has not built it yet; it plans the same name.
accessibility: The editor is a container named by label.
Each block's field is named by its kind (Heading 2, Numbered list, item 3); headings have the header trait.
Each block's action button is named Block actions: <kind>, has a hint, and offers Move up and Move down as accessibility actions, so moving never needs a drag.
Checklist boxes are standard toggles (Monarch checkbox style) named by the item's text; ticked state is the checkmark and the toggle value, not colour alone.
List markers and the quote bar are hidden from VoiceOver.
The slash menu announces how many options match while focus stays in the text.
Rows, the action buttons and the add button are at least 44 points high; text follows Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Return in a list item starts another item; Return in an empty item ends the list.
Markdown shortcuts only apply to paragraphs and only for kinds in kinds.
Typing in one block is undone as one step; moving the caret to another block starts a new step. The history keeps 100 steps and is lost when the view is recreated.
A table block without data shows an empty 3 by 3 table; deleting the table from its own menu deletes the block.
Embeds wait for a tap before loading anything from the site.
Duplicate ids in the document are not supported: give every block a unique id.
The editor needs a height: in a ScrollView give it a frame.

title: BookingFlow
wrapsNative: NavigationStack(path:) with navigationDestination(for:) for each step, a List of service Buttons, MonarchTimezoneSelect and MonarchSlotPicker in a ScrollView, MonarchTextField fields, a List of LabeledContent for the review, MonarchStepper(compact: .always) for progress, MonarchButton in safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom), and MonarchEmptyState(kind: .success) for the confirmation
summary: A recipe, not a component: booking an appointment step by step on a navigation stack: service, time, details, review and confirmation, with progress on every step.
whenToUse: When a visitor or a member of staff books an appointment, meeting or interview in a few ordered steps that end in one submit.
whenNotToUse: For only choosing a time use MonarchSlotPicker on its own. For moving an existing booking use the reschedule-dialog recipe. For long forms with branching sections use MonarchStepper with your own form.
api: NavigationStack(path: $path) { List { Section { MonarchStepper(steps, current: 0, compact: .always) }; Section("Choose a service") { Button { …; path.append(.time) } } }.navigationTitle("Book a session").navigationDestination(for: Step.self) { step in switch step { case .time: MonarchTimezoneSelect(…); MonarchSlotPicker(selection:day:slots:timeZone:) case .details: MonarchTextField(…) case .review: List { LabeledContent(…) } } } }
Continue and Book: MonarchButton(…, variant: .primary, isLoading:, fullWidth: true) in .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom). Confirmation: MonarchEmptyState(…, kind: .success).

options.name: steps
options.description: The step labels for the progress indicator; leave out steps that do not apply, such as choosing a host.

options.name: service step
options.description: The root of the stack: tapping a service chooses it and pushes the time step.

options.name: time step
options.description: Open times for the chosen day, with MonarchTimezoneSelect for the visitor's zone. Continue is disabled until a time is chosen.

options.name: details step
options.description: Name, email and any questions the product asks.

options.name: review step
options.description: The summary of every choice; Back changes any of them.

options.name: submit
options.description: Book on the review step; it shows "Booking…" while the request runs and keeps the steps when it fails.

options.name: confirmation
options.description: Replaces the steps after a successful booking.

states.name: service
states.description: The root list; the stepper shows step 1 of 4.

states.name: time
states.description: The slot picker; Continue is disabled until a time is chosen.

states.name: details
states.description: The fields; Continue is disabled until they are valid.

states.name: review
states.description: The summary and Book.

states.name: booking
states.description: Book shows a progress indicator and "Booking…".

states.name: failed
states.description: The steps stay; show MonarchInlineErrorRetry above Book with the reason.

states.name: booked
states.description: The confirmation replaces the steps and the stack returns to its root.

appearance: System lists and navigation bars with Monarch fields, slot picker, compact stepper and the primary Monarch button pinned above the home indicator. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web ships BookingFlow as one component with a steps or list layout, a summary aside and a focus move with "Step 2 of 4" announcements. On a phone each step is a screen on a navigation stack: the system back button and swipe go back a step, the navigation title names the step and VoiceOver reads it when the screen appears, and the compact stepper shows the progress. The web's summary aside becomes the review step. The web's brandColor tenant colour is not offered; Monarch buttons use the theme. useBookingFlow's next, back and goTo are the navigation path the app owns. Android has the same recipe coverage and status (available).
accessibility: Each step is its own screen; VoiceOver reads its navigation title when it appears and the back button names the previous step.
MonarchStepper reads the progress as "Step 2 of 4: Time".
Continue is disabled, not hidden, until the step is complete, so the reason stays discoverable.
Book announces its loading state through MonarchButton; the confirmation is text with a decorative symbol.
Every button is at least 44 points; the fields have visible labels.
edgeCases: Changing the day clears the chosen time in MonarchSlotPicker.
When nothing can be booked, show MonarchEmptyState instead of the first step.
At the largest text sizes each step scrolls and the Continue button stays above the keyboard and home indicator.
A failed booking keeps every choice so the person can try again.

title: BottomTabBar
wrapsNative: TabView(selection:content:) with tabItem(_:), tag(_:) and badge(_:)
summary: The standard TabView: three to five top-level destinations in the system tab bar, with the theme's accent as the selected colour. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For the top-level areas of an app that people switch between constantly. Give each tab a Label with a short title and an SF Symbol.
whenNotToUse: For views of one screen's content use MonarchTabs (see tabs). For more than five destinations, or on an iPad, use a sidebar (see sidebar-nav).
api: TabView(selection: Binding<SelectionValue>?, content: () -> Content)
func tabItem(_ label: () -> some View) -> some View
func tag(_ tag: some Hashable) -> some View
func badge(_ count: Int) -> some View

states.name: selected
states.description: The tab's symbol and title take the tint, and the system uses the filled variant of the symbol.

states.name: badge
states.description: A red system badge with a count or a text on the tab.

appearance: The system draws the bar with its material, above the home indicator. The selected tab takes the tint, which monarchTheme sets to the theme's accent; the badge is the system's red.
platformNotes: The parity map named TabView with Tab. Tab and its builder are iOS 18 API and do not compile against the iOS 17 deployment target, so the entry documents the tabItem form, which works on iOS 17 and later; an app that requires iOS 18 can write Tab("Home", systemImage: "house", value: .home) { … } instead. The web BottomTabBar draws its own bar with links, an active icon, a badge and badgeLabel, safe-area padding, a fixed position and hideFrom. On iOS the bar, the insets, the filled active symbol and the badge are the system's, and tabs are views, not links. Android uses the Material NavigationBar.
accessibility: System behaviour: the bar is a tab bar; each item is read with its title, "tab", its position and whether it is selected.
System behaviour: a badge is read with the tab ("3 items").
System behaviour: touching and holding the bar shows a large version of the item for people using large text.
Give every tab a title. An image without a title has no name.
edgeCases: More than five tabs on a phone become a More tab; keep to five.
Each tab keeps its own state, so put a NavigationStack inside each tab, not around the TabView.
The tab bar's titles do not scale with Dynamic Type; the system's large-content viewer covers that.

name: MonarchBreadcrumb
title: Breadcrumb
wrapsNative: HStack of Button with buttonStyle(.monarchLink(.subtle)), Menu for the collapsed levels, ViewThatFits with ScrollView(.horizontal) and ScrollViewReader
summary: A trail of the levels above the current screen, the current level last, with the middle levels of a long trail collapsed into a menu.
whenToUse: In a deep hierarchy where people need to jump back several levels at once: folders in a file browser, nested projects or categories.
whenNotToUse: On ordinary screens of a NavigationStack, where the navigation bar title and the back button already show the place (see back-link). For switching between sibling views use MonarchTabs.
api: MonarchBreadcrumb.init(_ items: [MonarchBreadcrumbItem], maxVisible: Int = 4, labels: MonarchBreadcrumbLabels = MonarchBreadcrumbLabels(), action: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchBreadcrumbItem) -> Void)
MonarchBreadcrumbItem.init(_ title: String, id: String? = nil, isLinked: Bool = true)
MonarchBreadcrumbLabels.init(label: String? = nil, more: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, current: String? = nil)

options.name: items
options.description: The levels from the root to the current screen. Each has a title, an id (the title by default) and isLinked.

options.name: maxVisible
options.description: The most levels shown. Above it the first level stays, the middle levels collapse into a menu and the last maxVisible - 2 stay. Values below 3 count as 3.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken name of the trail ("Breadcrumb"), of the menu button ("Show 3 more levels") and of the current level's value ("Current page").

options.name: action
options.description: Goes to the chosen level, for example by trimming a NavigationStack path. It is not called for the last level or for a level that is not linked.

states.name: linked ancestor
states.description: A button in the subtle link style: muted text, underlined while pressed or when Button Shapes is on.

states.name: not linked
states.description: An ancestor with isLinked false is muted text, and is a disabled item in the collapsed menu.

states.name: current
states.description: The last level is text in the default colour and a medium weight, never a link.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: An ellipsis button in the ghost button style stands for the middle levels and opens a Menu of them.

states.name: overflowing
states.description: When the trail is wider than the space, it scrolls sideways and starts scrolled to the current level.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the trail disables every link and the menu; links take the disabled text colour.

appearance: Text in the label type role. Ancestors use the muted text colour, the current level the default text colour, and the chevron separators the subtle text colour. The menu button is a ghost button. All roles come from the theme, so the trail follows light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Breadcrumb is a nav of links with href and a linkAs component. On iOS each level is a button that calls the action, so the app moves its NavigationStack path or reloads the folder. The web's locale prop is the environment's locale, used to format the hidden count. A web item without href is isLinked false. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The trail is one container named "Breadcrumb" (replaceable with labels.label); VoiceOver moves through its levels in order.
Ancestors are buttons with their title as the name. The last level is static text whose value is "Current page".
The chevron separators are decorative and hidden.
The collapsed-levels button is named "Show 3 more levels", with the number formatted for the locale; its menu is the system Menu, and levels without a screen are disabled in it.
Links and the menu button have a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points. Text scales with Dynamic Type and stays on one line; the trail scrolls instead of truncating.
The separators use the chevron.forward symbol, which points the reading direction in right-to-left languages.
edgeCases: An empty items array draws nothing; one item is shown alone as the current level.
Titles are not truncated. A very long trail scrolls sideways; at the largest text sizes this happens sooner.
Two levels may share a title; give them distinct ids so the action can tell them apart.
When items change, the trail scrolls to the new current level.

title: BubbleMenu
wrapsNative: The system edit menu that TextEditor and TextField show over a selection (with Format on TextEditor(text: Binding<AttributedString>, selection:) from iOS 26); selection actions go in ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard), or into the menu itself with UITextViewDelegate.textView(_:editMenuForTextIn:suggestedActions:) in UIKit; the open menu in the example is MonarchEditorToolbar(groups: MonarchEditorTool.inlineGroups) over the text with MonarchElevation
summary: The menu over selected text is the system edit menu; Monarch ships no floating toolbar of its own.
whenToUse: Whenever people select text in an editor: the system menu already offers Cut, Copy, Paste, Look Up, Translate and Share, and Format for rich text. Put actions about the selection (Comment, Ask about this) in a keyboard toolbar that is enabled while the selection is not empty.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a second floating toolbar over a selection; it would cover or fight the system menu. For a full set of formatting controls, use MonarchEditorToolbar or MonarchRichTextEditor.
api: TextEditor(text: Binding<String>)
TextEditor(text: Binding<AttributedString>, selection: Binding<AttributedTextSelection>) // iOS 26
ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard) { … }
UITextViewDelegate.textView(_:editMenuForTextIn:suggestedActions:) -> UIMenu? // UIKit

states.name: no selection
states.description: No menu; a selection action in the keyboard toolbar is disabled.

states.name: text selected
states.description: The system shows its edit menu next to the selection; the keyboard toolbar action becomes enabled.

states.name: rich text selected
states.description: On iOS 26, a rich TextEditor adds the system Format items to the menu.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Text with .textSelection(.enabled) offers Copy and Share only.

appearance: System appearance in every theme, including dark and the high-contrast settings. Only the keyboard toolbar button takes Monarch's ghost button style and theme colours.
platformNotes: The web BubbleMenu floats a Tiptap toolbar over the selection and takes focus with Alt+F10. iOS already shows its own edit menu at the selection, positioned and announced by the system, so Monarch adds nothing there. SwiftUI has no API to add items to that menu; a UIKit text view adds them in textView(_:editMenuForTextIn:suggestedActions:) (iOS 16 and later). The web placement and offset options have no counterpart. Android's plan is the same: its platform text selection menu, with no Monarch type.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver reads the edit menu's items and the rotor's Edit actions reach the same commands.
The keyboard toolbar action is a standard button with a text label, disabled while nothing is selected.
edgeCases: Plain TextField and TextEditor have no selection binding before iOS 18; selection actions need iOS 18 (TextSelection) or iOS 26 (AttributedTextSelection) in SwiftUI.
The keyboard toolbar only shows while the keyboard does; with a hardware keyboard, offer the same action elsewhere, such as a toolbar button.

examples.title: Inline formatting
examples.template:
// The menu open above the text, as the web shows it while words are selected. An app shows it when its own

ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {

        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
        .accessibilityLabel({{label}})
        .scrollContentBackground(.hidden)
        .padding(.top, theme.spacing.space8)

        .padding(.top, theme.spacing.space6)
    MonarchEditorToolbar(groups: MonarchEditorTool.inlineGroups) { _ in }
        .padding(.horizontal, theme.spacing.space2)
        .monarchElevation(.md, fill: \.bgRaised, in: RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius: theme.radius.md, style: .continuous))
        .padding(.leading, theme.spacing.space3)
}

@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme
@State private var text = {{text}}

ZStack(alignment: .topLeading) {

        .monarchTextStyle(.body)
        .accessibilityLabel("Sample text")
        .scrollContentBackground(.hidden)

        .padding(.horizontal, theme.spacing.space2)

name: MonarchBulkActionBar
title: BulkActionBar
wrapsNative: ViewThatFits of an HStack (wide) or a VStack with MonarchFlowLayout (narrow) of Text, MonarchButton and a Menu with .menuStyle(.button); placed by the app in safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) over a List(selection:)
summary: The bar shown while items are selected: the count, the actions for the selection with a More menu for the rest, and Clear selection, with the count announced.
whenToUse: Under a List or table with multiple selection when several actions apply to everything selected and the count should be visible and announced.
whenNotToUse: For actions on one row, use swipeActions and a Menu on the row (see row-actions-menu). For screen actions unrelated to a selection, use the navigation bar's toolbar. For a single action on the selection in an edit-mode list, a ToolbarItem(placement: .bottomBar) is enough.
api: init(count: Int, totalCount: Int? = nil, actions: [MonarchBulkAction] = [], maxVisibleActions: Int = 3, isBusy: Bool = false, busyActionID: String? = nil, labels: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels(), onClear: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, @ViewBuilder accessories: () -> Accessories)

init(count: Int, totalCount: Int? = nil, actions: [MonarchBulkAction] = [], maxVisibleActions: Int = 3, isBusy: Bool = false, busyActionID: String? = nil, labels: MonarchBulkActionBarLabels = MonarchBulkActionBarLabels(), onClear: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void) where Accessories == EmptyView
struct MonarchBulkAction: Identifiable { init(id: String, title: String, systemImage: String? = nil, isDestructive: Bool = false, isDisabled: Bool = false, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void) }
struct MonarchBulkActionBarLabels { var selected: (@Sendable (Int, Int?) -> String)?; var cleared, clear, more, bar: String? }

options.name: count
options.description: The number of selected items. The bar is shown while it is above zero and takes no room at zero.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The number of items that could be selected, for "3 of 120 selected".

options.name: actions
options.description: The actions. A destructive one uses the danger button variant and the destructive menu role.

options.name: maxVisibleActions
options.description: How many actions are buttons; the rest go into a More menu.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: Blocks every action while the app runs one.

options.name: busyActionID
options.description: The running action shows a progress indicator; the others and the More menu are disabled.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the count, the clear and More titles, the cleared announcement and the bar's spoken name.

options.name: onClear
options.description: Empties the selection.

options.name: accessories
options.description: Extra controls after the actions, such as a Picker for a property.

states.name: closed
states.description: Nothing is selected: nothing is drawn and the bar takes no room.

states.name: open
states.description: The count, the action buttons, More and Clear selection on a raised surface.

states.name: busy
states.description: With busyActionID the action shows progress and the others are disabled; with isBusy everything is disabled.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When one line does not fit, the count and Clear take the first line and the actions wrap below.

appearance: A raised surface (the surface background role, the medium elevation and the subtle border role) with a 12-point corner. The count is label-size semibold text in the default text role. Actions are small secondary MonarchButtons, destructive ones the danger variant; Clear selection is a ghost button.
platformNotes: The parity map named .toolbar(placement: .bottomBar) with EditMode. A bottom toolbar holds only a few plain items, cannot show the count with the actions and a More menu in Monarch styling, and does not exist on macOS, so the bar is a view the app places with safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) under a List(selection:) in EditMode, or inline above a table. The web toolbar has one tab stop with arrow keys; on iOS each control is its own element for VoiceOver and the system keyboard focus. The web can wait on a promise returned by an action; on iOS the app sets busyActionID or isBusy. Confirmation of destructive actions stays in the app (confirmationDialog). Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The bar is a container named "Bulk actions"; the count is read first, then each action, More and Clear selection.
Every change of the count is announced ("2 of 4 selected"), including when the bar first appears, and "Selection cleared" when it closes.
Icons are decorative; every action has a visible title.
Buttons keep 44-point touch targets; a running action keeps its button enabled and reads its progress through MonarchButton.
edgeCases: maxVisibleActions of 0 puts every action in the More menu; a negative value counts as 0.
An action that empties the selection closes the bar and announces "Selection cleared".
The count text uses the English plural-free form "3 selected"; pass labels.selected for languages that need plural forms.

title: BulkDestructiveFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) with interactiveDismissDisabled while running, holding a VStack that moves through three phases: MonarchConsequenceList and MonarchTypeToConfirmInput to confirm, ProgressView with .monarchLinear while deleting, MonarchBanner for the result
summary: A recipe, not a component: "Delete 37 leads" confirms a bulk deletion with a sample and its consequences, asks for the count to be typed, runs it with a progress bar while the sheet is locked, then reports the items that failed.
whenToUse: When people delete many selected items at once (from a MonarchBulkActionBar), the deletion cannot be undone, and some items may fail on the server.
whenNotToUse: For one item, or a few with no partial failure, use confirmationDialog. For a change that can be undone, delete at once and offer Undo (see undo-toast). For deleting a whole workspace, use MonarchTypeToConfirmInput with its name in a sheet.
api: func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> some View) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View
MonarchConsequenceList.init(_ items: [MonarchConsequence], heading: String? = nil, …)
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput.init(phrase: String, text: Binding<String>, label: String? = nil, …)
static func MonarchTypeToConfirmInput.matches(_ text: String, phrase: String) -> Bool
ProgressView(_ title: String, value: Double?, total: Double).progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear)
MonarchBanner.init(_ title: String? = nil, message: String, tone: MonarchTone = .info, …)

states.name: confirm
states.description: The title with the count, a sample of three names and "+34 more", the consequences, a field asking for the count, and a danger button disabled until the count matches.

states.name: running
states.description: A linear progress bar with "12 of 37 deleted"; the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: done
states.description: A success banner when every item was deleted.

states.name: partial
states.description: A warning banner with "36 of 37 leads deleted" and the items that failed with their reason; the app can offer a retry for those items.

appearance: A sheet on the system's sheet background with Monarch components: the danger MonarchButton, the consequence list's icons and tones, the linear progress style in the accent role, and success or warning banners.
platformNotes: The web BulkDestructiveFlow is a component built on WizardDialog with plural rules (Intl.PluralRules), a typeCountAbove threshold, an optional step-up authentication and a retry step. On iOS it composes existing parts in a sheet, so the app decides the threshold for typing the count, writes plural forms with its String Catalog, and runs re-authentication (for example LocalAuthentication) before the deletion. The web's progress callback is the app's own loop updating a counter. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the consequence list reads each consequence with its kind.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed count matches, and the delete button stays disabled until it does.
The standard ProgressView reads its title and value, so VoiceOver can follow "12 of 37 deleted".
Announce the result with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when the run ends, since focus does not move.
edgeCases: Lock the sheet with interactiveDismissDisabled while the deletion runs, so it cannot be dismissed half way.
Keep the failed items selected after Done so the person can retry or inspect them.
If nothing could be deleted (the request failed), show the error on the confirmation phase and keep the typed count.

name: MonarchBurndownChart
title: BurndownChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts: Chart with LineMark for the remaining and dashed ideal lines and the scope step line, PointMark with an annotation for each scope change and for lone and inspected points, RuleMark for the dashed today marker and the crosshair, chartXSelection(value:) for touch inspection, inside MonarchChartFrame (accessibilityChartDescriptor and View as table)
summary: A sprint burndown: work remaining each day against the ideal line, with the scope line and its changes, a today marker and a sentence saying whether the sprint is ahead or behind.
whenToUse: For a time-boxed iteration with an estimate of remaining work per day, to show whether it will finish on time, and to show scope changes next to progress so a flat stretch is explained.
whenNotToUse: For open-ended work without a fixed end, use MonarchLineChart of throughput or a stacked MonarchAreaChart for cumulative flow. To compare several sprints, use a bar chart of completed work per sprint.

MonarchBurndownChartPoint.init(date: Date, remaining: Double? = nil, scope: Double? = nil)
MonarchBurndownChartPoint.init(label: String, remaining: Double? = nil, scope: Double? = nil)
enum MonarchBurndownChartLine: String { case remaining, ideal, scope }

MonarchBurndownChartLabels.init(remaining: String? = nil, ideal: String? = nil, scope: String? = nil, day: String? = nil, today: String? = nil, scopeChange: String? = nil, change: (@Sendable (_ amount: String, _ added: Bool) -> String)? = nil, status: (@Sendable (_ day: String, _ remaining: String, _ ideal: String) -> String)? = nil, ahead: (@Sendable (_ amount: String) -> String)? = nil, behind: (@Sendable (_ amount: String) -> String)? = nil, onTrack: String? = nil, scopeSummary: (@Sendable (_ scope: String, _ added: String, _ removed: String) -> String)? = nil, notStarted: String? = nil, frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels())

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, a heading in the frame and the name VoiceOver reads.

options.name: points
options.description: One point per sprint day, in order, including days not reached yet (no remaining), each with a date or a label, remaining work and scope.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title. Default: the generated summary, such as "Mar 6: 24 remaining, ideal 17.8, 6.2 behind ideal. Scope 43, 5 added and 2 removed since the start".

options.name: idealStart
options.description: The work at the start of the ideal line. Default: the first day's scope, else its remaining. The ideal reaches zero on the last day.

options.name: todayIndex
options.description: The day of the today marker. Default: the latest day with a remaining value, when later days exist. An index outside the days draws no marker.

options.name: showsToday
options.description: Whether the today marker is drawn at all.

options.name: showsScope
options.description: Whether the scope line, its changes and the scope columns are shown, when any day has a scope.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error, drawn by the frame. A ready chart with no points is empty.

options.name: hiddenLines
options.description: The hidden lines. Kept inside when nil. The legend keeps one line visible.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected day, to share a crosshair between charts. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: dateFormat
options.description: How dated points are written on the axis, in the popover, the table and the summary.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The empty-state message.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The height of the plot; 240 points by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the frame's.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value, such as "24 pts", everywhere the chart writes one. Default: a number in the locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: in progress
states.description: The remaining line stops at the latest day with data; the dashed today marker stands on that day; the summary says how far ahead or behind the ideal it is.

states.name: ahead, behind, on track
states.description: The summary compares the latest remaining value with the ideal that day, rounded to two decimals.

states.name: not started
states.description: No day has a remaining value: the summary says "Not started" and only the ideal (and scope) are drawn.

states.name: scope changes
states.description: The scope is a step line; each day it changes has a dot and a "+5" or "−2" label, and the popover has a Scope change footer.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: While the plot is touched, or activeIndex is set: a crosshair, a point on the remaining line and a popover with remaining, ideal and scope that day.

states.name: line hidden
states.description: Remaining, ideal or scope can be hidden from the legend; the last visible line stays. Hidden lines stay in the data table.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: Drawn by MonarchChartFrame at the chart's height.

appearance: Remaining is the first data colour and the thickest line; the ideal is the neutral subtle text colour, dashed; scope is the second data colour, a thinner step line. Scope change labels are the default text colour; the today marker is a dashed strong border line with a muted label. The crosshair is the strong border colour and the popover the raised surface with a medium shadow. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts; days are placed by position so left-out days (weekends) make no flat stretch, as on the web. The generated summary, which the web gives only to assistive technology, is the visible description unless the app sets one, and it is the summary of the chart descriptor. A point has a date or a label instead of the web's mixed date, number or label. todayIndex nil means the default, and showsToday false means no marker (the web uses null). Touch inspection uses chartXSelection and clears when the finger lifts; there is no keyboard inspection, live region or onDaySelect drill-in. valueFormat, formatTick and formatX are formatValue and dateFormat. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one element named by the title, with the data as an accessibility chart descriptor whose summary is the description: where the sprint stands and how scope changed.
"View as table" shows the data table, where each row is read as the day, remaining, ideal, scope and scope change ("+5"), "No value" for days not reached.
Values are read with formatValue, so VoiceOver says "24 pts".
The inspection popover is hidden from VoiceOver.
The ideal differs from the other lines by its dash and its name; remaining and scope by their names and line weights, never by colour alone.
Legend toggles are switches with a 44-point target; the last visible line cannot be hidden.
edgeCases: Days not reached yet have no remaining value; the remaining line ends at the latest day with one and a lone value is a dot.
A gap in the middle of the remaining values breaks the line.
Without idealStart, scope or a first remaining value there is no ideal line.
A single day has an ideal equal to its start, drawn centred.
Float noise never reads as behind: the difference to ideal is rounded to two decimals.
No day with a scope means no scope line, legend entry or table columns, whatever showsScope says.
A ready chart with no points shows the empty state.

name: MonarchBusinessHoursEditor
title: BusinessHoursEditor
wrapsNative: Section groups for a Form: TextField for the name, DatePicker with displayedComponents: .date and .datePickerStyle(.compact) (in UTC) for the effective days and each date, MonarchTimezoneSelect for the zone, MonarchWeeklyHoursEditor for the weekly hours, Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) for closed or open and the opening and closing times, Button with .buttonStyle(.monarch(...)) and swipeActions for add and remove, Toggle for the default, MonarchInlineNotice for problems
summary: Edits a business-hours calendar: name, time zone, weekly hours, optional effective dates, holidays and special-hours dates, and whether it is the default.
whenToUse: For support, SLA or office-hours settings, where a calendar needs a zone, a weekly pattern and dates that replace it.
whenNotToUse: For a person's weekly availability alone use MonarchWeeklyHoursEditor; for people's time off use MonarchTimeOffPanel.

options.name: content

states.name: empty
states.description: No weekly hours and the note No holidays or exceptions.

states.name: closed date
states.description: A section headed by the date's name with its date, name field and the menu set to Closed all day.

states.name: special hours
states.description: Open at other times adds opening and closing menus, 10:00 to 16:00 to start.

states.name: date not chosen
states.description: A new date has a Choose a date button, which picks today (or the earliest allowed day) and shows the compact date picker.

states.name: errors
states.description: A missing name, no open interval, a date without a day or name, a day listed twice, special hours that close before they open, and an end day before the start day show in the section footer as danger text with an icon.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Under .disabled(true) every control is disabled.

states.name: read-only
states.description: The name, days, zone and hours are text; there are no add or remove buttons, and the Default switch is disabled.

appearance: System form sections on the grouped form background, with system controls, Monarch buttons, notes and read-only values in the muted text role and problems in the danger strong role with an icon. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme roles and the system form colours.
platformNotes: On iOS the editor is a series of Form sections (one per date, swipe to remove), the phone's settings layout; the web lays the name and dates out in a grid and each exception as one row of inline controls, and Android stacks the same controls in a Column. The value is a Binding, not value plus onValueChange; the web's onValueChange(value, errors) becomes MonarchBusinessHoursValue.validate, which the app calls when saving, as on Android. Names follow Swift: the web's isDefault and Android's default are isDefault; showName, showDefault, showEffectiveDates, allowSpecialHours and showErrors are showsName, showsDefault, showsEffectiveDates, allowsSpecialHours and showsErrors; requireName and requireOpen are isNameRequired and isOpenRequired; Android's errors nameRequired, noOpenHours, effectiveOrder and valid are isNameMissing, isOpenIntervalMissing, isEffectiveOrderInvalid and isValid; is24Hour is uses24HourClock; firstDayOfWeek (and the web's weekStartsOn) is firstWeekday and follows the environment calendar when nil; enabled is the SwiftUI .disabled modifier; the label default is defaultTitle; addIcon and removeIcon are fixed SF Symbols. Dates are Date values at midnight UTC (the same instant as Android's UTC-midnight epoch milliseconds, the web's YYYY-MM-DD); the compact DatePicker runs in UTC so the chosen day is the stored day. A date not yet chosen is a Choose a date button, because DatePicker cannot be empty; the Android confirm and cancel labels have no use because the compact picker needs no dialog. The time zone is an IANA id String; MonarchTimezoneSelect has no read-only mode, so read-only shows the id as text. The default is a Toggle (the iOS switch) where the web and Android use a checkbox. After a date is removed the web moves focus to the next remove button; iOS leaves focus to the system. The parity map lists time-off-panel and text-field as dependencies; the editor does not embed MonarchTimeOffPanel, because a calendar's holidays are dates of the calendar, not people's time off, and it uses the system TextField in its form sections instead of MonarchTextField, whose own label and border would repeat the section's.
accessibility: Section headings (Name, Holidays and exceptions, each date's name) are read as headers by the system form.
Each date's controls are named by its position: Date 1, Name of date 1, Hours on date 1, Date 1 opens and Date 1 closes.
A date not chosen yet is a button read as its label with the value Choose a date.
The remove button is read as Remove Christmas Day, or Remove date 1 without a name; the trailing swipe action is also offered as a VoiceOver action.
Each effective day's clear button is read as Clear Effective from.
Problems are text with an icon in the danger colour, and each new problem is announced once.
Fields, menus and buttons have touch targets of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A new date has no day and no name; its problems wait until the row is changed or showsErrors is set.
A saved time off the step grid stays selectable.
A date may hold several intervals in the data; the editor edits the first and keeps the rest, and the read-only view lists them all.
Days are compared in UTC: any time on 25 December UTC is the same day as midnight, so two such rows are a duplicate.
Names are cut at 100 characters, as on the web.
The editor is many sections long and does not scroll by itself: put it in a Form.

name: MonarchButtonGroup
title: ButtonGroup
wrapsNative: Button, ButtonStyle, HStackLayout, VStackLayout, PreferenceKey
summary: Related standard Buttons shown as one control: joined into one shape with a hairline between them, or kept apart with a small gap, and exposed to VoiceOver as one labelled group.
whenToUse: For two to four related actions of equal weight, such as Previous and Next or zoom in and out.
whenNotToUse: For choosing one option from a set, use a segmented Picker. For buttons that stay on or off, use Toggle with the toggle button style. For one main action with alternatives, use a single button and a Menu.
api: MonarchButtonGroup.init(_ label: String? = nil, axis: Axis = .horizontal, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, isAttached: Bool = true, fullWidth: Bool = false, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

options.name: label
options.description: What the buttons have in common, read by VoiceOver. Already localised.

options.name: axis
options.description: A row or a column.

options.name: variant
options.description: primary, secondary, ghost or danger, for every button.

options.name: size
options.description: sm, md or lg, for every button.

options.name: isAttached
options.description: Joins the buttons into one shape. When false they keep an 8-point gap.

options.name: fullWidth
options.description: Fills the available width. In a row the buttons share it.

options.name: content
options.description: The buttons: standard Button, ShareLink or other views that take a button style.

states.name: resting
states.description: One rounded shape. Secondary has a border; every variant has a hairline between neighbours.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Only the pressed button changes its fill; not animated when Reduce Motion is on.

states.name: disabled
states.description: A button disabled with disabled(_:) takes the disabled fill and text colour; the others are unchanged.

states.name: not attached
states.description: Each button is drawn alone with the Monarch button style.

appearance: The fills, text colours and pressed colours are those of the button variant in every theme. The line between two filled buttons (primary, danger) is the surface colour; for secondary it is the default border colour and for ghost the subtle border colour.
platformNotes: The web group joins any child and lets each child keep its own variant; here the group sets one variant and size for all its buttons, because a SwiftUI container cannot restyle each child separately on iOS 17. A view that sets its own button style, including MonarchButton, keeps it and is not joined, so use standard Buttons inside. In a row the joined shape is 32 to 40 points high inside a 44-point touch target; in a column every button is at least 44 points high because the buttons touch. Android uses the same name and parameters.
accessibility: The group is an accessibility container with the given label, so VoiceOver reads the label when focus enters it.
Every button stays a standard Button: its own element, trait, label and disabled state.
Every joined button is at least 44 points wide; in a row the touch target is 44 points high around the visible shape, in a column the visible button is at least 44 points high.
Labels scale with Dynamic Type and wrap; the joined shape grows to the tallest button.
The joined shape follows the buttons in right-to-left layouts.
The press transition is not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A view inside the group that sets its own button style, such as MonarchButton, is drawn alone and not joined.
One button gives a single rounded shape with no line. No buttons draw nothing.
With long titles in a row, the buttons wrap their text and all take the height of the tallest.
The label is optional; without one the buttons are read without a group name.

name: MonarchCalendarHeatmap
title: CalendarHeatmap
wrapsNative: A SwiftUI grid of rounded-rectangle days (HStack of VStack weeks in a horizontal ScrollView with defaultScrollAnchor(.trailing) for the year; Grid for the month), the environment Calendar for weeks and names, Date.FormatStyle for dates; inside MonarchChartFrame with the MonarchHeatmap scale and legend and an AXChartDescriptor
summary: Values by day on a calendar grid, a contribution-style year or a month calendar with day numbers, binned into four colour steps with a Less to More legend, today, notes, markers, tap inspection, drill-in and the days as a table.
whenToUse: To show one value per day over weeks or a year (activity, sign-ins, hours logged) so streaks, gaps and busy weeks stand out, or a month where each day opens its details (layout .month).
whenNotToUse: For two arbitrary categories such as weekday by hour use MonarchHeatmap. For a trend where exact values matter use MonarchBarChart or MonarchLineChart. To schedule or show events on dates use a calendar view or the system DatePicker with .graphical.

enum MonarchCalendarHeatmapLayout { case year, month }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading.

options.name: days
options.description: One entry per day with something to show: a date, a value (nil for no data), and optional value text, note, non-working flag and marker. Days in the range without an entry are no data; a later entry for the same day wins.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day drawn. The earliest entry when nil.

options.name: to
options.description: The last day drawn. The latest entry when nil.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: layout
options.description: year: weeks as columns and weekdays as rows, scrolling sideways; month: a calendar with day numbers and values.

options.name: today
options.description: The day outlined as today. Passed by the app; the component never reads the clock.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready without an entry in the range shows empty.

options.name: color
options.description: The data colour of the four steps.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when nil.

options.name: showsValues
options.description: Month layout: writes each day's value text (or note) under its number.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Shows the Less to More legend under the grid.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary VoiceOver reads.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the frame's, the legend's, the table headings, Today, the day counts, the summary and the highest day.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values. A number in the environment's locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called with the day when it is tapped or selected with VoiceOver; a day without an entry comes with value nil.

states.name: level
states.description: Each day with a value takes one of five fills: the muted background for zero, then the data colour mixed in at 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%.

states.name: no data
states.description: A day in the range without a value is empty with a thin subtle outline.

states.name: non-working
states.description: A day marked isInactive without a value above zero has the subtle background and a dashed outline.

states.name: today
states.description: The day of today has a thick accent outline.

states.name: inspected
states.description: After a tap or a VoiceOver swipe the day has a thick default-text outline and its date, value and note are written under the grid.

states.name: marker
states.description: A day with hasMarker has a small warning-coloured dot in its top trailing corner.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" lists every day with an entry: date, value and, when any day has one, note.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's placeholder, empty state and error with Try again, at the chart's height.

appearance: Steps mix the chosen data slot into the muted background, as MonarchHeatmap. Days without data use the subtle border colour, non-working days the subtle background with a dashed subtle border, today the accent solid colour, the inspected day the default text colour and markers the warning solid colour ringed with the surface colour. Text is the muted and default text colours, on a surface chip at the two strongest steps. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web draws an SVG that shrinks a year to fit the width; on iOS the year keeps 14-point days and scrolls sideways on a phone, opening at the latest week, as planned. Days are Date values read in the environment's Calendar, which also supplies the first weekday (the web's weekStartsOn), the time zone and the weekday and month names; the web takes ISO date strings and a locale. The inspected day is internal state, not a controlled activeDate. There is no keyboard navigation (arrows, Page Up/Down); VoiceOver adjusts day by day in the year and visits each day in the month. Inspection is written under the grid instead of a floating tooltip. Android ships the same MonarchCalendarHeatmap. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: Year layout: the grid is one adjustable element named by the generated summary ("181 days from Thu, Jan 1, 2026 to Tue, Jun 30, 2026. Total 812. Highest: …") or summary. Swiping up and down moves one day and its value reads the date, value, note and Today; with onSelect it has the button trait and a double tap selects the day.

Month layout: each day is its own element, labelled with its date and valued with its value, note and Today; it has the selected trait while inspected and the button trait with onSelect. Weekday headings are hidden.
Both layouts carry an AXChartDescriptor with one point per day with a value, for Audio Graphs.
The inspection text under the grid is hidden from VoiceOver because the element already reads it.
The legend is read as its name and its steps.
Zero, no data, non-working days, today and markers differ by fill, outline and dot, and are also in the spoken value and the table, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A range that ends before it starts, or no entries and no range, shows the empty state.
Entries outside from...to are ignored.
Days are compared by calendar day, so any time of day counts and daylight saving changes do not shift days.
In the year layout days are 14 points, below the 44-point touch target; tapping is a convenience and VoiceOver uses the adjustable element instead.
At the largest text sizes month names and weekday names in the year grid shrink to fit (minimum scale 0.6) and month names are skipped when they would overlap; month cells grow taller.
Tap inspection, horizontal scrolling and Audio Graphs were not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; the grid, styles, text and summary logic are unit-tested.

states.name: selected
states.description: The day has the accent subtle fill and an accent border, and the selected trait.

states.name: outside
states.description: Days of the previous and next month have the subtle text colour.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: dayState isUnavailable gives the muted background and the subtle date colour; the badge is drawn beside the date.

states.name: dots
states.description: Up to three dots in the event colour (hollow when tentative, disabled colour when cancelled or declined); the whole day is one button.

states.name: events
states.description: Dot chips with the start time; when more events exist than fit, the last row is "+N more", which opens a popover with every event as a bar chip.

states.name: drop target
states.description: While a chip is dragged over a day, the day takes the accent subtle fill.

states.name: empty
states.description: Days without events show only the date.

appearance: Weekday initials in the muted text colour, days separated by subtle border lines, dates in the label style with tabular figures. Today uses the accent solid fill, selection the accent subtle fill and accent border, unavailable days the muted background. Chips are MonarchEventChip in the event colour. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web view switches to dots below about 36rem of width and opens a day's list in a popover; the product owns month navigation and the grid has arrow-key focus movement. On iOS the automatic layout uses dots on a phone and the selected day is meant to be listed under the grid with MonarchAgendaList, as the system Calendar does, instead of a popover per day. Months are pages of a horizontal paging ScrollView that writes month, so a swipe and MonarchCalendarToolbar both navigate. Keyboard grid navigation (arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Down) is not offered: VoiceOver moves day by day and scrolls pages with three fingers. Events use MonarchAgendaEvent and the environment's Calendar (time zone, first weekday, locale) instead of ISO strings, an IANA zone and an hourCycle. Drag to move, from the plan, is added with draggable and dropDestination; the web has none. Hatching is a muted fill. renderEvent is not offered; use onSelectEvent. Android has no month view yet. Several closures are optional (dayState, onSelectDay, onMoveEvent, onSelectEvent). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is dayState.
accessibility: Each day is read as its long date and event count, then "today" and the badge when they apply, for example "Wednesday, November 4, 2026, 2 events, today, Holiday".
The selected day has the selected trait; today and selection are also shown by shape (circle, border), not colour alone.
In the dots layout the whole day is one button with a touch target of at least 44 points; dots are not read.
In the events layout the date, each chip and "+N more" are separate buttons; chips read title, time and status.
The weekday header is hidden from VoiceOver because each day's name carries its weekday.
Months are pages that VoiceOver scrolls with a three-finger swipe; programmatic month changes animate only without Reduce Motion.
Moving an event by drag has no VoiceOver equivalent in the view; apps should offer moving in their event editor.
edgeCases: An event ending exactly at midnight does not appear on the day it ends; an all-day event appears on its last day.
Events entirely outside the shown weeks are skipped; events starting earlier appear from the first shown day.
maxEvents below 1 is treated as 1, so a busy day shows only "+N more".
A month binding passed as a constant still pages on swipe but does not change month.
The pager holds 24 months on each side of the first month shown and moves its centre when month jumps outside it.
At accessibility text sizes the automatic layout uses dots, because chips no longer fit.

name: MonarchCalendarToolbar
title: CalendarToolbar
wrapsNative: ViewThatFits of HStack and VStack layouts with MonarchButton (Today), Button with buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost)) arrows, a heading Text, ProgressView with .monarchCircular, and Menu holding Picker with pickerStyle(.inline) for the view
summary: The header of a calendar: Today, previous and next, the range title with a busy indicator, a menu that switches between day, week, month and agenda views, and the app's actions.
whenToUse: Above a calendar view (a month grid, a week, an agenda) whose range the person moves through.
whenNotToUse: For choosing one date use DatePicker (see date-picker). For a screen title use the navigation bar; for two to four view choices with no navigation use Picker with pickerStyle(.segmented).

enum MonarchCalendarToolbarView: String { case day, week, month, agenda }
