options.name: title
options.description: The range shown, already formatted: "November 2026", "2 – 8 Nov 2026". Announced when it changes.

options.name: view
options.description: The current view. The switcher sets it, and the arrows are named for its unit.

options.name: views
options.description: The views offered, in order. With one view or none the switcher is not shown.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: Shows a small circular progress indicator, named "Loading", after the title.

options.name: isTodayDisabled
options.description: Disables Today, for example when the range already contains today.

options.name: isPreviousDisabled
options.description: Disables the previous arrow, for example at the start of a booking window.

options.name: isNextDisabled
options.description: Disables the next arrow.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Today", "Previous week", "Next week", "Calendar view", the view names, the units and "Loading".

options.name: onToday
options.description: Moves to the range that contains today.

options.name: onPrevious
options.description: Moves back one unit of the view.

options.name: onNext
options.description: Moves forward one unit of the view.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end: a New event button, a filter menu, a DatePicker. Pass it labelled, actions: { … }.

states.name: one line
states.description: Today, the arrows, the title, then the switcher and actions at the end.

states.name: two lines
states.description: When one line does not fit, the title goes on its own line above the controls.

states.name: stacked
states.description: At the largest text sizes the title, the navigation and the switcher with actions are on three lines.

states.name: busy
states.description: A small circular progress indicator after the title.

states.name: disabled controls
states.description: Today and either arrow can be disabled; they take the button style's disabled colours.

appearance: The title uses the heading type role in the default text colour. Today and the switcher are secondary Monarch buttons, the arrows ghost buttons, all at the sm size; the busy indicator uses the accent. Every colour comes from the theme, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named .toolbar items. A navigation bar has no room for Today, two arrows, a title, a switcher and actions at large text sizes, and toolbar placements differ between iPhone and iPad, so this is a header view that reflows with ViewThatFits; place it above the calendar or in safeAreaInset(edge: .top). The web's titleAs (heading level) is the header trait; its datePicker slot is part of actions. The web accepts product-defined view ids; this enum has the four built-in views only. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The title has the header trait and is announced with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when it changes.
The arrows are named for the view's unit ("Previous week", "Next month"); their chevrons are backward and forward symbols, so they follow the reading direction.
The switcher is a Menu named "Calendar view" whose value is the current view; inside it the system Picker marks the selected view.
The busy indicator is named "Loading".
Every button has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points; the layout reflows instead of truncating at large text sizes.
edgeCases: A long title wraps on its own line instead of pushing the controls off screen.
With views set to one view the switcher is hidden, but that view still names the arrows.
The announcement fires on every title change, including the app's own; set the title once per move.

name: MonarchCallControls
title: CallControls
wrapsNative: Toggle with a round ToggleStyle and accessibilityRepresentation, Menu with Button, Picker (.pickerStyle(.inline)) and Toggle items, and Button, in a MonarchFlowLayout
summary: The controls of a call: microphone, camera, screen sharing, raised hand, reactions, a More menu (layout, low data, devices, connection, picture in picture) and Leave.
whenToUse: On the call screen of an app that runs its own calls, under or over the video stage.
whenNotToUse: For a call that only continues in a small window, use the system's picture in picture (see mini-call). For an incoming call, use CallKit (see incoming-call). For formatting tools, use toggles with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()).
api: init(isMicOn: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isCameraOn: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isSharing: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isHandRaised: Binding<Bool>? = nil, layout: Binding<MonarchCallControlsLayout>? = nil, isLowData: Binding<Bool>? = nil, reactions: [String] = MonarchCallControls.defaultReactions, isMinimal: Bool = false, labels: MonarchCallControlsLabels = MonarchCallControlsLabels(), onReact: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onOpenDevices: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onOpenStats: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onPictureInPicture: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onLeave: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
static let defaultReactions: [String]
enum MonarchCallControlsLayout { case automatic, grid, speaker }

struct MonarchCallControlsLabels { init(toolbar:microphone:camera:shareScreen:raiseHand:react:reactWith:more:layout:layoutName:lowData:devices:stats:pictureInPicture:leave:) }  // every parameter optional

options.name: isMicOn
options.description: Whether the microphone is on. Shows the microphone toggle.

options.name: isCameraOn
options.description: Whether the camera is on. Shows the camera toggle.

options.name: isSharing
options.description: Whether the screen is shared. Shows the sharing toggle.

options.name: isHandRaised
options.description: Whether the hand is raised. Shows the hand toggle.

options.name: layout
options.description: The stage layout. Adds an inline choice of Automatic, Grid and Speaker to More.

options.name: isLowData
options.description: Audio-only mode. Adds a toggle to More.

options.name: reactions
options.description: The emoji offered in the reactions menu: 👍 👏 😂 ❤️ 🎉 😮.

options.name: isMinimal
options.description: Leaves out the hand, reactions and More, for a small window.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onReact
options.description: Sends a reaction. Shows the reactions menu.

options.name: onOpenDevices
options.description: Opens the app's device settings. Adds Devices to More.

options.name: onOpenStats
options.description: Opens the app's connection details. Adds Connection and data use to More.

options.name: onPictureInPicture
options.description: Continues the call in picture in picture. Adds an item to More.

options.name: onLeave
options.description: Leaves the call. Shows the wide Leave control.

states.name: device on
states.description: A round control with the muted fill and the default text colour, showing mic.fill or video.fill.

states.name: device off
states.description: The danger fill with a slashed symbol (mic.slash.fill, video.slash.fill).

states.name: sharing
states.description: The success fill with the stop-sharing symbol.

states.name: hand raised
states.description: The warning fill with the filled hand symbol.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A darker fill of the same tone.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The muted fill with the disabled text colour.

states.name: minimal
states.description: Only microphone, camera, sharing and Leave.

appearance: Round controls, at least 48 points and scaled with Dynamic Type, in capsule shapes: the muted background with a subtle border for normal controls; the danger solid fill for a device that is off and for Leave; the success solid fill while sharing; the warning solid fill for a raised hand, each with its on-solid text colour, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web toolbar labels toggles by the action ("Mute", "Unmute") with aria-pressed; on iOS each toggle keeps one name ("Microphone") and VoiceOver reads on or off as its value, as a standard Toggle does. The web keyboard shortcuts (M, V, S, H, F) and roving arrow-key focus are not offered; a hardware keyboard moves between the controls with Tab. Full screen is left out because an iOS call screen is already full screen. The extra slot for product controls is left out; place them beside the controls. The CallIcon glyphs are replaced by SF Symbols. Android ships MonarchCallControls.
accessibility: The controls are one container named "Call controls".
Microphone, camera, sharing and hand are given to VoiceOver as standard Toggles through accessibilityRepresentation: name, then on or off.
A state change changes the symbol as well as the colour.
Reactions, More and Leave are read by their titles through icon-only Labels; each reaction in the menu is read as "React" and the emoji.
Every control is at least 44 by 44 points and the row wraps onto a second line at large text sizes.
edgeCases: With no binding and no action the view is empty.
An empty reactions list hides the reactions menu.
The More menu appears only when it has an item; in the minimal form it never appears.
Whether the button style applies to the Menu triggers on every iOS version, and how VoiceOver reads the toggles, was not checked on a device.

options.name: labels

options.name: controls
options.description: The controls row under the tiles, usually MonarchCallControls.

states.name: grid
states.description: Tiles in equal columns: one, two up to four people, then three; at most two on a narrow screen or a compact surface.

states.name: spotlight
states.description: A pin, someone else's shared screen, the speaker in speaker mode or the other person in a one-to-one call is large; the others are in a filmstrip below that scrolls sideways, or in a column beside it on a wide full stage.

states.name: waiting
states.description: Alone on the call, the header reads "Waiting for others…" instead of the head count.

states.name: reconnecting
states.description: A warning callout with an offline symbol under the header, announced when it appears.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger callout with the product's message, announced when it appears or changes.

states.name: muted while speaking
states.description: A warning notice under the tiles, announced when it appears.

states.name: docked and pip
states.description: Smaller padding, at most two columns and no Pin or full screen buttons; docked shows Expand and Minimize.

appearance: The stage sits on the subtle background with a large rounded corner; the title is the default text colour and the timer and head count the muted text colour. Tiles, notices, the badge and the controls are the Monarch components with their own theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web's region becomes a SwiftUI accessibility container. The video is a view slot per participant instead of a MediaStream and onVideoElement; system picture in picture is opened by the product (see mini-call), so onPictureInPicture only reports the button. The web's 'mini' surface change is onMinimize. The timer is the system's Text timer style rather than a ticking component, so it needs no clock and is never announced every second. The web's muted hint mentions keyboard shortcuts; iOS says to turn the microphone on. The stage grows with its tiles instead of filling a container: give it a frame to fill a screen. The grid's narrow-screen cap follows the horizontal size class rather than a 30rem width. Android ships the same MonarchCallStage.
accessibility: The stage is an accessibility container labelled with the title, or "Call".
The title has the header trait.
The timer is labelled "Call duration" with the updates-frequently trait; VoiceOver reads the time when focused and does not announce each second.
Changes are announced once with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement, in this order of priority: a new error, losing the connection, the muted hint, a new head count.
Header buttons are plain buttons with an SF Symbol, an accessibility label and a 44-point target.
Each tile is MonarchCallTile: one element per person named by their name with speaking, muted, hand raised, screen, status and quality as its value.
edgeCases: A pinned or spotlighted id that is not among the participants is ignored and the grid is shown.
Your own shared screen never takes the spotlight; the speaker is never yourself.
Ids in a given layout without a participant draw nothing.
Many participants make the stage tall; it does not scroll itself, so put it in a ScrollView or give it a frame.
Long titles and names wrap; at the largest text sizes tiles grow taller than 16 by 9.
Announcements and the timer were not checked with VoiceOver on a device; the layout choice, columns, buttons, head count and announcements are unit-tested.

name: MonarchCallStatsPanel
title: CallStatsPanel
wrapsNative: VStack of Text, MonarchStatusBadge and LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch(.inline)) per person; the app presents it in .sheet
summary: The data a call has used and each person's round trip, packet loss and connection grade.
whenToUse: In a call's Connection panel, opened from the call controls (MonarchCallControls onOpenStats) and shown in a sheet, or in support and diagnostics views of a live call.
whenNotToUse: For one connection indicator on a person's tile, use a status badge or dot on the tile. Not for history or analytics of past calls; use a table or a chart.
api: MonarchCallStatsPanel.init(usage: MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage, peers: [MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer], isLowData: Bool = false, footnote: String? = nil, labels: MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels = MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels())
MonarchCallStatsPanelUsage.init(sentBytes: Int64, receivedBytes: Int64, upBitsPerSecond: Double? = nil, downBitsPerSecond: Double? = nil)

MonarchCallStatsPanelPeer.init(id: String, name: String, roundTripMilliseconds: Double? = nil, inboundLossPercent: Double? = nil, outboundLossPercent: Double? = nil, quality: MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality = .unknown)
enum MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality { case good, fair, poor, unknown }

MonarchCallStatsPanelLabels.init(dataUsed: String? = nil, usageSummary: (@Sendable (String, String, String) -> String)? = nil, lowData: String? = nil, connections: String? = nil, roundTrip: String? = nil, loss: String? = nil, noPeers: String? = nil, qualityNames: [MonarchCallStatsPanelQuality: String] = [:])

options.name: usage
options.description: Bytes sent and received, and the current upload and download rates in bits per second.

options.name: peers
options.description: One entry per remote person: name, round trip in milliseconds, inbound and outbound loss in percent, and a grade.

options.name: isLowData
options.description: Adds the note "Low data mode is on: audio only."

options.name: footnote
options.description: A closing note, such as how media is routed or encrypted. App copy: Monarch does not know how the app connects calls.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the heading, the usage line, the low data note, the list name, the number labels, the no-peers text and the grade names.

states.name: default
states.description: The heading and usage line, then one block per person: the name with a grade badge, the round trip and the loss.

states.name: low data
states.description: A muted note under the usage line.

states.name: not measured
states.description: A missing number shows a dash; an unknown grade is a neutral badge "Not measured yet".

states.name: no peers
states.description: "No one else is connected yet." instead of the people.

appearance: The heading is default text; the usage line, notes and footnote are muted caption text. Grades are subtle status badges: success for good, warning for unstable, danger for poor and neutral for not measured, each with its own icon. People are separated by the default divider. The same roles apply in light, dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a table with a column per number and signal bars for the grade; on a phone a four-column table does not fit at large text sizes, so each person is a block with LabeledContent rows and the grade is a MonarchStatusBadge, as the plan's dependencies say. The panel is the sheet's content, not the sheet: the app presents it with .sheet and adds a title, as in the example, because detents and navigation belong to the app. The parity map named a List; a VStack is used so the panel also sits inside a ScrollView or a popover. Bytes use the system byte count format (powers of 1024); rates and percentages use the environment locale. The web's formatCallBytes and formatCallRate helpers are not public API. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: "Data used this call" is a header; the usage line is plain text.
The people are a container named "Connection to each person".
Each person is one element read as the name, the round trip, the loss and the grade, such as "Alex Chen, Round trip 186 ms, Loss 3.4%, Unstable connection".
A number that was not measured is read as "Not measured yet", not as a dash.
The grade has an icon and a name, so it is not told by colour alone.
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type; long names wrap onto a second line.
edgeCases: Loss shows the worse of the two directions; a direction that is missing or not finite is ignored.
Negative or non-finite rates count as 0 bps; negative byte counts as 0.
Round trip is rounded to whole milliseconds; loss has one decimal.
Rates of 10 Mbps and more have no decimal.
The panel holds no timer: set new numbers as statistics arrive, every second or two.

options.name: isHandRaised

states.name: avatar
states.description: Without video the avatar is centred on the emphasis background.

states.name: video
states.description: The slot fills the tile, mirrored for your own camera.

states.name: speaking
states.description: A 2-point accent border.

states.name: muted
states.description: A crossed-out microphone in the name bar.

states.name: hand raised
states.description: A solid warning badge with a hand at the top leading corner.

states.name: pinned
states.description: The Pin button becomes Unpin with a crossed-out pin, and has the selected trait.

states.name: reaction
states.description: The emoji rises and fades in, stays for three seconds, then fades; it only fades with Reduce Motion.

states.name: poor connection

appearance: The tile on the emphasis background with large rounded corners; the name bar and the action buttons on the inverse background with inverse text; status text in the tone's strong inverse colour; the speaking border in the accent solid colour. The same roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web tile renders a MediaStream in a video element and offers the Fullscreen API; on iOS the video is a slot for the call SDK's own view, and full screen is the product's presentation through onFullScreen. Pinned is a binding instead of pinned and onPinnedChange. Reactions carry a Date and are timed with TimelineView, so no timer runs and tests inject the time. The avatar is 40 points at most, the largest MonarchAvatar size, where the web uses its extra-large avatar. Hover-only actions are always visible on touch screens.
accessibility: The tile is a container named by the participant; its name bar is one element read first, named "Ana (you)", with a value listing what is true now: "Speaking, Muted, Hand raised, Sharing screen, Presenting, Poor connection".
Speaking is also a thicker border, muted and the hand are symbols, and quality is the number of lit bars, so nothing depends on colour.
Pin and full screen are buttons named "Pin Ana", "Unpin Ana" and "Show Ana full screen", with 44-point touch targets; Pin has the toggle trait and the selected trait when pinned.
A new reaction is announced as "Ana reacted 👏"; the floating emoji itself is hidden.
The video and the avatar are hidden from VoiceOver.
The reaction stands still with Reduce Motion, and the tile grows taller at large text sizes.
edgeCases: A reaction with a sentAt in the future or more than three seconds ago is not shown.
Sending the same reaction again with a new sentAt replays it.
A long name or status wraps in the name bar and makes the tile taller instead of being cut.
With showsVideo false the slot is not drawn, so a frozen frame never shows.

name: MonarchCalloutBanner
title: CalloutBanner
wrapsNative: Text, Button, RoundedRectangle, Rectangle; safeAreaInset(edge: .top) for the page placement
summary: A banner for a screen or a section, with a tone, an optional title, one action and a dismiss button; also a compact notice that the view is narrowed.
whenToUse: For trials, maintenance and billing notices across the top of a screen, for a callout inside the content that can be dismissed, and for saying that a list is filtered.
whenNotToUse: For a plain status beside the content it is about, use MonarchBanner. For one line attached to a field or row, use MonarchInlineNotice. For a message that must interrupt, use the system alert modifier.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, message: String, systemImage: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .info, variant: MonarchCalloutBannerVariant = .callout, placement: MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement = .section, toneLabel: String? = nil, actionTitle: String? = nil, actionVariant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, dismissLabel: String? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchCalloutBannerVariant { case callout, scope }
enum MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement { case section, page }

options.name: title
options.description: A short title on the first line.

options.name: message
options.description: The message.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the SF Symbol of the tone.

options.name: tone
options.description: Selects the colours and the icon. Ignored by the scope variant.

options.name: variant
options.description: callout, or scope: a compact neutral notice that the view is narrowed.

options.name: placement
options.description: section is rounded and bordered; page is a full-width strip with a line below.

options.name: toneLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the tone.

options.name: actionTitle
options.description: Title of the action button. No button without it.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Dismiss" spoken name.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when the action button is activated.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Runs when the dismiss button is activated. No dismiss button without it.

options.name: actionVariant
options.description: How the action button is drawn.

states.name: dismissible
states.description: A close button at the trailing edge, when onDismiss is given. The app removes the banner.

appearance: A container with the subtle fill and the border of its tone, the icon in the strong colour of the tone and text in the default text colour. The neutral tone and the scope variant use the subtle background and the default border. The page placement has square corners and only a line along its lower edge.
platformNotes: The banner does not hide itself: the web keeps its own open state when uncontrolled, here the app removes the view in onDismiss. One action instead of the web's actions slot, placed under the text (the scope variant puts it at the trailing edge when it fits); there is no actionPlacement option. No accent tone, because MonarchTone has none. The landmark and live options have no equivalent: post an announcement when you insert a banner. Monarch does not install the banner in the safe area; the app does, with safeAreaInset(edge: .top). Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (action, onDismiss). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is action.
accessibility: The icon, title and message are one element, read as the tone name, the title, then the message.
The tone name is spoken, so the tone does not depend on colour or the icon; toneLabel replaces it. The neutral tone and the scope variant have no spoken tone.
The action and the dismiss button are separate buttons with touch targets of at least 44 points.
The dismiss button is named "Dismiss"; dismissLabel replaces the name.
The banner does not announce itself when it appears.
edgeCases: actionTitle without action, or action without actionTitle, shows no action button.
In the scope variant the action moves under the text when both do not fit on one line.
The dismiss button's touch target reaches 12 points into the banner's padding so that the glyph lines up with the content.

summary: A highlighted block inside a document: a tone, an icon and any content. The display form of the document callout block.
whenToUse: To set a note, a tip or a warning apart from the surrounding text in a document, an article or a help page.
whenNotToUse: For a status message with a title and an action, use MonarchBanner. For a banner across a screen, use MonarchCalloutBanner.
api: init(systemImage: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, toneLabel: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

options.description: One paragraph of text.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the SF Symbol of the tone.

options.name: tone
options.description: Selects the tint, the border and the icon.

options.name: toneLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the tone.

options.name: content

appearance: A container with 12-point corners, the subtle fill and the border of its tone, the icon in the strong colour of the tone and content in the default text colour. The neutral tone sits on the subtle background with the default border and a small dot as its icon.
platformNotes: Only the display form is offered. The web component is also a node of the rich-text editor with a tone picker above the text (the toolbar slot, CalloutBlockExtension and its messages); that editing form belongs to the block editor, which is not part of this entry. The web icon can be removed with null; here an icon is always shown. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The icon is read as the name of the tone before the content, so the tone does not depend on colour; toneLabel replaces the name.
The neutral tone has no spoken name and its dot is hidden from VoiceOver.
The block is a container: the views of the content stay separate elements, so links and buttons inside it are reachable.
Text in the content takes the body type role unless it sets its own, and scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Empty content draws the icon in an otherwise empty block.
The block fills the width it is given.

name: MonarchCard
title: Card
wrapsNative: VStack, RoundedRectangle, ShadowStyle.drop

whenToUse: At the end of a flow or onboarding step that reached a real milestone: an account or domain verified, a first project published, a workspace set up.
whenNotToUse: For routine confirmations (saved, sent), use a MonarchToast. For a success that needs no moment, use a MonarchBanner in the success tone. For an empty screen, use MonarchEmptyState with the success kind.

appearance: Centred text: the title in the default text role, the message in the muted role. The tile uses the tone's subtle background role and strong foreground role. The pieces use the five data colour roles, which have light, dark and high-contrast values.
platformNotes: The web ships two components: CelebrationPanel (inline) and Celebration (a dialog with a Continue button). On iOS one view covers both: place it inline, or present it with sheet(isPresented:) and put the Continue button in its actions. The web tone `accent` is not offered because MonarchTone has no accent case yet; any MonarchTone works, success by default. The web media slot takes any image; here the tile shows an SF Symbol. The web heading level has no iOS equivalent beyond the header trait. Android uses the same name and options.

appearance: A plain list on the system background: muted caption for the date and version, the title in the subheading type, badges in their tone colours, notes in the prose type and the link in the link colour with its external glyph. The navigation bar is the system one in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ChangelogFeed is a public changelog page with a timeline marker, permalinks, a heading level and an RSS link in the header. In an app it is a What's new screen: a plain List of entries with no timeline line, no permalinks and no RSS link, as the plan says; the title and description become the navigation title. Read more opens the full note in the browser. Dates are formatted in UTC, matching the web's default time zone. Android ships the same recipe with a LazyColumn.
accessibility: Each release title has the header trait, so the rotor moves from release to release.
Tags are MonarchBadge text, read with the entry; their tone is not the only signal.
Read more is a link with an external glyph that VoiceOver reads as opening outside the app.
Rows grow with Dynamic Type; nothing is truncated.
edgeCases: A release without notes or a link shows only its date, title and tags.
Long titles and notes wrap.
An empty list shows the empty state instead of an empty screen.

@Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme

private struct ReleaseTag: Hashable {

private struct Release: Identifiable {
    let id: String
    let date: Date
    let version: String?
    let title: String
    let tags: [ReleaseTag]
    let notes: String?
    let url: URL?
}

private let releases = [
    Release(
        id: {{entries.0.id}},
        date: {{entries.0.date|date}},
        version: {{entries.0.version}},
        title: {{entries.0.title}},
        tags: [ReleaseTag(label: {{entries.0.tags.0.label}}, tone: {{entries.0.tags.0.tone|tone}}), ReleaseTag(label: {{entries.0.tags.1.label}})],
        notes: {{entries.0.body}},
        url: URL(string: {{entries.0.href}})
    ),
    Release(
        id: {{entries.1.id}},
        date: {{entries.1.date|date}},
        version: nil,
        title: {{entries.1.title}},
        tags: [ReleaseTag(label: {{entries.1.tags.0.label}})],
        notes: {{entries.1.body}},
        url: nil
    ),
    Release(
        id: {{entries.2.id}},
        date: {{entries.2.date|date}},
        version: nil,
        title: {{entries.2.title}},
        tags: [ReleaseTag(label: {{entries.2.tags.0.label}})],
        notes: nil,
        url: nil
    ),
]

private func dateLine(_ release: Release) -> String {
    let utc = TimeZone(identifier: "UTC") ?? .current
    let style = Date.FormatStyle(date: .long, time: .omitted, locale: Locale(identifier: {{locale}}), timeZone: utc)
    return release.date.formatted(style) + (release.version.map { " \u{00B7} " + $0 } ?? "")
}

name: MonarchChartFrame
title: ChartFrame
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with slots; accessibilityChartDescriptor(_:) with AXChartDescriptor (Accessibility framework); Grid for the data table
summary: The card a chart sits in: title, description, header controls, legend, loading, empty and error states that keep the chart's height, and the data as a table through "View as table" and VoiceOver's chart descriptor.
whenToUse: Around any chart that Monarch does not draw itself, such as a Swift Charts Chart or a custom drawing, so it gets the same header, states and accessible data as every other chart.
whenNotToUse: For one headline number without a plot, use a card with text or MonarchDeltaIndicator. For a list of labelled values, use MonarchBarList or LabeledContent with the Monarch style.

options.description: One line under the title; also the summary of the chart descriptor.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error.

options.description: Whether the legend keeps the last visible series from being hidden.

options.name: contentAccessibility
options.description: .contain keeps the chart's own elements (a legend with values, a selected bar) reachable; the chart gives its plot the descriptor itself.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: content
options.description: The chart.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls in the header, such as a period Picker.

states.name: ready
states.description: The chart, the legend and, after "View as table", the data table in its place.

states.name: loading
states.description: A muted placeholder of the chart's height, spoken as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "This chart didn't load." and Try again when onRetry is set; otherwise the message with a warning icon in the strong danger colour.

appearance: A MonarchCard (surface fill, subtle border, large corner radius). The title is subheading text in the default colour, the description and footer caption text in the muted colour. The loading placeholder uses the muted background fill. Table headers use the muted text colour with hairline dividers between rows. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ChartFrame is a figure that always renders the data table for screen readers and offers headingLevel, emptyActions and a controlled showTable. On iOS the data reaches VoiceOver as an AXChartDescriptor (Audio Graphs and the chart data rotor) instead of a hidden table; the table view state is internal; the empty state has no action slot; and the title is a heading without levels. Swift Charts charts already provide their own descriptor; giving the frame a table replaces it with the frame's. Android ships the same MonarchChartFrame.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.

With a table, the chart is one element labelled with the title and carries an AXChartDescriptor: a categorical x axis, a numeric y axis named by valueTitle, and one series per table column, with the app's formatted values as point labels.
In the table, the header row is one element with the header trait and each row is read as the category, then each series and its value; a gap is read as "No value".
The loading placeholder is read as "Loading chart" and has the updates-frequently trait.
The error without retry combines its icon and text into one element; with onRetry it is MonarchInlineErrorRetry.
Without a table, the chart content keeps its own accessibility.
edgeCases: A long title wraps and the actions move under the heading when they do not fit beside it.
A wide table scrolls sideways inside the card.
Gaps (nil values) are drawn as a dash, read as "No value" and left out of the chart descriptor.
The value axis always includes zero; a series with only zeros gets a range of 0 to 1.
Audio Graphs and the chart rotor were not tried with VoiceOver on a device; the descriptor itself is unit-tested.

name: MonarchCheckboxGroup

summary: A labelled set of checkboxes for picking any number of choices, with an optional "Select all" that is checked, mixed or clear.
whenToUse: For a short list of independent choices where any number can be picked, such as notification topics or days of the week.
whenNotToUse: Not for one choice out of several (use a Picker or MonarchRadioCardGroup), not for a setting that applies at once (use a Toggle switch), and not for a long or searchable list (use List with selection or MonarchCombobox).

options.name: label
options.description: The visible group label, already localised. It names the group for VoiceOver.

options.name: selection
options.description: The ids of the checked choices.

options.name: options
options.description: The choices in order, each with an id, a label, an optional description and an optional disabled flag.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text, shown under the choices and read as the group's hint.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, such as "Choose at least one day". Shown with an icon in place of the help text and announced.

options.name: layout
options.description: vertical: one choice per line. horizontal: side by side, wrapping; stacked at the accessibility text sizes.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint. The group does not enforce a minimum; pass error.

options.name: showsSelectAll
options.description: Adds a "Select all" checkbox above the choices, which are indented under it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Select all" and for the field's spoken "Required" and error form.

states.name: select all off
states.description: No enabled choice is checked; the box is empty.

states.name: select all mixed
states.description: Some enabled choices are checked; the box is filled with a minus glyph and VoiceOver reads the mixed value. Pressing it checks every enabled choice.

states.name: select all on
states.description: Every enabled choice is checked; pressing it clears them. Disabled choices keep their state.

states.name: option disabled
states.description: The choice cannot be changed; its box, label and description use the disabled roles.

states.name: error
states.description: The error replaces the help text, with an icon, and is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every choice and select all are disabled and the label dims.

appearance: The label in the label style, then the checkboxes of MonarchCheckboxToggleStyle: accent strong fill when checked, surface fill and input border when not. Descriptions use the muted text role, disabled parts the disabled roles, and the error the danger strong role. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web group takes value and defaultValue; iOS uses one Binding<Set<String>>, so the order of checked values is not kept (read it from options). The form name for submission does not apply. Inside a web Field the group takes the Field's label; on iOS the label, help and error are parameters, drawn by MonarchFormField. The mixed state is the system's Toggle(sources:) mixed state, the same mechanism Android's tri-state checkbox mirrors.
accessibility: The choices are inside one container labelled with the group label, whose hint is the error ("Error: …"), the help text and "Required", each when present; a new error is announced.
Each choice is a standard Toggle given to VoiceOver through the checkbox style's accessibility representation, read with its label and description.
Select all is a standard Toggle(sources:isOn:), so VoiceOver reads its on, off and mixed values.
Every checkbox row is at least 44 points high and the whole row, label included, is the touch target.
The mixed state is shown by a minus glyph and checked by a check mark, not by colour alone.
edgeCases: With no options, select all is disabled.
Disabled choices are left as they are by select all, and are not counted when deciding between mixed and on.
Long labels and descriptions wrap; the horizontal layout wraps onto more lines and stacks at the accessibility sizes.

name: MonarchCodeBlock
title: CodeBlock
wrapsNative: ScrollView(.horizontal) of monospaced Text built from AttributedString, with Toggle (.monarchButton) for wrap and MonarchCopyButton
summary: A code sample with a header (title or language), copy, a wrap toggle, optional line numbers, light syntax colouring and a diff mode.
whenToUse: To show code people read or copy: an API request in settings, a configuration snippet in onboarding, a change in a message.
whenNotToUse: For a short token inside a sentence use MonarchInlineCodeStyle. For a single value to copy, such as a URL or key, use MonarchCopyField.
api: init(_ code: String, language: String? = nil, title: String? = nil, isDiff: Bool? = nil, isHighlighted: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = false, showsWrapToggle: Bool = true, isCopyable: Bool = true, isWrapped: Binding<Bool>? = nil, labels: MonarchCodeBlockLabels = MonarchCodeBlockLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchCodeBlockLabels { init(copy: String? = nil, copied: String? = nil, copiedAnnouncement: String? = nil, wrap: String? = nil, added: String? = nil, removed: String? = nil, codeName: (@Sendable (String?) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: code
options.description: The code, exactly as it should be copied.

options.name: language
options.description: A language id ("ts", "python", "bash", "diff"). Picks the highlighter and the header text. Highlighted: JavaScript and TypeScript, JSON, Python, shell, CSS and SCSS, HTML, XML and SVG, SQL, Go, Rust. Others are plain text.

options.name: title
options.description: Header text, such as a file name or what the snippet does. Also names the code. Defaults to the language name.

options.name: isDiff
options.description: Draws + and - lines as a diff. nil means true when language is "diff" or "patch".

options.name: isHighlighted
options.description: Turns syntax colouring on or off.

options.name: showsLineNumbers
options.description: Shows line numbers before the lines. They are not read by VoiceOver and not copied.

options.name: showsWrapToggle
options.description: Shows the "Wrap lines" toggle in the header.

options.name: isCopyable
options.description: Shows the copy button in the header.

options.name: isWrapped
options.description: Whether long lines wrap instead of scrolling sideways. Without it the component keeps the state itself, starting unwrapped.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: copy, copied, copiedAnnouncement, wrap, added, removed and codeName.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied code after each copy.

states.name: unwrapped
states.description: Default. Each line stays on one line and the code scrolls sideways inside the block.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Long lines wrap; the wrap toggle is on and drawn with the accent fill of MonarchToggleButtonStyle.

states.name: diff
states.description: Added and removed lines get the diff fills and a visible + or − marker; hunk headers use the info colour; file headers are muted and semibold.

states.name: copied
states.description: The copy button shows a checkmark and "Copied" for two seconds.

states.name: no header
states.description: With no title, no language, no wrap toggle and no copy button, the header is not drawn.

appearance: A subtle fill with a subtle border and medium corners; the header has the muted fill and the title in the muted text colour. Code uses the monospaced code type role. Keywords use the info strong role, strings success strong, numbers warning strong, tags danger strong, attributes and properties AI strong, and comments the muted text colour in italics. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The tokenizer is ported from the web and gives the same tokens, without the web's incremental mode for streaming code. The web code is a focusable scroll region for the keyboard; on iOS the region scrolls by touch and VoiceOver reads it line by line. The web has a CodeTabs companion for the same sample in several languages; on iOS put several MonarchCodeBlock views in MonarchTabs or a segmented Picker. AiCodeBlock's Apply and Insert are not part of this component. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The code is a VoiceOver container named after the title, else "<Language> code", else "Code".
Each line is one element read as its text; added and removed lines of a diff start with "Added:" or "Removed:"; lines with only white space are skipped.
Line numbers and diff markers are not read, and diff lines carry a visible + or − marker, so a change does not depend on colour alone.
The wrap control is a standard Toggle named "Wrap lines" with an on or off value.
The copy button is MonarchCopyButton named "Copy" followed by the code's name; it announces "Copied to clipboard".
The code reads left to right in right-to-left layouts; the header follows the layout direction.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; at large sizes the header actions move under the title, and the header buttons keep a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: A final line break does not add an empty line; Windows line breaks are treated as line breaks.
Tabs are drawn as four spaces; the copied code keeps its tabs.
Empty code draws one empty line.
An unknown language is plain text, and its id is shown as given in the header.
Very long code is drawn in full (not lazily); keep samples to a screenful or two.
The highlighter is not a grammar: unusual code can be coloured imperfectly, never changed.

states.name: one snippet

states.name: no snippets

states.name: synced
states.description: Choosing a tab in one set switches every visible set with the same syncKey that has that snippet, and the choice is restored on the next launch.

Changing tabs replaces the code block, so its wrap toggle resets.
The stored value is only written when syncKey is given.

appearance: Swatches are 28-point discs in the colour itself with a default-border hairline, in a grid of 44-point cells. The selection ring uses the default text colour and the check mark sits on the inverse background, so the mark is visible on any swatch in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web has a hex text box and a native colour input. On iOS the system colour picker already has a hex field, sliders, a spectrum, an eyedropper and saved colours, so Monarch adds no text box and there is no invalid-hex message; the selected value is shown as text beside the picker. The web's roving arrow-key focus is not reproduced: each swatch is a button. The value is the same lower-case #rrggbb text as on the web and Android, so a stored colour moves between platforms; opacity is not supported. A wide-gamut colour picked in the system picker is clamped to sRGB.
accessibility: Each swatch is a button named by its name and value, for example "Blue, #2563eb", with the selected trait on the chosen one.
The selection is also a ring and a check mark, so it does not depend on seeing the colour.
The custom row is the standard ColorPicker; its label is the row title followed by the selected value as text.
The label has the header trait.
Every swatch has a 44-point touch target; text and swatches scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A selection that is not a hex colour is treated as none.
MonarchColorSwatch(hex:name:) returns nil for text that is not a hex colour, so a list built with compactMap skips it.
Two swatches with the same colour have the same identity; keep the colours distinct.
While there is no selection the system picker opens on the theme's text colour; nothing is written until the person picks.

summary: A panel to show, hide, find and reorder the columns of a table, for a sheet, a settings screen or a saved-view editor.
whenToUse: To let people choose which columns a MonarchDataTable shows and in what order, usually in a sheet opened from a Columns button.
whenNotToUse: For a short list of on/off settings, use Toggles in a Form. For reordering other things, use a List with onMove (reorderable-list).

options.description: The columns in their default order. MonarchDataTableColumn.chooserColumn gives one.

options.description: The ids of hidden columns, the same set MonarchDataTable takes.

options.description: Column ids in display order. With it, rows reorder with onMove and accessibility actions; ids missing from it follow in their default order.

options.description: Offers the search field from this many columns. Pass Int.max for never.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.description: A switch per column, on when it is shown, with "5 of 8 shown" under the title.

states.name: required column
states.description: Always on and disabled, with "Always shown" under its name.

states.name: minimum reached
states.description: The switches of the last shown columns are disabled.

states.name: searching
states.description: Only matching columns are listed, reordering is off, and "No columns match." is shown when nothing matches.

states.name: some hidden
states.description: A Show all button appears under the list.

appearance: A system list. The title is subheading text in the default role and the count caption text in the muted role; notes, the search icon and the no-match text use the muted role. Switches are the system's and take the theme's accent tint. Show all and Reset are small ghost MonarchButtons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web panel moves columns with Move up and Move down icon buttons; on iOS rows reorder with List.onMove (drag a row, or the reorder controls when the app puts the list in edit mode), and VoiceOver users get Move up and Move down as accessibility actions. The web uses checkboxes; iOS uses the platform switch. The web takes a visibility record; on iOS it is the set of hidden ids. The search is a field inside the list rather than .searchable, so it works without a navigation container. The web headingLevel has no equivalent; the title has the header trait. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The title and count are one header element: "Columns, 5 of 8 shown".
Each column is a standard switch read with its name, its note and its state.
Columns that cannot be hidden and the last shown columns are disabled switches.
With order, each row has the accessibility actions "Move Status up" and "Move Status down" (only where the move is possible), and every move is announced.
The clear-search button is named "Clear search" and has a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: Ids in order that no longer exist are skipped; new columns follow in their default order.
Search ignores case and diacritics and trims spaces.
Show all also clears hidden ids of columns that are not listed.
The panel is a List and fills its space; present it in a sheet or give it a frame.

whenToUse: After someone picks a CSV or spreadsheet to import, on its own screen, to choose which product field each column fills.
whenNotToUse: To choose which columns a table shows, use MonarchColumnChooser. To preview the rows that will be imported, use MonarchPreviewRows.

options.name: mapping
options.description: Column name to field id. A column missing from it is not imported. Start from MonarchColumnMapping.mapping(from: suggest(...)).

options.name: fields
options.description: The fields the columns can be mapped to, with required flags, help and aliases.

options.name: suggestions
options.description: The suggestions behind the badges and Use suggestions. By default, MonarchColumnMapping.suggest(sources, fields:).

options.name: showsIssues
options.description: Shows the missing required fields and the duplicate errors. Pass false until the person first tries to go on.

options.name: showsBulkActions
options.description: Shows Use suggestions (when the mapping differs from them) and Don’t import any (when something is mapped).

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: picker names, the skip option, badges, the summary, the errors and the buttons.

states.name: suggested
states.description: A column set to its suggested field shows a success "Matched" badge for an exact match or an info "Suggested" badge for a close one.

states.name: not imported
states.description: The picker shows "Don’t import"; the column is missing from the mapping.

states.name: missing required
states.description: The summary section shows "Map a column to: …" with an error icon in the danger colour.

states.name: duplicate
states.description: Each column that chose the same field shows "<Field> is also chosen for <other columns>." under its picker.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true), the pickers and the bulk buttons cannot be used and take the system's disabled look.

appearance: A grouped list. Column headers in the default text colour, example values and help in the muted text colour, the chosen field as the picker's value in the accent colour. Errors use the danger strong colour with an icon. The roles follow light, dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ColumnMapping is a three-column grid (column, example values, field) with a native select per row and column headings on wide screens. On iPhone a three-column grid does not fit, so each column is a list row whose label holds the header and example values, with the standard menu picker as its value, and the headings are left out. The web size prop (sm, md) has no counterpart: list rows size themselves with Dynamic Type. The web disabled prop is the standard disabled(_:) modifier. The web value and onValueChange become one binding; the web's uncontrolled defaultValue is the app's initial state. The suggestion algorithm (normalising names, word overlap, containment and edit distance, threshold 0.75, each field once) is the same as the web's suggestColumnMapping. The view is a List, so give it its own screen or a height. Android shares the design.
accessibility: Each picker is named "Field for <column>" and its value is the chosen field or "Don’t import".
The example values, the suggestion badge, a duplicate error and the field's help are read as the picker's hint.
Errors are an icon and text in the danger colour, never colour alone; suggestions are a word in a badge, not only a tone.
Changes to the summary ("3 of 5 columns mapped") are announced.
The bulk buttons are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: A blank header is shown as its position, "#3".
Two columns with the same header share one entry in the mapping, because the mapping is keyed by name, as on the web.
A field id in the mapping that is not in fields does not count as mapped.
Long headers and values wrap; nothing is truncated.

whenToUse: Above a table or a list with optional columns or fields, when people choose which ones they see. On iPad at regular width with a SwiftUI Table, Table(columnCustomization:) gives the same choice in the column headers' own menu and saves it with @SceneStorage.
whenNotToUse: When people also reorder or search columns, use a sheet with a List in edit mode (onMove). For choosing one view of the data, use a segmented Picker (see view-switcher). For filters, use a Menu with a Picker.

states.description: A Toggle that is on shows a checkmark before the column's name.

states.name: last column
states.description: The last visible column's Toggle is disabled with disabled(_:), so the table is never empty (the web's minVisible of 1).

states.name: all shown
states.description: Show all columns is disabled when every column is visible.

appearance: The menu is drawn by the system in every theme, with light, dark and Increase Contrast; Monarch colours do not apply inside it. The trigger is a small secondary MonarchButtonStyle button; the theme's tint colours the checkmarks.
platformNotes: The web ColumnMenu is a component that takes DataTable's column state and offers minVisible, showAll, onReset and a trigger size. On iOS the same result is a few lines of standard Menu, Toggle and Button in the app, so Monarch adds no type: minVisible is disabled(_:) on the last visible Toggle, Show all and Reset are Buttons after a Divider, and the trigger size is the button style's size. The web keeps the menu open while items are checked; on iOS that is menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled). Android plans a Compose recipe for the same menu.
accessibility: System behaviour: the trigger is a button and each column is a toggle item read with its checked state.
The trigger's value says how many columns are shown ("3 of 4 shown"), set with accessibilityValue, like the web's hidden count.
A disabled last column is read as dimmed, so VoiceOver users know it cannot be hidden.
The system gives each item a row at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: Keep at least one column visible by disabling the last visible Toggle.

Keep the menu open on iOS with menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled) on each Toggle (the catalogue page does), or the menu closes after every change. That modifier does not exist on macOS, so the compiled example leaves it out.
Store the visible set with @AppStorage or @SceneStorage (as a joined string) if it should survive a relaunch.

summary: Two or three side-by-side columns inside a document, which stack into one column on narrow screens.
whenToUse: When two or three short pieces of document content read better next to each other: a comparison, an image beside its notes.
whenNotToUse: For screen layout around a document (a list beside a detail), use NavigationSplitView or MonarchResizablePanels when the person resizes the split. For data in rows and columns, use a table (MonarchTableBlock in a document). For a grid of equal items, use LazyVGrid.

options.name: ratio
options.description: The share of the width for the first of two columns, kept between 0.2 and 0.8 (0.5 when not finite). Three or more columns are equal.

options.name: content
options.description: The columns, one child view each. A column of several views goes in a VStack.

states.name: side by side
states.description: At 480 points wide or more, the columns sit next to each other with a 24-point gap, top-aligned.

states.name: stacked
states.description: Below 480 points, and at the accessibility text sizes, the columns stack in order with a 12-point gap.

appearance: No surface or colour of its own: only spacing from the space tokens. The columns' content brings its own colours.
platformNotes: The web ColumnsBlock is both a static component and a Tiptap editor node with a keyboard and pointer resize handle that writes the ratio into the document. iOS has no Tiptap document model, so only the static block is offered; for a split the person resizes, use MonarchResizablePanels. The web stacks with a container query at 30rem; iOS uses the width the layout is offered, 480 points. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The block is a container: VoiceOver reads the first column completely, then the next, in order.
At the accessibility text sizes the columns stack so text keeps a readable width.
Columns are placed from the leading edge, so the first column is on the right in right-to-left languages.
edgeCases: One child fills the width.
A column taller than the others sets the block's height; the others stay at the top.
Inside a horizontal ScrollView, which offers no width, the block assumes 480 points and lays the columns side by side.

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the field and is the title of the sheet.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the chosen option, or nil.

options.name: options
options.description: The options in order: id, label, description, hint, group, keywords, systemImage and isDisabled.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in the field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the field, also read as the hint.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown with an icon and announced.

options.name: clearOptionTitle
options.description: Adds a first row that clears the selection, such as "Unassigned". Hidden while searching.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows a progress row with "Loading…" in the list, for options that are being fetched.

options.name: isClearable
options.description: Shows a clear button in the field while something is chosen.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the chosen label as selectable text in the field box, with Read only in the hint. It does not open the list and has no clear button.

options.name: sortsByMatch
options.description: While searching, lists labels that start with the text first, then labels with a word that does, then the rest, keeping the order within each.

options.name: limit
options.description: Shows at most this many matches, with "Showing 50 of 120. Type to narrow the list."

options.name: searchText
options.description: The search text, for apps that search a server: bind it, pass a filter that keeps every option, and update options and isLoading from it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: filter
options.description: Decides whether an option matches the trimmed search text. By default the label, hint and keywords are searched, ignoring case and accents.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Offers "Create “text”" when no label equals the typed text. Return the new option to choose it; return nil to only close the sheet.

options.name: loadError
options.description: Shown in the list in place of the options when they failed to load; empty uses "Couldn’t load the options."

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Offers Try again beside loadError.

options.name: option.leadingText
options.description: Decorative text before an option's label, such as a flag emoji. Not read by VoiceOver.

options.name: option.labelLanguage
options.description: The language an option's label is written in, so VoiceOver reads an endonym in its own language.

states.name: empty
states.description: The prompt in the subtle text role; VoiceOver reads the value "None".

states.name: chosen
states.description: The option's label in the default text role, and a clear button when clearable.

states.name: open
states.description: A sheet at medium or large height with the search field, the options in groups, a check mark on the chosen one, and Cancel.

states.name: no match
states.description: "No matches", or the create row when onCreate is set.

states.name: loading
states.description: A progress indicator and "Loading…" at the end of the list.

states.name: error
states.description: The danger border and the message with an icon, announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the disabled fill and text roles; the field cannot be opened.

appearance: The field matches MonarchTextField: surface fill, input border and control radius, the danger strong border for an error, disabled roles when disabled. In the list, labels use the default text role, descriptions and hints the muted role, disabled options the disabled role and the check mark the accent strong role. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows the list in a popover under a typing field, with keyboard navigation (arrows, Home, End, Page Up and Down). On iPhone a long list belongs in a sheet with the system search field, so the field is a button and typing happens in .searchable. Planned coverage named a searchable List in a sheet; that is what this is. Only single selection is offered: for several values use MonarchTagInput or MonarchCheckboxGroup. The web's onSearch with built-in debounce and abort is replaced by binding searchText and running the search in the app, for example with .task(id:), which SwiftUI cancels when the text changes. Free media is a systemImage, and renderOption has no equivalent. The inline mode is not offered: the sheet is already a full picker. Several closures are optional (filter, onCreate, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is filter.
accessibility: The field is a button labelled with label, whose value is the chosen label or "None" and whose hint is the error ("Error: …"), the help text and "Required"; a new error is announced.
The clear button is a separate button named "Clear" with a 44-point touch target.
In the sheet each option is one button read with its label, description and hint; the chosen option has the selected trait and a check mark.
Disabled options cannot be chosen and use the disabled text role.
Icons are decorative; the label names the option.
edgeCases: A selection that is not in options shows the label remembered from an earlier choice, or else the raw id.
The search text is cleared when the sheet closes.
Groups keep the order in which they first appear; options without a group come first.
With a limit, matches are cut before grouping, and the note says how many matched.

title: ComingSoonState
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchBadge, MonarchEmptyState (ContentUnavailableView) and Label rows
summary: A recipe, not a component: an empty state that says a feature is planned, with a "Coming soon" badge, what the feature will do, what is planned and an optional "Notify me" action.
whenToUse: In a tab, a card or a screen for a feature that is announced but not available yet.
whenNotToUse: For a feature the person has no access to, use MonarchErrorState with the forbidden kind. For an empty list of a feature that exists, use MonarchEmptyState.
api: VStack { MonarchBadge(_:tone:systemImage:); MonarchEmptyState(_:message:systemImage:actionTitle:action:); Label(_:systemImage:) … }

states.name: with an action
states.description: MonarchEmptyState draws a button when actionTitle and action are given, such as "Notify me".

states.name: without a feature name
states.description: Use "Coming soon" as the empty state's title and leave the badge out.

appearance: An info-toned subtle badge with a clock above the standard empty state (icon, title, message, button), followed by muted body rows with check marks for what is planned.
platformNotes: The web ComingSoonState is a component with fixed "Coming soon" wording, the badge read as part of the heading, and a highlights list. On iOS it composes existing parts: MonarchEmptyState has no slot for a badge or a list, so they sit above and below it. The app supplies the wording, so Monarch ships no strings for it. Android shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: The badge is read before the title, as "Coming soon", then the title with the header trait.
The empty state's icon is decorative; its button has a 44-point touch target.
Each planned item is a Label read as its text; the check mark is part of the label and not a state.
edgeCases: Keep the planned list to three or four lines; it does not scroll on its own.
Change the button title after the person asks to be notified, so the screen confirms it.

summary: A recipe, not a component: a full-height sheet with the system search field and the app's actions as grouped results, opened from a button or Command-K on a hardware keyboard.
whenToUse: In an app with many actions or places, as one searchable way to run them: create a record, jump to a screen, change a setting.
whenNotToUse: For searching content (documents, people) use searchable with MonarchSearchResults on the screen itself; for a handful of actions use a Menu or a toolbar.
api: func sheet<Content: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> Content) -> some View
func searchable(text: Binding<String>, prompt: String) -> some View
func keyboardShortcut(_ key: KeyEquivalent, modifiers: EventModifiers = .command) -> some View
MonarchSearchResults.init(groups: [MonarchSearchResultGroup], query: String = "", …, onSelect: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchSearchResult, MonarchSearchResultGroup) -> Void)

MonarchSearchResult.init(_ title: String, id: String, path: [String] = [], snippet: String? = nil, …, systemImage: String? = nil, fileName: String? = nil, meta: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil)

states.name: closed
states.description: The trigger: a MonarchButton in a toolbar or header. Command-K opens it from a hardware keyboard.

states.name: open
states.description: A sheet with a navigation bar, Close, the search field and every command grouped with its symbol and shortcut.

states.name: filtered
states.description: Typing narrows the commands; matched words are highlighted by MonarchSearchResults and empty groups disappear.

states.name: no match
states.description: MonarchSearchResults shows its empty state, "No results for …".

states.name: ran
states.description: Choosing a command runs it and closes the sheet; the query is cleared on close.

appearance: The sheet, navigation bar and search field are the system's in every theme; rows are MonarchSearchResultItem rows with the symbol, the highlighted title and the shortcut as muted meta text.
platformNotes: The web CommandPalette is one component: a centred dialog with its own input, arrow-key navigation, recent items, nested pages and a global Mod+K hotkey. On iOS it is a recipe of system parts: a sheet is the phone's surface for a modal task, searchable gives the system field with dictation and the keyboard's Search key, and keyboardShortcut gives Command-K on a hardware keyboard and lists it in the iPad's shortcut overlay (it has no meaning on a phone without a keyboard). Arrow-key focus and Return in the list come from the system List. Nested pages are NavigationLink pushes inside the NavigationStack. The search field is not focused when the sheet opens on iOS 17; on iOS 18 add searchFocused.
accessibility: The trigger is a MonarchButton with a 44-point target; the shortcut is announced by the system on iPad.
The sheet has a Close button in the cancellation position and can be dismissed by swipe or the VoiceOver escape gesture.
Each command is a button read with its title and shortcut; group headings have the header trait and are read with their count.
The results summary is announced when the query changes, as MonarchSearchResults does.
edgeCases: Clear the query when the sheet closes so it opens fresh.
Run commands that open another sheet after the palette has dismissed (onDismiss), because a sheet cannot present while it is closing.
With many commands, filter by keywords as well as titles; MonarchSearchResults highlights only the title words that match.

name: MonarchCommentThread
title: CommentThread
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchMessageRow comments (each with .contextMenu for Delete), a MonarchButton fold and Resolve button, a MonarchMessageComposer reply field and .confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:presenting:actions:message:) before deleting
summary: One threaded discussion: the starting comment, replies with older ones folded, an optional quote, Resolve and Reopen, and a reply field that stays busy while the app saves.
whenToUse: A discussion anchored to one item and shown in place: a sheet opened from a highlighted passage, a card under a field, a ticket's detail screen. Review flows where threads are resolved when settled.
whenNotToUse: For a chat conversation use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow and MonarchMessageComposer. For a list of many threads with filters use a List of threads that each push a screen holding this view.
api: init(_ comments: [MonarchCommentThreadComment], quote: String? = nil, isResolved: Bool = false, visibleReplies: Int = 3, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchCommentThreadLabels = MonarchCommentThreadLabels(), onResolvedChange: (@MainActor (Bool) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onDelete: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onReply: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchCommentThreadComment: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable { init(id: String, author: String, body: String, createdAt: Date, avatarURL: URL? = nil, seed: String? = nil, canDelete: Bool = false) }

struct MonarchCommentThreadLabels: Sendable { init(thread:quote:showEarlier:earlierShown:reply:replyPlaceholder:send:resolve:reopen:resolved:resolvedHint:resolvedNotice:reopenedNotice:sentNotice:actionFailed:delete:deleteTitle:deleteMessage:cancel:), every parameter optional }

options.name: comments
options.description: The comments, oldest first. The first starts the thread; the rest are replies.

options.name: quote
options.description: The passage the thread is about, shown above it beside a bar.

options.name: isResolved
options.description: Shows the Resolved badge, makes the button Reopen and replaces the reply field with a hint.

options.name: visibleReplies
options.description: The latest replies kept visible; older ones fold behind "Show N earlier replies". One folded reply is never hidden.

options.name: now
options.description: Fixes "now" for the relative times, for tests and previews. The clock by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onResolvedChange
options.description: Resolves (true) or reopens the thread. Adds the Resolve button, which shows a spinner while it runs.

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Deletes the comment with this id after a confirmation dialog. Adds Delete to the context menu of comments with canDelete.

options.name: onReply
options.description: Posts the trimmed reply. Adds the reply field. The text clears when it returns and stays when it throws.

states.name: open
states.description: Resolve button (when onResolvedChange is given) and the reply field (when onReply is given).

states.name: folded
states.description: Between the first comment and the latest replies a ghost button reads "Show N earlier replies"; activating it shows them all and announces it.

states.name: resolved
states.description: A success Resolved badge with a check, the button reads Reopen, and the reply field is replaced by "This thread is resolved. Reopen it to reply."

states.name: busy
states.description: Resolve shows a spinner and the other buttons are disabled; the reply field shows its sending state until onReply returns.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger inline notice "That didn't work. Try again." is shown and announced; a reply keeps its text.

states.name: deleting
states.description: Delete in a comment's context menu opens a system confirmation dialog with a destructive Delete comment and Cancel.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no comments only the top row and the reply field are shown, so the first comment can be written.

appearance: Comments use MonarchMessageRow (default text for author and body, muted text for the time). The quote is muted text beside a bar in the strong border colour. The resolved badge uses the success tone; a failure uses the danger tone with an icon. All colours follow the theme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web thread shows an icon delete button on each comment and a Textarea with an Enter-to-send hint; on iOS Delete is in the comment's context menu, as messages offer actions on touch, and the reply field is MonarchMessageComposer, whose hardware-keyboard Return sends. The web mutes a resolved thread's text; iOS keeps the message rows' colours and marks the state with a Resolved badge and the spoken value. The web moves focus to the first revealed reply; iOS announces how many replies were shown. Comment bodies are plain text on iOS; the web accepts rich content. Android has no comment thread yet. Status experimental: it is a product composite until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The thread is a container named "Thread started by" and the first author, with the value Resolved while resolved.
The quote is one element read as "Quoted text" with the passage as its value.
Each comment is a MonarchMessageRow read as author, full date and time, and text; Delete is in its context menu, available through the VoiceOver actions.
Showing folded replies announces "3 earlier replies shown"; resolving, reopening, posting a reply and a failure are announced.
A failure is an icon and text, not colour alone; the resolved state is a badge with a check and text.
Every button is at least 44 points; the reply field is named Reply.
edgeCases: With visibleReplies at 0 every reply folds; a negative value counts as 0.
Exactly one reply more than visibleReplies is shown rather than folded behind a button for one item.
A reply of only spaces and line breaks is not posted.
Long names and bodies wrap; the top row lets the quote wrap beside the button.
New replies arriving while folded stay visible because the latest replies are always shown.
