name: MonarchCommentsPanel
title: CommentsPanel
wrapsNative: Content for a NavigationStack in a .sheet or .inspector: Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) for Open and Resolved, a List with .listStyle(.plain) of thread rows (Button with MonarchAvatar), .navigationDestination(item:) that pushes the selected thread as a MonarchCommentThread in a ScrollView, .navigationTitle and a .cancellationAction toolbar Close button
summary: Every comment thread of a document or record: Open and Resolved threads in a list, and one thread at a time pushed as a screen with its quote, replies, Resolve or Reopen and confirmed delete.
whenToUse: Beside a document or record that people discuss in threads anchored to passages: the comments sheet of a document editor on a phone, or the comments inspector beside it on iPad. Selecting a thread lets the app highlight its passage.
whenNotToUse: For one thread shown in place next to its passage, use MonarchCommentThread. For a chat conversation, use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow. For replies to one chat message, use MonarchThreadPanel.
api: init(_ threads: [MonarchCommentsPanelThread]?, filter: Binding<MonarchCommentsPanelFilter>, selectedThreadID: Binding<String?>, errorMessage: String? = nil, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchCommentsPanelLabels = MonarchCommentsPanelLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onClose: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onReply: (@MainActor (String, String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onResolvedChange: (@MainActor (String, Bool) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onDeleteComment: (@MainActor (String, String) async throws -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchCommentsPanelThread: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable { init(id: String, comments: [MonarchCommentThreadComment], quote: String? = nil, updatedAt: Date? = nil, isResolved: Bool = false, canResolve: Bool = true, canReply: Bool = true) }
enum MonarchCommentsPanelFilter: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case open, resolved }

struct MonarchCommentsPanelLabels: Sendable { init(title:close:filter:open:resolved:loading:emptyOpen:emptyResolved:emptyHint:commentCount:thread:), every parameter optional; thread: MonarchCommentThreadLabels }

options.name: threads
options.description: The threads, or nil while they load, listed in this order. Each has an id, its comments (MonarchCommentThreadComment, oldest first), an optional quote and updatedAt, isResolved, canResolve and canReply.

options.name: filter
options.description: Open or Resolved: which threads are listed. Changing it closes the open thread.

options.name: selectedThreadID
options.description: The thread pushed in full, or nil for the list. The panel sets it when a row is selected, and to nil after the back button, the back swipe, a filter change or a successful resolve. A thread not listed under the current filter shows the list.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Loading failed: shown instead of the list.

options.name: now
options.description: Fixes now for the relative times. Without it the times follow the clock and refresh every minute.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the open thread's (MonarchCommentThreadLabels).

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Try again to errorMessage, with MonarchInlineErrorRetry.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Adds a Close button in the cancellation position of the toolbar, on the list and on the open thread.

options.name: onReply
options.description: Posts a reply, given the thread id and the trimmed text. Shows the reply field on open threads with canReply. Throw to keep the text and show a failure.

options.name: onResolvedChange
options.description: Resolves (true) or reopens a thread. Shows Resolve or Reopen on threads with canResolve. On success the panel returns to the list; throw to show a failure.

options.name: onDeleteComment
options.description: Deletes a comment, given the thread id and the comment id, after a system confirmation dialog. Offered in the context menu of comments with canDelete.

states.name: list
states.description: The segmented Open and Resolved picker and one row per thread: the starter's avatar and name, the quote cut after two lines, and the number of comments with the last activity.

states.name: thread
states.description: The selected thread is pushed with the comment count as its inline title: a MonarchCommentThread with the quote, comments, Resolve or Reopen and the reply field. The back button and the back swipe return to the list.

states.name: loading
states.description: threads is nil: a MonarchLoadingState with three rows, read as Loading comments.

states.name: error
states.description: errorMessage is set: a MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again, or the message in the strong danger role without onRetry.

states.name: empty
states.description: No thread under the filter: a small MonarchEmptyState, No open comments with the hint Select text to start a discussion., or No resolved comments.

states.name: resolved
states.description: After a thread is resolved or reopened the panel returns to the list; MonarchCommentThread announces Thread resolved or Thread reopened.

appearance: No fill of its own, so it takes the sheet's or inspector's surface. The starter's name uses the default text role, the quote and the count line the muted text role, and the segmented picker and the navigation bar are the system controls in the theme's tint. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's CommentsPanel is a side panel that swaps the list for the thread in place, with an All comments back button, and keeps its filter and selection itself when uncontrolled. On iOS the thread is pushed onto the NavigationStack the panel sits in, so the system back button (titled with the previous screen) and the back swipe return to the list; there is no All comments label. Filter and selection are Bindings, as SwiftUI state is. The web's icon delete button on each comment is the comment's context menu here (MonarchCommentThread). The web's Show group name is the segmented Picker's hidden label. The web's Enter to send hint is left out: a hardware keyboard's Return sends and the on-screen keyboard's Return adds a line. Android swaps the views in place under a BackHandler and has emptyIcon and backIcon slots because it bundles no icons; iOS uses SF Symbols and the system back button. Android announces the resolved notice from the panel; on iOS MonarchCommentThread announces it once. Status experimental: it is a product composite until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The navigation title, Comments, is the screen's heading; the open thread's title is its comment count.
Open and Resolved are a segmented Picker with the system selected state.
Each thread row is one button read as the starter, the quote, the number of comments and the last activity; the avatar is decorative.
The back button and the back swipe return from a thread to the list; the system restores focus.
Loading is one element read as Loading comments; resolving, reopening, replies and failures are announced by MonarchCommentThread.
Rows, Close and Try again have touch targets of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A selectedThreadID that is not listed under the current filter shows the list, so a thread resolved by someone else does not stay open.
Switching the filter closes the open thread.
A thread without comments has no name or avatar in its row and reads 0 comments.
A long quote is cut after two lines in the list and shown in full in the thread.
Each thread starts with an empty reply field; the draft is not kept across threads.
Without now, the relative times refresh every minute while on screen.
The panel needs an enclosing NavigationStack for its title, its toolbar and pushing a thread.

                id: "c2",
                author: "Ben Okafor",
                body: "Confirmed. They are ready from the Monday.",
                createdAt: Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 1_773_141_000),
                canDelete: true
            ),
        ],
        quote: "The rollout starts in the second week of the quarter."
    ),
    MonarchCommentsPanelThread(
        id: "t2",
        comments: [

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including operator names and problems.

options.name: makeID
options.description: Makes the id of a new condition.

states.name: default
states.description: One card per condition with its title, a remove button, the field menu, the operator menu and the value input.

states.name: match switch
states.description: With a match binding and two or more conditions, "Match [all | any] of these conditions" above the list; the words wrap above and below the switch when the line does not fit.

states.name: no value
states.description: Operators such as is empty, is yes and is no show no value input.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No conditions. This applies every time." in muted text, then the add button.

states.name: errors shown
states.description: An incomplete condition gets a danger border and "Choose a field.", "Enter a value." or "The chosen value no longer exists. Pick another." with an icon.

states.name: full
states.description: At maxConditions the add button is replaced by "You can add up to 20 conditions."

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every control is disabled and the text uses the disabled role.

appearance: Each condition is a card on the surface fill with the subtle border, the danger border when a problem is shown. Titles and the match words use the muted text role, the problem the danger strong role. The menus are system menu pickers, the switch a system segmented picker, and the text and number inputs read the MonarchTextField tokens, so all follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: A condition is the MonarchCondition that MonarchQueryBuilder edits, and all or any is MonarchConditionMatch (the query builder's groups use MonarchQueryCombinator), so the conditions move between the two without conversion; the row view is shared code that MonarchQueryBuilder also uses for its rules. Compared with the web, the iOS operators come from MonarchConditionOperator, which has no is any of, is none of, multi-select or tags kinds yet, and MonarchConditionField has no group heading or disabled-with-reason field; those web options are not offered. The web's evaluateConditions is MonarchQueryGroup(id:combinator:rules:).matches(_:calendar:), and dates compare by day in a Calendar instead of as text. The web prop disabled is the SwiftUI .disabled modifier. Rows stack vertically on a phone instead of sitting on one line. Android has no entry yet.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Conditions" and each row a container named "Condition 1".
The field menu, operator menu, value and remove button are named with the position: "Condition 1 field", "Condition 1 operator", "Condition 1 value", "Remove condition 1".
The all or any switch is a segmented picker named "Conditions that must hold"; the words around it are hidden from VoiceOver.
A shown problem is text with an icon, not only a red border, and is read as the row's hint.
Removing a condition announces "Condition 1 removed."
The remove button, menus and switch have 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: A stored field the list no longer has shows as "region (removed)" in the field menu and is reported as the field problem.
A select value whose choice was removed shows no choice in the menu and is reported as the option problem.
A date value starts empty with a Choose a date button; the day it fills in comes from today.
Number values are parsed in the environment locale and keep the typed text until it is a number.
Changing the field resets the operator and value; changing the operator keeps a value of the same kind.

title: ConfirmDialog
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:), or confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:), with Button(role: .destructive) and Button(role: .cancel)
summary: Confirmation of a consequential action is the system alert, or the confirmation dialog, with a destructive button and Cancel. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Before an action that deletes or cannot be undone. Use confirmationDialog when the person started the action from a control on screen, and alert when the question interrupts. Say in the message what will change.
whenNotToUse: Do not confirm actions that are easy to undo; offer undo. For a choice between several options see choice-dialog.
api: func alert(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
func confirmationDialog(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
Button(_ title: String, role: ButtonRole?, action: () -> Void)

states.name: presented
states.description: The alert is centred over a dimmed screen; the confirmation dialog rises from the bottom on iPhone and is a popover on iPad.

states.name: destructive
states.description: A button with the destructive role is drawn in red.

states.name: type to confirm
states.description: An alert may contain a TextField; disable the destructive button until the text matches.

appearance: The system draws both in every theme, following the light or dark appearance. Destructive buttons are the system's red, not the theme's danger colour. Monarch does not colour the buttons.
platformNotes: The web ConfirmDialog stays open while the action runs and shows pending and error states, and has a consequences list, a confirm phrase, an acknowledgement checkbox and a reason field. The system alert closes when a button is tapped, so run the action afterwards and show progress and failure on the screen (a loading MonarchButton, a MonarchBanner). The confirm phrase is a TextField in the alert with the destructive button disabled until it matches. The acknowledgement checkbox and the reason field with validation need a sheet of your own. Android uses a Material AlertDialog.
accessibility: System behaviour: the alert is modal, VoiceOver reads the title and message, and focus returns to the presenting control afterwards.
System behaviour: the escape gesture chooses the button with the cancel role.
The destructive role is also spoken by its title, so name the button after the action ("Delete"), not "OK".
edgeCases: An alert with no buttons gets a system OK button.
Only one alert or dialog is presented at a time; a second one waits or is dropped.
With a hardware keyboard, Return activates the default action. Do not make a destructive button the default.

options.name: apps

states.name: ready
states.description: The rows on a surface with a subtle border, separated by dividers.

states.name: loading

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState: "No connected apps".

states.name: error

states.name: removing
states.description: The row's Remove access button shows progress.

states.name: removal failed

states.name: suspended app

appearance: Rows sit on the surface background with a subtle border. Logos are MonarchFavicons with a letter fallback. Names are body strong; domain and times are muted captions; scopes are captions with a check mark. Verified is a success badge with a check mark, Suspended a warning badge. Remove access is a small danger MonarchButton. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The confirmation is the system alert with a destructive button instead of the web's ConfirmDialog. The web's SectionCard is MonarchSectionHeader with a bordered surface. The web passes the id to onRevoke; iOS passes the whole app value. The logo is a URL only (no local Image), because the app value is Sendable data. The web's headingLevel has no equivalent: the title has the header trait. The web's danger-subtle button variant does not exist on iOS; the danger variant is used. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onRevoke). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title is a header, from MonarchSectionHeader.
Each app's name, badges, domain, times and workspace are one element: the name as its label and the rest as its value.
Each scope list is a group named "What Notes can access".
The logo is decorative.
Remove access is a standard button named "Remove access for Notes" with a 44-point touch target; the confirmation is a system alert.
Removal and failures are announced; a failure is also shown with an icon and text.
Badges are words, so the verified and suspended states do not depend on colour.
edgeCases: A logo that fails to load shows the first letter of the name.
An app with no dates, domain or scopes shows only its name and badges.
Two removals can run at once; each row tracks its own progress.
Long names wrap; badges move to the next line.

states.name: records
states.description: One bordered record per decision on the surface colour.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState with a shield symbol, and no download button.

states.name: exporting
states.description: The download button shows its spinner and ignores further taps.

states.name: export failed
states.description: An icon and "The download did not start. Try again." in the strong danger colour under the header, announced; the button can be used again.

appearance: Records use the surface colour, a subtle border and 12-point corners. Dates use the strong body style; line names the caption style in the muted colour; values the body style. Allowed categories have a filled check in the strong success colour, refused ones an empty cross in the muted colour, each followed by the words. All are theme roles.
platformNotes: The web shows a table on wide containers and stacked cards below 640 points; iOS always shows the stacked records, which suit a phone and large text. The web's ConsentRecord stores the date as an ISO string; on iOS it is a Date. The web's locale and timeZone props are replaced by dateFormat; now is not needed because relative times come from the system clock. headingLevel has no iOS equivalent (the title is a header). The record types are defined here because the consent manager is not built on iOS; a later consent preferences sheet should use them. Android builds the same component. The parity map lists badge as a dependency; the method is plain text, as on the web, so no badge is used.
accessibility: The title and each decision's date have the header trait, so the headings rotor moves between decisions.
Each line is one element read as its name, value and any note ("Choice, Custom choice, Browser privacy signal present").
Each category is one element read as its name and "Allowed" or "Not allowed"; the label is built by a tested pure function and the icon and colour are not the only signal.
The download button is a MonarchButton with a 44-point touch target and a busy state while exporting.
The export failure is posted as an announcement.
edgeCases: Records with the same date keep the order they were given in.
A record with no categories shows no categories list.
The relative time is static text refreshed every minute, not a ticking clock.
Long policy versions and category names wrap.

title: ConsentManager
wrapsNative: AppTrackingTransparency: ATTrackingManager.requestTrackingAuthorization() and ATTrackingManager.trackingAuthorizationStatus
summary: On iOS, consent to track across other companies' apps and websites is Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt, and the app keeps its own in-app consent state; Monarch ships no consent manager. The in-app choices are shown with MonarchConsentPreferences.
whenToUse: Call requestTrackingAuthorization() before any SDK reads the advertising identifier or links the person's data with other companies' data, at a moment the person understands why, and read trackingAuthorizationStatus before starting such an SDK. Use MonarchConsentPreferences for analytics and preferences that stay inside the app.
whenNotToUse: Do not build a custom pre-prompt that imitates the system alert, and do not ask again after the person answered: the system shows the prompt once. Do not use ATT for in-app analytics that are not tracking in Apple's sense; that is the app's own consent with MonarchConsentPreferences.
api: class func requestTrackingAuthorization() async -> ATTrackingManager.AuthorizationStatus
class var trackingAuthorizationStatus: ATTrackingManager.AuthorizationStatus { get }
enum ATTrackingManager.AuthorizationStatus { case notDetermined, restricted, denied, authorized }

states.name: not determined
states.description: The person has not been asked; requesting shows the system alert with the app's NSUserTrackingUsageDescription text.

states.name: authorized
states.description: Tracking across apps is allowed; the advertising identifier is available.

states.name: denied
states.description: The person said no, or turned tracking off in Settings; the identifier is zeros and the prompt does not show again.

states.name: restricted
states.description: Tracking is not allowed on this device, for example by a profile; the prompt does not show.

appearance: The prompt is a system alert in every theme. The app's explanation before it and its in-app choices use Monarch components.
platformNotes: The web's ConsentManager is a provider that decides the regime (opt-in, opt-out or notice) from the visitor's jurisdiction, honours Global Privacy Control, records each decision and feeds the cookie banner, preferences dialog and ConsentGate. On iOS, tracking across apps is governed by App Tracking Transparency in every country, so the system prompt replaces the regime logic for that purpose, and an app may not track without it. Consent for in-app analytics and preferences is app state: store it where the app keeps settings, show and change it with MonarchConsentPreferences, list decisions with MonarchConsentHistory, and gate SDKs in the app's own code. The request needs the NSUserTrackingUsageDescription key in Info.plist and an active app; call it after launch, not during it. Android has no equivalent system prompt; its plan composes the consent preferences.
accessibility: System behaviour: the tracking alert is read by VoiceOver with the app's usage description and its two buttons.
Monarch components around it keep their own behaviour: MonarchButton reports its title and state, MonarchConsentPreferences its switches.
edgeCases: trackingAuthorizationStatus can change while the app runs, when the person changes Settings; read it again when the app becomes active.
On a device where tracking is restricted, the request returns at once without a prompt.
The request requires the NSUserTrackingUsageDescription key in Info.plist; the catalogue page checks for the key before asking.

name: MonarchConsentPreferences
title: ConsentPreferences
wrapsNative: VStack for a sheet(isPresented:content:): a Toggle per category, Link to the policy, MonarchButtons
summary: Privacy choices for a sheet: one switch per category of optional storage or processing, with Reject all, Accept all and Save choices, the saved policy version and time, and Withdraw consent.
whenToUse: When an app asks for or lets people change consent to optional data uses such as analytics or advertising, opened from a first-run prompt or a Privacy setting.
whenNotToUse: Not for the system's App Tracking Transparency prompt, which iOS shows itself (ask with ATTrackingManager), not for marketing messages (use MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox) and not for the list of past decisions (use MonarchConsentHistory).
api: init(categories: [MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory], choices: [String: Bool] = [:], mode: MonarchConsentPreferencesMode = .categories, isGlobalPrivacyControl: Bool = false, record: MonarchConsentRecord? = nil, policyURL: URL? = nil, allowsWithdraw: Bool = true, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels = MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels(), onDecide: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchConsentMethod, [String: Bool]) -> Void)
struct MonarchConsentPreferencesCategory: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String, description: String, isRequired: Bool = false, isSaleOrSharing: Bool = false) }
enum MonarchConsentPreferencesMode { case categories, choice }
struct MonarchConsentPreferencesLabels { init(title:description:policy:alwaysOn:globalPrivacyControl:on:off:rejectAll:acceptAll:save:withdraw:policyVersion:saved:), every parameter optional }

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in order, each with a name, a description, and whether it is strictly necessary or sells or shares data.

options.name: choices
options.description: The saved choice by category id. Leave it empty until the person has chosen, so nothing optional is on.

options.name: mode
options.description: categories: a switch per category and Save choices. choice: the status of each category and only Reject all and Accept all.

options.name: isGlobalPrivacyControl
options.description: Whether a Global Privacy Control signal is on. Sale-or-sharing categories stay off with a note.

options.name: record
options.description: The saved decision: shows "Policy version 3 · Saved 2 days ago" and allows Withdraw consent.

options.name: policyURL
options.description: Adds a "Privacy policy" link under the description.

options.name: allowsWithdraw
options.description: Whether Withdraw consent is offered in categories mode when a decision is saved and not already withdrawn.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for the saved time. The current time by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, to translate or to use the legal team's wording.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Runs when a button is pressed with acceptAll, rejectAll, custom or withdrawn and every category's state, locks applied. Store the record and close the sheet here.

states.name: first time
states.description: Every optional switch is off; required ones are on, disabled and say "Always on".

states.name: saved
states.description: Switches show the saved choice; the record line and Withdraw consent appear.

states.name: Global Privacy Control
states.description: Sale-or-sharing switches are off and disabled, with a note saying why.

states.name: choice mode
states.description: Each category shows On (success strong), Off or Always on as a word; only Reject all and Accept all are offered.

appearance: A title, a muted description and an underlined policy link, then the categories separated by subtle dividers with switches tinted in the accent solid role. Reject all and Accept all are equal secondary buttons, side by side when they fit; Save choices is a full-width primary button and Withdraw consent a ghost button. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web dialog reads and writes a ConsentProvider; on iOS the app passes the categories, saved choices and record and stores the decision from onDecide, because consent storage is the app's. The component is the content of a sheet the app presents and closes, rather than a dialog with its own open state. The web's policyLink slot is policyURL. The record type is the shared MonarchConsentRecord and the method is MonarchConsentMethod, as in MonarchConsentHistory. A Global Privacy Control signal is a browser feature; on iOS the app passes it if it honours an equivalent setting. Apple's App Tracking Transparency prompt is separate and still required for tracking across apps.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Each category is a standard Toggle whose label includes its name, description and any note, so VoiceOver says why a locked switch cannot change.
Locked switches are disabled standard switches.
In choice mode each category is one element with its name as the label, its status word as the value and its description as the hint.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets; Reject all and Accept all stack vertically when they do not fit side by side.
edgeCases: Required categories are reported on and GPC-locked ones off whatever the person chose.
A saved decision older than seven days shows its date instead of a relative time.
Every decision reports every category, including ones missing from choices.

name: MonarchConsequenceList
title: ConsequenceList
wrapsNative: VStack, ForEach, Text; .redacted(reason: .placeholder) while loading
summary: A list of what an action deletes, changes and keeps, to read before confirming.
whenToUse: In a confirmation sheet or dialog for a destructive or far-reaching action, above the confirm button.
whenNotToUse: For a single sentence of consequence, write it in the dialog message. For a status after the action, use MonarchBanner.
api: init(_ items: [MonarchConsequence], heading: String? = nil, isGrouped: Bool = false, isLoading: Bool = false, loadingRowCount: Int = 3, loadingLabel: String? = nil, kindLabel: (@Sendable (MonarchConsequenceKind) -> String)? = nil, groupTitle: (@Sendable (MonarchConsequenceKind) -> String)? = nil)
struct MonarchConsequence { init(_ kind: MonarchConsequenceKind, _ label: String, detail: String? = nil, count: Int? = nil, id: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchConsequenceKind { case removed, changed, warning, kept }

options.name: items
options.description: The consequences, in reading order.

options.name: heading
options.description: A heading above the list.

options.name: isGrouped
options.description: Splits the items by kind under headings, in the order deleted, changed, warnings, kept.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows placeholder rows instead of the items.

options.name: loadingRowCount
options.description: The number of placeholder rows. At least 1.

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Checking what will change" spoken text.

options.name: kindLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of each kind.

options.name: groupTitle
options.description: Replaces the built-in heading of each group.

states.name: ungrouped
states.description: Rows in the given order; VoiceOver reads the kind before each row.

states.name: grouped
states.description: One block per kind that has items, each under its heading.

states.name: loading
states.description: Placeholder rows drawn by the system redaction, read as one element.

appearance: Each row has an icon in the strong colour of its kind (danger for removed, info for changed, warning, success for kept), the text in the default text colour and the detail in the muted text colour. Group headings are muted label text.
platformNotes: The web error slot is not offered: when the consequences cannot be worked out, show MonarchInlineErrorRetry in place of the list. The loading rows are the system placeholder redaction and do not shimmer. The count is formatted for the environment's locale; there is no locale parameter. label and detail are Strings where the web takes any content. The heading level option has no equivalent: headings have the header trait. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (kindLabel, groupTitle). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is kindLabel.
accessibility: Each row is one element. Ungrouped, it is read as the kind name, a colon, the count and label, then the detail.
Grouped, the kind name is left out of the row, because the group heading, which has the header trait, says it.
Each kind has its own icon shape, so the kind does not depend on colour. The icons are hidden from VoiceOver.
While loading, the rows are one element read as "Checking what will change". Nothing is announced when loading starts or ends.
edgeCases: Two items with the same kind and label need explicit ids.
A count of 0 is shown as 0.
A kind with no items has no group heading.
An empty list shows only the heading, if there is one.

title: Container
wrapsNative: frame(maxWidth:) centred with a second frame(maxWidth: .infinity), padding(.horizontal, _:) by horizontalSizeClass, and containerRelativeFrame(_:count:span:spacing:alignment:)
summary: Centring page content at a maximum width with side gutters is a pair of frame modifiers and horizontal padding. Monarch ships nothing and documents the widths and gutters.
whenToUse: On screens that can be wide (iPad, landscape) to stop text and forms from stretching: cap the width at 704 points for reading and forms, 1152 for app pages or 1280 for dashboards, and pad by 16 points in a compact width and 24 in a regular width. Use containerRelativeFrame to size a view as a part of its container.
whenNotToUse: Inside List, Form and NavigationStack the system already applies margins and readable widths; do not add another container there.
api: func frame(minWidth: CGFloat? = nil, idealWidth: CGFloat? = nil, maxWidth: CGFloat? = nil, minHeight: CGFloat? = nil, idealHeight: CGFloat? = nil, maxHeight: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment = .center) -> some View
func containerRelativeFrame(_ axes: Axis.Set, count: Int, span: Int = 1, spacing: CGFloat, alignment: Alignment = .center) -> some View
@Environment(\.horizontalSizeClass) var horizontalSizeClass

states.name: compact width
states.description: 16-point gutters (theme.spacing.space4). The content fills the width.

states.name: regular width
states.description: 24-point gutters (theme.spacing.space6). The content stops at the maximum width and is centred.

appearance: Layout only; nothing is drawn.
platformNotes: The web's Container has sizes narrow (44rem, 704 points), content (72rem, 1152), wide (80rem, 1280) and full, and gutters of 16px that become 24px from 768px. The native tokens carry no width tokens, so the numbers are written in the app; the gutters are steps of the space scale, and the size class replaces the 768px breakpoint. Android uses widthIn(max:) and window size classes in the same way.
accessibility: Layout only: no element is added and the reading order does not change.
Leading and trailing padding follow the layout direction.
A capped width keeps lines readable on wide screens; at large Dynamic Type sizes the content still fills a compact width.
edgeCases: The maximum width here includes the gutters, as on the web, because the padding is applied before the frame.
containerRelativeFrame measures the nearest container: a ScrollView, a column of a split view or the window.
On macOS the size class is always regular.

title: ContextMenu
wrapsNative: contextMenu(menuItems:), and contextMenu(menuItems:preview:) for a custom preview
summary: The standard context menu, opened by touching and holding a view, or by a secondary click with a pointer. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To offer shortcuts to the actions of an item: a row, a file, a message. Every action in the menu must also be reachable another way, such as a menu button, swipe actions or the detail screen.
whenNotToUse: Do not make a context menu the only way to an action; the gesture is hidden. For a visible button that opens a menu use Menu.
api: func contextMenu(menuItems: () -> some View) -> some View
func contextMenu(menuItems: () -> some View, preview: () -> some View) -> some View
func contentShape(_ kind: ContentShapeKinds, _ shape: some Shape) -> some View

states.name: open
states.description: The view lifts as a preview, the screen behind is blurred, and the menu appears beside it.

states.name: destructive item
states.description: A button with the destructive role is drawn in red.

appearance: The system draws the menu and the lifted preview in every theme. Set contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, …) to the view's own rounded shape so the preview has the right corners.
platformNotes: The web ContextMenu opens on right-click, Shift F10 or a long press and is composed of Monarch-styled items, checkboxes, radio groups and submenus. On iOS the menu is the system's: items are Button, Toggle, Picker and nested Menu, with Divider and Section for groups, and none of them is styled. The web's label and modal props have no equivalent. Android uses a DropdownMenu opened from a long press.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver offers the context menu through the Actions rotor and by a double tap and hold.
System behaviour: the menu is modal; focus moves into it and returns to the view when it closes.
Because the gesture is not discoverable, give the same actions a visible control, for example a Menu with an ellipsis icon that has a label.
edgeCases: An empty menu builder disables the context menu.
On a view inside a Button or a NavigationLink the long press wins over the tap only after the hold.
Items cannot show a custom view; only a title, an image and a role.
contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, …) is not available on macOS, where the examples are also compiled, so the compiled example leaves it out. The catalogue page uses it.

name: MonarchCookieConsentBanner
title: CookieConsentBanner

summary: The cookie or tracking notice of an app that shows web content or measures use: a card at the bottom of the screen with the regime's message, a link to the policy and equal choices.
whenToUse: On first run of an app that sets optional cookies in its web views or measures use, where the law asks for consent or a notice.
whenNotToUse: For the full per-category choices, use MonarchConsentPreferences in a sheet (the banner's Customize opens it). Tracking across other companies' apps and websites needs the system's App Tracking Transparency prompt, which this banner does not replace.

options.name: policyURL
options.description: The cookie policy, linked at the end of the message as "Cookie policy".

options.name: isGlobalPrivacyControl
options.description: In the opt-out regime, replaces the opt-out button with a line saying the signal was honoured.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in title, message, buttons, link and announcement.

options.name: onCustomize
options.description: Opens the per-category choices; without it Customize is not shown.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Records the choice; the app stores it and stops showing the banner.

states.name: opt-in
states.description: Customize (ghost), then Reject all and Accept all as equal secondary buttons.

states.name: opt-out

states.name: opt-out with Global Privacy Control

states.name: notice
states.description: The notice message and OK.

appearance: A raised card with a large shadow and the subtle border; the title is bold body text, the message the muted text colour, the policy link the link colour, underlined. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web banner reads the visitor's regime and stored choice from ConsentProvider and opens ConsentPreferences itself. On iOS the app passes the regime, stores the choice from onDecide and presents MonarchConsentPreferences from onCustomize; there is no corner-card position, since the card spans the bottom of the screen. Android does not ship this component.
accessibility: The card is a container named by its title, which has the header trait.
VoiceOver announces "Cookie notice shown at the bottom of the screen." when it appears, without moving focus.
The policy link is a link inside the message.
Each choice is its own button; rejecting is as prominent as accepting.

resetAfter of zero keeps the copied state until the view is recreated.

The value is written to the general pasteboard as plain text and replaces what was there.

name: MonarchCurrencySelect
title: CurrencySelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox (a .sheet with a List and .searchable) over the active ISO 4217 codes, with names from Locale.localizedString(forCurrencyCode:) and narrow symbols from Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency with .presentation(.narrow)
summary: A searchable picker for an ISO 4217 currency, with names and symbols in the reader's language.
whenToUse: For a billing, payout or display currency, where the list is long and people search by name, code or symbol.
whenNotToUse: Not for entering an amount; use MonarchCurrencyInput. For two or three currencies, use a Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) or .menu.
api: init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<String?>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, currencies: [String]? = nil, priority: [String] = [], locale: Locale? = nil, display: MonarchCurrencySelectDisplay = .name, showsSymbol: Bool = true, isRequired: Bool = false, isClearable: Bool = true, labels: MonarchCurrencySelectLabels = MonarchCurrencySelectLabels())
static var currencyCodes: [String]
enum MonarchCurrencySelectDisplay { case name, code, codeAndName }
struct MonarchCurrencySelectLabels { init(suggested: String? = nil, all: String? = nil, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen ISO 4217 code. Any case is read; the picker writes upper case.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in the field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the field.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown with an icon and announced.

options.name: currencies
options.description: Limits the list to these codes, such as what a payment provider supports. nil lists currencyCodes.

options.name: priority
options.description: Codes listed first under Suggested while nothing is typed.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of names and symbols and the sort order. The environment's locale when nil.

options.name: display
options.description: What the field and each row's label show: the name (Euro), the code (EUR) or both (EUR · Euro). With a code, the name is the row's description.

options.name: showsSymbol
options.description: Shows the symbol after the code at the end of each row, when it differs from the code.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds Required to the hint.

options.name: isClearable
options.description: Shows a clear button in the field while a currency is chosen.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces Suggested, All currencies and the combobox strings; the combobox's empty text is built in as No currencies match.

states.name: empty
states.description: The field shows the prompt in the subtle text colour.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The field shows the currency's label in the chosen display and a clear button when clearing is on.

states.name: suggestions
states.description: With priority and nothing typed, the list has a Suggested section and a section with the rest.

states.name: searching
states.description: The suggestions are hidden; matches are listed with labels that start with the query first.

states.name: no match
states.description: The list reads No currencies match.

states.name: error
states.description: The field border and message use the danger colour, with an icon; the error is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Label, value and border use the disabled roles; the sheet does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's: the input background and border (danger with an error) and the default text colour. In the list, the code and symbol are a muted caption at the end of each row and the chosen row has an accent check mark. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Names come from Foundation and symbols from its currency format, so wording can differ from the web's Intl and from Android. The code list is bundled (the same active currencies as the web) instead of Locale.Currency.isoCurrencies, which also lists funds, metals, test codes and retired currencies. The web's display values name, code and code-name are .name, .code and .codeAndName. The list opens in a sheet, as every MonarchCombobox does.
accessibility: The field is a button labelled with the label, whose value is the chosen row's label or None.
The help text, the error (read as Error: ...) and Required are the field's hint; a new error is announced.
The chosen row has the selected trait and a check mark, not colour alone.
Rows and the field are at least 44 points high.
Each row is read with its label, the name when the label is a code, then the code and the symbol.
edgeCases: A selection that is not in currencies is still listed first, so its name shows in the field.
A currency whose symbol is its code shows the code once.
Search finds a currency by symbol ($ finds every dollar) and, in other languages, by its English name.
Symbols depend on the locale: the narrow symbol of CAD is $ in English.

name: MonarchCursorList
title: CursorList
wrapsNative: List with .listStyle(.plain) and a MonarchLoadMore footer row; MonarchErrorState, MonarchLoadingState and MonarchEmptyState for the first-load states; accessibilityFocused(_:equals:) for the first new item
summary: A list loaded page by page from a cursor: the items, a load-more footer with a count, and the first-load, empty and error states.
whenToUse: For a screen or tab whose content is a long list fetched in pages from an API cursor (requests, activity, messages), when the app keeps the cursor in its model.
whenNotToUse: For a list loaded whole, use a List. For rows with several columns, use MonarchDataTable with a MonarchLoadMore footer. Inside another scroll view, use MonarchLoadMore under a LazyVStack instead, because a List does not size to its content.
api: init(_ items: [Item], label: String, hasMore: Bool, isLoading: Bool = false, isFailed: Bool = false, totalCount: Int? = nil, autoLoads: Bool = false, showsEnd: Bool = true, isDivided: Bool = true, focusesNewItems: Bool = true, loadingVariant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = .list, labels: MonarchCursorListLabels = MonarchCursorListLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onLoadMore: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void, @ViewBuilder row: @escaping (Item) -> Row) where Item: Identifiable
struct MonarchCursorListLabels { var loading, emptyTitle, emptyMessage, errorTitle, retry: String?; var footer: MonarchLoadMoreLabels }

options.name: items
options.description: Every item loaded so far, in order.

options.name: label
options.description: Names the list for VoiceOver.

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Whether there is another page. With no items and no more, shows the empty state.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: A page is being fetched. With no items, shows the loading state; otherwise the footer button shows progress.

options.name: isFailed
options.description: The last fetch failed. With no items, shows the error state; otherwise the footer shows the failure with retry.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The total, when the server knows it, for "Showing 20 of 140 items".

options.name: autoLoads
options.description: Loads the next page when the footer scrolls into view; the button stays as the fallback.

options.name: showsEnd
options.description: Whether "That's everything" is shown after the last page.

options.name: isDivided
options.description: Whether rows are separated by the list's lines.

options.name: focusesNewItems
options.description: Moves VoiceOver focus to the first item of a page asked for from the footer.

options.name: loadingVariant
options.description: The shape of the first-page placeholder.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the footer's.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats the failed request. By default onLoadMore.

options.name: onLoadMore
options.description: Loads the next page.

options.name: row
options.description: Draws one item.

states.name: ready
states.description: The items and the footer: a Load more button with the count, or the end line.

states.name: loading more
states.description: The footer button shows progress.

states.name: failed later
states.description: The footer shows "Couldn't load more." with Retry; the items stay.

states.name: first page loading
states.description: A MonarchLoadingState placeholder named "Loading".

states.name: first page failed
states.description: A MonarchErrorState, "This list could not be loaded", with Retry; while the retry runs the button is busy.

states.name: empty
states.description: A MonarchEmptyState, "Nothing here yet" with a message.

appearance: A plain list with a hidden background, so it sits on the screen's background; separators are the system's. The footer count and end line are caption text in the muted role; the states use their components' roles. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web CursorList chooses ul or ol and takes an item class; on iOS it is a List and the row closure draws each item. The web moves keyboard focus to the first new item after a page asked for by keyboard; on iOS VoiceOver focus moves to it after a page asked for from the footer. The web replaces the empty state with any node; on iOS the empty title and message are labels. The web count noun is built into its messages; on iOS pass labels.footer.count and labels.footer.loaded. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The list is named by label.
The footer is a MonarchLoadMore: its button is a standard button with a 44-point touch target, and new items, a failure and the end are announced.
After a page asked for from the footer arrives, VoiceOver focus moves to its first item.
The first-load placeholder, error and empty states are the shared Monarch states with their own labels.
edgeCases: With no items but more to load and no fetch running, the list shows only the footer, so the first page can be asked for.
A failure with items keeps them and shows the footer failure, not the error state.
A page that brings no new items moves no focus.
The list fills the space it is given; give it a frame when it sits in a stack.

title: CustomDomainConnect
wrapsNative: VStack (or a Form) of MonarchTextField, MonarchDomainProgress, MonarchDnsRecordTable and MonarchButton, with confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:) for removal
summary: A recipe, not a component: connect a custom domain by entering it, copying the DNS records, verifying, and following its progress to live, with removal behind a confirmation.
whenToUse: On the domain settings screen of a product that serves pages, booking sites or help centres on the customer's own domain.
whenNotToUse: For showing only the state of a domain that is already set up, use MonarchDomainProgress alone; for DNS records with no connection flow, use MonarchDnsRecordTable.
api: MonarchTextField.init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, isSecure: Bool = false)

MonarchDomainProgress.init(_ host: String, stage: MonarchDomainStage, problems: [MonarchDomainProblem] = [], dnsFound: MonarchDomainDnsSnapshot? = nil, checkedAt: Date? = nil, now: Date? = nil, isRechecking: Bool = true, notify: MonarchDomainNotify? = nil, labels: MonarchDomainProgressLabels = MonarchDomainProgressLabels())

MonarchDnsRecordTable.init(_ records: [MonarchDnsRecord], zone: String? = nil, layout: MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout = .automatic, labels: MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels = MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchButton.init(_ title: String, systemImage: String? = nil, trailingSystemImage: String? = nil, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, isLoading: Bool = false, loadingLabel: String? = nil, fullWidth: Bool = false, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)

func confirmationDialog<A: View, M: View>(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility = .automatic, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> A, @ViewBuilder message: () -> M) -> some View

states.name: enter
states.description: A Domain field with an example prompt and help; Connect domain is disabled until the text looks like a host, and a URL or a path shows the error under the field.

states.name: records
states.description: After connecting: MonarchDomainProgress at the DNS step, the records as cards with copy buttons, Verify DNS and Remove domain.

states.name: verifying
states.description: The app checks DNS and moves the stage (dns, ownership, certificate, page, live); records show Found or Waiting from isFound.

states.name: live
states.description: MonarchDomainProgress shows every step done; Verify DNS is disabled.

states.name: remove
states.description: A confirmation dialog with the domain in its title and a destructive Remove domain.

appearance: Every part keeps its Monarch styling: the field and buttons as elsewhere, the progress steps with tone icons and words, the records as cards on the surface colour. The confirmation dialog is the system's.
platformNotes: The web ships CustomDomainConnect as one pattern with domain normalisation (punycode, scheme and path stripping), a four-step stepper, a provider picker with product-written instructions, async onConnect, onVerify and onRemove, and its own messages. On iOS it is a recipe so the product keeps its own networking and copy: the app normalises the host (URLComponents can strip a pasted scheme and path), calls its API, and sets the stage and each record's isFound from its checks. MonarchDomainProgress replaces the web stepper and status badge. A provider picker is a Picker with .menu style above the records. Removal uses confirmationDialog, the iOS pattern for a destructive choice. Marked experimental because it is a product flow, not a primitive, until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The Domain field reads its label, value, help and error; the error has an icon and text.
The DNS records heading has the header trait; each record value and name is read with its copy button, as MonarchDnsRecordTable does.
MonarchDomainProgress reads each step with its state and announces when a step completes.
The disabled Connect domain and Verify DNS buttons are read as dimmed.
The removal dialog is the system dialog, with the destructive action announced as such.
edgeCases: People paste full URLs: strip the scheme, path and port before validating, or show the error as the recipe does.
DNS changes can take hours: keep the records visible while the stage is dns, and recheck on a timer with MonarchDomainProgress.recheckInterval(for:).
Several domains on one screen: give each its own section and include the host in the removal title.

examples.title: Full flow (simulated checks)
A connected domain
examples.code: MonarchDomainProgress("help.example.com", stage: .live, isRechecking: false)

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws the four steps as a row with each name beside its circle, which needs about 420 points; a phone column has 306, so each name sits under its circle (the stepper's stacked row) and the compact form takes over at larger text sizes.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: a phone layout stacks a label under its control rather than shrinking it

title: DangerZone
wrapsNative: Form Section(content:header:footer:) with Button(_:role: .destructive) rows, each confirmed with confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:); MonarchSectionCard(tone: .danger) with danger MonarchButtons and alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) on a scrolling page
summary: A recipe, not a component: the last settings section, holding irreversible actions (delete a workspace, transfer ownership, leave), with one row per action, its consequence, and a confirmation before each.
whenToUse: At the end of a settings screen, for actions that cannot be undone or that hand the workspace or account to someone else.
whenNotToUse: For a single destructive action next to the thing it affects, use a danger MonarchButton with a confirmation (confirm-dialog). For ordinary settings, use the settings-section recipe.
api: Section { Button("Delete workspace", role: .destructive) { isConfirming = true } } header: { Text("Danger zone") } footer: { Text(consequence) }
.confirmationDialog("Delete this workspace?", isPresented: $isConfirming, titleVisibility: .visible) { Button("Delete workspace", role: .destructive) { … } } message: { Text(…) }

MonarchSectionCard("Danger zone", description: …, tone: .danger) { VStack { Text(title).monarchTextStyle(.bodyStrong); Text(consequence).monarchTextStyle(.caption); MonarchButton(…, variant: .danger, size: .sm) { … } } }
.alert(title, isPresented: …, actions: { Button(…, role: .destructive) { … }; Button("Cancel", role: .cancel) {} }, message: { Text(…) })

options.name: heading
options.description: The section header, or the MonarchSectionCard title, whose danger tone is spoken with it.

options.name: consequence
options.description: One or two sentences saying what the action does and that it cannot be undone: the section footer, or a caption in the card.

options.name: disabled reason
options.description: Why an action is unavailable: the footer says so and the button is disabled.

states.name: ready
states.description: Each action is a destructive button row with its consequence under it.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: The button is disabled and the footer or caption says why.

states.name: confirming
states.description: The button opens a confirmation dialog (an action sheet on iPhone) or an alert, whose destructive button repeats the action.

states.name: done
states.description: The app reflects the result, usually by leaving the screen.

appearance: In a Form, the system's destructive button text colour on the grouped row background, and the system footer style. In the card form, MonarchSectionCard with the danger tone's border and icon, strong body titles, muted captions and small danger buttons. Both follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships DangerZone and DangerZoneItem with heading levels and a layout that places the action beside the text. On iOS, as in the Settings app, each destructive action is its own Form section with a destructive button and the consequence in the footer, so the recipe needs no Monarch type; Android also keeps it a recipe. Confirmation is the system confirmationDialog, which iOS shows as an action sheet, or an alert for a single question, as in the confirm-dialog entry. On a scrolling page the web's card is MonarchSectionCard with the danger tone, and the action sits under the text so long titles and large text never squeeze it. VoiceOver has no heading levels to set beyond the header trait.
accessibility: Form section headers are read as headings, and each footer is read after its button, so the consequence follows the action.
Destructive buttons have the destructive role, and VoiceOver focuses the confirmation when it opens.
In the card form the danger tone is spoken with the title by MonarchSectionCard, and item titles have the header trait.
The reason an action is unavailable is visible text, not only a dimmed button.
edgeCases: Put the danger zone last on the settings screen.
Keep each consequence to one or two sentences; longer text wraps.
For the most destructive actions, ask for a typed phrase in the alert (see confirm-dialog).

name: MonarchDashboardGrid
title: DashboardGrid
wrapsNative: VStack of HStack rows sized from onGeometryChange (widgets spanning columns); draggable(_:) and dropDestination(for:action:isTargeted:) in edit mode; Button with .buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost, size: .sm)) for Move earlier and Move later
summary: The responsive grid a dashboard's widgets sit in: one column on phones, more on wide screens, widgets spanning columns, and an edit mode in which people rearrange widgets by dragging or with buttons.
whenToUse: On a home or dashboard screen made of several independent MonarchWidgets, especially when each person should be able to put the widgets they use most first.
whenNotToUse: For equal tiles without spans or stored layouts, use MonarchSortableGrid. For a single list of sections, use a VStack. For many items of the same kind, use a LazyVGrid.
api: init(_ items: [Item], layout: Binding<[Item.ID]>, itemLabel: KeyPath<Item, String>, span: ((Item) -> MonarchDashboardGridSpan)? = nil, columns: Int = 3, isEditing: Bool = false, labels: MonarchDashboardGridLabels = MonarchDashboardGridLabels(), onLayoutChange: (@MainActor (_ from: Int, _ to: Int) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: @escaping (Item) -> Content) where Item: Identifiable
enum MonarchDashboardGridSpan { case columns(Int), full; static let one, two }
struct MonarchDashboardGridLabels { var label, dragHint: String?; var moveEarlier, moveLater: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var moved, dropped: (@Sendable (String, Int, Int) -> String)? }

options.name: items
options.description: The widgets in their default order.

options.name: layout
options.description: The order of ids stored for this person; empty for the default order. Unknown ids are skipped and new items appended; the grid writes the new order after each move.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: A widget's plain-text name, for the arrange bar, the button labels and the announcements.

options.name: span
options.description: The columns a widget spans on wide screens, clamped to the columns available. One by default.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns from 1024 points of grid width, 1 to 4. From 640 points the grid has at most two, below it one.

options.name: isEditing
options.description: Shows an arrange bar on each widget with Move earlier and Move later, and makes the bars draggable.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onLayoutChange
options.description: Called after each finished move with the old and new index, for example to save the layout.

options.name: content
options.description: Draws a widget, usually a MonarchWidget.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The widgets in rows; one column on phones.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each widget has an arrange bar in the subtle background: a grip, its name, and Move earlier and Move later buttons, disabled at the ends.

states.name: drop target
states.description: While a bar is dragged over a widget, that widget has an accent outline.

appearance: Widgets sit with a 16-point gap. The arrange bar uses the subtle background role with muted text and grip; the move buttons are small ghost MonarchButtons; the drop outline uses the accent strong role at twice the hairline. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web grid is a CSS grid with column spans; SwiftUI's LazyVGrid has no spans, so the iOS grid packs widgets into rows and sizes them from the measured width (it is not lazy; a dashboard has a few widgets). The web picks up a widget with Space and moves it with the arrow keys; on iOS the Move earlier and Move later buttons are the single-tap equivalent for touch, VoiceOver, Switch Control and keyboards, and dragging uses the system drag and drop. The web takes uncontrolled defaultLayout; on iOS the layout is a binding. The web widths are in rem of grid width (40rem, 64rem); iOS uses the 640 and 1024 point breakpoints. Android uses the same name and options. Several closures are optional (span, onLayoutChange). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is span.
accessibility: The grid is a container named "Dashboard".
In edit mode the bar reads the widget's name with the hint "Touch and hold, then drag to move."; its grip is hidden.
Move earlier and Move later are named with the widget ("Move Team load earlier"), have 44-point touch targets and are disabled at the ends.
Every move and drop is announced ("Team load moved to position 2 of 6.").
At the accessibility text sizes the grid has one column.
Moves animate with the motion tokens and are instant with Reduce Motion.
edgeCases: A stored layout with ids of removed widgets skips them; new widgets follow in their default order.
A widget whose span does not fit in what is left of a row starts the next row, leaving a gap.
In one column, spans have no effect and the move buttons point up and down; in several they point backward and forward and mirror right to left.
Drops from another grid or another app are ignored.

examples.code:
ScrollView {
    VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: theme.spacing.space4) {

            "Period",

            items: [

                MonarchSegmentedItem("Last 30 days", value: "Last 30 days"),
                MonarchSegmentedItem("This quarter", value: "This quarter"),

                MonarchStatCard("Assigned to you", value: 12.0).id("assigned")
                MonarchStatCard("Due this week", value: 4.0).id("due")

                    value: 27.0,
                    change: MonarchMetricChange(0.17, comparison: "vs last month")
                )
                .id("done")
        }
        MonarchInsightStrip(
            "Insights",

title: DataExportRequest
wrapsNative: MonarchCard with a MonarchBadge status, ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear), MonarchCheckboxGroup, Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) in a MonarchFormField, MonarchBanner and MonarchButton; Date.FormatStyle for dates; openURL for the download
summary: A Download your data card: choose what to include and the format, request an export, follow its status, and download the file until it expires.
whenToUse: On an account's privacy or data settings screen, where people request a copy of their data that the app builds in the background.
whenNotToUse: Not for exporting what is on screen right now (a report or a table); use ShareLink or a fileExporter. Not for deleting an account.
api: init(status: MonarchDataExportStatus = .idle, requestedAt: Date? = nil, readyAt: Date? = nil, expiresAt: Date? = nil, scope: [MonarchCheckboxGroupOption] = [], formats: [MonarchDataExportFormat] = [], defaultFormat: String? = nil, preparationNote: String? = nil, failureReason: String? = nil, downloadURL: URL? = nil, isRequesting: Bool = false, labels: MonarchDataExportRequestLabels = MonarchDataExportRequestLabels(), onDownload: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRequest: (@MainActor (MonarchDataExportRequestDetails) async throws -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchDataExportStatus: String, CaseIterable { case idle, requested, preparing, ready, expired, failed }
struct MonarchDataExportFormat: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String) }
struct MonarchDataExportRequestDetails { let scope: [String]; let format: String?; init(scope: [String], format: String?) }

struct MonarchDataExportRequestLabels { init(title:description:statuses:request:requestAgain:download:scopeLegend:scopeRequired:formatLabel:requested:preparing:preparingProgress:ready:expired:failed:requestFailed:), every parameter optional }

options.name: status
options.description: Where the export is, as the app reports it.

options.name: requestedAt
options.description: When the export was requested; named in the requested and preparing lines.

options.name: readyAt
options.description: When the file became ready; named in the ready line.

options.name: expiresAt
options.description: When the download stops working; named in the ready and expired lines.

options.name: scope
options.description: Kinds of data to choose from, all checked at first. No checklist when empty.

options.name: formats
options.description: File formats for a menu. No menu when empty.

options.name: defaultFormat
options.description: The id of the format chosen at first. The first format when nil.

options.name: preparationNote
options.description: How long preparing takes and how the person hears about it. Shown while idle, requested and preparing.

options.name: failureReason
options.description: Extra detail under the status line when failed.

options.name: downloadURL
options.description: The file's link when ready, opened with openURL. Only http and https links are used.

options.name: isRequesting
options.description: Shows the request button as busy, for apps that track the request themselves.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string; status lines are closures that receive the formatted dates.

options.name: onDownload
options.description: Runs when Download is tapped, after the link is opened. Shows Download when ready even without a link.

options.name: onRequest
options.description: Requests an export with the chosen scope ids (in listed order) and format. Shows the request form while idle, expired or failed. The button is busy while it runs; a thrown error is shown.

states.name: idle
states.description: A neutral Not requested badge and, with onRequest, the form with Request export.

states.name: requested
states.description: An info Requested badge and We received your request on <date>.

states.name: preparing
states.description: An info Preparing badge, the status line and an indeterminate MonarchProgressViewStyle bar.

states.name: ready
states.description: A success Ready badge, the dates, and a primary Download button.

states.name: expired
states.description: A neutral Expired badge and the form with Request a new export.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger Failed badge, the failure reason and the form with Request a new export.

states.name: requesting
states.description: The request button shows progress and ignores taps.

states.name: scope error
states.description: With nothing checked, the checklist shows Choose at least one kind of data. as its error.

states.name: request failed
states.description: A danger MonarchBanner with the error's description, announced.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the title in the subheading style, a status badge in its tone with an icon, a muted description and the status line in the default text colour. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's NativeSelect is a Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu); its Alert is MonarchBanner; its Checkbox list is MonarchCheckboxGroup, whose option type is reused for the scope. Dates use the environment's locale and time zone instead of the web's locale, timeZone and dateFormat props; they are formatted as an abbreviated date and short time. The web's download link with the download attribute is openURL, so the system decides how the file is saved. The web's headingLevel has no equivalent: the title has the header trait. The web's errorMessage closure is the error's LocalizedError description. Experimental: a product-screen composite that waits for a Rook iOS app to adopt it. Several closures are optional (onDownload, onRequest). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onDownload.
accessibility: The card is a container named by its title; the title has the header trait.
The status is a badge with an icon and a word, not colour alone.
A new status line is announced when the status changes.
The preparing bar is named Preparing your export and stops animating with Reduce Motion, from MonarchProgressViewStyle.
The scope error is the checklist's error, announced by MonarchCheckboxGroup; a failed request is announced.
The buttons are standard MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: The checklist and format keep what the person chose while the card is shown; a new scope list given later does not reset them.
A download link with another scheme (file, javascript) is ignored; Download then shows only with onDownload.
An error without a LocalizedError description shows The request did not go through. Try again.
Without onRequest, the card only reports status.

wrapsNative: ScrollView([.horizontal, .vertical]) with a LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders]) of rows under a pinned header row; pinned columns held at their edge with visualEffect measuring against the scroll view's named coordinate space; Menu for the column menu and row actions; Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox), and Toggle(sources:isOn:) for the mixed select-all; MonarchEditableCell for editing; at compact width MonarchDataTable(layout: .list) with a sheet holding a NavigationStack and Form as the record editor
summary: An editable grid of records: fixed-width columns that sort, pin, hide and resize from a menu on their header, cells that edit in place, selection, row actions and a load-more footer; at compact width a list of records whose editor opens in a sheet.
whenToUse: For spreadsheet-like screens on iPad and with hardware keyboards: many rows, values edited in place, wide data where key columns stay pinned.
whenNotToUse: For read-only records people scan, sort and open, use MonarchDataTable. For a long list without columns, use a List (virtual-list) or MonarchCursorList. For one record, use a Form.
