options.name: label
options.description: Names the grid for VoiceOver, such as "Invoices".

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, in the app's order. Row is Identifiable; its id is the selection key.

options.name: columns
options.description: Every column in its default order: title, id, numeric, sortable, hideable, pinnable, pinned, width, edit, the cell text and the sort rule.

options.name: sort
options.description: The sort: one column and a direction. With it, column menus offer Sort ascending, Sort descending and Clear sort, and the record list a Sort menu.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected ids. With it, rows get checkboxes and the header an on, off or mixed select-all checkbox.

options.name: hiddenColumns
options.description: Ids of hidden columns, as MonarchColumnChooser writes them. With it, column menus offer Hide column.

options.name: columnOrder
options.description: Column ids in display order; missing ids follow in their default order.

options.name: pinning
options.description: Every pinned column by id; a nil value inside the binding uses each column's own pin. With it, column menus offer Pin to start, Pin to end and Unpin.

options.name: columnWidths
options.description: Widths by column id, replacing the columns' own widths. With it, column menus offer Widen column and Narrow column in 16-point steps between 96 and 480 points.

options.name: layout
options.description: .table draws the grid, .list the records with an editor sheet; .automatic picks the grid at regular width below the accessibility text sizes.

options.name: density
options.description: Padding above and below cells; .compact keeps 44-point rows.

options.name: sortsRows
options.description: Whether the grid sorts rows itself; false when the server sorts.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Without rows shows placeholder rows; with rows shows an indeterminate progress bar above them.

options.name: footer
options.description: A load-more footer under the rows; with autoLoads: true it loads the next page when the end comes into view.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including those of the editable cells.

options.name: rowLabel
options.description: A row's name in spoken labels and the record list. By default the first shown cell.

options.name: isRowSelectable
options.description: Whether a row has a checkbox.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: A row's actions: an actions column with a menu, the context menu, VoiceOver actions and, in the record list, swipe actions.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a row: a tap on a read-only cell, a tap on a record without editable cells, or Open details in the record editor.

states.name: grid
states.description: A header row on the subtle fill pinned to the top, then a row per record: a checkbox column, start-pinned columns with a line at their inner edge, columns that scroll sideways together with the header, end-pinned columns and an actions column.

states.name: list
states.description: At compact width and accessibility text sizes: MonarchDataTable's list with select-all and Sort, one record per row with its name and a "Field value" line per column. Tapping a record with editable cells opens the record editor sheet.

states.name: sorted
states.description: The sorted header shows an arrow and reads "Sorted ascending" or "Sorted descending"; its menu offers the other direction and Clear sort.

states.name: pinned
states.description: A pinned column stays at its edge while the other columns scroll; its header reads "Pinned to start" or "Pinned to end". Pins that would take more than half the width scroll with the rest.

states.name: editing
states.description: An editable cell opens its MonarchEditableCell editor in place: a text field with Save and Cancel, a menu or the compact date picker. It shows progress while saving and keeps the editor open with the message when saving fails.

states.name: selected
states.description: The row fills with the accent's subtle fill and its checkbox is checked; the select-all checkbox is on, off or mixed.

states.name: loading
states.description: Without rows: placeholder rows named "Loading rows". With rows: an indeterminate progress bar above them.

states.name: empty
states.description: No rows: MonarchEmptyState with "Nothing here yet", or the labels' title and message.

appearance: Rows on the surface fill with a hairline subtle divider, the header row on the subtle background with muted labels, a default-border line at the inner edge of pinned columns, selected rows on the accent's subtle fill. Numeric cells align to the trailing edge with tabular digits; an empty cell shows a muted dash; the first cell is link-coloured when rows open. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: SwiftUI's Table does not edit cells, pin columns or scroll sideways, so Monarch draws the grid in one ScrollView that scrolls both ways, with a LazyVStack of rows and a header pinned as a section header; pinned columns are held at their edge by a visualEffect offset, so scrolling redraws no view body. It keeps DataTable's types (MonarchDataTableSort, MonarchDataTableRowAction, MonarchDataTableLayout) as the web DataGrid keeps DataTable's column model, and Android does the same. Matching Android, tapping a header opens the column menu (sort, pin, unpin, hide, widen, narrow) instead of sorting at once, and the web's drag-to-resize header edge becomes Widen column and Narrow column in 16-point steps, as the web's Alt+Arrow keys do, so resizing never needs a drag. iPhone gets the mobile pattern instead of a squeezed grid: MonarchDataTable's list of records and an editor in a sheet. State follows SwiftUI bindings instead of Android's value-and-callback pairs; a feature whose binding is absent is not offered, as on Android. Paging uses MonarchLoadMore (with autoLoads) instead of Android's onEndReached, as MonarchDataTable does on iOS; there is no actionsIcon or emptyState slot (the actions button uses the system ellipsis symbol and the empty state takes the labels' title and message). Each editable column carries a MonarchDataGridEdit with MonarchEditableCellValue and its own onCommit instead of the web's one onCellEdit with untyped values. Not offered: multi-sort, Shift-click range selection, type-to-edit, keyboard shortcuts for selection, the WAI-ARIA grid's single tab stop with arrow-key cell movement (the system focus moves between cells instead) and aria-rowcount for rows not yet loaded. Several closures are optional (rowLabel, isRowSelectable, rowActions, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is rowLabel. MonarchDataGridEdit has several optional closures (isEditable, format, validate). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is isEditable.
accessibility: The grid is a container named by label.

Headers have the header trait; a header with menu items is a button whose value is its sort and pin, such as "Sorted descending, Pinned to end" ("Not sorted" for a sortable column), and whose hint is "Column options".
A read-only cell is one element read as "Column: value", with "No value" for an empty cell; with onOpen it is a button whose hint is "Open details".
An editable cell is a MonarchEditableCell named "Column for row", such as "Customer for INV-1".
Row actions are an actions menu named "Actions for row", the row's context menu, and VoiceOver actions on each read-only cell of the row.
Row checkboxes are named "Select row"; the header's select-all checkbox is a Toggle over every selectable row, so VoiceOver reads it as on, off or mixed.
Column resizing, pinning and hiding are menu choices, so every change works with VoiceOver and Switch Control; nothing needs a drag.
In the list layout each record is one element; a record with editable cells has the hint "Edit" and opens the record editor, and with onOpen a VoiceOver action "Open details".
Headers, cells, checkboxes and the actions button are at least 44 points tall; checkboxes and the actions button at least 44 points wide.
edgeCases: Pinned columns that would take more than half of the grid's width scroll with the others, so a narrow iPad window is never filled by pinned columns.
Each column has a fixed width; long text wraps in its cell and the row grows.
Rows sort by the column's sortBy or its text compared as Finder does, stably; a sort on an unknown or unsortable column leaves the app's order.
Row ids must be unique; the same id twice breaks the lazy stack and the selection.
The grid fills the space it is given and scrolls both ways; give it a bounded height and do not put it inside another scroll view.
A column whose edit says a row is not editable shows that row's cell as read-only text, not a disabled control.

The value of an editable cell is read from the row: the app saves in onCommit and passes the changed rows back. The record editor finds its row by id on each change, so saved values show at once; when the row disappears the sheet closes.
Selecting all keeps selected rows that are not in rows (another page) and adds every selectable row.

title: DataSubjectRequestForm
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchRadioCardGroup, a segmented Picker in a MonarchFormField, MonarchTextFields, MonarchCountrySelect, a vertical TextField in a MonarchFormField, a Toggle with .monarchCheckbox and a primary MonarchButton, replaced by a success MonarchBanner
summary: A recipe, not a component: a privacy request form (get a copy, delete, correct, object, opt out) for the person the data is about or their authorised agent, with validation on send and a reference on success.
whenToUse: On a privacy or help screen where people exercise their data rights (GDPR, CCPA and similar laws) and the request goes to the company's privacy team.
whenNotToUse: For the signed-in person downloading their own data, use MonarchDataExportRequest. For deleting their own account, use the delete-account-flow recipe. For consent choices, use MonarchConsentPreferences.
api: MonarchRadioCardGroup("What would you like to do?", selection: $type, options: [MonarchRadioCardOption("access", title:, description:), …])
MonarchFormField("Who is this request for?") { Picker(…).pickerStyle(.segmented) }
MonarchTextField("Email", text: $email, helper:, error:)
MonarchCountrySelect("Country or region where the person lives", selection: $country, error:, isRequired: true)
MonarchFormField("Details", helper:, error:, isRequired:) { TextField("Details", text: $details, axis: .vertical) }
Toggle("The information I gave is accurate", isOn: $isAccurate).toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)
MonarchButton("Send request", variant: .primary, isLoading: isSending, fullWidth: true)
MonarchBanner("Request received", message:, tone: .success)

states.name: empty
states.description: Nothing chosen; errors are not shown until the first send.

states.name: agent
states.description: Choosing Someone I act for renames the person's fields and adds the agent's own name.

states.name: invalid
states.description: After Send, each missing or wrong answer shows its error with an icon, and the problem count is announced.

states.name: sending
states.description: The send button shows progress.

states.name: received
states.description: The form is replaced by a success banner with the reference.

appearance: Monarch's radio cards, text fields, country select, checkbox and primary button on the page background; errors use the danger roles with an icon, and the confirmation is a success banner. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web DataSubjectRequestForm is one component with default request types, an error summary that links to each field, a verification note, a response time note and translatable messages. On iOS it is a recipe built from Monarch fields: the request types are the app's MonarchRadioCardOptions (which types apply where is for the product's legal team), the relationship is a segmented Picker, the country is MonarchCountrySelect with Foundation's names, and the submission is the app's call. There is no error summary with links; each field shows and announces its own error. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: Every field has a visible label read by VoiceOver; required fields add Required to their hint.
Errors appear only after Send, each with an icon and text, and Monarch fields announce a new error.
The radio cards read their title and description and mark the choice with the selected trait.
The acknowledgement is a real Toggle with the checkbox style, read as a checkbox with its state.
edgeCases: Details become required for a correction, since the team needs to know what to fix.
Keep everything typed when the send fails, and show the failure with MonarchInlineNotice above the button.
Prefill the email of a signed-in person, but let them change it.
Long request descriptions wrap in the cards at every text size.

name: MonarchDataTable
title: DataTable
wrapsNative: SwiftUI.Table with TableColumnForEach and TableColumn(_:sortUsing:content:) at regular width (iOS 17.4 and later); List with .listStyle(.plain), swipeActions and contextMenu at compact width; Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) for selection; Menu for row actions and the compact sort
summary: Records in columns: a SwiftUI Table at regular width and a list of records with a labelled line per field at compact width, with sorting, selection, row actions, column visibility and order, and the loading, empty, filtered and error states.
whenToUse: For a screen of records with several fields each (tickets, invoices, people) that people scan, sort, select and act on, on iPhone and iPad.
whenNotToUse: For records with one or two fields, use a List. For a list fetched page by page with no columns, use MonarchCursorList. For a small fixed table inside a document, use MonarchTableBlock.

options.name: caption
options.description: Names the table for VoiceOver, such as "Open tickets".

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows, in the app's order.

options.name: columns
options.description: Every column in its default order: header, cell text, numeric alignment, sort rule, whether it sorts and hides, ideal width.

options.name: sort
options.description: The sort, one column and a direction. nil keeps the sort inside the table, starting unsorted.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected ids. With it, rows get checkboxes and a select-all checkbox appears above them.

options.name: hiddenColumns
options.description: Ids of hidden columns, as MonarchColumnChooser writes them.

options.name: columnOrder
options.description: Column ids in display order; missing ids follow in their default order.

options.name: layout
options.description: A table at regular width and a list at compact width or the accessibility text sizes, or always one of them.

options.name: sortsRows
options.description: Whether the table sorts rows itself; false when the server sorts and the app reloads on sort changes.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: With no rows, shows placeholder rows; with rows, the footer shows progress.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: With no rows, shows the error state with this message.

options.name: isFiltered
options.description: No rows means the filters matched nothing: the filtered empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: A load-more footer under the rows, for paged data.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: rowLabel
options.description: A row's name in spoken labels. By default the first shown column's text.

options.name: isRowSelectable
options.description: Whether a row has a checkbox.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: A row's actions: an actions menu, the context menu and, in the list, swipe and VoiceOver actions.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Retry to the error state.

options.name: onClearFilters
options.description: Adds Clear filters to the filtered state.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a row: the row's name (table) or the whole record (list) becomes a button.

states.name: table
states.description: A system Table with a checkbox column, the shown columns with sortable headers, and an actions column.

states.name: list
states.description: One record per row: checkbox, the name in bold (link-coloured when it opens), a "Field value" line per other column, and an actions menu; a Sort menu sits above the rows.

states.name: selected
states.description: Checked checkboxes and "3 selected" beside Select all rows.

states.name: loading
states.description: With no rows, a MonarchLoadingState of rows named "Loading rows".

states.name: failed
states.description: With no rows, a MonarchErrorState, "These rows could not be loaded", with the message and Retry.

states.name: filtered
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState, "No rows match these filters", with Clear filters.

states.name: empty
states.description: A MonarchEmptyState, "Nothing here yet".

appearance: The table and list are the system's, on the screen background. Cell text uses the default text role, field names, counts and empty cells (a dash) the muted role, an openable row name the link role, destructive actions the system destructive style. Checkboxes are the Monarch checkbox style. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: SwiftUI's Table shows only its first column at compact width, so Monarch supplies the compact row; at regular width the table is the system Table, whose dynamic columns need iOS 17.4 (on 17.0 to 17.3 the list is shown). Cells are text from each column's value; the web's custom cell renderers, expandable rows, column resizing, multi-column sort, keyboard grid navigation, pagination and select-all-matching are not offered: use a footer MonarchLoadMore for paging and let the app widen columns with width. Every column of the system Table can be clicked to sort, so a column that is not sortable ignores the request and keeps the current sort. Selection is a checkbox column and a select-all checkbox, not the system's edit-mode selection, so it works the same in both layouts. The web density option has no equivalent; rows use the system heights. Android uses the same name and options. Several closures are optional (rowLabel, isRowSelectable, rowActions, onRetry, onClearFilters, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is rowLabel.
accessibility: The table or list is named by caption.
In the list layout each record is one element read as "Ticket 42, Status: Open, Owner: Ana Lima", with "No value" for empty cells; with onOpen it is a button with the hint "Opens the details".
Row actions are VoiceOver actions on the record, and also a separate menu button named "Actions for" and the row's name.
Each checkbox is named "Select" and the row's name; Select all rows is a checkbox with the selected count beside it.
The compact Sort menu reads the sorted column and "sorted ascending" or "sorted descending" as its value.
In the table layout the system reads headers and cells; empty cells read "No value".
At the accessibility text sizes the automatic layout is the list, and field names stack above their values.
edgeCases: The default sort compares cell texts as Finder does ("Item 9" before "Item 10"); pass sortBy for grouped numbers, dates and amounts.
Sorting is stable: equal rows keep the app's order.
Hidden columns that cannot be hidden stay shown.
Select all only adds and removes the selectable rows on screen; other selected ids are kept.
Both layouts fill their space and scroll; do not nest the table in a ScrollView.

examples.template:
MonarchDataTable(
    {{caption}},
    rows: invoices,
    columns: [
        MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.0.header}}, id: {{columns.0.id}}, isHideable: false, value: { $0.customer }),
        MonarchDataTableColumn(
            {{columns.1.header}},
            id: {{columns.1.id}},
            value: { $0.status },
            tone: { invoice in
                switch invoice.status {
                case "Paid": .success
                case "Overdue": .danger
                default: .neutral
                }
            }
        ),
        MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.2.header}}, id: {{columns.2.id}}, value: { $0.issued }),
        MonarchDataTableColumn({{columns.3.header}}, id: {{columns.3.id}}, value: { $0.owner }),
        MonarchDataTableColumn(
            {{columns.4.header}},
            id: {{columns.4.id}},
            isNumeric: true,
            value: { $0.amount.formatted(.currency(code: "USD").precision(.fractionLength(0)).locale(Locale(identifier: "en_US"))) },
            sortBy: { $0.amount < $1.amount }
        ),
    ],
    sort: $sort,
    selection: $selection,
    rowActions: { _ in
        [
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.0}}) {},
            MonarchDataTableRowAction({{rowActions.1}}, isDestructive: true) {},
        ]
    },
    onOpen: { _ in }
)
.frame(height: 480)

states.name: empty
states.description: No range: a Choose dates button that sets the shortest range from today, inside the bounds.

states.name: chosen
states.description: Start and End rows with the system date buttons, the number of days, and Quick picks and Clear dates under them.

states.name: start moved
states.description: The end moves with it so the length is kept, then is held inside the length and latest-day bounds.

states.name: error
states.description: A first or last day rejected by isDateDisabled shows "That date is not available." with an icon in the danger colour, and is announced.

states.name: required

appearance: The label, required mark, help and error use MonarchFormField's styles: label in the default text colour, help in the muted colour, error in the strong danger colour with an icon. The date buttons and calendar are the system's, tinted by the app; the day count is muted caption text. Buttons are Monarch secondary and ghost buttons.
platformNotes: Planned as a custom range calendar; delivered as a wrapper over the system DatePicker instead, following the native-first rule: iOS has no range calendar (UICalendarView offers single, multiple and week selection, not a range), and Calendar, Reminders and Settings show a period as Start and End rows. The web DateRangePicker has typed inputs with a format hint, a one- or two-month calendar with a live preview of the range, week numbers, day dots and sizes; on iOS the system date button opens the system calendar, typing and the locale format are the system's, and day dots and sizes are not offered. The web's too-short, too-long and end-before-start errors cannot happen here because each picker only offers allowed days. The value is a ClosedRange<Date> rather than ISO strings. Android delivers the Material date range picker natively.
accessibility: Each picker is the system DatePicker, read as "Report period, Start" or "Report period, End" with its date as the value, so both keep their role, value and adjustable behaviour.
The help text, the error (read as "Error: …") and "Required" are the hint of both pickers; the visible label and help are hidden so they are not read twice.
A new error is announced with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement; the error has an icon and text, not colour alone.
Quick picks are a system menu with a Picker, so the current choice is read as selected; disabled presets are dimmed and not selectable.
Choose dates, Clear dates and Quick picks keep a 44-point touch target.
Text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Bounds are whole days: times are dropped and the range holds the first moment of each day.
When the latest day leaves less room than minimumDays, the last possible start is pulled back so the shortest range still fits.
maximumDays below minimumDays is raised to minimumDays.
A month preset follows the calendar: "month(-1)" in March is all of February, 28 or 29 days.
isDateDisabled is checked for the first and last day only; a disabled day inside the range is allowed, as on the web.
The app decides whether to block a range with an error; the binding still holds it.

whenToUse: For a moment in a form, a meeting, an interview, a scheduled send: a day and a wall-clock time. Show the zone the time belongs to next to it, and set the picker's time zone to that zone.
whenNotToUse: For a day only, use the date picker with displayedComponents: .date. For a length of time, use MonarchDurationInput. For a choice among a few fixed slots, use a Picker or MonarchRadioCardGroup.

states.name: set
states.description: Two compact buttons show the date and the time in the locale's formats and 12- or 24-hour clock; each opens the system calendar or time wheel.

states.name: limited
states.description: Moments outside the `in:` range cannot be chosen: earlier days are dimmed and earlier times on the first day are refused by the picker.

states.name: zone
states.description: With .environment(\.timeZone, zone) the picker shows and edits the wall-clock time in that zone; the zone's name is shown as the field's helper or with MonarchTimezoneSelect.

states.name: optional
states.description: The app keeps a Date? and shows Set and Clear buttons around the picker (the system picker always has a value).

states.name: invalid
states.description: MonarchFormField shows the app's error under the row with its icon.

states.name: disabled
states.description: System dimming, with disabled(_:).

appearance: The system compact picker: two rounded buttons in the system fill, the selected day and the time wheel tinted with the theme's accent. The label, helper and error come from MonarchFormField in the theme's text and danger roles, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DateTimePicker is a DatePicker plus a typed time field, with a YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm wall-clock string, a 15-minute arrow step, an hourCycle override, a defaultTime for a date picked first, presets, isDateDisabled and a timeZone slot. On iOS the system picker is the expected control: it parses and formats in the person's locale and clock, so there is no typed time to validate. The value is a Date, an instant; the zone the wall-clock time means is the picker's .environment(\.timeZone), so set it to the event's zone and store the zone with the date (or convert to DateComponents for a pure wall-clock value). min and max become the `in:` range. SwiftUI offers no minute step (UIDatePicker.minuteInterval is UIKit only) and no per-day disabling; validate the step or refuse disabled days with MonarchFormField's error, or offer MonarchMiniMonth in a sheet for days plus a time-only picker. Presets are a Menu that keeps the time. Android uses Material 3 DatePicker and TimePicker.
accessibility: System behaviour: the date and the time are two buttons, each read with the picker's title and its value; the calendar and the time wheels are navigable by VoiceOver.
With .labelsHidden() the visible label comes from MonarchFormField; the picker keeps its title for VoiceOver.
The zone is text in the helper, not only implied, so VoiceOver reads which zone the time belongs to.
Dynamic Type, the 12- or 24-hour clock and right-to-left layout are handled by the system.
edgeCases: A Date is an instant: the same value shows a different wall-clock time in another zone. Keep the zone with the value.
Daylight-saving gaps: a time that does not exist on that day in the zone is moved by the system to a valid one.
A selection outside the `in:` range is clamped by the picker.
Choosing a new day keeps the time; a preset should also keep it (combine the preset's day with the current hour and minute).

title: DeactivateFlow

summary: A recipe, not a component: confirm a reversible pause (a partnership, a tracker, a person) in a sheet that says where to turn it back on, lists what changes meanwhile and can record a reason; the same sheet confirms reactivation.
whenToUse: When an action stops something working but keeps its data, such as deactivating a user, pausing a partnership or turning off an integration, and when turning it back on.
whenNotToUse: When the action deletes data or cannot be undone, use a destructive confirmationDialog or a delete flow with MonarchTypeToConfirmInput. When the change is trivial and instant to reverse, change it directly with a Toggle and no confirmation. With nothing to list and no reason to ask, a plain confirmationDialog is enough.

MonarchTextField("Reason (optional)", text: $reason, helper: "Kept with the change history.")
MonarchButton("Deactivate", variant: .primary, isLoading: isWorking, fullWidth: true, action: confirm)
.interactiveDismissDisabled(isWorking)

states.description: Title "Deactivate …?", the description that nothing is deleted, the line saying where to reactivate, what changes while it is deactivated, the optional reason and Deactivate.

states.name: reactivate

states.description: The confirm button shows its spinner and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the buttons; the sheet stays open so the person can retry.

platformNotes: The web DeactivateFlow is a warning-toned ConfirmDialog. The iOS system alert and confirmation dialog cannot hold a consequence list or a text field, so the recipe uses a sheet with a primary (not destructive) confirm button, since nothing is deleted; Monarch has no warning button variant. For a pause with no consequences and no reason, use confirmationDialog with a non-destructive button instead. The web's mode, subject and reactivateFrom props become the app's own state and strings in the recipe.

The reversibility line is a Label whose icon is read with its text.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, not by icon colour alone.
The reason field is a MonarchTextField with its label and helper text.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while working; the sheet cannot be dismissed by swiping while the request runs.

Send the reason with the request only when it is not empty.
Reactivation can be offered from the same place the line names, so the promise in the line is true.

summary: Records a decision about an item (keep, review, let lapse) with a reason, next to the evidence for it, and shows who decided and when.
whenToUse: When a person must choose one of two to five outcomes for a record and others should see the choice and the reason.
whenNotToUse: For a simple confirmation use the system confirmationDialog. For a choice with no reason and no record, use a Picker.

options.name: title

options.name: options
options.description: The choices, in order. Each has a label, a value, and optionally a description, a note shown while selected, a badge tone, its own reason rule and a disabled flag.

options.name: value
options.description: The saved decision, or nil for none.

options.name: reason
options.description: The saved reason.

options.name: decidedAt
options.description: When the saved decision was made. Shown as a relative time.

options.name: decidedBy
options.description: Who made the saved decision.

options.name: allowsNone
options.description: Offers a "No decision" choice that clears the decision.

options.name: isReasonRequired
options.description: Every choice needs a reason. An option's own isReasonRequired overrides it.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the decision as a badge with the reason, without the form.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: reasonLimit
options.description: The longest reason accepted, in characters.

options.name: onDecide
options.description: Saves the decision. Without it the card is read-only.

options.name: context
options.description: Evidence for the decision, shown above the choices.

options.name: now
options.description: The date the decided line is measured from; the current time by default.

states.name: unchanged
states.description: The Save button is disabled while the form equals the saved decision.

states.name: selected choice
states.description: The row has an accent border, a subtle accent fill and a filled checkmark glyph; its note is shown under the choices.

states.name: reason missing
states.description: After Save is activated without a required reason, the field has a danger border and an error message with an icon.

states.name: near the limit
states.description: From 50 characters left, the number left is shown under the reason.

states.name: saving
states.description: The choices and the reason are disabled and the button shows progress until onDecide returns.

states.name: failed
states.description: The choice is kept and the error is shown with an icon above the button.

states.name: read-only
states.description: A badge in the option's tone, or "No decision yet", then the reason and who decided when.

appearance: A card on the surface colour. Choices are bordered rows on the surface colour; the selected row uses the subtle accent fill and the strong accent border. The reason field looks like MonarchTextField. Errors use the strong danger colour with an icon.
platformNotes: The web card uses radio inputs and a Textarea. iOS has no radio button and a Picker cannot show a description under each option outside a List, so the choices are button rows with a checkmark and the selected trait; the reason is a multi-line TextField drawn with the tokens of MonarchTextField. onDecide is an async throwing closure instead of a function that may return a promise. The web headingLevel, now and locale properties have no counterpart: the title is a heading, and the time uses the user's locale and is redrawn every minute.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each choice is a button with the selected trait, read as its label and description, inside a group named "Decision".
Selection is a glyph as well as a colour.
The note of a newly selected choice is announced.
A missing reason is announced and shown with an icon and text; it is also the hint of the field.
A successful save and a failed save are announced.
The time of the decision is read as an absolute date and time.
Every choice is at least 44 points high and the Save button has a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: A new value or reason from the app resets the form.
A reason of white space only counts as empty, and the reason is trimmed before it is passed to onDecide.
Text beyond reasonLimit is cut as it is typed or pasted.
An error that is not a LocalizedError shows the built-in failure text.
The built-in "characters left" text uses the English plural rule; pass labels.charactersLeft for other languages.
If the view is removed while onDecide runs, the task still finishes.
With allowsNone false and no saved value, no choice is selected and Save stays disabled until one is chosen.

whenToUse: In account settings of any app that lets people sign up. App Store Review Guideline 5.1.1(v) requires that an app offering account creation also lets people start deleting their account inside the app.
whenNotToUse: For leaving one workspace, use the leave-workspace-flow recipe. For deleting a workspace, use the delete-workspace-flow recipe. For erasing personal data on request without deleting the account, use the gdpr-erase-flow recipe.

MonarchBanner("Transfer or delete the workspaces you own first", message:, tone: .warning, actionTitle:, action:)
MonarchConsequenceList([MonarchConsequence(.removed, …), …], heading: "What happens")
MonarchDataExportRequest(status:, scope:, onRequest:)
MonarchFormField("Why are you leaving?") { Picker(…).pickerStyle(.menu) }
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase: email, text: $typed); MonarchButton("Delete account", variant: .danger).disabled(!MonarchTypeToConfirmInput.matches(typed, phrase: email))
.sheet(isPresented: $isVerifying) { MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(description:, methods:, onVerified:, onVerify:) }

states.name: export

appearance: A system sheet with a navigation bar and the back button on later steps; Monarch's banner, consequence list, export request, form fields, type-to-confirm input and danger button on the canvas background. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web DeleteAccountFlow is one component on a WizardDialog that adds the export and reason steps when onExport and reasons are given, and runs a StepUpRequirement. On iOS it is a recipe: each step is a pushed screen in a NavigationStack inside the sheet with the system back gesture, the export step is MonarchDataExportRequest, the reason is a menu Picker, and re-authentication is MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in a nested sheet (it can use Face ID or Touch ID through the device-owner method). App Store rules require this flow to be reachable inside an iOS app that offers sign-up; the app may finish deletion on its server or website but must start it in the app. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: Each step has a navigation title; the review heading has the header trait.
The blocking banner reads its title, message and action; the disabled Continue is read as dimmed.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed email matches; the delete button stays disabled until it does.
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog announces failures and moves focus to its field.
edgeCases: Matching the typed email is exact apart from surrounding spaces, as MonarchTypeToConfirmInput.matches does.
Leave out the export or reason step by not pushing it.
If the deletion fails after verification, keep the sheet open on the confirm step and show the error with MonarchInlineNotice.
Accounts in a grace period: say when the deletion takes effect on the deleted screen; that wording is the app's.

platformNotes: The web's DeleteWorkspaceFlow is one component built on a WizardDialog with numbered steps. On iOS it is a recipe: a sheet with a NavigationStack, so each step is a pushed screen with the system back button, which is how multi-step tasks work on a phone, and the step-up check is MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in a nested sheet. The web's impact counts become MonarchConsequence items with counts; its messages are written in the app. The web's gracePeriodDays changes only the copy ("Schedule deletion", the date) and is the app's choice here. MonarchConsequenceList reads each line with its kind and count, so removed and changed do not depend on the icons.
MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces when the typed name matches.
The disabled Delete workspace button has a caption that says why.
Failures are shown in words in a notice and announced; the sheet cannot be dismissed while deleting.
MonarchStepUpAuthDialog shows errors in words and supports the password, a code and the device owner check.
edgeCases: Check on the server that the person is an owner and re-authenticated; the recipe only gathers the confirmation.
Offer Transfer ownership instead only when there is another member who could own the workspace.
After the done screen closes, navigate away from the deleted workspace.
With a grace period, say when the deletion happens and how to cancel it.

options.name: value
options.description: The change. A ratio (0.12 is 12%) unless formatValue writes it another way. nil means there is nothing to compare with.

options.name: current, previous
options.description: In the second initialiser: the two periods. The change is (current − previous) / |previous|.

options.name: comparison
options.description: The comparison period after the change, such as "vs last month".

options.name: goodDirection
options.description: up, down or neither: which direction is an improvement.

options.name: variant
options.description: plain is inline text; subtle is a tinted pill.

options.name: size
options.description: sm is caption size, md is label size.

options.name: flatThreshold
options.description: Changes whose size is at or below this count as no change.

options.name: flatLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No change".

options.name: noDataLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No earlier data".

options.name: spokenLabel
options.description: Replaces the whole sentence VoiceOver reads.

options.name: showsIcon
options.description: Shows the arrow. The sign and the spoken direction remain without it.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes the size of the change, without a sign. The default is a percentage in the current locale.

states.name: better
states.description: A change in the good direction: the success colour, an arrow and a sign.

states.name: worse
states.description: A change in the other direction: the danger colour, an arrow and a sign.

states.name: neutral
states.description: goodDirection is neither: muted text, an arrow and a sign.

states.name: no change
states.description: Zero, inside flatThreshold, or written the same as zero: a dash symbol and "No change".

states.name: no data
states.description: nil or not finite: "No earlier data", with no arrow and no comparison.

appearance: Plain is coloured text: the success strong, danger strong or muted text colour. The pill adds the matching subtle fill. The comparison is muted text, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web formats percentages, numbers with a unit and currencies from options; here the default is a percentage and formatValue takes a closure for anything else. The web appearance values plain and pill are the variants plain and subtle. The web lets each spoken word (up, down, better, worse) be replaced; here those four come from the strings table and spokenLabel replaces the whole sentence. The current and previous initialiser always gives a ratio; for an absolute difference, subtract and pass the value. The arrows point up-right and down-right in both layout directions. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The indicator is one element that reads a sentence: "up 12% vs last month, better".
The direction is carried by the arrow, the sign and the spoken words; better and worse are spoken, so nothing depends on colour.
A decrease is written with a real minus sign (U+2212).
The arrow is decorative and hidden from VoiceOver.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; digits are monospaced so values line up in a column.
edgeCases: A change that the format writes as zero, such as 0.0001 as a percentage, is "No change", never "+0%".
With current and previous, a previous value of zero has no baseline and shows "No earlier data".
A negative baseline uses its absolute value, so −100 to −50 is an increase of 50%.
The comparison is not shown when there is no data.

states.description: One row per device, separated by dividers.

states.name: current
states.description: A success This device badge and no Remove button.

states.name: blocked
states.description: A danger Blocked badge and the device icon in the strong danger colour.

states.name: removing
states.description: The row's Remove button shows its spinner; other Remove buttons are disabled.

states.name: remove failed
states.description: A danger inline notice under the header, "Couldn’t remove <name>. Try again.", announced.

states.name: loading
states.description: A progress indicator with "Loading devices".

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState.

states.name: failed
states.description: A small MonarchErrorState with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the subheading style title and a caption line in the muted text colour. Rows have the device icon in the muted text colour (strong danger when blocked), the name in the strong body style, subtle success and danger badges, and caption lines in the muted text colour. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names List rows; the rows are a VStack inside a MonarchCard instead, because the list is placed inside the app's own scrolling settings screen, where a nested List would not size itself. The web's renderActions is rowActions, a view builder. The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent (the title is a header) and its locale prop is the SwiftUI locale environment. The confirmation is the system alert (confirm-dialog on iOS), which cannot stay open while the removal runs, so the pending state moves to the row's button and a failure appears as a notice in the card instead of inside the dialog. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onRemove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.

Each device is one element whose label is its name and whose value is the badges, the system, browser and location and the times, built by a tested pure function; Blocked and This device are words, not only colour or an icon.
The device icon is decorative and hidden.
The Remove button is a separate MonarchButton with a 44-point touch target, named "Remove <name>".
The confirmation is a system alert with a destructive button and a cancel button.
Removal and a failed removal are posted as announcements.
Rows stack the actions under the text when they do not fit, so nothing is cut off at the largest text sizes.
edgeCases: A device with a blank name reads "Unknown device".
Missing system, browser or location parts are left out of the detail line; with none, there is no detail line.
The app removes the device from devices after onRemove returns; the list does not remove it itself.
Only one removal runs at a time.

name: MonarchDevicePicker
title: DevicePicker
wrapsNative: Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) in MonarchFormField for the microphone and camera; AVKit AVRoutePickerView (UIViewRepresentable) for the audio output; AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus / requestAccess for access; MonarchInlineNotice for the access notices
summary: Microphone and camera menus and the system audio route picker for a lobby or a call's settings, with notices that explain camera and microphone access and a way to fix it.
whenToUse: To let people choose the microphone, camera and audio output of a call before joining and during it, or for any capture feature that should let people pick the input.
whenNotToUse: To list signed-in phones and computers, use the device list (device-list). To capture media, use AVFoundation: the picker only chooses ids and the product opens the session.
api: init(microphone: Binding<String?>? = nil, camera: Binding<String?>? = nil, microphones: [MonarchDevicePickerDevice] = [], cameras: [MonarchDevicePickerDevice] = [], showsAudioOutput: Bool = false, access: MonarchDevicePickerAccess? = nil, size: MonarchDevicePickerSize = .md, labels: MonarchDevicePickerLabels = MonarchDevicePickerLabels(), onRequestAccess: (@MainActor @Sendable () async -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchDevicePickerDevice.init(_ id: String, name: String)
MonarchDevicePickerDevice.init(camera: AVCaptureDevice)
MonarchDevicePickerDevice.init(input: AVAudioSessionPortDescription) // iOS
enum MonarchDevicePickerAccess { case granted, notDetermined, denied, unavailable }
enum MonarchDevicePickerSize { case sm, md }

MonarchDevicePickerLabels.init(microphone: String? = nil, camera: String? = nil, speaker: String? = nil, systemDefault: String? = nil, unnamedMicrophone: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, unnamedCamera: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, notDetermined: String? = nil, allowAccess: String? = nil, denied: String? = nil, openSettings: String? = nil, unavailable: String? = nil)

options.name: microphone
options.description: The chosen microphone's id; nil is "System default". Shows the microphone field.

options.name: camera
options.description: The chosen camera's id; nil is "System default". Shows the camera field.

options.name: microphones
options.description: The microphones offered, usually AVAudioSession.availableInputs mapped with init(input:).

options.name: cameras
options.description: The cameras offered, usually an AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession's devices mapped with init(camera:).

options.name: showsAudioOutput
options.description: Shows the speaker row: the current output's name and the system route picker (iOS only).

options.name: access
options.description: The access to explain. When nil, the picker reads AVCaptureDevice.authorizationStatus for the fields it shows, and again after asking.

options.name: size
options.description: sm uses small controls and tighter spacing for a popover during a call.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRequestAccess
options.description: Replaces the system request of Allow access (AVCaptureDevice.requestAccess for the shown kinds).

states.name: granted
states.description: No notice; the fields only.

states.name: not asked
states.description: An info notice "Allow camera and microphone access to choose devices." with Allow access, which shows the system prompt or runs onRequestAccess.

states.name: denied
states.description: A warning notice that access is off, with Open Settings, which opens the app's page in Settings (iOS).

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A neutral notice "No camera or microphone was found.", also shown when access is granted but no shown field has a device.

states.name: removed device
states.description: A selected id that is no longer listed stays selected as "Microphone 1" or "Camera 1".

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true) the menus and the notice's button are disabled and the labels take the disabled text colour.

appearance: System menus in the theme's tint inside MonarchFormField, with Monarch type and colours for the labels. Notices are MonarchInlineNotice in the info, warning or neutral tone. The route picker is tinted with the default text colour and the accent solid colour while another route is active.
platformNotes: The web lists devices with navigator.mediaDevices and selects outputs with setSinkId; on iOS the app lists inputs with AVAudioSession and cameras with AVCaptureDevice.DiscoverySession (the device initialisers convert them) and applies the choice itself, and audio output must use the system route picker, so there is no speaker menu and no speaker id. The picker does not observe hardware changes: the app passes new lists (for example on AVAudioSession.routeChangeNotification). Device names are always known on iOS, so the web's "names hidden" state becomes the not-asked state. The speaker row is iOS only and is left out of the macOS build convenience. Android ships the same MonarchDevicePicker with its own output picker.
accessibility: Each menu is the standard Picker named by its field label, with the current choice as its value; MonarchFormField gives it the label.
Notices are MonarchInlineNotice: the tone name, then the message; the action is a separate button with a 44-point target.
A notice that appears or changes is announced once.
The route picker is a 44-point system button labelled "Speaker" with the current output's name as its value; the visible label and name beside it are hidden from VoiceOver.
States are text, never colour alone.
edgeCases: Devices with an empty id are left out; an empty selection is the system default.
Devices without a name are numbered by their position: "Camera 2".

Allow access with the default request needs NSCameraUsageDescription and NSMicrophoneUsageDescription in the app's Info.plist; without them iOS ends the app. Pass onRequestAccess when the app asks elsewhere.
AVAudioSession.availableInputs only lists inputs for a record-capable session category; configure the session before listing.
The route picker, the system prompt and Open Settings were compiled for iOS but not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; options, access and notice logic are unit-tested.

title: Dialog
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) for a message; sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:) for content
summary: A modal is the system alert for a short message and the system sheet for content. Inside a Monarch theme the sheet's content uses Monarch components and colours. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Use alert to tell the person something or ask a short question. Use sheet for a focused task with its own controls: a form, a picker, details. Put Cancel and the confirming action in the sheet's toolbar.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a centred dialog box over a dimmed screen yourself. For a short bottom panel see drawer; for a destructive confirmation see confirm-dialog.
api: func alert(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, actions: () -> some View, message: () -> some View) -> some View
func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> some View) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View

states.name: alert
states.description: Centred over a dimmed screen, with a title, a message and up to a few buttons.

states.name: sheet
states.description: A card that covers most of the screen on iPhone and is a centred form sheet on iPad.

states.name: dismissal blocked
states.description: With interactiveDismissDisabled the sheet does not close on a swipe; a button must close it.

appearance: The system draws the alert and the sheet's card, corners and dimming. The sheet's content is the app's: give it a theme background such as bgCanvas and it follows the four themes, because a sheet inherits the environment of the view that presents it, including the Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web Dialog is one component with sizes, a footer, a close button with closeLabel, busy, closeOnOutsideClick, escapeGuard and fullScreenOnPhone. On iOS the size is the system's (presentationDetents changes a sheet's height, see drawer), the footer is the navigation toolbar of a NavigationStack inside the sheet, the close button is a toolbar button, escapeGuard is interactiveDismissDisabled, and fullScreenOnPhone is fullScreenCover. Focus trapping and focus return are the system's (see focus-trap). Android uses a Material Dialog or a full-screen dialog.
accessibility: System behaviour: alerts and sheets are modal; VoiceOver, Switch Control and the keyboard are confined to them.
System behaviour: focus returns to the presenting screen on dismissal.
System behaviour: the escape gesture dismisses a sheet and chooses Cancel in an alert.
Give a sheet a navigation title so it is announced, and a visible button that closes it.
edgeCases: A sheet presented from a sheet stacks; avoid more than two levels.
State changed in a sheet is not saved by dismissal; apply it in the confirming action or in onDismiss.
Alerts cannot contain custom views other than text fields and buttons.

name: MonarchDiffViewer
title: DiffViewer
wrapsNative: LazyVStack of rows of monospaced Text built from AttributedString (background, strikethrough and underline attributes), in a ScrollViewReader; Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) for the layout and MonarchButton for previous, next and expand
summary: Shows what changed between two texts or two versions of a document, unified or side by side: added and removed lines, changed words inside them, folded unchanged runs, totals and previous and next change buttons.
whenToUse: To review changes between two versions of a text, a configuration or a document (one block per paragraph), for example in a version history or before restoring a version.
whenNotToUse: Not for a patch that is already a diff (use MonarchCodeBlock with isDiff), not for comparing records field by field (use MonarchMergeDialog) and not for timesheet changes (use MonarchTimesheetDiff).
api: init(before: [String], after: [String], mode: Binding<MonarchDiffViewerMode>? = nil, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = .word, context: Int? = 3, beforeLabel: String? = nil, afterLabel: String? = nil, showsModeSwitch: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = true, labels: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels(), @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(before: String, after: String, mode: Binding<MonarchDiffViewerMode>? = nil, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = .word, context: Int? = 3, beforeLabel: String? = nil, afterLabel: String? = nil, showsModeSwitch: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = true, labels: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels(), @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(before: [String], after: [String], mode: Binding<MonarchDiffViewerMode>? = nil, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = .word, context: Int? = 3, beforeLabel: String? = nil, afterLabel: String? = nil, showsModeSwitch: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = true, labels: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels()) where Actions == EmptyView

init(before: String, after: String, mode: Binding<MonarchDiffViewerMode>? = nil, granularity: MonarchDiffViewerGranularity = .word, context: Int? = 3, beforeLabel: String? = nil, afterLabel: String? = nil, showsModeSwitch: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = true, labels: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels()) where Actions == EmptyView
MonarchDiffViewerLine.init(_ kind: MonarchDiffViewerLineKind, text: String, oldNumber: Int? = nil, newNumber: Int? = nil)
static func MonarchDiffViewerLine.diff(from before: [String], to after: [String]) -> [MonarchDiffViewerLine]
static func MonarchDiffViewerLine.lines(of text: String) -> [String]
enum MonarchDiffViewerLineKind { case same, added, removed }
enum MonarchDiffViewerMode { case unified, split }
enum MonarchDiffViewerGranularity { case line, word }

struct MonarchDiffViewerLabels { init(caption: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, before: String? = nil, after: String? = nil, mode: String? = nil, unified: String? = nil, split: String? = nil, stats: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, added: String? = nil, removed: String? = nil, blankLine: String? = nil, expand: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, previous: String? = nil, next: String? = nil, position: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, noChanges: String? = nil) }

options.name: before
options.description: The earlier text, split on line breaks, or its lines or blocks (one entry per paragraph for a document).

options.name: after
options.description: The later text, in the same shape.

options.name: mode
options.description: The layout when the app owns it. nil shows side by side at regular width and unified otherwise, and the reader's choice in the switch is kept inside the view.

options.name: granularity
options.description: word also marks the changed words inside a changed line; line marks whole lines only.

options.name: context
options.description: Unchanged lines kept around each change; longer runs fold behind a Show N unchanged lines button. nil never folds.

options.name: beforeLabel
options.description: The name of the earlier side, such as a version name; read in the caption and for side by side rows.

options.name: afterLabel
options.description: The name of the later side.

options.name: showsModeSwitch
options.description: Whether the segmented layout switch is shown. It is only shown at regular width.

options.name: showsLineNumbers
options.description: Whether line numbers are shown: both numbers in unified, one per side in side by side.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of the header, such as Restore.

states.name: unified
states.description: One column: removed lines, then added lines of each change, each with both line numbers and a + or − marker.

states.name: side by side
states.description: Two columns: the k-th removed line beside the k-th added line; an empty side has the subtle fill.

states.name: folded
states.description: Unchanged runs longer than the context fold into a full-width button that shows them.

states.name: current change
states.description: After previous or next, the first row of that change has an accent bar at its leading edge and is scrolled into view.

states.name: no changes
states.description: "No changes." in the muted text colour instead of the lines.

appearance: Added lines use the subtle success fill and removed lines the subtle danger fill; changed words have the success or danger border colour as a fill, removed words are struck through and added words underlined. Markers and totals use the strong success and danger colours, line numbers the subtle text colour, inside a container with a subtle border.
platformNotes: The diff algorithm is ported from the web (longest common subsequence over lines, then over words, with the same limits), not shared. The web is a table that scrolls sideways; on iOS long lines wrap so the text scales with Dynamic Type, and the layout switch appears only at regular width because two columns do not fit a phone. Previous and next scroll with ScrollViewReader and move VoiceOver focus; scrolling needs the view inside the app's ScrollView. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The lines are a container named "Changes from <before> to <after>".
Each unified line is one element read as its text after "Added" or "Removed"; an empty line reads "Blank line". Line numbers are not read.
A side by side row reads each side after its name, or once when the line is unchanged.
The totals read "3 added, 1 removed".
Previous and next announce "Change 2 of 5" and move VoiceOver focus to the change.
Changes are marked by + and − signs, strikethrough and underline as well as colour.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; buttons have 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: Inputs with more than a million line pairs show every line removed and added; lines with more than 250,000 word pairs are not split into words.
A change of the texts resets the expanded runs and the current change.
A run of unchanged lines only one longer than the context is shown instead of folded.
An empty before shows every line as added.

name: MonarchDnsRecordTable
title: DnsRecordTable
wrapsNative: VStack of cards, or Grid with GridRow at a regular width; MonarchCopyField for each name and value, MonarchStatusBadge for the found state
summary: The DNS records a user must add at their DNS provider to connect a custom domain or verify a sender: type, name and value with copy buttons, what each record is for, and whether public DNS already shows it.
whenToUse: On a custom domain or email sender setup screen, to list the records to create, with names relative to the user's zone and a found or waiting state per record.
whenNotToUse: For one value to copy use MonarchCopyField. For general tabular data use MonarchDataTable. For the progress of the whole connection use MonarchDomainProgress beside it.
api: init(_ records: [MonarchDnsRecord], zone: String? = nil, layout: MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout = .automatic, labels: MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels = MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchDnsRecord: Identifiable { init(id: String? = nil, type: String, name: String, value: String, purpose: MonarchDnsRecordPurpose? = nil, ttl: String? = nil, priority: Int? = nil, isFound: Bool? = nil) }
enum MonarchDnsRecordPurpose { case routing, verification, certificate, custom(String) }
enum MonarchDnsRecordTableLayout { case automatic, cards, table }

struct MonarchDnsRecordTableLabels { init(type: String? = nil, name: String? = nil, value: String? = nil, ttl: String? = nil, priority: String? = nil, status: String? = nil, found: String? = nil, waiting: String? = nil, purpose: (@Sendable (MonarchDnsRecordPurpose?) -> String)? = nil, copyName: (@Sendable (MonarchDnsRecord, String) -> String)? = nil, copyValue: (@Sendable (MonarchDnsRecord, String) -> String)? = nil, fullName: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, label: (@Sendable (String?) -> String)? = nil, summary: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: records
options.description: The records, in the order the user should create them. Each has a type, a full name, a value, and optionally a purpose, TTL, priority and found state (isFound: true is Found, false is Waiting, nil when not checked).

options.name: zone
options.description: The DNS zone the user manages, such as example.com. Names inside it are shown relative to it (book, @ for the apex) with "Full name: …" under the card.

options.name: layout
options.description: cards: one card per record. table: a Grid with one row per record. automatic: cards in a compact width or at accessibility text sizes, a table otherwise.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the column and term headings, Found and Waiting, the purpose headings, the spoken names of the copy fields, the full name line, the container name and the found announcement.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied text after a name or value is copied.

states.name: not checked
states.description: A record with isFound nil has no status badge; the table has no Status column when no record was checked.

states.name: waiting
states.description: isFound false shows a neutral "Waiting" status badge.

states.name: found
states.description: isFound true shows a success "Found" status badge. When the number of found records changes, "1 of 2 records found." is announced.

states.name: cards
states.description: Each record is a card with its purpose as a heading, the status, the type, the name and value copy fields, the priority and TTL when given, and the full name when it is shown relative to the zone.

states.name: table
states.description: A header row (Type, Name, Value, and Priority, TTL and Status only when a record uses them) and one row per record with small icon-only copy fields.

states.name: empty
states.description: No records draws nothing inside the named container.

appearance: Cards and the table use the surface fill with the default border and the container radius. Headings use the default text colour, terms and the full name line the muted text colour, and type, TTL and priority the code type role. The copy fields and status badges keep their own look in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web table scrolls sideways inside itself when narrow; on iOS the automatic layout switches to cards in a compact width and at accessibility text sizes instead, and the table's copy fields shorten long values in the middle. The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent: the card heading is a header for VoiceOver. TTL is a string the app formats. The web's DnsProviderGuide (provider-by-provider steps) is not part of this component. Android uses the same name and the same record model.
accessibility: The records are one container named "DNS records for <zone>" (or "DNS records").
Each card heading has the header trait, so the rotor moves between records.
A name is read as "name of the CNAME record" with its value, and its copy button as "Copy name of the CNAME record"; a value as "value of the CNAME record book".
The visible terms Name and Value are not read again, because the copy fields carry their own spoken names.
The found state is a word in a status badge, not only a colour.
When the number of found records changes, the summary "1 of 2 records found." is announced.
In the table, each row is a container read as its type and shown name, and the column headings have the header trait.
Copy buttons keep a 44-point touch target and confirm with "Copied" and an announcement.
edgeCases: A name outside the zone, or any name without a zone, is shown in full with no full name line.
The zone and names are compared ignoring case and a trailing dot.
Long values (DKIM keys) wrap in full in the cards and are shortened in the middle in the table; the copied value is always complete.
Priority and TTL appear in a card only when the record has them, and as columns only when any record has them.
The found announcement fires on a change only, not when the view first appears.

        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "TXT", name: "_verify.book.example.com", value: "site-verification=4f1a9c2e", purpose: .verification, isFound: true),
    ],
    zone: "example.com"
)

        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "MX", name: "example.com", value: "mx1.example.net", priority: 10),
        MonarchDnsRecord(type: "MX", name: "example.com", value: "mx2.example.net", priority: 20),
    ],
    zone: "example.com",
    layout: .table
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web draws Type, Name and Value in one row; the row needs about 560 points with two copy buttons, and a phone column has 306, so Type and Name share the first row and Value takes the one below.

title: DocsPanel
wrapsNative: MonarchLinkedDocsPanel, which draws its own MonarchSectionCard; DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) and .task to load on open; on iPhone a NavigationLink row in a List that pushes a screen with the panel
summary: A recipe, not a component: the record-page block for linked docs and links, as MonarchLinkedDocsPanel in a record screen, behind a Docs disclosure that loads only when opened, or as a Docs row that opens its own screen on iPhone.
whenToUse: On a record's detail screen, to show and manage the docs and links attached to the record; behind a disclosure or a row in long screens so docs load only when someone opens them.
whenNotToUse: For files uploaded to the record, use the file list components. To pick one doc, use a Picker or MonarchCombobox.
api: MonarchLinkedDocsPanel(items, onLinkDoc: …, onAddLink: …, onUnlink: …, onOpen: …)

List { NavigationLink { MonarchLinkedDocsPanel(…) } label: { LabeledContent("Docs", value: "2") } }

options.name: collapsible
options.description: Wrap the panel in a DisclosureGroup with the Monarch style; its content is built only while expanded, so load the items in .task there.

options.name: row

options.name: count

states.name: closed

states.name: loading

appearance: MonarchLinkedDocsPanel's section card; the Monarch disclosure header when collapsible; the system list row with a chevron for the row form. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those parts.
platformNotes: The web ships DocsPanel with a frame prop (card, divider, none) and a collapsible mode with its own disclosure button and strings. On iOS MonarchLinkedDocsPanel is already the card and DisclosureGroup is the disclosure, so DocsPanel is a recipe, as on Android. The toggle text and count are the disclosure's label, and loading on open is a .task inside the disclosure's content, which SwiftUI builds only while expanded. On iPhone a record's sections are usually rows that push their own screen, so the recipe also shows a NavigationLink row. The web's doc icon is left out of the label. Experimental, like MonarchLinkedDocsPanel, until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The disclosure is one button read with Expanded or Collapsed, from DisclosureGroup and the Monarch style.
The count is part of the disclosure's label or the row's value, so it is read with it.
The row is a NavigationLink, read as a button that opens a screen.
Inside, the panel's title is a heading and its actions are Monarch buttons with 44-point targets, from MonarchLinkedDocsPanel.
edgeCases: Closing the disclosure removes the panel: keep the items in the record's state, above it.
Without a known count, label the disclosure or row Docs only.
Items that fail to load: pass errorMessage and onRetry to the panel.

name: MonarchDocumentRelations
title: DocumentRelations
wrapsNative: A VStack of rows (Button, MonarchFileTypeIcon, Text) with contextMenu; the add sheet is a NavigationStack with a List, a Picker of types and .searchable(text:prompt:)
summary: Typed links between documents (Parent of, Supersedes, Related to), read the right way round from either side, with a sheet to add one by searching and a remove button on each.
whenToUse: On a document's detail or info screen, to show and edit how it connects to other documents.
whenNotToUse: For untyped links inside the text, use a link in the editor. For a document's folder or parent page, use MonarchPageTree or a navigation stack.
api: init(_ relations: [MonarchDocumentRelation], types: [MonarchDocumentRelationType] = MonarchDocumentRelationType.defaults, candidates: [MonarchDocumentRelationTarget] = [], defaultType: String? = nil, showsEmpty: Bool = false, labels: MonarchDocumentRelationsLabels = MonarchDocumentRelationsLabels(), onSearch: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchDocumentRelationTarget) -> Void)? = nil, onAdd: (@MainActor (String, String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onRemove: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchDocumentRelation.init(id: String, type: String, direction: MonarchDocumentRelationDirection = .outgoing, target: MonarchDocumentRelationTarget)
enum MonarchDocumentRelationDirection { case outgoing, incoming }
MonarchDocumentRelationTarget.init(id: String, title: String, description: String? = nil, fileName: String? = nil)
MonarchDocumentRelationType.init(value: String, label: String, inverse: String? = nil)
static var MonarchDocumentRelationType.defaults: [MonarchDocumentRelationType]

MonarchDocumentRelationsLabels.init(label: String? = nil, add: String? = nil, sheetTitle: String? = nil, sheetDescription: String? = nil, type: String? = nil, search: String? = nil, results: String? = nil, noResults: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil, remove: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, added: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, removed: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, failed: String? = nil, none: String? = nil)

options.name: relations
options.description: This document's relations: type, direction and the document at the other end.

options.name: types
options.description: The relation types, their labels and inverses. The defaults are the web's seven types with built-in English labels.

options.name: candidates
options.description: Documents that can be linked, listed in the add sheet without those already related, at most twelve.

options.name: defaultType
options.description: The type chosen when the sheet opens; related-to, or the first type, by default.

options.name: showsEmpty
options.description: Shows "No relations yet." when there are none.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings. Type labels are replaced by passing types.

options.name: onSearch
options.description: Searches on the server as the person types; update candidates with the results. Without it, candidates are filtered by title.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a related document, usually by pushing it in the navigation stack. Without it, rows are not interactive.

options.name: onAdd
options.description: Adds a relation with the target's id and the type's value. Shows Add relation. Throw to keep the sheet open with the error.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes a relation by its id. Shows a remove button on each row; a thrown error is shown under the list.

states.name: read only
states.description: Rows without remove buttons and without the add button; not interactive without onOpen.

states.name: empty
states.description: Nothing is drawn, or "No relations yet." with showsEmpty, then the add button.

states.name: adding
states.description: The chosen document shows a progress indicator and the other results are disabled until onAdd returns; the sheet then closes.

states.name: removing
states.description: The row's remove button becomes a progress indicator and the other remove buttons are disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: The error's description, or "That didn’t work. Try again.", with an icon in the danger colour, in the sheet or under the list.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle borders: the file type icon, the relation with its arrow in the muted text colour, the title in the default text colour and the description in the muted colour. The remove button is a muted cross. Errors use the danger strong colour with an icon. The roles follow light, dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DocumentRelations shows a list with links and a modal dialog with a select and a search field. On iOS the add dialog is a sheet with its own navigation stack, the standard picker of types and the system search field (searchable) instead of MonarchCombobox, which would open a second sheet over the first, and choosing a result adds the relation directly. The web's href and renderLink become onOpen, so the app pushes the document in its navigation stack. Rows also have a context menu with Open and Remove. The web's promise callbacks become async throwing closures; an error's localized description is shown like the web's error message. Each target can carry a file name for MonarchFileTypeIcon, which the web does not show. The web moves focus to the next remove button after a removal; on iOS VoiceOver keeps its place in the list and the removal is announced. Android shares the design.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Relations".
Each row is one element read as "Parent of, Q3 plan, Finance", a button when onOpen is set.
The remove button is a separate element named "Remove relation to Q3 plan" with a 44-point target.
Adding and removing are announced ("Relation to Q3 plan added").
The relation's arrow and the file icon are decorative; the relation is said in words, never by the arrow alone.
In the sheet, the type picker is a standard picker and each result is a button read as its title and description.
edgeCases: An incoming relation of a type missing from types reads as its own value.
A type without an inverse is its own inverse, such as related-to.
Documents already related are left out of the results, so the same pair cannot be linked twice from this side.
Long titles and descriptions wrap.
