name: MonarchDomainProgress
title: DomainProgress
wrapsNative: VStack of three steps drawn as a vertical stepper, ProgressView for the step in progress, MonarchInlineNotice for problems, TimelineView(.everyMinute) for the last check time, RelativeDateTimeFormatter
summary: Stage-by-stage progress for connecting a custom domain (DNS record found, HTTPS certificate issued, live), with the problems the product found, what public DNS shows right now and that checking continues on its own.
whenToUse: On a custom domain screen while the domain connects, usually above MonarchDnsRecordTable, fed by the product's status endpoint.
whenNotToUse: For a general multi-step flow the user moves through, such as a wizard, use MonarchStepper. For a single status use MonarchStatusBadge.
api: init(_ host: String, stage: MonarchDomainStage, problems: [MonarchDomainProblem] = [], dnsFound: MonarchDomainDnsSnapshot? = nil, checkedAt: Date? = nil, now: Date? = nil, isRechecking: Bool = true, notify: MonarchDomainNotify? = nil, labels: MonarchDomainProgressLabels = MonarchDomainProgressLabels())
nonisolated static func recheckInterval(for stage: MonarchDomainStage?, suggested: Duration? = nil, isStopped: Bool = false) -> Duration?
enum MonarchDomainStage: String { case dns, ownership, certificate, page, live }
enum MonarchDomainStep: String { case dns, certificate, live }
enum MonarchDomainStepState: String { case done, current, todo, error }
struct MonarchDomainProblem { init(_ message: String, code: String? = nil, severity: MonarchDomainProblemSeverity = .blocking, step: MonarchDomainStep? = nil) }
enum MonarchDomainProblemSeverity { case blocking, info }
struct MonarchDomainDnsSnapshot { init(cnames: [String] = [], a: [String] = [], aaaa: [String] = []) }
enum MonarchDomainNotify { case email, inApp }

struct MonarchDomainProgressLabels { init(title: (@Sendable (MonarchDomainStep, MonarchDomainStepState, MonarchDomainStage) -> String)? = nil, detail: (@Sendable (MonarchDomainStep, MonarchDomainStepState, String) -> String)? = nil, state: (@Sendable (MonarchDomainStepState) -> String)? = nil, listLabel: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, announcement: (@Sendable (Int, Int, String, String) -> String)? = nil, dnsSeen: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, noRecord: String? = nil, rechecking: (@Sendable (MonarchDomainNotify?) -> String)? = nil, checked: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: host
options.description: The custom host name, such as book.example.com. Used in the live step text, the DNS line and the list name.

options.name: stage
options.description: dns or ownership: the DNS step is in progress. certificate: DNS done, certificate in progress. page: certificate done, the site load check in progress. live: every step done.

options.name: problems
options.description: What the last check found. A blocking problem marks its step (the current one by default) as needing attention and is shown as a warning notice; when there is none, the first informational problem is shown as a neutral notice.

options.name: dnsFound
options.description: What public DNS shows for the host right now, shown as "Public DNS for <host> shows CNAME → …" or "no record yet". nil hides the line.

options.name: checkedAt
options.description: When the product last checked. Shown as "Checked 2 minutes ago."

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for checkedAt, for tests and previews. Without it the time is relative to the current time and updates every minute.

options.name: isRechecking
options.description: Whether the product keeps checking on its own; adds "We keep checking automatically…".

options.name: notify
options.description: How the product tells the user it went live: email or inApp changes the end of the rechecking sentence.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: step titles and details, spoken states, the list name, the announcement, the DNS line, the rechecking sentence and the last check line.

states.name: done
states.description: The step marker is the success fill with a check mark, and the line after it is the success colour.

states.name: current
states.description: The step marker is the accent fill with a spinner; with Reduce Motion the spinner is replaced by a still dot.

states.name: todo
states.description: The step marker is an empty circle with the default border, and the title is muted.

states.name: error
states.description: A blocking problem: the step marker is the warning fill with an exclamation mark, and the problem is shown as a warning notice.

states.name: live
states.description: Every step is done and the DNS, rechecking and last check lines are hidden.

appearance: Markers use the success, accent and warning solid roles with their on-solid colours for symbols, and the default border for steps not started. Titles use the default text colour (muted before a step starts), details and status lines the muted text colour. Notices keep their own tone colours in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Built as its own vertical stepper rather than on MonarchStepper, because MonarchStepper always draws its current step as in progress (it cannot show every step done once live) and has no in-progress spinner. The web's messages that accept rich content (dnsSeen, checked) take and return strings on iOS, and the host and records are not set in code font inside the sentence. The web's polling helper domainPollMs is recheckInterval(for:suggested:isStopped:), returning a Duration. Android uses the same name and model.
accessibility: The steps are one container named "Progress for <host>".
Each step is one element: its title as the label and "<state>, <detail>" as the value, such as "in progress, Being issued now, usually 1 to 5 minutes."
The state is a spoken word and a symbol in the marker, not only a colour; markers are hidden from VoiceOver.
When the active step or its state changes, "Step 2 of 3: HTTPS certificate, in progress." is announced.
Problems are MonarchInlineNotice, which speaks the tone name with the message.
With Reduce Motion the in-progress marker does not animate.
edgeCases: A blocking problem on a step that is already done does not change it.
A blocking problem without a step marks the current step; with several problems all blocking ones are shown and informational ones are hidden.
Long host names wrap in the step details and the DNS line.
The marker scales with Dynamic Type; titles and details wrap at the largest sizes.
The view never checks DNS itself; the app polls and passes the new stage.

name: MonarchDonutChart
title: DonutChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts Chart with SectorMark (innerRadius and angularInset); inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend and an AXChartDescriptor
summary: Parts of one whole as a donut inside a chart frame: the total in the middle, a legend of values and shares, folding of small segments into Other, and every segment in the data table.
whenToUse: For two to six parts of one whole where the share matters more than an exact comparison, such as assets by type on a dashboard card.
whenNotToUse: To compare or rank parts precisely, or for many categories, use MonarchBarList or MonarchBarChart. For values that change over time or do not add up to a whole, use MonarchBarChart or a line chart.
api: init(_ title: String, segments: [MonarchDonutChartSegment], description: String? = nil, centerValue: String? = nil, centerLabel: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, sort: MonarchDonutChartSort = .descending, maxSegments: Int = 6, legendContent: MonarchDonutChartLegendContent = .both, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, size: CGFloat? = nil, thickness: CGFloat? = nil, percentDigits: Int = 0, showsCenterValue: Bool = true, showsLegend: Bool = true, isTableToggleShown: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, labels: MonarchDonutChartLabels = MonarchDonutChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchDonutChartSegment.init(_ key: String, label: String, value: Double, color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)

MonarchDonutChartLabels.init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), other: String? = nil, segment: String? = nil, value: String? = nil, share: String? = nil, total: String? = nil)
enum MonarchDonutChartLegendContent { case both, value, percent, none }
enum MonarchDonutChartSort { case descending, none }

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the donut's accessibility label.

options.name: segments
options.description: The parts: key, label, value (negative and non-finite count as 0) and an optional colour slot.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: centerValue
options.description: The large text in the middle.

options.name: centerLabel
options.description: Small text under the centre value, such as "assets".

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: sort
options.description: Largest slice first, or the given order.

options.name: maxSegments
options.description: The most slices drawn (at least 2); the smallest beyond it fold into a neutral Other slice.

options.name: legendContent
options.description: What each legend entry shows after its label: both ("412 · 48%"), value, percent or none.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready with a total of 0 shows empty.

options.name: size
options.description: The outer diameter, and the height kept in every status.

options.name: thickness
options.description: The ring's thickness, kept between 4 points and half the size.

options.name: percentDigits
options.description: Decimal places in shares.

options.name: showsCenterValue
options.description: Whether the middle shows the centre value.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Whether the legend shows beside or under the donut.

options.name: isTableToggleShown
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Other, Segment, Value, Share, Total and the frame's strings.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values in the centre, legend, table and summary. A number in the current locale by default.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: ready
states.description: The donut with its centre text and the legend.

states.name: folded
states.description: With more segments than maxSegments, the smallest are drawn as one Other slice in the neutral colour; the legend shows Other, the table lists every segment.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" replaces the donut with every segment, then the total, with Value and Share columns.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's muted placeholder of the donut's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet"; also shown automatically when the total is 0.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: Slices take the theme's data slots 1 to 5 in order, and Other the subtle text colour, over a ring in the muted background colour that shows in the gaps between slices. The centre value is heading text in the default text colour, the centre label caption text in the muted colour. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts SectorMark instead of the web's SVG circles. The web dims the other slices on hover and shows a native tooltip; iOS has no hover, and every value and share is already in the legend, so slices are not interactive. The centre value is a String rather than any node. The legend is MonarchChartLegend in a column beside the donut, moving under it when there is no room. Android ships the same MonarchDonutChart. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The donut, with its centre text, is one accessibility element labelled with the title. Its value is the generated summary ("Total 874. Laptops 412 (47%), …") or the summary parameter.
The donut carries an AXChartDescriptor with one value per segment and no total, so Audio Graphs compares the parts; point labels are the app's formatted values.
Each legend entry is one element read as its label, value and share; the colour marker is hidden.
"View as table" shows every segment, the total and the shares as text; each row is read as the segment, then its value and share.
Segments are told apart by the legend's names and the table, not by colour alone; slices are separated by a gap.
Every built-in word (Other, Segment, Value, Share, Total and the frame's strings) can be replaced through labels.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as 0; a total of 0 shows the empty state.
A share under the smallest step reads "<1%" and one just under the whole ">99%", so rounding never hides a segment; a very small slice can still be thinner than the gap on the ring.
maxSegments below 2 is treated as 2, so Other never stands alone.
A long centre value or label shrinks to half its size, then truncates, to stay inside the hole at large text sizes.
Long legend labels wrap; the legend moves under the donut when the row does not fit.
Audio Graphs was not tried with VoiceOver on a device; the descriptor and summary are unit-tested.

name: MonarchDownloadReportButton
title: DownloadReportButton
wrapsNative: MonarchButton for one format or Menu with .buttonStyle(.monarch(_:size:)) for several; fileExporter(isPresented:document:contentType:defaultFilename:onCompletion:) with a FileDocument for the file URL to save a prepared file; ProgressView with .monarchLinear; MonarchInlineErrorRetry
summary: Downloads a report in one or several formats, with progress while the file is prepared, a note when it is prepared in the background, the system save dialog for a ready file, and Try again on failure.
whenToUse: Next to a report, table or chart whose data people take away as CSV, Excel or PDF.
whenNotToUse: To share a file or link that already exists, use ShareLink with .buttonStyle(.monarch()). Do not keep people waiting on a long export: return .queued and tell them by notification when the file is ready.
api: init(formats: [MonarchDownloadReportFormat] = [.csv], progress: Double? = nil, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .sm, labels: MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels = MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels(), errorMessage: (@MainActor (any Error, MonarchDownloadReportFormat) -> String)? = nil, onDownload: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchDownloadReportFormat) async throws -> MonarchDownloadReportResult)

enum MonarchDownloadReportResult { case downloaded, queued(message: String?), file(URL) }
struct MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels { init(label:single:preparing:downloaded:queued:error:progress:) }  // every parameter optional

options.name: formats
options.description: The formats offered. One shows a plain button titled "Download CSV"; several open a menu titled "Download" with each format's label and description.

options.name: progress
options.description: How far the download is, 0 to 1, while it runs. Drawn as a linear progress bar under the button; without it only the button's spinner shows.

options.name: variant
options.description: The button's visual weight.

options.name: size
options.description: The button's height and padding.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Turns a thrown error into the text shown. Default: "The CSV download failed."

options.name: onDownload
options.description: Prepares the file. Return .file(url) to open the system save dialog, .downloaded when the app saved or shared it, .queued(message:) when it is prepared in the background; throw on failure.

states.name: idle
states.description: A button with a download symbol; with several formats, a chevron and a menu.

states.name: preparing
states.description: The button shows a spinner, reads "Preparing CSV…" as its value and does not start a second download; the progress bar shows when progress is given.

states.name: saving
states.description: The system save dialog is open for the prepared file.

states.name: saved
states.description: Back to idle; "CSV downloaded" is announced.

states.name: queued
states.description: A muted note under the button says the file is prepared in the background; it is announced.

states.name: failed
states.description: An inline error with Try again, which repeats the same format; the message is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(true) uses the button's disabled colours.

appearance: The Monarch button of the chosen variant and size, a linear Monarch progress bar under it, the queued note in the caption role and muted text colour, and the inline error row in the danger tone, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: On the web onDownload saves the file through the browser. On iOS a file needs a place to go, so returning .file(url) opens the system save dialog (fileExporter), and an app that shares instead (ShareLink, a share sheet) returns .downloaded. A cancelled save dialog returns to idle without a message. The web passes the format id to onDownload; iOS passes the whole format. Android ships MonarchDownloadReportButton.
accessibility: The button is a standard Button or Menu with a 44-point touch target; the icons are decorative.
While the file is prepared the button's value is "Preparing CSV…".
Preparing, saved, queued and failed are announced with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement.
The progress bar is named "Download progress" and reads its percentage (system behaviour).
A failure is an inline error with text, an icon and a Try again button, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A progress value outside 0 to 1 is clamped; a value that is not finite is not drawn.
Only one download runs at a time; activating the button again while it is busy does nothing.
The saved file's content type comes from its extension (csv, pdf, xlsx), or plain data.
The menu is disabled while a download runs.
The save dialog, its cancellation and the announcements were compiled and unit-tested as state logic but not run on a device.

name: MonarchDragHandle
title: DragHandle
wrapsNative: Shape (grip dots), accessibilityActions(_:), accessibilityValue(_:); the caller attaches gesture(_:) or draggable(_:)
summary: The grip an item is dragged by: a dotted glyph in a 44-point touch target with a spoken name, idle, grabbed and dropped states, and move actions for VoiceOver and Switch Control.
whenToUse: When you build a drag interaction outside a List (a board column, a canvas, a custom stack) and need the handle part with an accessible way to move the item.
whenNotToUse: In a List, use the system reordering with onMove(perform:), which brings its own handle and accessibility.
api: MonarchDragHandle.init(_ label: String, state: MonarchDragHandleState = .idle, axis: MonarchDragHandleAxis = .vertical, size: MonarchDragHandleSize = .md, hint: String? = nil, actionLabels: [MonarchDragHandleDirection: String] = [:], stateLabels: [MonarchDragHandleState: String] = [:], onMove: (@MainActor (MonarchDragHandleDirection) -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchDragHandleState { case idle, grabbed, dropped }
enum MonarchDragHandleAxis { case vertical, horizontal, both }
enum MonarchDragHandleSize { case sm, md }
enum MonarchDragHandleDirection { case up, down, backward, forward }

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name, naming the item: "Reorder Design review".

options.name: state
options.description: idle, grabbed or dropped. The view that moves items owns it.

options.name: axis
options.description: vertical, horizontal or both. Selects the grip pattern and the move actions.

options.name: size
options.description: sm: 24 points. md: 32 points. The touch target is 44 points at both.

options.name: hint
options.description: A spoken hint, already localised.

options.name: actionLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in action names "Move up", "Move down", "Move backward", "Move forward".

options.name: stateLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken values "Picked up" and "Dropped".

options.name: onMove
options.description: Moves the item one step. Without it the handle offers no actions.

states.name: idle
states.description: Muted grip dots, no fill.

states.name: grabbed
states.description: Accent subtle fill, accent strong dots and a 1-point accent outline. Spoken value "Picked up".

states.name: dropped
states.description: Success subtle fill and success strong dots, as a brief confirmation. Spoken value "Dropped".

states.name: disabled
states.description: Dots in the disabled text role and no actions, with the standard disabled(_:) modifier.

appearance: The dots use the muted text role at rest, the accent roles while grabbed and the success roles when dropped, in every theme. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: On the web the handle is a button with keyboard instructions and aria-pressed. On iOS it is not a button: activating it does nothing, the drag is a gesture the caller attaches, and assistive technology uses the named move actions instead of arrow keys. The web's hover style and custom icon slot are not offered. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The handle is one element named by label; the grip is decorative.
With onMove, VoiceOver and Switch Control get one named action per direction of the axis: "Move up" and "Move down", "Move backward" and "Move forward", or all four.
The grabbed and dropped states are spoken as the element's value; an idle handle has no value.
The grabbed handle has an outline as well as a colour change.
The touch target is at least 44 by 44 points at both sizes, and the glyph scales with Dynamic Type.
The state change is not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: The handle does not move anything itself and does not announce the new position; post an announcement from onMove.
It installs no gesture. A drag works only when the caller attaches one.
backward and forward are positions in reading order, so they need no change for right-to-left layouts.
An empty override in actionLabels or stateLabels is ignored.

title: Drawer
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:onDismiss:content:) with presentationDetents(_:) and presentationDragIndicator(_:)
summary: A bottom drawer is the system sheet with detents and a visible drag indicator. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a short task or a set of options that should leave part of the screen visible: filters, a picker, details of a map pin. Offer a medium detent, and a large one if the content can grow.
whenNotToUse: For a task that needs the whole screen use a plain sheet or fullScreenCover (see dialog). For choosing one of a few actions use confirmationDialog (see choice-dialog).
api: func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> some View) -> some View
func presentationDetents(_ detents: Set<PresentationDetent>) -> some View
func presentationDragIndicator(_ visibility: Visibility) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View

states.name: medium
states.description: The sheet covers about half the screen; the content behind is dimmed.

states.name: large
states.description: Dragging the indicator up grows the sheet to full height, when the large detent is offered.

states.name: dragged down
states.description: Dragging down past the smallest detent closes the sheet, unless interactiveDismissDisabled is set.

appearance: The system draws the sheet's card, its corner radius, the grab handle and the dimming in every theme. The content is the app's: give it a theme background such as bgRaised and it follows the four themes.
platformNotes: The web Drawer is a bottom panel for phones with a grab handle and dragToClose, built on the web Sheet. On iOS it is the same sheet as any other, sized with detents; the grab handle is presentationDragIndicator(.visible), and dragToClose={false} is interactiveDismissDisabled(). Detents can also be a fixed height or a fraction. On an iPad at regular width the sheet is centred and detents have no effect. Android uses ModalBottomSheet.
accessibility: System behaviour: the sheet is modal and confines VoiceOver, Switch Control and keyboard focus.
System behaviour: the drag indicator is an adjustable element; VoiceOver swipes up and down to change the detent.
System behaviour: the escape gesture closes the sheet.
Keep a visible button that closes the drawer, so closing does not depend on a drag.
edgeCases: A scroll view inside a sheet with several detents first grows the sheet and then scrolls.
With interactiveDismissDisabled and no close button the drawer cannot be closed.
On a phone in landscape a medium detent is as tall as the screen.

title: DropZone
wrapsNative: .dropDestination(for:action:isTargeted:) on the region, with a Transferable that has a FileRepresentation; .fileImporter (through MonarchFileUpload) as the path that always works
summary: SwiftUI's drop destination on an existing region, such as a file list or a conversation, so files can be dropped where they belong, with the same checks as MonarchFileUpload and its picker button as the path that works everywhere. Monarch ships no type.
whenToUse: On iPad and Mac, when a file list, a folder or a conversation should also accept files dragged from another app. Always keep a visible button that opens the system picker.
whenNotToUse: For a form field that takes files, use MonarchFileUpload, which already accepts drops on its own area. On iPhone, where drag and drop between apps is limited, the picker button alone is the expected path.
api: func dropDestination<T: Transferable>(for payloadType: T.Type = T.self, action: @escaping ([T], CGPoint) -> Bool, isTargeted: @escaping (Bool) -> Void = { _ in }) -> some View

static func MonarchFileUpload.validate(_ files: [MonarchFileUploadFile], allowedContentTypes: [UTType] = [.item], maxSize: Int64? = nil, maxFiles: Int? = nil, currentCount: Int = 0, labels: MonarchFileUploadLabels = MonarchFileUploadLabels(), locale: Locale = .autoupdatingCurrent, validate: (@Sendable (MonarchFileUploadFile) -> String?)? = nil) -> (accepted: [MonarchFileUploadFile], rejected: [MonarchFileUploadRejection])

states.name: idle
states.description: The region looks as it always does; the MonarchFileUpload button above it is the visible way in.

states.name: targeted
states.description: isTargeted reports true while files are held over the region: draw the container shape in the accent subtle fill with the accent border.

states.name: refused
states.description: MonarchFileUpload.validate returns the refused files with a message each; show them in a danger MonarchInlineNotice and announce the count.

states.name: full or disabled
states.description: Return false from the action without taking the files, and disable the picker button with disabled(_:).

appearance: The region keeps its own look. While files are held over it, it gets the accent subtle fill and the accent border on the container shape; refusals use the danger notice. The roles follow light, dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web DropZone is a component that listens to the region or the whole window, shows an overlay while files are dragged, and refuses a wrong type before the drop. On iOS the system drop destination does this: the region is the view the modifier is on, and a whole-screen zone is the modifier on the screen's root view. The dragged type is known only after the drop, so refusals come then, through MonarchFileUpload.validate with the same messages as MonarchFileUpload. Dropped files arrive as a temporary copy through a FileRepresentation and are deleted by the system after the import, so the Transferable copies them first. Dragging files between apps is an iPad and Mac interaction; the picker is the main path on iPhone. Android uses Modifier.dragAndDropTarget with the same rules.
accessibility: Dragging is an extra: the MonarchFileUpload picker button is a standard button with a 44-point target, and is how VoiceOver, Switch Control and keyboard users add files.
The targeted state is a fill and a border, and the button keeps its text, so nothing relies on colour alone.
After a drop, post an announcement with the number of files added and refused, because focus does not move.
edgeCases: Two drop destinations nested in each other: the innermost takes the drop. Do not put a drop destination around a MonarchFileUpload, which has its own.
A drop of several files where some are refused: add the accepted ones and list the refused ones; do not refuse the whole drop.
Delete the temporary copies after uploading them.

title: DropdownMenu
wrapsNative: Menu, with Button, Toggle, Picker, Section, Divider and a nested Menu as its items; buttonStyle(.monarch()) on the Menu for the trigger
summary: A list of actions that opens from a button is the standard SwiftUI Menu. Monarch ships nothing; the trigger takes the Monarch button style.
whenToUse: For several related actions behind one button, such as Actions or a More button on a row. Put a Toggle in the menu for an item that is on or off, a Picker for one choice out of several, and a Menu for a submenu.
whenNotToUse: Not for choosing a form value on its own (use a Picker with the menu style). For actions on a row or card the person presses and holds, use contextMenu, which takes the same items. For a destructive action that needs confirming, use confirmationDialog.

Button(_ title: String, systemImage: String, role: ButtonRole? = nil, action: () -> Void)
Toggle(_ title: String, isOn: Binding<Bool>)
Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<SelectionValue>, content: () -> Content)
func contextMenu<MenuItems: View>(menuItems: () -> MenuItems) -> some View

states.name: open
states.description: The system draws the menu next to the trigger and dims nothing. A tap outside closes it.

states.name: checked
states.description: A Toggle that is on, and the selected option of a Picker, show a checkmark before the title.

states.name: destructive
states.description: A Button with the destructive role is drawn in the system's red.

states.name: disabled
states.description: An item with disabled(true) is dimmed and cannot be chosen.

platformNotes: The web builds DropdownMenu from Radix parts (content, item, checkbox item, radio item, label, separator, submenu). On iOS each part is a standard view inside Menu: Button, Toggle, Picker, Section with a header, Divider and a nested Menu. The web item's tone danger is role: .destructive, its icon is systemImage, and its shortcut is keyboardShortcut, which the system shows when a hardware keyboard is attached. Items cannot be given custom layouts or Monarch colours. Android uses the Material 3 DropdownMenu in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: the trigger is a button, and the items are read in order with their checked state.
System behaviour: the menu is dismissed with the escape gesture or a tap outside, and focus returns to the trigger.
An icon-only trigger needs a label: use Label("Actions", systemImage:) with labelStyle(.iconOnly) or accessibilityLabel.
The system gives each item a row at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: The system may reverse the order of items when the menu opens upwards; set menuOrder(.fixed) to keep the order.
A menu closes after any item is chosen, including a Toggle; set menuActionDismissBehavior(.disabled) on an item that should keep it open.
primaryAction on Menu makes a tap run an action and a long press open the menu, which is the split-button behaviour.

summary: Likely duplicates of a record, why each one matched, and buttons to open, merge or dismiss each one.
whenToUse: Under a create form while the person types, or on a record screen, when the app has found records that may be the same.
whenNotToUse: For the merge itself, present your own merge screen from onMerge. For a single validation message, use MonarchInlineNotice.

options.name: matches
options.description: The likely duplicates. Nothing is drawn when it is empty.

options.name: footer
options.description: A closing line, for example "You can still create it."

options.name: variant
options.description: hint is a warning box that is announced; panel is a plain section.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in heading.

options.name: openLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Open" title.

options.name: mergeLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Merge" title.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Not a duplicate" title.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a match. No button without it.

options.name: onMerge
options.description: Merges a match. No button without it.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Says a match is not a duplicate. No button without it.

states.name: one match
states.description: The heading is singular.

states.name: several matches
states.description: The heading is plural, with one card per match.

states.name: no matches
states.description: Nothing is drawn and no space is taken.

appearance: The hint is a container with the warning subtle fill, the warning border and a warning icon beside the heading; the panel has no fill or border. Each match is a MonarchCard without a shadow, with the kind as a neutral badge and the confidence as an outlined warning badge.
platformNotes: The web takes an href per match and opens it in a new tab; here onOpen hands the match to the app, which navigates. The web meta slot takes any content; detail is a String. The heading level option has no equivalent: the heading has the header trait. The heading chooses between a singular and a plural string by count, not by plural rules, so a translation needs only those two forms. The variant names hint and panel are the web's. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (onOpen, onMerge, onDismiss). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onOpen.
accessibility: The heading has the header trait.
The name, badges, reasons and detail of a match are one element.
Each button is read as its title and the name of the record, for example "Merge: Example Ltd".
The hint variant posts an announcement with the heading and the names of the matches when it appears and when the set of matches changes. The panel variant does not.
Buttons have a touch target of at least 44 points and stack vertically when they do not fit on one line.
The confidence is text, so it does not depend on colour.
edgeCases: A score outside 0 through 1 is limited to that range; a not-a-number score is not shown.
Empty reasons are left out; reasons are joined with the list format of the environment's locale.
Matches must have unique ids.
With no action given, a match shows no buttons.

whenNotToUse: For a time of day, use DatePicker with .hourAndMinute. For a handful of fixed lengths (15, 30, 60 minutes), use a segmented Picker. For a plain count, use MonarchNumberInput.
api: init(_ label: String, minutes: Binding<Int?>, minimum: Int = 0, maximum: Int? = nil, step: Int = 15, largestUnit: MonarchDurationInputUnit = .hours, minutesPerDay: Int = 1440, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, showsStepper: Bool = true, labels: MonarchDurationInputLabels = MonarchDurationInputLabels(), format: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, parse: (@Sendable (String) -> Int?)? = nil)
enum MonarchDurationInputUnit { case hours, days }

struct MonarchDurationInputLabels { init(invalid: String? = nil, range: (@Sendable (Int, Int?) -> String)? = nil, valueText: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, errorHint: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: minutes
options.description: The duration in whole minutes, or nil when empty. Written only when the text is read (Return or leaving the field) or stepped, never while typing.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The shortest allowed duration in minutes. Shorter text is flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The longest allowed duration in minutes. Longer text is flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: step
options.description: Minutes added or removed by one press of the stepper or an arrow key.

options.name: largestUnit
options.description: Writes 26 hours as "26h" (.hours) or "1d 2h" (.days).

options.name: minutesPerDay
options.description: Minutes in a "d" when reading and writing; 480 for 8-hour work days.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Replaces the built-in placeholder "e.g. 1h 30m".

options.name: helper
options.description: Supporting text under the field.

options.name: error
options.description: Error message from the app; replaces the helper and the field's own message while present.

options.name: showsStepper
options.description: Shows the system stepper beside the field.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the invalid and range messages, the spoken value and the spoken error prefix.

options.name: format
options.description: Writes minutes as text. The default writes "0m", "45m", "1h 30m".

options.name: parse
options.description: Reads trimmed, non-empty text as minutes, or nil when it cannot be read. Empty text always saves nil.

states.name: empty
states.description: The binding is nil; the placeholder shows in the subtle text colour. The first step starts from the minimum.

states.name: focused
states.description: The theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: unreadable
states.description: Danger border, an icon and "Use a duration like 1h 30m, 90m or 1.5h." under the field. The text stays; the binding keeps its last value.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Danger border, an icon and "Enter between 15m and 2h." (or "at least" / "at most"). Nothing is saved.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the field's own, drawn the same way.

states.name: at a bound
states.description: The half of the stepper that would pass the bound is disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:); keys do nothing.

appearance: The measures and colours of MonarchTextField: a surface fill, an input border and the control radius, with the theme's focus ring and the danger strong role for errors. Digits are monospaced so the value does not shift while it is stepped. The stepper is the system control.
platformNotes: Matches the web's DurationInput: the same forms are read, the same "1h 30m" format is written, the value is whole minutes and unreadable text is kept and flagged, never saved. The web's size option (sm, md, lg) is not offered: the field is always at least 44 points high, like the other Monarch fields. The web steps with ArrowUp and ArrowDown and moves by an hour with PageUp and PageDown; on iOS the system Stepper does the stepping, and with a hardware keyboard the same keys and Escape are handled with onKeyPress. Home and End have no equivalent. With a minimum of 0 and a maximum, the range message is "Enter at most 2h." where the web says "Enter between 0m and 2h.". Unit words are read in English (d, h, m, hours, minutes), as on the web; the spoken value is spelled out by the system's DateComponentsFormatter in the person's language. Android uses the same name and parser. Several closures are optional (format, parse). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is format.
accessibility: The field is one element: the label, the typed text, and the error (spoken as "Error: …") or else the helper as the hint.
A new error is announced when it appears and is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
The stepper is the system control with the same label, the duration spelled out ("1 hour, 30 minutes") as its value, and the increment and decrement actions.
Autocorrection is off so unit letters are not replaced.
The field is at least 44 points high and text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: "1h30" is 90 minutes: a bare number after hours counts as minutes. After any other unit it is unreadable.
"1.5" with no unit is minutes, rounded to 2.
"1:75" and "1:5" are unreadable: a clock needs two-digit minutes below 60.
A step from text that does not read starts from the saved value; from an empty field it starts at the minimum.
A step snaps to the step grid: 50 minutes plus 15 is 1 hour, 50 minus 15 is 45 minutes.
Changing the binding from outside rewrites the text and clears the message.

name: MonarchEditableCell
title: EditableCell
wrapsNative: Button that swaps to TextField with @FocusState for text and number cells; Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) for select cells; DatePicker(displayedComponents: .date) in the compact style for date cells
summary: A table or list cell that edits one value in place, text, number, select or date, with validation, an asynchronous save and an error that keeps the draft.
whenToUse: For one value in a row that people often correct without opening a form: a title, a quantity, a status, a due date. Use it in MonarchDataTable cells and in list rows.
whenNotToUse: For several related fields that change together, push a Form or open a sheet. For a free-text heading on a detail screen, use MonarchInlineEditText.
api: init(_ label: String, value: Binding<MonarchEditableCellValue>, kind: MonarchEditableCellKind = .text, options: [MonarchEditableCellOption] = [], placeholder: String? = nil, minimum: Double? = nil, maximum: Double? = nil, minimumDate: Date? = nil, maximumDate: Date? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, isNumeric: Bool? = nil, startsEditing: Bool = false, savesOnFocusLoss: Bool = true, labels: MonarchEditableCellLabels = MonarchEditableCellLabels(), format: (@MainActor (MonarchEditableCellValue) -> String)? = nil, validate: (@MainActor (MonarchEditableCellValue) -> String?)? = nil, onCancel: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onCommit: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchEditableCellValue) async throws -> Void)
enum MonarchEditableCellKind: String { case text, number, select, date }
enum MonarchEditableCellValue: Hashable { case empty, text(String), number(Double), date(Date); var isEmpty: Bool }
struct MonarchEditableCellOption: Identifiable, Hashable { init(_ label: String, value: String, isDisabled: Bool = false) }

struct MonarchEditableCellLabels { init(edit: String? = nil, saving: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil, save: String? = nil, invalidNumber: String? = nil, required: String? = nil, belowMinimum: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, aboveMaximum: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, noValue: String? = nil, saveFailed: String? = nil, error: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: What the cell holds, for example "Status for Acme". Read by VoiceOver; not drawn.

options.name: value
options.description: The saved value. Written after a successful save.

options.name: kind
options.description: The editor: text field, number field, menu of choices or compact date picker.

options.name: options
options.description: The choices of a select cell; a disabled choice is shown but cannot be chosen.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: The text of an empty cell and the prompt of text and number fields.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The lowest value of a number cell.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The highest value of a number cell.

options.name: minimumDate
options.description: The earliest day of a date cell; also the picker's range.

options.name: maximumDate
options.description: The latest day of a date cell; also the picker's range.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Refuses an empty value. A required select cell offers no None choice.

options.name: isNumeric
options.description: Trailing alignment with tabular figures. nil means number cells only.

options.name: startsEditing
options.description: Opens the text or number field when the cell first appears.

options.name: savesOnFocusLoss
options.description: Leaving a text or number field saves the draft.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: format
options.description: The text of a value in view mode. The default is the option label, the number or day in the locale, or the text.

options.name: validate
options.description: Returns a message to refuse a value before saving.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Runs when the person leaves a field without saving.

options.name: onCommit
options.description: Persists a new value. Not called for an unchanged value. Throw to refuse it with the error's description.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The value as body text, trailing-aligned with tabular figures for numbers; an empty cell shows the placeholder in the subtle colour.

states.name: editing
states.description: Text and number cells: a bordered field with the focus ring and save and cancel icon buttons at its trailing end.

states.name: choosing
states.description: Select cells are always a system menu button showing the current choice; date cells are the compact date picker. Choosing saves at once.

states.name: empty date
states.description: An empty date cell shows the placeholder (or None); touching it shows a picker on today, moved into the range, with save and cancel.

states.name: saving
states.description: A small progress indicator replaces the buttons and the control is disabled; VoiceOver reads Saving.

states.name: invalid
states.description: The field border turns to the danger colour and the message is shown under it with an icon; the draft is kept.

states.name: failed
states.description: The error's description (or Couldn’t save. Try again.) is shown; a typed draft is kept, a chosen value goes back to the saved one.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Plain text in the disabled colour for every kind; no control.

appearance: The value is body text in the default text colour, or the subtle colour when empty and the disabled colour when disabled. The field is a surface-coloured box with the input border, the control radius and the focus ring; errors use the danger strong role. The save glyph uses the accent strong role and the cancel glyph the muted text role. Menus and date pickers are the system controls tinted by the theme. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web cell is a button that opens a text input, a native select or a date input; Enter or F2 opens, Enter saves and Escape cancels. On iOS a touch keyboard has no Escape or F2, so text and number fields carry save and cancel icon buttons (Return saves; a hardware Escape still cancels). Select and date cells use the system menu and compact date picker, which already open on touch, so choosing saves at once; a failed save puts the saved value back instead of keeping an open editor. The web's ISO date strings are Dates at the start of the day in the environment's calendar, and numbers are parsed in the person's locale instead of JavaScript Number(). A non-required date cell is cleared from its context menu. The web's trigger="none" mode for a grid that owns focus is not offered: SwiftUI lists have no cell focus model; use startsEditing for a row that was just added. Android has no editable cell yet. Several closures are optional (format, validate, onCancel). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is format.
accessibility: In view mode a text, number or empty date cell is one button: the label, then the shown value (or the placeholder) as the value, then "Edit" as the hint.
The field, the menu and the date picker carry the label; the menu and the picker keep their system roles and values.
An error is announced when it appears, spoken as the editor's hint ("Error: …") and shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
While a save runs the field's spoken value is "Saving" and the progress indicator is named "Saving".
The save and cancel icon buttons are named "Save" and "Cancel" and have 44-point touch targets; every cell is at least 44 points high.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; numbers keep tabular figures.
edgeCases: A value equal to the saved one closes the editor without calling onCommit; empty text and .empty count as equal, and dates are compared by day.
A draft that has just been refused or failed is not saved again when focus leaves the field.
A second save and Cancel are ignored while a save runs.
Number drafts accept the locale's grouping and decimal separators and ignore spaces; anything else is refused with Enter a number.
A select value that matches no option is shown as its raw text.
startsEditing formats a number draft in the current locale, because the environment is not available before the view appears.

name: MonarchEditorToolbar
title: EditorToolbar
wrapsNative: Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton) and Button per tool, Menu with a Picker for the text style, alert with a TextField for links, in a horizontal ScrollView; placed with ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .keyboard)
summary: A formatting toolbar for a text editor: undo and redo, a text style menu, inline styles, lists, quotes, code and links, plus product controls.
whenToUse: Above the keyboard or above an editor where people format rich text, such as notes, comments or documents.
whenNotToUse: Not for a plain text field (no formatting) and not for the actions of a screen (use the navigation bar's toolbar items).
api: init(groups: [[MonarchEditorTool]] = MonarchEditorTool.defaultGroups, active: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = [], disabled: Set<MonarchEditorTool> = [], labels: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), onLink: (@MainActor (URL?) -> Void)? = nil, action: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchEditorTool) -> Void)

enum MonarchEditorTool: Hashable { case undo, redo, paragraph, heading(Int), bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link, bulletList, orderedList, taskList, blockquote, codeBlock, custom(id: String, title: String, systemImage: String); static let defaultGroups: [[MonarchEditorTool]]; static let inlineGroups: [[MonarchEditorTool]] }

struct MonarchEditorToolbarLabels { init(toolbar: String? = nil, tools: [MonarchEditorTool: String] = [:], textStyle: String? = nil, linkTitle: String? = nil, linkAddress: String? = nil, linkApply: String? = nil, linkRemove: String? = nil, linkCancel: String? = nil, linkHelp: String? = nil) }

options.name: groups
options.description: The tools in groups separated by dividers. Neighbouring paragraph and heading tools become one text style menu. MonarchEditorTool.inlineGroups gives inline formatting only.

options.name: active
options.description: The formats that are on at the caret or selection, and the current text style. The app's editor works these out.

options.name: disabled
options.description: Tools that cannot be used now, such as undo with nothing to undo.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the toolbar name, every tool name (by tool), the text style menu and the link form.

options.name: onLink
options.description: Makes the link tool open a form for the address. Receives a safe URL to apply, or nil when Remove link is pressed. Without it, the link tool goes to action.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when a tool is pressed or a text style is chosen. The app applies it to its editor.

states.name: on
states.description: A toggle whose format is active has the accent fill and border of the Monarch toggle button style.

states.name: disabled tool
states.description: Drawn in the disabled colours and cannot be pressed.

states.name: link form
states.description: A system alert with an address field, Apply (disabled until the address is valid), Remove link when a link is active, and Cancel.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every control is disabled, for example while the editor loads.

appearance: Small ghost Monarch buttons and toggle buttons with SF Symbols, separated by thin dividers in the subtle border role, in a row that scrolls sideways. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web toolbar drives a Tiptap editor directly. iOS has no Monarch rich text editor yet, so this toolbar is editor-agnostic: the app passes which formats are on and applies what is pressed (for example to an AttributedString in its own editor). Headings are one text style menu instead of a button per level, to fit a phone. The link popover is a system alert with a text field. The web's arrow-key roving focus and keyboard shortcut hints are not offered; iOS moves through the controls with VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access, and hardware shortcuts belong to the app's text view.
accessibility: The toolbar is a container named "Formatting".
Format tools are standard toggles with the Monarch toggle button style, so VoiceOver reads their name and on or off value; the on state is also a filled surface.
Undo, redo and product tools are standard buttons named by their title.
The text style menu is a standard menu named "Text style" whose value is the current style; its entries are a picker with a check mark on the current one.
Group dividers are hidden from VoiceOver.
Every control has a 44-point touch target; icons have spoken names through their Label titles.
edgeCases: Empty groups are dropped, so two dividers never meet.
Heading levels outside 1 through 6 use the level 6 symbol.
A link typed as a bare domain becomes https; an email becomes mailto; javascript, data and other schemes are refused.

name: MonarchEmailVerificationBanner
title: EmailVerificationBanner
wrapsNative: The MonarchCalloutBanner surface and tokens with MonarchButton actions in a MonarchFlowLayout, a task(id:) countdown and AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: A notice that the email address is not verified yet, with the address, a Resend button that waits out a cooldown, and an optional Change email button.
whenToUse: While a signed-in person has not verified their email address, or after they changed it and the new one is not verified.
whenNotToUse: On the verification screen itself, where entering a code is the task, use MonarchOtpPinInput. For general notices, use MonarchCalloutBanner.
api: init(email: String, tone: MonarchTone = .warning, placement: MonarchCalloutBannerPlacement = .section, cooldownSeconds: Int = 60, initialCooldown: Int = 0, labels: MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels = MonarchEmailVerificationBannerLabels(), onChangeEmail: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onResend: @escaping @MainActor () async throws -> Void)

options.name: email
options.description: The address waiting for verification, shown in the message.

options.name: tone
options.description: warning when features are locked until verified; info when nothing is blocked yet. Other tones draw as warning.

options.name: placement
options.description: A rounded callout in the content, or a full-width strip for safeAreaInset(edge: .top).

options.name: cooldownSeconds
options.description: Seconds before another send after a successful one.

options.name: initialCooldown
options.description: Seconds already remaining when the banner appears, for example right after sign-up sent the first email.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, message, button titles, the sent line, the dismiss name and the fallback error.

options.name: onChangeEmail
options.description: Shows a Change email button.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a dismiss button. The banner does not hide itself; remove it here.

options.name: onResend
options.description: Sends the email again. Throwing shows the error's description (or the fallback) and starts no cooldown.

states.name: ready
states.description: Resend email can be used.

states.name: sending
states.description: The resend button shows its spinner; taps do nothing.

states.name: sent
states.description: A check and "Verification email sent" in the strong success colour, announced; the cooldown starts.

states.name: cooldown
states.description: The button reads "Resend in 42s", counts down every second and is disabled until 0.

states.name: error
states.description: An icon and the failure in the strong danger colour, announced; Resend is available at once.

appearance: The same surface as MonarchCalloutBanner: the subtle fill and border of the warning or info tone with its icon in the strong colour, rounded in a section, a strip with a line below on a page. Resend is a small secondary button, Change email a small ghost button.
platformNotes: The web also exports useResendCooldown for other resend controls; on iOS the cooldown logic is internal (MonarchResendCooldownState) and should be promoted if another component needs it. On the web the cooldown button keeps focus with aria-disabled; on iOS it is disabled, which VoiceOver still reaches and reads as dimmed. The web's landmark and actionPlacement props have no iOS equivalent. The parity map names MonarchBanner; the component reuses MonarchCalloutBanner's tokens instead, because MonarchBanner and MonarchCalloutBanner have one action and this banner needs two. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (onChangeEmail, onDismiss). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onChangeEmail.
accessibility: The icon, title and message are one element read as the tone name, the title and the message with the address.
Resend, Change email and Dismiss are separate buttons with 44-point touch targets.
During the cooldown the resend button is disabled; VoiceOver reads it as dimmed with the seconds left in its title.
"Verification email sent" and failures are posted as announcements; both have an icon and text.
The address is part of the message text, not only shown visually.
edgeCases: Long addresses wrap inside the message.
The countdown runs while the banner is on screen; a banner removed and shown again starts from initialCooldown.
An error without a LocalizedError description shows the fallback text.

name: MonarchEmbedBlock
title: EmbedBlock
wrapsNative: WKWebView in a UIViewRepresentable (NSViewRepresentable on the macOS host) with a non-persistent WKWebsiteDataStore and a WKNavigationDelegate allow-list; MonarchLinkCard for other links and MonarchInlineNotice for unusable ones
summary: Shows a video, design or demo from an allow-listed site in a web view, and any other web link as a link card; only a provider's own embed address is ever loaded.
whenToUse: In a document or a post where someone pastes a link to a video (YouTube, Vimeo, Loom), a design (Figma) or a code demo (CodePen) that should play or be explored in place.
whenNotToUse: Not for arbitrary web pages (use MonarchLinkCard or open the link in SFSafariViewController), not for the app's own video (use AVKit's VideoPlayer) and not for a link preview with an image (use MonarchLinkCard).
api: init(url: String, caption: String? = nil, title: String? = nil, providers: [MonarchEmbedProvider] = MonarchEmbedProvider.defaults, requiresTapToLoad: Bool = false, labels: MonarchEmbedBlockLabels = MonarchEmbedBlockLabels())
static func resolve(_ url: String, providers: [MonarchEmbedProvider] = MonarchEmbedProvider.defaults) -> MonarchEmbedResolution
MonarchEmbedProvider.init(id: String, name: String, hosts: [String], aspectRatio: CGFloat = MonarchEmbedProvider.videoAspectRatio, embedURL: @escaping @Sendable (URL) -> URL?)
static let MonarchEmbedProvider.defaults: [MonarchEmbedProvider]
static let MonarchEmbedProvider.videoAspectRatio: CGFloat
static let MonarchEmbedProvider.documentAspectRatio: CGFloat
enum MonarchEmbedResolution { case frame(url: URL, embedURL: URL, provider: MonarchEmbedProvider); case link(url: URL, host: String); case invalid(String); var kind: MonarchEmbedResolutionKind }
enum MonarchEmbedResolutionKind { case frame, link, invalid }
struct MonarchEmbedBlockLabels { init(frameTitle: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, load: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, invalid: String? = nil) }

options.name: url
options.description: The URL someone pasted: a share link, not an embed code. Spaces around it are ignored.

options.name: caption
options.description: Shown under the content in the muted text colour, and the spoken name of the web view when there is no title. For a link card it is also the card's title.

options.name: title
options.description: The spoken name of the web view when it differs from the caption.

options.name: providers
options.description: The sites that may be shown in a web view: YouTube (as youtube-nocookie.com), Vimeo, Loom, Figma and CodePen by default. Each has exact hosts, an aspect ratio and a function that gives its https embed address.

options.name: requiresTapToLoad
options.description: Whether nothing is loaded from the site until the person taps "Load YouTube content".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken name of the web view, the load button and the message for an unusable link.

states.name: frame
states.description: An https link with no port on an allow-listed host with an embeddable form: a web view at the provider's aspect ratio (16:9 for video, 4:3 for Figma and CodePen) on the subtle fill, with a subtle border.

states.name: waiting for a tap
states.description: With requiresTapToLoad, a placeholder with a play symbol and a load button in place of the web view.

states.name: link
states.description: Any other http or https link: MonarchLinkCard with the host (without www.) and the full URL.

states.name: invalid
states.description: Another scheme, a relative or malformed URL, or a URL with a user name or password: MonarchInlineNotice "This link can't be shown." in the warning tone.

appearance: The web view sits on the subtle background fill inside a container shape with a subtle border; the caption uses the muted text colour. The site's own page decides the colours inside the web view and does not follow the Monarch theme or high contrast.
platformNotes: The web uses a sandboxed iframe with the provider's allow attributes. On iOS the plan named WKWebView, or SwiftUI's WebView on iOS 26; the package targets iOS 17, so it is a WKWebView in a representable. The sandbox is replaced by: a non-persistent website data store, no windows opened by script, media that waits for a tap and plays inline, a navigation policy that keeps the main frame on the embed's host and opens tapped links elsewhere in the browser, and https only for frames inside the embed. The request carries the app's bundle id as an https Referer, which video sites ask of apps. requiresTapToLoad has no web equivalent; the web lazy-loads the frame. The web's Tiptap editor extension (URL field and caption field) is not part of the iOS component: an app's editor composes MonarchTextField with this view. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The web view is a container named by title, then caption, then "YouTube content"; the site's page supplies the elements inside it.
The load button reads "Load YouTube content" and has a 44-point touch target.
A link card is read as MonarchLinkCard: one link with the title, site and URL.
An unusable link is a notice with a warning icon and text, not colour alone.
The caption scales with Dynamic Type; the web view keeps its aspect ratio at every text size.
edgeCases: An allow-listed host over http, with a port, or with a path that has no embed form (for example youtube.com/feed) becomes a link card, never a web view.
A provider whose embed address is not https is ignored for that URL.
A YouTube id must be 11 letters, digits, - or _; a Loom id 16 to 64 hexadecimal digits.
The web view does not scroll on its own; its content is sized by the aspect ratio.
Matrix fixtures and examples use requiresTapToLoad, so tests never reach the network; the loaded web view is checked by its configuration and navigation policy.

whenNotToUse: To open another app, use a Link or openURL. For web content from a third party, use MonarchEmbedBlock. For a card of your own content, use MonarchCard.

The contract is a browser one, so on iOS the frame draws no web content itself: the app shows the screen natively or in its own web view and sets the state. "Open in a new tab" becomes "Open page", which opens the page with the system. Android does not ship this component.

whenNotToUse: In a text field, the system keyboard's emoji key already offers every emoji; do not add a picker beside it. For a fixed set of reactions, use a Menu of Buttons (see MonarchCallControls).

options.name: maxRecents

states.name: browsing
states.description: The search row, the category bar and the grid of sections with headings; the current category button has the emphasis fill.

states.name: searching
states.description: The category bar is hidden and one section, Search results, lists the matches; the count is announced.

states.name: no results
states.description: "No emoji found" in the muted text colour.

states.name: skin tone

states.name: disabled

appearance: The search row uses the text field's fill and input border; headings use the caption role in the muted text colour; the selected category has the emphasis background; emoji are drawn by the system in the title type role, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: iOS has no emoji picker outside the keyboard, so Monarch draws one and ships the same 517-emoji index as the web. The planned .searchable is not used: it needs a navigation bar, which a picker in a popover or inline does not have, so the picker draws its own search row from the text field tokens. The web keyboard navigation (arrow keys, Home, End, Page Up and Down) and the hover preview are not offered; VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access move between the buttons. The current category follows taps on the category bar, not scrolling. EmojiPickerPopover maps to presenting the picker with popover(isPresented:) or sheet(isPresented:). Android's plan covers it with the platform's emoji picker instead.
accessibility: The picker is a container named "Emoji picker".
Each emoji is a button named by its name ("thumbs up"), not read as the character.
Category buttons are named by category; the current one has the selected trait and a fill, so it is not shown by colour alone.
Section headings have the header trait.
The skin tone menu is named "Skin tone" with the tone's name as its value, and offers a standard inline picker.
The number of results is announced after each change to the search.
Cells, category buttons and the clear button are at least 44 points and grow with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A recent emoji missing from the categories is shown and read as itself.
Duplicate emoji across categories appear once in search results.
The grid is about 288 points high, scaled with Dynamic Type; it scrolls.
Names and keywords of the built-in index are English data, not built-in strings; pass categories for another language.
Flags and some newer emoji depend on the system's emoji font.
The announcement after each keystroke and the scroll to a category were compiled and unit-tested as logic but not checked with VoiceOver on a device.

name: MonarchEmptyState
title: EmptyState
wrapsNative: VStack, Image, Text
summary: What will appear in an empty view and the action that creates it, with Monarch's type, colours and buttons.
whenToUse: When a list, a screen or a card has nothing in it: before anything was created, when filters hide everything, or when everything is done.
whenNotToUse: When the region failed to load, use MonarchErrorState. For search with no results, the system ContentUnavailableView.search is also a good fit.
api: init(_ title: String, message: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, kind: MonarchEmptyStateKind = .firstRun, size: MonarchEmptyStateSize = .md, tip: String? = nil, tipKey: String? = nil, actionTitle: String? = nil, secondaryActionTitle: String? = nil, clearFiltersLabel: String? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, secondaryAction: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onClearFilters: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchEmptyStateKind { case firstRun, filtered, success }
enum MonarchEmptyStateSize { case sm, md, lg }

options.name: title
options.description: What is empty.

options.name: message
options.description: What will appear here, or what to do next.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the SF Symbol of the kind.

options.name: kind
options.description: Why the view is empty. Selects the default icon and its colour.

options.name: size
options.description: sm is a tight block, md sits in a card or list, lg fills the height and centres itself.

options.name: tip
options.description: A short hint under the buttons.

options.name: actionTitle
options.description: Title of the main button. No button without it.

options.name: secondaryActionTitle
options.description: Title of the second button. No button without it.

options.name: clearFiltersLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Clear filters" title.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when the main button is activated.

options.name: secondaryAction
options.description: Runs when the second button is activated.

options.name: onClearFilters
options.description: Clears the app's filters. With the filtered kind it adds a button before the others.

options.name: tipKey
options.description: A key named in the tip, drawn as a key cap where it first appears.

states.name: first run
states.description: A tray icon in the muted text colour.

states.name: filtered
states.description: A filter icon, and a "Clear filters" button when onClearFilters is given.

states.name: success
states.description: A check mark icon in the success colour.

appearance: Centred icon, title in the default text colour and message in the muted text colour, in one centred column (as the web). The icon is muted, or the strong success colour for the success kind. The main button is the primary Monarch button, clear filters is secondary and the second action is ghost.
platformNotes: Drawn by Monarch as on the web (a 20 point glyph on a 40 point rounded tile, 8 points between title and message, 32 points above and below), not by ContentUnavailableView, which scales any icon to its own large size. Up to two actions by title and closure instead of the web's actions slot; the web children slot (extra content after the actions) is not offered. The web's line layout (one row with icon, text and actions) is not offered. Web sizes compact, inline and page are sm, md and lg here. tip is a String, so it cannot hold a keyboard-shortcut element. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (action, secondaryAction, onClearFilters). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is action.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
The icon is hidden from VoiceOver; the title and message carry the meaning.
Buttons are standard buttons with the Monarch style and touch targets of at least 44 points.
Title, message, icon and buttons scale with Dynamic Type; text wraps.
edgeCases: actionTitle without action, or action without actionTitle, shows no button.
onClearFilters is ignored unless kind is filtered.
With size lg the state takes all the height it is offered; put it in a container with a bounded height, not directly in a ScrollView.

name: MonarchEntityPicker
title: EntityPicker
wrapsNative: Button field that presents a .sheet with a NavigationStack, a List of Buttons with MonarchAvatar and .searchable(text:placement:prompt:); a debounced search runs in .task(id:)
summary: A field for picking one or several people or records from a list that can be searched on the app's server, shown with avatars, in a sheet.
whenToUse: For an owner, an assignee, reviewers, a company or a project, where people recognise the entity by its name and picture and the list may be too long to load at once.
whenNotToUse: Not for plain text values (use MonarchCombobox), not for several plain values (use MonarchMultiSelect), and not for a few fixed choices (use Picker).

struct MonarchEntityPickerLabels: Sendable { init(select: String? = nil, search: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil, done: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, tooShort: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, failed: String? = nil, create: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, summary: (@Sendable (String, Int) -> String)? = nil, clear: String? = nil, noSelection: String? = nil, field: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the field and is the title of the sheet.

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen id, or the chosen ids in pick order. The array form lets several be picked and keeps the sheet open until Done.

options.name: entities
options.description: The entities to pick from: id, name, description, hint, a picture (image or url), systemImage, shape, keywords, isDisabled, group (a heading) and status (a presence dot). With search, shown until the first search runs.

options.name: selectedEntities
options.description: Entities for chosen ids that may not be in entities, so the field can show their names and pictures.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in the field while nothing is chosen. "Select…" when nil.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the field, also read as the hint.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown with an icon and announced.

options.name: clearOptionTitle
options.description: Single choice only. Adds a first row that clears the selection, such as "Unassigned". Hidden while searching.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows a progress row while entities is empty.

options.name: minSearchLength
options.description: The shortest text search runs for. Shorter text shows "Type at least N characters to search."

options.name: debounce
options.description: How long to wait after typing before search runs. A newer text cancels the wait and the older search.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: search
options.description: Loads the entities matching the trimmed text. Throw to show "The results could not be loaded." with Try again. Without it, entities are filtered by name, hint and keywords.

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Offers "Create “text”" when no shown name equals the typed text. The returned entity is chosen; nil chooses nothing.

states.name: empty
states.description: The field shows the prompt in the subtle text colour.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The field shows the avatar and name, or "First +N" for several, and a clear button.

states.name: searching
states.description: The list shows a progress row while the search waits or runs.

states.name: too short
states.description: The list asks for more characters and does not search.

states.name: failed
states.description: The list shows the error with a Try again button that reruns the same text.

states.name: no match
states.description: The list shows "No matches", or the create row when there is a create handler.

states.name: error
states.description: The border takes the danger colour and the message shows under the field with an icon.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Text takes the disabled colours and the field does nothing. A disabled entity's row is dimmed and cannot be chosen.

appearance: The field has the input background and border of a text field, with a small avatar before the name. Rows show a medium avatar, the name in the default text colour, the description and hint in the muted colour, and an accent-strong check mark when chosen. Dark and high-contrast themes resolve the same roles.
platformNotes: The web opens a popover under a trigger; on iPhone the list opens in a sheet with the system search field, the pattern of Mail and Contacts pickers. The web's custom trigger, renderOption, renderValue, footer and sm/md/lg sizes are not offered: rows are fixed avatar rows with 44-point targets, and a footer action belongs in the screen or the sheet's toolbar. Search is an async closure cancelled through Swift task cancellation instead of an AbortSignal. Android uses the same name and a bottom sheet. Several closures are optional (search, onCreate). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is search.
accessibility: The field is one button labelled with the field's label; its value is every chosen name joined with commas, or "None".
The hint reads the error ("Error: …"), the help text and "Required", each when present; a new error is announced.
Avatars are decorative, because the name is written beside them.
The clear button is a separate button named "Clear".
Each row is a button read with its name, description and hint; chosen rows have the selected trait and a check mark.
Rows, the field and the clear button are at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: A chosen id that is in neither entities nor selectedEntities, and was not picked in this session, shows the raw id.
An answer that arrives after the text changed is dropped, because the task that asked for it was cancelled.
Long names wrap in the field and in the rows.
Picking a chosen row in the multiple form removes it.

title: ErrorPage
wrapsNative: MonarchErrorState (ContentUnavailableView) with size .lg in a frame that fills the screen on the canvas background
summary: A recipe, not a component: a whole screen that failed (not found, forbidden, server error, offline or maintenance) as MonarchErrorState filling the screen.
whenToUse: When a whole destination cannot be shown: a deep link to something deleted, a screen the person may not see, the service down for maintenance.
whenNotToUse: For a part of a screen that failed, use MonarchErrorState at its normal size or MonarchInlineErrorRetry. For an empty list, use MonarchEmptyState.
api: MonarchErrorState(_ title: String, message: String?, kind: MonarchErrorStateKind, size: .lg, requestID: String?, isRetrying: Bool, actionTitle: String?, onRetry: (() -> Void)?, action: (() -> Void)?).frame(maxWidth: .infinity, maxHeight: .infinity).background(theme.colors.bgCanvas)

options.name: actionVariant
options.description: How the second button is drawn.

options.name: secondaryActionTitle / secondaryAction
