states.name: not found and forbidden
states.description: kind .notFound or .forbidden: no retry button; offer a way out with actionTitle and action.

states.name: server, offline and maintenance
states.description: kind .server, .offline or .maintenance: a retry button with onRetry; isRetrying makes it busy.

states.name: with a request id

appearance: The large empty-state layout of MonarchErrorState centred on the canvas background, with the kind's icon, the title, the message and the buttons.
platformNotes: The web ErrorPage is a component with a large faint numeral (404, 403, 500), an optional brand above, a support slot, a copy button for the request id and a retry when the browser comes back online. On iOS a destination that fails is a screen inside the app's navigation, so the recipe fills it with MonarchErrorState; the numeral is left out because it means little in an app, and the title says what happened. To retry when the network returns, watch NWPathMonitor in the app and call the same retry. Android shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: The title has the header trait and the icon is hidden from VoiceOver (MonarchErrorState).
The retry and action buttons are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets; while retrying, the retry button reads "Retrying".
To have VoiceOver start at the title after navigation, post AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged when the screen appears.
edgeCases: Keep the message to what the person can do next; do not show raw error text.
In a sheet, apply the same frame so the state is centred in the sheet.

name: MonarchErrorState
title: ErrorState
wrapsNative: VStack, Image, Text
summary: A region failed to load: what failed, why in plain words, and a retry button, in the layout of MonarchEmptyState.
whenToUse: When a screen, a list or a card could not load its content and nothing can be shown in its place.
whenNotToUse: For a compact row inside a card, or above stale data that is still shown, use MonarchInlineErrorRetry. For an empty result, use MonarchEmptyState.
api: init(_ title: String, message: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, kind: MonarchErrorStateKind = .error, size: MonarchEmptyStateSize = .md, requestID: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, retryLabel: String? = nil, retryingLabel: String? = nil, requestIDLabel: String? = nil, actionTitle: String? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchErrorStateKind { case error, forbidden, notFound, offline, server, maintenance }

options.name: title
options.description: What failed.

options.name: message
options.description: Why, in plain words, and what to do.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the SF Symbol of the kind.

options.name: kind
options.description: Selects the icon, its colour and whether a retry is offered.

options.name: size
options.description: The same sizes as MonarchEmptyState.

options.name: requestID
options.description: The id of the failed request, shown in the code type role under the buttons.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Shows the retry button as busy; its action does not run.

options.name: retryLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Try again" title.

options.name: retryingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Retrying" spoken value.

options.name: requestIDLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Request ID" text.

options.name: actionTitle
options.description: Title of a second button, such as "Contact support". No button without it.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Runs when the retry button is activated. No retry button without it.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when the second button is activated.

states.name: retrying
states.description: A spinner replaces the icon of the retry button and VoiceOver reads "Retrying" as its value.

states.name: forbidden, notFound
states.description: A muted icon and no retry button, even when onRetry is given.

states.name: maintenance
states.description: A muted icon; retry is offered.

states.name: error, offline, server
states.description: An icon in the strong danger colour; retry is offered.

appearance: The layout of MonarchEmptyState: a centred icon, the title in the default text colour and the message in the muted text colour. The icon uses the strong danger colour for failures and the muted text colour for no access, not found and maintenance. The request id is muted, in the monospaced code role.
platformNotes: The web has a copy button beside the request id; here the id uses the system text selection, so it is copied with the standard Copy menu, and Monarch does not write to the pasteboard. One extra action by title and closure instead of the web's actions slot. The web errorKindFromStatus helper is not offered. The busy state is always controlled with isRetrying. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (onRetry, action). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the icon is hidden from VoiceOver. The title and message say what failed, so nothing depends on the icon or its colour.
While isRetrying is true the retry button stays focusable, does not run its action and has the value "Retrying".
The request id is one element read as its label, a colon and the id.
Buttons have touch targets of at least 44 points.
The state does not announce itself when it replaces content; post an announcement if the failure follows a user action.
edgeCases: onRetry is ignored for the forbidden and notFound kinds.
An empty requestID shows no request id row.
A long request id moves under its label.
A trailing closure is the retry action.

name: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditor
title: EscalationPolicyEditor
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchCard levels, each with MonarchDurationInput (TextField with a Stepper) for the delay and MonarchCheckboxGroup (Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox)) for the targets
summary: Edits an escalation ladder: at each level, after how long and whom to notify, so an alert or request nobody acts on reaches someone else.
whenToUse: In incident, on-call or support settings, where an admin sets who is told when nobody acknowledges.
whenNotToUse: For ordered approvers use MonarchApprovalChainEditor. For one response-time target use MonarchSlaIndicator to show it and a MonarchDurationInput to set it.
api: init(levels: Binding<[MonarchEscalationLevel]>, targets: [MonarchEscalationTarget], timing: MonarchEscalationPolicyTiming = .cumulative, description: String? = nil, defaultStepMinutes: Int = 15, minLevels: Int = 1, maxLevels: Int = 10, showsErrors: Bool = false, labels: MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels = MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels(), makeID: @escaping @MainActor () -> String = { UUID().uuidString })
nonisolated static func validate(_ levels: [MonarchEscalationLevel], timing: MonarchEscalationPolicyTiming = .cumulative) -> [String: MonarchEscalationLevelProblem]
MonarchEscalationLevel.init(id: String, afterMinutes: Int, targets: [String] = [])
MonarchEscalationTarget.init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil)
enum MonarchEscalationPolicyTiming { case cumulative, interval }
enum MonarchEscalationLevelProblem { case targets, order }
MonarchEscalationPolicyEditorLabels.init(label:level:after:notify:summary:nobody:remove:add:noTargets:problem:maxReached:), every parameter optional

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels in order: id, minutes before the level fires, and the ids of the targets it notifies.

options.name: targets
options.description: What a level can notify: channels, people, rotas.

options.name: timing
options.description: cumulative: times count from the start and must increase. interval: each time counts from the previous level.

options.name: description
options.description: Help under the list.

options.name: defaultStepMinutes
options.description: Minutes added to the last level for a new one.

options.name: minLevels
options.description: The fewest levels; remove is disabled at this count.

options.name: maxLevels
options.description: The most levels; the add button becomes "A policy can have up to 10 levels.".

options.name: showsErrors
options.description: Shows each level's problem, for example after a save attempt.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: makeID
options.description: Makes the id of a new level.

states.name: levels
states.description: One card per level: "Level 1", the summary, Remove, After (a duration with a stepper) and Notify (checkboxes).

states.name: no targets
states.description: A warning with an icon: there is nothing to notify yet.

states.name: missing targets
states.description: With showsErrors, the checkbox group shows "Choose at least one target …".

states.name: out of order
states.description: With showsErrors and cumulative timing, the delay shows "This level must come later than the one before it.".

states.name: at the minimum
states.description: Remove is disabled.

states.name: full
states.description: The add button is replaced by a muted note.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every control is disabled.

appearance: Monarch cards on the surface colour with a label-weight title, a muted summary, the Monarch duration field and checkboxes; the no-targets warning uses the strong warning role and problems the strong danger role, each with an icon. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows a numbered marker beside each level and an ordered list; iOS shows the number in the title and reads each level as one container. The web uses Checkbox and DurationInput; iOS uses MonarchCheckboxGroup and MonarchDurationInput, whose stepper replaces the web's arrow keys. Levels are not reordered, as on the web: their order is the order of their delays. The web moves focus after add and remove; iOS leaves focus to VoiceOver. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The list is a container named "Escalation levels".
Each level is a container read as "Level 1, After 1 hour, 30 minutes, notify On-call rota", with the delay spelled out in the locale; the visible short summary is hidden to avoid reading it twice.
The remove button is named "Remove level 1" and is disabled at minLevels.
The delay and the targets are labelled fields; problems are text with an icon on the field they concern.
The no-targets warning is text with an icon, not only colour.
Touch targets are at least 44 points.
edgeCases: A delay cleared in the field becomes one minute.
Target ids that are no longer offered are read by their id in the summary and dropped when a box is changed.
Interval timing never reports order problems.
Long target names wrap in the checkbox group and the summary.

name: MonarchEventChip
title: EventChip
wrapsNative: Button with a custom ButtonStyle; Text, Circle, RoundedRectangle
summary: One event in a calendar view: a colour dot or bar, the title, the time and the status, as a button that opens the event or as a label.
whenToUse: For each event in a month cell (dot), an agenda or all-day row (bar) or a time grid (block).
whenNotToUse: Not for a status without a time (use MonarchBadge) and not for a selectable filter chip. For a whole calendar that belongs to the device, EventKitUI shows the person's own events.
api: init(_ title: String, time: String? = nil, timeLabel: String? = nil, detail: String? = nil, color: Color? = nil, status: MonarchEventChipStatus = .confirmed, variant: MonarchEventChipVariant = .dot, isPast: Bool = false, statusLabel: String? = nil, isCompact: Bool = false, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchEventChipStatus: String { case confirmed, tentative, cancelled, declined }
enum MonarchEventChipVariant { case dot, bar, block }

options.name: title
options.description: The event title, already localised.

options.name: time
options.description: The visible time, already formatted. Leave it out for an all-day event in an all-day row.

options.name: timeLabel
options.description: The time as VoiceOver reads it when time is abbreviated, such as "9:30 to 10:15" or "All day".

options.name: detail
options.description: A second, muted line in bar and block chips.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's colour, for the dot, the bar and the tint only. nil is the theme's accent.

options.name: status
options.description: confirmed, tentative, cancelled or declined.

options.name: variant
options.description: dot, bar or block.

options.name: isPast
options.description: The event has ended: muted title and a faded marker.

options.name: statusLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in name of the status, in the visible word and in the spoken name.

options.name: isCompact
options.description: A block chip on one line, time then title, without the status word and the detail.

options.name: action
options.description: Opens the event. With it the chip is a Button; without it a label.

states.name: confirmed
states.description: A filled dot or a solid bar; bar and block chips have a light tint of the event colour.

states.name: tentative
states.description: A hollow dot or a dashed bar, a lighter tint and a border in the event colour. The status word is drawn in bar and block chips and spoken in all.

states.name: cancelled, declined
states.description: Muted text, the title struck through, the marker in the strong border colour and a muted fill instead of the tint. The status word is drawn in bar and block chips and spoken in all.

states.name: past
states.description: Muted title and the marker at reduced opacity.

states.name: pressed
states.description: With an action: a dot chip gets the muted fill, a tinted chip a stronger tint, a cancelled chip the emphasis fill.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) stops the action. The look does not change.

appearance: Text uses the default and muted text colours of the theme in every theme. The event colour (the accent unless the app gives one) is the dot, the bar and a tint laid over the surface colour at 14 percent. The app's colour is used as given in light, dark and high contrast, so choose one that is visible on both canvases.
platformNotes: The same statuses, variants and compact density as the web and Android. The web chip is always a button or a link; here the action is optional, and a link is an action that opens the URL. The web's asChild is not needed: wrap the chip in a NavigationLink instead. The web tints with color-mix; here the event colour is drawn over the surface at the same ratio. Hover is the pressed state.
accessibility: One element read as "title, time, status, detail". The status is left out when confirmed and the detail in a dot chip.
timeLabel replaces the visible time in the spoken name.
With an action the element has the button trait and a touch target at least 44 points high; the visible chip stays compact inside it.
The status is never colour alone: a hollow or dashed marker, a struck-through title, and the status word.
The text scales with Dynamic Type. A dot chip is one line and wraps at the accessibility sizes.
edgeCases: A block chip fills the frame it is given and clips what does not fit. A frame under 44 points high with an action overlaps its neighbours' touch targets.
A long title in a dot chip is truncated at the standard sizes.
In a bar chip the time moves under the title when both do not fit on one line.
isPast is not spoken; the time already says when the event was.
An empty title leaves the spoken name to the time and status.

}

name: MonarchEventPopover
title: EventPopover
wrapsNative: Content view for popover(isPresented:) with presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover), or sheet(isPresented:) with presentationDetents; Date.FormatStyle for the times; LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch(.inline)) for detail rows without an icon; MonarchBadge for the status; MonarchFlowLayout for the actions
summary: The content of a quick view of a calendar event: colour swatch, title, subtitle, status badge, date and time in a stated zone, labelled details, a note and actions.
whenToUse: When a tap on an event chip in a calendar, agenda or month view should show the event's essentials without leaving the screen.
whenNotToUse: For editing an event, push a form or present a sheet with the full editor. For a one-line summary inside a grid, use MonarchEventChip.
api: init(_ title: String, subtitle: String? = nil, start: Date? = nil, end: Date? = nil, isAllDay: Bool = false, color: Color? = nil, status: MonarchEventChipStatus? = nil, details: [MonarchEventPopoverDetail] = [], note: String? = nil, timeZone: TimeZone? = nil, labels: MonarchEventPopoverLabels = MonarchEventPopoverLabels(), @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(_ title: String, subtitle: String? = nil, start: Date? = nil, end: Date? = nil, isAllDay: Bool = false, color: Color? = nil, status: MonarchEventChipStatus? = nil, details: [MonarchEventPopoverDetail] = [], note: String? = nil, timeZone: TimeZone? = nil, labels: MonarchEventPopoverLabels = MonarchEventPopoverLabels())  // Actions == EmptyView
struct MonarchEventPopoverDetail { init(_ label: String, value: String, systemImage: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchEventPopoverLabels { var time, allDay, status: String? }

options.name: title
options.description: The event title, a header.

options.name: subtitle
options.description: A second line under the title, such as the calendar or the service.

options.name: start
options.description: When the event starts. Without it there is no time row.

options.name: end
options.description: When the event ends; for an all-day event its last day, inclusive. An end before the start is ignored.

options.name: isAllDay
options.description: Shows the day or day range and "All day" instead of times.

options.name: color
options.description: The event's colour for the swatch. The default is the accent role.

options.name: status
options.description: Confirmed, tentative, cancelled or declined, shown as a badge in the success, warning, neutral or danger tone.

options.name: details
options.description: Labelled rows under the time. A row with systemImage shows the icon instead of the label and still speaks the label.

options.name: note
options.description: A sentence on a subtle fill under the details, such as a cancellation reason.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone the times are shown in, named after the times. The default is the environment's zone.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Time, All day and the status name.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons at the bottom, laid out in a wrapping row. The app dismisses the popover from them.

states.name: spans days
states.description: The start day and time on the first line part, the end day and time and zone after it.

states.name: all day
states.description: The day or "first – last" day range, then "All day".

states.name: confirmed, tentative, cancelled, declined
states.description: A badge with the status name in its tone; cancelled and declined titles are struck through.

states.name: no time
states.description: Without start the time row is left out.

appearance: Title in the default text role, subtitle, labels, the time and the note in the muted text role, the note on the subtle background role, the swatch in the event's colour or the accent solid role, and the status badge in its tone's subtle colours. All roles keep their contrast in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web EventPopover includes its own Popover and trigger. On iOS this is the popover's content: the app presents it with .popover from the chip, which the system shows as a popover on iPad and, with .presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover), on iPhone; or as a sheet with a medium detent. The system handles dismissal and focus return. The web's hourCycle option has no counterpart: iOS follows the person's 12/24-hour setting through the locale. Product-specific statuses (the web's custom status node) are not supported; pass labels.status to rename the built-in one. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the swatch and the clock icon are decorative.
The status is a badge with its name in words, so it does not rely on colour; cancelled and declined titles are also struck through.
The time row is one element read as "Time" with the date and time as its value.
Each detail row is one element read as its label and value, also when it shows an icon instead of the label.
Actions are separate standard buttons.
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type; actions wrap onto more lines when they do not fit.
edgeCases: Long titles and subtitles wrap; the status badge stays at the trailing edge.
Times are formatted in timeZone, so an event at 14:30 UTC shows as Sat 9:30 AM EST in New York and Sun 3:30 AM in Auckland.
An end earlier than the start is ignored and only the start is shown.
The popover asks for an ideal width of 320 points; on iPhone the compact popover may be narrower, and the text wraps.

name: MonarchFacetedFilterPanel
title: FacetedFilterPanel
wrapsNative: DisclosureGroup(isExpanded:content:label:) with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) per facet, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) per option, MonarchRangeSlider per range facet; presented by the app in .sheet(isPresented:) with presentationDetents on iPhone
summary: A panel of filter groups: checkboxes with match counts and minimum to maximum range sliders, each group collapsible and clearable, with a clear-all button.
whenToUse: On a search or catalogue screen whose backend returns facet counts, when several filters apply together and people benefit from seeing them all at once. On iPhone present it in a sheet from a Filters button.
whenNotToUse: For one or two filters above a list use a Menu with a Picker or MonarchSavedViews; for a single exclusive choice use a segmented Picker; for nested AND and OR conditions use MonarchQueryBuilder.
api: MonarchFacetedFilterPanel.init(facets: [MonarchFacet], selection: Binding<[String: MonarchFacetSelection]>, showsTitle: Bool = true, labels: MonarchFacetedFilterPanelLabels = MonarchFacetedFilterPanelLabels())
MonarchFacet.init(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchFacetKind, isInitiallyExpanded: Bool = true)
static func MonarchFacet.options(id: String, label: String, options: [MonarchFacetOption], maxVisible: Int = 6, isInitiallyExpanded: Bool = true) -> MonarchFacet
static func MonarchFacet.range(id: String, label: String, bounds: ClosedRange<Double>, step: Double = 1, unit: String? = nil, isInitiallyExpanded: Bool = true) -> MonarchFacet
enum MonarchFacetKind { case options([MonarchFacetOption], maxVisible: Int), range(ClosedRange<Double>, step: Double, unit: String?) }
MonarchFacetOption.init(id: String, label: String, count: Int? = nil, isDisabled: Bool = false)
enum MonarchFacetSelection { case options(Set<String>), range(ClosedRange<Double>) }
MonarchFacetedFilterPanelLabels.init(title:clearAll:clearGroup:clearGroupLabel:activeCount:showMore:showFewer:noOptions:range:), every parameter optional

options.name: facets
options.description: The groups in order: .options with choices, their counts and how many show before Show more, or .range with bounds, step and unit.

options.name: selection
options.description: The active filters by facet id. A facet without a filter has no entry: no checked options, or a range equal to the bounds.

options.name: showsTitle
options.description: Shows the Filters heading. Hide it inside a sheet whose navigation title already says it; Clear all stays.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, Clear all, Clear, the spoken group clear name, the active count, Show more, Show fewer, No options and the range slider's Minimum and Maximum.

states.name: no filters
states.description: Clear all is disabled; group headers show only their names.

states.name: active
states.description: A group with filters shows "2 selected" under its name in the accent colour, and a Clear button at the top of its content.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: The group shows only its header; the chevron points forward. isInitiallyExpanded sets the first state.

states.name: more options
states.description: Past maxVisible, a Show 4 more button reveals the rest and becomes Show fewer. Checked options stay visible.

states.name: empty facet
states.description: An options facet with no options shows "No options".

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the panel gives every control its disabled colours and stops changes.

appearance: Groups are separated by dividers. Headings use the default text role, counts the muted role, and the active count the accent strong role. Checkboxes and the range slider use their Monarch styles and adapt to the dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web FacetedFilterPanel is a sidebar with typed minimum and maximum number inputs and an invalid state when the minimum is above the maximum. On iOS a range is a two-thumb MonarchRangeSlider between known bounds, so it cannot be inverted and has no invalid state; a range facet needs bounds. On iPhone the panel goes in a sheet rather than a sidebar. The web's footer slot is the sheet's toolbar, and the web's heading levels are a single header trait. The web value is an object of arrays and min/max pairs; here it is a dictionary of MonarchFacetSelection. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The panel is a container named "Filters"; the visible title has the header trait.
Each group header is one button that reads the group name, the active count ("2 selected") and Expanded or Collapsed.
Each option is a checkbox whose name is the label and the count in the current locale ("Done, 1,204"); the count is not only visual.
A group's clear button is named after the group ("Clear Status filter").
Each range thumb is adjustable and reads the facet name, Minimum or Maximum, and the value with its unit ("25 MB").
Checked options are never hidden behind Show more.
Every button and checkbox has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points and its text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Unchecking the last option of a facet, or moving a range back to its full bounds, removes the facet from the selection.
A stored range outside the bounds is shown clamped to the bounds.
A stored value of the wrong kind for its facet (a range for an options facet) is ignored and not counted.
A count of 0 is shown; disable the option if it cannot be chosen.
Long labels and counts wrap at the largest text sizes.

name: MonarchFavicon

wrapsNative: AsyncImage, Image
summary: The icon of a website at a fixed size, with a letter tile while it loads, when it fails and when there is no icon.
whenToUse: Beside the name or address of a website, in link lists, bookmarks and source citations.
whenNotToUse: For a person or an organisation use the avatar. For an app's own symbols use MonarchIcon.
api: init(image: Image?, name: String, label: String? = nil, size: MonarchFaviconSize = .sm, shape: MonarchFaviconShape = .rounded)
init(url: URL?, name: String, label: String? = nil, size: MonarchFaviconSize = .sm, shape: MonarchFaviconShape = .rounded)
enum MonarchFaviconSize { case sm, md, lg }
enum MonarchFaviconShape { case rounded, circle, square }

options.name: image
options.description: An icon the app already has, or nil for the letter tile. First initialiser.

options.name: url
options.description: The address of the icon, loaded with AsyncImage. Only http and https URLs are loaded. Second initialiser.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the site, its domain or its URL. Its first letter or digit is the fallback letter.

options.name: label
options.description: What VoiceOver reads. Without it the favicon is decorative.

options.name: size
options.description: sm 16, md 20 or lg 24 points, before Dynamic Type.

options.name: shape
options.description: rounded (4-point corners), circle or square.

states.name: image
states.description: The picture fills the tile and is clipped to the shape.

states.name: fallback
states.description: A tile in the muted background colour with one upper-case letter in the muted text colour. Shown while loading, on failure and without a source.

appearance: The picture is drawn as it is. The letter tile uses the muted background and muted text roles, which resolve per theme, including high contrast.
platformNotes: The web Favicon takes a domain and an optional resolveSrc function, and a size in pixels. iOS follows the Monarch image convention instead: one initialiser with an Image and one with a URL, and three named sizes. Like the web, Monarch never calls a favicon service by itself. The web also accepts base64 data URLs; on iOS an app with image data passes an Image.
accessibility: Decorative and hidden from VoiceOver unless label is given.
With a label it is one element with the image trait, read as the label.
The tile and the letter scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A URL with a scheme other than http or https, or without a host, is not loaded and the letter tile is shown.
A name with no letter or digit gives a question mark.
A name that is a URL or starts with www. is reduced to its host name before the letter is taken.
AsyncImage does not cache beyond the shared URL cache; an app with its own image pipeline passes an Image.
The letter is sized as 0.6 of the tile rather than with a type role, so it fits every size.

title: FavoritesList
wrapsNative: Section in a List, ForEach with .onMove(perform:) and .onDelete(perform:), .environment(\.editMode, …) on the section, MonarchButton (ghost) as the Edit button
summary: A sidebar section of pinned destinations with a starred heading, the current destination marked, and an Edit button that turns on reorder and delete for that section.
whenToUse: In a sidebar or navigation list where people pin projects, views or documents and want to reorder or unpin them.
whenNotToUse: For the app's fixed destinations, use a plain List section or a TabView. For reordering arbitrary content, use a List with onMove (see reorderable-list).
api: init(items: [MonarchFavoriteItem], isEditing: Binding<Bool>? = nil, showsIcon: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, labels: MonarchFavoritesListLabels = MonarchFavoritesListLabels(), onRemove: (@MainActor (MonarchFavoriteItem) -> Void)? = nil, onReorder: (@MainActor ([MonarchFavoriteItem]) -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchFavoriteItem) -> Void)
struct MonarchFavoriteItem: Identifiable { init(_ title: String, id: String, systemImage: String? = nil, isCurrent: Bool = false) }
struct MonarchFavoritesListLabels { var title, edit, editLabel, done, removed, moveUp, moveDown: String? }

options.name: items
options.description: The pinned destinations, in order. isCurrent marks the screen the person is on.

options.name: isEditing
options.description: Edit mode controlled by the app. Without it the Edit button keeps its own state.

options.name: showsIcon
options.description: Whether a star comes before the heading.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: Shown when there are no items. Without it the section is left out when empty.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Favorites, Edit, Edit favorites, Done, the removal announcement and the move actions.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes an item. With it rows can be deleted, by swipe or in edit mode.

options.name: onReorder
options.description: Receives the new order. With it rows show a reorder handle in edit mode.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens a destination when its row is tapped outside edit mode.

states.name: browsing
states.description: Rows are buttons with an optional icon and the name; the Edit button shows when onRemove or onReorder is given.

states.name: current
states.description: The current destination is semibold in the accent's strong text on its subtle fill, with the selected trait.

states.name: editing
states.description: The section's rows show the system delete control and, with onReorder, the reorder handle; rows stop opening their destination; the button reads Done.

states.name: empty
states.description: With emptyMessage, the heading and the message in muted text; without it nothing is drawn.

appearance: A list section whose heading is a star and a label in the muted text role. Rows use the default text role with muted icons; the current row uses the accent's subtle fill and strong text, which keep their contrast in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web FavoritesList is a nav of links with its own remove buttons and a ReorderableList. On iOS the section sits in the app's List and uses the system's edit mode, delete control and reorder handle, and rows report a selection instead of following an href. Swipe to delete also works outside edit mode, as everywhere in iOS. The web's FavoriteToggle (the star button that pins a page) is not a separate type: use Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()) and a star symbol, shown in the examples. Edit mode is set with .environment(\.editMode, …) on this section only, which exists on iOS alone; on the macOS host build the section has no edit mode. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The heading (star and title) is one element with the header trait; the star is decorative.
Rows are buttons named by the destination; the current one has the selected trait and is also set in a semibold weight, so it is not shown by colour alone.
The Edit button is named Edit favorites and reads Done while editing.
In edit mode each row has Move up and Move down accessibility actions (when onReorder is given), and the system delete control.
After a removal, "Roadmap removed from favorites." is announced.
Rows are at least 44 points tall and the names wrap and scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: With neither onRemove nor onReorder there is no Edit button and no swipe to delete.
Removing the last item ends edit mode; with no emptyMessage the section then disappears.
Long names wrap; the heading's Edit button stays at the trailing edge.
Edit mode controls are drawn by the system List, so they need a device or simulator to see; outside a List the section is a plain stack.

name: MonarchFieldRenderer
title: FieldRenderer
wrapsNative: A switch over MonarchFormFieldType to existing inputs: MonarchFormField around a TextField (axis: .vertical for long text, TextField(value:format:) for numbers), a Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) (select), Button rows with a check mark (radio), a Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) (yes or no), DatePicker with displayedComponents .date or .hourAndMinute, and a compact MonarchFileUpload; MonarchCheckboxGroup, MonarchMultiSelect, MonarchRatingPicker, and a Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) for a consent
summary: Renders one form question from data: the right Monarch input for its type, with the label, help, required mark, error and an optional “filled in automatically” note.
whenToUse: Questions are authored by admins and stored as data, or a form shows answers that were filled in automatically and people must check them.
whenNotToUse: When the form is fixed in code, compose MonarchFormField, MonarchTextField and the other inputs directly.
api: init(_ field: MonarchFormFieldDefinition, value: Binding<MonarchFormFieldValue?>, problem: MonarchFormFieldProblem? = nil, error: String? = nil, confidence: Double? = nil, confidenceThreshold: Double = 0.6, today: @escaping () -> Date = { Date() }, labels: MonarchFieldRendererLabels = MonarchFieldRendererLabels())

struct MonarchFormFieldDefinition: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, type: MonarchFormFieldType, label: String, description: String? = nil, placeholder: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, options: [MonarchFormFieldOption] = [], minLength: Int? = nil, maxLength: Int? = nil, min: Double? = nil, max: Double? = nil, minDate: Date? = nil, maxDate: Date? = nil, minSelections: Int? = nil, maxSelections: Int? = nil, rows: Int = 4, allowedContentTypes: [UTType] = [.item], maxFileSize: Int64? = nil, maxFiles: Int = 1, consentText: String? = nil, conditions: [MonarchCondition] = [], conditionMatch: MonarchConditionMatch = .and, isReadOnly: Bool = false); func problem(for value: MonarchFormFieldValue?) -> MonarchFormFieldProblem?; func isVisible(in values: [String: MonarchFormFieldValue], calendar: Calendar = .current) -> Bool }

enum MonarchFormFieldType: String, CaseIterable { case shortText = "short-text", longText = "long-text", email, phone, url, number, date, time, select, multiSelect = "multi-select", radio, checkboxes, yesNo = "yes-no", consent, rating, file, section }
enum MonarchFormFieldValue: Hashable, Sendable { case text(String), number(Double), date(Date), flag(Bool), values([String]), files([MonarchFormFieldFile]); var isEmpty: Bool }
enum MonarchFormFieldProblem: Hashable, Sendable { case required, mustAgree, email, url, notANumber, min(Double), max(Double), minLength(Int), maxLength(Int), minSelections(Int), maxSelections(Int) }
struct MonarchFormFieldOption: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(value: String, label: String) }
struct MonarchFormFieldFile: Hashable, Sendable { init(name: String, size: Int64? = nil, file: MonarchFileUploadFile? = nil) }

struct MonarchFieldRendererLabels: Sendable { init(required: String? = nil, mustAgree: String? = nil, email: String? = nil, url: String? = nil, number: String? = nil, min: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, max: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, minLength: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, maxLength: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, minSelections: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, maxSelections: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, yes: String? = nil, no: String? = nil, choose: String? = nil, chooseDate: String? = nil, chooseTime: String? = nil, clear: String? = nil, aiFilled: String? = nil, aiCheck: String? = nil, remove: String? = nil, removeFile: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: field
options.description: The question: its type, label, help, required flag, options, limits, conditions and read-only flag.

options.name: value
options.description: The answer, or nil for none. Set to nil when an optional select, date, time or rating is cleared.

options.name: problem
options.description: A problem from MonarchFormFieldDefinition.problem(for:), shown as the error with its built-in message.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, such as a server error; replaces the message of problem.

options.name: confidence
options.description: The confidence, from 0 to 1, of an answer filled in automatically; shows a note under the question.

options.name: confidenceThreshold
options.description: The confidence under which the note asks people to check the answer.

options.name: today
options.description: The current day, where Choose a date and Choose a time start. Inject a fixed day in tests.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings and messages.

states.name: empty
states.description: The input shows its placeholder, Choose…, a Choose a date or Choose a time button, no chosen option or no files.

states.name: answered
states.description: The input shows the answer: text, the chosen option with a check mark, the system date or time picker with Clear when optional, a rating or the chosen files.

states.name: error
states.description: The message shows under the question with an icon in the danger colour, becomes part of the input's hint and is announced.

states.name: filled in automatically
states.description: With confidence, a note with a bot (cpu) icon says the answer was filled in; below the threshold it asks for a check in the warning colour.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Text and number questions show the answer as selectable text in the field; other questions are disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true), every input is disabled, remove buttons and the upload row are hidden, and text takes the disabled colour.

states.name: section
states.description: A heading with an optional description and no input.

appearance: Each question uses the look of the input it renders: text questions use the text field's surface fill and input border (danger border with an error), options sit in one bordered list with the accent check mark on the chosen one, menus, segmented controls and date pickers are the system's. Errors use the danger text colour, the automatic-fill note the AI text colour or, when unsure, the warning text colour; section descriptions and help use the muted text colour. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the colour roles.
platformNotes: Same question types, checks, order of checks and default messages as the web and Android (validateFormField is MonarchFormFieldDefinition.problem(for:), which returns a typed problem; the renderer turns it into the message and error replaces it). Differences: a date answer is a Date, as the system DatePicker gives it, where the web stores YYYY-MM-DD and Android UTC milliseconds; a time stays HH:MM. Dates and times are a button that sets them and then the compact system DatePicker, with Clear for optional questions. A radio question is a list of rows with a check mark, the iOS settings pattern, because iOS has no radio button; yes or no is a segmented Picker. File limits are UTType values and bytes (allowedContentTypes, maxFileSize) as in MonarchFileUpload, where the web takes an accept string and megabytes. Text length counts characters, where the web counts UTF-16 code units. Conditions are MonarchCondition values with MonarchConditionMatch, as MonarchConditionEditor edits them; a list answer equals or contains a value when one of its items is that value. A rating keeps MonarchRatingPicker's own label, so it shows no visible required mark; Required is in its hint and its error is drawn under it. headingLevel and locale are not parameters: VoiceOver headings have no levels here and the locale comes from the environment. The answer is a Binding instead of value and onChange, and disabled(_:) replaces the disabled prop. The text field is a private copy of MonarchTextField's look, because MonarchTextField has no read-only, several-line or label-less form.
accessibility: Questions without a label of their own sit in a MonarchFormField: the input is named by the label, its hint is the error, the help and Required, and a new error is announced.
Checkboxes and multi-select questions use the labels, required marks, hints and errors of MonarchCheckboxGroup and MonarchMultiSelect.
Radio options are buttons in a group named by the label, each at least 44 points high; the chosen one has the selected trait and a check mark, not colour alone.
A consent is one checkbox named by its statement; its hint is the error, the help and Required, and a new error is announced. The visible required mark is hidden from VoiceOver.
A rating is MonarchRatingPicker's adjustable element; the renderer adds the error, help and Required to its hint and announces a new error.
Read-only text is static text whose value is the answer, selectable with the system text selection.
A section is a heading.
Each chosen file's remove button is named Remove followed by the file name.
The automatic-fill note is text read as one element; its icon is decorative.
edgeCases: Typing stops at maxLength; problem(for:) also reports a stored answer that is too long.
Spaces alone are no answer, and length checks ignore spaces at either end, as on the web.
A yes-or-no question whose answer is not a flag counts as unanswered.
A select or radio answer that is not one of the options shows no choice.
A time answer that is not HH:MM shows Choose a time.
Choose a date starts on today, moved inside minDate and maxDate; a reversed minDate and maxDate is ignored except for the minimum.
A rating with min above max falls back to 1 to 5.
Use isVisible(in:calendar:) to leave out questions whose conditions do not hold; the renderer does not hide itself.
Files the upload control rejects are listed by MonarchFileUpload and never reach the answer.

enum MonarchFileCardLayout { case card, row }
struct MonarchFileCardLabels { init(select: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, actions: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, type: String? = nil) }

options.name: name
options.description: The file name with its extension. Shortened in the middle when it does not fit, so the extension stays visible.

options.name: isSelected
options.description: Shows a selection checkbox bound to this value: at the top leading corner of a card, at the start of a row.

options.name: size
options.description: The size in bytes, shown in the locale's file units, such as "2.4 MB".

options.name: contentType
options.description: The MIME type. With the name it decides the type icon and the type in the meta line.

options.name: meta
options.description: More text after the size, already localised, such as "Edited yesterday" or an owner.

options.name: thumbnail / thumbnailURL
options.description: A preview image, given directly or loaded with AsyncImage. The type icon on a subtle tile is shown without one, while loading and on failure.

options.name: badges
options.description: Short states shown as neutral MonarchBadges under the name, such as "Shared".

options.name: layout
options.description: card: a 4:3 preview above the name, for grids. row: a small preview beside the name, for lists.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken names of the checkbox and the menu, and for the type in the meta line.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens the file, for example with Quick Look. Makes the preview, name and meta one button with a pressed state.

options.name: menu
options.description: The items of the actions menu, shown behind an ellipsis button at the top trailing corner of a card or the end of a row.

states.name: rest
states.description: Surface background with a subtle border.

states.name: pressed
states.description: With onOpen: the card turns to the subtle background with the default border; a row tints its open area.

states.name: selected
states.description: The checkbox is ticked and the card has the accent subtle background and a thicker accent border.

states.name: disabled

title: FilePreview
wrapsNative: quickLookPreview(_:) from the QuickLook framework, on any view
summary: Quick Look, the system file viewer, presented with the quickLookPreview modifier. Monarch ships nothing; the row that opens it is made of Monarch components.
whenToUse: To show the content of a file the app has on disk: images, PDF, text, video, audio, iWork and Office documents. Set the bound URL to present the viewer.
whenNotToUse: For a file that is still remote, download it first: Quick Look needs a file URL. For a type Quick Look cannot show, offer ShareLink or fileExporter instead. For a video poster in a list, use MonarchVideoThumbnail.

states.description: Quick Look shows the file's icon, name and size with its own share button.

appearance: System appearance: Quick Look draws its own chrome and follows the system light, dark and contrast settings, not the Monarch theme. The row that opens it uses Monarch colours.
platformNotes: The web FilePreview draws the file inline in the page and Android builds a MonarchFilePreview. On iOS Quick Look is the expected viewer and covers more types (PDF with search, Live Photos, Office and iWork documents, 3D models), so Monarch adds no view of its own. The differences: the preview is presented over the screen, not inline; it needs a local file URL; captions, the download link and the failed state of the web component are Quick Look's own controls or the app's. The fallback of the web component (type icon, name, message, download) is composed from MonarchFileTypeIcon, Text and ShareLink.
accessibility: System behaviour: Quick Look is fully operable with VoiceOver, including its close, share and page controls.
The control that opens the preview is an ordinary MonarchButton; give it a title that names the action.
edgeCases: The URL must be a file URL the app can read; a remote URL shows nothing.
A security-scoped URL from a document picker must be accessed with startAccessingSecurityScopedResource before it is presented.
Use the collection form to let people swipe between several files.

whenToUse: Beside a file name in a list, an attachment chip or an upload row, and as the large mark of a file that has no preview.
whenNotToUse: When a real thumbnail of the file exists, show the thumbnail. For a general symbol that is not a file type, use MonarchIcon.

appearance: Each family has its own SF Symbol, tinted from the data palette (images and video data 1, documents and text data 2, spreadsheets and code data 3, audio and presentations data 4, PDF data 5) or the muted text colour for archives and other files. The large size sits on a muted tile with a subtle border and 8-point corners. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web and Android draw one page outline with a mark inside; iOS uses a distinct SF Symbol per family, which is what the Files app does. The extension and MIME tables are the web's, so a file gets the same family on every platform; a type the tables do not list is looked up with UTType, and MonarchFileTypeFamily(_: UTType) accepts a UTType directly, which the web cannot. The large size is a 24-point glyph on a 40-point tile (the web draws 28 on 40). The web's FileTypeGlyph is not a separate type: pass isDecorative.
accessibility: The icon is one image element whose label is the family name, for example "PDF document", from the component's strings table or the label parameter.
With isDecorative the icon is hidden from VoiceOver.
Every family has a different symbol, so the type does not depend on the tint.
The glyph and the tile scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A name with no extension, a leading-dot name such as .env and an unknown extension give the other family.
application/octet-stream and an empty MIME type are ignored and the extension decides.
A double extension uses the last part: backup.tar.gz is an archive.
The icon is not interactive and has no touch target of its own.

name: MonarchFileUpload
title: FileUpload
wrapsNative: .fileImporter(isPresented:allowedContentTypes:allowsMultipleSelection:onCompletion:), PhotosPicker(selection:maxSelectionCount:matching:) and .dropDestination(for:action:isTargeted:) with a Transferable FileRepresentation
summary: An area for adding files through the system document picker, the system photo picker and drag and drop, with checks of type, size and count that explain every refusal.
whenToUse: Wherever people attach files that the app then uploads: attachments on a form, documents for a record, an avatar.
whenNotToUse: Not for showing upload progress (use MonarchUploadQueue), not for files already attached (use MonarchFileList or MonarchAttachmentChip), and not when the app only needs a photo with no checks (use PhotosPicker directly).

options.name: allowedContentTypes
options.description: The accepted types, matched by conformance (.image accepts PNG and HEIC). The document picker shows only these.

options.name: maxSize
options.description: The largest size of one file, in bytes.

options.name: maxFiles
options.description: The most files in total, counting currentCount. Extra files are refused in order, keeping the first valid ones.

options.name: currentCount
options.description: Files already attached. When it reaches maxFiles the buttons are disabled and the hint says the limit is reached.

options.name: hint
options.description: Text under the title. By default it is made from the limits, such as "Up to 10 MB each · 5 files max".

options.name: systemImage
options.description: A decorative SF Symbol at the start. Default square.and.arrow.up.

options.name: variant
options.description: zone: a dashed bordered area with the parts stacked and centred. compact: one row; stacked at the accessibility text sizes.

options.name: allowsMultipleSelection
options.description: Whether several files can be chosen at once. By default yes, unless maxFiles is 1.

options.name: allowsPhotos
options.description: Adds "Choose photos", which opens PhotosPicker for the images and videos the allowed types accept.

options.name: showsErrors
options.description: Shows the refusals in a danger MonarchInlineNotice under the area. Turn off to show them yourself.

options.name: isInvalid
options.description: Draws the danger border, for example when a required file is missing.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in text and message.

options.name: validate
options.description: An extra check after type and size. Return a message to refuse the file.

options.name: onFiles
options.description: Receives the accepted and refused files of every pick or drop. The app uploads the accepted files.

states.name: rest
states.description: Surface fill with the input border; the zone's border is dashed.

states.name: drag over
states.description: While files are dragged over it (iPad, Mac): the accent subtle fill and accent border, and the title says "Drop to upload".

states.name: refused files
states.description: The danger border and a danger notice listing each refusal; announced.

states.name: limit reached
states.description: currentCount reached maxFiles: the disabled roles, disabled buttons and "Limit reached: 5 files attached."

states.name: loading photos
states.description: The photo button shows a progress indicator while the chosen photos are copied.

states.name: invalid
states.description: isInvalid: the danger border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the disabled roles, and picking and dropping do nothing.

appearance: A container-radius area on the surface fill with an input-coloured border (dashed for the zone), a muted icon, the title in the label style and the hint in the muted caption style; buttons are MonarchButtonStyle secondary small. Drag over uses the accent subtle and accent border roles, errors the danger roles. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web input's accept string becomes UTType values, matched by conformance. The browse button opens the system document picker (.fileImporter); its URLs are security-scoped, so the app calls startAccessingSecurityScopedResource() before reading. Photos and dropped files are copied to the temporary directory, because the system removes its copy when the import ends; the app deletes them after uploading. Dropping is available where the system supports drag and drop (iPad, Mac); on iPhone the buttons are the way in. The web's paste option and capture attribute have no direct equivalent: use MonarchFileUpload.validate for files the app gets from the pasteboard or the camera. The web greys out a drag of the wrong type before the drop; on iOS the type is known only after the drop, so the refusal comes then.
accessibility: "Browse files" and "Choose photos" are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets; they are the way in for VoiceOver and Switch Control.
The title and the hint are read as one element; the icon is decorative.
After a pick or drop, the number of files added and every refusal are announced.
Refusals are shown with a danger icon and text, not colour alone.
edgeCases: A file of unknown type is accepted only when any data is allowed; its type falls back to its extension first.
A file of unknown size passes the size check.
With single selection, extra dropped files are refused as "up to 1 file".
The refusals shown are those of the latest pick; a new pick replaces them.
A photo that cannot be loaded is skipped.

title: FilterBar
wrapsNative: searchable(text:prompt:) on a List in a NavigationStack, safeAreaInset(edge: .top) with a horizontal ScrollView of MonarchTag chips (isSelected for quick filters, onRemove for active ones), a toolbar Button that opens MonarchFacetedFilterPanel in a sheet with presentationDetents, and a Menu with a Picker for sorting

whenToUse: Above any filterable list of records (tickets, orders, people), where people narrow results by status, owner or other fields.
whenNotToUse: For a handful of fixed views use a segmented Picker or MonarchSavedViews. For building conditions with operators use MonarchQueryBuilder. For search across the whole app use the command palette recipe.

.sheet(isPresented:) { NavigationStack { ScrollView { MonarchFacetedFilterPanel(facets:selection:showsTitle: false) } } }.presentationDetents([.medium, .large])
Menu { Picker("Sort by", selection:) { … } } label: { Label("Sort", systemImage: "arrow.up.arrow.down") } for sorting and display options

appearance: The system navigation bar search field, Monarch tags in the neutral tone (filled when selected), ghost Monarch buttons, and the facet panel in a sheet. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web FilterBar is one component: a search input on the leading edge, FilterChips with popover editors, an Add filter menu, Clear all, a result count and trailing controls, which below a width move into a bottom sheet behind a "Filters (n)" button. On a phone that narrow layout is the only one, so iOS composes it: search moves into the navigation bar with searchable, chips scroll sideways in the top safe-area inset, and editing a filter happens in the sheet with MonarchFacetedFilterPanel instead of a popover per chip. readFilterParams and writeFilterParams (URL query strings) have no counterpart; persist filters with the app's own state, such as SceneStorage. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The search field is the system's, named by its prompt.
Quick filters are MonarchTag toggles read with their selected state; active filters are tags with a remove button named "Remove Status filter".
The toolbar button includes the number of active filters in its name.
Announce the result count when it changes (AccessibilityNotification.Announcement), as the web's live region does.
Every chip and button is at least 44 points.
edgeCases: Many chips scroll sideways; keep Clear all at the end of the row so it is reached last.
Removing the last value of a facet removes the facet from the selection.

title: FocusTrap
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:content:), fullScreenCover(isPresented:content:), alert and confirmationDialog; accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal) for a custom overlay
summary: Keeping focus inside a modal surface is done by the system's modal presentations. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Present modal content with sheet, fullScreenCover, alert or confirmationDialog: VoiceOver, Switch Control and the hardware keyboard are confined to it until it is dismissed. For an overlay you draw yourself in the same view tree, add the isModal trait to it.
whenNotToUse: Do not confine focus for content that is not modal, such as an inline panel or a popover the person can ignore; leave the rest of the screen reachable.
api: func sheet<Content: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> Content) -> some View
func fullScreenCover<Content: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, onDismiss: (() -> Void)? = nil, content: @escaping () -> Content) -> some View
func accessibilityAddTraits(_ traits: AccessibilityTraits) -> some View

states.name: presented
states.description: Focus is inside the presentation. Content behind it is not reachable by assistive technology.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: The system returns VoiceOver focus to the presenting screen.

appearance: The system draws the presentation in every theme; Monarch draws nothing. The content of the presentation uses Monarch components as usual.
platformNotes: The web needs a FocusTrap component and hook because a browser lets Tab leave a dialog. On iOS the presentation is a separate layer the system manages, so there is nothing to build; Android relies on Dialog and ModalBottomSheet in the same way. The web's initialFocus is @AccessibilityFocusState or @FocusState, returnFocus is automatic, and onEscape is the dismissal of the presentation.
accessibility: System behaviour: a presented sheet, cover, alert or dialog confines VoiceOver, Switch Control and Full Keyboard Access to itself.
System behaviour: when it is dismissed, focus returns to the presenting screen.
accessibilityAddTraits(.isModal) on a custom overlay makes VoiceOver ignore its sibling elements. It does not confine hardware-keyboard focus; disable or hide the content behind the overlay as well.
The escape gesture (two-finger Z) dismisses a system presentation. Add accessibilityAction(.escape) to a custom overlay.
edgeCases: fullScreenCover has no swipe to dismiss; give it a visible close control.
interactiveDismissDisabled() stops the swipe on a sheet with unsaved changes; keep a button that dismisses.
fullScreenCover is not available on macOS, so the compiled examples use sheet.

name: MonarchForceGraph
title: ForceGraph
wrapsNative: SwiftUI Canvas with symbols, DragGesture and MagnifyGesture, inside MonarchChartFrame; a built-in force layout
summary: A network of linked nodes placed by a small built-in force layout, with groups in data colours, link kinds, drag, pan and zoom.
whenToUse: To show how a few dozen items connect, such as linked notes, service dependencies or people and teams, where the shape of the network matters.
whenNotToUse: For a hierarchy, use a tree or an outline. For exact links of many items, use a List; the table of this graph is the same data as text.

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, shown as the frame's heading.

options.name: nodes
options.description: The nodes. A repeated id keeps the first node.

options.name: edges
options.description: The links, without direction. Links to unknown nodes and to the same node are ignored.

options.name: groups
options.description: The groups in legend order. The distinct group keys of the nodes, labelled by key, when nil.

options.name: edgeKinds
options.description: Kinds of link with a colour and dash, listed in a second legend when used.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. A ready chart without nodes shows the empty state.

options.name: height
options.description: The height of the canvas. 420 points when nil.

options.name: showsLabels
options.description: Draws each node's label under it.

options.name: selectedID
options.description: The id of a node drawn with an accent ring, such as the open document.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that VoiceOver reads for the graph.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: layoutOptions
options.description: Link distance, repulsion, collision, gravity and steps of the layout.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are formats with %1$@ placeholders.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with a node when it is tapped or selected with VoiceOver, for example to open it.

states.name: ready
states.description: Nodes as dots in their group's colour with labels, links as lines in their kind's colour and dash, on the subtle background, with zoom in, zoom out and Reset view.

states.name: inspected node
states.description: After a tap, the node has a default-text ring, its links are thicker and opaque, other nodes and links fade, and its group, links and description are written under the canvas.

states.name: selected node
states.description: selectedID draws an accent ring.

states.name: orphan node
states.description: A node without links is a dashed outline on the surface colour.

states.name: moved, panned, zoomed
states.description: Dragging moves a node or pans; pinching or the buttons zoom between 0.35 and 3 times; Reset view undoes all three. Zoom buttons are disabled at the limits.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists every node by label with its group and its links.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no nodes.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's placeholder at the canvas height.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Nodes use the data colours by group (the sixth group and later, ungrouped and unlinked nodes are neutral) with a surface-coloured outline; links use the kind's colour or neutral at reduced opacity; the canvas is the subtle background and labels are default text, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ForceGraph shows a tooltip on hover and moves between nodes with the arrow keys, nearest in the pressed direction; on iOS a tap inspects a node and writes its details under the canvas, and VoiceOver moves through the nodes in label order by swiping up and down. Pinch zooms as well as the buttons. The layout is the same algorithm as the web's and gives the same shape, though not identical numbers. The controlled activeId is not offered and the layout is not public. The group legend uses dots, the shape of the nodes, where the web uses squares. Dragging on the canvas does not scroll an enclosing scroll view, like a map. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The canvas is one element labelled with the generated summary (nodes, links, groups and the most connected node) or the summary given.
It is adjustable: swiping up and down visits the nodes in label order; its value reads the node's label, group, number of links and the linked nodes with their kinds.
With onSelect it has the button trait and a double tap selects the current node.
It carries an AXChartDescriptor for Audio Graphs: the nodes along the x axis and each node's number of links.
Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset view are labelled buttons with 44-point targets.
View as table is the list alternative: every node with its group and links as text.
Colour is not the only key: groups are named in the legend and in each node's spoken text, and link kinds are dashed as well as coloured.
Node labels scale with Dynamic Type and are truncated at 144 points.
edgeCases: A link to an unknown node or to itself is ignored, and does not count as a connection.
Nodes with a repeated id: the first wins.
A single node or nodes at one place are centred at the largest fit scale.
Graphs over 300 nodes use approximate repulsion and collision and fewer steps; the layout runs on the main thread when the nodes, links or options change.
Moved nodes keep their place until Reset view or until the graph changes; a node that is removed loses its moved place.

title: FormActionsBar
wrapsNative: toolbar with ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) and ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction), with confirmationDialog and interactiveDismissDisabled
summary: Save and Discard for a form are toolbar items of the navigation bar, which stays in reach while the form scrolls. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: On any screen or sheet that edits something: Save in the confirmation position, Discard or Cancel in the cancellation position, both tied to whether the form has unsaved changes.
whenNotToUse: For a single action inside the content, such as a sign-in button under two fields, use MonarchButton in the layout.
api: func toolbar<Content: ToolbarContent>(@ToolbarContentBuilder content: () -> Content) -> some View
ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) { Button("Save") { … } }
ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) { Button("Discard") { … } }
func confirmationDialog(_ title: String, isPresented: Binding<Bool>, titleVisibility: Visibility, actions:, message:) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool) -> some View

states.name: clean
states.description: Save and Discard are disabled with disabled(_:) while nothing has changed.

states.name: dirty
states.description: Both are enabled. interactiveDismissDisabled(true) stops a sheet from being swiped away with unsaved changes.

states.name: pending
states.description: A ProgressView replaces Save and Discard is disabled while the save runs.

states.name: error
states.description: A failed save is shown in the form with MonarchBanner in the danger tone, or with the system alert.

states.name: confirming discard
states.description: confirmationDialog asks before the changes are dropped, with a destructive action and a cancel action.

appearance: System appearance: the navigation bar draws the items, with the confirmation action emphasised, tinted with the accent of the Monarch theme.
platformNotes: The web FormActionsBar is a sticky bar at the bottom of the page and Android builds a MonarchFormActionsBar. On iOS the navigation bar is where people look for Save and Cancel, and it already stays visible, so a second bar would duplicate it. What the web component does itself is done with system pieces here: the discard confirmation is confirmationDialog, leaving with unsaved changes is interactiveDismissDisabled, and the pending and error states are the app's state. The web's "You have unsaved changes" text has no fixed place in a navigation bar; show it in the form if it is needed.
accessibility: System behaviour: toolbar items are buttons with their titles as labels, and a disabled item is announced as dimmed.
Give the ProgressView that replaces Save an accessibility label such as "Saving".
The confirmation dialog is announced when it appears and its destructive action is identified as such.
edgeCases: The toolbar needs a NavigationStack above it; a sheet needs its own.
On iPad and Mac Catalyst the confirmation dialog is a popover anchored to the item.
interactiveDismissDisabled affects only sheets and popovers, not a pushed screen; hide or replace the back button with navigationBarBackButtonHidden to guard a pushed form.

title: FormBuilder
wrapsNative: MonarchTabs for Build and Preview, Menu for the field palette, List with ForEach.onMove in edit mode and accessibilityActions Move up and Move down for the field list, sheet(item:) with NavigationStack, Form, Picker(.menu) and Toggle for field settings, and Form of MonarchFieldRenderer for the preview
summary: A recipe, not a component: a form builder on a phone, with Build and Preview tabs, an Add a field menu, a reorderable list of fields, a settings sheet per field and a live preview rendered by MonarchFieldRenderer.
whenToUse: When people design their own forms in an app (intake, surveys, request forms) and the questions are stored as MonarchFormFieldDefinition data.
whenNotToUse: To fill in a form, render it with MonarchSchemaDrivenForm or MonarchFieldRenderer alone. For a fixed form the app defines, use MonarchFormField and the form controls directly.
api: MonarchTabs("Form builder", selection: $tab, items: [MonarchTabsItem("Build", value: "build"), MonarchTabsItem("Preview", value: "preview")])
Menu { ForEach(palette, id: \.self) { type in Button(typeName(type)) { fields.append(MonarchFormFieldDefinition(…)) } } } label: { Label("Add a field", systemImage: "plus") }
List { ForEach(fields) { field in … }.onMove { fields.move(fromOffsets: $0, toOffset: $1) } }.environment(\.editMode, .constant(.active))
View.accessibilityActions { Button("Move up") { … }; Button("Move down") { … } }
View.sheet(item: $editing) { NavigationStack { Form { MonarchTextField(…); Picker("Type", selection:) {…}.pickerStyle(.menu); Toggle("Required", isOn:) } } }
MonarchFieldRenderer(field, value: $answers[field.id])

options.name: fields
options.description: The form, owned by the app in @State; the same data MonarchFieldRenderer and MonarchSchemaDrivenForm render and the app stores. Definitions are structs with var properties, so the settings sheet edits them through a Binding.

options.name: palette
options.description: The field types the builder offers, named by an app function; the Add a field menu and the Type picker use it.

options.name: settings
options.description: The settings sheet of one field: question, type, required, and any type-specific settings (options, limits) the app supports.

options.name: preview
options.description: MonarchFieldRenderer for every visible field, with answers kept in @State so conditions can be tried.

states.name: build
states.description: The Add a field menu, then the fields in a list in edit mode, each with its type, a required mark as text, a reorder control and an Edit button.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState says there are no fields yet.

states.name: editing
states.description: A sheet with the question, the type, Required, Remove field and Done. A blank question shows an error.

states.name: preview
states.description: The form as people will fill it in, rendered by MonarchFieldRenderer in a Form.

appearance: MonarchTabs, the system menu, list, sheet and form around Monarch text, fields and buttons. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components and the system controls; the type line uses the muted text role.
platformNotes: The web FormBuilder is one component with three columns on wide screens (palette, field list, settings) and fewer on smaller ones; a phone has no room for side-by-side panes, so Build and Preview are tabs, the palette is a system Menu behind Add a field and each field's settings open in a sheet. Every part exists already (MonarchTabs, MonarchFieldRenderer, the system list reordering that reorderable-list documents), so iOS keeps it a recipe, as Android does. Android uses a DropdownMenu, a ModalBottomSheet, MonarchSelect and MonarchSwitchRow; iOS uses Menu, sheet with presentationDetents, Picker(.menu) and Toggle, which are what select and switch are on iOS. Android uses MonarchReorderableList; iOS uses ForEach.onMove in edit mode with the Move up and Move down accessibility actions from the reorderable-list recipe. MonarchFormFieldDefinition is a struct with var properties on iOS, so fields are edited in place through a Binding instead of rebuilt. The web's condition editor, duplicate, undo after remove, maximum field count and the full per-type settings (options, limits, accepted files) are not in the recipe: the app adds the settings it supports to the sheet, and MonarchConditionEditor for logic.
accessibility: Build and Preview are MonarchTabs, with the selected state.
Each field row is one element with its question and type; it has the accessibility actions Move up and Move down as the drag equivalent, and each move is announced with the new position.
Each Edit button is named Edit and the question, so the buttons can be told apart.
The type and required mark are text under the question, not colour.
Settings controls are labelled: the question is a MonarchTextField with an error for a blank question, the type a Picker and Required a Toggle.
The preview is the real form, with MonarchFieldRenderer's labels, required marks and errors.
edgeCases: The list is a scrolling List: make it the screen's list, or give it a bounded height inside a scrolling page.
Removing the field that is being edited closes the sheet; the settings binding reads the field by id, so a field removed elsewhere cannot crash the sheet.
Changing the type keeps the question; settings that belong to the old type are dropped by the app.
The list stays in edit mode so the reorder controls are always shown; an app that also deletes by swipe adds onDelete or switches edit mode with EditButton.
