name: MonarchFormField
title: Field
wrapsNative: VStack or HStack around any control, with accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint applied to the control
summary: A visible label, one control, help text and an error message, with the label and supporting text given to the control for VoiceOver.
whenToUse: For a control that has no label, help or error of its own: a Picker, a Stepper, a Toggle with a description, MonarchTagInput, MonarchRangeSlider or a custom control.
whenNotToUse: MonarchTextField, MonarchPasswordInput and MonarchNumberInput already have a label, help and error; use them alone. Inside a system Form, a plain Toggle or Picker with a Section footer is the native layout.
api: init(_ label: String, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, layout: MonarchFormFieldLayout = .stack, isRequired: Bool = false, mode: MonarchFormFieldMode = .single, optionalText: String? = nil, labels: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels(), @ViewBuilder control: () -> Control)
enum MonarchFormFieldLayout { case stack, row }
struct MonarchFormFieldLabels { init(required: String? = nil, error: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }
enum MonarchFormFieldMode { case single, group }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label. It is also the VoiceOver label of the control.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text. Under the control in the stack layout, under the label in the row layout.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown with an icon under the control and announced when it appears. An empty string is no error.

options.name: layout
options.description: stack puts the label above the control; row puts the label and help text before the control and the error under both.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint of the control.

options.name: mode
options.description: .group for several controls that give one value: each keeps its own label and the field names the group.

options.name: optionalText
options.description: Text after the label of an optional field, such as "Optional". Ignored when isRequired is true.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken "Required" and "Error: …".

options.name: control
options.description: One control without a visible label of its own.

states.name: default
states.description: Label in the default text colour, help text in the muted colour.

states.name: required
states.description: A mark in the danger colour after the label; "Required" at the end of the hint.

states.name: error
states.description: The error replaces the help text in the stack layout and appears under the row in the row layout, in the danger colour with an icon. It is the first part of the hint and is announced when it changes to a new message.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Set with disabled(_:). The control is disabled by the environment; the label, mark and help text take the disabled text colour.

appearance: The label uses the label type style in the default text colour, help text the caption style in the muted text colour, the required mark and the error the strong danger colour. The field draws no box of its own, so it is the same in light, dark and both high-contrast themes apart from those roles.
platformNotes: On the web, Field gives the control its id, aria-describedby, aria-invalid and aria-required through context, and NativeSelect is part of the same file. On iOS there is no id wiring: the field applies accessibilityLabel and accessibilityHint to the control, and there is no invalid or required trait, so the error and "Required" are spoken in the hint. The control is not told it is invalid, so it does not change its border; MonarchTextField has its own error parameter for that. The platform select is Picker, used inside the field. The row layout is an HStack rather than LabeledContent, because LabeledContent restyles its content outside a Form. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The visible label, mark, help text and error are hidden from VoiceOver; the control is labelled with the label instead.
The hint of the control is the error ("Error: …"), the help text and "Required", in that order, each when present; the order is built by a tested pure function.
When the error changes to a new message, it is posted as an announcement.
The error has an icon and text, and the required mark is backed by the spoken "Required", so neither depends on colour.
The row layout becomes a stack at the accessibility text sizes.
edgeCases: The label and hint are applied to the whole control slot. Put one control in it: a control made of several elements, such as MonarchRangeSlider, has its own label parameter and is better given the same text there.
A Toggle in the row layout should use labelsHidden(), or its own label is drawn twice.
A long label and help text wrap; in the row layout the control keeps its size and the text column takes the rest.

name: MonarchFreshnessIndicator
title: FreshnessIndicator
wrapsNative: HStack of Text and MonarchButton, redrawn by TimelineView
summary: How fresh a data set or a sync is ("Updated 3 minutes ago"), turning to warning and danger as it ages, with an optional refresh button.
whenToUse: Above a table, a dashboard or a synced list whose data can age, so people know whether to trust it and can refresh it.
whenNotToUse: For where one value came from, use MonarchProvenance. For whether the person's own edits are saved, use MonarchSaveStatusIndicator.
api: init(updatedAt: Date?, source: String? = nil, details: [String] = [], error: String? = nil, status: MonarchFreshnessStatus? = nil, staleAfter: Duration? = nil, expiredAfter: Duration? = nil, variant: MonarchFreshnessIndicatorVariant = .inline, isRefreshing: Bool = false, labels: MonarchFreshnessIndicatorLabels = MonarchFreshnessIndicatorLabels(), onRefresh: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchFreshnessStatus { case fresh, stale, expired, never, checking, error }
enum MonarchFreshnessIndicatorVariant { case inline, banner }
struct MonarchFreshnessIndicatorLabels { var updated: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var never, checking, stale, expired, error, refresh, refreshing, refreshed, refreshFailed: String? }

options.name: updatedAt
options.description: When the data was last updated or synced. nil means never.

options.name: source
options.description: Names the data or its source, shown first.

options.name: details
options.description: Further facts appended with middle dots. Empty strings are skipped.

options.name: error
options.description: The error text for the error status. Without it "Status unavailable" is shown.

options.name: status
options.description: Overrides the status worked out from the age, for example checking or error.

options.name: staleAfter
options.description: The age after which the data is stale (warning). nil never turns stale.

options.name: expiredAfter
options.description: The age after which the data is expired (danger). nil never expires.

options.name: variant
options.description: inline is a line of muted text; banner is a bordered bar.

options.name: isRefreshing
options.description: A refresh the app tracks is running; the button shows progress.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onRefresh
options.description: Adds a refresh button. The button is busy until the function returns; a thrown error is announced as "Refresh failed."

states.name: fresh
states.description: Success-coloured dot and "Updated 3 minutes ago".

states.name: stale
states.description: Warning-coloured dot, and "Out of date" in bold warning text after the time.

states.name: expired
states.description: Danger-coloured dot, and "Very out of date" in bold danger text after the time.

states.name: never
states.description: Subtle grey dot and "Never updated".

states.name: checking
states.description: Info-coloured dot and "Checking…" in place of the time.

states.name: error
states.description: Danger-coloured dot and the error text, after the time when there is one.

states.name: refreshing
states.description: The refresh button shows a progress indicator and the title "Refreshing…", and ignores further taps.

appearance: Caption text in the muted text colour with a dot in the solid colour of the status tone (subtle text colour for never). Status words are bold, in the strong colour of the tone. The banner adds the subtle background and a subtle border with the control corner radius. The refresh button is a small ghost MonarchButton.
platformNotes: The web component also takes an actions slot for further controls and a live flag to stop the clock; here the line always redraws every minute and the app places other controls beside the view. The web treats onRefresh returning a promise as busy; here onRefresh is an async function. Pull to refresh with refreshable(action:) is the usual companion on iOS. Android shares the name and the statuses.
accessibility: The dot is decorative; stale, expired and error are also written as words, so colour is never the only signal.
The line is one element whose label is the source and the parts joined with pauses, for example "Directory, Updated 2 hours ago, Out of date".
When the status turns stale, expired or error after the first draw, the status words are announced.
The refresh button is a separate standard button with a 44-point touch target; while it runs its value is "Refreshing…", and "Refreshed." or "Refresh failed." is announced at the end.
The text and the dot scale with Dynamic Type; the button moves under the text when they do not fit on one line.
edgeCases: An update time in the future reads "Updated in 2 minutes" and counts as fresh.
The line is redrawn every 60 seconds and one second after each limit, so the status changes on time without a timer in the app.
A long source or many details wrap onto further lines; the dot stays on the first line.

name: MonarchFunnelChart
title: FunnelChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts BarMark(xStart:xEnd:y:) for each stage's bar, inside MonarchChartFrame; Button for selectable stages
summary: A conversion funnel: how many reach each step, the share that continues to the next step and how many drop off.
whenToUse: To show a fixed sequence of steps that people pass through, such as sign-up or hiring, where the drop between steps matters.
whenNotToUse: For values that are not steps of one flow, use MonarchBarList. For change over time, use a line or bar chart in MonarchChartFrame.
api: MonarchFunnelChart.init(_ title: String, stages: [MonarchFunnelChartStage], description: String? = nil, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, alignment: MonarchFunnelChartAlignment = .center, showsSteps: Bool = true, summary: String? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, labels: MonarchFunnelChartLabels = MonarchFunnelChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, formatRate: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchFunnelChartStage) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchFunnelChartStage.init(_ label: String, value: Double, key: String? = nil, color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
enum MonarchFunnelChartAlignment { case center, leading }

MonarchFunnelChartLabels.init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), stage: String? = nil, value: String? = nil, fromPrevious: String? = nil, ofFirst: String? = nil, step: String? = nil, oneStage: String? = nil, stages: String? = nil, overall: String? = nil, largestDrop: String? = nil, describeFirst: String? = nil, describe: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, shown as the frame's heading.

options.name: stages
options.description: The steps, first (widest) to last.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. A ready chart without stages shows the empty state.

options.name: alignment
options.description: Centred bars read as a funnel; leading bars are easier to compare.

options.name: showsSteps
options.description: Shows the line between stages with the share that continued and the number dropped.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that VoiceOver reads for the chart.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are formats with %1$@ placeholders.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a count. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

options.name: formatRate
options.description: Writes a share from 0 to 1. The default is a percentage with at most one decimal.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes every stage a button, for example to list the people who dropped.

states.name: ready
states.description: One row per stage: the step line, the label with its value and share of the first stage, and the bar.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A selectable stage has the muted background while pressed.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table replaces the bars with the counts, the share of the previous stage and the share of the first.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no stages.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's placeholder at the chart's height.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Bars use the first data colour (or the stage's colour slot) on the card surface. Labels and values are default text, the share and step line muted text and the step arrow subtle text, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web FunnelChart highlights a stage on hover and keyboard focus and announces it in a live region; on iOS there is no hover, every stage is its own VoiceOver element instead, and a selectable stage is a button with a pressed state. The web controlled activeIndex is not offered. Web align start is alignment .leading here. Number formats are closures instead of Intl options. The table toggle and its state are inside the component. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, formatRate, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The stages are an accessibility container labelled with the generated summary: the number of stages, the overall conversion and the largest drop, or the summary given.
The container carries an AXChartDescriptor with one point per stage and the formatted counts as point labels, for Audio Graphs.
Each stage is one element read as its label and value, then the share of the previous and of the first stage.
With onSelect each stage is a button at least 44 points high.
Bars and step arrows are hidden from VoiceOver; every number they show is also text.
The frame title is a heading, and View as table lists every count and share.
Labels and values scale with Dynamic Type; the label and value stack when they do not fit on one line, and bar height scales too.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as zero.
A stage after a stage of zero continues at 0%, without dividing by zero.
A stage larger than the one before shows a share above 100% and is not counted as a drop.
A value above zero but tiny next to the widest stage still draws a sliver of bar.
Stage keys default to the label, so give a key when two stages share a label.
The kept height is 76 points per stage with step lines and 56 without, never under 120; text at large sizes makes it taller.

name: MonarchGanttTimeline
title: GanttTimeline
wrapsNative: ScrollView(.horizontal) with anchorPreference, backgroundPreferenceValue and overlayPreferenceValue Canvas drawing (gridlines, weekends, spans, today line, dependency arrows); LongPressGesture sequenced before DragGesture with sensoryFeedback for moving and resizing; accessibilityActions, focusable and onKeyPress; Form with DatePicker in a sheet (Change dates); Menu with an inline Picker (zoom) and Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) (chart or list); DisclosureGroup with .monarch (unscheduled); help(_:) on lane milestones; MonarchCalendarToolbar, MonarchButton, MonarchDivider, MonarchIcon; Date.FormatStyle
summary: Items as bars on a calendar from their first to their last day, with dependency arrows, milestones, a today line, zoom from weeks to years and a list view that writes every date in words and changes dates with the system date pickers.
whenToUse: To plan and reschedule dated work where overlaps and dependencies matter: tasks, phases or issues with start and due dates, in a project or roadmap screen. Save each onChange as it arrives and pass the new items back.
whenNotToUse: For work that moves through statuses without dates use a board or MonarchStepper. For events at times of day use MonarchAgendaList or a calendar. For one date use DatePicker (see date-picker).
api: init(_ items: [MonarchGanttTimelineItem], state: Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState>? = nil, groups: [MonarchGanttTimelineGroup] = [], dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency] = [], milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone] = [], zoomLevels: [MonarchGanttTimelineZoom] = [.month, .quarter, .year], undated: MonarchGanttTimelineUndated = .list, today: Date? = Date(), showsToolbar: Bool = true, labels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineItem) -> Void)? = nil, itemMeta: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineItem) -> AnyView)? = nil, groupMeta: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineGroup) -> AnyView)? = nil, @ViewBuilder toolbarActions: () -> ToolbarActions)

init(_ items: [MonarchGanttTimelineItem], state: Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState>? = nil, groups: [MonarchGanttTimelineGroup] = [], dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency] = [], milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone] = [], zoomLevels: [MonarchGanttTimelineZoom] = [.month, .quarter, .year], undated: MonarchGanttTimelineUndated = .list, today: Date? = Date(), showsToolbar: Bool = true, labels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineItem) -> Void)? = nil, itemMeta: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineItem) -> AnyView)? = nil, groupMeta: (@MainActor (MonarchGanttTimelineGroup) -> AnyView)? = nil) where ToolbarActions == EmptyView

struct MonarchGanttTimelineDates: Hashable, Sendable { init(start: Date?, end: Date?); func shifted(_ shift: MonarchGanttTimelineShift, by days: Int, in calendar: Calendar = .current) -> MonarchGanttTimelineDates }
enum MonarchGanttTimelineShift: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case move, start, end }
enum MonarchGanttTimelineZoom: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case week, month, quarter, year }
enum MonarchGanttTimelineView: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case chart, list }
enum MonarchGanttTimelineUndated: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case list, row }

struct MonarchGanttTimelineState: Hashable, Sendable { init(start: Date? = nil, zoom: MonarchGanttTimelineZoom = .month, view: MonarchGanttTimelineView = .chart, collapsed: Set<String> = []); var start: Date?; var zoom: MonarchGanttTimelineZoom; var view: MonarchGanttTimelineView; var collapsed: Set<String>; mutating func toggle(_ id: String) }

struct MonarchGanttTimelineLabels: Sendable { init(timeline: String? = nil, rowHeader: String? = nil, zoom: String? = nil, zoomName: (@Sendable (MonarchGanttTimelineZoom) -> String)? = nil, earlier: String? = nil, later: String? = nil, today: String? = nil, view: String? = nil, chart: String? = nil, list: String? = nil, milestones: String? = nil, hint: String? = nil, bar: (@Sendable (_ label: String, _ start: String, _ end: String, _ progress: String?) -> String)? = nil, conflict: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, milestone: (@Sendable (_ label: String, _ date: String, _ isDone: Bool) -> String)? = nil, ended: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, starts: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, noDates: String? = nil, unscheduled: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, changed: (@Sendable (_ label: String, _ start: String, _ end: String) -> String)? = nil, changeDates: String? = nil, startDate: String? = nil, endDate: String? = nil, save: String? = nil, cancel: String? = nil, duration: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, progress: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, dependsOn: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, expanded: String? = nil, collapsed: String? = nil, children: (@Sendable (_ count: Int, _ isExpanded: Bool) -> String)? = nil, moveEarlier: String? = nil, moveLater: String? = nil, startEarlier: String? = nil, startLater: String? = nil, endEarlier: String? = nil, endLater: String? = nil, range: (@Sendable (_ from: String, _ to: String) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: items
options.description: The rows: id, label, start and end dates (one of them makes a one-day marker, neither makes it unscheduled), parentID for sub-tasks, groupID, progress from 0 to 1, tone (nil is the accent), isEditable, conflict text and a short meta text.

options.name: state
options.description: The first visible day, the zoom, chart or list, and the collapsed parents. nil keeps the state inside the timeline; with a binding the app reads and sets every value.

options.name: groups
options.description: Heading rows; items with a matching groupID are listed under them. A group with dates shows a thin span on its row.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Links between items, drawn as arrows (finish to start, start to start or finish to finish) and written as "Depends on" in the list. isConflict draws the arrow dashed in the strong danger colour.

options.name: milestones
options.description: Dated checkpoints drawn as diamonds: on their item's row with itemID, otherwise in a lane under the header with their name.

options.name: zoomLevels
options.description: The zoom levels offered in the toolbar's zoom menu. With one level or none there is no menu.

options.name: undated
options.description: Top-level items without dates go in an Unscheduled disclosure group under the chart (.list) or stay as chart rows that say "No dates" (.row).

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day of the today line, read in the environment's calendar. nil hides the line and disables Today. Pass a fixed date in tests and previews.

options.name: showsToolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar: Today, Earlier, Later, the visible range, the zoom menu, the chart and list switch and toolbarActions.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the bar description, the VoiceOver action names, the date sheet and the announcement after a change.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Called once per finished drag, arrow key, VoiceOver action or date sheet save, with the item and its new dates at the start of their days. Without it the timeline is read-only. The timeline never changes items itself.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each bar and the name of each list row a button that opens the item.

options.name: toolbarActions
options.description: Extra controls at the end of the toolbar, such as a filter or a New item button.

options.name: itemMeta
options.description: Extra content under an item's name, after its meta text, in the chart's row labels and the list, such as a status badge or an assignee avatar. VoiceOver reads it where it is drawn.

options.name: groupMeta
options.description: Extra content under a group's heading, after its meta text.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onChange bars have no drag, no key handling and no VoiceOver actions; with onOpen they are still buttons.

states.name: editable
states.description: A visible hint above the chart; each bar moves by touch and hold then drag, its ends by holding within 12 points of an end, by the arrow keys of a hardware keyboard and by six VoiceOver actions. The list shows Change dates, which opens a sheet with two system date pickers.

states.name: dragging
states.description: The bar follows the finger by whole days with a large shadow, the dependency arrows follow it, a haptic tick marks each day and the pick-up has an impact haptic. Release reports the change once.

states.name: conflict
states.description: The bar uses the danger tone with a dashed 2-point outline; the conflict text is read with the bar and written in the list in the strong danger colour.

states.name: one-day marker
states.description: An item with only a start or an end is a small diamond centred on its day; it can only be moved.

states.name: parent
states.description: The row label is a button that reads Expanded or Collapsed and shows a Hide or Show caption; a parent without dates shows a bracket over its children's span.

states.name: outside the window
states.description: The row says "Ended Jan 9, 2026" or "Starts Mar 2, 2026" instead of a bar.

states.name: unscheduled
states.description: Items without dates are listed in an Unscheduled disclosure group under the chart, or as rows saying "No dates".

states.name: list
states.description: A row per group and item with the dates, length, progress, dependencies and conflict in words, then the unscheduled items and the milestones.

appearance: The chart sits on the surface colour with a subtle outline; the header, weekends (week and month zoom) and group rows use the subtle background, gridlines and row lines the subtle border. A bar is a light tint of its tone with an outline and a bottom progress strip in the tone's solid fill (accent by default; neutral uses the muted background and the strong border) and its label in the default text colour. The today line and its label use the accent fill with accent-on-solid text. Arrows use the subtle text colour, or the strong danger colour dashed when broken. Done milestones are filled with the accent; open ones are the surface with a muted outline. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Matches Android's MonarchGanttTimeline names and options, in Swift form: dates are Date values read as calendar days in the environment's calendar and time zone (Android uses UTC day keys in epoch milliseconds, the web ISO strings), the state is a Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState> (nil keeps it inside) instead of a remembered state object, Booleans are isEditable, isDone, isConflict and showsToolbar, and the toolbar arrows come from MonarchCalendarToolbar's SF Symbols, so there are no icon parameters. The web table view becomes a list of rows, the phone and VoiceOver pattern; its date inputs become one Change dates button that opens a sheet with two system DatePickers in a Form (SwiftUI has no date range picker). Web pointer drag becomes touch and hold then drag, so a plain swipe still scrolls the calendar; web keyboard moves stay for hardware keyboards (arrow keys, Shift for the end, Option for the start, without the web's Up and Down jumps between bars) and are also VoiceOver actions. The chart scrolls sideways only, not in two axes as the plan said: it does not scroll vertically, so put it in a scrolling screen, and a drag does not scroll the calendar at its edge. The time axis runs left to right in every layout direction, as on the web and Android; the row labels stay at the leading edge. Weeks start on the calendar's firstWeekday (Android always uses Monday). onChange returns nothing: the web's promise with a saving state and rollback is replaced by the app passing new items (or the old ones) back. Tones are MonarchTone with nil for the web's accent tone, because MonarchTone has no accent. Title and meta are plain strings, not view slots, and the conflict has no warning glyph: the dashed outline and the words carry it. Lane milestones use help(_:), the native tooltip, which iOS exposes as the accessibility hint. Experimental because it is a product pattern not yet adopted by a Rook iOS app. Several closures are optional (onChange, onOpen, itemMeta, groupMeta). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onChange.
accessibility: Each bar is one element read as "<label>, <first day> to <last day>, <n>% complete", with ". Conflict: <message>" when there is a conflict; a one-day marker reads one date.
Every bar has a touch area at least 44 points wide and as tall as the row, around a narrower visible bar; rows are at least 44 points tall.
With onOpen a bar has the button trait and a default action, and the name of a list row is a button.

Editable bars offer VoiceOver actions: Move a day earlier, Move a day later, Start a day earlier, Start a day later, End a day earlier, End a day later (markers only the first two). Locked items and read-only timelines offer none.
After a change the new dates are announced: "Design: Jan 12, 2026 to Jan 24, 2026".
A parent's row label is a button whose value is Expanded or Collapsed, with a visible Hide or Show caption.
The chart and the list are containers named "Timeline"; group labels and list headings have the header trait; header ticks, the today label, gridlines and arrows are hidden from VoiceOver.
Milestones are images read as "Milestone <name>, <date>" with ", done" when reached.
The list writes every date, length, progress, dependency and conflict, so nothing in the chart depends on dragging, colour or position alone.
Rows grow with their label at every Dynamic Type size, so labels wrap instead of being cut; a drag gives a haptic tick per day.
edgeCases: Start after end is swapped; dates at any time of day are read as their calendar day.
A drag, key press or action never lets the first day pass the last when changing one end.
Unknown parent ids, self-parents and parent cycles are ignored; items of groups that are not listed go at the end.
Bars narrower than five edge zones (60 points) hide their label; every bar is at least 6 points wide on screen.
Items outside the visible window show "Ended …" or "Starts …" in their row.
A dependency to an item that is not shown (collapsed or unscheduled) is not drawn.
Long labels wrap and make their row taller; the label inside a bar is cut with an ellipsis but read in full.
The year zoom spans 730 days at 1.6 points a day; the week zoom 28 days at 40 points a day.

name: MonarchGauge
title: Gauge
wrapsNative: Gauge with a custom GaugeStyle
summary: A half-circle meter for one reading against a scale, built on the SwiftUI Gauge: bands give the scale a meaning, a target is marked, and the value is written as text.
whenToUse: For one reading that people judge against a range: utilisation, a health score, a quota used.
whenNotToUse: For progress towards completion, use ProgressView. For several quotas, use MonarchUsageMeter. For a value over time, use MonarchSparkline. In a tight row, the system Gauge styles (accessoryCircular, linearCapacity) are smaller.
api: MonarchGauge.init(_ label: String? = nil, value: Double?, in range: ClosedRange<Double> = 0...100, description: String? = nil, bands: [MonarchGaugeBand] = [], target: Double? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil, indicator: MonarchGaugeIndicator = .arc, size: MonarchGaugeSize = .md, noValueLabel: String? = nil, valueLabel: String? = nil, showsRange: Bool = true, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil)
MonarchGaugeBand.init(_ range: ClosedRange<Double>, tone: MonarchTone, label: String? = nil)

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label under the gauge and its spoken name. "Gauge" is spoken without one.

options.name: value
options.description: The reading. nil shows an empty track and a dash.

options.name: range
options.description: The scale.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: bands
options.description: Stretches of the scale with a tone and a name.

options.name: target
options.description: A target on the scale, marked with a tick and added to the spoken value.

options.name: tone
options.description: The colour of the value arc. nil takes the tone of the value's band, or the accent without bands.

options.name: indicator
options.description: arc fills the track to the value; needle draws the bands on the track and points at the value.

options.name: size
options.description: sm (120), md (160) or lg (200) points wide at most.

options.name: noValueLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text "No data".

options.name: valueLabel
options.description: Replaces the value VoiceOver reads.

options.name: showsRange
options.description: Writes the ends of the scale under the arc.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes every number. The default is a number in the current locale.

states.name: with a value
states.description: The track is filled to the value (arc) or a needle points at it; the value is written in or under the dial.

states.name: in a band
states.description: The arc takes the band's colour and the band's name is written under the value.

states.name: no value
states.description: An empty track, a dash, and "No data" as the spoken value.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Drawn at the nearest end of the scale; the text shows the real value.

appearance: A muted track; the value arc in the accent colour, or the solid colour of its band's tone. Bands use the solid tone colours, and the strong border colour for neutral. The tick and the needle use the default text colour, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web draws its own SVG and exposes a meter role; here the control is a SwiftUI Gauge with an internal GaugeStyle, and the spoken value is set explicitly because a custom gauge style does not carry one. The web size is a number of pixels and the thickness can be set; here there are three sizes and the thickness is 12% of the width. The web tones include accent; here nil is the accent and the other tones are MonarchTone. The scale starts at the leading end, so the dial and its range are mirrored in right-to-left layouts; the web one is not. At accessibility text sizes, and with a needle, the value is written under the dial instead of inside it. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The gauge is one element. Its label is the given label, or "Gauge".
The value is the reading and the name of its band ("72, At risk"), or the reading and the range ("72 (from 0 to 100)"), followed by the target ("Target 80").
Without a value it reads "No data".
The value and the band name are written as text, so the reading does not depend on the arc or its colour.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; the dial keeps its size, and at accessibility sizes the value moves under it so it is never clipped.
The change of the arc and the needle is animated, and not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A range whose ends are equal is widened by one.
A value that is not finite is treated as no value.
A value exactly on the boundary of two bands belongs to the upper one.
A band without a label falls back to the range in the spoken value; give every band a label.
Bands that reach beyond the range are drawn up to its end.

title: GdprEraseFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:content:) with interactiveDismissDisabled, holding a NavigationStack with navigationDestination(for:) for the steps; MonarchConsequenceList (removed and kept), MonarchInlineNotice, Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox), MonarchTypeToConfirmInput, a nested sheet with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog, MonarchEmptyState and LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch) for the audit reference
summary: A recipe, not a component: an admin erases one person's personal data in a sheet that shows what is erased and what is kept with why, asks for an acknowledgement and a typed confirmation, confirms it is them with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog, and ends with the audit reference.
whenToUse: In an admin or privacy screen, to act on a request to erase a person's data (the right to erasure).
whenNotToUse: To delete a whole workspace use the delete workspace recipe. To deactivate an account that can come back use the deactivate recipe.
api: MonarchButton("Erase personal data", variant: .danger) { isOpen = true }
.sheet(isPresented: $isOpen) { NavigationStack { review } .interactiveDismissDisabled(isErasing) }

review: MonarchConsequenceList(erased, heading: "Will be erased"); MonarchConsequenceList(kept, heading: "Will be kept") with each reason as the detail; MonarchInlineNotice(…, title: "This cannot be undone", tone: .warning); NavigationLink("Continue", value: …)

confirm: Toggle("I understand this cannot be undone", isOn:).toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox); MonarchTypeToConfirmInput(phrase:text:onMatchChange:); MonarchButton("Erase data", variant: .danger).disabled(!(understands && isMatched))
.sheet(isPresented: $isVerifying) { MonarchStepUpAuthDialog(description:, onVerified:, onVerify:) }
done: MonarchEmptyState("Personal data erased", kind: .success); LabeledContent("Reference", value: auditID).labeledContentStyle(.monarch)

states.name: review
states.description: What is erased and what is kept (each kept item with the reason and retention period as its detail), a warning notice that it cannot be undone, and Continue.

states.name: review loading
states.description: MonarchConsequenceList with isLoading; Continue is disabled with a caption saying the summary must load.

states.name: confirm
states.description: The pushed screen: the acknowledgement checkbox, the type-to-confirm field (the person's email by default) and a danger Erase data button disabled until both are done, with a caption that says so.

states.name: verifying
states.description: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in a nested sheet; the erasure runs only after it succeeds.

states.name: erasing
states.description: The danger button shows its spinner and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice on the confirm screen, announced.

states.name: done
states.description: A success MonarchEmptyState, the audit reference as a selectable labeled value, "Logged in the audit log", and Close.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component or a system sheet and navigation bar in the theme: two MonarchConsequenceLists with the removed and kept icons, a warning notice, the Monarch checkbox and the danger MonarchButton.
platformNotes: The web's GdprEraseFlow is one component built on a WizardDialog. On iOS it is a recipe: a sheet with a NavigationStack, so review and confirm are pushed screens with the system back button, and the step-up check is MonarchStepUpAuthDialog in a nested sheet. The web's erased and retained lists become MonarchConsequence items of the removed and kept kinds, with the retention reason as the detail. The web's messages, confirmPhrase and auditId are the app's own values here. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The navigation title of each step is read when the step appears; the system back button returns to review.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each item with its kind, so erased and kept do not depend on the icons.
The acknowledgement is a Monarch checkbox read with its checked state; MonarchTypeToConfirmInput announces a match.
The disabled Erase data button has a caption that says what is missing.
The audit reference can be selected and copied.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while erasing.
edgeCases: Re-check the request and the admin's rights on the server; the recipe only gathers the confirmation.
List retained data with the legal reason and how long it is kept, in the words of the policy.
Use something specific to the person as the phrase, such as their email, so the wrong person is not erased.
Record the audit entry on the server and show its id; do not invent one on the device.

name: MonarchGoalTree
title: GoalTree
wrapsNative: Nested VStack rows with a Button toggle per goal (chevron, Expand/Collapse labels); ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.monarchLinear); MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchAvatar, MonarchFlowLayout, MonarchEmptyState
summary: Nested goals (objectives and key results) with progress, status, owner and alignment; branches open and close and each goal can carry its own actions.
whenToUse: For OKRs and other goal hierarchies, where readers scan progress and status and drill into the key results of an objective.
whenNotToUse: For a file or folder hierarchy without progress, use List(_:children:) or OutlineGroup (tree-view). For a flat list of tasks, use a List with MonarchOnboardingChecklist or rows.
api: MonarchGoalTree.init(_ goals: [MonarchGoal], expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isQuietChildren: Bool = true, labels: MonarchGoalTreeLabels = MonarchGoalTreeLabels(), canAddChild: ((MonarchGoal, Int) -> Bool)? = nil, onAddChild: (@MainActor (MonarchGoal) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: @escaping (MonarchGoal) -> Actions)

MonarchGoalTree.init(_ goals: [MonarchGoal], expandedIDs: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, isQuietChildren: Bool = true, labels: MonarchGoalTreeLabels = MonarchGoalTreeLabels(), canAddChild: ((MonarchGoal, Int) -> Bool)? = nil, onAddChild: (@MainActor (MonarchGoal) -> Void)? = nil) where Actions == EmptyView

MonarchGoal.init(id: String, parentID: String? = nil, title: String, progress: Double, status: MonarchGoalStatus, ownerName: String? = nil, ownerAvatarURL: URL? = nil, meta: String? = nil, alignedTo: String? = nil)
enum MonarchGoalStatus { case notStarted, onTrack, atRisk, offTrack, done }

MonarchGoalTreeLabels.init(status: (@Sendable (MonarchGoalStatus) -> String)? = nil, expand: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, collapse: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, alignedTo: String? = nil, addChild: String? = nil, addChildTo: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, childCount: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, empty: String? = nil)

options.name: goals
options.description: Every goal, flat. Nesting comes from parentID; a missing or self-referencing parent makes a top-level goal, and a cycle stops at the first repeat.

options.name: expandedIDs
options.description: The ids of open goals. Kept inside when nil, with every goal that has children open at first.

options.name: isQuietChildren
options.description: Children that are on track or not started hide their badge; their status is still spoken.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the status names, the button names, Aligned to, Add key result, the child count and the empty text.

options.name: canAddChild
options.description: Which goals get the add-child button, from the goal and its depth (0 at the top). Top-level goals when nil.

options.name: onAddChild
options.description: Adds an "Add key result" button inside the open goals canAddChild allows. Receives the parent; the app adds the goal.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls at the end of each goal's row, such as a Menu with Check in and History.

states.name: open
states.description: The chevron points down and the children (and the add button) are shown, indented.

states.name: closed
states.description: The chevron points toward the reading direction and the heading shows the number of children, such as "3 key results".

states.name: quiet children
states.description: Children on track or not started have no badge.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty state, No goals yet.

appearance: Top-level titles use the strong body role and children the body role. Status badges are subtle MonarchStatusBadge capsules in the neutral, info, warning, danger or success tone with a symbol. The bar uses the Monarch linear progress style (accent fill on the muted track) with the percentage in muted caption text. The same roles adapt to dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named OutlineGroup; it cannot be controlled from outside, cannot name its disclosure button "Expand …" and cannot show a child count or an add button, so the tree draws its own rows with a Button toggle. The progress bar is always in the accent colour because MonarchProgressViewStyle has no tone; the web colours the bar by status. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1 (the web takes 0 to 100). Titles, facts and alignment are plain strings. Android uses the same name and API shape. Several closures are optional (canAddChild, onAddChild). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canAddChild.
accessibility: Each goal is one element read as its title, status, owner, facts, alignment and, when closed, its number of children.
The goal's value is its progress as a percentage in the user's locale.
The open and close button is a separate element named "Expand …" or "Collapse …" with a 44-point target.
The add button is named "Add key result to …".
Status badges carry a symbol and a word, so status does not rely on colour; quiet children still speak their status.
The chevron's turn follows Reduce Motion; avatars are hidden from VoiceOver because the owner is in the goal's label.
edgeCases: Progress outside 0 to 1 is clamped; not-a-number and infinity read as 0%.
Long titles wrap; badges and facts flow onto the next line.
A goal whose only child is the add button still has a toggle.
Deep trees indent by half a touch target per level; keep them to three levels on a phone.

title: Grid
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:))], spacing:) for responsive tiles; LazyVGrid with flexible GridItems for a set number of columns; Grid with GridRow for aligned rows and columns
summary: A responsive grid is the standard LazyVGrid, and a table-like layout is the standard Grid, with spacing from the Monarch space scale. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: LazyVGrid with an adaptive GridItem for card grids and tiles: as many columns as fit items of a minimum width. Flexible GridItems for a set number of columns. Grid with GridRow for a small form or a key and value layout whose columns must line up.
whenNotToUse: For a single row that wraps use MonarchFlowLayout (see inline). For long, uniform, selectable rows use List.
api: LazyVGrid(columns: [GridItem], alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, pinnedViews: PinnedScrollableViews = .init(), content: () -> Content)
GridItem(_ size: GridItem.Size = .flexible(), spacing: CGFloat? = nil, alignment: Alignment? = nil)
Grid(alignment: Alignment = .center, horizontalSpacing: CGFloat? = nil, verticalSpacing: CGFloat? = nil, content: () -> Content)
appearance: Layout only; nothing is drawn.
platformNotes: The web's Grid takes minItemWidth (default 16rem) or column counts per breakpoint, a gap from the space scale (default 16px) and fit or fill. On iOS minItemWidth is GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:)), which behaves like the web's fit: columns stretch to share the width. Columns per breakpoint become a count chosen from horizontalSizeClass. Pass theme.spacing values for the gaps; the column gap is set on the GridItem and the row gap on the grid. Android uses LazyVerticalGrid with GridCells.Adaptive.
accessibility: Layout only: no element is added. VoiceOver reads the items in source order, row by row.
Columns follow the layout direction.
Scale the minimum item width with @ScaledMetric so that fewer columns are used at large Dynamic Type sizes.
edgeCases: LazyVGrid creates items lazily only inside a ScrollView; elsewhere it lays out every item.
An adaptive minimum wider than the grid still gives one column, which then overflows; cap it with the available width if items can be that wide.
Grid is not lazy and sizes each column to its widest cell.

name: monarchTextStyle(_:)
title: Heading
wrapsNative: Text with .monarchTextStyle(_:) and .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) or .accessibilityHeading(_:)
summary: A heading is a Text with one of the heading roles of monarchTextStyle(_:) and the header trait. Monarch ships no separate heading type.
whenToUse: For the title of a screen, a section or a card. Choose the role by how large the heading should look: display, title, heading, subheading, bodyStrong or label.
whenNotToUse: Not for the title in a navigation bar; set navigationTitle and leave it to the system. Not for emphasis inside running text; use bodyStrong without the header trait.
api: func monarchTextStyle(_ style: MonarchTextStyle) -> some View
Text("…").accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader)
Text("…").accessibilityHeading(_ level: AccessibilityHeadingLevel)

options.name: style
options.description: The look. display is the web size 4xl, title 2xl, heading xl, subheading lg, bodyStrong base and label sm.

states.name: muted
states.description: A secondary heading takes foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textMuted).

states.name: one line
states.description: lineLimit(1) keeps the heading to one line and ends it with an ellipsis.

appearance: The role sets size, weight, tracking and line spacing; display and title are set tight. The modifier sets no colour: a heading takes the default text colour of the theme, or the muted text colour for a secondary heading.
platformNotes: The web Heading sets the outline level (h1 to h6) and the visual size separately. iOS has no document outline: the header trait makes a text a heading for VoiceOver, and accessibilityHeading(_:) adds a level (h1 to h6) for the rotor when a screen has nested sections. The web sizes 3xl and 5xl have no role; display (4xl) is the nearest. The web weight option is not offered: the role decides the weight. Tone and truncation are the standard foregroundStyle and lineLimit. Android covers this with MonarchText.
accessibility: accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader) lets VoiceOver users move between headings with the rotor.
accessibilityHeading(_:) gives the heading a level from h1 to h6; without it the level is unspecified.
Every role scales with Dynamic Type, including the accessibility sizes.
A heading wraps by default, so no text is lost at large sizes.
edgeCases: The role does not make a text a heading for VoiceOver; the trait must be added.
With lineLimit(1) the cut-off part is still read by VoiceOver, because the label is the whole text.
Text balancing (the web text-wrap: balance) is not available in SwiftUI.

name: MonarchHeatmap
title: Heatmap
wrapsNative: Swift Charts RectangleMark with chartOverlay(_:) and SpatialTapGesture, inside MonarchChartFrame
summary: A matrix of values as shaded cells, such as activity by weekday and hour, with a Less to More legend.
whenToUse: To show where values cluster across two categories, such as weekday by hour or team by week.
whenNotToUse: To compare exact values, use a table or MonarchBarList. For one value per calendar day over months, use a calendar heatmap.

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns, leading to trailing.

options.name: cells
options.description: The values in any order. A row and column pair without a cell is no data.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. A ready chart without any value shows the empty state.

options.name: color
options.description: The data colour of the steps.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when nil.

options.name: showsValues
options.description: Writes each value in its cell when the cell is at least 24 points (scaled with Dynamic Type).

options.name: showsLegend

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that VoiceOver reads for the matrix.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the frame's. Sentences with values are formats with %1$@ placeholders.

options.name: formatValue

options.name: onRetry

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with the tapped cell, or the cell selected with VoiceOver; its value is nil when it has no data.

states.name: ready
states.description: Square cells in five levels: the muted background for zero, four mixes of the data colour, and an outlined empty cell for no data.

states.name: cell selected
states.description: A tapped cell gets a default-text outline, and its row, column and value are written under the matrix.

states.name: values shown
states.description: Values are written in cells with room; on the two strongest levels they sit on a surface chip.

states.name: table
states.description: View as table lists one row per heatmap row and one column per heatmap column, with notes.

states.name: empty
states.description: The frame's empty state, also when the chart is ready but has no value.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's placeholder.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error message, with Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: Levels mix the chosen data colour into the muted background at a quarter, half, three quarters and in full; zero is the muted background and no data is a subtle-border outline on the surface. Axis labels and the legend are muted text; a selected cell is outlined in default text. The mix is computed from the theme's roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes keep five distinct steps.
platformNotes: The web Heatmap shows a tooltip on hover and moves an active cell with the arrow keys; on iOS a tap selects a cell and its details are written under the matrix, and VoiceOver moves through the cells by swiping up and down. The web mixes colours in OKLab; here the mix is per sRGB channel, so middle steps differ slightly in hue. The web maxCellSize and gap props are fixed here (36 points, a small gap), the controlled activeCell is not offered, and the legend is not a separate public view. Column labels that do not fit are dropped by Swift Charts instead of the web's measured spacing. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The matrix is one element labelled with the generated summary (its size and its highest cell) or the summary given.
It is adjustable: swiping up and down visits the cells row by row and its value reads the current cell as row, column and value with its note.
With onSelect it has the button trait and a double tap selects the current cell.
It carries an AXChartDescriptor for Audio Graphs: the columns along the x axis, one series per row, cells without data left out.
The legend is one element named Legend whose value lists each step's range, so the shades are not the only key.
The frame title is a heading, and View as table lists every value as text.
Axis labels, values and the legend scale with Dynamic Type; values show only in cells large enough for the scaled text.
edgeCases: Cells for keys that are not in rows or columns are ignored.
Two cells for the same position: the later one wins.
Negative values are level 0; values that are not finite are no data.
When every value is zero or less, every positive threshold is zero and any later positive value is level 1.
Many columns make cells narrow; Swift Charts drops column labels that would overlap.
A value is written in its cell only when the cell is at least 24 points at the current text size.

summary: A recipe, not a component: the home screen of in-app help, a searchable list of published articles grouped by category, search results while typing, and a contact row at the end.
whenToUse: As the first screen of an app's help, pushed from Settings or presented in a sheet from a Help button, when the app ships a list of articles.
whenNotToUse: For one help topic next to a control, use MonarchInfoTooltip or a footer in the Form section. For a full knowledge base on the web, link to it with Link instead of rebuilding it in the app.

appearance: A system grouped list and navigation bar with the large title, a system search field in the navigation bar, Monarch text styles in the rows, and MonarchSearchResults, the section header and the link in their own theme roles in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web HelpCenterHome is one component with columns, rows, cards and dense layouts, a page heading, an inline SearchInput, router links and a footer. On a phone the expected pattern is a navigation stack: a grouped list of categories, the system search field from .searchable, and a pushed article screen, so Monarch ships no type and the four web layouts become the one list. The web's filterHelpArticles (every word, ignoring case and accents) is localizedStandardContains on each word; groupHelpArticles is grouping by category in first-seen order, articles without one under General. The web's unavailable state is the app not showing the help entry at all. The footer is a Section footer. Android composes the same with its own list and SearchBar.
accessibility: The navigation title is the screen's heading; category section headers have the header trait from the system List.
Each article row is a navigation link read as a button with its title.
The search field is the system field, with its prompt as its label; MonarchSearchResults announces the result count when it changes.
The contact link is named by its text and marked external by MonarchLinkStyle.
Rows and links keep 44-point touch targets and scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Search matches every typed word in the title or category, ignoring case and diacritics; an empty query shows the categories again.
Articles without a category go under a General section, named by the app.
A long list keeps search in the navigation bar; set .searchable(placement: .navigationBarDrawer(displayMode: .always)) to keep the field visible.
When the help is presented in a sheet, add a Done toolbar button that dismisses it.

title: HoverCard
wrapsNative: contextMenu(menuItems:preview:), which shows the preview card on a touch and hold (and a secondary click with a pointer)
summary: A preview card for a link, such as a person or a document, is the system context menu with a custom preview, opened by touching and holding. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To let people peek at what a link points to (a profile, a ticket, a file) and act on it, without opening it.
whenNotToUse: Never for anything essential: touch has no hover and many people never touch and hold. Put the same information one tap away (the link itself, or an info button with a popover, see info-tooltip).

func contentShape(_ kind: ContentShapeKinds, _ shape: some Shape) -> some View

states.name: resting
states.description: The link looks like any link.

states.name: previewing
states.description: After a touch and hold the system lifts the preview card above a blurred screen, with the menu items under it. A tap on the preview can open the destination.

appearance: The system draws the lift, the blur and the menu. The preview is the app's view: give it the theme's raised background and Monarch components so it matches the theme in light, dark and both high-contrast modes.
platformNotes: The web HoverCard opens after a delay on pointer hover or keyboard focus and closes when both leave. Touch has no hover, so iOS uses the touch-and-hold context menu, which also opens with a secondary click on a pointer. There is no delay to set. With a pointer on iPad, onHover could open a popover, but a popover then takes the next tap, so it is not recommended. Android composes the same idea from a long-press gesture.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver offers the context menu actions in the rotor of the link, so the actions are reachable without the gesture; the preview itself is not read.
Keep the link's own action (a tap) as the main way to the content.
Text in the preview scales with Dynamic Type; keep it short so it fits.
edgeCases: The preview sizes to its content; give it a width with frame(idealWidth:) for long text.
A context menu with no items still shows the preview.
Set contentShape(.contextMenuPreview, …) so the lifted shape matches the link's background.

platformNotes: The web ships IdentityBar as a sticky <header> with product, start, search, notifications, actions and account slots. On iOS the navigation bar is the banner, so the recipe fills the bar's slots instead of drawing a bar: the product goes in the navigation placement, search uses searchable, which the system places under the title, and the trailing actions go in the primary action group. The web's sticky option is the navigation bar's own behaviour. The start slot (breadcrumb or space switcher) is the navigationTitle or a title menu. Rook account opens in the browser; use openURL in its action.
accessibility: The product label has the header trait; its icon is part of the label.
The search field is the system search field with its prompt as the placeholder and label.
MonarchNotificationsBell reads "Notifications" with the unread count.
The account menu is named "Account: <name>" with accessibilityLabel; the avatar inside is decorative and keeps a 44-point target with monarchMinimumHitTarget().
Sign out uses the destructive role, which VoiceOver announces.
edgeCases: On a narrow phone the system may move toolbar items into an overflow menu; keep the trailing group to the bell and the account.
A long product name truncates in the bar; keep it short.
Without search, leave out searchable.

wrapsNative: ViewThatFits with HStack and VStack, Text with an AttributedString, TimelineView(.everyMinute) with Date.RelativeFormatStyle, MonarchButton; placed with .safeAreaInset(edge: .top)

whenToUse: While a support or admin person is signed in as, or viewing as, another person, and anything they do happens in that person's account.
whenNotToUse: For a read-only preview with no real actions, a MonarchCalloutBanner is enough. For ordinary notices such as a trial ending, use MonarchCalloutBanner with the page placement.

struct MonarchImpersonationBannerLabels { init(viewingAs: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, started: String? = nil, reason: String? = nil, stop: String? = nil, stopLabel: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, stopError: String? = nil) }

options.name: name
options.description: The person being viewed as, in bold in the main line.

options.name: detail
options.description: A second identifier, such as their email, in brackets after the name in the muted inverse colour.

options.name: reason
options.description: Why the session started, such as a ticket number, after "Reason:".

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the session started, shown as "Started 5 minutes ago" and refreshed every minute.

options.name: isStopping
options.description: Controls the busy state of Stop when the app tracks the stop itself; tracked from onStop when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the main line, "Started", "Reason:", "Stop", its spoken name and the fallback error.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Ends the session. The button is busy while it runs and ignores taps; throwing shows the error's description (or the fallback) in the banner.

states.name: active
states.description: The eye icon, the main line, the start and reason line, and Stop.

states.name: stopping
states.description: Stop shows its spinner and ignores taps.

states.name: error

appearance: Inverse colours (the inverse background with inverse text, muted inverse text for the detail and meta line) and a three-point edge and icon in the solid warning colour, so it looks unlike every other banner in light, dark and high-contrast themes. Stop is a small secondary button; when the text and button do not fit on one line, the button moves below and fills the width.
platformNotes: The web's sticky prop is replaced by placement: on iOS the app puts the banner in safeAreaInset(edge: .top) of its root view, which keeps it above scrolling content. The web's now and locale props are not needed; the relative time uses the system clock and locale. A replacement main line from labels is shown without bold, because the bold name needs the built-in format. Android builds the same component. The parity map names MonarchBanner and lists callout-banner as a dependency; the banner is drawn on its own instead, because its inverse colours, warning edge and missing dismiss button are what set it apart from callout banners, as on the web.
accessibility: The icon is decorative; the text is one element read as the main line with the name and detail, then the start and reason line.
The main line is posted as an announcement when the banner appears, like the web's status region.
Stop is named "Stop viewing as" and the name, which starts with its visible title, and has a 44-point touch target; it shows a busy state while stopping.
A failed stop is announced and shown with an icon and text.
There is no dismiss button: the only way out is to stop.
edgeCases: Long names, details and reasons wrap.
The app removes the banner when the session ends; a successful onStop does not hide it by itself.
With isStopping set, taps while it is true are ignored even if onStop has returned.

whenToUse: When people bring a spreadsheet of records into the app, such as contacts, products or members, and need to match columns and see problems before anything is saved.
whenNotToUse: For attaching a file to a record use MonarchFileUpload alone. For a short task without a file use the wizard-dialog recipe. On iPad or Mac, where a wide table fits, the same steps can be pushed screens instead of a sheet.

states.description: MonarchFileUpload limited to one CSV file; a file that cannot be read, or has no data rows, shows a danger MonarchInlineNotice and stays on this step.

states.name: map
states.description: MonarchColumnMapping pre-filled from MonarchColumnMapping.suggest; Check rows is disabled while a required field has no column.

states.name: preview
states.description: MonarchPreviewRows shows each row's status; rows with errors are skipped and the button reads "Import 2 rows". Nothing is saved yet.

states.name: importing
states.description: A linear ProgressView reads Importing 2 rows…, the import button shows its spinner, and Back and Cancel are disabled.

states.name: results

states.name: started
states.description: After the first step the sheet cannot be swiped away; Cancel in the toolbar closes it.

appearance: A system sheet on the theme's surface colour with MonarchStepper, Monarch text styles, the mapping and preview components in their own theme colours, the Monarch linear progress style, and a bottom bar with a secondary Back and a primary next button.
platformNotes: The web ImportWizard is one component that parses the CSV itself, offers a template download and a downloadable problems CSV, validates rows through a callback, picks a duplicate rule and reports created, updated, skipped and failed counts. On iOS the app composes the steps: it reads the file with TabularData's DataFrame (or its own parser), validates rows into MonarchPreviewRow errors and warnings, and shows the report; a problems file can be offered with ShareLink, and a duplicate rule with a Picker on the preview step. The web shows the preview as a wide table; on iPhone MonarchPreviewRows lays rows out for the narrow screen. Android plans the same recipe. Status experimental: it is a product pattern until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: MonarchStepper reads "Step 2 of 4" and each step's state; the step title has the header trait.
Post an AccessibilityNotification.Announcement of the new step when Continue or Back changes it, since focus stays on the button.
MonarchFileUpload, MonarchColumnMapping and MonarchPreviewRows keep their own labels, values and announcements.
The progress view is read with its title and percentage; failures are text with an icon, not colour alone.
Cancel is in the toolbar with the cancellation placement, so it remains once swiping the sheet away is disabled.
edgeCases: A file with only a header row, or without column names, stays on the upload step with a message.
Duplicate header names: give the later ones a suffix before building the mapping sources.
Very large files: read and validate off the main actor and show the first rows in the preview; MonarchPreviewRows pages its rows.
When no row can be imported, disable the import button and say why.
Reset every step's state when the sheet is presented again.

states.name: read
states.description: Regular title, muted age, no mark.

states.name: unread
states.description: An accent dot before a bold title, and the age in the default text colour and semibold.

states.name: unread count
states.description: An accent capsule with the count, or 99+, at the end of the first line instead of the dot.

states.name: selected
states.description: The List's own selection highlight, and checkboxes in edit mode.

states.name: swiping
states.description: The system swipe actions with tinted buttons: info for read, accent for archive, danger for delete.

appearance: Title in the default text colour, preview and age in the muted text colour, the unread dot and count in the accent's solid colour with its on-solid text. Swipe actions are tinted with the info, accent and danger solid colours. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web row is a link with its own checkbox, long-press selection, current and keyboard-cursor states. On iOS opening, the open-conversation highlight, multi-selection in edit mode and keyboard focus come from List, NavigationLink and List(selection:), so the row does not draw them. Swipe actions follow Mail and have no web equivalent. Age units are overridable together through labels.age; the short date uses the view's locale and calendar.
accessibility: The row is one element read as the title, the unread state ("3 unread"), the channel, the full date and time, the preview, then the badges and trailing content.
The compact age is replaced by the full date and time for VoiceOver.
The unread dot and count are hidden; the state is spoken after the title, and shown by a bold title, so it does not depend on colour.
Swipe actions are also available as VoiceOver actions, named "Read" or "Unread", "Archive" and "Delete".
The avatar is decorative; a channel symbol is read only when it has a label.
The row is at least 44 points high and grows with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A time in the future reads as now.
Counts above 99 show 99+, while VoiceOver reads the exact number.
A count of zero with isUnread false is a read row.
Older than 30 days shows a short date, with the year when it is not the current year.
The title and preview are cut to one line each; badges and trailing content share the last line.

name: MonarchIncidentTimeline
title: IncidentTimeline
wrapsNative: VStack of updates on a drawn line, MonarchStatusBadge for each stage, MonarchTag for Automated, MonarchFlowLayout for the header, DateFormatter with a fixed time zone
summary: The story of one incident: each update with its stage (investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved), time and text, joined by a line, with system-posted updates tagged Automated.
whenToUse: On a status page or an incident detail screen, to show every update posted during one incident in order.
whenNotToUse: For a feed of many kinds of activity across objects use MonarchActivityTimeline. For the overall state of a service use MonarchStatusBadge or MonarchUptimeBar.
api: init(_ updates: [MonarchIncidentUpdate], stages: [String: MonarchStatusDefinition] = [:], density: MonarchIncidentTimelineDensity = .regular, isLive: Bool = false, timeZone: TimeZone? = TimeZone(identifier: "UTC"), labels: MonarchIncidentTimelineLabels = MonarchIncidentTimelineLabels())

struct MonarchIncidentUpdate: Identifiable { init(id: String, stage: String, body: String, time: Date, isAutomated: Bool = false, author: String? = nil); init(id: String, stage: MonarchIncidentStage, body: String, time: Date, isAutomated: Bool = false, author: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchIncidentStage: String { case investigating, identified, monitoring, resolved }
enum MonarchIncidentTimelineDensity { case regular, compact }

struct MonarchIncidentTimelineLabels { init(list: String? = nil, automated: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, investigating: String? = nil, identified: String? = nil, monitoring: String? = nil, resolved: String? = nil) }

options.name: updates
options.description: The updates in the order to show them, usually oldest first. Each has a stage key, the text (line breaks kept), the time, whether the system posted it and an optional author.

options.name: stages
options.description: Product stages by key, or overrides of the label and tone of the standard ones. Looked up before the standard stages.

options.name: density
options.description: compact tightens the space between updates for cards and side panels.

options.name: isLive
options.description: Announces an update added while the view is shown, for a page that refreshes while someone reads it.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone of the times. UTC by default, so every reader quotes the same time; the zone name is shown. nil is the device's zone (.autoupdatingCurrent), read each time.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list name, the Automated tag, the empty text and the four standard stage labels.

states.name: investigating
states.description: Danger tone badge and dot, "Investigating".

states.name: identified
states.description: Warning tone badge and dot, "Identified".

states.name: monitoring
states.description: Info tone badge and dot, "Monitoring".

states.name: resolved
states.description: Success tone badge and dot, "Resolved".

states.name: product stage
states.description: A key from stages uses its label and tone; an unknown key is made readable ("partial_outage" is "Partial outage") with the neutral tone and a strong border dot.

states.name: automated
states.description: An update the system posted carries an "Automated" tag after the time.

states.name: empty
states.description: No updates shows "No updates posted yet" in the muted text colour.

appearance: Dots use the solid role of the stage tone (the strong border for neutral) on a line in the default border colour. Badges keep the status badge look; times and authors use the muted text colour, the body the default text colour, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web accepts rich content for the body and author and a footer slot; on iOS they are strings, and the app places its own form under the view. The web formats times with Intl in UTC; iOS uses the locale's month, day and 24-hour time pattern with the zone name in the given time zone, so the characters differ slightly from the web. Stage tones are given as MonarchStatusDefinition, the same type the status badge uses. Android uses the same name and model.
accessibility: The updates are one container named "Incident updates".
Each update is one element read as the stage, the time, the author and "Automated", then the text.
The stage is a word in a badge as well as a colour; dots and the line are hidden from VoiceOver.
With isLive, an update added while the view is shown is announced with the same text.
Text wraps at every Dynamic Type size and the dot column scales with it.
edgeCases: Updates are shown in the order given; the view does not sort them.
Stage keys are matched to the standard stages ignoring case; product keys in stages are matched exactly and win.
An empty body shows only the header line.
Removing updates or replacing the list with a shorter one announces nothing.

whenNotToUse: Do not draw a custom ringing screen. For a message that is not a call, use a notification.

On iOS the system popover moves VoiceOver focus into the explanation, which reads it, so no announcement is added. The web's align and iconNode are not offered: the system positions the popover, and the glyph is one of two SF Symbols. contentClassName has no equivalent. Android plans the native tooltip instead of a component.
accessibility: The button is named by label, "More information" by default; the glyph is hidden from VoiceOver.
System behaviour: when the popover opens, VoiceOver focus moves into it and reads the explanation; the escape gesture or a tap outside closes it and focus returns to the button.

wrapsNative: AttributedString runs (inlinePresentationIntent .code, SwiftUI foregroundColor and backgroundColor attributes) drawn by Text
summary: The look of a code fragment inside running text, as attributes of an AttributedString run: the monospaced face at the size of the surrounding text, on a muted background (subtle) or without one (plain).
whenToUse: For a function name, a path, a command or a value to type inside a sentence. Use markdown(_:in:textStyle:) for text with backticks, attributedString(_:in:textStyle:) for a single fragment.
whenNotToUse: Not for a block of code or anything longer than a few words; set that as its own Text with the code role of monarchTextStyle. Not for keyboard shortcuts; use MonarchKbd.
api: init(variant: MonarchInlineCodeVariant = .subtle)
static let subtle: MonarchInlineCodeStyle
static let plain: MonarchInlineCodeStyle
func attributes(in theme: MonarchTheme, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body) -> AttributeContainer
