func markdown(_ markdown: String, in theme: MonarchTheme, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body) -> AttributedString
enum MonarchInlineCodeVariant { case subtle, plain }

options.name: variant
options.description: subtle draws a muted background behind the code; plain only switches to the monospaced face.

options.name: theme
options.description: The theme from the environment. An attributed string holds colours, not roles, so the theme is passed in.

options.name: textStyle
options.description: The type role of the surrounding text. Used only when the theme has its own code font family, to size that font.

appearance: The code is in the default text colour and the monospaced face. Subtle adds the muted background colour of the theme behind the characters; plain adds nothing. The colours are those of the theme passed in, so the text is rebuilt when the theme changes.
platformNotes: The web InlineCode is an element; on iOS running text is one Text, so the style produces AttributedString runs instead of a view. Text draws the background flush with the characters: the padding and the rounded corners of the web chip are not available, and the code is the size of the surrounding text, not 0.9 of it. The web nowrap option is not offered; a long token breaks where it does not fit. Android covers this with a text style in MonarchTypography.
accessibility: The code run is part of the Text and is read by VoiceOver in place, as its characters.
Code differs from the text around it by the monospaced face, so it is recognisable without the background colour, including in the plain variant.
With the system font the run follows the size of the surrounding text at every Dynamic Type size. A custom code font family is sized from the given role and scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: The attributed string holds resolved colours. Build it in the view body from the environment's theme so that it follows light, dark and high contrast.
markdown(_:in:textStyle:) reads inline Markdown only and keeps white space. An unmatched backtick is shown as it is. Text that cannot be parsed is shown unchanged.
applied(to:in:textStyle:) styles only runs whose inline presentation intent contains code and keeps their other attributes.
A long token such as a hash wraps by character where it does not fit a line.

title: InlineEditText
wrapsNative: Button that swaps to TextField (or TextEditor for several lines) with @FocusState; MonarchButton for Save and Cancel
summary: Text that turns into a field in place, with an asynchronous save, a pending state and an error that keeps the editor open.
whenToUse: For one value that is edited where it is shown: a title, a name, a short description.
whenNotToUse: For several fields edited together, use a form with MonarchTextField and Save in the toolbar. For text that is always editable, use MonarchTextField.
api: init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, isMultiline: Bool = false, startsEditing: Bool = false, trimsWhitespace: Bool = true, savesOnFocusLoss: Bool = true, editHint: String? = nil, saveTitle: String? = nil, cancelTitle: String? = nil, savingLabel: String? = nil, failureMessage: String? = nil, validate: (@MainActor (String) -> String?)? = nil, onCancel: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSave: @escaping @MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)

options.name: label
options.description: What the text is, for example "Title". Read by VoiceOver; not drawn.

options.name: text
options.description: The saved value. Written after a successful save.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in view mode while the value is empty, and as the placeholder of the field.

options.name: error
options.description: An error from the app, for example an edit conflict, shown while editing.

options.name: isMultiline
options.description: Uses a TextEditor: Return adds a line and Save saves.

options.name: startsEditing
options.description: Opens the editor when the view first appears.

options.name: trimsWhitespace
options.description: Trims the draft before comparing and saving.

options.name: savesOnFocusLoss
options.description: Saves the draft when focus leaves the field.

options.name: editHint
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Edit" hint.

options.name: saveTitle
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Save" title.

options.name: cancelTitle
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Cancel" title.

options.name: savingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Saving" spoken value of the Save button.

options.name: failureMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in message of a failed save whose error has no description.

options.name: validate
options.description: Returns a message to refuse a draft before saving.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Runs when the person cancels.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Persists a new value. Not called when the value is unchanged. Throwing keeps the editor open.

states.name: viewing
states.description: The value in the default text colour with a small pencil; an empty value shows the prompt in the subtle colour.

states.name: editing
states.description: A bordered field with the focus ring, and Save and Cancel buttons under it.

states.name: saving
states.description: The field is disabled, Save shows progress and Cancel is disabled.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger border, and an icon and message under the field. The draft is kept.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(_:) the value is plain text in the disabled colour and cannot be edited.

appearance: View mode is body text with a muted pencil. The editor is a surface-coloured field with an input border and 8-point corners, the theme's focus ring, a small primary Save button and a ghost Cancel button. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: On the web, Enter saves and Escape cancels, and Save and Cancel buttons are optional for a single line. A touch keyboard has no Escape key, so on iOS the two buttons are always shown; Return still saves a single line and a hardware Escape still cancels. The web shows a spinner inside the field; here the Save button shows the progress. The value is a binding that the component writes after onSave succeeds, in place of the web's controlled value. The web's controlled editing state is reduced to startsEditing, and onSaveError is the error thrown by onSave, which the app can catch inside its own closure. The multi-line editor has a fixed height that scales with Dynamic Type and scrolls, because TextEditor does not size itself to its text. Several closures are optional (validate, onCancel). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is validate.
accessibility: In view mode it is one button: label, then the value (or the prompt) as the value, then "Edit" as the hint.
In edit mode the field has the same label, and an error is its hint, spoken as "Error: …".
A new error is announced when it appears, and is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
While saving, the Save button's value is "Saving".
The text in view mode and the field are at least 44 points high; text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A draft equal to the saved value closes the editor without calling onSave.
A draft that has just been refused or has failed is not saved again when focus leaves the field.
A second save and Cancel are ignored while a save runs.
An error of a type that conforms to LocalizedError shows its errorDescription; any other error shows failureMessage or the built-in sentence.
With no value and no prompt the view mode shows only the pencil.
If the view goes away while a save runs, the save still finishes and writes the binding.

name: MonarchInsightStrip
title: InsightStrip
wrapsNative: ScrollView(.horizontal) with containerRelativeFrame and scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), VStack, LazyVGrid; MonarchAiInsightCallout
summary: A row of insights for the top of a dashboard, each labelled with whether a rule or a model raised it, ordered most severe first.
whenToUse: At the top of a dashboard or a record, for a few things that need attention now.
whenNotToUse: For one message about the content next to it use MonarchBanner. Do not label a rule-based insight as AI.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, insights: [MonarchInsight], layout: MonarchInsightStripLayout = .scroll, isLoading: Bool = false, error: String? = nil, labels: MonarchInsightStripLabels = MonarchInsightStripLabels(), limit: Int? = nil, sortsBySeverity: Bool = true, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDismiss: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchInsight { init(id: String, title: String, why: String, tone: MonarchTone = .info, origin: MonarchInsightOrigin, evidence: String? = nil, actionTitle: String? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) }
enum MonarchInsightOrigin { case rule, ai }
enum MonarchInsightStripLayout { case scroll, stack, grid }

struct MonarchInsightStripLabels { init(showMore: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, showLess: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil, retry: String? = nil, dismiss: String? = nil, evidence: String? = nil, ruleOrigin: String? = nil, aiOrigin: String? = nil) }

options.name: title
options.description: A heading for the strip.

options.name: insights
options.description: The insights. Each has an id, a title, a reason, a tone, an origin and optionally evidence and one action.

options.name: layout
options.description: scroll is one row that scrolls sideways one card at a time, stack one column, grid as many columns as fit.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows three placeholder cards instead of the insights.

options.name: error
options.description: A failure message, which replaces the insights.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: limit
options.description: Show at most this many, with a toggle for the rest.

options.name: sortsBySeverity
options.description: Orders danger, warning, info, success, neutral; the given order is kept within a tone.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: With error, adds a "Try again" button.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button to every insight; the app removes the insight.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three cards drawn as placeholders with redacted(reason: .placeholder).

states.name: error
states.description: The message with an icon in the strong danger colour, and "Try again" when onRetry is given.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Nothing needs attention right now." with a checkmark.

states.name: limited
states.description: Only the first insights are shown, with "Show N more"; then "Show fewer".

appearance: Each insight is a MonarchAiInsightCallout: the tone sets the fill, border, leading bar and icon; the title, the reason and an origin label follow, neutral for a rule and in the assistant colours for a model.
platformNotes: Like the web, the strip is built from the insight callout (MonarchAiInsightCallout). Severity is MonarchTone (danger for critical, success for positive) instead of a separate severity type, and the spoken prefix is the tone name. Evidence is a String in a collapsed section, not arbitrary content. The default layout is the scrolling row; grid and stack are also offered. Moving VoiceOver focus to the next insight after a dismissal, which the web does, is not implemented. The web empty={null} has no counterpart: leave the strip out instead. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onDismiss). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each insight title is read with the tone name first and the origin label after it, then the reason follows, so neither the tone nor the origin depends on colour or an icon.
The evidence section, the action and the dismiss button are separate elements with 44-point touch targets.
The dismiss button is named "Dismiss insight".
The loading placeholder is one element named "Loading insights".
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps inside the cards.
edgeCases: In the scrolling row every card is 86% of the width, so cards in one row can differ in height.
A limit of zero or less is ignored.
An insight with an actionTitle but no action shows no button.
After a dismissal VoiceOver focus is left to the system.
The built-in "Show N more" text is English; pass labels.showMore for other languages.

            actionTitle: "Review renewals",
            action: {}
        ),
        MonarchInsight(
            id: "usage",
            title: "Weekly use is falling",
            why: "Active people fell from 48 to 29 over the last 30 days.",
            tone: .warning,
            origin: .ai
        ),
        MonarchInsight(

            why: "A response is due on 19 November.",

name: MonarchInstallVerify
title: InstallVerify
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchCodeSnippetTabs, MonarchCopyButton and a mailto Link for the developer handoff, ProgressView while waiting, Link for the test page, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when connected
summary: Install a snippet on a website and wait for it to report: code for each platform with copy, a handoff to a developer (copy the instructions or email them), then a waiting status until the product sees the code.
whenToUse: In an onboarding or settings screen where a person adds a script, tag or plugin to their own website and the product confirms it is live.
whenNotToUse: For code examples with nothing to verify use MonarchCodeSnippetTabs. For a key alone use MonarchCopyField or MonarchKeyCreatedDialog. For domain records use MonarchDnsRecordTable and MonarchDomainProgress.
api: init(snippets: [MonarchInstallSnippet], status: MonarchInstallVerifyStatus, selection: Binding<String>? = nil, targets: [MonarchInstallTarget] = [], connectedOn: [String]? = nil, developerInstructions: String? = nil, testURL: URL? = nil, isTestDisabled: Bool = false, testHint: String? = nil, part: MonarchInstallVerifyPart = .all, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchInstallVerifyLabels = MonarchInstallVerifyLabels(), onConnected: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder credential: () -> Credential)
init(snippets:status:selection:targets:connectedOn:developerInstructions:testURL:isTestDisabled:testHint:part:now:labels:onConnected:) where Credential == EmptyView
struct MonarchInstallSnippet { init(_ label: String, code: String, language: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, id: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchInstallTarget { init(_ label: String, lastSeen: Date? = nil, id: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchInstallVerifyStatus { case waiting, connected, unavailable }
enum MonarchInstallVerifyPart { case all, install, verify }

struct MonarchInstallVerifyLabels { var installHeading, verifyHeading, platforms, shareInstructions, emailDeveloper, shareSubject, waitingTitle, connectedBody, unavailableTitle, unavailableBody, targets, notSeen, openTest, openTestHint: String?; var waitingBody, connectedTitle: (@Sendable ([String]) -> String)?; var seen: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? }

options.name: snippets
options.description: The ways to install, one tab each, with an optional line on where the code goes. One snippet shows without tabs.

options.name: status
options.description: waiting, connected or unavailable. The app changes it when the code reports.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected snippet's id, when the app controls it. Kept inside otherwise.

options.name: targets
options.description: The sites the install is expected on, each with when it last reported.

options.name: connectedOn
options.description: The sites named in the connected title. By default the targets that reported.

options.name: developerInstructions
options.description: Plain text for a developer. Shows a copy button and an Email them link.

options.name: testURL
options.description: A page where the install can be tried, opened in the browser. Addresses that are not http or https are not shown.

options.name: isTestDisabled
options.description: Disables the test button; say why in testHint.

options.name: testHint
options.description: One line under the test button.

options.name: part
options.description: Both halves under Install and Verify headings, or one half without a heading for a step of a wizard.

options.name: now
options.description: The time relative times are measured from. By default the time of drawing; inject it in tests.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onConnected
options.description: Runs once, the first time this view shows the connected status, for example to move a wizard on.

options.name: credential
options.description: The key or credential the snippet needs and its state, above the snippets, such as a MonarchCopyField.

states.name: waiting
states.description: An info-tinted box with a system progress indicator, "Waiting for your site…" and which sites to open.

states.name: connected
states.description: A success-tinted box with a check mark and "Connected on www.example.com"; the change is announced.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A neutral box with an info symbol, "Live verification isn’t available" and how to check by hand.

states.name: site seen or not
states.description: Each site has a dot (success once seen, neutral before) and "seen 5 minutes ago" or "not seen yet".

states.name: test disabled
states.description: The Open a test page button is disabled with the hint under it.

states.name: install or verify only
states.description: One half, without headings.

appearance: Headings in the default text role. The snippets are MonarchCodeSnippetTabs with the pill tabs. The status box is the subtle surface of its tone (info, success or neutral) with the tone's border; help text and times use the muted text role. The copy button and the test button are secondary Monarch buttons and Email them a ghost link. All follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The copy button and the Email them mailto link are the web's. The web's snippet box is a multi-line copy field; on iOS it is a code block with its copy button inside MonarchCodeSnippetTabs. The test page opens in the browser with Link instead of a new tab. The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent: headings carry the header trait. Times are RelativeDateTimeFormatter text instead of RelativeTime with a tooltip. Android has no entry yet. Marked experimental as a product composite until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: "Install" and "Verify" have the header trait.
The status box is one element read as its title and text; while waiting it has the updates-frequently trait.
A change to connected is announced with the connected title.
Each site is one element read as its name with "seen 5 minutes ago" or "Not seen" as its value; the dot is hidden.
The test button is a link with the hint "Opens in Safari."
The code block, tabs and buttons are standard controls with 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: A test URL with another scheme (javascript:, file:) or no host is not shown.
onConnected runs once for the life of the view, including when it first appears already connected.
Site names are joined with commas; pass labels.waitingBody and labels.connectedTitle for "a, b and c" in other languages.
Long host names wrap; the code block scrolls sideways inside itself.

title: InviteMembersDialog
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) with a NavigationStack, a ScrollView around MonarchTagInput, MonarchRolePicker, MonarchAppAccessPicker and MonarchTextField, cancellation and confirmation ToolbarItems, and interactiveDismissDisabled(_:) while sending
summary: A recipe, not a component: invite people by email with a role and app access, from a sheet with Cancel and Send in the navigation bar, reporting the addresses that could not be invited.
whenToUse: When a workspace admin adds people by email from a members screen.
whenNotToUse: For assigning existing members to something, use MonarchAssigneePicker. For a shareable invite link, show the link with a ShareLink instead of a form.
api: .sheet(isPresented: $isOpen) { NavigationStack { ScrollView { form }.navigationTitle("Invite people").toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .cancellationAction) { … } ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) { Button("Send invite") { … } } } }.interactiveDismissDisabled(isSending) }
MonarchTagInput("Email addresses", tags: $emails, separators: [",", " "], maxCount:, validate: { value, _ in … })
MonarchRolePicker("Role", selection: $role, roles: [MonarchRoleOption(…)], layout: .compact)
MonarchAppAccessPicker([MonarchAppAccessOption(…)], selection: $apps, label: "App access")
MonarchTextField("Personal note (optional)", text: $note)
MonarchBanner("Some invitations were not sent", message:, tone: .warning)

states.name: empty
states.description: Send invite is disabled until at least one valid address and a role are chosen.

states.name: filled
states.description: Each address is a removable tag; the confirmation button reads Send 3 invites.

states.name: invalid address
states.description: MonarchTagInput refuses the text and shows why, such as “ana” is not an email address.

states.name: sending
states.description: A progress bar shows and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: partial failure
states.description: A warning banner lists the addresses that failed with the reason; only those stay in the field.

states.name: done
states.description: The sheet closes and "Invited 3 people" is announced.

appearance: A system sheet with a navigation bar; the fields are Monarch's tag input, role picker, app access picker and text field on the canvas background, and failures are a warning MonarchBanner. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web InviteMembersDialog is one component with a trigger, controlled open state, email parsing, maxEmails and plural messages. On iOS it is a recipe: a sheet with Cancel and Send in the navigation bar is the system's form pattern, MonarchTagInput splits and checks the addresses, plural text comes from the app's String Catalog, and the app's invite call returns the failed addresses. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The sheet's navigation title is read first; Cancel and Send are the system's toolbar buttons.
MonarchTagInput announces each address added or removed and reads why an address was refused.
MonarchRolePicker and MonarchAppAccessPicker read each choice with its selected state.
Announce the result with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when the sheet closes.
edgeCases: Keep the addresses that failed in the field so the admin can fix and resend them.
Lock the sheet with interactiveDismissDisabled while sending.
Pasting several addresses at once is split on the separators.
The role picker's compact layout keeps the sheet short; use .cards when roles need their descriptions.

name: MonarchInvoiceView
title: InvoiceView
wrapsNative: VStack and Grid with LabeledContent (.monarch(.inline)), MonarchMoney and MonarchStatusBadge; printing through ImageRenderer to PDF and UIPrintInteractionController
summary: A read-only invoice: issuer and billed party, number, dates and status, billed lines, totals, notes and small print, with an optional Print button that opens the system print panel.
whenToUse: Showing an invoice that has been issued (sent, paid, overdue or cancelled), in an invoice detail screen or a client portal, and printing it or saving it as a PDF.
whenNotToUse: For many invoices, use a list of rows with MonarchMoney and MonarchStatusBadge. For a payment receipt file, use MonarchReceiptPreview. For payroll, use MonarchPayslipView. Monarch for iOS has no line items editor yet for creating invoice lines.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, number: String? = nil, status: MonarchStatusDefinition? = nil, issueDate: Date? = nil, dueDate: Date? = nil, details: [MonarchInvoiceDetail] = [], brand: Image? = nil, from: MonarchInvoiceParty? = nil, to: MonarchInvoiceParty? = nil, items: [MonarchInvoiceLineItem], currencyCode: String, locale: Locale? = nil, taxRate: Decimal? = nil, discount: MonarchInvoiceDiscount? = nil, totals: MonarchInvoiceTotals = MonarchInvoiceTotals(), notes: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, isPrintButtonShown: Bool = false, labels: MonarchInvoiceViewLabels = MonarchInvoiceViewLabels(), onPrint: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(_ title: String? = nil, number: String? = nil, status: MonarchStatusDefinition? = nil, issueDate: Date? = nil, dueDate: Date? = nil, details: [MonarchInvoiceDetail] = [], brand: Image? = nil, from: MonarchInvoiceParty? = nil, to: MonarchInvoiceParty? = nil, items: [MonarchInvoiceLineItem], currencyCode: String, locale: Locale? = nil, taxRate: Decimal? = nil, discount: MonarchInvoiceDiscount? = nil, totals: MonarchInvoiceTotals = MonarchInvoiceTotals(), notes: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, isPrintButtonShown: Bool = false, labels: MonarchInvoiceViewLabels = MonarchInvoiceViewLabels(), onPrint: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) where Actions == EmptyView
MonarchInvoiceParty.init(_ name: String, details: [String] = [])
MonarchInvoiceDetail.init(_ label: String, value: String)
MonarchInvoiceLineItem.init(_ id: String, description: String, detail: String? = nil, quantity: Decimal, unitPrice: Decimal, amount: Decimal? = nil)
MonarchInvoiceTotals.init(subtotal: Decimal? = nil, discount: Decimal? = nil, tax: Decimal? = nil, total: Decimal? = nil, amountPaid: Decimal? = nil, amountDue: Decimal? = nil)
enum MonarchInvoiceDiscount { case percent(Decimal), amount(Decimal) }

MonarchInvoiceViewLabels.init(title: String? = nil, from: String? = nil, to: String? = nil, issueDate: String? = nil, dueDate: String? = nil, lineItems: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, quantity: String? = nil, unitPrice: String? = nil, amount: String? = nil, subtotal: String? = nil, discount: String? = nil, tax: String? = nil, taxWithRate: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, total: String? = nil, amountPaid: String? = nil, amountDue: String? = nil, noItems: String? = nil, notes: String? = nil, print: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Invoice", for example "Tax invoice" or "Credit note".

options.name: number
options.description: The invoice number, shown after the title; the heading is also the invoice's accessibility name.

options.name: status
options.description: A status badge beside the title. The app owns the vocabulary ("Paid", "Overdue").

options.name: issueDate
options.description: Shown as "Issue date" with a long date in the locale and the environment's time zone.

options.name: dueDate
options.description: Shown as "Due date" with a long date.

options.name: details
options.description: Further facts after the dates, such as terms or a purchase order number.

options.name: brand
options.description: A logo above the title, scaled with the title text size. Decorative: hidden from VoiceOver.

options.name: from
options.description: Who issues the invoice, under the heading "From".

options.name: to
options.description: Who is billed, under the heading "Bill to".

options.name: items
options.description: The billed lines. Empty shows "No line items.".

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of every amount, which are in major units.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of amounts, quantities and dates. Default: the environment's.

options.name: taxRate
options.description: The tax rate in percent. Used to work out tax when totals.tax is nil, and then shown in the label ("Tax (20%)").

options.name: discount
options.description: A percentage or amount discount, used when totals.discount is nil.

options.name: totals
options.description: Totals from the billing system, shown exactly. Amount paid and amount due are shown only when given.

options.name: notes
options.description: Payment instructions or a note under the totals, with the heading "Notes".

options.name: footer
options.description: Small print at the bottom, in the caption style.

options.name: isPrintButtonShown
options.description: Shows a secondary Print button in the header (on iOS, or anywhere with onPrint).

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, for example in the invoice's own language.

options.name: onPrint
options.description: Runs instead of the built-in printing, for example to print the billing system's PDF.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra header actions after Print, such as Send or Download. Not printed.

states.name: stacked lines
states.description: At compact width and at the accessibility text sizes each line is a block: description and detail, then "Qty 2 · Unit price £400.00" and the amount.

states.name: table
states.description: At regular width the lines are a grid with Description, Qty, Unit price and Amount columns; numbers align to the trailing edge.

states.name: worked-out totals
states.description: Totals not given are worked out from the lines, the tax rate and the discount, rounded to the currency's minor unit.

states.name: given totals
states.description: Totals from the billing system are shown exactly; the tax label then has no rate.

states.name: paid and due
states.description: Amount paid and amount due rows appear after the total when given; amount due is in the strong body style.

states.name: empty
states.description: No lines shows "No line items." in muted text; the totals are zero.

states.name: printing
states.description: Print renders the invoice as A4 PDF pages in the light theme at the default text size, with the table layout and without the actions, and opens the system print panel.

appearance: The title uses the title type role in the default text colour; section headings, column headings and fact labels use the muted text colour; amounts use tabular digits. Rows are separated by dividers in the subtle border colour and the total has a divider above it and a larger type role. There are no fills apart from the status badge, so the same roles read in light, dark and both high-contrast themes, and the printed copy uses the light theme.
platformNotes: The web InvoiceView is an article with a real table and print styles, and takes ReactNode slots and decimal or minor-unit amounts. On iOS amounts are Decimal in major units, dates are Date values formatted by the view, and the status is a MonarchStatusDefinition drawn as a MonarchStatusBadge. Printing uses ImageRenderer to make PDF pages and UIPrintInteractionController, because a SwiftUI view cannot be printed directly; the system panel also offers saving as a PDF. The parity map named List sections; the view is a plain stack instead, because a List cannot sit inside a screen's ScrollView with other content and cannot be rendered to PDF. The heading level option has no iOS equivalent; headings are marked with the header trait. Android ships the same MonarchInvoiceView.
accessibility: The invoice is a container named by its heading, such as "Invoice INV-1042"; the heading has the header trait.
"From", "Bill to", "Line items" and "Notes" are headers, so the rotor can move between them.

Each line is one element read as its description and detail, then "Qty", "Unit price" and "Amount" with their values, in both layouts; the column headings are hidden because every line names its columns.
Each fact and each total is one element read as its label and then its value.
The status badge has words and an icon, so the status never depends on colour.
The brand image is decorative and hidden.
Text wraps at every Dynamic Type size; at the accessibility sizes lines stack and totals put the amount under the label.
The Print button is a MonarchButton with a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: Totals are worked out only for values left nil; a given total is never corrected, even when it disagrees with the lines.
A negative discount is ignored; a discount larger than the subtotal is capped at it.
A zero-decimal currency such as JPY rounds lines to whole units.
Dates are written in the environment's time zone; pass a date at the start of the local day for a date-only value.
Printed pages are cut at the page height, so a long invoice can split a line across two pages.
Printing and the print panel were checked by compiling for iOS and by a unit test of the PDF pages on the host; the panel was not opened on a device.

parityExceptions.reason: The web lays the line items out as a four column table (description, quantity, unit price, amount), which needs about 390 points; a phone column has 306, so each line stacks its description, its quantity and unit price, and its amount, with the same figures and totals. For the same reason the Print button sits under the title instead of beside it.

options.name: tags

options.name: dueDate

options.name: isSelected
options.description: Tints the card with the accent, adds a check mark and the selected trait.

options.name: isDragging
options.description: Lifts the card with a larger shadow.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the due and overdue text, the priority names and every spoken phrase.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Changes the status from the card. Receives the chosen status id.

options.name: onPriorityChange

states.name: default
states.description: Surface fill, default border, extra-small shadow.

states.name: selected
states.description: Subtle accent fill, a thicker accent border and a check mark before the key.

states.name: dragging
states.description: A large shadow lifts the card.

states.name: overdue
states.description: The due date turns the strong danger colour, its symbol becomes an exclamation mark and the word Overdue is added. Completed and cancelled issues are never overdue.

states.name: editable
states.description: Status and priority open menus with every option, when their change handlers are given.

appearance: The card uses the MonarchCard surface, radius and padding. The key is muted caption text, the title strong body text. Priority symbols are strong danger (urgent), strong warning (high), default text (medium, low) or muted (none); status symbols are subtle, muted, strong warning or strong success by category. The same roles adapt to dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web card uses its PriorityPicker and StatusPicker; iOS uses the system Menu with an inline Picker, as the priority-picker and status-picker entries recommend. MonarchCard has no selected state, so the card draws the same surface with its own fill for selection. The due date is a Date read in the environment's calendar and time zone (the web also accepts YYYY-MM-DD strings), and today is a Date rather than a string. Web labels are called tags here because labels names the strings parameter. Android uses the same name and API shape. Several closures are optional (onStatusChange, onPriorityChange, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onStatusChange.
accessibility: The card is a container; its parts are read in order.
The title is read with the key first ("STR-142, Sign-in fails…") and has the selected trait on a selected card.
The title is a link or a button when the issue can be opened.
Priority is read as "Priority: High", status as "Status: In progress", the due date as "Due Mar 12, Overdue" and the assignee as "Assigned to Ana Ruiz" or "Unassigned".
Every priority level and status category has its own symbol, and overdue is written, so nothing relies on colour.
The status and priority menus have touch targets at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: Long titles wrap; tags and the due date flow onto new lines while the assignee stays at the end.
A url with another scheme (mailto, javascript) is ignored; the title falls back to onOpen or plain text.
A due date later today is not overdue; overdue compares days, not times.
With onStatusChange but no statuses, the status is read-only.

name: MonarchJsonViewer
title: JSONViewer
wrapsNative: LazyVStack of Button rows over a flattened model of the open part of the tree, a TextField search field, MonarchCopyButton for the path and value, AttributedString for matches
summary: A collapsible, searchable tree for a JSON document, with copy path and copy value for the selected node, that stays fast on large payloads.
whenToUse: To inspect an API response, a webhook payload, a log entry's body or a configuration document inside the app.
whenNotToUse: For JSON the user should read as text or edit, use MonarchCodeBlock with the json language. For a general hierarchy of app objects use List with children (tree view).
api: init(_ value: MonarchJsonValue, expandDepth: Int = 1, maxChildren: Int = 100, maxStringLength: Int = 500, isSearchable: Bool = true, maxMatches: Int = 500, isCopyable: Bool = true, rootPath: String = "$", labels: MonarchJsonViewerLabels = MonarchJsonViewerLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (String, MonarchJsonValue) -> Void)? = nil, onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)

enum MonarchJsonValue: Equatable, ExpressibleBy…Literal { case object([(key: String, value: MonarchJsonValue)]), array([MonarchJsonValue]), string(String), number(String), bool(Bool), null; init(parsing text: String) throws; init(data: Data) throws }
struct MonarchJsonParseError: Error { let offset: Int; init(offset: Int) }

struct MonarchJsonViewerLabels { init(label: String? = nil, search: String? = nil, searchPrompt: String? = nil, clearSearch: String? = nil, matches: (@Sendable (Int, Bool) -> String)? = nil, collapseAll: String? = nil, copyPath: String? = nil, copyValue: String? = nil, selectedPath: String? = nil, keys: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, items: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, showMore: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, truncated: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, expanded: String? = nil, collapsed: String? = nil) }

options.name: value
options.description: The document. Build it with MonarchJsonValue(parsing:) or (data:), which keep the order of object keys and the exact text of numbers, or with literals.

options.name: expandDepth
options.description: Levels open at first: 1 shows the root's children, 0 only the root.

options.name: maxChildren
options.description: Children shown per object or array before a "Show more" row; each Show more adds this many. At least 1.

options.name: maxStringLength
options.description: Strings longer than this are cut in the tree with "… (n characters)". Copy value always copies the whole string.

options.name: isSearchable
options.description: Shows the search field and the match count.

options.name: maxMatches
options.description: The search stops after this many matches and the count shows "500+ matches".

options.name: isCopyable
options.description: Shows the footer with the selected path, Copy path and Copy value.

options.name: rootPath
options.description: The first part of shown and copied paths: $ gives $.users[0].name, an empty string gives users[0].name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: the tree name, the search field, the match count, Collapse all, the copy buttons, the selected path, the summaries, Show more, the cut string suffix and the spoken open state.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with the formatted path and the value when the selection changes.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied text after the path or the value is copied.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: A closed object or array shows a forward chevron and its summary: { } 3 keys or [ ] 2 items.

states.name: expanded
states.description: An open container shows a down chevron and its children, indented one level.

states.name: selected
states.description: The selected row has the muted fill and the selected trait; the footer shows its path. The root is selected at first.

states.name: searching
states.description: Containers that hold a match open, matched text is highlighted and bold, and the toolbar shows the match count.

states.name: show more
states.description: A container with more children than maxChildren ends with a link-coloured "Show 100 more (250 hidden)" row. Search reveals hidden children that match.

states.name: collapsed all
states.description: Collapse all clears the search, closes every container below the root and selects the root.

appearance: A surface-filled box with a subtle border. Keys use the info strong colour (array indexes muted), strings success strong, numbers accent strong, booleans and null warning strong, summaries and punctuation muted. Matches use the warning subtle fill. The colours come from the theme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web takes any JavaScript value and shows circular references, undefined and Dates; on iOS the input is MonarchJsonValue, a value type that cannot be circular, parsed by a small parser that keeps key order (JSONSerialization does not). The web's tree keyboard pattern (arrows, Home, End, *) is replaced by touch: tapping a row selects it and opens or closes it, and VoiceOver moves row by row. The search field is the viewer's own TextField, because .searchable needs a navigation container. onCopy receives the text only; the web also passes whether it was the path or the value. The toolbar has no slot for extra actions. Android uses the same name. Several closures are optional (onSelect, onCopy). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onSelect.
accessibility: The tree is a container named "JSON".
Each row is a button read as "key: value", such as "amount: 4200" or "lines: [ ] 2 items".
Containers have "expanded" or "collapsed" as their value; the chevron is decorative.
The selected row has the selected trait, and the footer path is read as "Selected" with the path as its value.
Matches are bold as well as highlighted, so they are not shown by colour alone.
A new match count is announced while searching.
Rows, Show more, the copy buttons and the clear button are at least 44 points tall.
Copy path and Copy value are MonarchCopyButton, which confirms with "Copied" and an announcement.
edgeCases: Only open containers are walked, so a closed 10 MB document costs one row; search walks the whole document once per query and stops at maxMatches.
Long keys and values wrap; very long strings are cut at maxStringLength in the tree only.

A repeated key in parsed text keeps its first position and its last value, as JSON.parse does. Repeated keys written in a dictionary literal are not merged; avoid them, because rows are identified by path.
Numbers keep the text they were written with (1.50, 12345678901234567890).
A primitive root is one row; an empty object or array cannot open.
MonarchJsonValue(parsing:) rejects nesting deeper than 100 levels with MonarchJsonParseError, which also bounds the recursion of search, flattening and copying.

name: MonarchKanbanBoard
title: KanbanBoard
wrapsNative: Horizontal ScrollView with scrollTargetLayout(), .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal, count:span:spacing:) and scrollPosition(id:); a vertical ScrollView with LazyVStack per column; draggable(_:) cards with dropDestination(for: String.self, action:isTargeted:) on each card, the end of each column and each column tab; spring-loaded column tabs (springLoadingBehavior(.enabled)); a Menu per card with the other columns, Move up and Move down and the same moves as accessibilityActions; sensoryFeedback for pick-up, target changes and drops; AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: A board of columns of cards where people move cards within and between columns by dragging, a Move menu or VoiceOver actions, with counts against work-in-progress limits.
whenToUse: For work that moves through stages, such as To do, Doing and Done, or a sales pipeline.
whenNotToUse: For planning work into sprints or releases with points and capacity, use MonarchBacklogPlanner. For ordering one list, use a List with onMove; for a grid of tiles, MonarchSortableGrid.
api: init(columns: Binding<[MonarchKanbanColumn<Item>]>, itemLabel: @escaping (Item) -> String, canMove: ((_ item: Item, _ toColumnID: String, _ fromColumnID: String) -> Bool)? = nil, isWipLimitEnforced: Bool = false, isItemEnabled: ((Item) -> Bool)? = nil, isReadOnly: Bool = false, minimumColumnWidth: CGFloat? = nil, scrollPosition: Binding<String?>? = nil, labels: MonarchKanbanBoardLabels = MonarchKanbanBoardLabels(), onMove: (@MainActor (_ move: MonarchKanbanMove<Item.ID>, _ columns: [MonarchKanbanColumn<Item>]) async throws -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder card: @escaping (Item, MonarchKanbanCardState) -> Card)

struct MonarchKanbanColumn<Item: Identifiable>: Identifiable { init(id: String, title: String, items: [Item], wipLimit: Int? = nil, emptyText: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil); func withItems(_ items: [Item]) -> MonarchKanbanColumn<Item> }
struct MonarchKanbanMove<ItemID: Hashable>: Hashable { let itemID: ItemID; let fromColumnID: String; let fromIndex: Int; let toColumnID: String; let toIndex: Int }
struct MonarchKanbanCardState: Hashable, Sendable { let columnID: String; let index: Int; let isDropTarget: Bool; let isPending: Bool; let isEnabled: Bool }

struct MonarchKanbanBoardLabels: Sendable { var moveToSection, moveUp, moveDown, empty, columns: String?; var moveMenu: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var moveTo: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var countText, count: (@Sendable (Int, Int?) -> String)?; var moved, dropped: (@Sendable (String, String, Int, Int) -> String)?; var notAllowed, failed: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? }

options.name: columns
options.description: The columns leading to trailing, each with an id, a title, its cards and an optional wipLimit, emptyText and systemImage. Updated at once on every move.

options.name: itemLabel
options.description: The plain-text name of a card, such as its key, used in the Move menu's name and in announcements.

options.name: canMove
options.description: Whether a card may go to another column (card, to, from). Its own column always takes it. Refused columns are disabled in the menu, left out of the VoiceOver actions and refuse drops.

options.name: isWipLimitEnforced
options.description: A column at or over its wipLimit refuses cards from other columns.

options.name: isItemEnabled
options.description: Whether a card can be moved, such as one the person may not edit. Every card when nil.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Turns off dragging, the Move menu and the VoiceOver move actions. The environment's isEnabled (.disabled(true)) does the same.

options.name: minimumColumnWidth
options.description: The narrowest a column gets, scaled with Dynamic Type. A phone shows one column per page; wider screens as many as fit.

options.name: scrollPosition
options.description: The id of the first column in view, to choose the column shown or follow it. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onMove
options.description: Saves a finished move with the columns after it. While it runs the card's state has isPending; throwing puts the card back and announces it.

options.name: card
options.description: The content of a card, such as a MonarchIssueCard. The Move menu is added after it.

states.name: default
states.description: Columns are panels with a header (optional symbol, title as a heading, count) and their cards; each movable card has a Move menu button at its trailing edge.

states.name: paged
states.description: When not every column fits, one column (on a phone) or as many as fit fill the width, a swipe snaps to the next, and a row of column tabs above shows the column in view with an accent underline.

states.name: dragging
states.description: Touch and hold a card for the system drag preview. The column under the finger gets the accent border and an accent line shows where the card will land: above the card it is over, or after the last card. Pick-up plays an impact haptic and each change of target a selection haptic.

states.name: turning the page
states.description: Holding a dragged card over a column tab spring-loads the tab and shows that column; dropping on the tab puts the card at the end of that column.

states.name: dropped
states.description: The card moves, the drop is announced and a success haptic plays.

states.name: refused
states.description: A drop on a column canMove refuses, or a full one with isWipLimitEnforced, is refused, announced ("ENG-101 cannot move to Done.") and plays an error haptic. In the Move menu the column is disabled.

states.name: at and over the limit
states.description: The count reads "2 / 2" with a warning symbol, in the strong warning colour at the limit and the strong danger colour over it; VoiceOver reads "2 cards, limit 2, at the limit".

states.name: pending
states.description: While onMove runs the card stays in its new place and its state has isPending true.

states.name: failed
states.description: When onMove throws, the card goes back to its column and position and "Could not move ENG-101. It is back in To do." is announced.

states.name: locked and read only
states.description: A card isItemEnabled refuses, and every card with isReadOnly or a disabled environment, has no Move menu, no move actions and cannot be dragged.

states.name: empty
states.description: A column with no cards shows its emptyText, or "No cards", in the muted text colour; the area is still a drop target.

appearance: Columns are panels in the subtle background colour with a subtle border and the large radius; the column a card is dragged over gets a thicker accent border. Column titles use the subheading style in the default text colour; counts use the caption style in the muted text colour, the strong warning colour at the limit and the strong danger colour over it. Tabs use the label style, muted when not selected and accent with an accent underline when selected. The insertion line is the strong accent colour. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web lays all columns side by side and scrolls the board sideways; on iOS the board is a horizontal ScrollView with view-aligned snapping, one column per page on a phone and as many as fit minimumColumnWidth on wider screens, with a row of column tabs when not every column is in view (Android uses a HorizontalPager with a Material tab row). Dragging is the system drag and drop (draggable and dropDestination with String payloads, which are Transferable) started by a touch and hold anywhere on the card, so there is no drag handle; Android uses a long press and its own drag overlay. Dropping on a card takes its place; the board does not reorder cards during the drag. Moving to another column during a drag is done by holding the card over the spring-loaded column tab instead of Android's 600 millisecond edge hold; a column does not scroll itself when the card nears its top or bottom edge. Because SwiftUI's drop API does not say which card is being dragged before the drop, a refused column is refused and announced on drop, not marked "Not allowed here" while the card is over it, and picked-up and cancelled announcements are not made (the system plays its own lift; Monarch adds an impact haptic when the drag first reaches a target). The Move menu is always on for movable cards (Android has moveMenu, on by default; the web has it off by default) and replaces the handle's actions: Move up and Move down within the column and Move to another column, which puts the card at its end (Android's Move backward and Move forward keep the position). Swift idiom renames: key is the Item's Identifiable id, itemEnabled is isItemEnabled, enforceWipLimits is isWipLimitEnforced, enabled is the environment's isEnabled plus isReadOnly, pagerState is scrollPosition, minColumnWidth is minimumColumnWidth, cardContent is card, and columns is a Binding instead of a value with onMove updating it. onMove is async throws where Android's is a suspend function. Column icons are SF Symbol names, not view slots; column actions and footers, menuIcon, the card state's dragging and overlay flags, and the labels handle, move, blocked, pickedUp and cancelled are not offered. Columns cannot collapse. Several closures are optional (canMove, isItemEnabled, onMove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canMove.
accessibility: Each column title has the header trait; its count is read in words, such as "1 card, limit 2", and at or over the limit it is also a symbol, not only a colour.
Column tabs are buttons named by the column title with the count as their value and the selected trait on the column in view; the row is named "Columns".
Each movable card's Move menu is named "Move ENG-101 to…" and lists the other columns, Move up and Move down; refused columns are disabled and moves that cannot happen are disabled.
The Move menu also carries Move up, Move down and "Move to Doing" for every column that takes the card as VoiceOver actions.
Moves are announced ("ENG-101: Doing, position 1 of 2."), as are drops ("ENG-101 dropped in Doing, position 1 of 2."), refused drops and failed saves.
Pick-up, a change of target and the drop play system haptics through sensoryFeedback; a refused drop plays the error haptic.
The insertion line and the drop-target border are hidden from VoiceOver.
Tabs and Move menu buttons have touch targets of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: The binding updates at once; if onMove throws, the card goes back to its old column and position even if other cards moved meanwhile, clamped to the end of that column.
Dropping a card where it was, or choosing a move that changes nothing, does not call onMove.
Moving to a column from the menu or the VoiceOver actions puts the card at its end.
Give the board a bounded height: each column scrolls vertically inside it.
With isWipLimitEnforced a column already over its limit keeps its cards and still lets them move within it.
Drag payloads are the board's own namespace and the card's id as text; ids must be unique across columns, and drops from another board or app are ignored.
Long titles and card text wrap; at the largest text sizes columns get wider because minimumColumnWidth scales with Dynamic Type.

name: MonarchKbd

summary: A keyboard key or shortcut drawn as a key cap, such as ⌘K. By default it is drawn only while a hardware keyboard is attached.
whenToUse: Beside a command that has a keyboard shortcut, as a hint for people who use a hardware keyboard, and in a list of shortcuts (with isAlwaysVisible).
whenNotToUse: Do not use it to define a shortcut; that is keyboardShortcut(_:modifiers:) on the control, which also lists the shortcut in the system's shortcut overlay on iPad. Not for code; use MonarchInlineCodeStyle.
api: init(_ keys: String, labels: MonarchKbdLabels = MonarchKbdLabels(), isAlwaysVisible: Bool = false)

struct MonarchKbdLabels { init(command: String? = nil, shift: String? = nil, option: String? = nil, control: String? = nil, return: String? = nil, escape: String? = nil, delete: String? = nil, tab: String? = nil, space: String? = nil, capsLock: String? = nil, upArrow: String? = nil, downArrow: String? = nil, leftArrow: String? = nil, rightArrow: String? = nil) }

options.name: keys
options.description: The key or shortcut as it is shown, such as "⌘K", "Esc" or "⇧⌘P".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the names VoiceOver reads for the key glyphs ⌘ ⇧ ⌥ ⌃ ↩ ⎋ ⌫ ⇥ ␣ ⇪ ↑ ↓ ← →.

summary: The content of a sheet that shows a newly created secret exactly once: the value with a copy button, a "store it now" warning, and an acknowledgement the person must tick before the sheet can close.
whenToUse: Right after the server returns a new API key, token, signing secret or client secret that cannot be shown again; with kind public, after creating a publishable key.
whenNotToUse: For a secret that stays viewable in settings use MonarchSecretField on the settings screen. For recovery codes use MonarchRecoveryCodes.
api: init(_ secret: String, label: String? = nil, name: String? = nil, title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, kind: MonarchKeyCreatedDialogKind = .secret, requiresAcknowledgement: Bool? = nil, isMasked: Bool = false, isMultiline: Bool = false, note: String? = nil, labels: MonarchKeyCreatedDialogLabels = MonarchKeyCreatedDialogLabels(), onCopy: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onDone: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchKeyCreatedDialogLabels { init(title: String? = nil, label: String? = nil, secretNoticeTitle: String? = nil, secretNotice: String? = nil, publicNoticeTitle: String? = nil, publicNotice: String? = nil, acknowledge: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, acknowledgeRequired: String? = nil, done: String? = nil, copy: String? = nil, copied: String? = nil) }

options.name: secret
options.description: The value to show once.

options.name: label
options.description: What the value is, such as "Signing secret". Names the copy button ("Copy Signing secret") and goes into the acknowledgement. "API key" when nil.

options.name: name
options.description: The name the person gave it, shown above the value instead of the label.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the title "Copy your new key".

options.name: description
options.description: Text under the title.

options.name: kind
options.description: secret: a warning notice and an acknowledgement before closing. public: an information notice and nothing to confirm.

options.name: requiresAcknowledgement
options.description: Overrides whether the checkbox must be ticked before closing (by default only for a secret).

options.name: isMasked
options.description: Shows the value in a read-only MonarchSecretField with a reveal toggle; copy works without revealing.

options.name: isMultiline
options.description: Wraps the whole value over several lines, for certificates and private keys. Ignored when masked.

options.name: note
options.description: Extra text under the value, such as when an old key stops working.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string: title, default label, both notices, the acknowledgement, the "confirm first" message, Done, Copy and Copied.

options.name: onCopy
options.description: Runs with the copied text after each copy.

options.name: onDone
options.description: Runs when Done closes the sheet after the value was acknowledged, before the sheet dismisses itself.

states.name: unacknowledged
states.description: For a secret: the sheet cannot be swiped down and has no drag indicator; Done stays enabled.

states.name: nudged
states.description: Done pressed before ticking: "Confirm that you have saved it before you close this dialog." is shown under the checkbox in the danger colour with an icon, announced, given as the checkbox hint, and VoiceOver moves to the checkbox.

states.name: acknowledged
states.description: The checkbox is ticked: the drag indicator appears, the sheet can be swiped away, and Done calls onDone and closes it.

states.name: public
states.description: An information notice, no checkbox; the sheet can close at once.

states.name: masked
states.description: The value is dots until revealed with the eye toggle.

states.name: new secret
states.description: When the secret changes, the acknowledgement and the message reset.

appearance: The sheet has the surface fill. The title uses the heading type role, the description and note the muted text colour. The notice is MonarchBanner in the warning or info tone; the value keeps the copy field or secret field look; Done is the primary button. All roles adapt to light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web dialog blocks Escape, outside clicks and its close button until acknowledged; on iOS the sheet's swipe to dismiss is disabled and there is no close button, only Done. The web passes any content as children under the value; on iOS that is a note string, and other content goes in the app's own view. Copy failures cannot happen with UIPasteboard, so there is no onCopyError. The copy button of the plain field is the secondary copy button rather than the web's primary variant. Android uses the same name. Several closures are optional (onCopy, onDone). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onCopy.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
The notice is MonarchBanner, which speaks its tone with the title and message.
The plain value is read as the label ("API key") with the value; the visible name above it is not read twice. Its copy button is "Copy API key" and announces the copy.
The acknowledgement is a Toggle with the checkbox style and a visible label.
Pressing Done too early announces why, sets the checkbox hint and moves VoiceOver focus to the checkbox.
Done, the copy button, the reveal toggle and the checkbox have 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: The sheet cannot be dismissed by a swipe while unacknowledged, but the app can still close it by changing its presentation state.
onDone is not called when the app closes the sheet itself.
Long and multi-line values wrap in full with isMultiline; a single-line value is shortened in the middle on screen and copied whole.
At the largest text sizes the content scrolls inside the sheet.

whenToUse: Add keyboardShortcut to the buttons and menu items of the actions people repeat. The title of the control is the name shown in the system's list, so every shortcut needs a control with a title.
whenNotToUse: Do not build a sheet that lists shortcuts, and do not bind a key to open one. Do not reuse the system's shortcuts (Command C, Command H, Command Tab).

states.name: Command held
states.description: On an iPad with a hardware keyboard the system shows the app's shortcuts, grouped by menu, with their titles.

appearance: The system draws the overlay. Nothing in it is themed by Monarch.
platformNotes: The web KeyboardShortcutsSheet is a side sheet opened with "?" that lists groups of shortcuts, can be filtered and shows the Command or Control symbol for the platform. On iOS the list is the system's: holding Command on iPadOS shows every shortcut the visible screen declares, and shortcuts in the app's commands menus (the commands scene modifier) are grouped under their menu. There is nothing to filter or translate; the titles are the controls' own. An iPhone has no such overlay, and shortcuts still work with a connected keyboard. Android shows the system's shortcut helper in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: a shortcut runs the control's action, so it does the same as activating the control with VoiceOver or touch.
System behaviour: a disabled control's shortcut does nothing and is dimmed in the list.
Every shortcut must also be reachable as a visible control or menu item; a shortcut alone cannot be found without a keyboard.
edgeCases: A shortcut works only while its control is in the view tree of the active scene.
Two controls with the same shortcut on one screen: the system picks one. Keep them unique.
Letter keys are matched by the character the layout produces, so a shortcut may sit on another key on a non-US keyboard.

The labels and groups are listed in order.

title: KPIRow
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid with two GridItem(.flexible()) columns (one at accessibility text sizes), or ScrollView(.horizontal) with LazyHStack, containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal, count:span:spacing:), scrollTargetLayout() and scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned); accessibilityElement(children: .contain) with accessibilityLabel names the row
summary: A recipe, not a component: the row of key figures at the top of a dashboard, as MonarchStatCards in a two-column grid or in a sideways row that snaps card by card, with one loading and error state for the whole row.
whenToUse: At the top of a dashboard or a report screen, for three to six figures with their change against the previous period.
whenNotToUse: For a single figure use MonarchStatCard on its own. For figures that belong to one record use LabeledContent with the Monarch style. For a trend over time use a chart.
api: LazyVGrid(columns: Array(repeating: GridItem(.flexible(), spacing: theme.spacing.space3), count: dynamicTypeSize.isAccessibilitySize ? 1 : 2), spacing: theme.spacing.space3) { MonarchStatCard(…) }

ScrollView(.horizontal) { LazyHStack(spacing: theme.spacing.space3) { MonarchStatCard(…).containerRelativeFrame(.horizontal, count: 5, span: 4, spacing: theme.spacing.space3) }.scrollTargetLayout() }.scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned)
.accessibilityElement(children: .contain).accessibilityLabel("This month")
MonarchStatCard(_:value:isLoading: true) for each placeholder; MonarchInlineErrorRetry(_:variant: .banner, onRetry:) in place of the row

options.name: columns
options.description: Two on a phone, one at accessibility text sizes; an iPad layout can use GridItem(.adaptive(minimum:)) for as many as fit.

options.name: scroll
options.description: Keeps one row: each card takes four fifths of the width so the next one shows, and scrolling stops on a card.

options.name: size / variant
options.description: Passed to every MonarchStatCard: .sm for dense rows, .lg for a hero row, .plain inside another card.

options.name: loading
options.description: Every card's isLoading; with no figures yet, four placeholder cards labelled Loading.

options.name: error
options.description: Replaces the row with MonarchInlineErrorRetry in its banner variant.

options.name: label
options.description: Names the group for VoiceOver, for example This month.

states.name: ready
states.description: The cards with their values, changes and sparklines.

states.name: loading
states.description: Each card shows its own loading placeholder; with no figures yet, placeholder cards keep the row's height.

states.name: error
states.description: One banner with Try again in place of the row, not an error per card.

states.name: scrolling
states.description: A sideways row that stops on each card, with the next card partly visible.

appearance: Every part is MonarchStatCard: the surface, border, value, change and sparkline in their roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow. Cards are spaced by space3.
platformNotes: The web ships KPIRow as a component over StatCardGroup with columns, minItemWidth, overflow, loading and error props. On iOS it is a recipe: a LazyVGrid or a snapping horizontal ScrollView already lays out the cards, and MonarchStatCard owns the loading, error and value states, so a wrapper would only rename SwiftUI's layout parameters. The web's minItemWidth breakpoint becomes two columns on a phone and one at accessibility text sizes; its overflow scroll becomes scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned), the system's snapping. The web's role group with aria-label is an accessibility container with a label. The web makes a scrolling row a tab stop for the keyboard; on iOS the scroll view scrolls with swipes and VoiceOver moves into it card by card. Android has not covered this entry yet.
accessibility: The row is a container named by its label, so VoiceOver says This month when it moves into it.
Each card keeps MonarchStatCard's reading: label, value and change in one element, with the change direction spoken.
In the scrolling row VoiceOver moves card by card and scrolls the next one into view.
One column at accessibility text sizes, so values are never truncated.
edgeCases: An odd number of cards leaves the last grid row half filled; use an even number or the scrolling row.
Cards in one grid row take the height of the tallest; a long hint in one card makes its row taller.
Keep the figures to six or fewer; more belong in a report.

title: LanguageSelect

summary: A searchable picker for a language, each listed under its own name with its name in the interface's language below.
whenToUse: For the language of an account, a document or subtitles, where people look for their own language whatever the interface language is.
whenNotToUse: Not for the app's own language on iOS: send people to the app's page in Settings, where iOS manages per-app languages. For two or three languages, use a Picker.
api: init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<String?>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, languages: [String]? = nil, priority: [String] = [], locale: Locale? = nil, labelStyle: MonarchLanguageSelectLabelStyle = .endonym, showsTag: Bool = false, isRequired: Bool = false, isClearable: Bool = true, labels: MonarchLanguageSelectLabels = MonarchLanguageSelectLabels())
static var languageTags: [String]
enum MonarchLanguageSelectLabelStyle { case endonym, localized }
struct MonarchLanguageSelectLabels { init(suggested: String? = nil, all: String? = nil, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen BCP 47 tag. Any form is read (EN-us); the picker writes the canonical tag (en-US).

options.name: prompt

options.name: helper

options.name: priority
options.description: Tags listed first under Suggested while nothing is typed, such as Locale.preferredLanguages.

options.name: locale
options.description: The interface's language: each row's second name and the sort order use it. The environment's locale when nil.

options.name: labelStyle
options.description: Which name each row shows first: the language's own name (Deutsch) or the interface's (German).

options.name: showsTag
options.description: Shows the tag at the end of each row.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds Required to the hint.

options.name: isClearable
options.description: Shows a clear button in the field while a language is chosen.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces Suggested, All languages and the combobox strings; the combobox's empty text is built in as No languages match.

states.name: empty
states.description: The field shows the prompt in the subtle text colour.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The field shows the language's first name and a clear button when clearing is on.

states.name: suggestions
states.description: With priority and nothing typed, the list has a Suggested section and a section with the rest.

states.name: searching
states.description: The suggestions are hidden; matches are listed with labels that start with the query first.

states.name: no match
states.description: The list reads No languages match.

states.name: error
states.description: The field border and message use the danger colour, with an icon; the error is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Label, value and border use the disabled roles; the sheet does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's. Each row has the first name in the default text colour and the second name as a muted caption under it; the tag, when shown, is a muted caption at the end. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Names come from Foundation, which names regional variants as English (United Kingdom) where the web's Intl says British English. The web marks each endonym with its lang so screen readers switch voice; MonarchComboboxOption carries plain strings, so VoiceOver reads every name in the device's voice. The list opens in a sheet, as every MonarchCombobox does.
accessibility: The field is a button labelled with the label, whose value is the chosen row's label or None.
The help text, the error (read as Error: ...) and Required are the field's hint; a new error is announced.
The chosen row has the selected trait and a check mark, not colour alone.
Rows and the field are at least 44 points high.
Each row is read with both names, then the tag when it is shown.
VoiceOver reads names in the device's voice, not in the language they are written in.
edgeCases: Tags are canonicalised, so pt-br and PT-BR both choose pt-BR; strings that are not languages are dropped.
When both names are the same (English in an English interface), only one is shown.
Right-to-left names such as العربية are laid out by the text system inside a left-to-right row.
A selection outside languages is still listed first, so its name shows in the field.

appearance: Names and values are in the default text role, ranks, secondary lines and the "(you)" tag in the muted role. Bars are the Monarch linear progress style: the accent solid fill on the muted background. The current row uses the accent subtle background and the accent border. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web bars use the first data colour; iOS reuses the Monarch linear progress style, whose fill is the accent role. The web names become links with href and "N more" links to moreHref; on iOS rows and "N more" are buttons whose actions the app uses to navigate. The web secondary line and badge take any content; on iOS they are strings, the badge drawn as a MonarchBadge. The web change takes any DeltaIndicator props; on iOS each entry has a ratio, and the comparison and good direction are set once for the board. The web's sort, format and notation map to the shared MonarchBarListSort, MonarchMetricFormat and isCompact. There is no ordered-list role on iOS, so each row speaks its rank. At the accessibility text sizes the value and change move under the name and the avatar is dropped, so the name keeps its width. Android uses the same name and options. Several closures are optional (onShowMore, onSelect, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onShowMore.
accessibility: Each row is one element read as "Rank 1: Ana Lima, (you), 3 breached, Tier 2, 42 tickets solved, up 12%, better".
Avatars and bars are hidden; the name and the number with its unit carry the data.
The viewer's row is marked in words, not only by its tint.
With onSelect each row is a button with a 44-point touch target.
The placeholder rows are one element named "Loading ranking".
The board is a container named by label.
edgeCases: Equal values share a rank and the next rank skips: 1, 1, 3.
Bars are relative to the largest magnitude shown, so a negative value draws a bar of its size; all zero draws empty bars.
limit 0 or a negative limit shows every row.
A total smaller than the rows shown adds no "N more".
Long names wrap; the value column keeps its width.

title: LeaveWorkspaceFlow
wrapsNative: alert(_:isPresented:actions:message:) for the blocked case; sheet(isPresented:content:) with presentationDetents and interactiveDismissDisabled for the confirmation, holding MonarchConsequenceList, MonarchInlineNotice and MonarchButtons
summary: A recipe, not a component: a member leaves a workspace after a confirmation that lists what they lose and what stays, or learns why they cannot leave yet and how to fix it.
whenToUse: In workspace settings, for a member who wants to leave a shared workspace.
whenNotToUse: To remove someone else, use the revoke access recipe. To delete the workspace for everyone, ask with MonarchStepUpAuthDialog and a type-to-confirm field.
api: MonarchButton("Leave workspace", systemImage: "rectangle.portrait.and.arrow.right", variant: .danger) { … }
.alert("You can’t leave yet", isPresented: $isBlocked) { Button("Transfer ownership") { … }; Button("Close", role: .cancel) {} } message: { Text(reason) }
.sheet(isPresented: $isConfirming) { MonarchConsequenceList([…]); MonarchButton("Leave workspace", variant: .danger, isLoading: isLeaving, fullWidth: true) { … } }
.interactiveDismissDisabled(isLeaving)

states.name: confirm
states.description: A sheet with the title naming the workspace, a line saying it happens at once, the consequence list and a danger Leave workspace button with Cancel.

states.name: leaving
states.description: Leave workspace shows its spinner; Cancel is disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice in the sheet; the person can try again.

states.name: blocked
states.description: When the person is the last owner, or the app has another reason, the button opens an alert that says why and offers the fix (Transfer ownership) instead of leaving.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component or a system alert in the theme: the heading style title, MonarchConsequenceList with its kind icons, the danger and ghost MonarchButtons.
platformNotes: The web's LeaveWorkspaceFlow is one component built on ConfirmDialog and Dialog. On iOS it is a recipe: a system alert cannot hold a list or stay open while a request runs, so the confirmation is a sheet (which keeps the pending and error states inside it), and the blocked case, which only needs a sentence and two buttons, is a system alert. The web's default consequences and messages are written in the app here. The web's fixAction can be any element; in the alert it is a button. The parity map lists alert (MonarchBanner on iOS) as a part; the blocked explanation is a short modal message with a fix, which on iOS is the system alert, so MonarchBanner is not used. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The sheet's title has the header trait.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, so removed, kept and warning do not depend on the icon.
The alert is the system's, read in full by VoiceOver with its buttons; Close has the cancel role.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while leaving.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while leaving, so the result is not lost.
edgeCases: Check whether the person is the last owner on the server as well; the recipe's check only decides which dialog opens.
After leaving, navigate away from the workspace: its screens are no longer available.
List the apps the person loses by name when the workspace has several.

whenToUse: Beside the name of an API, endpoint, SDK or feature to say how far along it is, or for a custom stage such as a customer's lifecycle stage.
whenNotToUse: Not for the status of a record such as Paid or Draft (use MonarchBadge) and not for live presence (use MonarchStatusDot).

init(stage: String, label: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil, showsDot: Bool = true)
enum MonarchLifecycle: String { case planned, preview, stable, deprecated }

options.name: lifecycle
options.description: The built-in stage: planned, preview, stable or deprecated.

options.name: stage
options.description: In the second initialiser, the key of a stage. One of the four built-in names is drawn as that stage; any other key is neutral and shown as readable text unless label and tone are given.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in label. Already localised.

options.name: tone
options.description: Replaces the tone of the stage: planned neutral, preview info, stable success, deprecated warning, anything else neutral.
