platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchBadge as the base. MonarchBadge colours its text with the tone and has no dot, so this component draws the web's quieter look from the same tone palette. The web's accent tone is not offered because MonarchTone has no accent case; the web's sm size is not offered, the label is the caption role and follows Dynamic Type. The web's messages map is the label parameter and the strings table. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: Read as its label; the dot is hidden from VoiceOver, so the label carries the meaning without the colour.
The label and the dot scale with Dynamic Type.
Not interactive: it has no button trait and no action.
edgeCases: A stage key the app does not know is shown as the key with underscores and hyphens turned into spaces and a capital first letter; that text is not localised.
Keys are matched exactly: "Stable" is not the built-in stage stable.
An empty key with no label draws a capsule with only the dot.
Long labels wrap inside the capsule.

name: MonarchLightbox
title: Lightbox
wrapsNative: fullScreenCover(isPresented:content:), TabView with tabViewStyle(.page), MagnifyGesture, ScrollView, AsyncImage, ShareLink and AVKit's VideoPlayer
summary: A full-screen viewer for images and videos: swipe or step between items, pinch, double-tap or use buttons to zoom, with a caption and a position count.
whenToUse: To look at one or more pictures or videos at full size from a thumbnail, with a caption that belongs to the design: attachments in a conversation, a gallery on a record.
whenNotToUse: Not for documents, PDFs or files of unknown type, and not when captions are not needed: Quick Look (quickLookPreview) previews any file with the system's own viewer. Not for a single decorative image.
api: init(_ items: [MonarchLightboxItem], selection: Binding<Int>, isLooping: Bool = false, maximumZoom: Double = 4, labels: MonarchLightboxLabels = MonarchLightboxLabels(), onClose: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)

func monarchLightbox(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, items: [MonarchLightboxItem], selection: Binding<Int>, isLooping: Bool = false, maximumZoom: Double = 4, labels: MonarchLightboxLabels = MonarchLightboxLabels()) -> some View
MonarchLightboxItem.init(image: Image?, alt: String, caption: String? = nil, shareURL: URL? = nil)
MonarchLightboxItem.init(url: URL?, alt: String, caption: String? = nil, kind: MonarchLightboxItemKind = .image, shareURL: URL? = nil)
enum MonarchLightboxItemKind { case image, video }

MonarchLightboxLabels.init(title: String? = nil, previous: String? = nil, next: String? = nil, zoomIn: String? = nil, zoomOut: String? = nil, resetZoom: String? = nil, close: String? = nil, share: String? = nil, position: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, unavailable: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil)

options.name: items
options.description: The images and videos, in order. Each has alt text, and optionally a caption and a file to share.

options.name: selection
options.description: The index of the item on screen, starting at 0. An index outside the items shows the nearest item.

options.name: isPresented
options.description: In the monarchLightbox modifier: whether the viewer covers the screen.

options.name: isLooping
options.description: Whether the next button on the last item goes to the first, and back. Swiping does not wrap.

options.name: maximumZoom
options.description: The largest zoom factor of an image. Values below 1 count as 1, which turns zoom off.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the viewer's name, the button names, the position text, the loading and the unavailable text.

options.name: onClose
options.description: In the view's initialiser: called by the close button and the escape gesture. The modifier supplies it.

states.name: fitted
states.description: The image fits the stage. A sideways swipe moves to the next or previous item. The zoom-out and reset buttons are disabled.

states.name: zoomed
states.description: The image is larger than the stage and a drag pans it. The level is shown as a percentage on the reset button. The zoom-in button is disabled at the largest zoom.

states.name: first or last item
states.description: Without looping, the previous or next button is disabled.

states.name: single item
states.description: No position count and no previous and next buttons.

states.name: loading
states.description: An image from a URL shows a progress indicator until it arrives.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: An item with no source, an image that failed to load, and an empty list of items show "This file can’t be shown." in place of the media. Zoom is hidden.

states.name: video
states.description: The system player with its own controls. Zoom is hidden. The video pauses when another item is shown.

appearance: The viewer fills the screen with the canvas colour. The position count, the group of tools and the caption sit on the raised background colour, the tools with the medium elevation; text is the default text colour and disabled buttons use the disabled roles of the button style. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Lightbox is a Radix dialog over a translucent scrim with arrow buttons beside the image; here it is a full-screen cover on the opaque canvas, and swiping between items is the main gesture, with the previous and next buttons kept under the image for VoiceOver, Switch Control and pointer users. Pinch and double tap are added to the web's zoom buttons. The web's Download link is a ShareLink, whose sheet offers saving. The web's trigger prop is not needed: any button sets isPresented. The web's caption tracks for video are not offered; the system player shows the subtitles the stream itself carries. The web's check of the URL scheme is not repeated: AsyncImage and AVPlayer load what the app gives them. On macOS, which is only a build convenience, the pager shows the current item without swiping and the modifier uses a sheet. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The viewer is a container named "Media viewer" with the modal trait, and the escape gesture calls onClose. Presented with the modifier it is a full-screen cover, so the system confines focus to it.
An image is one element with its alt text as the label, the image trait and the zoom level as its value; VoiceOver's adjust gesture and zoom action step the zoom.
Moving to another item posts an announcement with the position and the item's alt text, such as "2 of 5: Team photo".
Zoom in, zoom out, reset zoom, share, close, previous and next are buttons with spoken names and 44-point touch targets. A zoom button announces the new level.
A video's alt text is the label of the player.
Zooming by double tap and stepping with the buttons animate unless Reduce Motion is on. The toolbar wraps to two rows and the caption scrolls at large text sizes.
edgeCases: Zoom belongs to one item: moving to another item returns to fitted.
While zoomed, a sideways drag pans the image and does not change the item; zoom out first, or use the buttons.
An empty alt is allowed by the type but leaves the image without a spoken name; always give one.
A caption taller than about a third of a phone screen scrolls inside its box.
A selection outside the items is shown as the nearest item; the binding is not rewritten until the person moves.
The left and right arrow keys of a hardware keyboard step between items, and Escape closes.

name: MonarchLineChart
title: LineChart
wrapsNative: Swift Charts: Chart with LineMark (series per run of values), AreaMark(x:yStart:yEnd:series:) for the area variant, PointMark for lone and inspected points, RuleMark for reference lines and the crosshair, chartXSelection(value:) for touch inspection, inside MonarchChartFrame (accessibilityChartDescriptor and View as table)
summary: A line or area chart for trends over time or ordered categories, with several series, gaps, reference lines, touch inspection, legend toggles and a data table.
whenToUse: To show how one or more measures change over days, weeks or months (traffic, sign-ups, revenue, latency), to compare a period with the previous one (a dashed series), or to show a trend against a target (a reference line).
whenNotToUse: To compare unordered categories, use a bar chart or MonarchBarList. For a small trend in a table cell or a card, use MonarchSparkline. For two measures in different units, draw two charts and share activeIndex instead of a second axis.
api: MonarchLineChart.init(_ title: String, dates: [Date], series: [MonarchLineChartSeries], description: String? = nil, xTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine] = [], variant: MonarchLineChartVariant = .line, curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = .linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, includesZero: Bool = true, valueDomain: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, showsPoints: Bool = false, isLegendInteractive: Bool = true, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, dateFormat: Date.FormatStyle = .dateTime.month(.abbreviated).day(), emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

MonarchLineChart.init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchLineChartSeries], description: String? = nil, xTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, referenceLines: [MonarchLineChartReferenceLine] = [], variant: MonarchLineChartVariant = .line, curve: MonarchLineChartCurve = .linear, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, includesZero: Bool = true, valueDomain: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, showsPoints: Bool = false, isLegendInteractive: Bool = true, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchLineChartSeries.init(_ key: String, label: String, values: [Double?], color: MonarchChartColor? = nil, isDashed: Bool = false)
MonarchLineChartReferenceLine.init(_ value: Double, label: String? = nil)
enum MonarchLineChartVariant { case line, area }
enum MonarchLineChartCurve { case linear, monotone }

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, a heading in the frame and the name VoiceOver reads.

options.name: dates
options.description: The x values, in order. Points are spaced by time, so uneven dates show.

options.name: categories
options.description: The x values, in order, already localised. Points are spaced evenly.

options.name: series
options.description: The measures, each with a key, a label, one value per x value (nil is a gap), an optional colour slot and isDashed.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title: the period, the unit or the question it answers.

options.name: xTitle
options.description: The heading of the x column of the data table. Built in: "Date" or "Category".

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure, for the data table and VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed horizontal lines with a label and value: targets, baselines, service levels.

options.name: variant
options.description: line, or area: the line with a soft fill down to the baseline.

options.name: curve
options.description: linear, or monotone: smooth without overshooting the data.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error, passed to the frame. A ready chart without x values is empty.

options.name: includesZero
options.description: Whether the value axis keeps zero. Turn it off for values far from zero.

options.name: valueDomain
options.description: Fixes the value axis, such as 0...100 for percentages.

options.name: showsPoints
options.description: A dot on every point. Lone points between gaps always get one.

options.name: isLegendInteractive
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected index. Bind several charts with the same x values to one value to share the crosshair.

options.name: dateFormat
options.description: How dates are written in the popover and the data table (dates initialiser). Set its time zone for fixed output.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the frame's empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart: the source, the last update.

options.name: height
options.description: The height of the plot, kept in every status. 240 points when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the frame's built-in strings; noValue is also the popover's text for a gap.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values in the popover, the table, VoiceOver and reference labels. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

states.name: default
states.description: One line per visible series in its colour slot, with axes from Swift Charts; dashed series have a dashed line.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: While the plot is touched, or activeIndex is set: a vertical crosshair, a larger point on each visible series and a popover with the x value and every visible series' value.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The series leaves the plot and the value range; its legend entry is struck through; it stays in the data table.

states.name: gap
states.description: A missing value breaks the line; a lone value between gaps is a dot.

states.name: area
states.description: Each line has a soft fill of its colour down to zero, or to the lowest value when zero is left out.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The frame's placeholder, empty state or error with Try again, at the chart's height.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" swaps the plot for the data table.

appearance: Series use the theme's data colours 1 to 5 in order (a sixth series and later are neutral, the subtle text colour); the area fill is the series colour at low strength. Reference lines and their labels are the muted text colour, dashed; the crosshair is the strong border colour; the popover is the raised surface with a medium shadow. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: Built on Swift Charts, which draws the axes, ticks and grid and spaces date values by time; the web draws its own SVG. Touch inspection uses chartXSelection: the crosshair follows the finger and clears when it lifts, where the web keeps the last tapped point. There is no keyboard inspection, live region or generated text summary: VoiceOver gets the data through the frame's accessibility chart descriptor, whose Audio Graph describes each series. The web xScale option is the choice of initialiser (dates or categories); dates cannot be spaced evenly. The web onPointSelect (drill-in) and the frame's header actions are not offered. locale, valueFormat and xFormat are the environment locale, formatValue and dateFormat; value-axis ticks use Swift Charts' own number format. Right-to-left layout follows Swift Charts. Android uses the same names. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The frame's title is a heading; the plot is one element named by the title, with the data as an accessibility chart descriptor (Audio Graphs and the chart's data table in the rotor).
"View as table" shows the data table, where each row is read as the x value followed by every series and its value, "No value" for a gap. Hidden series stay in the table.
Values are read with formatValue, so VoiceOver says "410 ms" rather than "410".
The inspection popover is hidden from VoiceOver.
Series differ by their names in the legend and, where isDashed is set, by a dashed line and marker, not by colour alone.
Legend toggles are switches named by the series; the last visible series cannot be hidden.
Text in the frame, legend, popover and reference labels scales with Dynamic Type; the plot keeps its height.
edgeCases: Missing, nil and non-finite values are gaps, never zero; a series shorter than the x values ends in gaps, and extra values are dropped.
A ready chart with no x values shows the empty state.
A single series has no legend; its name is the title.
With includesZero off and no valueDomain, the area fills down to the lowest visible value.
Reference lines are part of the value range, so a target far above the data stays visible.
An activeIndex outside the x values is ignored.
Duplicate categories are separate points in the table but share one position on the axis; give unique categories.

name: MonarchLineItemsEditor

wrapsNative: Two List/Form Sections: ForEach rows with .swipeActions(edge: .trailing) to remove, MonarchTextField, MonarchNumberInput (TextField(value:format:)) and MonarchCurrencyInput fields, MonarchMoney amounts, Picker (.segmented, .menu) for discount type and tax rate, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Editable invoice, quote or proposal rows (description, quantity, unit price) with each row's amount and an optional discount, tax and total computed exactly in Decimal.
whenToUse: To create or edit the billable rows of an invoice, quote, proposal or purchase order inside a Form or List, or to show the rows of a sent document read-only with the same totals.
whenNotToUse: For a finished invoice laid out as a document, use MonarchInvoiceView. For payroll lines that are calculated, not typed, use MonarchPayslipView. For editable tables of non-monetary data, use MonarchDataTable.
api: MonarchLineItemsEditor.init(items: Binding<[MonarchLineItem]>, currencyCode: String, taxRate: Binding<Decimal>? = nil, taxRateOptions: [MonarchLineItemsTaxRateOption] = [], discount: Binding<MonarchLineItemsDiscount>? = nil, error: String? = nil, minimumItems: Int = 0, isRequired: Bool = false, isReadOnly: Bool = false, isTaxRateEditable: Bool = false, isDiscountEditable: Bool = false, showsTotals: Bool = true, labels: MonarchLineItemsEditorLabels = MonarchLineItemsEditorLabels(), makeItem: (@MainActor () -> MonarchLineItem)? = nil)

options.name: items
options.description: The rows. Each has an id, a description and a Decimal quantity and unit price (nil while the field is empty, counted as zero). Every edit, addition and removal writes a new array.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code of the document. Sets the symbol, the unit price heading and the minor unit (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3). The editor never converts.

options.name: taxRate
options.description: The tax as a percentage of the discounted subtotal (18 for 18%). nil for no tax row. Pass .constant(18) for a fixed rate.

options.name: taxRateOptions
options.description: Preset rates offered in a menu picker when the tax rate is editable. Empty for a typed percentage.

options.name: discount
options.description: A percentage or amount off the subtotal, capped at it. nil for no discount row.

options.name: error
options.description: An error for the whole list, such as "Add at least one item", shown under the rows with an icon and announced.

options.name: minimumItems
options.description: Rows cannot be removed below this count.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: A marker after the heading, spoken as "Required".

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Rows as text (description and "12 × $95.00") without fields, buttons or swipe actions, for a sent document.

options.name: isTaxRateEditable
options.description: Whether the tax rate can be changed in the totals: a menu of taxRateOptions or a percent field.

options.name: isDiscountEditable
options.description: Whether the discount value (percent or currency field) and kind (segmented picker) can be changed.

options.name: showsTotals
options.description: Whether the totals section (subtotal, discount, tax, total) is shown.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: makeItem
options.description: Builds the row added by Add item. Default: an empty row with one unit and a new UUID.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each row has a header (Item n and its amount), a remove button, the description field, and the quantity and unit price fields side by side (stacked at accessibility text sizes). Add item follows the rows.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No items yet. Add one to start." in place of the rows; totals are zero.

states.name: error
states.description: The error under the rows in the danger text colour with an icon; a new error is announced.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Rows are text; no fields, add or remove; the discount and tax rates are written in their titles ("Tax (18%)").

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true), every field and button is disabled, swipe actions are not offered and the rate editors are hidden.

states.name: at the minimum
states.description: Remove buttons are disabled and swipe actions are not offered.

appearance: Rows and totals use the list's own section background. Row headers are the muted label style with the amount in the default text colour; fields are the Monarch field surface and border; the required marker and the error are the danger text colour; the total row is the strong body style above a divider. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the same roles.
platformNotes: On iOS the editor is two Sections for the app's Form or List instead of a table, so it sits among the app's own sections; rows are removed by the standard swipe action or a remove button. Numbers are typed in standard number fields, which commit on submit or when the field loses focus and refuse text that is not a number, so there is no invalid-number state and no parseDecimal; values are Decimal rather than strings. A unit price is rounded to the currency's decimals by MonarchCurrencyInput. Enter does not add a row and focus does not move to a new row (the Monarch fields keep their focus private); the addition is announced instead. The web locale prop is the environment locale. computeLineItemTotals is MonarchLineItemsTotals. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The heading is a header, read as "Line items, Required" when required.
Each row starts with a header read as "Item 2, Amount $1,140.00".
The description, quantity and unit price fields are named by their visible labels and keep the behaviour of MonarchTextField, MonarchNumberInput and MonarchCurrencyInput.
The remove button is read as "Remove item 2: Design hours" and has a 44-point target; the swipe action is also in the VoiceOver actions rotor.
Adding and removing a row is announced ("Item 3 added", "Item 2 removed"), and so is a new error.
Each totals row is one element read as its title and amount, such as "Total, $2,257.13".
edgeCases: Each row is rounded to the minor unit half away from zero (1 × 1.005 USD is $1.01) and totals are sums of whole minor units, so the total equals the rows shown.
A discount larger than the subtotal, or over 100%, is capped at the subtotal; a negative discount is ignored; a negative subtotal gets no discount.
Empty quantity or price fields count as zero.
A long description wraps.
The swipe action only works inside a List or Form; outside one, the remove button still works.
Rows are matched by id: give every row a unique, stable id.

summary: A preview of a shared link from data the app unfurled: picture, site, title and description as one link, with an optional remove button.
whenToUse: Under a message, post or comment that contains a link the app's server has unfurled, so people see where it leads before opening it.
whenNotToUse: For a plain link in text, use Link or Text with Markdown. For a record inside the app with its own actions, build a product card. LPLinkView (LinkPresentation) is the system alternative when the app lets the system fetch the preview itself.
api: init(_ title: String, url: URL, description: String? = nil, siteName: String? = nil, image: Image?, imageSize: CGSize? = nil, favicon: Image? = nil, isVideo: Bool = false, size: MonarchLinkCardSize = .md, dismissLabel: String? = nil, videoLabel: String? = nil, onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

enum MonarchLinkCardSize { case sm, md }

options.name: title
options.description: The page title.

options.name: url
options.description: The link. Only http, https and mailto open; anything else shows the card as plain text.

options.name: description
options.description: The page description, up to two lines.

options.name: siteName
options.description: The site above the title; the host name without www by default.

options.name: image / imageURL
options.description: The page's picture, or nil for none. A URL is loaded with AsyncImage.

options.name: imageSize
options.description: The picture's natural size; its ratio is kept between 1.2 and 2.2, and 2.2 when unknown.

options.name: favicon / faviconURL
options.description: The site's icon; without it MonarchFavicon draws a letter tile.

options.name: isVideo
options.description: Draws a play mark on the picture and adds "Video" to the spoken name.

options.name: size
options.description: md: banner above the text. sm: thumbnail beside it.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Remove the preview of" and the title.

options.name: videoLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken word "Video".

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a remove button in the corner.

states.name: loading picture
states.description: A muted placeholder keeps the picture's space while AsyncImage loads; it stays if loading fails.

states.name: not a safe link
states.description: The card is shown as plain text and does not open.

states.name: dismissible
states.description: A remove button with a surface-coloured circle sits in the top trailing corner.

appearance: A MonarchCard (surface fill, subtle border). The site is caption text in the muted colour with a small favicon, the title body-strong text in the default colour, the description caption text in the muted colour. The picture has the control corner radius; its placeholder uses the muted background fill. The play mark is the inverse text colour on the inverse background. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web LinkCard opens in a new tab with rel attributes, has a footer slot, and comes with LinkCardList and LinkCardSkeleton. On iOS the link opens through the openURL environment (the app can intercept it); there is no footer (place product actions below the card); a list is a VStack of cards; and a skeleton is the card with redacted(reason: .placeholder). A failed picture keeps its placeholder instead of disappearing, per the Monarch image convention. Android ships the same MonarchLinkCard.
accessibility: A safe link is the standard Link, one element with the link role, read as the site, the title, the description and "Video" for a video.
A link that does not open is one plain element with the same spoken text.
The picture, the play mark and the favicon are hidden from VoiceOver.
The remove button is a separate element named "Remove the preview of" and the title, with a 44-point touch target.
Text scales with Dynamic Type; the thumbnail and play mark scale with it.
edgeCases: Long titles are limited to two lines and descriptions to two lines; VoiceOver reads them in full.
Very tall or very wide pictures are cropped to the 1.2 to 2.2 ratio range.
Without a site name and with a URL that has no host (mailto), the site line is left out.
Opening the link was not tried on a device; the card uses the standard Link.

name: MonarchLinkStyle
title: Link
wrapsNative: Link and Button, with a ButtonStyle
summary: The Monarch look for a text link: a button style for the SwiftUI Link, or for a Button that navigates, in the variants inline, standalone and subtle.
whenToUse: For a link that is its own view: under a field, at the end of a row, in a footer, after a paragraph. Use Link when it opens a URL and Button when it navigates inside the app.
whenNotToUse: For a link in the middle of a sentence, write the sentence as Markdown in Text and set tint to the theme's link colour; a view cannot flow inside a line of text. For an action that changes something use MonarchButton.
api: MonarchLinkStyle.init(_ variant: MonarchLinkVariant = .inline, isExternal: Bool = false, externalLabel: String? = nil)
static func monarchLink(_ variant: MonarchLinkVariant = .inline, isExternal: Bool = false, externalLabel: String? = nil) -> MonarchLinkStyle
enum MonarchLinkVariant { case inline, standalone, subtle }

options.name: variant
options.description: inline: link colour, underlined. standalone: link colour, medium weight, no underline. subtle: muted text colour, no underline.

options.name: isExternal
options.description: Whether the link leaves the app. Adds an arrow.up.forward icon after the title, read as "opens in the browser".

options.name: externalLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "opens in the browser", read after the title.

states.name: resting
states.description: inline is underlined in the link colour; standalone is the link colour in medium weight; subtle is the muted text colour.

states.name: pressed
states.description: Every variant is underlined; subtle takes the default text colour.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The disabled text colour. Set with the standard disabled(_:) modifier.

states.name: Button Shapes on
states.description: Every variant is underlined at rest, so the link is not told from text by colour alone.

states.name: external
states.description: A small arrow icon follows the title.

appearance: The title and icon use the link text role (inline, standalone) or the muted text role (subtle), and the disabled text role when disabled. The underline is the text colour. The style draws no background. The high-contrast themes resolve the same roles to stronger colours.
platformNotes: The parity map lists this entry as a style named MonarchLinkStyle, and that is what is built; Android builds a MonarchLink composable because Compose has no link control. The style does not set the type size: like the web link it takes the font of the text around it, so apply monarchTextStyle to the link or its container. The web underlines inline links at 40% of the text colour and standalone and subtle links on hover; iOS has no hover on touch, so the underline is full strength, and the other variants are underlined while pressed and when Button Shapes is on. The web adds the external icon and note for target="_blank"; here isExternal is explicit, because where a URL opens is decided by the app: Link opens the default browser, and an app that wants an in-app browser sets the openURL environment action and presents SFSafariViewController (UIKit) itself. asChild has no equivalent; the style applies to any Button or Link.
accessibility: Link keeps the system's link trait and Button its button trait; the style changes only the look.
With isExternal the icon carries a label, so VoiceOver reads it after the title: "Terms of service, opens in the browser".
When the Button Shapes accessibility setting is on, every variant is underlined.
The touch target is at least 44 by 44 points; the visible text is centred in it.
The title scales with Dynamic Type through the font of its container and wraps, aligned to the leading edge.
edgeCases: Without monarchTextStyle on the link or its container the title uses the system body font.
The 44-point minimum height makes a link taller than a line of text; it is not meant to sit inside a paragraph.
A Button that opens a screen is read as a button. Add accessibilityAddTraits(.isLink) when it should be read as a link.
A label that is not text (an HStack with an icon) is underlined only on its text.

whenNotToUse: For uploaded files use MonarchFileList or MonarchUploadQueue. For document-to-document relations use MonarchDocumentRelations.

options.name: items
options.description: What is linked to the record, or nil while loading.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Hides linking, adding and unlinking.

options.name: notice
options.description: Replaces the list, such as a message that the person has no access to docs.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Something went wrong loading or changing links, shown above the list.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Shows Try again busy.

options.name: docOptions
options.description: The docs the picker offers. Docs already linked (by docID) are left out.

options.name: isSpaceFilterShown
options.description: Shows the space filter menu when the rows span more than one space.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again with errorMessage.

options.name: onLinkDoc
options.description: Links a doc, given its id. Shows Link doc in the Add menu; throwing shows "That didn’t link. Try again.".

options.name: onDocQueryChange
options.description: Called as the picker's search text changes, to search on the server and update docOptions. Without it the picker filters docOptions itself.

options.name: onCreateDoc
options.description: Shows New doc at the top of the picker.

options.name: onAddLink
options.description: Adds a link, given its address and title (the host when no title is typed). Shows Add link in the Add menu; throwing keeps the form open with the failure.

options.name: onUnlink
options.description: Unlinks a row. Shows an unlink button on rows that allow it; throwing shows the failure.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens a row: the app pushes the doc or opens the link.

states.name: list
states.description: One row per doc or link: the file type icon or a link symbol, the title, the secondary line and a status badge.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The space menu shows one space; a caption says how many rows other spaces hold, with Show all.

states.name: unlinking
states.description: The row's unlink button shows a spinner; other unlink buttons are disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger inline notice with "That didn’t unlink. Try again." or "That didn’t link. Try again.", announced.

states.name: loading
states.description: items is nil: the section card's skeleton rows, read as Loading linked docs.

states.name: empty
states.description: A muted sentence that invites linking, or "Nothing linked yet." when read only.

states.name: notice
states.description: An info inline notice in place of the list and the Add menu.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with onRetry, or a danger notice, above the list.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard with a secondary Add menu button. Rows have a small file type tile or a muted link symbol, the title in the strong body style, a caption in the muted text colour and a neutral MonarchBadge for the status. The pickers are system sheets with the system list, search field and form. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web panel opens a popover combobox to link a doc and an inline form to add a link; on iOS both are sheets: a NavigationStack with the system search field over a List, and a Form with Cancel and Add in the toolbar, the phone pattern for picking and entering data. The web's space filter chips become a menu Picker. The web's onSearchDocs promise becomes onDocQueryChange plus docOptions the app updates. Linking, adding and unlinking are async throwing handlers, so the panel keeps the busy and failed states itself; Android takes an unlinkingId from the app instead. The web's controlled filter and linkedDocIds are not offered: the filter is internal and linked docs are found by docID. Opening a row is the app's job (onOpen), since a native app pushes a doc screen or opens Safari.
accessibility: The title has the header trait (from MonarchSectionCard).
Each row is a button whose label is the title and whose value is the secondary line and status, built by a tested pure function; the icon is decorative.
Unlink is a separate button with a 44-point target named "Unlink <title>"; while it runs it shows a spinner.
Link and unlink failures are shown in words and posted as announcements.
The Add menu is a system Menu; the doc picker and link form are system sheets with a search field, a form and a Cancel button.
An invalid web address is explained in words with an icon under the field and announced.
edgeCases: Only http and https addresses with a host are accepted; javascript: and bare host names are rejected.
A link without a typed title is titled with its host, without www.
A filter for a space that no longer has rows shows every row.
The panel never removes or adds rows itself: the app updates items after each handler returns.
Only one unlink runs at a time.

whenToUse: For the rows of a list of records, settings or people, on the Monarch canvas.
whenNotToUse: For a table of columns use MonarchDataTable. For a grouped settings screen of system controls the system List and Form fit.
api: MonarchListRow.init(_ title: String, subtitle: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, showsChevron: Bool = false, showsDivider: Bool = true, trailing: () -> Trailing)
func monarchListRowStyle() -> some View

platformNotes: The system List draws its own insets, separators and fill. In a List, add monarchListRowStyle() to the row and monarchCanvas() to the list so the screen sits on the Monarch canvas. The web has no single list item; the row follows the menu item and description list metrics.
accessibility: The title, supporting text and trailing text are read as one element; the icon and chevron are hidden.
The row is at least 44 points high and grows with Dynamic Type.
The chevron flips in a right-to-left layout.
edgeCases: A long title wraps; the row grows.
Wrap the row in a Button or NavigationLink to make it act.

title: LiveRegion
wrapsNative: AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(_:).post(); AttributedString.accessibilitySpeechAnnouncementPriority; accessibilityAddTraits(.updatesFrequently)
summary: Telling a screen reader about a change without moving focus is a posted announcement on iOS, not a rendered region. Monarch ships nothing and uses the same call inside its components.
whenToUse: Post an announcement when something changes that the person did not directly cause or cannot see: a save finished, a result count changed, an error appeared, an item moved. For a value that changes continuously, add the updatesFrequently trait to the element instead.
whenNotToUse: Do not announce what VoiceOver already reads: the new value of the focused control, or a screen change. When a new screen or a large part of one appears, post AccessibilityNotification.ScreenChanged or LayoutChanged instead.
api: AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(_ announcement: String).post()
AccessibilityNotification.Announcement(_ announcement: AttributedString).post()
var AttributedString.accessibilitySpeechAnnouncementPriority: AccessibilityNotification.Announcement.Priority (.low, .default, .high)
func accessibilityAddTraits(_ traits: AccessibilityTraits) -> some View

states.name: polite
states.description: The default priority. The announcement may be dropped if other speech interrupts it.

states.name: assertive
states.description: The high priority interrupts current speech. Keep it for errors and for the steps of a drag.

appearance: Nothing is drawn. If sighted people need the message too, show it with a banner or text as well.
platformNotes: The web renders an aria-live region and changes its text; the web component also offers a useAnnouncer hook. iOS has no live region: the app posts the announcement at the moment of the change. Android sets a live-region property on a composable instead. Monarch components that announce (the text field's error, the stop button's stopped state, the typing dots) call the same API.
accessibility: System behaviour: the announcement is spoken by VoiceOver and shown on a braille display without moving focus.
Nothing is spoken when no assistive technology is running; posting is always safe.
An element with the updatesFrequently trait is re-read at intervals while it has focus, instead of on every change.
edgeCases: An announcement posted in the same moment as a screen change is usually lost; post it after the transition.
The same text posted twice is spoken twice. No padding character is needed, unlike on the web.
The priority attribute needs the AttributedString form.

name: MonarchLoadMore
title: LoadMore
wrapsNative: VStack footer of Text, MonarchButton and MonarchInlineErrorRetry; onAppear for auto-loading
summary: The footer of a paginated list: a Load more button with loading, failure and retry, an end-of-list line, an optional count and announcements.
whenToUse: At the end of a List or LazyVStack that loads pages from a cursor, with a button, or loading on its own when it scrolls into view.
whenNotToUse: For a list that is loaded whole, show nothing. For a first load, use MonarchLoadingState; for a first load that failed, use MonarchErrorState. For new content at the top, use refreshable(action:).
api: init(hasMore: Bool, isLoading: Bool = false, isFailed: Bool = false, loadedCount: Int? = nil, totalCount: Int? = nil, showsCount: Bool? = nil, showsEnd: Bool = true, autoLoads: Bool = false, labels: MonarchLoadMoreLabels = MonarchLoadMoreLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onLoadMore: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)
struct MonarchLoadMoreLabels { var loadMore, loading, failed, retry, end: String?; var count: (@Sendable (Int, Int?) -> String)?; var loaded: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? }

options.name: hasMore
options.description: Whether there is another page. False shows the end line.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: A page is being fetched; the button shows progress and ignores taps.

options.name: isFailed
options.description: The last fetch failed; shows the failure with a retry button and pauses auto-loading.

options.name: loadedCount
options.description: The items on screen. Shown in the count; increases are announced.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: The total, when the server knows it.

options.name: showsCount
options.description: Whether the count is shown. By default when loadedCount is given.

options.name: showsEnd
options.description: Whether "That's everything" is shown and announced at the end.

options.name: autoLoads
options.description: Loads the next page when the footer appears on screen; the button stays as the fallback.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the count and the announcement.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Runs when retry is activated. By default onLoadMore.

options.name: onLoadMore
options.description: Loads the next page.

states.name: idle
states.description: A small secondary Load more button, with the count above it.

states.name: loading
states.description: The button shows a progress indicator and the title "Loading…".

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn't load more." with a danger icon and a Retry button; while a retry runs, the button is busy.

states.name: done
states.description: "That's everything" in muted text, or nothing with showsEnd false.

appearance: Centred under the list with vertical padding. The count and the end line are caption text in the muted text colour. The button is a small secondary MonarchButton; the failure is a MonarchInlineErrorRetry in the danger tone.
platformNotes: The web also ships a useLoadMore hook that keeps the cursor and pages; on iOS the app's model keeps them, and the footer only shows the state. Auto-loading uses onAppear inside a lazy container instead of an IntersectionObserver, so there is no root margin: put the footer inside the List or LazyVStack. The web returns keyboard focus to the end line when the button disappears; on iOS VoiceOver focus is not moved. Android shares the name and the options.
accessibility: The button is a standard button with a 44-point touch target; while loading its value is "Loading…".
A failure is a MonarchInlineErrorRetry: the message is read with the danger tone's name and the retry button is separate.
New items are announced ("20 more items loaded."), as are a failure and the end of the list.
The button stays when auto-loading, so VoiceOver and Switch Control users load pages on purpose.
edgeCases: With autoLoads, a page that still leaves the footer on screen loads the next one when loading ends, until the screen is filled.
A failure pauses auto-loading until the retry succeeds.
The plural rules of the built-in count and announcement are English; pass labels.count and labels.loaded for other languages.

name: MonarchLoadingState
title: LoadingState
wrapsNative: Text placeholders with redacted(reason: .placeholder), or ProgressView with .progressViewStyle(.circular)
summary: A placeholder for content that is loading: skeleton rows, cards or paragraphs, or a labelled spinner, announced once.
whenToUse: In place of a list, a grid or a detail page during its first load, when the real layout cannot be drawn yet.
whenNotToUse: When the real views can be drawn with sample data, apply redacted(reason: .placeholder) to them instead (see skeleton). For the next page of a list, use MonarchLoadMore. For a load that failed, use MonarchErrorState.
api: init(_ label: String, variant: MonarchLoadingStateVariant = .list, rows: Int = 4)
enum MonarchLoadingStateVariant { case list, rows, cards, detail, spinner }

options.name: label
options.description: What is loading, such as "Loading tickets". Read and announced; shown by the spinner variant.

options.name: variant
options.description: list (avatar and two lines), rows (a line and a short value), cards (a grid of blocks), detail (a title and paragraphs) or spinner.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows or cards drawn by list, rows and cards. Negative counts draw none.

appearance: Placeholder lines are the system redaction bars drawn with the subtle text colour; avatars and cards are filled with the muted background colour and the container corner radius. The spinner is the system circular ProgressView with the label in muted body text. Nothing moves.
platformNotes: The web skeleton shimmers; the system placeholder on iOS is still, so nothing needs stopping under Reduce Motion. The web marks the region aria-busy; iOS has no busy state, so the label is announced once instead. Android shares the name and the variants.
accessibility: The view is one element read as the label; the placeholders are hidden from VoiceOver.
The label is announced once when the view appears.
The spinner variant also shows the label.
Placeholder lines are text, so their height follows Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Placeholder lines are one line each and are cut at the edge at the largest text sizes.
Card columns are at least 160 points wide, so a phone in portrait shows two columns.
Showing the view again announces the label again; keep it on screen for the whole load.

name: MonarchLocationFields
title: LocationFields
wrapsNative: MonarchCountrySelect or MonarchCombobox for the country, MonarchRegionSelect for the region, MonarchCombobox with searchText and .task(id:) or MonarchTextField with .textContentType(.addressCity) for the city, and MonarchTextField with .textContentType(.postalCode) for the postal code, in a VStack
summary: Country, region, city and postal code as one address block, labelled with each country's own words, with lists from the built-in data or an injected adapter.
whenToUse: In a form that needs where someone is (billing, shipping, a company's registered address) as separate, structured parts.
whenNotToUse: For a full street address found by typing, use MonarchAddressAutocomplete. For only a country or only a region, use MonarchCountrySelect or MonarchRegionSelect on their own.
api: init(_ legend: String? = nil, value: Binding<MonarchLocationValue>, adapter: MonarchLocationAdapter = MonarchLocationAdapter(), fields: [MonarchLocationField] = MonarchLocationField.allCases, required: Set<MonarchLocationField> = [], errors: [MonarchLocationField: String] = [:], priorityCountries: [String] = [], locale: Locale? = nil, cityMinQuery: Int = 2, cityDebounce: Duration = .milliseconds(250), allowsCustomCity: Bool = true, labels: MonarchLocationFieldsLabels = MonarchLocationFieldsLabels())

struct MonarchLocationValue: Equatable, Hashable, Sendable { var country: String?; var region: String?; var regionName: String; var city: String; var cityID: String?; var postalCode: String; init(country: String? = nil, region: String? = nil, regionName: String = "", city: String = "", cityID: String? = nil, postalCode: String = "") }
enum MonarchLocationField: String, CaseIterable { case country, region, city, postalCode }

struct MonarchLocationAdapter: Sendable { init(countries: (@Sendable () async throws -> [MonarchLocationOption])? = nil, regions: (@Sendable (String) async throws -> MonarchLocationRegions)? = nil, cities: (@Sendable (MonarchLocationCityQuery) async throws -> [MonarchLocationCity])? = nil) }
struct MonarchLocationOption: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchLocationRegions: Hashable, Sendable { init(_ regions: [MonarchRegion], label: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchLocationCity: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, name: String, description: String? = nil, region: MonarchRegion? = nil) }
struct MonarchLocationCityQuery: Hashable, Sendable { let country: String; let region: String?; let query: String }

struct MonarchLocationFieldsLabels: Sendable { init(country:region:city:postalCode:countriesLoadFailed:regionsLoadFailed:citiesLoadFailed:chooseCountryFirst:typeMore:noMatch:useTyped:), every parameter optional }

options.name: legend
options.description: A visible heading over the fields, with the header trait.

options.name: value
options.description: The address. A new country clears the region, city and postal code; a different listed region clears the city.

options.name: adapter
options.description: Where the countries, regions and cities come from. A nil closure uses the built-in country list, the built-in region lists with a text field for other countries, and a city text field.

options.name: fields
options.description: The fields to show, in order.

options.name: required
options.description: Fields that must be filled; the country, region and city search fields show a required mark and add Required to their hint.

options.name: errors
options.description: An error message per field, shown with an icon and announced.

options.name: priorityCountries
options.description: Country codes listed first under Suggested in the built-in country list.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the built-in country names. The environment's locale by default.

options.name: cityMinQuery
options.description: Letters needed before cities are searched while no region is chosen. With a region, its cities are listed at once.

options.name: cityDebounce
options.description: How long to wait after typing before the city search runs.

options.name: allowsCustomCity
options.description: Offers a Use “text” row that keeps the typed text as the city when it is not among the results.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces the field labels, the load errors, Choose a country first, the city list's messages and the Use “text” row.

states.name: no country
states.description: The region field is disabled with Choose a country first; a city search field is disabled with the same prompt.

states.name: listed region
states.description: A MonarchRegionSelect list labelled with the country's word, such as State or Province or territory.

states.name: typed region
states.description: A text field for a country without a list, or when the adapter returns no regions.

states.name: loading
states.description: The country or region list shows Loading... while the adapter runs; the city list shows a progress indicator while it searches.

states.name: load failed
states.description: The country or region field has an inline error with Try again; a failed city search shows Couldn't load the cities. as the list's text.

states.name: error
states.description: A field with a message has the danger border, an icon and the text, and the message is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every field uses its disabled roles and cannot be changed.

appearance: The fields are MonarchCountrySelect, MonarchRegionSelect, MonarchCombobox and MonarchTextField, so they share the input background, border and error roles; the legend uses the subheading style in the default text role. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web LocationFields lays the fields out in a grid in a fieldset; on iOS they stack in one column, which fits a phone and Dynamic Type. The web adapter's AbortSignal is Swift task cancellation. Without an adapter the web needs a country list from the product; iOS uses MonarchCountrySelect with Foundation's country names and MonarchRegionSelect's built-in lists, so the default works with no data. The postal code label follows the country (ZIP code for US, Postcode for GB and AU, PIN code for IN), which the web does not do. MonarchTextField has no required mark, so required applies the mark to the list fields only. The web value's cityId is cityID, following Swift naming. A failed city search has no Try again button in the list; typing again searches again. Android plans the same component. MonarchLocationAdapter has several optional closures (countries, regions, cities). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is countries.
accessibility: The legend has the header trait and the fields are one container, so VoiceOver can move through the block.
Each field is the button or text field of the component it is built on, labelled with the field's label, valued with the chosen name, and with the error, help and Required in its hint.
The city and postal code text fields tell AutoFill they hold the city and the postal code; the region text field tells it the state.
A failed country or region load is an inline error with a Try again button.
edgeCases: Changing the country clears every other part, so a region or city of another country never stays behind.
A city chosen before a region fills in the city's region; a region chosen afterwards that differs clears the city.
Typed city text is stored with cityID nil, so the app can tell it from a listed city.
Adapter regions are loaded once per country while the view is shown; a failed load is asked again only after Try again.
Long legends and labels wrap at every text size.

title: LogDrawer
wrapsNative: sheet(item:) or sheet(isPresented:) with presentationDetents([.medium, .large]), a NavigationStack with a navigationTitle and a confirmationAction ToolbarItem, a ScrollView, and LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch)
summary: A recipe, not a component: the full record of one log entry (an API request, a webhook delivery, a job run) in a sheet, with method and path, status, request ID with copy, time, duration and the payload.
whenToUse: When a row of a request log, a webhook delivery list or a job history is tapped and the app shows everything recorded about that entry.
whenNotToUse: For the list of entries itself use List or MonarchDataTable. For a value that only needs copying use MonarchCopyField. On iPad with room for a detail column, show the same content in a NavigationSplitView detail instead of a sheet.
api: List(entries) { … }.sheet(item: $selected) { entry in NavigationStack { ScrollView { VStack { LabeledContent("Operation") { MonarchMethodBadge(…); Text(path) } LabeledContent("Status") { MonarchStatusBadge(…) } HStack { LabeledContent("Request ID") { Text(id) }; MonarchCopyButton(value: id, target: "request ID", isIconOnly: true) } MonarchCodeBlock(body, language: "json") }.labeledContentStyle(.monarch) }.navigationTitle("Request details").toolbar { ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction) { Button("Close") { … } } } }.presentationDetents([.medium, .large]) }

states.name: closed
states.description: Only the list or button that opens the sheet.

states.name: open
states.description: A sheet at medium height that can be pulled to large, titled "Request details", with Close in the confirmation slot.

states.name: loading
states.description: While the entry loads, the sheet shows MonarchLoadingState with the detail variant and the label "Loading details".

states.name: load error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with "The details did not load." and Try again.

states.name: status tones
states.description: The status badge uses success for 2xx, info for 3xx, warning for 4xx and danger for 5xx, with the code as its text.

appearance: The system sheet and navigation bar. Terms and values use the Monarch labeled content style (muted term above the value), the method badge and status badge keep their tones, ids and paths use the code type role, and the payload is a MonarchCodeBlock. All adapt to light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships LogDrawer as one component: a side sheet from the right that fills the screen on phones, with request, fields, loading, error, onRetry, locale, now and messages props. On iOS it is a recipe: a sheet with detents is the system's surface for a record's details, Close goes in the navigation bar, and each fact is a LabeledContent the app lists itself. The web's httpStatusTone helper is a small function in the recipe. There is no relative time with a tooltip; show Text(date, style: .relative) or a formatted date.
accessibility: The sheet is modal for VoiceOver and the navigation title is read first.
Each fact is one element read as the term and the value, through the Monarch labeled content style.
The request ID copy button is a separate element named "Copy request ID" and announces the copy; keep it outside the LabeledContent so it is not merged into the fact.
The status is a word in a badge, not only a colour.
Close is in the standard place and is reached with the escape gesture (two-finger scrub).
edgeCases: Long paths and ids wrap in the code type role; the payload code block scrolls sideways inside itself or wraps with its toggle.
Leave out a fact the entry does not have instead of showing an empty value.
At the largest text sizes the content scrolls inside the sheet; pull the sheet to large.

name: MonarchLogViewer
title: LogViewer
wrapsNative: ScrollViewReader and ScrollView with a LazyVStack of monospaced Text built from AttributedString; MonarchToggleGroup for the level filters; Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton) for Follow and Wrap; MonarchButton for the jump button; MonarchEmptyState
summary: A streaming log with level filters and counts, search that filters or highlights, follow mode that keeps the newest line in view, and a wrap toggle.
whenToUse: To show the output of a build, a job, a deployment or a service: many short lines that arrive while the reader watches.
whenNotToUse: For a fixed snippet of code or a command, use MonarchCodeBlock. For a searchable audit trail of user actions, use MonarchActivityTimeline or a table.
api: MonarchLogViewer.init(_ lines: [MonarchLogLine], levels: Binding<Set<MonarchLogLevel>>? = nil, query: Binding<String>? = nil, isFollowing: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isWrapped: Binding<Bool>? = nil, searchMode: MonarchLogViewerSearchMode = .filter, showsTimestamps: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = false, isLoading: Bool = false, labels: MonarchLogViewerLabels = MonarchLogViewerLabels(), @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

MonarchLogViewer.init(_ lines: [MonarchLogLine], levels: Binding<Set<MonarchLogLevel>>? = nil, query: Binding<String>? = nil, isFollowing: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isWrapped: Binding<Bool>? = nil, searchMode: MonarchLogViewerSearchMode = .filter, showsTimestamps: Bool = true, showsLineNumbers: Bool = false, isLoading: Bool = false, labels: MonarchLogViewerLabels = MonarchLogViewerLabels()) where Actions == EmptyView
MonarchLogLine.init(id: String, message: String, level: MonarchLogLevel = .info, time: Date? = nil, source: String? = nil)
enum MonarchLogLevel { case debug, info, warn, error }
enum MonarchLogViewerSearchMode { case filter, highlight }

MonarchLogViewerLabels.init(log: String? = nil, levels: String? = nil, levelName: (@Sendable (MonarchLogLevel) -> String)? = nil, search: String? = nil, searchPrompt: String? = nil, clearSearch: String? = nil, follow: String? = nil, wrap: String? = nil, count: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, jumpToLatest: String? = nil, newLines: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, followPaused: String? = nil, followResumed: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, noMatches: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil)

options.name: lines
options.description: The lines, oldest first. Append to the array to stream.

options.name: levels
options.description: The levels shown. Kept inside, with all four on at first, when nil.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text. Kept inside when nil. Trimmed and matched against the message and the source, ignoring case.

options.name: isFollowing
options.description: Whether the newest line is kept in view. Kept inside, on at first, when nil. The viewer sets it to false when the reader drags toward older lines and to true when they return to the end.

options.name: isWrapped
options.description: Whether long lines wrap. Kept inside, off at first, when nil. Unwrapped lines scroll sideways.

options.name: searchMode
options.description: filter hides lines without a match; highlight keeps every line. Both mark the matches.

options.name: showsTimestamps
options.description: Shows the time of each line as 24-hour HH:mm:ss.SSS in the environment's time zone.

options.name: showsLineNumbers
options.description: Shows each line's 1-based position in lines, which stays the same when filters hide lines.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows Loading log while lines is empty.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the level names, the count and the jump button.

options.name: actions
options.description: Extra controls after Follow and Wrap, such as ShareLink or a Clear button.

states.name: following
states.description: Every new line scrolls the log to the end. The Follow toggle is on.

states.name: paused
states.description: The log stays where the reader is. A Jump to latest button floats over the bottom of the log and becomes "3 new lines" when lines arrive.

states.name: wrapped
states.description: Long lines wrap inside the width; otherwise each line is one row and the log scrolls sideways.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The footer reads "2 of 5 lines". When nothing is left, a filtered empty state offers Clear filters, which empties the search and turns every level back on.

states.name: loading
states.description: A spinner and Loading log while there are no lines yet.

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty state, No log lines yet.

appearance: The log sits in a rounded area on the subtle background with a subtle border. Lines use the code type role. Level names are bold, debug in the muted text colour and info, warn and error in the strong colour of their tone; warning and error lines have the subtle tone background. Sources are in the accent's strong colour and search matches have the subtle warning background and an underline. In dark and high-contrast themes the same roles are used.
platformNotes: The web LogViewer measures and virtualises rows itself; on iOS a LazyVStack builds rows as they scroll into view. The web pauses following from the scroll position; here a drag toward older lines pauses it, and the bottom of the log coming back into view after the reader scrolled resumes it, because iOS 17 offers no scroll position callback. Home and End keys of the web are not offered; Follow and the jump button do the same. The time formatter is fixed to HH:mm:ss.SSS and cannot be replaced. Android uses the same name and API shape.
accessibility: The log area is a container named "Log".
Each line is one element read as its level, time, source and message.
The level filters are a toggle group named "Levels"; each filter is a switch read with its count.
Follow and Wrap lines are toggles read with their on or off value.
Pausing and resuming following are announced: "Following paused" and "Following new lines".
Search matches are underlined as well as tinted, and the level is written as a word, so neither relies on colour.
The search field has a 44-point clear button named "Clear search".
VoiceOver scrolling does not pause following; turn Follow off to read back.
edgeCases: Lines without a time leave out the time column; lines without a source leave out the source.
Long lines without wrap make the whole log scroll sideways.
Ids must be unique and stable; a repeated id confuses the scroll target.
The viewer never grows with its lines: give it a height with frame(height:), otherwise it is about twelve lines tall.
Line numbers keep their positions in the full list, so a filtered log shows gaps.

examples.setupTemplate:
private let lines = [
    MonarchLogLine(id: {{lines.0.id}}, message: {{lines.0.message}}, level: {{lines.0.level|case}}, time: {{lines.0.time|date}}, source: {{lines.0.source}}),

enum MonarchLogoCloudLayout { case row, grid }

options.name: title
options.description: A short line above the logos, shown in small capitals; also the spoken name of the cloud.

options.name: logos

options.name: layout

platformNotes: The web LogoCloud also swaps in a dark-theme image through <picture> and restores colour on hover. On iOS the app passes the Image (an asset with light and dark appearances covers the dark logo), there is no hover, and a URL image is loaded by the app. Links open with the system, as every Link does. Android does not ship this component.

Each logo is one element read as the organisation's name, whether it shows an image or a wordmark.
A logo with a destination is a link and is at least 44 points tall.
The title has the header trait.
edgeCases: Long names wrap inside their row or cell.
Two logos with the same name share an identity; give each organisation a distinct name.
Images keep their aspect ratio at the size's height; a very wide image takes a row of its own.

name: MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox
title: MarketingConsentCheckbox
wrapsNative: Toggle with MonarchCheckboxToggleStyle, one per channel; SwiftUI.Link for the policy
summary: An opt-in to marketing messages: one checkbox, or one per channel, with the notes that belong to it, that reports the exact wording shown with every change.
whenToUse: On sign-up, checkout and contact forms where the person may agree to marketing by email, text message, phone or post.
whenNotToUse: For agreeing to terms, or any other checkbox, use Toggle with the monarchCheckbox style. For notification settings that take effect at once, use a standard Toggle.
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, selection: Binding<Set<MonarchMarketingChannel>>, channels: [MonarchMarketingChannel] = [.email], description: String? = nil, policyTitle: String? = nil, policyURL: URL? = nil, showsUnsubscribeNote: Bool = true, unsubscribeNote: String? = nil, channelLabels: [MonarchMarketingChannel: String] = [:], onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchMarketingConsent) -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchMarketingChannel: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case email, sms, phone, post }

struct MonarchMarketingConsent: Sendable, Hashable { let channels: [MonarchMarketingChannel: Bool]; let text: String; let date: Date; var granted: Set<MonarchMarketingChannel>; init(channels:text:date:) }

options.name: label
options.description: The question. Built in: "Send me product news by email" for one channel, "Send me product news" for several.

options.name: selection
options.description: The channels the person agreed to. Start it empty.

options.name: channels
options.description: The channels to ask about. One checkbox each when there are several.

options.name: description
options.description: What is sent and how often.

options.name: policyTitle
options.description: The title of a link to the privacy policy. Shown only with policyURL.

options.name: policyURL
options.description: Where the privacy policy is.

options.name: showsUnsubscribeNote
options.description: Shows the note that consent can be withdrawn.

options.name: unsubscribeNote
options.description: Replaces the built-in "You can unsubscribe at any time."

options.name: channelLabels
options.description: Replaces the built-in labels of the channel checkboxes.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Runs on every change with the channels, the wording shown and the time.

states.name: one channel
states.description: One checkbox whose label is the question, with the notes under it.

states.name: several channels
states.description: The question as a heading, the notes, then one checkbox per channel.

states.name: ticked
states.description: The checkbox look of MonarchCheckboxToggleStyle: an accent box with a check mark.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(_:) the checkboxes, the question and the notes use the disabled colours and the link does not open.

appearance: Checkboxes are drawn by MonarchCheckboxToggleStyle. The question above several checkboxes is label text; the notes are caption text in the muted colour; the policy link is underlined caption text in the link colour. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ignores defaultChecked so the boxes cannot start ticked. On iOS the state is a binding the app owns, as it is for every SwiftUI control, so the component cannot enforce that: the documentation tells the app to start the set empty and to bind a stored choice only on a settings screen. The web posts hidden form inputs (name, textName) and listens for a form reset; a native app has no form post, so the app sends the MonarchMarketingConsent it receives in onChange. The wording is built from the strings the component draws, not read back from the screen. The web takes React nodes for the label and notes; here they are plain strings and the policy is one title and one URL.
accessibility: Each checkbox is a standard Toggle behind the Monarch checkbox look: toggle role, on and off values, and the whole row as the touch target.
With several channels the question has the header trait.
The notes are read as text after the question; the policy link is a standard Link with a 44-point touch target.
The link is underlined, so it does not depend on colour.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps.
edgeCases: An empty channels array asks about email; a channel listed twice is shown once.
The record lists every shown channel, ticked or not, so a withdrawal is recorded as well as a grant.
policyTitle without policyURL shows no link and is left out of the recorded wording.
A channel in the selection that is not shown stays in the selection untouched.
onChange does not run when the app changes the binding itself.

whenNotToUse: Not for several files or attachments (use MonarchFileUpload with MonarchUploadQueue), and not for a profile picture with cropping (use MonarchAvatarUpload).

struct MonarchMediaUploadResult: Hashable, Sendable { init(url: URL, warnings: [String] = []) }

struct MonarchMediaUploadContext: Sendable { let kind: MonarchMediaUploadKind; init(kind: MonarchMediaUploadKind, progress: @escaping @Sendable (Double) -> Void); func reportProgress(_ fraction: Double) }

struct MonarchMediaUploadLabels: Sendable { init(addImage:addMedia:uploadFailed:cancel:cancelled:imageUploaded:videoUploaded:replaceImage:replaceVideo:removeImage:removeVideo:imageRemoved:videoRemoved:previewImage:previewVideo:warnings:close: String? = nil, imageHint: (@Sendable (String?) -> String)? = nil, videoHint: (@Sendable (String?, String?) -> String)? = nil, videoNotAllowed: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, tooLarge: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, tooLong: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, durationUnreadable: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, checking: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, uploading: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, fileUpload: MonarchFileUploadLabels = MonarchFileUploadLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It is a header.

options.name: url
options.description: The address of the stored file, or nil when empty. An upload sets it; Remove sets it to nil.

options.name: kind
options.description: The kind of the current file. When nil, the kind of the latest upload, or a guess from the address's extension.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the label.

options.name: kinds
options.description: The kinds that are taken.

options.name: maxImageSize
options.description: The largest image, in bytes. Larger images are refused with the file name and the limit.

options.name: maxVideoSize
options.description: The largest video, in bytes.

options.name: maxVideoDuration
options.description: The longest video, in seconds, read from the file's metadata before upload.

options.name: videoUnavailable
options.description: Why videos cannot be added, in the product's words. Shown in the hint when kinds has no video, and videos can then be picked so the refusal explains itself.

options.name: previewLabel
options.description: The spoken name of the image preview. "Uploaded image" when nil.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, and for the file picker area's strings.

options.name: onUpload
options.description: Stores the file, reports progress through the context and returns the stored address and any warnings. Cancel cancels its task. Throw to show an error.

states.name: empty
states.description: A dashed area with the title, the hint lines and Browse and Photos buttons.

states.name: checking
states.description: An indeterminate progress bar with "Checking clip.mov…" and Cancel upload.

states.name: uploading
states.description: A progress bar, indeterminate until the first report, with "Uploading photo.jpg · 40%" and Cancel upload.

states.name: filled
states.description: The image preview or the video poster, a compact Replace area and Remove.

states.name: refused
states.description: The file picker area shows the refusal as a danger notice with an icon.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger notice with the error's description, or "The upload failed. Try again."; the field returns to empty or to the previous file.

states.name: warnings
states.description: A warning notice led by "Uploaded with warnings." with one line per warning.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The pickers and buttons do nothing and take the disabled colours.

appearance: The empty field is the file upload area with its dashed border. The image preview is a 16 to 9 rounded frame on the muted background with a subtle border; the video preview is the video thumbnail with a play mark. Remove is a small danger button. Dark and high-contrast themes resolve the same roles.
platformNotes: The web has a drop zone and a hidden file input; on iPhone the pickers are the system photo picker and document picker (drag and drop also works on iPad), through MonarchFileUpload. The web's transform callback is not offered: an app shrinks or converts the file inside onUpload. Cancellation is Swift task cancellation instead of an AbortSignal, and progress is a fraction from 0 to 1 instead of a percentage. The value is the stored file's address only; an app with its own image pipeline previews the stored image elsewhere. Android uses the same name.
accessibility: The label is a header and the help text follows it.
Browse, Photos, Cancel upload, Replace and Remove are standard buttons with 44-point touch targets.
Progress is a standard progress view whose label is the file name and whose value is the percentage when known.
Refusals and upload errors are announced and shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
"Image uploaded" or "Video uploaded", "Upload cancelled" and "Image removed" are announced.
The image preview is one image element named "Uploaded image" or previewLabel; the video preview is a "Play" button that opens the system player.
edgeCases: A file without a size is not checked for size.
Starting a new pick while one uploads cancels the earlier one; its late answer and progress are ignored.
A video's length is read only when maxVideoDuration is set.
A remote video's poster is captured with AVFoundation and may take a moment; the thumbnail placeholder shows until then.

summary: Site-style navigation for a product's public, help or tour screens: a row of entries, where an entry with groups opens a panel of grouped links with symbols, descriptions and badges, and an optional featured card.
whenToUse: For a band of destinations that need a description each, such as a help centre, a product tour or the public screens of an app.
whenNotToUse: For an app's top-level navigation, use a TabView or NavigationSplitView. For a few actions on one object, use a Menu. For settings, use a List.

MonarchMegaMenuItem.init(_ id: String, label: String, destination: URL?)
