options.name: items
options.description: The top-level entries: menus with groups and a featured card, or plain links.

options.name: openItem
options.description: The id of the entry whose panel is open. Without it the menu keeps its own.

options.name: exploreLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Explore" action of the featured card and the hint of a menu entry.

options.name: onNavigate
options.description: Called with the chosen link; without it the link's destination opens with openURL.

states.name: closed
states.description: A row of entries; a menu entry has a down chevron.

states.name: open
states.description: The entry is filled and its chevron turned; its panel is a popover under it with the groups and the featured card.

states.name: link
states.description: A link row with a symbol tile, a badge, a description and, for an external link, an outward arrow.

appearance: Entries use the label role, muted until open. Group headings are captions in small capitals in the muted colour; link titles are bold body text, descriptions muted; symbol tiles use the subtle background with the accent's strong colour; badges use the accent tone. The panel uses the raised background and the featured card the subtle one. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web MegaMenu opens panels on hover with a delay, as a disclosure navigation with columns, and as a menu dialog on narrow screens. iOS has no hover: an entry opens its panel on tap, as a popover under it on iPhone and iPad, and it closes when a link is chosen or with a tap outside. Groups stack in one column. Android does not ship this component.
accessibility: Each entry is a button; a menu entry has the hint "Explore".
Group headings have the header trait.
Each link is one button read as its title, its badge and its description; an external link also has the link trait.
The featured card is one button with the hint "Explore".
Symbols are decorative and hidden from VoiceOver.
edgeCases: Many entries wrap onto a second row; keep the entries few.
A tall panel scrolls within the popover's height.
A link with neither a destination nor onNavigate does nothing when chosen.

name: MonarchMemberRow
title: MemberRow
wrapsNative: Row view with Picker(.menu) for the role, .swipeActions and .confirmationDialog, on MonarchAvatar and MonarchBadge
summary: One member of a workspace, space or channel: avatar, name, email, role, status (active, invited, suspended) and actions that are confirmed and may run asynchronously.
whenToUse: In a list of people with a role that some viewers may change, including pending invitations with resend and revoke.
whenNotToUse: For choosing people to add, use a searchable picker. For a dense table with many columns per person, use a Table with MonarchAvatar cells. For choosing a role with descriptions, use MonarchRolePicker.
api: init(_ name: String, image: Image?, email: String? = nil, meta: String? = nil, presence: MonarchPresenceStatus? = nil, status: MonarchMemberRowStatus = .active, statusTone: MonarchTone? = nil, role: String? = nil, roles: [MonarchRoleOption<String>] = [], badges: [String] = [], isSelf: Bool = false, canChangeRole: Bool? = nil, canRemove: Bool? = nil, removeConsequences: [String] = [], labels: MonarchMemberRowLabels = MonarchMemberRowLabels(), onRoleChange: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onResend: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onRemove: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(_ name: String, image: Image?, …) where Actions == EmptyView and init(_ name: String, url: URL?, …) where Actions == EmptyView, with the same parameters except actions
enum MonarchMemberRowStatus { case active, invited, suspended }

struct MonarchMemberRowLabels { init(you:invited:suspended:presence:roleLabel:chooseRole:resend:resendLabel:resent:remove:revoke:removeTitle:revokeTitle:removeDescription:revokeDescription:removeConfirm:revokeConfirm:cancel:failed:), every parameter optional }

options.name: name
options.description: The display name; also seeds the avatar's initials and colour. For an invitation, the email.

options.name: image / url
options.description: The avatar picture, or its URL loaded with AsyncImage. Initials show without it, while loading and on failure.

options.name: email
options.description: Email or handle under the name, truncated in the middle.

options.name: meta
options.description: Extra detail: joined date, invite expiry, availability.

options.name: presence
options.description: Presence dot on the avatar, also read after the name.

options.name: status
options.description: Invited adds an info badge, Resend invite and Revoke; suspended a warning badge and a muted name.

options.name: statusTone
options.description: The tone of the status badge. nil keeps the default: info for invited, warning for suspended.

options.name: role
options.description: The value of the member's role, one of roles.

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles allowed here (the role picker's type). Titles also show for a read-only role; disabled options cannot be picked.

options.name: badges
options.description: Extra neutral badges after the name, such as "Guest".

options.name: isSelf
options.description: The signed-in person: "(You)" after the name; role picker and Remove hidden by default.

options.name: canChangeRole
options.description: Shows the role picker. By default when onRoleChange is given and it is not your own row.

options.name: canRemove
options.description: Shows Remove. By default when onRemove is given and it is not your own row.

options.name: removeConsequences
options.description: Lines added under the message of the remove confirmation.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string; closures receive the member's name.

options.name: onRoleChange
options.description: Makes the role a picker. The new role shows while it runs; a thrown error restores the previous role and shows the error in the row.

options.name: onResend
options.description: Sends an invitation again; shown for invited rows. "Invite sent again." is shown and announced when it returns.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes the member or revokes the invitation after a confirmation. The app removes the row; a thrown error is shown in the row.

options.name: actions
options.description: More trailing controls before Remove, such as a Menu. Name them after the member.

states.name: active
states.description: No status badge.

states.name: invited
states.description: Info badge "Invited", a Resend invite button, and Remove becomes Revoke invite.

states.name: suspended
states.description: Warning badge "Suspended" and the name in the muted text colour.

states.name: self
states.description: "(You)" after the name; the role is text and Remove is hidden unless canChangeRole or canRemove say otherwise.

states.name: read-only role
states.description: Without onRoleChange the role title is muted text.

states.name: busy
states.description: A progress indicator beside the role picker while onRoleChange runs, a loading Resend button, and a progress indicator in place of Remove while onRemove runs.

states.name: error
states.description: The failure under the identity with an icon in the danger colour, announced.

states.name: done
states.description: "Invite sent again." under the identity with an icon in the success colour, announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Every control disabled with disabled(_:); swipe actions are hidden.

appearance: The name in the default text colour (muted when suspended), email and meta in the muted text colour, status badges in the info and warning tones, the remove icon in the muted text colour. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow it.
platformNotes: Matches the web's MemberRow. The web's role select is a native select; on iOS it is a menu Picker. The web keeps the remove dialog open while onRemove runs and shows its error there; the system confirmation dialog closes when a button is tapped, so on iOS the Remove button shows progress and the error appears in the row. Consequences are listed as lines of the dialog's message, not a styled list. Rows also offer Remove and Resend as trailing swipe actions inside a List. The role is a value plus onRoleChange: the row shows the new role while the change runs and until the app's role changes, and restores it on failure; there is no uncontrolled defaultMemberRole. MemberList is not needed: a List or a VStack of rows is the container. When the row is narrow, the controls move under the identity. Android uses the same name. Several closures are optional (onRoleChange, onResend, onRemove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRoleChange.
accessibility: The identity is one element: the name ("Priya Raman, You") as the label, then status, presence, badges, a read-only role, email, meta and any notice as the value.
The avatar is decorative next to the visible name; presence is read in words.
The role picker is named "Role for <name>", Resend "Resend invite, <name>", Remove "Remove <name>" or "Revoke invite for <name>".
Resend success and every failure are announced and shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
Swipe actions are also available from the VoiceOver actions rotor inside a List.
The remove and role controls keep a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: A role value that is not in roles is shown as its raw value.
With no role yet, the picker shows "Choose a role" until one is picked.
A second change while a role change runs is ignored; the picker is disabled until it finishes.
Errors thrown with a LocalizedError description are shown in its words; other errors show "That did not work. Try again.".
Long names truncate at the end and emails in the middle, so the controls stay on screen.

title: MentionPicker
wrapsNative: A full-width VStack of Buttons (MonarchAvatar and Text) in a ScrollView when long, placed with safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) above the composer and the keyboard; redacted(reason: .placeholder) while loading; MonarchInlineErrorRetry on failure; .task(id:) runs the product's search

whenToUse: In a message or comment composer where people mention others with @ or channels with #.
whenNotToUse: Not for general search suggestions; use searchable(text:) with searchSuggestions. Not for choosing people in a form; use a Picker or a List with a selection.

options.name: query
options.description: The mention being typed, from MonarchMentionQuery.find. Nothing is drawn while it is nil.

options.name: items
options.description: The suggestions from the product's search, people and channels.

options.name: status
options.description: loading shows placeholder rows, failed shows the error, ready shows the items or "No matches".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the list's name, the group headings, the state texts, the retry button and the count announcement.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Repeats a failed search; adds a retry button to the error.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Receives the chosen suggestion. Replace the query with query.replacing(in:with:) and close the query.

states.name: closed
states.description: No query: nothing is drawn.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three placeholder rows, redacted, read as "Searching…".

states.name: results
states.description: A row per suggestion; people and channels under headings when both are present; more than four scroll.

states.name: disabled suggestion
states.description: Text in the disabled colour; the row cannot be chosen.

states.name: no matches
states.description: "No matches". After a query with a space finds nothing, the picker closes.

states.name: failed
states.description: "Couldn’t load suggestions." with a retry button when onRetry is given.

appearance: A strip on the surface colour with a subtle top border; labels in the default text colour, details and headings in the muted text colour, disabled rows in the disabled text colour; avatars with their fallback colours and a square number-sign tile for channels. The same roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web anchors a listbox to the caret with aria-activedescendant and arrow keys, and ships hooks that debounce and abort the search. SwiftUI gives no caret rectangle, so iOS shows a full-width strip above the composer in the bottom safe-area inset, and suggestions are buttons. The product runs its search in .task(id: query), which cancels the previous one; Monarch adds no debounce timer. MonarchMentionQuery.find assumes the caret is at the end unless a caret index is passed, because TextField does not expose its selection on iOS 17. The token format of MonarchMentionItem.token matches the web's formatMentionToken; the web's parseMentionTokens has no iOS counterpart in this release.
accessibility: Each suggestion is a button whose label is its name and detail; a disabled suggestion is dimmed and not activatable.
The list is a container named "Suggestions"; group headings have the header trait.
The result count, "Searching…", "No matches" and the error are announced as the state changes, so focus can stay in the text field.
Avatars and the channel tile are hidden from VoiceOver.
Rows are at least 44 points high and grow with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A trigger inside a word, such as an email address, does not open the picker.
A query ends after two words, a line break or a word longer than 40 characters.
Replacing a query removes one space after it, so a mention typed mid-sentence does not leave two spaces.
A query's range belongs to the text it was found in; find it again after the text changes.

appearance: The trigger is a Monarch button: the accent fill for primary, the surface with the default border for secondary, no fill for ghost, the danger fill for danger; disabled uses the muted fill and disabled text roles. The menu itself is the system's, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web MenuButton is a Radix DropdownMenu trigger with an items shorthand, controlled open state, alignment, side and a chevron that turns while open. On iOS the system Menu places and animates the menu, takes Button, Toggle, Picker, Divider and nested Menu items, and has no open binding, alignment or side; the chevron does not turn. Links in the menu are Link items. Keyboard shortcut hints are keyboardShortcut(_:) on the items. Android composes the same with its own menu.
accessibility: VoiceOver reads the trigger as a button with the menu's title, and a hint that it opens a menu (system behaviour).
An icon-only trigger needs accessibilityLabel; the recipe and the catalogue give one.
The chevron is decorative (MonarchIcon(systemName:) hides it).
Destructive items use Button(role: .destructive), which the system reads and colours; pair them with a confirmation.
The trigger keeps a 44-point touch target at every size.
edgeCases: A long title wraps inside the trigger rather than widening it past the screen.
On macOS (host builds only) Menu draws a pull-down button and the button style may not apply; iOS is the supported platform.
The menu does not open while the trigger is disabled; there is no loading state, so disable it or show progress elsewhere.
Whether VoiceOver reads the menu hint on every iOS version was not checked on a device.

whenToUse: When duplicate records (contacts, companies, tickets) are combined and the person decides which record survives and which values it keeps.
whenNotToUse: To show possible duplicates before merging, use MonarchDuplicatePanel. To delete duplicates without keeping values, use a confirmationDialog. To edit one record, use a form.

options.description: What else happens, shown with MonarchConsequenceList under "What happens".

options.description: Problems that stop the merge, shown in a warning MonarchBanner; the merge button is disabled.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.description: Runs when Cancel is pressed; the dialog then dismisses itself.

options.name: onMerge
options.description: Performs the merge. While it runs the dialog is busy; returning dismisses it; throwing shows the error's description (or the built-in message) and keeps every choice.

states.name: choosing
states.description: The record choice with a Kept badge on the selected record, a choice per differing field (defaulting to the kept record's value, or the first other value when it is empty), and matching fields listed once.

states.name: blocked
states.description: With blockers, or fewer than two records, the merge button is disabled and the blockers are shown as a warning.

states.name: merging
states.description: The merge button becomes a progress indicator, the form and Cancel are disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger MonarchBanner with the message under the form; it is announced and the choices stay as they were.

appearance: A grouped form on the canvas background role with rows on the surface role. Titles use the default text role, descriptions, sources and matching values the muted role, empty values the subtle role. The Kept badge is a subtle success MonarchBadge. The toolbar buttons and the checkmarks of the pickers are drawn by the system with the app's tint.
platformNotes: The web MergeDialog is a modal dialog with radio groups and a full-screen layout on phones; on iOS it is sheet content with the standard Form, inline Pickers and toolbar placements, so the app presents it with sheet(isPresented:). The web values and consequences can be any node; on iOS values are strings and consequences are MonarchConsequence items. The web onMerge returns a promise; here it is an async throwing closure. The web size option has no meaning in a sheet; use presentationDetents. The web children slot (extra content) is not offered. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: Each choice is a standard inline Picker, so VoiceOver reads every option and its selected state.
A value option is one element that reads its value and its source, such as "hello@acme.com, from Acme Ltd"; an empty value reads "Empty".
Section headings have the header trait; the Kept badge is hidden because the selected state already says it.
A failure is announced. While merging the progress indicator is named with the merge button's title.
Cancel and Merge are toolbar buttons with the system's touch targets and keyboard shortcuts (Escape and Return).
edgeCases: A value that is blank after trimming counts as empty, and values equal after trimming count as matching.
Changing the kept record moves every field the person has not picked to the new record's value, or fills it from another record when it is empty.
With one record the dialog shows it and the merge button is disabled.
The count in the merge button uses the English plural form; pass labels.confirm for other languages.

states.name: empty
states.description: The placeholder in the subtle text colour; the send button is disabled.

states.name: ready
states.description: Text or attachments present: the send button is enabled.

states.name: sending
states.description: The send button shows a spinner and Sending…; another send is blocked.

states.name: replying
states.description: A context bar with a reply icon, Replying to the author, the excerpt and a dismiss button.

states.name: editing
states.description: A context bar with a pencil and Editing message, a Cancel button and Save instead of Send.

states.name: note mode
states.description: The box uses the warning subtle fill and warning border; the send title can change, such as Add note.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: The count turns the danger colour and the send button is disabled.

states.name: focused
states.description: The Monarch focus ring around the box.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle fill and border, disabled text colour, no emoji button, and the reason under the box.

states.name: draft status
states.description: Saving draft…, Draft saved or Draft not saved under the box.

appearance: The box uses the surface fill with the input border, the text in the default text colour and the placeholder in the subtle text colour; the send button is the primary button. A note uses the warning subtle fill and warning border; disabled uses the subtle fill and subtle border. The reply rule uses the strong border colour, the edit rule the accent border. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web composer is a rich text editor with a formatting toolbar; iOS has plain text until the rich text editor exists, so mentions are written as @Label and reported as items. On the web Enter sends; on iOS the on-screen keyboard's Return adds a line and the send button sends, while hardware Return (or Command-Return) sends through onKeyPress and keyboardShortcut. The web shows a send-key hint under the box; iOS does not, because most people type on the on-screen keyboard. Files arrive by paste, drop and picker on the web; on iOS onAttach lets the app present the system file importer or photo picker. The emoji picker is built in as a sheet instead of a product slot, and the emoji is added at the end of the text because iOS 17 gives no caret position. Draft debouncing is the app's: it owns the text binding.
accessibility: The text field is named by label; the placeholder is its prompt.
The reply or edit context is one element read as its title and excerpt; the dismiss button is separate and named Stop replying.
The emoji, attach and dismiss buttons are named icon buttons with 44-point touch targets.
The send button is a MonarchButton; while sending it reads Sending… and is busy.
The character count is read as characters left, or characters over the limit, not as a fraction.
The draft status uses MonarchSaveStatusIndicator, which announces saved and error.
Mention suggestions use MonarchMentionPicker, which announces the result count while focus stays in the text field.
The note mode is named by its segment as well as shown by the warning tint.
The text grows from one to eight lines with Dynamic Type and then scrolls.
edgeCases: Only white space cannot be sent; the sent text is trimmed.
If onSend throws, the text and picked mentions stay.
A mention whose @Label was edited out of the text is not reported.
The same person picked twice is reported once.
selectedMode with a value that is not a mode falls back to the first mode.
Over the limit, typing is not cut; sending is off until the text is shortened.

title: MessageRow

summary: One message in a conversation: avatar, author, time and body, with grouped, pending, failed, edited and deleted states, reactions, a thread reply count and per-message actions in a context menu.
whenToUse: Chat channels, direct messages, threads, ticket conversations with internal notes, and comment threads, as the rows of a List or a LazyVStack.
whenNotToUse: Not for a feed of system events with verbs and objects; use MonarchActivityTimeline. Not for a notification that leads elsewhere; use MonarchNotificationCenter. Not for a conversation in an inbox list; use MonarchInboxRow.

states.name: first of a group
states.description: Avatar, bold author, tags and the time above the body.

states.name: grouped
states.description: No avatar or header; the body lines up under the first message and the row is tighter.

states.name: pending
states.description: The body is muted and Sending… is shown under it. No context menu.

states.name: failed
states.description: A danger icon and the error under the body, with Retry and Discard when given. Announced by VoiceOver. No context menu.

states.name: edited
states.description: An (edited) marker after the body, a link when the edit history can be opened.

states.name: deleted
states.description: The body is replaced by This message was deleted. in muted italics; reactions, replies and actions are hidden.

states.name: internal
states.description: A warning subtle tint with a leading bar in the warning border colour.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: An accent subtle tint, animated in and out unless Reduce Motion is on.

states.name: system
states.description: A centred muted caption with the time, without avatar, author, reactions or actions.

appearance: Author in the default text colour, time in the muted text colour and the body in the default text colour (muted while pending or deleted). Internal notes use the warning subtle fill and warning border bar; a highlight uses the accent subtle fill; a failure uses the danger strong colour with an icon. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: On the web the per-message actions are a hover toolbar that also appears on focus; on iOS they are the row's context menu, which is how messages offer actions on touch. The web shows a grouped message's clock time in the gutter on hover; iOS has no hover on touch, so the gutter stays empty and the time is read by VoiceOver. The reaction bar's add button opens MonarchEmojiPicker in a sheet instead of a separate reactionAction slot. Tags are strings shown as neutral badges rather than arbitrary content, and a footer goes in the content builder. The body is a SwiftUI view, not HTML.
accessibility: The author, tags, full date and time, body, edited marker and Sending… are combined into one element.
A grouped message still begins with the author and the full date and time for VoiceOver, through an element that is not drawn.
The visible relative or clock time is replaced by the full date and time for VoiceOver.
An edited message with onShowEdits has a Show edit history VoiceOver action.
When the status becomes failed the error is announced; the error is an icon and text, and Retry and Discard are separate buttons.
Reactions use MonarchReactionBar: toggle buttons named by emoji name and count. The thread button is a separate button.
The avatar is decorative; the author is read from the header text.
Retry, Discard, the thread button and reaction chips have touch targets of at least 44 points; text wraps at every Dynamic Type size.
edgeCases: A time in the future reads as now.
Reactions whose counts are all zero hide the bar.
A failed or pending message has no context menu, so actions such as Edit cannot run on a message the server does not have.
Long author names wrap in the header with the tags and time; long bodies wrap without a line limit.
A system row ignores the author, tags, reactions, replies and actions.

summary: A recipe, not a component: a conversation's messages grouped by day, with a New messages divider, older history loaded at the top, who has seen the last message and who is typing under it.
whenToUse: For the message area of a chat, a channel or a support conversation: MonarchVirtualMessageList draws the day separators, the unread divider, grouping and Jump to latest; the rows are MonarchMessageRows.
whenNotToUse: For the replies to one message, use MonarchThreadPanel. For comments anchored to a document, use MonarchCommentThread. For a feed of events rather than messages, use MonarchActivityTimeline.

MonarchTypingIndicator.init(_ names: [String], text: String? = nil, reservesSpace: Bool = true, announcesChanges: Bool = true)

MonarchReadReceipt.init(_ readers: [MonarchReadReceiptReader], display: MonarchReadReceiptDisplay = .text, maxAvatars: Int = 3, labels: MonarchReadReceiptLabels = MonarchReadReceiptLabels(), onShowReaders: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

states.name: grouped by day
states.description: A Today, Yesterday or full date separator before the first message of each day, in the environment's locale and calendar.

states.name: unread
states.description: With firstUnreadID, a New messages divider above the first unread message, in the accent roles.

states.name: grouped
states.description: Consecutive messages by one author within groupWindow (five minutes) get context.isGrouped, drawn without a repeated name and avatar.

states.name: older history
states.description: With hasOlder and onLoadOlder, older messages load when the top comes into view; isLoadingOlder and isOlderFailed show progress or a retry.

states.name: seen and typing
states.description: MonarchReadReceipt after the last message and MonarchTypingIndicator under it, both in the list's footer.

appearance: The separators use the muted text role with subtle border lines, and the New messages divider the accent strong text and accent border roles. The rows, read receipt and typing indicator keep their own roles. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's MessageTimeline is one component with exported helpers (shouldGroupMessages, formatMessageDay, the separators) for products that virtualise rows themselves. On iOS, as on Android, MonarchVirtualMessageList already builds only the rows near the screen and draws the day separators, the unread divider, grouping and the jump button, so the timeline is this recipe and there is no separate type. The web's imperative handle (scrollToBottom, scrollToItem) is the list's scrollToID and its Jump to latest button. Android puts the typing indicator in a status slot; the iOS list has a footer, which holds both the receipt and the indicator. Day separators follow the environment's locale and calendar, including its time zone.
accessibility: MonarchVirtualMessageList is a container named Messages and announces messages that arrive; scrolling stays quiet.
Day separators and the New messages divider are headers, so the VoiceOver rotor moves between days.
Each MonarchMessageRow reads its author, full date and body as one element.
MonarchTypingIndicator announces who starts typing; MonarchReadReceipt reads who has seen the message.
edgeCases: Keep firstUnreadID fixed while the conversation is open, so the divider does not move as the reader catches up.
Pass now and set the locale and calendar in the environment for output that does not depend on the device, for example in screenshots.
The list scrolls itself: give it the full screen or a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.
The header shows only once all history is loaded (hasOlder is false).

name: MonarchMethodBadge
title: MethodBadge
wrapsNative: Text, RoundedRectangle
summary: An HTTP method label (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) in the code typeface, with a tone per method.
whenToUse: In endpoint lists, API references and request logs, before the path of a request.
whenNotToUse: Not for a status in words (use MonarchBadge) and not for an HTTP status code. It is not a button.
api: init(_ method: String, tone: MonarchTone? = nil)
nonisolated static func tone(for method: String) -> MonarchTone

options.name: method
options.description: The HTTP method in any case. It is trimmed and shown in upper case.

options.name: tone
options.description: Replaces the tone chosen from the method. nil keeps GET success, POST info, PUT and PATCH warning, DELETE danger and everything else neutral.

appearance: A rounded rectangle with the tone's subtle fill, strong text and border; the neutral tone is the muted background with muted text and no border. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The parity map named MonarchBadge as the base. MonarchBadge is a capsule in the caption role and cannot take the code typeface or a minimum width, so this component draws its own surface from the same tone palette. The web's sm and md sizes are not offered: the text is the code role (14 points) and follows Dynamic Type. Android uses the same name and tones.
accessibility: Read as the method name, which is always the visible text, so colour is never the only signal.
The text scales with Dynamic Type; the minimum width scales with it.
Not interactive: it has no button trait and no action.
edgeCases: A method outside GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE is neutral, including HEAD and OPTIONS.
An empty method draws an empty badge at the minimum width.
A long method wraps inside the badge and is centred; real methods are one word.
With a custom code font family in the theme typography, that family is used.

name: MonarchMetric
title: Metric
wrapsNative: VStack of Text (or MonarchFlowLayout when inline) with .monospacedDigit(), numbers written by FloatingPointFormatStyle (.number, .percent, .currency(code:), .notation(.compactName)); the change is a MonarchDeltaIndicator
summary: One number with its label, an optional unit and an optional change, formatted for the locale, with no surface around it.
whenToUse: When a figure sits inside another surface: a card or widget header, a panel, a table footer or a toolbar; or when several small figures sit in a row.
whenNotToUse: For a dashboard tile with its own surface, loading and error states, put the metric in a MonarchWidget. For an amount of money inside running text, format it with Text(value, format: .currency(code:)). For a change on its own, use MonarchDeltaIndicator.
api: init(_ label: String, value: Double?, unit: String? = nil, change: MonarchMetricChange? = nil, format: MonarchMetricFormat = .number, size: MonarchMetricSize = .md, isCompact: Bool = false, emptyLabel: String? = nil, layout: MonarchMetricLayout = .stacked, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .leading)

init(_ label: String, text: String?, spokenText: String? = nil, unit: String? = nil, change: MonarchMetricChange? = nil, size: MonarchMetricSize = .md, emptyLabel: String? = nil, layout: MonarchMetricLayout = .stacked, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .leading)
static func formatted(_ value: Double, format: MonarchMetricFormat = .number, isCompact: Bool = false, locale: Locale = .current) -> String

struct MonarchMetricChange { init(_ value: Double?, comparison: String? = nil, goodDirection: MonarchDeltaIndicatorGoodDirection = .up, variant: MonarchDeltaIndicatorVariant = .plain, flatThreshold: Double = 0, formatValue: (@Sendable (Double) -> String)? = nil); init(current: Double?, previous: Double?, …) }
enum MonarchMetricFormat { case number, percent, currency(code: String) }
enum MonarchMetricSize { case sm, md, lg }
enum MonarchMetricLayout { case stacked, inline }

options.name: label
options.description: What the number measures, such as "Open tickets". Always visible.

options.name: value
options.description: The number. nil shows a muted dash that VoiceOver reads as "No data".

options.name: text
options.description: In the second initialiser: the value already written by the app. nil or empty shows the dash.

options.name: spokenText
options.description: In the second initialiser: what VoiceOver reads instead of text.

options.name: unit
options.description: Written smaller and muted after the value, never split from itself. Hidden for an empty value.

options.name: change
options.description: The change versus an earlier period, drawn by MonarchDeltaIndicator under the value (or after it when inline).

options.name: format
options.description: number, percent (a ratio: 0.12 is 12%) or currency(code:).

options.name: size
options.description: sm for dense rows, md, lg for a headline figure. lg also makes the change one size larger.

options.name: isCompact
options.description: Writes 12K or €3.4M with the compact notation; VoiceOver reads the full value.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "No data" read for a missing value.

options.name: layout
options.description: stacked puts the label above the value; inline puts label, value and change on one line that wraps.

options.name: alignment
options.description: The alignment of the stacked layout; .trailing for numeric columns.

states.name: default
states.description: The label in muted text, the value in the default text colour with tabular figures, the unit muted, the change under it.

states.name: empty
states.description: A dash in the subtle text colour instead of the value, read as "No data"; the unit is hidden.

states.name: compact
states.description: The value is written short (12K); the spoken value is the full number.

appearance: No surface. The label and unit use the muted text role, the value the default text role (the subtle role for the empty dash), in every theme including high contrast. The change takes MonarchDeltaIndicator's success and danger roles together with its arrow and sign.
platformNotes: The web value accepts any React node and Intl.NumberFormat options; on iOS a number is written with Foundation format styles (number, percent, currency) in the environment's locale, and any other value is passed as text with an optional spoken form. The web `align` start/end is a SwiftUI HorizontalAlignment. The web shows the full compact value as a hover title; iOS has no hover, so only VoiceOver gets it. The change takes the main DeltaIndicator options; its flat and no-data labels keep their built-in text. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The metric is one element: the label is its label, and the value is the full number with its unit and the change as a sentence, such as "840 ms, down 8% vs last week, better".
A compact figure is read in full ("12,345"), and the dash for a missing value is read as "No data" or emptyLabel.
The change's meaning is carried by its arrow, its sign and the spoken sentence, not by colour.
Text uses Monarch type roles, so it scales with Dynamic Type and wraps instead of truncating.
edgeCases: A value that is not finite (infinity, NaN) is shown as empty.
Very long values wrap; the unit stays on one line beside or under the value.
Percent takes a ratio: pass 0.12 for 12%.
Currency digits follow the currency: JPY has none.

examples.title: Number, unit and change
examples.template:
MonarchMetric(
    {{label}},
    value: {{value|double}},
    unit: {{unit}},
    change: MonarchMetricChange({{change.value}}, comparison: {{change.comparison}}, goodDirection: {{change.goodDirection|case}})
)
examples.code:
MonarchMetric(
    "Median response",
    value: 182.0,
    unit: "ms",
    change: MonarchMetricChange(-0.08, comparison: "vs last week", goodDirection: .down)
)

examples.title: A compact headline figure
examples.code:
MonarchMetric(
    "Revenue",
    value: 1_284_000,
    change: MonarchMetricChange(current: 1_284_000, previous: 1_190_000, comparison: "vs last month"),
    format: .currency(code: "EUR"),
    size: .lg,
    isCompact: true
)

title: MiniCall
wrapsNative: AVKit: AVPictureInPictureController (startPictureInPicture(), isPictureInPictureSupported())
summary: A call that continues while people do something else is shown in the system's picture-in-picture window. Monarch ships no floating call window.
whenToUse: To keep a call visible when the person leaves the call screen or the app. For a video call, create the controller with AVPictureInPictureController.ContentSource(activeVideoCallSourceView:contentViewController:).
whenNotToUse: Do not build a draggable in-app window; it cannot leave the app and duplicates the system one. For an audio-only call the system's call indicator in the status bar or Dynamic Island is enough.
api: AVPictureInPictureController(playerLayer: AVPlayerLayer)
AVPictureInPictureController(contentSource: AVPictureInPictureController.ContentSource)
func startPictureInPicture()
class func isPictureInPictureSupported() -> Bool

states.name: not supported
states.description: isPictureInPictureSupported() is false; offer no button.

states.name: possible
states.description: isPictureInPicturePossible is true while there is video to show.

states.name: active
states.description: The system window floats above the app and other apps, with its own controls, and can be dragged to a corner or hidden at the edge.

appearance: System appearance in every theme. The button that starts it is an ordinary Monarch button.
platformNotes: The web MiniCall is a draggable in-page window with a timer, mute, expand and leave. Android uses its own picture-in-picture mode. On iOS the system draws the window and its controls; mute and leave stay in the app's call screen and in the system call controls. The app needs the Audio, AirPlay, and Picture in Picture background mode.
accessibility: System behaviour: the picture-in-picture window is accessible and can be moved and closed with VoiceOver.
Give the button that starts it a title or an accessibility label.
edgeCases: Picture in picture starts only while isPictureInPicturePossible is true, which needs a layer that is showing video.
The video-call content source (iOS 15) needs UIKit: a source UIView and an AVPictureInPictureVideoCallViewController.
Keep a strong reference to the controller while the window is open.
The example and the catalogue page were compiled but the window was not run.

examples.title: Inline
examples.setup: @Environment(\.monarchTheme) private var theme

parityExceptions.reason: The web mini call is a floating tile; native floats a call as system picture-in-picture (AVPictureInPictureController, started by the app with its own call layer), so no Monarch view is the floating window. The example draws the same tile, with the same speaker, timer, count and mute, expand and leave controls, from Monarch parts.

name: MonarchMiniMonth
title: MiniMonth
wrapsNative: A month grid drawn by Monarch (LazyVGrid with the system calendar and locale), with an earliest and latest day, unavailable days and up to three dots under days with events
summary: A month calendar for choosing a day: the system calendar view with an earliest and latest day, days the app marks unavailable, and up to three dots under days that have events.
whenToUse: For a calendar that shows which days have events or are available: a sidebar calendar beside an agenda, a booking day picker with unavailable days.
whenNotToUse: Not for a plain date field in a form: use DatePicker, which is compact and needs no Monarch code. Not for choosing a range of days or several days; this component selects one day.
api: init(selection: Binding<Date?>, visibleMonth: Binding<Date>? = nil, minimumDate: Date? = nil, maximumDate: Date? = nil, today: Date? = nil, isDateDisabled: (@MainActor (Date) -> Bool)? = nil, dayInfo: (@MainActor (Date) -> MonarchMiniMonthDayInfo?)? = nil)
MonarchMiniMonthDayInfo.init(dotCount: Int, description: String? = nil)
MonarchMiniMonthDayInfo.init(dots: [MonarchTone], description: String? = nil)

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected day: the first moment of that day in the environment's calendar, or nil for none.

options.name: visibleMonth
options.description: Any date in the month on screen. The calendar writes the first day of the month the person moves to. Without it the calendar starts on the month of the selection, or today.

options.name: minimumDate
options.description: The earliest day that can be chosen. Earlier months cannot be reached.

options.name: maximumDate
options.description: The latest day that can be chosen. Later months cannot be reached.

options.name: today
options.description: The day drawn as today. The clock by default; fixes it for tests and previews.

options.name: isDateDisabled
options.description: Returns true for a day that cannot be chosen. Called for every visible day.

options.name: dayInfo
options.description: The dots and their description for a day. Dots are accent-coloured (dotCount) or toned (dots); at most three are drawn.

states.name: selected
states.description: The system draws the day in a filled circle in the theme's accent.

states.name: today
states.description: Today's number is outlined, as on the web; `today` fixes which day it is.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: Days outside the bounds and days the app disables are dimmed by the system and cannot be chosen.

states.name: with dots
states.description: Up to three 6-point dots under the day number: the accent, or the solid colour of a tone; the neutral tone is the subtle text colour.

states.name: month and year picker
states.description: Tapping the month title opens the system's wheel picker for month and year.

appearance: The grid, the weekday names, the month title and its arrows are drawn by the system and follow light, dark and Increase Contrast. Monarch sets the tint to the accent role and draws the dots from the accent and tone roles of the theme. Day numbers use system label colours, not Monarch text roles.
platformNotes: The grid is drawn by Monarch, as the web draws it. Week numbers are not offered. Also not offered: a highlighted range and range preview (it selects single or several separate days), several months side by side, hiding the days of neighbouring months, a fixed number of week rows, and a footer (put a button under the calendar). The month title opens a month list, as the web's month and year pickers do. The locale and first weekday come from the environment's calendar and locale rather than props. Tapping the selected day clears the selection, which the web does not do. The web's accent dot tone is the dotCount initialiser, because MonarchTone has no accent case. On macOS, which is only a build convenience and has no UICalendarView, the host build shows the graphical DatePicker with the bounds and without disabled days and dots. Android builds its own grid under the same name. Several closures are optional (isDateDisabled, dayInfo). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is isDateDisabled.
accessibility: VoiceOver labels, traits and gestures of the days, the month title and the arrows are the system calendar view's.

The dots view of a day carries the app's description as its accessibility label. Whether VoiceOver reads it with the day was not verified on a device, so also show the selected day's events as text under the calendar.
The meaning of a dot is never colour alone only if the app gives a description.
Dynamic Type and right-to-left layout are handled by the system view. Changing the visible month from the binding animates unless Reduce Motion is on.
Each day is a system cell; the grid takes the full width it is offered.
edgeCases: A selection outside the bounds is not shown as selected; the binding is left as it is.
A latest day before the earliest day leaves only the earliest day available.
A visibleMonth outside the bounds shows the nearest month inside them.
isDateDisabled and dayInfo are asked again for the visible month on every SwiftUI update, so they must be cheap and must not change state.
The time zone is the environment calendar's: pass a calendar with the workspace's time zone to show workspace days.

Experimental: the UICalendarView wrapper has been compiled and laid out but not yet seen drawn on a simulator or device; dot placement, tint, dark appearance, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver reading of the dots are unverified. It becomes available after the simulator run and a VoiceOver check.

examples.title: Sidebar calendar with events
A booking day in the next 30 days, weekends unavailable
examples.setup:
@Environment(\.calendar) private var calendar
@State private var day: Date?
examples.code:
MonarchMiniMonth(
    selection: $day,
    minimumDate: .now,
    maximumDate: calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: 30, to: .now),
    isDateDisabled: { date in calendar.isDateInWeekend(date) },
    dayInfo: { date in
        calendar.isDateInWeekend(date)
            ? nil
            : MonarchMiniMonthDayInfo(dots: [.success], description: "Available")
    }
)

name: MonarchMoney
title: Money
wrapsNative: Text with Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency (presentation, sign(strategy:), notation(.compactName), precision) and .monospacedDigit()
summary: An amount of money in one currency, written by the system's currency format in fixed-width digits, with an empty state and a spoken full value for compact amounts.
whenToUse: Prices, invoice lines, balances, payroll figures and renewal costs, including amounts stored as integer minor units next to an ISO 4217 code.
whenNotToUse: For entering an amount, use a TextField with a currency format. Do not add amounts in different currencies; list them per currency. For a number that is not money, use Text(monarchTabular:format:).
api: init(_ amount: Decimal?, currencyCode: String, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = .standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = .automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = .symbol, usesAccountingSign: Bool = false, fractionDigits: ClosedRange<Int>? = nil, locale: Locale? = nil, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body, tonesNegative: Bool = false, emptyText: String? = nil, emptyLabel: String? = nil)

init(minorUnits: Int?, currencyCode: String, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = .standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = .automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = .symbol, usesAccountingSign: Bool = false, fractionDigits: ClosedRange<Int>? = nil, locale: Locale? = nil, textStyle: MonarchTextStyle = .body, tonesNegative: Bool = false, emptyText: String? = nil, emptyLabel: String? = nil)

static func formatted(_ amount: Decimal, currencyCode: String, notation: MonarchMoneyNotation = .standard, signDisplay: MonarchMoneySignDisplay = .automatic, currencyDisplay: MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay = .symbol, usesAccountingSign: Bool = false, fractionDigits: ClosedRange<Int>? = nil, locale: Locale = .autoupdatingCurrent) -> String
enum MonarchMoneyNotation { case standard, compact }
enum MonarchMoneySignDisplay { case automatic, always, exceptZero, never }
enum MonarchMoneyCurrencyDisplay { case symbol, narrowSymbol, code, name }

options.name: amount
options.description: The amount in major units (19.99 for $19.99), or nil when there is none.

options.name: minorUnits
options.description: With the second initialiser: the amount in minor units (cents, paise). 1999 with USD is $19.99; the conversion is exact.

options.name: currencyCode
options.description: The ISO 4217 code, such as USD, EUR or INR.

options.name: notation
options.description: standard writes every digit; compact writes $1.3M and VoiceOver reads the full amount.

options.name: signDisplay
options.description: automatic, always (also +$0.00), exceptZero (+$42.00 for gains) or never.

options.name: currencyDisplay
options.description: symbol, narrowSymbol ($), code (USD) or name (US dollars).

options.name: usesAccountingSign
options.description: Writes negatives in parentheses where the locale does: ($42.00).

options.name: fractionDigits
options.description: The least and most digits after the decimal separator. Default: the currency's own (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3).

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale to write in. Default: the environment's locale.

options.name: textStyle
options.description: The type role.

options.name: tonesNegative
options.description: Colours a negative amount with the danger text colour. The sign or parentheses always carry the meaning.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Replaces the built-in "—" shown for a missing amount.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "No amount" that VoiceOver reads for a missing amount.

states.name: standard
states.description: The amount in the inherited text colour with tabular digits.

states.name: negative
states.description: A minus sign, or parentheses with usesAccountingSign; with tonesNegative the text uses the danger text colour.

states.name: compact
states.description: The short form is shown; VoiceOver reads the full amount.

states.name: empty
states.description: A nil amount shows an em dash in the muted text colour, read as "No amount".

appearance: Text in the chosen type role with fixed-width digits, in the inherited foreground. Toned negatives use the danger strong text colour and missing amounts the muted text colour, in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Formatting is Foundation's Decimal.FormatStyle.Currency, so the output can differ in small ways from the web's Intl.NumberFormat (for example the compact form in some locales). The web takes numbers, bigints or decimal strings; iOS takes Decimal or Int minor units. The web hover title for compact amounts has no touch equivalent; VoiceOver reads the full amount. Android ships MonarchMoney with the same options.
accessibility: A compact amount is read as the full amount through accessibilityLabel.
A missing amount shows "—" and is read as "No amount" (both replaceable).
Negative amounts keep their sign or parentheses, so colour is never the only cue.
The text scales with Dynamic Type through its type role.
edgeCases: Minor units are converted with the currency's own digits from the system (USD 2, JPY 0, KWD 3); unknown codes use 2.
Large minor-unit amounts up to Int.max convert exactly through Decimal.
fractionDigits 0...0 rounds the amount for display only.
A long amount in a large type role at the largest text size can wrap at a space in the currency name; it is not truncated.
The currency is never converted; the code only selects the symbol and the digits.

name: MonarchMultiSelect
title: MultiSelect
wrapsNative: Button field that presents a .sheet with a NavigationStack, a List of toggling Buttons and .searchable(text:placement:prompt:); the picks are MonarchTag views in a MonarchFlowLayout
summary: A field for choosing several values from a long list, searched in a sheet, with the chosen values shown as removable tags.
whenToUse: For several choices out of more options than fit as checkboxes, such as labels, people or apps, especially options loaded from a server.
whenNotToUse: Not for a short list where every option should be visible (use MonarchCheckboxGroup), not for free-form values (use MonarchTagInput), and not for one value (use MonarchCombobox or Picker).
api: init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<[String]>, options: [MonarchComboboxOption], prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, maxSelections: Int? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, isLoading: Bool = false, sortsByMatch: Bool = false, limit: Int? = nil, searchText: Binding<String>? = nil, labels: MonarchMultiSelectLabels = MonarchMultiSelectLabels(), filter: (@Sendable (MonarchComboboxOption, String) -> Bool)? = nil, onCreate: (@MainActor (String) -> MonarchComboboxOption?)? = nil)

struct MonarchMultiSelectLabels: Sendable { init(select: String? = nil, change: String? = nil, done: String? = nil, count: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, list: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the field and is the title of the sheet.

options.name: selection
options.description: The ids of the chosen options, in the order they were picked.

options.name: options
options.description: The options in order, with the same fields as a combobox option: label, description, hint, group, keywords, systemImage and isDisabled.

options.name: prompt
options.description: The button's text while nothing is chosen. "Select…" when nil.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the field, also read as the hint.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown with an icon and announced.

options.name: maxSelections
options.description: The most values that can be chosen. Other rows are disabled at the limit and "2 of 3 selected" shows under the field and in the list.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows a progress row with "Loading…" in the list.

options.name: sortsByMatch

options.name: limit

Long labels wrap inside the tags and the rows; the tags wrap onto more lines.
With maxSelections of 0 nothing can be chosen.
The search text is cleared when the sheet closes.

whenToUse: When someone opens an app, or a deep link into one, that their workspace has not given them access to.
whenNotToUse: For a screen that is empty because there is no content yet, use MonarchEmptyState alone. For a missing permission on one action inside an app, disable the action and explain it in place.

@Environment(\.openURL) to open the admins' contact link

states.name: switching

On iOS it is a recipe: the app's navigation shows this view in place of the app's root, the request is the app's own call, links open with openURL, and VoiceOver focus moves to a new screen by itself. Back to workspace is the system back button or the app's tab bar rather than a link. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: MonarchEmptyState's title has the header trait and the lock symbol is decorative.
Request access and Contact an admin are separate buttons of at least 44 points.

The workspace switcher is a button labelled with the current workspace.
edgeCases: If the request fails, keep Request access and show the failure with MonarchInlineErrorRetry under the empty state.
Without a workspace name, say "Ask a workspace admin" instead of naming the workspace.
Long app and workspace names wrap; the empty state is centred and scrolls inside the app's ScrollView.

states.name: unread item
states.description: An accent dot before a bold title, and a semibold age, from MonarchInboxRow.

states.name: read item
states.description: Regular title and muted age.

states.name: unread tab
states.description: Only unread items; the tab shows the unread count, 99+ above 99.

states.description: Three redacted placeholder rows, read as Loading notifications.

appearance: The surface background with plain list rows; day headings in the muted text colour; the unread dot from the accent's solid colour; the Unread tab's count uses the info tone. The mark-read swipe action is tinted with the info solid colour. The same roles in every theme, including both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component is a bell that opens a popover. On iOS the bell is MonarchNotificationsBell and the list is this view, presented in a .sheet with its own navigation bar, because popovers become sheets on iPhone anyway. Marking one item read is a leading swipe action, also a VoiceOver action, instead of a per-row button. Rows reuse MonarchInboxRow, so titles and messages are cut to one line each, and times are compact (5m, 3h) rather than 18 minutes ago. Items have no href: onSelect navigates. A custom empty state and a custom trigger are not offered. The Unread count uses the info tone because MonarchTone has no accent tone yet. Without now, day headings are computed when the view renders and do not change at midnight while it stays open.
accessibility: The tabs are MonarchTabs: a tab bar named Show, with the unread count in the Unread tab's name.
Each item is one button read as the title, Unread when unread, the full date and time, and the message, from MonarchInboxRow.
The unread dot is hidden; the state is spoken and shown by a bold title, not colour alone.
The mark-read swipe action is also a VoiceOver action named Mark as read.
Day headings have the header trait.
The loading placeholder is one element named Loading notifications; its redacted rows are not read.
Rows are at least 44 points high and grow with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: unreadCount larger than the loaded items keeps the tab count and enables Mark all as read.
Loading wins over an error; an error wins over the empty state; load more is hidden in all three.
An empty errorMessage is treated as no error.
Counts above 99 show 99+.
Items keep the order given inside each day; days appear in the order of their first item.

name: MonarchNotificationsBell
title: NotificationsBell
wrapsNative: Button with a private ButtonStyle, overlay(alignment:) with alignment guides for the count
summary: The button that opens an app's notifications: a bell with the unread count on it, or a full-width row with the title and the count.
whenToUse: In a toolbar, a header, a menu or a sidebar, as the one entry to the app's in-app notifications. The app presents the notifications in the action.
whenNotToUse: For the count on a tab of a TabView use the system badge(_:) modifier. For a status that is not a count of notifications use MonarchBadge.
api: MonarchNotificationsBell.init(unreadCount: Int = 0, variant: MonarchNotificationsBellVariant = .icon, title: String? = nil, unreadLabel: String? = nil, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)
enum MonarchNotificationsBellVariant { case icon, row }

options.name: unreadCount
options.description: The number of unread notifications. Zero or less shows no badge. Above 99 the badge reads "99+".

options.name: variant
options.description: icon: a square icon button with the count on the bell. row: a full-width row with the title and the count at the trailing edge.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in name "Notifications", which is also the visible title of a row.

options.name: unreadLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken value "3 unread". Pass the whole phrase for the current count.

options.name: action
options.description: Opens the notifications: present a sheet or a popover, or push a screen.

states.name: no unread
states.description: The bell alone, in the muted text colour. No badge and no spoken value.

states.name: unread
states.description: A solid danger badge with the count: on the bell's top trailing corner for icon, at the trailing edge for row.

states.name: more than 99 unread
states.description: The badge reads "99+". VoiceOver still reads the exact count.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A muted fill appears and the bell and title take the default text colour.

states.name: disabled
states.description: The bell and title use the disabled text colour, set with the standard disabled(_:) modifier. The badge keeps its colours.

appearance: No fill at rest; the bell and title use the muted text role and, while pressed, the default text role on a muted background with the control corner radius. The count is a solid MonarchBadge in the danger roles with a ring in the surface colour where it overlaps the bell. The same roles resolve to stronger colours in the high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: On the web the bell owns the NotificationCenter panel and passes its props through (items, filters, mark as read, load more, a See all link). On iOS the button and the presentation are separate: this component is the trigger with the count, and the app presents its notifications from the action, so there is no open state, panel side, closeOnSelect or seeAllHref. The web derives the count from unread items when unreadCount is missing; here the app always passes it. The web's collapsed row (icon only, with a tooltip, for a collapsed rail) is the icon variant; iOS has no tooltips. Android ships the same two variants.
accessibility: A standard Button named "Notifications", or by title.
The unread count is the accessibility value ("3 unread"), not part of the name. It is the exact count even when the badge shows "99+", and it is empty when nothing is unread.
The bell and the badge are hidden from VoiceOver, so the count is read once.
The touch target is at least 44 by 44 points in both variants.
The bell, the title and the count scale with Dynamic Type; a long title wraps.
The unread state is a badge with a number, not a colour change.
edgeCases: A negative count is treated as zero.
The badge on the icon variant extends past the trailing and top edges of the button's 36-point box; leave space2 around it.
The built-in "%@ unread" is one string for every count. Languages with plural forms pass unreadLabel.
The ring around the badge is the surface colour. On another background it shows as a thin ring of that colour.
The numbers are formatted for the current locale.

name: MonarchNumberInput
title: NumberInput
wrapsNative: TextField(_:value:format:prompt:) and Stepper(_:onIncrement:onDecrement:)
summary: A labelled number field that reads and writes numbers in the person's locale, with a stepper that never drifts, helper text and an error state.
whenToUse: For a number that is typed or nudged: a quantity, a price, a percentage, a weight.
whenNotToUse: For a value picked from a small range by feel, use Slider. For a number that is only stepped and never typed, a plain Stepper in a Form is enough. For digits that are not a quantity (a phone number, a code), use MonarchTextField with a number keyboard.

init(_ label: String, value: Binding<Double?>, minimum: Double? = nil, maximum: Double? = nil, step: Double = 1, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, showsStepper: Bool = true, rangeMessage: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels()) where Format == FloatingPointFormatStyle<Double>

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or nil while the field is empty. Every edit that reads as a number is written at once, so an action tapped straight after typing reads what is shown.

options.name: format
options.default: the locale's number format, up to three fraction digits or as many as step has
options.description: How the number is shown and read, for example .percent or .currency(code:). It is given the locale of the environment.

options.name: minimum
options.description: The smallest allowed value. Typed values below it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: maximum
options.description: The largest allowed value. Typed values above it are flagged; steps stop at it.

options.name: step
options.description: The amount one press of the stepper adds or removes.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

options.name: helper
options.description: Supporting text under the field.

options.name: error
options.description: Error message; replaces the helper and the range message while present.

options.name: showsStepper
options.description: Whether the − and + buttons are shown beside the field. Each is a 44-point target named "Increase <label>" and "Decrease <label>".

options.name: rangeMessage
options.description: Replaces the built-in message for a value outside the bounds.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken "Required" and the form of an error.

states.name: empty
states.description: The value is nil and the prompt shows in the subtle text colour. The first step starts from the minimum, or from 0.

states.name: focused
states.description: Draws the theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: out of range
states.description: Danger border, and an icon and "Enter a number from 0 to 99." under the field. The value is kept.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's message in place of the range message, drawn the same way.

states.name: at a bound
states.description: The half of the stepper that would pass the bound is disabled.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: The field has the measures and colours of MonarchTextField: a surface fill, an input border and 8-point corners, with the focus ring of the theme. Digits are monospaced so the number does not shift while it is stepped. The stepper is the system control.
platformNotes: The web parses the text itself and keeps text it cannot read on screen with "Enter a number.". On iOS the field is the standard TextField(value:format:): text the format cannot parse is put back to the last value when editing ends, which is the platform behaviour, so there is no not-a-number message. The web never stores an out-of-range value; here the binding holds what was typed and the field flags it, so the app must not treat a flagged value as valid. Arrow keys, Page Up and Page Down, and the largeStep option have no touch equivalent and are not offered. The − and + buttons are the system Stepper, which repeats while held; its halves are about 47 by 32 points, below the 44-point target, because the system control's size is fixed. There is no size option: the field is always at least 44 points high. The value is a Double; steps are calculated in decimal arithmetic so they do not drift.
accessibility: The field is one element: label, the formatted number as the value, then the error (spoken as "Error: …") or else the helper as the hint.
A new error or range message is announced when it appears, and is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
The stepper is the system control with the same label, the formatted number as its value, and the increment and decrement actions.
The keyboard is the decimal pad, or one with a minus sign unless the minimum rules out negative numbers.
The field is at least 44 points high and text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A value between grid points steps to the next grid point in that direction: 5 with a step of 10 goes to 10 or to 0. The grid starts at the minimum, or at 0.
A step that is not positive disables the stepper.
The decimal pad has no Return key: the number is committed when focus leaves the field.
With the .percent format the value is a fraction: 0.15 shows as 15%, and a step of 0.05 moves it by five points.
Very large or very small numbers follow the format; the default shows at most three fraction digits unless the step has more.

title: OAuthConsentScreen
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchAvatar (square, for the app), MonarchBadge, MonarchInlineNotice, MonarchCard with the account, MonarchConsequenceList for the permissions, two full-width MonarchButtons, and Link with the Monarch link style in a MonarchFlowLayout
summary: A recipe, not a component: the screen where a person allows or cancels a third-party app's access to their account, showing which app asks, which account would grant access, and what the app could do.
whenToUse: In an identity provider's app, when another app asks for access to the signed-in account (an OAuth or OpenID Connect authorization request).
whenNotToUse: Not for the system permission prompts (camera, location), which iOS shows itself. To list apps that already have access, use MonarchConnectedAppsList; to remove access, use the revoke access recipe.
api: MonarchAvatar(image: nil, name: app.name, systemImage: "app", shape: .square, size: .lg, isDecorative: true)
MonarchBadge("Verified", tone: .success, systemImage: "checkmark.seal")
MonarchInlineNotice("Only continue if you know and trust Notes.", title: "This app hasn’t been verified", tone: .warning)
MonarchConsequenceList(scopes, heading: "Notes will be able to:", kindLabel: { $0 == .warning ? "Sensitive" : "Allowed" })
MonarchButton("Cancel", variant: .secondary, isLoading: isDenying, fullWidth: true) { … }
MonarchButton("Allow", variant: .primary, isLoading: isAllowing, fullWidth: true) { … }
Link("privacy policy", destination: url).buttonStyle(.monarchLink(.inline, isExternal: true))

states.name: verified
states.description: The app's logo or initial, its name and domain, a success Verified badge, the account card, the permissions, then Cancel and Allow of equal width.

states.name: unverified
states.description: No badge, and a warning MonarchInlineNotice "This app hasn’t been verified" above the account.

states.name: sensitive permission
states.description: A warning row in the permission list, read as "Sensitive", with a detail line.

states.name: pending
states.description: The pressed button shows its spinner and both are disabled until the request returns.

states.name: failed
states.description: Put a danger MonarchInlineNotice with the message above the buttons.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: the square avatar on its fallback colour, the success badge, the warning notice, the raised card, the consequence list with success and warning icons, secondary and primary buttons, and inline links.
platformNotes: The web's OAuthConsentScreen is one component with its own pending and error state. On iOS it is a recipe, because the authorization request, the redirect and the account picker belong to the identity provider's app. The permission list is MonarchConsequenceList with kept rows for ordinary permissions and warning rows for sensitive ones, renamed "Allowed" and "Sensitive" through kindLabel. Permissions held back until the app is verified go in a second MonarchConsequenceList under their own heading. An app that only signs in to another provider uses ASWebAuthenticationSession, which shows that provider's own page, not this screen. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
The app's name and domain, and the signed-in account, are each read as one element; the avatars are decorative.
Each permission is one element read as its kind and its text, such as "Sensitive: Read and change your notes"; the kind also has its own icon.
Cancel and Allow are buttons of equal width and weight, with 44-point touch targets; while pending the spinner's button is named "Loading".
The policy links use the Monarch link style, which says they open outside the app.
edgeCases: Show only http and https policy links; drop any other scheme from the app's data.
A long app name wraps; keep the domain visible so people can spot an imitation.
When the person cannot grant access (a policy blocks it), show only Cancel with the reason in a MonarchInlineNotice.

name: MonarchOnboardingChecklist
title: OnboardingChecklist
wrapsNative: MonarchCard containing a DisclosureGroup (.disclosureGroupStyle(MonarchDisclosureGroupStyle)) whose label is a ProgressView (.monarchLinear)
summary: A first-run checklist: steps with a done state and an optional call to action, a progress summary, and collapse and dismiss controls.
whenToUse: To guide people through setting up a product with a short list of steps (three to seven) that the app can mark done from its own data.
whenNotToUse: For a linear form split into pages use MonarchStepper. For a to-do list people tick themselves use Toggle with .monarchCheckbox.
api: init(_ title: String, steps: [MonarchOnboardingStep], description: String? = nil, completeMessage: String? = nil, isCollapsible: Bool = true, isExpanded: Binding<Bool>? = nil, labels: MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels = MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels(), onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder action: @escaping (MonarchOnboardingStep) -> Action)

init(_ title: String, steps: [MonarchOnboardingStep], description: String? = nil, completeMessage: String? = nil, isCollapsible: Bool = true, isExpanded: Binding<Bool>? = nil, labels: MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels = MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels(), onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) where Action == EmptyView
struct MonarchOnboardingStep: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable { init(id: String, title: String, description: String? = nil, isDone: Bool = false) }

struct MonarchOnboardingChecklistLabels { init(progress: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, progressLabel: String? = nil, dismiss: String? = nil, done: String? = nil, notDone: String? = nil, current: String? = nil, complete: String? = nil, expanded: String? = nil, collapsed: String? = nil) }

options.name: title
options.description: The heading, such as "Get started". Read as a header.

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps in order: id, title, optional description and isDone. The app decides when each is done.

options.name: description
options.description: Text under the heading.

options.name: completeMessage
options.description: Replaces "All done. You are set up.", shown when every step is done.

options.name: isCollapsible
options.description: Makes the progress row a disclosure that shows and hides the steps.

options.name: isExpanded
options.description: Whether the steps are shown. Without it the component keeps the state itself, starting expanded. Bind it to keep the state across launches.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: progress, progressLabel, dismiss, done, notDone, current, complete, expanded and collapsed.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Shows a dismiss button that runs this. The app hides the checklist and remembers it.

options.name: action
options.description: The call to action of a step, such as a small MonarchButtonStyle button. Shown only while the step is not done.

states.name: in progress
states.description: The bar and "n of m done" show progress; the first open step has a subtle fill and an accent ring with its number.

states.name: step done
states.description: The marker is a filled success circle with a check; the title is muted; the description and action are hidden.

states.name: complete
states.description: Every step is done: a success message with a check appears above the steps.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: Only the heading and the progress row are shown; the chevron turns.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no steps the progress reads "0 of 0 done" and the checklist is not complete.

appearance: A MonarchCard (surface fill, subtle border, small shadow). The progress uses MonarchProgressViewStyle (accent fill on a muted track). Open steps have a number in a strong-border ring, the current step an accent-strong ring on the subtle fill, done steps a success-solid circle with a check in the on-solid colour. The complete message uses the success subtle fill and success strong text. All are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the theme.
platformNotes: The web turns the progress bar to the success tone when complete; MonarchProgressViewStyle has no tone, so the bar stays accent and the success message shows completion. The web sets a heading level; iOS marks the title as a header without a level. The web places the action beside the step on wide screens; iOS places it under the step text. Collapse uses isExpanded, the SwiftUI convention, where the web uses collapsed. Android has the same parameters.
accessibility: The title is a header.
With collapsing, the progress row is the disclosure button, read as "Setup progress, n of m done" with the value "Expanded" or "Collapsed"; hidden steps are removed from VoiceOver.
Without collapsing, the progress row is one element named "Setup progress" with "n of m done" as its value.

Each step is one element read as its title, with the value "Done" or "Not done" ("Not done, Current step" for the first open step) and its description as the hint; the step number and marker are not read.
Each step's action is a separate element after the step.
Done is shown by a check in the marker and by the spoken value, not by colour alone.
The dismiss button is named "Dismiss checklist" and, like the disclosure row, has a 44-point touch target.
Markers and text scale with Dynamic Type; the expand animation is removed with Reduce Motion.
edgeCases: The checklist does not hide itself on dismiss; the app removes it.
Step ids must be unique; they identify the rows.
An empty step list is never complete.
Long titles and descriptions wrap; the marker stays at the top of the step.

MonarchOnboardingChecklist(
    "Get started",
    steps: [
        MonarchOnboardingStep(id: "a", title: "Verify your email", isDone: true),
        MonarchOnboardingStep(id: "b", title: "Add a payment method"),
