name: MonarchOrgChart
title: OrgChart
wrapsNative: ScrollView([.horizontal, .vertical]) with a custom zoom Layout and scaleEffect, MagnifyGesture, ScrollViewReader.scrollTo, anchorPreference with overlayPreferenceValue for dotted lines, draggable and dropDestination, contextMenu and accessibilityActions; the list layout is a ScrollView with a LazyVStack
summary: People as cards under their managers, with teams that open and close, teams loaded on demand, zoom and pan, dotted reporting lines and drag to move; an indented list in a compact width or at accessibility text sizes.
whenToUse: To show who reports to whom across an organisation, let people explore teams, open a person's details, and let admins move people to a new manager. Large organisations pass childCount and load teams with onLoadChildren.
whenNotToUse: For a hierarchy of things rather than people (folders, departments), use List with children (the tree-view entry). For goals with progress, use the goal tree. For a flat directory with filters, use MonarchDataTable.
api: init(_ nodes: [MonarchOrgChartNode], expanded: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, focusID: String? = nil, dottedLines: [MonarchOrgChartDottedLine] = [], layout: MonarchOrgChartLayout = .auto, isZoomable: Bool = true, labels: MonarchOrgChartLabels = MonarchOrgChartLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchOrgChartNode) -> Void)? = nil, onLoadChildren: (@MainActor (MonarchOrgChartNode) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onMoveRequest: (@MainActor (MonarchOrgChartNode, MonarchOrgChartMoveTarget) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchOrgChartNode: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, parentID: String? = nil, name: String, title: String? = nil, meta: String? = nil, avatarURL: URL? = nil, kind: MonarchOrgChartNodeKind = .person, isDashed: Bool = false, childCount: Int? = nil) }
enum MonarchOrgChartNodeKind: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case person, vacancy }
struct MonarchOrgChartDottedLine: Hashable, Sendable { init(from: String, to: String) }
enum MonarchOrgChartLayout: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case auto, chart, list }
enum MonarchOrgChartMoveTarget: Hashable, Sendable { case manager(String), topLevel, unspecified }
struct MonarchOrgChartLabels: Sendable { init(label:vacant:dashed:alsoReportsTo:reports:expanded:collapsed:loading:expand:collapse:move:moveHint:loadFailed:zoomIn:zoomOut:zoomReset:zoomLevel:) }

options.name: nodes
options.description: Every person and open position, flat. Reporting lines come from parentID; a node whose manager is missing is top level; cycles are not drawn.

options.name: expanded
options.description: The ids of people whose team is shown. nil keeps the state inside the chart, starting with the top level, the level under it when there are three or fewer top-level people, and the path to focusID.

options.name: focusID
options.description: The person to highlight: the path to them opens, the chart scrolls to them, and their card has an accent border and halo and the selected trait.

options.name: dottedLines
options.description: Secondary reporting lines: dashed curves in the chart layout, and "Also reports to …" in the spoken label in both layouts.

options.name: layout
options.description: chart, list, or auto: the chart in a regular width at standard text sizes, the list otherwise.

options.name: isZoomable
options.description: Shows the zoom buttons (40% to 160%) and allows pinching, in the chart layout.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Called when a card is tapped, for example to open a panel. Without it, cards are not buttons.

options.name: onLoadChildren
options.description: Loads a team whose childCount is larger than the reports in nodes; the app adds the reports to nodes. The team opens when it returns; a thrown error is announced.

options.name: onMoveRequest
options.description: Turns on moving and shows the move hint. Receives the person and .manager(id) for a drop on a card, .topLevel for a drop on the background, or .unspecified when Move was chosen from the card's menu or VoiceOver actions.

states.name: expanded and collapsed
states.description: The chip under a manager shows a forward chevron and the number of reports when the team is hidden, and a down chevron when it is shown; the team is drawn beneath, joined by lines.

states.name: loading
states.description: While onLoadChildren runs, the chip shows a spinner and is disabled, and the spoken value says "Loading team".

states.name: focused
states.description: The focusID card has an accent border with a subtle accent halo and the selected trait.

states.name: vacancy
states.description: A muted card with a dashed border and a briefcase tile instead of an avatar; read with "Open position". It cannot be moved or receive people.

states.name: temporary line
states.description: isDashed draws a dashed border; read with "Temporary reporting line".

states.name: drop target
states.description: While a card is dragged over another, the target takes the subtle accent fill and strong accent border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true), text takes the disabled role, borders the subtle role, the halo is removed and nothing responds.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no nodes the chart draws nothing inside its scroll view.

appearance: Cards use the surface background with a subtle border, the muted background for open positions, the strong border role for dashed borders, and the accent solid and subtle roles for the focused card. Names are in the body strong style and default text role; titles and meta in the caption style and muted role. Connector lines and chips use the default border role; dotted lines the subtle text role. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web OrgChart is an ARIA tree with roving focus and arrow keys; on iOS each person is one VoiceOver element with actions to show or hide the team and to move, which is the platform's equivalent, and the chart reads in tree order. The web switches to the list below 40rem of its own width; iOS switches by size class and also at accessibility text sizes. The web's renderNode and ReactNode meta are not offered: meta is a line of text, because a card is one element and must not hold controls. The web's toolbar slot is not offered: put export or other buttons beside the chart. Ctrl/Cmd + wheel zoom becomes pinch, and pointer panning is the scroll view's own. The web's keyboard M shortcut becomes a Move item in the card's context menu and a VoiceOver action. While dragging, any person card highlights as a target; a refused drop (own team, current manager) is rejected when dropped, because SwiftUI's drop targeting does not expose the dragged item. The parity map named a custom tree Layout: the tree is laid out with stacks (lines are laid-out rectangles that follow right to left), and a custom Layout reports the zoomed size to the scroll view. Android builds MonarchOrgChart with the same API. Several closures are optional (onSelect, onLoadChildren, onMoveRequest). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onSelect.
accessibility: The chart is a container named "Organisation chart" (labels.label).
Each card is one element read as name, title, meta, then "Open position", "Temporary reporting line" and "Also reports to …" when they apply.
The value says "Team shown" or "Team hidden" (or "Loading team") and the number of direct reports; a person without reports has no value.
Accessibility actions "Show team" or "Hide team" and, with onMoveRequest, "Move…"; with onSelect the card is a button.
The focused person has the selected trait.
Avatars, the vacancy icon, connector lines, dotted lines and the count chips are hidden from VoiceOver.
A team that fails to load is announced ("Could not load Ana Silva’s team."); the zoom buttons have spoken names and announce the new level.
Chips and zoom buttons have 44-point touch targets; cards are at least 44 points high and widen with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Nodes with a missing manager, or that are their own manager, are top level; nodes in a cycle are not drawn; a repeated id keeps its first node.
Long names and titles wrap inside the card; the card width scales with Dynamic Type.
The list stops indenting after four levels, so deep teams keep room on a phone.
The chart scrolls itself in both directions, so it needs a height from its parent.
Scrolling to focusID uses the unzoomed position; away from 100% zoom the person may not be centred exactly.
Teams opened or closed while another team loads are kept when it finishes.

name: MonarchOtpPinInput
title: OTPPinInput
wrapsNative: TextField or SecureField with .textContentType(.oneTimeCode), drawn as cells
summary: A one-time code or PIN drawn as one cell per character, over a single standard text field with the one-time-code content type.
whenToUse: For a verification code sent by message or email, or a short PIN.
whenNotToUse: For a password use MonarchPasswordInput. For free text use MonarchTextField.
api: init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, length: Int = 6, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, mode: MonarchOtpPinInputMode = .numeric, size: MonarchOtpPinInputSize = .md, isMasked: Bool = false, lengthHint: String? = nil, groupSize: Int? = nil, onComplete: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchOtpPinInputMode { case numeric, alphanumeric }
enum MonarchOtpPinInputSize { case md, lg }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: text
options.description: The code. It receives only cleaned text: digits, or digits and A to Z in upper case, never longer than length.

options.name: length
options.description: The number of characters. Values under 1 count as 1.

options.name: helper
options.description: Supporting text under the cells.

options.name: error
options.description: Error message; replaces the helper while present.

options.name: mode
options.description: numeric accepts digits and opens the number pad; alphanumeric accepts A to Z and digits.

options.name: size
options.description: md cells are 44 by 44 points, lg cells 52 by 48.

options.name: isMasked
options.description: Shows dots instead of the characters and uses a SecureField.

options.name: lengthHint
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken "Code length: 6".

options.name: groupSize
options.description: Draws a wider gap after every this many cells. Visual only.

options.name: onComplete
options.description: Runs each time the code reaches length characters.

states.name: empty
states.description: Empty cells with the input border.

states.name: focused
states.description: The cell that takes the next character has the theme's focus ring and, while empty, a caret.

states.name: filled
states.description: Each typed character is shown in its cell, or as a dot when masked.

states.name: error
states.description: Danger border on every cell, and an icon and message under the cells.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: Surface-coloured cells with an input border and 8-point corners. The active cell has the theme's focus ring, which is wider and in the text colour in the high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The same single-field design as the web, where one input sits under drawn slots. iOS uses the system one-time-code content type for autofill from Messages instead of autocomplete="one-time-code". The caret does not blink. The web's hover state and readOnly have no counterpart here.
accessibility: One VoiceOver element, the real text field: label, then the code as its value (hidden by the system when masked).
The hint is the code length, then the error (spoken as "Error: …") or else the helper text.
A new error message is announced when it appears.
The error is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
Cells are at least 44 points high and the whole row focuses the field.
The cells keep left-to-right order in right-to-left layouts, because a code is read left to right.
Cells and characters scale with Dynamic Type; cells shrink in width to fit the available width.
edgeCases: Digits from any script (Arabic-Indic, full-width) are stored as ASCII digits.
A binding set from outside to text that is not clean is shown cleaned; the binding is rewritten only on the next edit.
onComplete also runs when an edit replaces one complete code with another.
A masked input uses SecureField, which the system may clear when editing starts again.
With many cells at the largest text sizes, characters scale down to half size before they clip.

wrapsNative: MonarchTabs, which scrolls sideways in a ScrollView when its tabs do not fit
summary: A recipe, not a component: a tab strip with more tabs than fit. MonarchTabs already scrolls sideways and brings the selected tab into view; when the extra tabs should sit in a More menu, compose MonarchTabs with a Menu.
whenToUse: For the sections of a record or a page when there are more of them than fit across a phone, for example six sections of a project.
whenNotToUse: For the top-level destinations of an app use TabView (see bottom-tab-bar), which has its own More tab. For two to four sections use MonarchTabs alone or a segmented Picker.

Menu(content: () -> some View, label: () -> some View)
Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<Value>, content: () -> some View).pickerStyle(.inline)

states.name: scrolling
states.description: MonarchTabs on its own: the strip scrolls sideways and a newly selected tab scrolls into view.

states.name: more menu
states.description: The first tabs are in the strip and the rest in a More menu; the menu's label shows the chosen tab's name when one of its tabs is selected.

states.name: selected in the menu
states.description: No tab in the strip is marked; the More button carries the name, and the Picker in the menu marks it with a checkmark.

appearance: The strip is MonarchTabs (line or pill) and the More button a ghost Monarch button; the menu is the system's.
platformNotes: The web OverflowTabs measures the strip and moves the last tabs into a More menu as the width shrinks. On iOS MonarchTabs scrolls instead, which keeps every tab one swipe away and needs no measuring; the More menu recipe splits at a fixed count chosen by the app. The web's TabsContent panels are the app's own views switched on the selection. Android uses the scrolling tab row of Material 3 natively.
accessibility: MonarchTabs is a tab bar with each tab a button with the selected trait; VoiceOver reaches scrolled-off tabs by swiping.
The More button names the selected overflow tab, so the selection is not hidden in the menu; the inline Picker in the menu reads which tab is selected.
Every tab and the More button have a touch target of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: With the More menu, choose the split so the strip fits at the largest text size, or let the strip scroll as well.
Tab values must be unique across the strip and the menu.

Long titles truncate in the bar; keep them short and put the full name in the content.

title: PageOutline
wrapsNative: VStack of Buttons; the app scrolls with ScrollViewReader.scrollTo in onNavigate
summary: A document's headings as a nested list, with the section being read marked as current; picking a heading lets the app scroll to it.
whenToUse: For long documents, articles and help pages, in a sheet on a phone or beside the document on a wide screen.
whenNotToUse: Not for moving between screens or pages of an app (use a List with NavigationLink or a tab bar) and not for a short page with two or three headings.

options.name: headings
options.description: The headings in document order, each with its text, level 1 through 6 and the id used to scroll to it.

options.name: currentID
options.description: The id of the heading of the section being read. The app works it out from the scroll position.

options.name: maxLevel
options.description: The deepest heading level listed.

options.name: stats
options.description: The word count and reading time shown under the list, such as "1,234 words · 6 min read". MonarchPageOutlineStats(text:) counts them.

options.name: isTitleHidden
options.description: Hides the visible "On this page" title, for example when a sheet's navigation title already says it. The outline keeps it as its spoken name.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the title, the empty message, the stats line and the spoken "Current section".

options.name: onNavigate
options.description: Runs when a heading is picked. Scroll to it here, for example with ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(heading.id, anchor: .top), and close the sheet.

states.name: current
states.description: The current heading is in the accent strong colour and a stronger weight, with an accent bar at its leading edge.

states.name: other headings
states.description: Muted text with a subtle bar, indented one step per nesting level.

states.name: empty
states.description: "Headings you add appear here." in muted text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the headings use the disabled text colour and cannot be picked.

appearance: A title in the label style, then the headings in the body style with a thin leading bar in the subtle border role, the current one in the accent strong and accent solid roles. The stats line is a muted caption. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web outline reads headings from a Tiptap editor or the page and spies on the scroll position itself. On iOS the app passes the headings and the current id, because only the app knows its document model and scroll view, and scrolls to a heading in onNavigate with ScrollViewReader. There is no rich text editor on iOS yet, so the editor mode and its caret tracking are not offered; MonarchPageOutlineStats(text:) replaces the editor word count.
accessibility: The outline is a container named by its title; the visible title has the header trait.
Each heading is a standard button with a 44-point touch target.
The current heading has the selected trait and the value "Current section", and is shown with a stronger weight and a bar as well as colour.
The indent of nested headings scales with Dynamic Type and follows the layout direction.
edgeCases: Skipped levels (a level 3 under a level 1) add one step of indent, not two.
Blank headings and headings deeper than maxLevel are left out.
Long headings wrap; nothing is truncated.
Levels outside 1 through 6 are clamped.

whenToUse: In the sidebar of a document, handbook or course with several pages in sections, where people open pages and, when allowed, reorder, move, add, rename and delete them.
whenNotToUse: Not for the headings inside one page (use MonarchPageOutline), not for a general hierarchy of any depth (use List with children, the tree-view entry), and not for a flat reorderable list (use List with onMove).

states.name: navigation
states.description: Without handlers: the groups as section headings and the pages as rows; the open page is the selected row.

states.name: editing
states.description: In edit mode with onReorder, each page has the system reorder control.

states.name: empty group
states.description: "No pages yet." in the muted role under the heading.

states.name: dialog
states.description: An alert asks for a name (rename, add) or confirms a delete; the confirm button stays disabled until the input is valid.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the disabled text roles, and nothing can be chosen or edited.

appearance: A system list: group names in the label style and muted role as section headings, page numbers in the caption style, tabular digits and subtle role, titles in the body style and default role. The selection highlight, reorder controls, menus and alerts are the system's, tinted by the theme. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web PageTree is a nav with links and a drag-and-keyboard ReorderableList; on iOS it is a List with selection, so it belongs in the sidebar of a NavigationSplitView and the app navigates when the selection changes. The web's href and renderLink are replaced by the selection binding. The web's collapse toggle is not offered: the split view's sidebar button hides the sidebar. The footer slot is not offered: put content after the list. Page menus on the web are a button per row; here they are the row's context menu (long press) and a swipe action, as iOS lists do, with VoiceOver actions for moving. The web's prompt and confirm dialogs become alerts with a TextField. Pages move between groups only through "Move to", because List's onMove reorders within one section. The parity map named List(children:); a two-level grouping reads better as Sections, which also give headings to VoiceOver.
accessibility: The list is named "Pages"; group names are headings.
Each page row is read by its title; the number is hidden from VoiceOver. The open page has the system's selected trait.
With onReorder each page has "Move up" and "Move down" accessibility actions, and every move is announced, such as "Welcome moved to position 2 of 4." or "Welcome moved to Guides."
The add button and the group menu are named with the group ("Add page to Basics", "Actions for Basics") and have 44-point touch targets.
Delete actions use the destructive role; deleting a group with pages requires typing its name, so it is not done by one tap.
edgeCases: A blank title is shown and announced as "Untitled page".
The last page and the last group cannot be deleted: their delete actions are hidden.
Page numbers run across groups and are padded to two digits; past 99 they grow.
The tree does not change groups itself: the app updates them in the handlers, so a handler that does nothing leaves the order as it was.

summary: A recipe, not a component: numbered pages with Previous and Next buttons and a compact range such as “81–100 of 143”, built from Monarch buttons as the web Pagination draws them. MonarchLoadMore is the alternative for a feed that loads at its end.
whenToUse: For any long list that the server returns in pages and where a person needs to jump to a page: invoices, tickets, search results, audit logs. Use the numbered pages as the primary layout.
whenNotToUse: For a list that fits in memory, show it all in a List. For a feed that loads at its end, use MonarchLoadMore; for a cursor-based feed with its own spinner, use MonarchCursorList.

Keep loaded items when a page fails, and retry only that page.
When items can be added or removed on the server while paging, page by cursor, not by number.

appearance: A MonarchCard with the subheading style title, a caption line in the muted text colour and a small primary Add button. Rows have the key symbol in the muted text colour, the name in the strong body style, a subtle info badge and caption lines in the muted text colour, then small ghost buttons. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Monarch does not create passkeys: on iOS the app runs ASAuthorizationController (with ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider) inside onAdd, because the relying party and the server challenge are the app's; Android does the same with CredentialManager. The web detects browser support from window.PublicKeyCredential; iOS 17 always supports passkeys, so isSupported is a parameter for apps that know they are blocked. The web renames in place with an inline editor; iOS asks for the name in a system alert with a text field (prompt-dialog on iOS) whose Save is disabled while the name is blank or unchanged. The confirmation is a system alert, which cannot stay open while the removal runs, so the pending state moves to the row and a failure appears as a notice in the card. The web's headingLevel and locale props have no equivalent (the title is a header; the SwiftUI locale environment is used). Several closures are optional (onRetry, onAdd, onRename, onRemove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Each passkey is one element whose label is its name and whose value is Synced, the detail and the times, built by a tested pure function.
The key symbol is decorative and hidden.
Rename and Remove are separate MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets, named "Rename <name>" and "Remove <name>".
Rename and the removal confirmation are system alerts; the removal button has the destructive role.
Adding, removing and every failure are posted as announcements.
The unsupported state is said in words in a warning notice, not only by the disabled button.
edgeCases: The app updates passkeys after onAdd, onRename and onRemove return; the list does not change itself.
A name made only of spaces cannot be saved; the saved name is trimmed.
The last-method warning appears only when isLastSignInMethod is true and exactly one passkey is left.
Only one rename or removal runs at a time.

The reveal control is given to VoiceOver as a standard Toggle named "Show password" in both states; its value says whether the password is shown.
A new error message is announced when it appears.
The error is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
The field and the toggle each have a 44-point touch target.
Text scales with Dynamic Type.

whenToUse: For a 'Forgot password' flow in an app that signs people in with its own email and password.

MonarchPasswordInput("New password", text: $password, purpose: .new)

MonarchButton("Send reset link", variant: .primary, isLoading: isWorking, fullWidth: true) { … }
.onOpenURL { url in … }

states.description: The email field and Send reset link. An invalid address shows its error on the field.

states.name: sent
states.description: Check your email, naming the address, with a way back to use a different email.

states.name: reset
states.description: Opened by the emailed link: the new password with the strength meter and the confirmation. Change password stays disabled until every rule is met and the two match.

states.name: done
states.description: Password changed, with Back to sign in.

states.name: working
states.description: The primary button shows its spinner while the request or the save runs.

states.name: failed
states.description: A request or save that throws puts its message in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the step; an expired link is shown the same way on the reset step.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: titles in the title style, MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput with their own borders and errors, the strength meter's segments, and full-width primary buttons.
platformNotes: The web's PasswordResetForm is one component with a step prop and messages; on iOS it is a recipe, because the steps, the network calls and the link handling belong to the app. The link returns through a Universal Link (an associated domain) handled with onOpenURL, which the web gets from the page URL. The web's resend cooldown on the sent step is not part of the recipe: Monarch's cooldown logic is internal to MonarchEmailVerificationBanner today. The web moves focus to each step's heading; SwiftUI keeps VoiceOver focus where it can, so the recipe marks each title as a header and the app can post an announcement when the step changes. On a device, add keyboardType(.emailAddress) and textInputAutocapitalization(.never) to the email field; they are left out of the compiled example because the host build also targets macOS.
accessibility: Each step's title has the header trait.
The email and password fields are MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, so labels, errors and announcements of errors come from those components.
The password inputs use the new-password content type, so iOS offers a strong password and saves it to the keychain.
The strength meter reads each rule as met or not met, not by colour alone.
Buttons are MonarchButtons with 44-point touch targets and a busy state while working.
edgeCases: Say that a link was sent whether or not an account exists, so the form does not reveal which addresses have accounts.
The reset step needs the token from the link; keep it in the app and send it with the new password.
A link opened after it expired should show the error on the reset step and offer to request a new one.

name: MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter

whenNotToUse: Not under a sign-in password field. For generic progress use ProgressView with the monarchLinear style.

struct MonarchPasswordRule { init(id: String, label: String, test: @escaping @Sendable (String) -> Bool); static var defaults: [MonarchPasswordRule] }

enum MonarchPasswordStrength: Int, Comparable { case veryWeak, weak, fair, good, strong; static func score(_ password: String, rules: [MonarchPasswordRule] = MonarchPasswordRule.defaults) -> MonarchPasswordStrength }

options.name: password
options.description: The password to rate. It is only read.

options.name: rules
options.description: The requirements listed under the bar. An empty list hides the list.

options.name: showsRules
options.description: Whether to list the requirements.

options.name: strengthText
options.description: Replaces the built-in strength line. Receives nil for an empty password.

options.name: rulesLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Password requirements" spoken name of the list.

options.name: ruleText
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken text of a rule. Receives the rule's label and whether it is met.

options.name: score
options.description: A custom strength estimator. By default MonarchPasswordStrength.score(_:rules:).

states.name: empty
states.description: No segment is filled, the line reads "Password strength: Not entered" and no rule is met.

states.name: very weak, weak
states.description: One segment in the danger colour.

states.name: fair
states.description: Two segments in the warning colour.

states.name: good, strong
states.description: Three or four segments in the success colour.

states.name: rule met
states.description: A filled check symbol and the success text colour; otherwise an empty circle and the muted text colour.

platformNotes: The same rules, score and texts as the web. Rule tests are Swift closures. Lengths are counted in Unicode scalars, as the web counts code points, so the two agree on the same password. Several closures are optional (strengthText, ruleText, score). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is strengthText.
accessibility: The bar is hidden from VoiceOver; the strength is always in words.
The strength line is announced when it changes.
Each rule is one element read as "Met: …" or "Not met: …".
Met and not met differ by icon as well as colour.
The list is a container named "Password requirements".
Text scales with Dynamic Type; the bar keeps its height.
edgeCases: An empty password scores nothing even with a custom score function.
With no rules, any password that is not empty scores good, or strong from 14 characters.
The default score counts rules, not entropy; pass a stronger estimator through score.
The meter does not announce while the strength stays the same.

enum MonarchPaymentMethodCardExpiry { case valid, expiring, expired; static func status(month: Int, year: Int, now: Date = .now, soonMonths: Int = 1, calendar: Calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian)) -> MonarchPaymentMethodCardExpiry }

struct MonarchPaymentMethodCardLabels { init(name:expires:expiredOn:defaultBadge:expiringBadge:expiredBadge:makeDefault:remove:actionLabel:removeTitle:removeMessage:removeConfirm:cancel:failed:) }  // every parameter optional

options.name: brand
options.description: A network id (visa, mastercard, amex, rupay, discover, diners, jcb, unionpay, maestro) shown by its display name, or any display name.

options.name: last4
options.description: The last four digits, exactly as the payment provider returns them.

options.name: expiryMonth
options.description: The expiry month, 1 to 12.

options.name: expiryYear
options.description: The expiry year, two or four digits.

options.name: holderName
options.description: The cardholder's name, shown before the expiry.

options.name: brandImage
options.description: The network's logo. Default: the creditcard symbol. Always decorative.

options.name: expiry
options.description: Replaces the status worked out from the date, when the payment provider already reports it.

options.name: now
options.description: Today, for working out the status.

options.name: isDefault
options.description: Shows the Default badge and hides Make default.

options.name: isRemoveDisabled
options.description: Disables Remove, for example on the only method of an active subscription.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onMakeDefault
options.description: Shows Make default on a card that is not the default. Progress shows on the button while it runs; a thrown error is shown with Try again.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Shows Remove, which asks for confirmation in an alert first. Progress shows on the button while it runs; a thrown error is shown with Try again.

options.name: actions
options.description: Further buttons after Make default and Remove. Pass it labelled (actions:) after the closures.

states.name: valid
states.description: No expiry badge; the expiry line reads "Expires MM/YY".

states.name: expiring
states.description: A warning badge "Expires soon" with a warning icon, this month or next.

states.name: expired
states.description: A danger badge "Expired" with an icon, the line reads "Expired MM/YY", and Make default is disabled.

states.name: default
states.description: A Default badge in the accent colours; Make default is hidden.

states.name: working
states.description: The button of the running action shows progress and reads "Loading" as its value; a second action does not start.

states.name: failed
states.description: An inline error with Try again under the card; the failure is announced.

states.name: remove disabled
states.description: Remove uses the disabled colours and cannot be activated.

appearance: A Monarch card (surface fill, default border, extra-small shadow) with the network image in the muted text colour, the name in the subheading role, holder and expiry in the caption role and muted text colour. The Default badge uses the accent subtle fill and accent strong text; expiry badges use the warning and danger tone palettes. Correct in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web card shows a removal ConfirmDialog that stays open while removal runs and shows a rejection inside the dialog. A system alert cannot show progress, so on iOS the alert closes, the Remove button shows progress and a failure appears under the card with Try again. The web onMakeDefaultError callback is replaced by the same inline error. The heading level option has no iOS equivalent; the name is a heading. The web uses an accent badge tone; MonarchTone has no accent case, so the Default badge draws the accent roles itself. Android ships MonarchPaymentMethodCard. Several closures are optional (onMakeDefault, onRemove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onMakeDefault.
accessibility: The network image is hidden; the name, badges, holder and expiry are combined into one element with the header trait.
Expiry states are badges with text and an icon, never colour alone.
Make default and Remove are read as their title and the card, for example "Remove, Visa ending in 4242".
Removal is confirmed in a system alert with a destructive and a cancel button.
A failed action is announced with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement.
Action buttons keep 44-point touch targets; the badges and the actions wrap onto new rows at large text sizes.
edgeCases: Two-digit years are read as 20YY.
A card is valid to the end of its expiry month, in the Gregorian calendar.
Without a month and a year the status is valid unless expiry is given.
Retrying a failed removal does not ask for confirmation again.
An unknown network id is shown as given, so pass a localised display name.
Changes in onMakeDefault or onRemove that remove the card from the list end the card's view; that is expected.

On iOS amounts are Decimal in major units and the status is a MonarchStatusDefinition. The heading level option has no iOS equivalent; headings use the header trait. Each group heading is a MonarchSectionHeader with the header trait, so the rotor moves between Earnings, Deductions and the other groups.
Each line is one element read as its name, its note and its amount.
Each summary row, detail and year-to-date figure is read as its label and then its value.
Net pay is marked by a larger type role and a divider, not by colour.
While downloading, the button is read as "Preparing the PDF".

edgeCases: Deductions are passed and shown as positive amounts; the group heading says they are deductions.
Totals are never checked against the lines; a mismatch is shown as given.
Reimbursements of zero are left out of the summary.
A long line name wraps; its amount never wraps.
Download presentation (share sheet or file save) is the app's; the view only runs onDownload.

title: PeekPanel
wrapsNative: inspector(isPresented:content:) with inspectorColumnWidth(min:ideal:max:); presentationDetents inside it for compact widths
summary: A side panel that previews a record next to its list is the SwiftUI inspector: a trailing column at regular width and a sheet on a phone. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To read records one after another without leaving the list: the inspector shows the selected record, with previous and next buttons, and the list stays usable beside it at regular width.
whenNotToUse: Not for editing that must be finished or cancelled (use sheet). For a list whose detail is the main content, use NavigationSplitView, which gives the detail the larger column.
api: func inspector<V: View>(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> V) -> some View
func inspectorColumnWidth(min: CGFloat? = nil, ideal: CGFloat, max: CGFloat? = nil) -> some View
func presentationDetents(_ detents: Set<PresentationDetent>) -> some View

states.name: regular width
states.description: A trailing column beside the content. The content stays interactive; nothing is dimmed.

states.name: compact width
states.description: The system presents the same content as a sheet. With presentationDetents it can rest at medium height so the list stays visible.

states.name: closed
states.description: isPresented is false. The column or sheet is removed.

appearance: The system draws the column, its separator and the sheet in every theme. The content inside uses Monarch components and the theme's colours.
platformNotes: The web PeekPanel draws its own header (title, position, previous, next, open full record, close), sizes and keyboard shortcuts. On iOS the container is the inspector and the header is ordinary content: a title, MonarchButton or toolbar items for previous and next, and a NavigationLink or button for the full record. The web's size is inspectorColumnWidth, placement inline or overlay is decided by the system from the width, and its J and K shortcuts are keyboardShortcut on the two buttons. On a phone the panel is a sheet, so it covers part of the list. Android uses a supporting pane or a bottom sheet in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: at regular width the inspector is a column in the same window, so VoiceOver and the keyboard move between the list and the panel freely.
System behaviour: at compact width it is a sheet, which confines focus until it is dismissed with a swipe, the escape gesture or a close button.
Give the previous and next buttons labels, and disable them at the ends rather than hiding them.
Announce the new record when stepping, or move VoiceOver focus to the title with AccessibilityFocusState.
edgeCases: The sheet form has no close button of its own; add one for people who do not swipe.
Without presentationDetents the sheet is full height and hides the list.
Stepping past the first or last record must be prevented by the app; the inspector knows nothing about the list.

whenToUse: On a members or team screen, under the member list, so admins can see who has not joined, send the invitation again, share the link another way or take the invitation back.
whenNotToUse: For people who already joined use MonarchMemberRow rows in a List. For the invitee's side (accepting an invitation) build a screen, not a list.
api: init(_ invites: [MonarchPendingInvite], title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, state: MonarchSectionCardState = .ready, isRetrying: Bool = false, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchPendingInvitesListLabels = MonarchPendingInvitesListLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onResend: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onRevoke: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchPendingInvite { init(id: String, email: String, role: String? = nil, invitedBy: String? = nil, sentAt: Date? = nil, expiresAt: Date? = nil, isExpired: Bool? = nil, link: String? = nil) }

struct MonarchPendingInvitesListLabels { init(title:, listLabel:, invitedBy:, sent:, expires:, expired:, copyLink:, copyTarget:, revoked:, loading:, emptyTitle:, errorTitle:, resend:, revoke:, row: MonarchMemberRowLabels = MonarchMemberRowLabels()) }

options.name: invites
options.description: The invitations, shown in the order given.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Pending invitations".

options.name: description
options.description: A line under the title.

options.name: state
options.description: Ready, loading, empty or error, as in MonarchSectionCard. A ready empty list shows the empty state.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Shows the retry button busy in the error state.

options.name: now
options.description: The reference time for relative times and expiry. Without it they follow the clock, updated every minute.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the member row strings in row.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries loading. Shows a retry button in the error state.

options.name: onResend
options.description: Sends the invitation again, given its id. Without it rows have no Resend invite. Throwing shows the error in the row.

options.name: onRevoke
options.description: Revokes the invitation, given its id, after a confirmation. Without it rows have no Revoke. The app removes the invitation from invites on success; throwing shows the error in the row.

states.name: ready
states.description: One member row per invitation, separated by dividers, each with an info Invited badge.

states.name: expired
states.description: The status badge reads Expired, the expiry is left out of the detail line and Copy link is hidden; Resend stays.

states.name: resending
states.description: The row's Resend invite button shows its spinner; on success the row shows and announces "Invite sent again.".

states.name: revoke confirmation
states.description: A system confirmation dialog titled "Revoke the invite for <email>?" with a destructive Revoke invite button.

states.name: revoking
states.description: The row's revoke button turns into a progress indicator until onRevoke returns; success is announced.

states.name: failed
states.description: The row shows the error under the detail line in the danger colour, with an icon, and announces it.

states.name: loading
states.description: The section card's skeleton rows, read as "Loading invitations".

states.name: empty
states.description: The section card's empty state, "No pending invitations".

states.name: error
states.description: The section card's error state, "Couldn’t load invitations", with a retry when onRetry is given.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard on the raised surface with its border. Rows are MonarchMemberRow: an initials avatar, the email in the strong body style, an info Invited badge, the role and a caption detail line in the muted text colour, and ghost buttons. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The parity map names List rows. Each invitation is a MonarchMemberRow, which carries trailing swipe actions (Resend, Revoke) when the app places the rows in a List; this component puts the rows in a MonarchSectionCard like the web, so it can sit under the member list on a scrolling screen, and there the visible buttons do the same. The web's async getInviteLink is the link field on each invitation, copied with MonarchCopyButton. The revoke confirmation is the system confirmation dialog of the member row, which cannot stay open while the revoke runs, so the pending state moves to the row and a failure is shown in the row instead of inside the dialog. The web's Resend "Sent" label for three seconds is the member row's "Invite sent again." note. The web's detail slot (for example an app access summary) and headingLevel are not offered; locale comes from the SwiftUI environment. Marked experimental as a product pattern until a Rook app adopts it. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onResend, onRevoke). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title has the header trait (MonarchSectionCard).
Each invitation is one element read as the email, with Invited or Expired, the role and the detail line as its value, so expiry never depends on colour.
The detail line is built by a tested pure function: "Invited by Sam Rivera · Sent 2 days ago · Expires in 5 days".
Resend invite, Copy link and Revoke are separate buttons named after the email: "Resend invite, ana@example.com", "Copy link for ana@example.com", "Revoke invite for ana@example.com".
Every button keeps a 44-point touch target.
A resend, a revoke and a failure are posted as announcements.
edgeCases: isExpired overrides the expiry worked out from expiresAt; an invitation is expired at the exact expiry time.
An invitation without a link, with a blank link or expired has no Copy link.
An invitation with no sender and no dates has no detail line.
Long email addresses stay on one line and truncate at the end, as member names do; VoiceOver reads the full address.
The list does not remove a revoked invitation itself; the app removes it from invites.

name: MonarchPeriodSelector
title: PeriodSelector
wrapsNative: Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented), inside ViewThatFits(in: .horizontal) with a Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) fallback; MonarchDateRangePicker (two DatePicker rows) for the custom period; Date.IntervalFormatStyle for the resolved dates
summary: Picks the period a dashboard or report covers, from presets such as today, the last 7 or 30 days and this quarter, or a custom date range, and gives the app the resolved first and last day.
whenToUse: When a dashboard, report or chart can be scoped to a period and every app should name and compute periods the same way.
whenNotToUse: For a single date, use DatePicker. For any range without presets, use MonarchDateRangePicker directly.
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, selection: Binding<MonarchPeriod>, presets: [MonarchPeriodPreset] = [.today, .last7Days, .last30Days, .thisQuarter, .custom], variant: MonarchPeriodSelectorVariant = .segmented, showsRange: Bool = false, today: Date = Date(), minimumDate: Date? = nil, maximumDate: Date? = nil, maximumDays: Int? = nil, labels: MonarchPeriodSelectorLabels = MonarchPeriodSelectorLabels())

struct MonarchPeriod { init(_ preset: MonarchPeriodPreset, range: ClosedRange<Date>? = nil); var preset: MonarchPeriodPreset; var range: ClosedRange<Date>?; func resolved(today: Date, calendar: Calendar) -> ClosedRange<Date>? }

enum MonarchPeriodPreset: String { case today, yesterday, last7Days = "7d", last14Days = "14d", last30Days = "30d", last90Days = "90d", last180Days = "180d", last365Days = "365d", thisWeek = "this-week", thisMonth = "this-month", lastMonth = "last-month", thisQuarter = "this-quarter", lastQuarter = "last-quarter", thisYear = "this-year", custom }
enum MonarchPeriodSelectorVariant { case segmented, menu }
MonarchPeriodSelectorLabels.init(presets: [MonarchPeriodPreset: String] = [:], customRange: String? = nil, dateRange: MonarchDateRangePickerLabels = MonarchDateRangePickerLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The name of the control, read by VoiceOver. Built in: "Period".

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen preset, and the days of a custom period.

options.name: presets
options.description: The presets offered, in order.

options.name: variant
options.description: Segments, which become a menu when they do not fit or at the accessibility text sizes, or a pop-up menu.

options.name: showsRange
options.description: Shows the resolved dates under the control, such as "Oct 9 – Nov 7, 2026".

options.name: today
options.description: The day presets count from. Pass the workspace's day to match the server.

options.name: minimumDate
options.description: The earliest day a custom period can start.

options.name: maximumDate
options.description: The latest day a custom period can end. By default today.

options.name: maximumDays
options.description: The longest custom period in days, such as 366 for reports.

options.name: labels
options.description: Preset names merged per preset, the custom range label, and the date range picker's strings.

states.name: preset
states.description: The chosen preset is the selected segment or the menu's title; with showsRange its first and last day are written under it.

states.name: custom
states.description: A MonarchDateRangePicker labelled "Custom period" appears under the presets, starting from the dates shown before; its end is limited to maximumDate (today by default) and its length to maximumDays.

states.name: custom without dates
states.description: With no range yet, the picker shows its Choose dates button and resolved(today:calendar:) returns nil.

states.name: menu
states.description: The menu variant, and the segmented variant when its segments do not fit or at the accessibility text sizes, is a system pop-up button showing the chosen preset.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) the picker and the date pickers are the system's disabled controls.

appearance: The system segmented control or pop-up button in the app's tint, the custom range in MonarchDateRangePicker's look, and the resolved dates in the caption style with the muted text role. The controls follow the system's light, dark and increased-contrast appearance.
platformNotes: iOS uses the system segmented control and pop-up menu instead of the web's SegmentedControl and Select; segments that do not fit become the menu instead of scrolling sideways as on the web, because a segmented control does not scroll and does not grow with Dynamic Type. The web's size (sm, md) is not offered: the system controls have one height that follows Dynamic Type. The value is a MonarchPeriod holding Date values, and resolved(today:calendar:) plays the web's resolvePeriod: rolling presets end today and count today, this week starts on the calendar's first weekday (the web's weekStartsOn), and dates are the first moment of each day in the calendar's time zone. The raw values of MonarchPeriodPreset are the web's preset names. The binding replaces the web's onValueChange; read the resolved dates in onChange. Android has no PeriodSelector yet.
accessibility: The picker is named by label ("Period") and keeps the system's segmented control or pop-up button role, with the chosen preset as its value.
The custom range is a MonarchDateRangePicker named "Custom period": its pickers read "Custom period, Start" and "Custom period, End".
The resolved dates are static text written in the locale.
Segments become a menu at the accessibility text sizes, so every preset name stays readable.
edgeCases: Choosing the preset already chosen changes nothing.
Choosing Custom starts from the dates already shown, so nothing jumps; the custom dates are kept while another preset is chosen and come back with Custom.
A custom range is never cleared from the selector; it has no clear button.
Last month and last quarter are whole months, including February in a leap year and the last quarter of the previous year in January.
Presets resolve against today and the environment's calendar; pass both to match a server in another time zone.

name: MonarchPermissionMatrix
title: PermissionMatrix
wrapsNative: ViewThatFits choosing between a Grid of Toggles in the Monarch checkbox style (roles as columns) and, at compact width, MonarchTabs for the role with one Toggle row per permission
summary: Which permissions each role has: roles by permissions, edited with checkboxes or shown read only, grouped, with cells that cannot change and say why.
whenToUse: In workspace or organisation settings where admins review and change what each role may do.
whenNotToUse: To give one person a role, use MonarchRolePicker. For an AI assistant's access to apps use MonarchAiPermissionScope.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, selection: Binding<[String: Set<String>]>, roles: [MonarchPermissionMatrixRole], permissions: [MonarchPermissionMatrixPermission], layout: MonarchPermissionMatrixLayout = .automatic, isReadOnly: Bool = false, labels: MonarchPermissionMatrixLabels = MonarchPermissionMatrixLabels(), lockReason: (@MainActor (String, String) -> String?)? = nil)
struct MonarchPermissionMatrixRole { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchPermissionMatrixPermission { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, group: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchPermissionMatrixLayout { case automatic, grid, byRole }
struct MonarchPermissionMatrixLabels { init(permissionHeader:, rolePicker:, cellLabel:, allowed:, notAllowed:, locked:) }

options.name: title
options.description: A heading above the matrix, with the header trait.

options.name: selection
options.description: The granted permission ids by role id. A missing role has none.

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles, in order: columns of the grid, tabs of the compact layout.

options.name: permissions
options.description: The permissions, in order. Those with the same group are listed together under its heading, groups in the order they first appear.

options.name: layout
options.description: automatic shows the grid when it fits the width and one role at a time otherwise; grid always shows the grid, scrolling sideways; byRole always shows one role at a time.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows a check or a dash with Allowed or Not allowed instead of checkboxes.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the column heading, the role picker name, the cell name, Allowed, Not allowed and the default lock reason.

options.name: lockReason
options.description: Given a role id and a permission id, why the cell cannot change, or nil when it can. An empty string uses "This can’t be changed".

states.name: grid
states.description: A header row of roles, a divider, group headings and one row per permission with a checkbox per role.

states.name: one role at a time
states.description: A tab strip of roles, the role's description, then group headings and a checkbox row per permission.

states.name: locked
states.description: The checkbox is disabled with a lock symbol; in the compact layout the reason is written under the row.

states.name: read only
states.description: A check in the strong success colour or a dash in the subtle text colour, read as Allowed or Not allowed.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every checkbox and tab uses the disabled colours and cannot be changed.

appearance: Role and permission names use the label and body styles in the default text colour, descriptions and group headings the caption and label styles in the muted text colour. Checkboxes are the Monarch checkbox style. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows a table with arrow-key grid navigation (WAI-ARIA grid); iOS has no arrow keys on a phone, so the grid relies on VoiceOver moving cell by cell, and on a phone the grid does not fit, so the automatic layout shows one role at a time with MonarchTabs. The web's controlled and uncontrolled value with onValueChange is a SwiftUI binding; watch it with onChange to save. The web's isLocked may return a rich reason; here it is a String. disabled is the SwiftUI .disabled modifier. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: Each editable cell is a standard toggle (the Monarch checkbox style keeps the system toggle for VoiceOver), named "<permission> for <role>" in the grid by a tested pure function, and by the permission in the compact layout, where the selected role tab gives the role.
A locked cell is disabled and its reason is the accessibility hint; in the compact layout it is also written under the row.
Read only, each cell is one element with the cell name as label and Allowed or Not allowed as value, so the mark's shape and colour are not the only signal.
The title, the column heading, role headings and group headings have the header trait.
The role picker is MonarchTabs: a tab bar with the selected trait and 44-point tabs.
At large text sizes the automatic layout moves to one role at a time, so no text is cut off.
edgeCases: With no roles, only the title is shown.
A role id in the selection that is not in roles is kept and ignored.
The forced grid scrolls sideways when it is wider than the screen.
Locked cells keep whatever the selection says; the app decides their value.

name: MonarchPhoneCountrySelect
title: PhoneCountrySelect
wrapsNative: MonarchCombobox (a .sheet with a List and .searchable) over a bundled E.164 calling-code table, with names from Locale.localizedString(forRegionCode:)
summary: A searchable picker for the country calling code of a phone number, with the bundled calling codes and a parser that finds the country of a typed number.
whenToUse: Before a phone number field, so people choose the country of the number; MonarchPhoneCountry.matching(_:preferred:) can preset it from a pasted number.
whenNotToUse: Not for a postal or billing country; use MonarchCountrySelect. Not for validating or formatting the number itself.
api: init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<String?>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, countries: [String]? = nil, preferred: [String] = [], locale: Locale? = nil, showsFlags: Bool = true, isRequired: Bool = false, isClearable: Bool = false, labels: MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels = MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels())
struct MonarchPhoneCountry: Identifiable { let code: String; let dialCode: String; let leadingDigits: [String]; init(code: String, dialCode: String, leadingDigits: [String] = []) }
static var MonarchPhoneCountry.all: [MonarchPhoneCountry]
static func MonarchPhoneCountry.country(code: String) -> MonarchPhoneCountry?
static func MonarchPhoneCountry.matching(_ phone: String, preferred: String? = nil) -> MonarchPhoneCountry?

struct MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels { init(suggested: String? = nil, all: String? = nil, option: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, combobox: MonarchComboboxLabels = MonarchComboboxLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen country's ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, because several countries share a calling code. Read the calling code with MonarchPhoneCountry.country(code:).

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown in the field while nothing is chosen.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the field.

options.name: error
options.description: An error message, shown with an icon and announced.

options.name: countries
options.description: Limits the list to these ISO codes. nil lists every country in MonarchPhoneCountry.all.

options.name: preferred
options.description: ISO codes listed first under Suggested. Each country is listed once.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the names and the sort order. The environment's locale when nil.

options.name: showsFlags
options.description: Shows each country's flag emoji at the end of its row.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds Required to the hint.

options.name: isClearable
options.description: Shows a clear button in the field. Off by default because a phone number needs a country.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replaces Suggested, All countries, the row text (Portugal (+351)) and the combobox strings; the combobox's empty text is built in as No matching country.

states.name: empty
states.description: The field shows the prompt in the subtle text colour.

states.name: chosen
states.description: The field shows the row text, such as Portugal (+351); no clear button unless isClearable.

states.name: suggestions
states.description: With preferred, those countries come first under Suggested and the rest under All countries.

states.name: searching
states.description: Matches by name, ISO code or digits, with labels that start with the query first.

states.name: no match
states.description: The list reads No matching country.

states.name: error
states.description: The field border and message use the danger colour, with an icon; the error is announced.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Label, value and border use the disabled roles; the sheet does not open.

appearance: The field is MonarchCombobox's. Each row is the name and calling code in the default text colour with the flag at the end. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: Neither iOS nor Android exposes calling codes publicly, so the table is bundled: the same 243 entries and shared-code rules as the web. Names come from Foundation. The web reports the code and the calling code in onValueChange; iOS binds the ISO code and the app reads the calling code from MonarchPhoneCountry. MonarchComboboxOption has no slot before the label, so the flag is at the end of the row. The web's listLabel has no equivalent: the sheet's title is the field label.
accessibility: The field is a button labelled with the label, whose value is the chosen row's label or None.
The help text, the error (read as Error: ...) and Required are the field's hint; a new error is announced.
The chosen row has the selected trait and a check mark, not colour alone.
Rows and the field are at least 44 points high.
Each row is read with its text, including the calling code, then the flag emoji as VoiceOver names it.
edgeCases: Countries that share +1, +7, +44 and others are told apart by their leading digits; without them, preferred or the code's main country (US for +1) wins.
matching reads numbers that start with + or 00, in Arabic-Indic, Persian or full-width digits, with bidirectional marks, spaces, dots, dashes and brackets.
Searching 44, +44 or 1242 finds the countries with that calling code.
Unknown codes in countries and preferred are ignored.

    locale: Locale(identifier: "en_US"),
    showsFlags: false
)

name: MonarchPhoneInput
title: PhoneInput
wrapsNative: TextField with .keyboardType(.phonePad) and .textContentType(.telephoneNumber), beside a Button that opens MonarchPhoneCountrySelect's searchable country list (a .sheet with a List and .searchable)
summary: A phone number field with a country calling code button, which writes one E.164 value such as +442079460958.
whenToUse: Whenever a form asks for a phone number that has to be dialled or texted from anywhere: sign-up, delivery contact, two-step verification.
whenNotToUse: Not for a calling code on its own; use MonarchPhoneCountrySelect. Not for an extension or an internal short number; use MonarchTextField with .keyboardType(.phonePad).
api: init(_ label: String, value: Binding<String?>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, defaultCountry: String = "US", countries: [String]? = nil, preferred: [String] = [], locale: Locale? = nil, showsFlags: Bool = true, isRequired: Bool = false, labels: MonarchPhoneInputLabels = MonarchPhoneInputLabels(), onCountryChange: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)
static func toE164(dialCode: String, national: String, country: String? = nil) -> String?
static func isValidE164(_ value: String) -> Bool
static func parse(_ phone: String, preferred: String? = nil) -> MonarchPhoneInputDetails?
struct MonarchPhoneInputDetails: Sendable, Hashable { let country: String; let dialCode: String; let national: String; init(country: String, dialCode: String, national: String) }

struct MonarchPhoneInputLabels: Sendable { init(country: String? = nil, invalid: String? = nil, countrySelect: MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels = MonarchPhoneCountrySelectLabels(), field: MonarchFormFieldLabels = MonarchFormFieldLabels()) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised. It names the number field.

options.name: value
options.description: The number in E.164, or nil when empty. Any international form (+44 20 7946 0958, 0044…) is read when it is set.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder text in the number field while it is empty.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the row.

options.name: error
options.description: An error from the app, shown with an icon and announced. The component's own incomplete-number message takes its place while it shows.

options.name: defaultCountry
options.description: The ISO code of the country when the value does not give one. Read once, when the view is created.

options.name: countries
options.description: Limits the country list to these ISO codes. nil lists every country in MonarchPhoneCountry.all.

options.name: preferred
options.description: ISO codes listed first in the country list under Suggested.

options.name: locale
options.description: The language of the country names in the list and the spoken value. The environment's locale when nil.

options.name: showsFlags
options.description: Shows the flag on the country button and in the list.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds Required to the hint.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Country code, Enter a complete phone number., the country list strings and the spoken Required and error prefix.

options.name: onCountryChange
options.description: Receives the ISO code when the country changes, from the list, a pasted number or a shared calling code.

states.name: empty
states.description: The number field shows the prompt in the subtle text colour; the button shows the default country's flag and calling code.

states.name: typing
states.description: The value is not changed on each keystroke; a pasted full international number moves to its country at once and keeps the national digits.

states.name: committed
states.description: When the field loses focus, Return is pressed or the country changes, a valid number is written as E.164 and the field shows its national digits.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A number outside 8 to 15 digits, or an international number with no known calling code, keeps its text, is not written, and shows Enter a complete phone number. with an icon and a danger border.

states.name: error
states.description: An app error shows under the row with an icon, and both borders take the danger colour.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Both parts take the disabled fill, border and text colours and do not respond.

states.name: accessibility sizes
states.description: At the accessibility text sizes the country button sits above the number field instead of beside it.

appearance: The button and the field are separate bordered controls on the surface fill with the input border, as MonarchTextField; an error turns both borders to the strong danger colour. The calling code and number use the default text colour, the chevron the muted secondary colour. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web shows the country select and the input in one row with a hidden form input; iOS has no form submission, so the binding is the value. The country list is the one MonarchPhoneCountrySelect shows, opened from a compact flag and calling code button, because the full combobox field does not fit beside a number on a phone. The web's Escape to restore the last value has no counterpart on the phone pad. The web's sm, md and lg control sizes are not offered: iOS fields have one size that grows with Dynamic Type. Android has no PhoneInput yet; the names follow the web and the plan (MonarchPhoneInput). The web reports details in onValueChange; iOS gives MonarchPhoneInput.parse(_:preferred:) and onCountryChange.
accessibility: The visible label is hidden from VoiceOver and given to the number field, whose value is the typed number.
The field's hint is the error (read as Error: …), the help text and Required, each when present; a new error is announced.
The country button is named Country code and its value is the country and calling code, such as Portugal (+351), in the chosen language.
Errors are an icon and text and a border, not colour alone.
The number field and the button are laid out left to right in right-to-left languages, as phone numbers are written.
The button and the field are at least 44 points high; at the accessibility text sizes they stack.
The country list's rows are buttons with the selected trait and a check mark on the current country.
edgeCases: One trunk 0 is dropped (020 7946 0958 under +44 is +442079460958), except for Italy, San Marino and Vatican City.
Countries sharing a calling code are resolved from the number: 242 555 0100 typed under US is written as +12425550100 and the country moves to the Bahamas.
Digits typed in Arabic-Indic, Persian or full-width forms, and bidirectional marks from pasted text, are read.
A value set by the app that has no known calling code is shown as digits under the current country.
Clearing the field and leaving it writes nil; it is not an error. Use error to require a number.
The phone pad has no Return key, so the value is written when focus leaves the field; read the binding after focus moves, for example on submit of the form.

name: MonarchPlanCard
title: PlanCard
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (VStack, ViewThatFits)
summary: One plan in a plan picker: its name, price, who it is for, what it includes and a call to action, on a Monarch card.
whenToUse: In a plan picker or an upgrade screen, one card per plan.
whenNotToUse: For a single price in running text, write it as text. Do not use it to sell digital goods outside the store's billing: an in-app purchase must go through StoreKit, and the card only presents the plan.
api: MonarchPlanCard.init(_ name: String, price: String? = nil, period: String? = nil, priceNote: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, featuresLabel: String? = nil, features: [MonarchPlanCardFeature] = [], badge: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, isHighlighted: Bool = false, isCurrent: Bool = false, currentPlanLabel: String? = nil, notIncludedLabel: String? = nil, @ViewBuilder action: () -> Action)

MonarchPlanCard.init(_ name: String, price: String? = nil, period: String? = nil, priceNote: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, featuresLabel: String? = nil, features: [MonarchPlanCardFeature] = [], badge: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, isHighlighted: Bool = false, isCurrent: Bool = false, currentPlanLabel: String? = nil, notIncludedLabel: String? = nil) where Action == EmptyView
MonarchPlanCardFeature.init(_ label: String, hint: String? = nil, isIncluded: Bool = true)

options.name: name
options.description: The plan name, already localised. A heading.

options.name: price
options.description: The price as the product writes it, such as "$12" or "Contact us". Never formatted by the card.

options.name: period
options.description: Text after the price, such as "per seat / month".

options.name: priceNote
options.description: A line under the price, such as "Billed yearly".

options.name: description
options.description: One or two sentences on who the plan is for.

options.name: featuresLabel
options.description: A heading above the features.

options.name: features
options.description: What the plan includes. A string literal is an included feature; isIncluded: false lists one it does not have.

options.name: badge
options.description: A short label beside the name, such as "Recommended".

options.name: footer
options.description: Small print under the features.

options.name: isHighlighted
options.description: Emphasises the card as the recommended plan.

options.name: isCurrent
options.description: Adds the "Current plan" badge.

options.name: currentPlanLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in badge text "Current plan".

options.name: notIncludedLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken prefix "Not included:".

options.name: action
options.description: The call to action, normally one button.

states.name: default
states.description: A card with the subtle border and the smallest shadow.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: A 2-point accent border, a larger shadow and a solid badge.

states.name: current
states.description: An outline badge with "Current plan" beside the name.

appearance: The card surface with the subtle border in every theme. Included features have a checkmark in the success colour and default text; features that are not included have a dash and muted text. A highlighted card adds an accent border twice as wide as a normal border.
platformNotes: The web card takes any node for the name, price, features and footer and a heading level; here they are strings, the action is a view, and the name always has the header trait. The web badge on a highlighted card uses the accent tone; MonarchBadge has no accent tone, so it is a solid neutral badge. On the web the action follows the description and so it does here. An app that sells digital goods must use StoreKit for the purchase itself; the card does not start a purchase. Android uses the same name and parameters.
accessibility: The name has the header trait.
The price and its period are read as one element.
Each feature is one element. A feature that is not included is read with "Not included:" before it and shows a dash, so the difference does not depend on colour.
The action stays a separate element with its own touch target.
Highlighting is a wider border and a badge with text, not colour alone. The badge text is read with the header row.
All text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; the name and badges, and the price and period, stack vertically when they do not fit on one line.
edgeCases: Only the name is required; every other part is left out when it is nil or empty.
A price without a period, and a period without a price, are both drawn.
A feature's hint is read after its label, separated by a comma.
The card fills the available width, like MonarchCard.
