wrapsNative: TextEditor(text: Binding<AttributedString>, selection: Binding<AttributedTextSelection>) (iOS 26), with MonarchEditorToolbar above it and MonarchMentionPicker below it; formatting through AttributedString.transformAttributes(in:) and transform(updating:)
summary: A rich-text editor on the system's TextEditor and an AttributedString: a formatting toolbar for bold, italic, strikethrough, code, links, headings and lists, a prompt, a character count against a limit, and @mention suggestions. Requires iOS 26.
whenToUse: For descriptions, notes, comments and replies that need inline formatting, links, headings or lists, in an app on iOS 26 or later.
whenNotToUse: For plain text, use TextField(axis: .vertical) or TextEditor(text: String). For block documents with tables, callouts and embeds, compose the block components (MonarchTableBlock, MonarchCalloutBlock). Before iOS 26 there is no Monarch rich-text editor.
api: @available(iOS 26.0, macOS 26.0, *) init(_ label: String, text: Binding<AttributedString>, prompt: String? = nil, tools: [[MonarchEditorTool]] = MonarchRichTextEditor.defaultTools, maxLength: Int? = nil, showsCharacterCount: Bool? = nil, isReadOnly: Bool = false, isInvalid: Bool = false, mentionItems: [MonarchMentionItem]? = nil, mentionStatus: MonarchMentionPickerStatus = .ready, labels: MonarchRichTextEditorLabels = MonarchRichTextEditorLabels(), onMentionSearch: (@MainActor (MonarchMentionQuery?) -> Void)? = nil, onMention: (@MainActor (MonarchMentionItem) -> Void)? = nil, onTool: (@MainActor (MonarchEditorTool) -> Void)? = nil)
static var defaultTools: [[MonarchEditorTool]]
static func isOverLimit(_ text: AttributedString, maxLength: Int?) -> Bool

MonarchRichTextEditorLabels.init(count: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, countOfLimit: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, remaining: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, toolbar: MonarchEditorToolbarLabels = MonarchEditorToolbarLabels(), mentions: MonarchMentionPickerLabels = MonarchMentionPickerLabels())

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the text view, already localised. Show a visible label nearby, for example with MonarchFormField.

options.name: text
options.description: The document. Formatting is stored as SwiftUI attributes (font, strikethroughStyle, link).

options.name: prompt
options.description: Shown while the document is empty.

options.name: tools
options.description: The toolbar's tools in groups; [] for no toolbar. Undo, redo, body text, headings 1 to 3, bold, italic, strikethrough, code, link and both lists are applied by the editor; custom tools go to onTool; checklists, quotes, code blocks and headings 4 to 6 are left out.

options.name: maxLength
options.description: The most characters. Shows the count against it and the danger border when passed; typing is not stopped.

options.name: showsCharacterCount
options.description: Shows the count. By default, shown when there is a maxLength.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the document as Text, without the toolbar or the box.

options.name: isInvalid
options.description: Draws the danger border, for a validation error shown nearby.

options.name: mentionItems
options.description: The suggestions for the mention being typed; nil turns mentions off.

options.name: mentionStatus
options.description: The state of the mention search: loading, ready or failed.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the count strings, and the toolbar's and mention picker's labels.

options.name: onMentionSearch
options.description: Receives the mention being typed after @ or #, or nil when there is none; search and update mentionItems. Also called by the picker's retry.

options.name: onMention
options.description: Receives the chosen person or channel after "@Name " is written into the text.

options.name: onTool
options.description: Receives the custom tools of the toolbar.

states.name: empty
states.description: The prompt in the muted text colour over the text area.

states.name: focused
states.description: The theme's focus ring around the box.

states.name: formatting on
states.description: The toolbar toggles of the formats at the caret or the whole selection are on; the text style menu shows the paragraph's style.

states.name: over the limit
states.description: The count turns the danger colour, the border the danger colour, and the text view's hint says how many characters are over.

states.name: invalid
states.description: The danger border.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(true): the subtle fill and border, and neither the text nor the toolbar can be used.

states.name: read only
states.description: The document as Text, without the box or the toolbar.

states.name: mentioning
states.description: MonarchMentionPicker under the text while @ or # and a name are typed, with its loading, empty and error states.

appearance: A box in the surface colour with the input border and medium corners: the toolbar, a subtle divider, then the text in the default text colour. Headings use the theme's title, heading and subheading weights. The count is a caption in the muted colour, danger when over. The roles follow light, dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web RichTextEditor is built on Tiptap and stores HTML or Tiptap JSON. iOS has no shared engine: the editor is SwiftUI's TextEditor on an AttributedString, which exists from iOS 26, so the component is available from iOS 26 only. The parity map named a UITextView with TextKit 2 below iOS 26; that second engine is not built, because it would store formatting as UIKit attributes, unlike the SwiftUI attributes of the iOS 26 editor, before the document interchange format is agreed. It stays experimental until that format is agreed: no HTML, Markdown or JSON conversion is shipped, and the app stores the AttributedString (it is Codable) or converts it. Differences from the web: checklists, quotes and code blocks are not offered, because the system text view has no block structure; lists are text prefixes ("• ", "1. "); headings are levels 1 to 3; maxLength does not stop typing, because TextEditor has no hook to refuse an edit, so the app checks isOverLimit before saving; a mention is written as plain "@Name " and reported through onMention, where the web inserts a mention node; pasted and dropped files are not handled (use MonarchFileUpload beside the editor); the toolbar sits above the text, not above the keyboard, and the web's toolbarPosition and toolbarEnd are not offered. The web's text style shortcuts (Command-B and so on) are the system's on a hardware keyboard. Inline formats in a heading: italic, code, strikethrough and links apply; bold has no effect because the heading is bold already. Links are a link attribute set from the toolbar's link form, not the MonarchLinkStyle button style. Android plans a Compose editor with the same scope.
accessibility: The text view is the standard TextEditor, named by label, with its text as the value and all system editing gestures, rotor actions and dictation.
The toolbar is MonarchEditorToolbar: a container named "Formatting" whose toggles read their name and on or off state, with 44-point targets.
The count reads "268 characters left" or "3 characters over the limit"; over the limit, the text view's hint says so too.
The prompt is hidden from VoiceOver, as with a text field's prompt.
Mention suggestions are MonarchMentionPicker buttons; results and states are announced so focus can stay in the text.
Formatting is not conveyed by colour: bold, italic, strikethrough and headings are type changes, and links are underlined by the system.
edgeCases: Return at the end of a list item starts the next item; Return on an empty item ends the list.
Text pasted from another app keeps its fonts; a font of an unknown size is treated as body text by the toolbar.
The document stores fonts by text style, so it scales with Dynamic Type, and the system typeface's text styles are used rather than Monarch's token sizes so that formatted and plain runs match.

name: MonarchRoadmap
title: Roadmap
wrapsNative: MonarchGanttTimeline with undated: .row, the quarter zoom and the roadmap's names (and through it ScrollView(.horizontal) with Canvas drawing, LongPressGesture sequenced before DragGesture with sensoryFeedback, accessibilityActions, Menu with an inline Picker, Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented), and Form with DatePicker in a sheet)
summary: Projects over months and quarters, grouped by initiative, with progress, the health last reported in words, milestones and dependencies between projects, on the Gantt timeline.
whenToUse: To give leads a long-range view of projects across teams: when each runs, how far along it is, what was last reported and which projects block others. Pass onChange only where people really replan on this screen.
whenNotToUse: To schedule individual tasks by dragging use MonarchGanttTimeline directly. For a status-only overview without dates use a List of rows with MonarchStatusBadge.
api: init(_ items: [MonarchRoadmapItem], state: Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState>? = nil, groups: [MonarchRoadmapGroup] = [], dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency] = [], milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone] = [], zoomLevels: [MonarchGanttTimelineZoom] = [.month, .quarter, .year], today: Date? = Date(), showsToolbar: Bool = true, labels: MonarchRoadmapLabels = MonarchRoadmapLabels(), timelineLabels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder toolbarActions: () -> ToolbarActions)

init(_ items: [MonarchRoadmapItem], state: Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState>? = nil, groups: [MonarchRoadmapGroup] = [], dependencies: [MonarchGanttTimelineDependency] = [], milestones: [MonarchGanttTimelineMilestone] = [], zoomLevels: [MonarchGanttTimelineZoom] = [.month, .quarter, .year], today: Date? = Date(), showsToolbar: Bool = true, labels: MonarchRoadmapLabels = MonarchRoadmapLabels(), timelineLabels: MonarchGanttTimelineLabels = MonarchGanttTimelineLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem, MonarchGanttTimelineDates) -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor (MonarchRoadmapItem) -> Void)? = nil) where ToolbarActions == EmptyView

struct MonarchRoadmapItem: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, label: String, start: Date? = nil, end: Date? = nil, groupID: String? = nil, progress: Double? = nil, progressText: String? = nil, health: MonarchRoadmapHealth? = nil, tone: MonarchTone? = nil) }
struct MonarchRoadmapGroup: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, label: String, start: Date? = nil, end: Date? = nil, health: MonarchRoadmapHealth? = nil) }
enum MonarchRoadmapHealth: String, Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case onTrack, atRisk, offTrack, notReported }

struct MonarchRoadmapLabels: Sendable { init(health: (@Sendable (MonarchRoadmapHealth) -> String)? = nil, count: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, meta: (@Sendable (_ first: String, _ second: String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: items
options.description: The projects: id, label, start and target dates (neither makes a row that says "No dates"), groupID, progress from 0 to 1, progressText such as "8/20", health (nil writes none, .notReported writes "No health reported") and tone (nil takes it from health).

options.name: state
options.description: The first visible day, the zoom, chart or list. nil keeps the state inside the roadmap, which opens at the quarter zoom (nine months visible); a binding starts from the app's value.

options.name: groups
options.description: Initiatives, themes or teams as heading rows, in order. Each heading says how many projects it has and its health; a group with dates shows a thin span. Projects without a known group follow the groups.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Links between projects, drawn as arrows and written as "Depends on" in the list.

options.name: milestones
options.description: Dated checkpoints: on a project's row with itemID, otherwise in a lane under the header.

options.name: zoomLevels
options.description: The zoom levels offered in the toolbar's zoom menu.

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day of the today line, read in the environment's calendar; nil hides the line and disables Today. Pass a fixed date in tests and previews.

options.name: showsToolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar: Today, Earlier, Later, the visible range, the zoom menu, the chart and list switch and toolbarActions.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the roadmap's own strings: the health words, the group count and the joiner of a heading's second line.

options.name: timelineLabels
options.description: Replacements for the timeline's strings. The chart is named "Roadmap" and the row header says "Project" unless timeline or rowHeader is given here; every other value is passed through.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Makes dates editable (touch and hold then drag, arrow keys, VoiceOver actions, the date sheet in the list) and is called with the roadmap project and its new dates. Without it the roadmap is read-only.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each bar and list row a button that calls back with the roadmap project.

options.name: toolbarActions
options.description: Extra controls at the end of the toolbar, such as a team filter.

states.name: read only
states.description: The default. Bars have no drag, no key handling and no VoiceOver actions; with onOpen they are still buttons that open the project.

states.name: editable
states.description: With onChange, everything the timeline offers to change dates, and onChange receives the roadmap project, not a timeline row.

states.name: health
states.description: On track, at risk, off track or no health reported is written in words on the row heading's second line, after the progress text; at risk tints the bar warning and off track danger.

states.name: no health tracked
states.description: With health nil nothing is written about health and the bar keeps the accent colour.

states.name: no dates
states.description: A project without dates stays in its group as a row that says "No dates" instead of moving to an Unscheduled section.

states.name: out of view
states.description: A project outside the visible window says "Ended …" or "Starts …" on its row.

states.name: list
states.description: The list view writes each project's dates, length, progress, progress text and health and its dependencies.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no items the roadmap shows its toolbar and the chart header with no rows; show MonarchEmptyState instead when the app has nothing planned.

appearance: As MonarchGanttTimeline: on the surface colour with subtle lines, group headings on the subtle background. Bars are a light tint of the accent with the accent's solid fill as outline and progress strip; at-risk bars use the warning tone and off-track bars the danger tone. The second line of each heading (progress text, health, count) is in the muted text colour. Dark and both high-contrast themes swap in their own roles.
platformNotes: Matches Android's MonarchRoadmap names and options in Swift form: dates are Date values read as calendar days in the environment's calendar (Android uses UTC day keys, the web ISO strings), groupID instead of groupId, health cases in lower camel case, state is an optional Binding<MonarchGanttTimelineState> (nil keeps it inside, at the quarter zoom) instead of a remembered state object, the toolbar Boolean is showsToolbar, there is no timeZone parameter (the environment's timeZone is used) and no icon parameters (the toolbar arrows are SF Symbols from MonarchCalendarToolbar). The web shows health as a Badge with a dot next to the progress text; MonarchGanttTimeline takes its row meta as a plain String, so iOS, like Android, writes the progress text and the health word on one muted line ("8/20 · On track") with no dot or badge colour: the words carry the meaning, the bar tint repeats it. The web's hidden no-health dash becomes the visible words "No health reported" (.notReported), and the web's undefined versus null becomes nil (nothing written) versus .notReported. The item title is a plain label, not a view slot. Progress is 0 to 1 instead of 0 to 100, and onChange returns nothing (the web's promise and rollback become the app passing new items back). The web's accent tone is tone nil, because MonarchTone has no accent case; an app cannot force the accent colour on an at-risk or off-track project. defaultZoom becomes the state parameter. Everything else (sideways-only chart scrolling, touch and hold to drag, the list as the phone and VoiceOver alternative) is as described for gantt-timeline. Experimental because MonarchGanttTimeline is experimental and no Rook iOS app has adopted it; the API is plain public, not behind an SPI. Several closures are optional (onChange, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onChange.
accessibility: Each bar is one element read as "<project>, <start> to <end>, <n>% complete"; with onOpen it is a button with a touch area at least 44 points wide and as tall as the row.
Health is written as words ("On track", "At risk", "Off track", "No health reported") in the row heading, never shown by the bar colour alone.
A group heading has the header trait and reads its name, its project count and its health.
Without onChange bars have no VoiceOver actions; with onChange they offer the timeline's six move and resize actions (the drag equivalent) and every change is announced.
The chart and the list are containers named "Roadmap" for VoiceOver, and the row header says "Project", both replaceable through timelineLabels.
Project names stay at the leading edge in right-to-left layouts, and headings wrap at every Dynamic Type size without cutting text.
edgeCases: A project without dates stays in its group as a "No dates" row; a project with only one date is a one-day marker.
A group with no projects says "0 projects"; a groupID that matches no group puts the project after the groups.
Without progressText and health a project heading has no second line.
An explicit tone always wins over the health tint.
Callbacks receive the MonarchRoadmapItem value the app passed; with duplicate ids the first project is reported.
The roadmap maps the projects again on every render; the mapping is linear in the number of projects.

name: MonarchRolePicker
title: RolePicker
wrapsNative: MonarchRadioCardGroup (Buttons with a card ButtonStyle) for cards; Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) and selectionDisabled(_:) for compact
summary: Chooses a role for a person, with what each role can do in plain words, as radio cards or a compact menu picker. Roles that cannot be chosen stay visible with the reason.
whenToUse: In invite, member and sharing forms, where the person must understand what a role allows before choosing it.
whenNotToUse: Not for choices without descriptions (use a standard Picker) and not for several permissions at once (use a list of toggles).
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, selection: Binding<Value?>, roles: [MonarchRoleOption<Value>], helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, layout: MonarchRolePickerLayout = .cards, placeholder: String? = nil)
struct MonarchRoleOption<Value: Hashable> { init(_ value: Value, title: String, description: String? = nil, capabilities: [String] = [], isDisabled: Bool = false, disabledReason: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchRolePickerLayout { case cards, compact }

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the built-in label "Role".

options.name: selection
options.description: The value of the chosen role, or nil for no choice yet.

options.name: roles
options.description: The roles, from least to most access.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the control.

options.name: error
options.description: An error under the control, with an icon; replaces the helper text.

options.name: layout
options.description: cards shows every role with its description and capabilities; compact is a menu picker with the chosen role's description under it.

options.name: placeholder
options.description: Replaces the compact picker's built-in "Choose a role", shown while nothing is chosen.

states.name: selected
states.description: Cards: the radio card's filled mark and heavier border. Compact: the role's name in the picker and its description under it.

states.name: role disabled
states.description: The card is drawn in the disabled colours with the reason under the description; in the menu the row cannot be chosen and shows the reason.

states.name: error
states.description: The error text in the danger strong colour with an exclamation icon.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Apply disabled(_:) to disable every role.

appearance: The cards layout is MonarchRadioCardGroup and takes its colours. The compact layout is the system menu picker tinted with the default text role. Helper text uses the muted text role; errors the danger strong role.
platformNotes: The web's compact layout is a custom Select with descriptions in each option; iOS uses the system menu Picker, which shows the description as a subtitle where the system menu supports one, and the chosen role's description under the control. Capabilities are shown as lines of the card description, because MonarchRadioCardOption takes one description string. The web's required marker, invalid styling and form name have no iOS equivalent; validation is shown with error. The helper text is under the cards rather than under the label, because MonarchRadioCardGroup draws its own label.
accessibility: Cards: each role is a button named by its title, with the description, capabilities and reason as its value, and the selected trait when chosen.
The cards are a group named by the label.
Compact: the standard menu Picker named by the label; disabled roles cannot be chosen.
The error has an icon and text, so it does not depend on colour.
Every role card and the picker are at least 44 points high.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no role shows no card selected and the compact placeholder is not shown; keep the selection to a value in roles.
Long descriptions and many capabilities wrap inside the card.

appearance: The system sidebar list and navigation bar, Monarch switchers and avatar, and the system badge. The theme's accent tints selection. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow the system and the Monarch theme roles.
platformNotes: The web RookRail is a 48-point rail of icons that expands to labels, remembers its state in the rook_rail cookie shared across Rook apps, and becomes a top bar with a drawer below 768 px. iOS has no navigation drawer; its pattern for many destinations is a sidebar, so the recipe uses NavigationSplitView: on iPhone the sidebar is the root list and destinations push, on iPad it sits beside the content and collapses with the system button. Android uses a modal navigation drawer for the same role. The cookie and the expanded state do not apply: each app restores its own destination (for example with SceneStorage). Keyboard shortcuts and tooltips of the collapsed rail are not offered; VoiceOver reads each row's label. Links to Rook ID and other products leave the app, so the web's "opens in a new tab" becomes the hint "Opens in Rook ID". The web's theme toggle and notifications slots go into the account menu and the toolbar (the identity-bar recipe). Rook-specific: apps outside Rook use the app-shell recipe.
accessibility: The sidebar's navigation title names the app and is read first.
Each destination is a standard navigation row read as its label; the selected one has the selected trait.
The unread count is a system badge, text rather than a colour; check on a device that VoiceOver reads it with the row.
Workspace links have the hint "Opens in Rook ID" so leaving the app is not a surprise.
The account menu is named "Account menu for …" and its avatar is decorative.
Rows and buttons are at least 44 points; symbols in labels are decorative.
edgeCases: Long app or destination names truncate in the sidebar title and wrap in rows at the largest text sizes.
With no spaces, MonarchSpaceSwitcher hides itself.
Restore the selected destination when the app relaunches; the web's shared cookie has no iOS counterpart.
Many destinations: group them in Sections with headers instead of one long list.

title: RovingFocusGroup
wrapsNative: The system focus engine: @FocusState with focused(_:equals:), focusable(_:), and onKeyPress(_:action:) for arrow keys in a custom group
summary: Moving focus between the items of a toolbar, list or grid with a hardware keyboard is done by the system focus engine. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Nothing is needed for standard controls: with a keyboard, Tab (and the arrow keys under Full Keyboard Access) already moves between them. Use @FocusState to read or move focus in code, focusable() to let a custom view take focus, and onKeyPress to move focus with the arrow keys inside a group of custom views.
whenNotToUse: Do not add key handling to standard controls or build a roving tab index for them. Without a hardware keyboard none of this applies: touch and VoiceOver reach every element directly.
api: @FocusState var focused: Value?
func focused<Value: Hashable>(_ binding: FocusState<Value?>.Binding, equals value: Value) -> some View
func focusable(_ isFocusable: Bool = true) -> some View
func onKeyPress(_ key: KeyEquivalent, action: @escaping () -> KeyPress.Result) -> some View

states.name: focused
states.description: The system draws its focus indicator on the focused control. A custom view can use monarchFocusRing(_:in:) driven by @FocusState.

appearance: The system focus indicator in every theme. Monarch text fields, and custom views that use monarchFocusRing, draw the theme's focus ring.
platformNotes: The parity plan names focusSection() for this entry, but that modifier is unavailable on iOS (it exists on macOS and tvOS), so it is not used here. The web needs RovingFocusGroup and useRovingFocus because a browser puts every control in the Tab order and gives arrow keys no meaning. On iOS and iPadOS the focus engine and Full Keyboard Access move between standard controls; only a group of custom focusable views needs onKeyPress. The web's loop, columns and grid orientation options have no ready-made equivalent. Android's focus system plays the same role.
accessibility: System behaviour: with a hardware keyboard, Tab moves between the controls that take keyboard focus.
System behaviour: Full Keyboard Access reaches every control, including ones that do not take focus by default, and moves with the arrow keys.
VoiceOver and Switch Control do not use keyboard focus; they reach every element in reading order.
edgeCases: On iOS most buttons take keyboard focus only when Full Keyboard Access is on; text fields always do.
A view made focusable() must show that it has focus, for example with monarchFocusRing(_:in:).
onKeyPress reports physical keys: swap the left and right arrows when layoutDirection is rightToLeft, as the second example does.
onKeyPress is called only while the view, or a view inside it, has focus.

title: RowActionsMenu
wrapsNative: A ghost icon Button and a popover of text Buttons (a shortcut hint at the end of a row, a danger row after a MonarchDivider) with confirmationDialog for destructive items; Menu with Button items and .menuStyle(.button) remains the choice for the system menu
summary: The per-row actions of a list or table are the standard SwiftUI Menu behind a "⋯" button, swipe actions and a context menu, with destructive items last. Monarch ships nothing; the trigger takes the Monarch button style.
whenToUse: For the actions on one row, card or item: a "⋯" Menu that is always visible, swipeActions for the one or two most frequent actions on List rows, and contextMenu (press and hold) with the full set.
whenNotToUse: For actions on several selected rows, use MonarchBulkActionBar. For a single obvious action, put a button on the row. For screen-level actions, use the navigation bar's toolbar.

appearance: The menu, swipe buttons and context menu are drawn by the system in every theme and follow light, dark and Increase Contrast. The "⋯" trigger is a small ghost MonarchButtonStyle button. Swipe buttons take tint(_:) for a non-destructive colour; destructive ones are the system red.

On iOS the app lists the items in that order with a Divider before the destructive ones and presents confirmationDialog itself, so Monarch adds no type. iOS adds swipe actions and a context menu, which the web does not have; use the same items in all three. The web shortcut hint is keyboardShortcut on the Button, shown by the system with a hardware keyboard. Android plans a Compose recipe for the same menu.
accessibility: Name the icon-only trigger after the row ("Actions for Acme Ltd") with the Label's title, so rows are told apart.

System behaviour: destructive items are announced with their role, and the confirmation dialog takes focus.
The trigger keeps a 44-point touch target through MonarchButtonStyle.
edgeCases: Swipe actions only work on rows of a List; on other stacks use the "⋯" Menu and contextMenu.
Set allowsFullSwipe: false when the first swipe action is destructive and must be confirmed.

appearance: The navigation bar and toolbar are the system's; each part is a MonarchSectionCard on the card surface with its title and help text in the muted colour; problems use the danger tone with its icon. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the components' colour roles.
platformNotes: The web RuleBuilder is one form component with props for triggers, fields, action types, messages and an async onSubmit. On iOS it is a recipe of Monarch components on a full screen pushed or presented in a sheet, because a rule is a create-or-edit task with Save and Cancel in the navigation bar, and the app owns the rule's model and storage. Like the web, the problem summary takes focus when saving is blocked: the banner is one element with accessibilityFocused, set in the update after it appears. The web single-trigger mode is a Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) in place of the checkboxes. There is no Android entry yet.
accessibility: Cancel and Save rule are the navigation bar's cancellation and confirmation actions, with 44-point targets.
Each section card's title is a heading, so the VoiceOver rotor moves between When, If, Then and Options.
Trigger checkboxes are toggles read with their label and checked state.
The condition and action editors keep their own accessibility: named rows, announced removals and reorder actions without dragging.
When saving is blocked VoiceOver moves to the problem summary, which reads all problems as one message, and each is also text next to its part, not only colour.
edgeCases: Compute the problems from the same state that is saved, so the banner and the per-part errors agree.
Keep showsErrors false until the first save, so a new rule does not open full of errors.
Ignore a second Save while the first is still saving.

whenNotToUse: Not for a countdown to a deadline; use MonarchSlaIndicator. Not for a static duration; use Text with Duration formatting. Not for showing the timer outside the app; that is a Live Activity in the product.

init(startedAt: Date?, label: String? = nil, variant: MonarchRunningTimerVariant = .panel, warnAfter: TimeInterval? = 12 * 3600, isStartDisabled: Bool = false, isPending: Bool = false, showsWhenStopped: Bool = false, now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchRunningTimerLabels = MonarchRunningTimerLabels(), onStart: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onStop: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onStopAt: (@MainActor (Date) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onDiscard: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onOpen: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) where Fields == EmptyView
enum MonarchRunningTimerVariant { case panel, indicator }

struct MonarchRunningTimerLabels { init(start:stop:stopAndLog:moreActions:discard:discardTitle:discardMessage:discardConfirm:stoppedEarlier:stoppedEarlierTitle:stoppedEarlierMessage:stoppedAt:started:workDuration:save:cancel:stoppedAtFuture:stoppedAtTooEarly:failed:running:stopped:defaultLabel:longRunning:openHint:), every parameter optional; started, workDuration and longRunning are (@Sendable (String) -> String)? }

options.name: startedAt
options.description: When the running timer started; nil when no timer runs. The app changes it when an action succeeds.

options.name: label
options.description: What is being timed, such as an issue key. Shown under the panel's clock and in the indicator ("Timer" when nil). The indicator drops it when the chip does not fit.

options.name: variant
options.description: panel: a large clock with buttons and fields. indicator: a compact chip with a stop button and a menu.

options.name: warnAfter
options.description: Shows a warning once the timer has run this many seconds: a message on the panel, warning colours and a warning icon on the indicator. nil turns it off.

options.name: isStartDisabled
options.description: Starting is not allowed yet, for example until a required project is chosen.

options.name: isPending
options.description: An action runs outside the component: Start shows a spinner and the other buttons are disabled.

options.name: showsWhenStopped
options.description: Keeps the indicator visible, at 0:00:00, while no timer runs. Otherwise the indicator draws nothing while stopped.

options.name: now
options.description: A fixed reference time, which also stops the clock. For previews, snapshots and tests.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onStart
options.description: Starts a timer. Adds Start to the stopped panel. The button shows a spinner until it returns; a thrown error is shown.

options.name: onStop
options.description: Stops the timer and logs the time. Adds Stop to the panel and the stop button to the indicator.

options.name: onStopAt
options.description: Stops the timer at an earlier time. Adds "I stopped earlier", which opens a sheet with a date and time picker between the start and now.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: Throws the running time away. Adds Discard (an icon button on the panel, a menu item on the indicator), confirmed by an alert first.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Opens what is being timed. Makes the indicator's clock a button.

options.name: fields
options.description: Fields for the entry being timed, such as a project picker. Shown in the panel between the clock and the buttons.

states.name: stopped
states.description: The panel shows 0:00:00 in the muted text colour and Start; the indicator is hidden unless showsWhenStopped.

states.name: running
states.description: The clock ticks every second in the strong accent colour; the panel shows Stop, "I stopped earlier" and Discard; the indicator has the accent surface.

states.name: long running
states.description: After warnAfter the panel shows a warning message with a triangle icon; the indicator takes the warning colours and the triangle icon.

states.name: busy
states.description: The button of the action in progress shows a spinner and the others are disabled; isPending shows the same from outside.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error appears under the buttons (panel) or turns the indicator to the danger colours with an exclamation icon, and is announced.

states.name: start disabled
states.description: Start is disabled until isStartDisabled is false.

appearance: The panel is a surface card with the subtle border; the clock is the title type role with tabular digits, in the strong accent colour while running and the muted text colour while stopped. The indicator is a control-shaped chip: the accent subtle fill, border and strong text while running, the warning roles when long running, the danger roles after a failure and the surface fill with the default border while stopped. All colours are theme roles, so the dark and high-contrast themes need nothing else.
platformNotes: The parity map named Text(timerInterval:). The timer uses TimelineView with a per-second schedule instead, so the clock reads 0:04:09 on every platform (Text(timerInterval:) writes 4:09 and gives no hook for the long-running warning or the spoken time). The web's datetime-local input is a DatePicker limited to the range between the start and now, so the web's "required" and "invalid" errors cannot happen; the future and too-early checks remain. The web's description hover text is not offered: iOS has no hover on touch. The web shows the clock in the monospaced family; here it uses tabular digits of the text face. The indicator drops the label when it does not fit (the web hides it below 30rem). Showing the timer outside the app (Live Activity, ongoing notification) stays in the product. Several closures are optional (onStart, onStop, onStopAt, onDiscard, onOpen). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onStart.
accessibility: The clock is one element: its label is the timer's label and the time in words ("ENG-142, 4 minutes, 9 seconds"); its value is the state ("Timer running" or "Timer stopped") and a failure if there is one; it has the updatesFrequently trait.
Starting and stopping are announced; the ticking is not.
With onOpen the indicator's clock is a button with the hint "Opens what is being timed.".
The indicator's stop button is named "Stop timer and log time" and its menu button "More timer actions"; each has a 44-point touch target.
The panel's Discard is an icon button whose name is "Discard without logging".
Failures are shown as text with an icon and announced; the long-running warning is text with an icon, not colour alone.
The earlier-stop sheet has a heading, a standard DatePicker, and the length of work that will be saved as text.
edgeCases: A start in the future shows 0:00:00.
Times of 100 hours and more widen the clock (100:00:00).
When startedAt becomes nil the discard confirmation and the earlier-stop sheet close.
The earlier-stop sheet suggests one hour after the start, or now if that is sooner; Save is disabled for a time less than a minute after the start.
The sheet cannot be dismissed while it saves.
With now set the clock does not tick.

name: MonarchSaveStatusIndicator
title: SaveStatusIndicator
wrapsNative: Label with a ProgressView or SF Symbol icon, in TimelineView(.everyMinute), and MonarchButton for retry
summary: A small inline status for saving: "Unsaved changes", "Saving…", "Saved · 2 minutes ago" or "Couldn't save" with a retry button.
whenToUse: In an editor's toolbar or next to a form's buttons, wherever edits are saved in the background.
whenNotToUse: For the freshness of data the app fetched, use MonarchFreshnessIndicator. For a one-off confirmation after a button press, use a toast.
api: init(_ status: MonarchSaveStatus, savedAt: Date? = nil, errorMessage: String? = nil, announcesSaving: Bool = false, labels: MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels = MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchSaveStatus { case idle, unsaved, saving, saved, error }
struct MonarchSaveStatusIndicatorLabels { var unsaved, saving, saved, error, retry: String? }

options.name: status
options.description: idle (nothing drawn), unsaved, saving, saved or error.

options.name: savedAt
options.description: When the last save finished; shown as relative time after "Saved".

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Replaces "Couldn't save" with the reason.

options.name: announcesSaving
options.description: Also announces "Saving…". Off by default so autosaves stay quiet.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry button to the error status.

states.name: idle
states.description: Nothing is drawn.

states.name: unsaved
states.description: A small dot in the warning colour and "Unsaved changes".

states.name: saving
states.description: A small system spinner and "Saving…".

states.name: saved
states.description: A check mark in the success colour, "Saved" and the relative time.

states.name: error
states.description: A warning triangle and the text in the danger colour, with a retry button when onRetry is given.

appearance: Caption text in the muted text colour. Icons take the strong colour of their meaning: warning for unsaved, success for saved, danger for error, where the text is also in the danger colour.
platformNotes: The web announces through a polite live region; iOS posts an announcement, which VoiceOver may speak over other speech. Android shares the name and the statuses.
accessibility: The icon and words are a standard Label, read with the time as one element; the icon is decorative and the words carry the meaning.
When the status turns saved or error, the outcome is announced; saving is announced only with announcesSaving.
The retry button is a separate standard button with a 44-point touch target.
Text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: The relative time is redrawn every minute.
The same outcome twice in a row (saved, then saved again) is not announced again, because the status did not change; set the status to saving in between.
An empty errorMessage falls back to "Couldn't save".

name: MonarchSavedViews
title: SavedViews
wrapsNative: Menu with buttonStyle(.monarch()), Section per group of Toggle items, action Buttons, alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:) with a TextField for naming and with a destructive Button for deleting
summary: A menu button that switches between named views of a list (filters, sort and columns), with an Edited marker and actions to save, save as new, discard, rename, set the default and delete.
whenToUse: Above a list, table or board where people keep named combinations of filters and sort, and come back to them.
whenNotToUse: For a few fixed filters use MonarchTabs or a segmented Picker; for one filter use a Menu with a Picker (see dropdown-menu). For switching between list and grid layouts see view-switcher.
api: MonarchSavedViews.init(_ views: [MonarchSavedView], selection: Binding<String?>, isModified: Bool = false, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, maxNameLength: Int = 80, labels: MonarchSavedViewsLabels = MonarchSavedViewsLabels(), onSaveNew: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onSaveChanges: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onDiscardChanges: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRename: (@MainActor (String, String) -> Void)? = nil, onDelete: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onSetDefault: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchSavedView.init(_ name: String, id: String, count: Int? = nil, isShared: Bool = false, isDefault: Bool = false, isReadOnly: Bool = false, group: String? = nil)

MonarchSavedViewsLabels.init(view:noView:modified:shared:isDefault:views:saveChanges:saveAsNew:discardChanges:rename:setDefault:delete:saveTitle:renameTitle:name:save:cancel:nameRequired:nameTaken:deleteTitle:deleteMessage:deleteConfirm:), every parameter optional

options.name: views
options.description: The views in menu order, each with a name, an id and optionally a count, isShared, isDefault, isReadOnly and a group.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the selected view, or nil for none (the button then reads "All items").

options.name: isModified
options.description: Whether the current filters differ from the selected view. Shows an Edited badge and offers to save or discard.

options.name: size
options.description: The size of the menu button. The web's xs is sm; the touch target is 44 points at every size.

options.name: maxNameLength
options.description: The longest name the naming field accepts.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the menu items, the alert titles, the validation messages and the delete confirmation.

options.name: onSaveNew
options.description: Stores the current state under the new, trimmed name and selects it. Offers Save as new view….

options.name: onSaveChanges
options.description: Saves the current state into the selected view. Offered when modified and not read-only.

options.name: onDiscardChanges
options.description: Reapplies the selected view. Offered when modified.

options.name: onRename
options.description: Renames the view with the id to the new name. Offered for a selected view that is not read-only.

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Deletes the view with the id after the person confirms. Offered for a selected view that is not read-only.

options.name: onSetDefault
options.description: Makes the view with the id open by default. Offered for a selected view that is not already the default.

states.name: selected
states.description: The button shows the view's name with a chevron; in the menu the view's toggle is on.

states.name: edited
states.description: A warning badge reading "Edited" after the name, and Save changes and Discard changes in the menu.

states.name: none selected
states.description: The button reads "All items".

states.name: read-only
states.description: Save changes, Rename and Delete are not offered.

states.name: naming
states.description: An alert with a Name field; Save stays disabled while the name is empty or used by another view (ignoring case and spaces).

states.name: deleting
states.description: An alert titled "Delete “Open deals”?" with a destructive Delete view and Cancel.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the menu gives the button its disabled colours and it does not open.

appearance: The button is a secondary Monarch button; the Edited marker is a warning badge. The menu and alerts are the system's, drawn in every theme; destructive items are the system's red.
platformNotes: The web SavedViews keeps the naming and delete dialogs open while a returned promise is pending and shows a save failure inside them. System alerts close when a button is tapped, so the callbacks are synchronous: the app saves afterwards and reports a failure itself (for example with MonarchToast). The validation message is the alert's message; the system may not refresh it while the alert is open, but Save is disabled whenever the name is not valid. The web's visually hidden "View:" prefix is the button's accessibility label "View". Android builds the same component with the same name. Several closures are optional (onSaveNew, onSaveChanges, onDiscardChanges, onRename, onDelete, onSetDefault). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onSaveNew.
accessibility: The menu button is named "View" and its value is the selected view's name followed by "Edited" when modified.
Edited is a word in a badge, not only a colour.
In the menu each view is a Toggle, so VoiceOver reads whether it is selected; its count, Shared and Default view are read as its second line.
Groups are menu sections with their heading.
The naming and delete steps are system alerts with a cancel button; the escape gesture cancels.
The button has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points and its text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Only actions with a callback are offered; with no callbacks the menu only switches views.
Names are trimmed before they are passed to onSaveNew and onRename, and cut to maxNameLength while typing.
Renaming a view to its own name, in another case, is allowed.
A long view name stays on one line in the button; give the button room or keep names short.

name: MonarchSavingsPanel
title: SavingsPanel
wrapsNative: MonarchSectionCard with Text, MonarchFlowLayout of MonarchStatusBadge chips, a VStack of item rows (MonarchMoney, MonarchStatusBadge, Date.FormatStyle), Button with a plain style for chips and rows
summary: What unused items cost to keep: a headline with the count and renewal cost per currency, the reasons they count as unused, the decisions made so far, what letting them lapse would save, and the top items.
whenToUse: On a billing or asset overview, to show what renewing unused things (domains, licences, seats) would cost and what has been decided about them, with a way into each group and item.
whenNotToUse: For a list of upcoming renewals with owners and next steps use MonarchRenewalsPanel. For a single KPI use MonarchStatCard.
api: init(unusedCount: Int, costs: [MonarchSavingsAmount] = [], unpricedCount: Int = 0, categories: [MonarchSavingsCategory] = [], decisions: [MonarchSavingsDecisionCount] = [], potentialSavings: [MonarchSavingsAmount] = [], items: [MonarchSavingsItem] = [], maxItems: Int = 6, registry: MonarchStatusRegistry? = nil, title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, locale: Locale? = nil, calendar: Calendar? = nil, isLoading: Bool = false, errorMessage: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, labels: MonarchSavingsPanelLabels = MonarchSavingsPanelLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onCategorySelect: (@MainActor (MonarchSavingsCategory) -> Void)? = nil, onItemSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchSavingsItem) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions)

init(unusedCount: Int, costs: [MonarchSavingsAmount] = [], unpricedCount: Int = 0, categories: [MonarchSavingsCategory] = [], decisions: [MonarchSavingsDecisionCount] = [], potentialSavings: [MonarchSavingsAmount] = [], items: [MonarchSavingsItem] = [], maxItems: Int = 6, registry: MonarchStatusRegistry? = nil, title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, locale: Locale? = nil, calendar: Calendar? = nil, isLoading: Bool = false, errorMessage: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, labels: MonarchSavingsPanelLabels = MonarchSavingsPanelLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onCategorySelect: (@MainActor (MonarchSavingsCategory) -> Void)? = nil, onItemSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchSavingsItem) -> Void)? = nil) where Actions == EmptyView
struct MonarchSavingsAmount { init(_ amount: Decimal, currencyCode: String) }
struct MonarchSavingsCategory { init(id: String, count: Int, label: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchSavingsDecisionCount { init(id: String, label: String, count: Int) }
struct MonarchSavingsItem { init(id: String, name: String, category: String? = nil, date: Date? = nil, amount: MonarchSavingsAmount? = nil, isUnpriced: Bool = false, decision: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchSavingsPanelLabels { init(title:, headline:, categories:, decisions:, potentialSavings:, items:, more:, unpriced:, emptyTitle:, emptyMessage:, errorTitle:, loading:) }

options.name: unusedCount
options.description: How many items are unused. Zero shows the empty state.

options.name: costs
options.description: The renewal cost of the unused items, one amount per currency, joined with + in the headline. Never converted or added across currencies.

options.name: unpricedCount
options.description: Unused items without a price; counted in the headline, never estimated.

options.name: categories
options.description: The unused items grouped by reason, shown as badges with counts. Groups with no items are hidden.

options.name: decisions
options.description: How many items have each decision, on one line.

options.name: potentialSavings
options.description: What letting the marked items lapse would save, one amount per currency.

options.name: items
options.description: The unused items to list, most urgent first.

options.name: maxItems
options.description: Lists at most this many items, then "and <n> more".

options.name: registry
options.description: Statuses for the category and decision badges, looked up before those installed with monarchStatusRegistry(_:).

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title Savings.

options.name: description
options.description: A line under the title.

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of amounts and dates. Default: the environment's.

options.name: calendar
options.description: The calendar and time zone of dates. Default: the environment's calendar in the environment's time zone.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows skeleton rows.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Shows the error state with this message.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Shows Try again busy.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Retries loading. Shows Try again in the error state.

options.name: onCategorySelect
options.description: Opens the items of a category. Makes each category a button.

options.name: onItemSelect
options.description: Opens an item. Makes each item a button with a chevron.

options.name: actions
options.description: Buttons or a menu at the trailing edge of the header, such as Review all.

states.name: summary
states.description: The headline, categories, decisions, potential savings and items, each shown only when given.

states.name: shortened
states.description: More items than maxItems: the first ones and "and <n> more".

states.name: loading
states.description: The section card's skeleton rows, read as Loading savings.

states.name: empty
states.description: unusedCount of zero: a small MonarchEmptyState, Nothing unused.

states.name: error
states.description: A small MonarchErrorState with the message and Try again when onRetry is given.

appearance: A MonarchSectionCard. The headline is in the subheading style, categories are small MonarchStatusBadges with a count, decisions a muted label line, potential savings strong body text in the strong success colour, and items have the name in the strong body style with outlined category badges, a muted date, the amount and a decision badge. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web's category and item links (href with renderLink) become onCategorySelect and onItemSelect, which the app uses to push a filtered list or the item's screen. The web's emptyIcon is the empty state's own symbol here, and its minorUnits flag is not offered (pass major units as Decimal, as MonarchMoney does). The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent. The parity map names List rows; the rows are a VStack inside the card because the panel sits in the app's own scrolling screen. Android builds the same component, with an emptyIcon slot. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onCategorySelect, onItemSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title has the header trait (from MonarchSectionCard).
Each category is one element read as its label and count; with onCategorySelect it is a button with a 44-point touch target.
The decision line is read with the prefix Decisions.
Each item is one element whose label is its name and whose value is its category, date, amount and decision, built by a tested pure function; with onItemSelect it is a button.
Badges have words and icons, so categories and decisions never depend on colour.
edgeCases: Costs in several currencies are joined with +, never converted or summed.
An item with isUnpriced shows No price; an item with neither an amount nor isUnpriced shows no amount.
Categories with a count of zero are hidden.
A negative maxItems lists no items and counts them all as more.

name: MonarchSchemaDrivenForm
title: SchemaDrivenForm
wrapsNative: Form with .formStyle(.grouped) of MonarchFieldRenderer rows in Section groups, inside ScrollViewReader; FocusState and AccessibilityFocusState for the first invalid question; ToolbarItem(placement: .confirmationAction / .cancellationAction), confirmationDialog and interactiveDismissDisabled for edit forms; LabeledContent with .labeledContentStyle(.monarch) when read only
summary: A form generated from a list of question definitions: the right input for each question, sections and conditional questions, validation, and a Save button that shows progress and errors.
whenToUse: For forms whose questions are data: admin-authored intake forms, settings defined on the server, surveys and applications. The same MonarchFormFieldDefinition values drive MonarchFieldRenderer and the form builder's preview.
whenNotToUse: For a fixed form known at build time, compose a Form of MonarchTextField, Picker and the other inputs directly, which allows custom layout. For a single question, use MonarchFieldRenderer.
api: init(_ fields: [MonarchFormFieldDefinition], values: Binding<[String: MonarchFormFieldValue]>, validateOn: MonarchSchemaDrivenFormValidateOn = .blur, isReadOnly: Bool = false, isDirty: Bool? = nil, errors: [String: String] = [:], labels: MonarchSchemaDrivenFormLabels = MonarchSchemaDrivenFormLabels(), onSubmit: (@MainActor ([String: MonarchFormFieldValue]) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onDiscard: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchSchemaDrivenFormValidateOn: Hashable, Sendable, CaseIterable { case blur, submit }

struct MonarchSchemaDrivenFormLabels: Sendable { init(submit: String? = nil, submitFailed: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil, saving: String? = nil, discard: String? = nil, discardTitle: String? = nil, discardMessage: String? = nil, discardConfirm: String? = nil, keepEditing: String? = nil, fields: MonarchFieldRendererLabels = MonarchFieldRendererLabels()) }

enum MonarchSchemaDrivenFormDefaults { static func visibleFields(_ fields: [MonarchFormFieldDefinition], values: [String: MonarchFormFieldValue], calendar: Calendar = .current) -> [MonarchFormFieldDefinition]; static func problems(_ fields: [MonarchFormFieldDefinition], values: [String: MonarchFormFieldValue], calendar: Calendar = .current) -> [String: MonarchFormFieldProblem]; static func submittedValues(_ fields: [MonarchFormFieldDefinition], values: [String: MonarchFormFieldValue], calendar: Calendar = .current) -> [String: MonarchFormFieldValue] }

options.name: fields
options.description: The questions and section headings, in order. A section question starts a Section that lasts until the next one.

options.name: values
options.description: The answers keyed by question id; a missing key is no answer, and clearing an answer removes its key.

options.name: validateOn
options.description: .blur shows a typed question's error once the person leaves it and a choice's once it is answered; .submit waits for a submit attempt.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the shown answers as LabeledContent rows instead of inputs.

options.name: isDirty
options.description: nil puts the Save button after the questions; a value makes Save (and Discard with onDiscard) navigation bar buttons, Save enabled while true, and stops the sheet from being swiped away while true.

options.name: errors
options.description: Messages from the app, such as the server's, keyed by question id; shown at once, in place of the question's own error.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for Save, the failure message, what VoiceOver reads for an unanswered question in the read-only view, the discard confirmation, and the questions' strings.

options.name: onSubmit
options.description: Receives the shown answers once they are valid; without it there is no Save button. Throw to show the error's description in a danger banner. A trailing closure is this parameter.

options.name: onDiscard
options.description: With isDirty, shows Discard in the navigation bar; it asks for confirmation, then calls this.

states.name: editing
states.description: Each shown question with its input, label, help and required mark; no errors until validateOn says.

states.name: invalid
states.description: After a submit attempt, every invalid question shows its message; the form scrolls to the first one and moves VoiceOver focus, and keyboard focus for a typed question, to it.

states.name: submitting
states.description: Save shows the MonarchButton loading state (or a progress indicator named Saving in the navigation bar) and the questions are disabled until onSubmit returns.

states.name: failed
states.description: onSubmit threw: its description, or The form could not be saved. Try again., in a danger MonarchBanner after the questions, announced to VoiceOver.

states.name: dirty
states.description: With isDirty, Save is enabled in the navigation bar while true; Discard asks Discard unsaved changes? before calling onDiscard.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(true): inputs, Save and Discard are disabled.

states.name: read only
states.description: The shown answers as LabeledContent rows: option labels, Yes or No, an abbreviated date, a locale number and file names, joined as a locale list; an unanswered question shows a dash, read as Not set.

appearance: A grouped system Form with the canvas background role behind the sections and the surface role on each row. Questions take the roles of the inputs MonarchFieldRenderer chooses; section headings use the subheading text style and default text role, their help the caption style and muted text role. Save is a full-width primary MonarchButton and a failure a danger MonarchBanner. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's SchemaDrivenForm has its own field schema (text, textarea, number, select, checkbox, switch, date) with regular-expression patterns, custom validate functions and nested section objects. iOS, like Android, renders the MonarchFormFieldDefinition schema that MonarchFieldRenderer and the form builder use, so it covers more types (email, phone, web address, time, radio, checkboxes, multi-select, yes or no, consent, rating, file) and their rules; there is no pattern or validate function: the app adds its own checks through errors. Sections are section questions in the flat list, shown as system Form sections with the heading as the header, and conditions are MonarchCondition values. Differences from Android, in Swift idiom: values is a Binding instead of values plus onValuesChange (so the changed question id is not passed; use onChange), enabled is the disabled(_:) modifier, the answers dictionary has no nil values (no key means no answer, and submittedValues leaves unanswered questions out instead of mapping them to null), onSubmit is an async throwing closure, and readOnly, dirty are isReadOnly, isDirty. Android's state, contentPadding and locale parameters are not offered: the system Form scrolls itself, and the locale, calendar and time zone come from the environment. Android's secondaryActions are not offered: Cancel and other actions belong in the navigation bar, where the app adds them with toolbar. Android pins a MonarchFormActionsBar under the questions with dirty; iOS has no such bar (form-actions-bar is native on iOS) and puts Save and Discard in the navigation bar, so the form must be in a NavigationStack in that mode. Touch has no blur: a typed question counts as left when keyboard focus moves away or another question is answered. Several closures are optional (onSubmit, onDiscard). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onSubmit.
accessibility: Each question keeps the semantics of MonarchFieldRenderer: the label names the input, the required mark and help are its hint, and a new error is announced.
Section headings have the header trait.
An invalid submit scrolls to the first invalid question and moves VoiceOver focus to it with AccessibilityFocusState; a typed question also takes keyboard focus.
A failed submit posts its message as an accessibility announcement and stays visible in a danger MonarchBanner, whose tone is spoken.
While saving, the Save MonarchButton shows its loading state; in the navigation bar a ProgressView named Saving replaces Save, and the questions are disabled.
In the read-only view an unanswered question shows a dash that VoiceOver reads as Not set.
Save has a 44-point touch target and wraps at the largest text sizes.
edgeCases: Hidden questions, and every question of a hidden section, are neither validated nor submitted; their answers stay in values.
errors win over the question's own message and show before any submit attempt; they do not block Save, which only checks the questions' own rules.
A question with isReadOnly keeps a readable text field; other read-only questions are disabled, as in MonarchFieldRenderer.
onSubmit = nil shows no Save button; MonarchSchemaDrivenFormDefaults.problems and submittedValues let the app submit from its own button.
The form is a scrolling Form: give it the screen or a bounded height and do not put it in a ScrollView.
A section heading with no shown questions still shows its header; a form with no questions is an empty Form with only Save.
With isDirty, Save and Discard appear only inside a NavigationStack, because they are toolbar items.

name: MonarchScopeSelector
title: ScopeSelector
wrapsNative: DisclosureGroup(isExpanded:content:label:) with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) per resource, Toggle(sources:isOn:label:) for select all and Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) per scope; a Button with buttonStyle(.monarch(.ghost)) pages the groups
summary: Chooses the scopes (permissions) to grant, grouped by resource such as an API, with a per-group count, select all, loading groups, paging and optional auto-selection.
whenToUse: When creating or editing an API key, an OAuth app or an integration grant that is limited to a set of scopes.
whenNotToUse: For a short flat list of choices use MonarchCheckboxGroup; for role-based access (viewer, editor, admin) use a Picker; for an AI assistant's permissions see ai-permission-scope.
api: MonarchScopeSelector.init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<Set<String>>, groups: [MonarchScopeGroup], initiallyExpanded: Set<String> = [], isLabelHidden: Bool = false, isReadOnly: Bool = false, pageSize: Int = 10, autoSelect: MonarchScopeSelectorAutoSelect? = nil, labels: MonarchScopeSelectorLabels = MonarchScopeSelectorLabels())
MonarchScopeGroup.init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, scopes: [MonarchScopeOption], isLoading: Bool = false, emptyMessage: String? = nil)
MonarchScopeOption.init(_ value: String, label: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, isDisabled: Bool = false)
enum MonarchScopeSelectorAutoSelect { case all, added }
MonarchScopeSelectorLabels.init(empty:loading:noScopes:count:selectAll:showMore:), every parameter optional

options.name: label
options.description: The visible title, such as "Scopes". It also names the selector for VoiceOver.

options.name: selection
options.description: The selected scope strings.

options.name: groups
options.description: The resources in order, each with a name, an optional description and symbol, its scopes, a loading flag and an empty message.

options.name: initiallyExpanded
options.description: The ids of the groups open at first. Pass every id to open them all.

options.name: isLabelHidden
options.description: Hides the title; VoiceOver still reads it as the container's name.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Disables every checkbox and hides select all; the groups still open so the grant can be reviewed.

options.name: pageSize
options.description: How many groups show before "Show 10 more of 25", and how many each tap adds.

options.name: autoSelect
options.description: .all selects every enabled scope of each group that loads with none selected, once per group; .added does it only for groups added after the selector appears.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the empty message, Loading scopes…, No scopes available., the count, Select all and Show more.

states.name: collapsed
states.description: A group shows its name, description and "0 of 2 scopes".

states.name: expanded
states.description: Select all (checked, mixed or clear) above the indented scope checkboxes, each with its description.

states.name: granted
states.description: A group with selected scopes shows its count in the accent colour.

states.name: loading
states.description: The summary reads "Loading scopes…" and the content is a progress indicator.

states.name: no scopes
states.description: The summary reads "No scopes available." or the group's emptyMessage, and the group has no content.

states.name: empty
states.description: With no groups, "There are no scopes to choose from."

states.name: read only
states.description: Checkboxes are disabled and select all is hidden; groups still open.

states.name: paged
states.description: Past pageSize, a Show 10 more of 25 button adds the next page.

appearance: Groups are separated by dividers; names use the default text role, descriptions the muted role, scope strings the code font, and a granted group's count the accent strong role. Checkboxes use the Monarch checkbox style in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ScopeSelector puts Select all / Clear all as a button on each group header, so a group can be granted without opening it, and moves focus to the first new group after Show more. On iOS select all is the system's Toggle(sources:) inside the open group, with the system's mixed state, and focus after paging is left to VoiceOver. The web's emptyState slot is the empty text here; use the labels to change it. Group icons are SF Symbols. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: The selector is a container named by its label; the visible label has the header trait.
Each group header is one button that reads the name, the description, the summary ("1 of 2 scopes") and Expanded or Collapsed. The symbol is decorative.
Select all is a checkbox whose value is on, off or mixed.
Each scope is a checkbox read with its label, or its scope string, and its description.
A loading group's progress indicator is named "Loading scopes…".
Every checkbox and button has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points and the text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Auto-selection runs once per group id, only after the group has loaded and only when none of its scopes is selected; clearing them later is respected.
Disabled scopes keep their state; select all skips them.
Selected values not in any group are kept in the selection.
Long API names and scope strings wrap at the largest text sizes.

name: MonarchScoreRing
title: ScoreRing
wrapsNative: ProgressView(value:total:) with a private ProgressViewStyle that draws the ring and the number
summary: A circular score: a ring filled to the score with the number written in the middle, coloured by the band the score falls in.
whenToUse: For a score out of a fixed maximum that people compare to good and bad bands: profile strength, SEO score, health score.
whenNotToUse: For progress of a task, use ProgressView with the monarchCircular style. For a value on a range without a score, use MonarchGauge.
api: init(_ label: String? = nil, value: Double?, max: Double = 100, description: String? = nil, color: MonarchScoreRingColor = .auto, thresholds: [MonarchScoreRingThreshold] = MonarchScoreRingThreshold.defaults, size: MonarchScoreRingSize = .md, showsMax: Bool? = nil, format: (@Sendable (Double) -> String)? = nil, labels: MonarchScoreRingLabels = MonarchScoreRingLabels())
enum MonarchScoreRingColor { case auto, accent, tone(MonarchTone) }
enum MonarchScoreRingSize { case sm, md, lg }
struct MonarchScoreRingThreshold { init(minimum: Double, tone: MonarchTone); static let defaults: [MonarchScoreRingThreshold] }
struct MonarchScoreRingLabels { var name: String?; var valueText: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)?; var ofMax: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var noValue: String? }

options.name: label
options.description: Shown under the ring and read as its name.

options.name: value
options.description: The score. nil shows an empty ring and a dash. Limited to 0 through max.

options.name: max
options.description: The top of the scale. Zero, negative or infinite values fall back to 100.

options.name: description
options.description: A second line under the label.

options.name: color
options.description: auto takes the tone of the band; accent is the brand colour for a score with no good or bad meaning; tone(_) is fixed.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: The bands auto uses: 80 success, 60 info, 40 warning, below 40 danger.

options.name: size
options.description: sm 48, md 80, lg 120 points before Dynamic Type.

options.name: showsMax
options.description: Shows "/ 100" under the number. By default on md and lg.

options.name: format
options.description: Formats the number in the middle and in the spoken value. By default a whole number in the current locale.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Score", "78 out of 100", "/ 100" and "No score yet".

states.name: no score
states.description: An empty track and a dash in the middle; read as "No score yet".

states.name: zero
states.description: An empty track and the number 0.

states.name: full
states.description: A closed ring.

appearance: The track is the muted background colour; the arc is the solid colour of the band's tone, the solid accent, or the muted text colour for the neutral tone. The number is the default text colour and "/ 100" and the description are muted.
platformNotes: The web takes the diameter and the stroke width in pixels; here three sizes keep the ring on the spacing scale, and the ring scales with Dynamic Type. The web's accent tone is the accent case of MonarchScoreRingColor, because MonarchTone has no accent case. Android shares the name and the options.
accessibility: The ring and the label are one element, named by the label or "Score", with the value "78 out of 100" or "No score yet".
The score is always written as a number, so the band colour is never the only signal.
The description is separate static text.
The ring scales with Dynamic Type and the number shrinks to stay inside it.
edgeCases: Scores above max are shown as max, below zero as zero; not-a-number counts as no score.
A label longer than the ring wraps and is centred under it.
The arc starts at the top. Its direction in right-to-left layouts follows SwiftUI's handling of the Circle shape and has not been checked on a device.

states.name: fit
states.description: The whole picture fits a 16 by 9 area; Zoom out and Fit are disabled.

states.name: zoomed
states.description: The picture is larger than the area and pans by dragging; the level is shown as a percentage.

states.name: waiting
states.description: "Waiting for the shared screen…" on the muted background.

states.name: local, preview hidden
states.description: A notice with a "Show preview" button replaces the picture.

states.name: picture in picture active
states.description: The button shows the exit symbol, is named "Exit picture in picture" and has the selected trait.

appearance: The picture sits on the inverse background colour with 12-point corners; the waiting text and the notice sit on the muted background. Controls are ghost buttons; Stop sharing is a danger button.
platformNotes: The web takes a MediaStream and starts browser picture in picture and full screen itself. On iOS the picture is a slot for the call SDK's view, and picture in picture (AVPictureInPictureController needs the video layer) and full screen (a presentation) are started by the product through onPictureInPicture and onFullScreen; the view only shows the buttons and their state. Zoom adds pinch and double tap to the web's buttons, and steps through the same levels: 100%, 150%, 200%, 300%. The web keyboard shortcuts (+, -, 0) are not offered.
accessibility: The picture is one element named "Screen shared by …" with the image trait and the zoom level as its value.
The picture responds to the VoiceOver zoom gesture and to swipe up and down, which step through the zoom levels.
The controls are a group named "Shared screen controls"; icon buttons have spoken names and 44-point touch targets.
A zoom level chosen with a button is announced.
The picture-in-picture button has the selected trait while active.
The content of the shared screen is not described.
edgeCases: Pinching does not keep the point under the fingers in place; the scroll position is kept.
A zoom binding outside 1 to 3 is clamped.
When the controls do not fit one row they wrap to two, below the presenter line.
With isLocal and isWaiting the notice has no "Show preview" button.
VoiceOver cannot pan the zoomed picture.

title: ScrollArea
wrapsNative: ScrollView with scrollIndicators(_:axes:) and scrollBounceBehavior(_:axes:)
summary: The standard SwiftUI ScrollView. The system draws the scroll indicators in every theme. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For a panel, a log or a row of items that scrolls inside a screen. Set a height or a maximum height on it, and use scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize) so short content does not move.
whenNotToUse: For a whole screen of rows use List, which scrolls itself and reuses rows. Do not put a vertical ScrollView inside another vertical ScrollView.
api: ScrollView(_ axes: Axis.Set = .vertical, content: () -> Content)
func scrollIndicators(_ visibility: ScrollIndicatorVisibility, axes: Axis.Set = [.vertical, .horizontal]) -> some View
func scrollBounceBehavior(_ behavior: ScrollBounceBehavior, axes: Axis.Set = [.vertical]) -> some View
func scrollIndicatorsFlash(onAppear: Bool) -> some View

states.name: scrolling
states.description: The system indicator appears while the content moves and fades afterwards.

states.name: content fits
states.description: With scrollBounceBehavior(.basedOnSize) the content does not bounce and no indicator is shown.

appearance: The indicators are drawn by the system and follow the light or dark appearance. The scroll view has no background; put it on a theme colour.
platformNotes: The web ScrollArea styles thin scrollbars to match the theme and makes the region focusable and labelled only when it scrolls. On iOS the indicators are the system's and cannot be themed, and a scroll view needs no focus stop: VoiceOver scrolls with three fingers and Full Keyboard Access scrolls the focused region. The web's height and maxHeight are frame(height:) and frame(maxHeight:). Not available: the web's edge shadows (shadows) and onScrollableChange; iOS 17 has no public signal for whether content overflows. Android uses its own scroll modifiers in the same way.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver scrolls with a three-finger swipe and announces the page.
System behaviour: moving VoiceOver or keyboard focus to an element outside the visible part scrolls it into view.
Add accessibilityLabel to the ScrollView only when the region needs a name of its own, for example a log.
edgeCases: A ScrollView takes all the height it is offered; without a frame it fills the screen.
scrollIndicators(.visible) is a request. The system still hides the indicator when the content fits.
A horizontal ScrollView inside a vertical one works; two on the same axis do not.
