name: MonarchStackedBarChart
title: StackedBarChart
wrapsNative: MonarchBarChart (Swift Charts BarMark with yStart/yEnd stacking, chartXSelection / chartYSelection, an AXChartDescriptor) with layout .stacked by default and the 100% offset computed before drawing; inside MonarchChartFrame with MonarchChartLegend
summary: Stacked bars showing how each category's total splits into parts, as values or as shares of 100%, vertical or horizontal, with totals, inspection, legend toggles, drill-in and the data as a table.
whenToUse: To show a total per period or category and what it is made of, such as tickets by status per month, or to compare the mix across categories regardless of their size with offset .expand.
whenNotToUse: For one series per category use MonarchBarChart, or MonarchBarList for a ranked list. For a single whole use MonarchStackedProportionBar or MonarchDonutChart. For parts over a continuous time axis use a Swift Charts AreaMark in MonarchChartFrame.
api: init(_ title: String, categories: [String], series: [MonarchBarChartSeries], description: String? = nil, categoryTitle: String? = nil, valueTitle: String? = nil, summary: String? = nil, orientation: MonarchBarChartOrientation = .vertical, layout: MonarchBarChartLayout = .stacked, offset: MonarchStackedBarChartOffset = .normal, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, hiddenSeries: Binding<Set<String>>? = nil, highlightedIndex: Int? = nil, referenceLines: [MonarchBarChartReferenceLine] = [], valueRange: ClosedRange<Double>? = nil, showsValueLabels: Bool = false, isLegendToggleable: Bool = true, isTableToggleShown: Bool = true, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, height: CGFloat? = nil, labels: MonarchStackedBarChartLabels = MonarchStackedBarChartLabels(), formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (Int) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchStackedBarChartLabels.init(bar: MonarchBarChartLabels = MonarchBarChartLabels(), shareSeries: String? = nil)
enum MonarchStackedBarChartOffset { case normal, expand }
MonarchBarChartSeries.init(_ key: String, label: String, values: [Double?], color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
MonarchBarChartReferenceLine.init(_ value: Double, label: String? = nil)

options.name: title
options.description: The chart's name: the frame heading and the plot's accessibility label.

options.name: categories
options.description: The categories in display order, already formatted by the app.

options.name: series
options.description: The parts, each with a key, a label, one value per category and an optional colour slot. The first series sits on the baseline.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title.

options.name: categoryTitle
options.description: The heading of the category column of the table and the name of VoiceOver's category axis.

options.name: valueTitle
options.description: What the values measure; the name of VoiceOver's value axis.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated spoken summary.

options.name: orientation
options.description: vertical columns or horizontal bars.

options.name: layout
options.description: stacked (one bar of parts per category) or grouped (the parts side by side).

options.name: offset
options.description: normal stacks the values; expand stacks each category's shares so every bar is 100% long. Only applies when stacked.

options.name: status
options.description: ready, loading, empty or error. Ready with no categories or no series shows empty.

options.name: hiddenSeries
options.description: The keys of hidden series. Without it the chart keeps its own set, changed by the legend.

options.name: highlightedIndex
options.description: A category to emphasise; the bars of the others are dimmed.

options.name: referenceLines
options.description: Dashed lines at a value. Not drawn with the 100% offset.

options.name: valueRange
options.description: Fixes the value axis. With the 100% offset the axis is always 0...1 (0% to 100%).

options.name: showsValueLabels
options.description: Writes each stack's total at its end (each bar's value when grouped). With the 100% offset the total is 100%.

options.name: isLegendToggleable
options.description: Whether legend entries show and hide their series. The legend appears with two or more series.

options.name: isTableToggleShown
options.description: Whether "View as table" is offered.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The message of the empty state.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart.

options.name: height
options.description: The plot height: 240 points for columns; 32 points per category, at least 120, for bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the bar chart's (frame, category, total, no data, details, clear) and the share summary sentence.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes values with the normal offset. With the 100% offset values are percentages in the environment's locale, with at most one decimal.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Drill-in: called with the category index (an index into the app's categories, also with the 100% offset) from Details or from the category's VoiceOver action.

states.name: ready
states.description: The stacked plot, the legend (two or more series) and "View as table".

states.name: 100% offset
states.description: Every bar is 100% long; the value axis, value labels, inspection row, table and summary show percentages. Reference lines are not drawn.

states.name: inspecting
states.description: After a touch or drag: the category's band is shaded and a row under the plot reads every part and the stack's total, with Details (when onSelect is set) and Clear.

states.name: highlighted
states.description: With highlightedIndex, the other categories' bars are drawn at reduced opacity.

states.name: series hidden
states.description: The part leaves the bars and the others keep their colours. With the 100% offset the others keep their shares, so the bar ends short of 100%. The table still lists it.

states.name: grouped
states.description: With layout .grouped the parts stand side by side and the offset is ignored.

states.name: loading
states.description: The frame's muted placeholder of the plot's height, read as "Loading chart".

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState with "No data yet" and the empty message.

states.name: error
states.description: The frame's error, with Try again when onRetry is set.

appearance: As MonarchBarChart: parts take the theme's data slots 1 to 5 in series order, then the subtle text colour; the grid uses the subtle border colour, the zero line the strong border colour, labels the muted text colour and the inspected band the muted background. Every colour is a theme role, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes are covered.
platformNotes: The web's StackedBarChart is its BarChart with stacking on and the 100% offset; the iOS component is the same composition over MonarchBarChart (Swift Charts). The web separates stacked parts with a hairline in the surface colour; MonarchBarChart has no option for a separator between parts, so iOS parts touch (a request to add one to MonarchBarChart is recorded). With the 100% offset the web formats axis ticks with no decimals and other values with one; iOS uses one formatter with at most one decimal for both. Inspection uses touch selection and a row under the plot rather than a hover tooltip; there is no keyboard arrow navigation. Android ships the same MonarchStackedBarChart. Several closures are optional (formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is formatValue.
accessibility: The plot is one accessibility element labelled with the title. Its value is the generated summary or the summary parameter: with values, MonarchBarChart's summary (categories, then each shown series' total and highest category); with the 100% offset, the categories, then each shown series' average share and largest share.
The plot carries MonarchBarChart's AXChartDescriptor, with a Total series when stacked; with the 100% offset the values are shares and are read as percentages.
With onSelect, the plot has one VoiceOver custom action per category, named "Details, <category>".
The legend is MonarchChartLegend: each entry is a switch that is on while its series is shown; the last visible series cannot be hidden.
"View as table" shows every value, and a Total column when stacked, as text.
Parts are told apart by the legend's names, the inspection row and the table, not by colour alone.
edgeCases: With the 100% offset, negative values count as zero and a category whose positive total is zero has zero shares everywhere.
Shares are computed over every series, hidden ones included, so hiding a part leaves a gap instead of rescaling the others.
Gaps (nil) and values that are not finite draw nothing and are written "No value" in the inspection row and "–" in the table.
In the values offset, negative parts stack down from zero separately from the positive parts.
More than five series: the sixth and later are neutral.
Touch inspection and Audio Graphs were not tried on a device or with VoiceOver; the share logic and summary are unit-tested.

name: MonarchStackedProportionBar
title: StackedProportionBar
wrapsNative: GeometryReader with an HStack of Rectangle segments clipped to a Capsule; MonarchChartLegend (square markers) as the legend, or a MonarchFlowLayout list for status tones and the remainder
summary: One horizontal bar split into proportions, with a legend that lists each part's value and share.
whenToUse: To show how one whole divides (pipeline stages, storage by type, monitors by state) inside a card or row where a donut chart would be too large. With total and remainderLabel it shows the use of a capacity.
whenNotToUse: For one value against a target, use ProgressView with .monarch or MonarchUsageMeter. To rank or compare many parts, use MonarchBarList. For breakdowns over time, use a stacked bar chart.
api: MonarchStackedProportionBar.init(_ label: String, segments: [MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment], total: Double? = nil, remainderLabel: String? = nil, legendContent: MonarchStackedProportionBarLegendContent = .both, size: MonarchStackedProportionBarSize = .md, showsLegend: Bool = true, hidesZero: Bool = true, percentDigits: Int = 0, emptyLabel: String? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil)
MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment.init(_ key: String, label: String, value: Double, color: MonarchChartColor? = nil)
MonarchStackedProportionBarSegment.init(_ key: String, label: String, value: Double, tone: MonarchTone)
enum MonarchStackedProportionBarSize { case sm, md, lg }
enum MonarchStackedProportionBarLegendContent { case both, value, percent, none }

options.name: label
options.description: Names the legend for VoiceOver, such as "Lead pipeline".

options.name: segments
options.description: The parts, in display order. Each has a key, a label, a value, and a palette colour or a status tone.

options.name: total
options.description: The size of the whole, for a capacity. The sum of the parts when nil or smaller than the sum; the rest is empty track.

options.name: remainderLabel
options.description: The legend name of the empty remainder, such as "Free". Without it the remainder is drawn but not listed.

options.name: legendContent
options.description: What each legend entry shows after its label: both ("1,204 · 34%"), value, percent or none.

options.name: size
options.description: The thickness of the bar: sm 4, md 8 or lg 12 points.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Whether the legend is drawn. Off, VoiceOver still reads every entry from the bar.

options.name: hidesZero
options.description: Whether parts with a value of 0 are left out of the bar and the legend.

options.name: percentDigits
options.description: The decimal places of shares. Shares too small to write read "<1%".

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in text "No data yet", shown when every value is 0.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

states.name: default
states.description: The parts in palette colours, in order, each at least 4 points wide, separated by 2-point gaps; the legend lists every part.

states.name: status mode
states.description: Every segment has a tone: segments and legend markers use the solid tone colours, and neutral uses the subtle text colour.

states.name: remainder
states.description: A total above the sum leaves empty track; with remainderLabel it is listed with an outlined marker.

states.name: legend hidden
states.description: Only the bar is drawn; VoiceOver reads the label and every entry.

states.name: empty
states.description: Every value is 0 or there are no segments: an empty track and "No data yet".

appearance: Segments use the theme's data colours 1 to 5 in order (the sixth part and later are neutral), or in status mode the solid success, warning, danger and info colours and the subtle text colour. The track is the muted background. The legend is caption text in the default text colour. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a native tooltip when the pointer hovers a segment; touch has no hover, so the legend carries every value and there is no tooltip. The web minSegmentWidth option is a fixed 4 points here. The web locale and valueFormat options are the environment locale and formatValue. A mix of tones and palette colours is not rejected by the type system as on the web; tones are ignored, as the web does at run time. Segments are laid out from the leading edge, so the bar is mirrored in right-to-left layouts. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The bar is hidden from VoiceOver while the legend is shown; the legend is a container named by label.
Each legend entry is one element read as its label, then its value and share, such as "Replied, 182 · 9%".
With showsLegend off, the bar is one element read as label with every entry as its value.
With no data, one element reads the label and "No data yet".
Every part has a text label, so no part is told apart by colour alone; the remainder's marker is outlined, not filled.
Legend text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps onto more rows.
edgeCases: Negative and non-finite values count as 0.
A share under 1% reads "<1%" and one just under the whole reads ">99%" (with percentDigits, the thresholds move by the same number of places).
Many tiny parts can need more than the bar's width at their minimum; the excess is clipped by the capsule.
Palette slots follow the segment's position before zeros are hidden, so hiding a zero part never repaints the others. Pin color when a filter can remove parts.
A total smaller than the sum is ignored.
Status mode needs a tone on every segment; a partial set of tones is ignored.

name: MonarchStageJourney
title: StageJourney
wrapsNative: ScrollView(.horizontal) with ScrollViewReader for the stage strip, MonarchFlowLayout and MonarchButton for the moves, TimelineView(.everyMinute) with RelativeDateTimeFormatter for times; MonarchStageHistory is a VStack timeline
summary: Where an item is in its pipeline and what can happen next: a strip of stages grouped by phase, a card for the current stage with how long it has been there, and buttons for the moves the product allows; with MonarchStageHistory for the record of past moves.
whenToUse: On the detail screen of an item that moves through fixed stages: a patent application, a deal, a candidate, an order. Use the strip variant in a header or a row.
whenNotToUse: Not for the steps of a form or a setup flow the user goes through; use MonarchStepper. Not for a free status with no order; use MonarchStatusBadge.
api: init(_ stages: [MonarchStageJourneyStage], currentID: String, terminal: MonarchStageJourneyTerminal? = nil, enteredAt: Date? = nil, currentMeta: String? = nil, variant: MonarchStageJourneyVariant = .full, transitions: [MonarchStageJourneyTransition] = [], now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchStageJourneyLabels = MonarchStageJourneyLabels(), onTransition: (@MainActor (MonarchStageJourneyTransition) async throws -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

init(_ stages: [MonarchStageJourneyStage], currentID: String, terminal: MonarchStageJourneyTerminal? = nil, enteredAt: Date? = nil, currentMeta: String? = nil, variant: MonarchStageJourneyVariant = .full, transitions: [MonarchStageJourneyTransition] = [], now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchStageJourneyLabels = MonarchStageJourneyLabels(), onTransition: (@MainActor (MonarchStageJourneyTransition) async throws -> Void)? = nil) where Content == EmptyView
struct MonarchStageJourneyStage: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String, group: String? = nil, description: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchStageJourneyTransition: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String, kind: MonarchStageJourneyTransitionKind = .forward, needsInput: Bool = false, isDisabled: Bool = false) }
enum MonarchStageJourneyTransitionKind { case forward, exit, back }
enum MonarchStageJourneyTerminal { case success, closed }
enum MonarchStageJourneyVariant { case full, strip }
struct MonarchStageJourneyLabels { init(stages:now:since:done:current:success:closed:nextSteps:moveTo:backTo:needsInput:moved:failed:), every parameter optional }
struct MonarchStageHistory: View { init(_ entries: [MonarchStageHistoryEntry], now: Date? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, labels: MonarchStageHistoryLabels = MonarchStageHistoryLabels()) }
struct MonarchStageHistoryEntry: Identifiable { init(id: String, from: String? = nil, to: String, at: Date, actor: String? = nil, meta: String? = nil, note: String? = nil, isBackward: Bool = false) }
struct MonarchStageHistoryLabels { init(started: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, to: String? = nil, movedBack: String? = nil, empty: String? = nil) }

options.name: stages
options.description: Every stage in pipeline order, each with an id, a label, an optional group (phase) and an optional description shown while it is current.

options.name: currentID
options.description: The id of the current stage. Stages before it are done. With an unknown id every stage is upcoming and no card is shown.

options.name: terminal
options.description: The current stage ends the journey: success (granted, won, hired) or closed (withdrawn, lost).

options.name: enteredAt
options.description: When the item entered the current stage, shown as "since 3 days ago" and updated once a minute.

options.name: currentMeta
options.description: A short note shown as a neutral MonarchBadge next to the current stage.

options.name: variant
options.description: full: strip, card and moves. strip: the strip only.

options.name: transitions
options.description: The moves from the current stage: forward (the first is primary), exit (quiet) and one back ("Back to …").

options.name: now
options.description: A fixed reference time for enteredAt, which also stops the minute updates.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onTransition
options.description: Called with the chosen move; its button shows a spinner until it returns and a thrown error is shown in the card. The product then changes currentID. Without it no moves are shown.

options.name: content
options.description: Extra content at the end of the card, such as a checklist.

states.name: done
states.description: A stage before the current one: accent subtle fill, accent border and a checkmark; read as "done".

states.name: current
states.description: The current stage: solid accent fill and medium weight; read as "current stage" and selected.

states.name: upcoming
states.description: A stage after the current one: outlined with muted text.

states.name: success
states.description: The current stage ended the journey well: solid success stage, success-tinted card with a filled checkmark; read as "Completed".

states.name: closed
states.description: The journey ended early: emphasis stage with a strong border, subtle card with an x mark; read as "Closed".

states.name: moving
states.description: The chosen move's button shows a spinner and the other moves are disabled.

states.name: failed
states.description: A thrown error is shown in the card with an icon and announced.

appearance: Stages are capsules in the caption type role, grouped under small uppercase phase names in the muted text colour. Done stages use the accent subtle fill and border with a strong accent checkmark, the current stage the solid accent and its on-solid text, upcoming stages the default border and muted text. The card is the surface colour with the subtle border, the success roles when the journey succeeded and the subtle background when closed. All colours are theme roles, so the dark and high-contrast themes need nothing else.
platformNotes: The parity map named a horizontal stage strip and a timeline; both are here, the timeline as MonarchStageHistory, which the web exports from the same module (StageHistory). The strip scrolls sideways inside itself and starts scrolled to the current stage. The web's currentMeta and history actor, meta and note take any content; here they are strings (currentMeta is shown as a badge); put richer content in the card's content slot. The web's DateInput accepts strings and numbers; here times are Date. Times use RelativeDateTimeFormatter in the environment's locale instead of the RelativeTime component, because a fixed reference time is needed for snapshots and the strip needs plain text.
accessibility: The strip is a container named "Stages"; each stage is one element read by its name, with "done", "current stage" or the outcome as its value; the current stage has the selected trait.
Done stages have a checkmark and the ended stage its outcome symbol, so the status is not colour alone.
The card's title ("Now: Examination") is a heading and is read with the outcome ("Now: Granted, Completed"); "Next steps" is a heading too.
A move button is read as "Move to Granted" or "Back to Filed", with ", asks for details" when needsInput is true.
A change of current stage is announced ("Moved to Granted"); a failed move is announced with its message.
Each history entry is one element read as the move in words ("Filed to Examination"), "(moved back)", the time, the actor, the facts and the note; the dots and the line are hidden.
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type; move buttons are MonarchButton with 44-point touch targets and wrap onto new rows.
edgeCases: An unknown currentID shows every stage as upcoming and no card.
Stages without a group are shown without a phase name; a group name repeated later starts a new run.
Only the first back move is shown.
A transition with isDisabled stays disabled; while a move runs the other moves are disabled.
An empty history shows "No stage moves yet." or emptyMessage.
Long stage names do not wrap in the strip; the strip scrolls instead.

name: MonarchStatCard
title: StatCard
wrapsNative: MonarchMetric (Text with Foundation format styles) on the MonarchCard surface, with MonarchInfoTooltip (popover), MonarchSparkline, Button with a plain style for the drill-down, .redacted(reason: .placeholder) while loading, MonarchInlineErrorRetry
summary: One KPI for a dashboard: a MonarchMetric (label, value, unit and change) on a card, with an optional hint, an explanation behind an info button, a trend sparkline and a drill-down.
whenToUse: On a dashboard or overview screen, for a headline number people scan and may open for the detail behind it. Several sit in a MonarchDashboardGrid or a LazyVGrid.
whenNotToUse: For a number inside a row, a header or a table footer use MonarchMetric on its own. For a chart with axes use the chart components.
api: init(_ label: String, value: Double?, unit: String? = nil, change: MonarchMetricChange? = nil, format: MonarchMetricFormat = .number, isCompact: Bool = false, hint: String? = nil, help: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, sparkline: [Double?]? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, variant: MonarchStatCardVariant = .card, size: MonarchMetricSize = .md, isLoading: Bool = false, errorMessage: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, emptyLabel: String? = nil, helpLabel: String? = nil, loadingLabel: String? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

init(_ label: String, text: String?, spokenText: String? = nil, unit: String? = nil, change: MonarchMetricChange? = nil, hint: String? = nil, help: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, sparkline: [Double?]? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, variant: MonarchStatCardVariant = .card, size: MonarchMetricSize = .md, isLoading: Bool = false, errorMessage: String? = nil, isRetrying: Bool = false, emptyLabel: String? = nil, helpLabel: String? = nil, loadingLabel: String? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchStatCardVariant { case card, plain }

options.name: label
options.description: What the number measures. Always visible.

options.name: value
options.description: The number, formatted by MonarchMetric. nil shows a dash read as No data.

options.name: text
options.description: In the second initialiser: the value as the app wrote it, such as "4.8 / 5".

options.name: spokenText
options.description: What VoiceOver reads for a text value when it differs from the text.

options.name: unit
options.description: A unit written smaller after the value.

options.name: change
options.description: The change versus an earlier period, drawn by MonarchDeltaIndicator with its comparison and good direction.

options.name: format
options.description: A plain number, a percentage of a ratio, or a currency.

options.name: isCompact
options.description: Writes 1.2K or €3.4M; VoiceOver reads the full value.

options.name: hint
options.description: A caption under the value, such as "38 of 52 people". Say here why a tone is set.

options.name: help
options.description: How the metric is defined, shown in a popover from an info button.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: A decorative SF Symbol before the metric.

options.name: sparkline
options.description: A trend under the value, drawn by MonarchSparkline. Hidden from VoiceOver.

options.name: tone
options.description: A threshold or emphasis: the border takes the tone's border colour and the tone's icon is added, read as the tone's name.

options.name: variant
options.description: A card with a border and surface, or plain inside another surface.

options.name: size
options.description: sm for dense rows, md, or lg for a headline figure.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows a redacted placeholder for the value, read as Loading.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Replaces the value with this message.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: Shows Try again busy.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in No data read for a missing value.

options.name: helpLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the info button, About <label>.

options.name: loadingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in Loading read while loading.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again with an error.

options.name: action
options.description: Opens the details behind the number: the metric becomes a button with a chevron.

states.name: value
states.description: The metric, hint and sparkline.

states.name: empty
states.description: A muted dash read as No data.

states.name: loading
states.description: The metric with a placeholder value under .redacted(reason: .placeholder); no sparkline or drill-down.

states.name: error
states.description: The label and the message, as MonarchInlineErrorRetry with onRetry or a danger MonarchInlineNotice without.

states.name: tone
states.description: For info, success, warning and danger, the border takes the tone's border colour and the tone's icon appears before the metric.

states.name: drill-down
states.description: With action, the metric area is a button with a forward chevron; the system shows the pressed state.

appearance: The MonarchCard surface and radius with the subtle border, or the tone's border; the metric in MonarchMetric's styles (muted label, strong figure, tinted change); the hint in the caption style and muted text colour; the sparkline in the accent colour or the tone. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web StatCard renders its own value; on iOS the value, unit, change and formatting are MonarchMetric, so the two never disagree. The web's accent tone is not offered: MonarchTone has no accent case yet. The web's tone colours the value itself; here the tone colours the border and adds the tone's icon, because MonarchMetric owns the value colour and a tone must not rely on colour alone. The web's href and linkComponent become action, which the app uses to push a screen; the web's deprecated delta, deltaDirection and deltaTone are covered by change. The web's visual slot is systemImage plus sparkline, and semantics (a description list) has no iOS equivalent: the metric is one VoiceOver element. Android has no StatCard yet. Several closures are optional (action, onRetry). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is action.
accessibility: The metric is one element: label, then value, unit and change as a sentence (from MonarchMetric); compact figures are read in full.
With action the metric is a button with the hint "Shows the details" and a decorative chevron.
The info button is a separate MonarchInfoTooltip with a 44-point target, named "About <label>".
A tone adds an icon read as the tone's name, so the threshold is not only a colour.
The sparkline is hidden from VoiceOver; the value and change carry the data.
While loading the value reads Loading.
edgeCases: A long label and hint wrap; nothing has a fixed height.
The drill-down is not offered while loading or after an error.
An empty errorMessage counts as no error.
The sparkline accepts gaps (nil) as MonarchSparkline does.

name: MonarchStatusBadge
title: StatusBadge
wrapsNative: Text and Image in a Capsule (as MonarchBadge), or MonarchStatusDot for the dot variant
summary: A status shown as words, a tone and a distinct icon or dot, looked up by key in a registry of built-in and app-defined statuses.
whenToUse: Wherever the same set of statuses appears many times (services, tickets, deployments) and should look the same everywhere.
whenNotToUse: For a one-off label, use MonarchBadge. For a live state such as "Running" with a pulse, use MonarchStatusDot. For something people act on, use MonarchTag.
api: init(_ status: String?, registry: MonarchStatusRegistry? = nil, label: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, showsIcon: Bool = true, variant: MonarchStatusBadgeVariant = .subtle, size: MonarchStatusBadgeSize = .md)
init(_ definition: MonarchStatusDefinition, showsIcon: Bool = true, variant: MonarchStatusBadgeVariant = .subtle, size: MonarchStatusBadgeSize = .md)
MonarchStatusDefinition.init(_ label: String, tone: MonarchTone, systemImage: String? = nil, description: String? = nil)
MonarchStatusRegistry.init(_ definitions: [String: MonarchStatusDefinition])
MonarchStatusRegistry.init<Key: RawRepresentable>(_ definitions: [Key: MonarchStatusDefinition]) where Key.RawValue == String
static var MonarchStatusRegistry.builtIn: MonarchStatusRegistry
func MonarchStatusRegistry.merging(_ other: MonarchStatusRegistry) -> MonarchStatusRegistry
func MonarchStatusRegistry.resolve(_ key: String?) -> MonarchStatusDefinition
func monarchStatusRegistry(_ registry: MonarchStatusRegistry) -> some View
enum MonarchStatusBadgeVariant { case subtle, outline, solid, dot }
enum MonarchStatusBadgeSize { case sm, md }

options.name: status
options.description: The key: built-in (operational, degraded, partial, down, maintenance, unknown, success, warning, danger, info, neutral) or from a registry. nil is unknown.

options.name: registry
options.description: Statuses for this badge only, looked up before the installed registries and the built-in set.

options.name: label
options.description: Replaces the registry's label.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: Replaces the registry's SF Symbol; in the dot variant it replaces the dot.

options.name: showsIcon
options.description: Hides the icon when false; the label still carries the meaning.

options.name: variant
options.description: subtle, outline, solid or dot.

options.name: size
options.description: sm uses caption text, md label text.

options.name: definition
options.description: Second initialiser: the label, tone and symbol given directly.

states.name: known
states.description: The registry's label, tone and symbol.

states.name: unknown
states.description: The neutral tone, a question mark symbol and a label made from the key ("pending_delete" reads "Pending delete"); nil reads "Unknown".

appearance: Subtle is a tinted capsule with strong-coloured text, outline a capsule with the tone's border, solid a filled capsule, all from the tone roles of the theme. The dot variant is a MonarchStatusDot: a dot in the tone's solid colour and default-coloured text.
platformNotes: The web registry also accepts a custom #rrggbb colour per status, passed through a contrast guard. iOS takes colours only from the theme by role, so a status picks one of the five tones; workspace-defined colours are not offered. The web has no accent tone equivalent here because MonarchTone has no accent case. The web's StatusRegistryProvider is the monarchStatusRegistry(_:) modifier; defineStatuses is a MonarchStatusRegistry built from a dictionary, typed by an enumeration with string raw values. Android shares the name and the built-in set.
accessibility: One element read as the label.
The icon and the dot are decorative; every built-in health status has a symbol of a different shape, and the label always names the status.
An unknown key is read as words made from the key, never as a raw identifier.
Text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A long label wraps inside the capsule; keep labels to a few words.
Nested monarchStatusRegistry(_:) calls add up; the innermost wins where two define the same key.
The description of a definition is not drawn; use it for a legend.

whenToUse: To show the state of an item in a dense place such as a list row or a table cell, where a badge is too heavy.
whenNotToUse: For a status that should stand out, use MonarchBadge. Do not use the dot without words: with isLabelHidden, show a legend near it.

enum MonarchStatusDotSize { case sm, md }

options.name: label
options.description: The words for the status, already localised.

options.name: tone
options.description: neutral, info, success, warning or danger. Selects the colour of the dot.

options.name: size
options.description: sm is an 8-point dot with caption text, md a 10-point dot with label text.

options.name: isPulsing

options.name: isLabelHidden

The dot and the pulse are decorative; the meaning is in the words.
The pulse does not run when Reduce Motion is on.
The dot and the text scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A long label wraps; the dot stays on the first line.

With Reduce Motion on, a pulsing dot looks the same as a still one.

title: StatusPageView
wrapsNative: List with Section headers (or a ScrollView with a VStack), NavigationLink to an incident's detail, refreshable(action:) for a new check, and a Form-style field and button for subscribing
summary: A recipe, not a component: a service status page as an in-app screen, with the overall state, active incidents and their updates, each service's state and uptime history, and an email subscription.
whenToUse: When an app shows the health of its own or a customer's services: an in-app status screen, the status tab of a monitoring product, or a support screen during an outage.
whenNotToUse: For one service's history alone use MonarchUptimeBar; for one incident's updates use MonarchIncidentTimeline; for a short outage notice above other content use MonarchCalloutBanner with placement .page. A public status website stays on the web.
api: List { Section { MonarchCalloutBanner(overallTitle, message: updated, tone: overallTone) } Section("Active incidents") { ForEach(incidents) { NavigationLink { ScrollView { MonarchIncidentTimeline(incident.updates) } } label: { Text(title); MonarchStatusBadge(state, size: .sm) } } } Section("Services") { ForEach(services) { Text(name); MonarchStatusBadge(state, size: .sm); MonarchUptimeBar(name, segments: days, size: .sm) } } Section("Subscribe to updates") { MonarchTextField("Email", text: $email); MonarchButton("Subscribe", variant: .primary) { … } } }.refreshable { await reload() }

states.name: operational
states.description: The banner reads "All systems operational" in the success tone.

states.name: degraded or partial outage
states.description: The banner takes the warning tone and the worst service state; affected services show their badge.

states.name: down
states.description: "Service disruption" in the danger tone.

states.name: maintenance
states.description: "Under maintenance" in the info tone; scheduled work is listed as an incident with the maintenance stage.

states.name: no data
states.description: "Awaiting first checks" in the neutral tone; uptime bars show no-data segments.

states.name: subscribing
states.description: The Subscribe button shows progress; the result replaces the field's helper text.

appearance: System list sections on the grouped background. The overall state is a MonarchCalloutBanner, states are MonarchStatusBadge words with tone and icon, history is MonarchUptimeBar segments in the status roles, and updates are a MonarchIncidentTimeline. All follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web ships StatusPageView as one component with a header, stats row, legend, maintenance list, past incidents grouped by day and a subscribe form. On iOS it is a recipe of existing components in a List: the stats row and legend are left out (each MonarchUptimeBar can show its legend and reads its own summary), an incident opens its timeline in a detail screen instead of expanding in place, and pull to refresh replaces the web's polling. The web's deriveOverallState is a short function in the recipe (worst of down, partial, degraded, maintenance, operational). Android plans it as a recipe as well.
accessibility: Section titles are headers, so the rotor moves between incidents, services and subscribing.
The overall state is the banner's title read with its tone name; service states are badge words, not only colours.
Each MonarchUptimeBar reads a summary of the period and is adjustable day by day.
The incident timeline reads each update with its stage, time and author.
The subscribe result is the field's helper text; post an announcement when it changes so VoiceOver hears it.
edgeCases: With no services, show MonarchEmptyState in the services section instead of an empty list.
With many services, group them in one Section per service group.
Incident times use MonarchIncidentTimeline's time zone (UTC by default); pass the page's time zone when it has one.
Long service names wrap above the badge at the largest text sizes.

title: StatusPicker
wrapsNative: A Button trigger and a popover of Buttons grouped under category headings, each icon in its category's colour (a system Menu draws every icon in the tint); Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) and a Section per category remains the choice for the system menu
summary: Shows and changes the workflow status of an issue, task or ticket, with the team's own status names grouped under five fixed categories, using the standard menu picker. Monarch ships no type.
whenToUse: In issue rows, cards and detail screens where the status can be changed. Group statuses by category with a Section and give each category its own SF Symbol, as in the examples, so the status never depends on colour.
whenNotToUse: For a read-only status, show the Label without a menu, or use MonarchStatusBadge. For moving through the linear steps of a form, use MonarchStepper. For urgency, use the priority-picker entry.
api: Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<SelectionValue>, content: () -> Content)
func pickerStyle(_ style: MenuPickerStyle) -> some View
Section(_ title: String, content: () -> Content)
Label(_ title: String, systemImage: String)
Menu(content: () -> Content, label: () -> Label)

states.name: selected
states.description: The menu shows a checkmark next to the current status; the trigger shows its name (and, in the Menu form, its category symbol in the category colour).

states.name: no status
states.description: Use an optional selection with a "No status" row tagged nil, as the web's none message does.

states.name: disabled
states.description: System dimming, with disabled(_:).

appearance: System menu in every theme. In the Menu form the trigger takes the Monarch button style and the symbol takes the category's theme role, as on the web: the subtle text colour for backlog and cancelled, the muted text colour for not started, the strong warning colour for in progress and the strong success colour for completed. Inside the system menu the symbols take the menu's own colour, so the symbol shape and the name carry the status.
platformNotes: The web ships StatusPicker on DropdownMenu with drawn glyphs (dashed ring, ring, half-filled ring, check, cross), and Android builds MonarchStatusPicker. On iOS the standard menu picker gives the menu, the category sections, the checkmark, hardware keyboard and VoiceOver behaviour, so Monarch ships no type. A system menu shows SF Symbols, not custom drawings, so the categories use circle.dashed, circle, circle.righthalf.filled, checkmark.circle.fill and xmark.circle.fill. The web's STATUS_CATEGORIES order is the order of the Category enum in the examples; its StatusGlyph for read-only displays is a Label with the same symbol and colour. The web's sm and md sizes map to the Monarch button sizes on the Menu trigger; the glyph-only trigger is the symbol with monarchMinimumHitTarget().
accessibility: System behaviour: the picker is read as a pop-up button with the current status as its value; menu items are read by name under their section, with the selected one marked.
In the Menu form, accessibilityLabel("Status: In progress") names the trigger with the current status, as the web does; a glyph-only trigger keeps that name.
Every category has its own symbol shape and every status its own name, so the status never depends on colour.
A glyph-only trigger needs monarchMinimumHitTarget() for a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: A category with no statuses is skipped, so no empty section appears.
A long status name wraps in the Menu trigger at large text sizes; the system menu truncates as it does for any item.
Section titles inside a menu picker are drawn by the system; on some iOS versions a menu shows sections as separators only, and the symbols still group the statuses.

name: MonarchStepUpAuthDialog
title: StepUpAuthDialog
wrapsNative: Content for sheet(isPresented:content:) with presentationDetents, interactiveDismissDisabled and Environment(\.dismiss); Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented) (or .menu when it does not fit); MonarchPasswordInput, MonarchOtpPinInput; LocalAuthentication LAContext.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication) for the device owner check
summary: Asks a signed-in person to confirm it is still them, with their password, an authenticator code, a passkey or Face ID, Touch ID or the device passcode, before a high-risk action.
whenToUse: Before deleting or transferring a workspace or account, erasing personal data, revoking keys or revealing a secret.
whenNotToUse: To sign in, use the sign-in form recipe. To confirm an action that is not sensitive, use a confirmation alert (confirm-dialog). Do not use the device owner check alone where the server must know who is acting: it only proves who holds the device.
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, methods: [MonarchStepUpMethod] = [.password], labels: MonarchStepUpAuthDialogLabels = MonarchStepUpAuthDialogLabels(), errorMessage: (@MainActor (any Error) -> String?)? = nil, onForgot: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onCancel: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onVerified: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onVerify: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchStepUpCredential) async throws -> Void)
enum MonarchStepUpMethod: String { case password, code, passkey, deviceOwner }
enum MonarchStepUpCredential { case password(String), code(String), passkey, deviceOwner; var method: MonarchStepUpMethod }
enum MonarchStepUpBiometry { case faceID, touchID, opticID, passcode }

struct MonarchStepUpAuthDialogLabels { init(title:, description:, methodPicker:, methodName:, passwordLabel:, passwordRequired:, codeLabel:, codeHelper:, codeIncomplete:, passkeyDescription:, passkeyButton:, deviceOwnerDescription:, deviceOwnerButton:, deviceOwnerUnavailable:, submit:, cancel:, forgot:, genericError:) }

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "Confirm it’s you".

options.name: description
options.description: Why the person is asked, such as "Deleting a workspace needs your password." Also the reason the system shows with Face ID.

options.name: methods
options.description: The methods offered, most preferred first; the first is shown first. Repeats are dropped; empty means the password. With more than one, a picker switches between them.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including method names and the Face ID, Touch ID, Optic ID and passcode button titles.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Turns a thrown error into a message. Without it, or when it returns nil, the error's LocalizedError description or "That did not work. Try again." is shown.

options.name: onForgot
options.description: Starts password recovery. Shows a Forgot your password? link-style button under the password field.

options.name: onCancel
options.description: Called when the sheet closes without verifying, by Cancel or by swiping it down.

options.name: onVerified
options.description: Called after onVerify succeeds, just before the sheet closes itself. Run the protected action here.

options.name: onVerify
options.description: Checks the credential with the server. Return when accepted; throw to show the failure. For .passkey run ASAuthorizationController here. For .deviceOwner the system check has already passed.

states.name: password
states.description: The password field with show and hide, and the forgot button when onForgot is given.

states.name: code
states.description: Six code cells in two groups of three; the code submits itself when complete and is cleared after a failure.

states.name: passkey
states.description: A line of text and a Use passkey primary button.

states.name: device owner
states.description: A line of text and a primary button named after the device's check: Use Face ID, Use Touch ID, Use Optic ID or Use passcode.

states.name: missing entry
states.description: Confirm with an empty password or fewer than 6 digits shows "Enter your password." or "Enter all 6 digits." on the field, announced.

states.name: verifying
states.description: The primary button shows its spinner; the fields, picker and Cancel are disabled and the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: failed
states.description: The message is shown on the password or code field, or in a danger notice for passkey and device owner, and announced. A cancelled system sheet shows nothing.

appearance: The surface background, a lock shield symbol in the strong accent colour, the heading style title and a body line in the muted text colour, then the method picker, the field and full-width primary and ghost buttons. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web dialog becomes the content of a SwiftUI sheet: the app presents it with .sheet(isPresented:) and the sheet closes itself on success through the dismiss action, at medium and large detents. The web's open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange and trigger are the sheet's binding. iOS adds the deviceOwner method, which uses LocalAuthentication (Face ID, Touch ID, Optic ID or the passcode); the app needs NSFaceIDUsageDescription in its Info.plist. The web's totp method is called code. forgotHref is replaced by onForgot, because a link out of a sheet is the app's navigation. Focus does not move into the field on open: SwiftUI gives VoiceOver the sheet's first element, and the keyboard opens when the person taps the field. The system Face ID and passkey sheets are the system's and cannot be styled. Android builds the same component with BiometricPrompt. Several closures are optional (errorMessage, onForgot, onCancel, onVerified). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is errorMessage.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.

The password and code fields are MonarchPasswordInput and MonarchOtpPinInput, so their labels, the show-password toggle, the one-time-code content type and the field errors come from those components.
Missing entries and failures are written in words and posted as announcements.
The method picker is a standard segmented Picker named "Verification method", or a menu Picker when the segments do not fit at large text sizes.
The primary button names what happens (Confirm, Use passkey, Use Face ID), and every button has a 44-point touch target.
The sheet cannot be dismissed by a swipe while verifying, so an announcement is not lost.
edgeCases: Each presentation starts clean, on the first method, because the sheet content is created anew.
Changing the method clears the errors.
On a device without a passcode the device owner method shows "Set a passcode on this device to use it to confirm."
Cancelling Face ID, the passcode or the passkey sheet leaves the dialog open with no error.

name: MonarchStepper
title: Stepper
wrapsNative: HStack and VStack of step markers, ViewThatFits for the compact form, Button for reached steps, ProgressView with MonarchProgressViewStyle
summary: Multi-step progress for wizards, onboarding and setup flows: a row or a column of numbered steps, or a compact "Step 2 of 5" with a progress bar.
whenToUse: At the top of a multi-step flow (horizontal, which becomes compact on a phone) or beside it on a wide screen (vertical). Pass onSelect to let people go back to steps they have reached.
whenNotToUse: Not for the progress of a task that runs by itself; use ProgressView with the Monarch progress style. Not for switching between unrelated views; use a TabView or a Picker. It is not the system Stepper, which changes a number.
api: init(_ steps: [MonarchStepperStep], current: Int, furthest: Int? = nil, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = .horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = .automatic, isFinished: Bool = false, isBusy: Bool = false, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchStepperStep, Int) -> Void)? = nil)

init(_ steps: [MonarchStepperStep], currentID: String, furthestID: String? = nil, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = .horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = .automatic, isFinished: Bool = false, isBusy: Bool = false, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchStepperStep, Int) -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchStepperStep { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, isOptional: Bool = false, isComplete: Bool = false, hasError: Bool = false, isDisabled: Bool = false) }
enum MonarchStepperOrientation { case horizontal, vertical }
enum MonarchStepperCompactMode { case automatic, always, never }

struct MonarchStepperLabels { init(progress: String? = nil, stepOf: (@Sendable (Int, Int) -> String)? = nil, complete: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, current: String? = nil, optional: String? = nil) }

options.name: steps
options.description: The steps, in order. Each has an id, a label, and optionally a description and the flags isOptional, isComplete, hasError and isDisabled.

options.name: current / currentID
options.description: The current step, by position from 0 or by identifier. Steps before it are complete. A position outside the steps is moved inside; an unknown identifier selects the first step.

options.name: furthest / furthestID
options.description: The furthest step the user has reached, when they have gone back. Steps up to it stay selectable. By default the current step.

options.name: orientation
options.description: horizontal or vertical.

options.name: compact
options.description: automatic shows the compact form when a horizontal row does not fit the width; always and never fix the form.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: the name "Progress", "Step 2 of 5", "completed", "needs attention", "current step" and "Optional".

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Makes reached steps (complete ones and any up to furthest, except the current and disabled ones) buttons. Receives the step and its position.

options.name: isFinished
options.description: Every step is done: all markers show the check mark (a step with an error keeps its own), no step is current, and the compact form reads the last step as completed with a full bar.

options.name: isBusy
options.description: The current step is working, for example while it saves: its marker shows a progress indicator in place of its number and VoiceOver adds "in progress" (labels.busy). Ignored when isFinished.

states.name: complete
states.description: A filled accent marker with a checkmark; the line after it is in the accent colour.

states.name: current
states.description: An accent-bordered marker with the number and a tinted ring; the name is semibold.

states.name: upcoming
states.description: A bordered marker with the number; the name is muted.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger-tinted marker with an exclamation mark; the name is in the danger colour. Takes precedence over every other state.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With onSelect, a step marked isDisabled is not a button and its name is in the disabled text colour.

states.name: pressed
states.description: A selectable step shows the muted background colour while pressed.

states.name: compact
states.description: "Step 2 of 5", the name of the current step and a progress bar filled up to the current step.

appearance: Markers are circles sized from the control token and scaled with Dynamic Type. The accent roles of the theme colour the current and finished steps, the danger roles a step with an error, the strong border and muted text an upcoming step. The lines between steps use the default border colour, or the accent after a finished step. The same roles apply in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web Stepper switches to the compact form below a width of 36rem; iOS uses ViewThatFits, so the row is shown whenever the names fit on one line and the compact form otherwise, which also covers large text sizes. The web step status override ('complete' or 'error') is the two flags isComplete and hasError. The web step label is any node; here it is a String. Hover styles do not exist; a pressed state replaces them. MonarchTone has no accent case, so the accent colour roles are used directly. Android has the same component.
accessibility: The list is an accessibility container named "Progress" (labels.progress).

Each step is one element. Its label is the position and the name ("Step 2 of 5, Address"); its value is the state ("completed", "needs attention" or "current step"), then "Optional" and the description.
A selectable step is a Button, so it has the button trait and is activated by a double tap; its touch target is at least 44 points high.
State is shown by a checkmark, an exclamation mark or the number, and by the weight of the name, not by colour alone. Markers and lines are hidden from VoiceOver.
The compact form is one element named "Progress" whose value is the position and name of the current step; the bar is not read separately.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps; the markers scale with it. Marker colour changes are animated and the animation is skipped with Reduce Motion.
A selectable step shows the focus ring when focused from a hardware keyboard.
While busy, the current step's value adds "in progress"; when finished, the compact form reads the last step as completed.
edgeCases: No steps draws nothing.
A horizontal stepper with compact never squeezes the names, which wrap; prefer automatic on a phone.
With automatic, a long description makes the row too wide and the compact form is shown.
A vertical stepper is never compact unless compact is always.
furthest before current is ignored: the current step counts as reached.
A number of more than two digits shrinks to stay inside the marker.
Step identifiers must be unique; they identify the rows.

title: Sticky
wrapsNative: LazyVStack(pinnedViews: [.sectionHeaders]) for headers that pin while scrolling; safeAreaInset(edge:content:) for a bar fixed to an edge
summary: Pinned section headers and safe-area insets, both standard SwiftUI. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: Use pinnedViews when a section header should stay at the top while its section scrolls under it. Use safeAreaInset for a filter bar or an action bar that is always at the top or bottom of a scroll view; the content is inset so nothing is hidden behind it.
whenNotToUse: For the title and actions of a screen use the navigation bar and toolbar, which the system already keeps in place. In a List, section headers pin on their own in the plain style.
api: LazyVStack(alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, pinnedViews: PinnedScrollableViews = .init(), content: () -> Content)
func safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, content: () -> some View) -> some View

states.name: pinned
states.description: A section header stays at the top edge of the scroll view until the next header pushes it away.

states.name: inset bar
states.description: The bar stays at its edge and the scroll content ends above or below it.

appearance: A pinned header needs an opaque background, or the rows show through it: use a background role of the theme such as bgSurface. For a bar in a safe-area inset, the system bar material follows the light and dark appearance.
platformNotes: The web Sticky pins any element to the top or bottom with an offset, adds a shadow when stuck (elevateWhenStuck) and reports it (onStuckChange). On iOS the two cases are separate APIs: pinnedViews for headers and footers of a lazy stack, safeAreaInset for a bar that never scrolls. There is no stuck signal on iOS 17. A header that must change when pinned reads its own position with a GeometryReader in the scroll view's coordinate space, or, from iOS 18, uses onScrollGeometryChange. The web's offset is the safe area, which the system applies. Android uses stickyHeader in LazyColumn.
accessibility: Pinned headers stay in the reading order at the start of their section; mark them with the header trait.
A bar in a safe-area inset is read after the scroll content for the bottom edge and before it for the top edge.
System behaviour: the scroll content is inset by the bar, so VoiceOver focus is never behind it.
edgeCases: pinnedViews works in LazyVStack, LazyHStack and the lazy grids, not in VStack.
A pinned header without a background is drawn over the rows.
safeAreaInset on a view that does not scroll only moves the content.

whenToUse: A customer's or a workspace's subscriptions in a billing screen, where each row may open the subscription.
whenNotToUse: For one subscription's details, use LabeledContent with the .monarch style. For plans to choose from, use MonarchPricingTable. For general tabular data with sorting and selection, use SwiftUI Table.

MonarchSubscription.init(_ id: String, name: String, plan: String? = nil, quantity: Int = 1, customer: String? = nil, status: String, amount: Decimal?, currencyCode: String, interval: MonarchSubscriptionInterval? = .month, intervalCount: Int = 1, monthly: MonarchSubscriptionMonthly? = nil, renewalDate: Date? = nil, renewsAutomatically: Bool = true, cancelsAt: Date? = nil, changesAt: Date? = nil)
enum MonarchSubscriptionInterval { case day, week, month, year }
enum MonarchSubscriptionMonthly { case amount(Decimal, currencyCode: String), notConverted }

MonarchSubscriptionsTableLabels.init(caption: String? = nil, subscription: String? = nil, customer: String? = nil, status: String? = nil, price: String? = nil, monthly: String? = nil, renewal: String? = nil, customPrice: String? = nil, quantity: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, interval: (@Sendable (MonarchSubscriptionInterval?, Int) -> String)? = nil, priceSuffix: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, spokenPrice: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, spokenOneTimePrice: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, cancels: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, changes: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, renews: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, ends: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, evergreen: String? = nil, notConverted: String? = nil, notConvertedHint: String? = nil, noValue: String? = nil, emptyTitle: String? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil)

options.name: subscriptions
options.description: The rows, in display order. Empty shows the empty state.

options.name: registry
options.description: Statuses that add to or replace the built-in subscription statuses (MonarchSubscriptionsTable.statuses).

options.name: locale
options.description: The locale of amounts and dates. Default: the environment's; dates use the environment's time zone.

options.name: isCustomerShown
options.description: Shows the customer column (or the customer before the renewal in stacked rows). Turn it off on one customer's screen.

options.name: isMonthlyShown
options.description: Shows the monthly column at regular width. nil: when any row has a monthly figure.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the billing period words and the spoken price.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Opens a subscription. Each row becomes a button; stacked rows get a chevron and table names use the link colour.

states.name: stacked rows
states.description: At compact width and at the accessibility sizes: name and price with its period, the plan line, the customer and renewal, then the status badge. The monthly column is not shown, as on the web below 48rem.

states.name: table
states.description: At regular width: Subscription, Customer, Status, Price, Monthly and Renewal columns with numbers aligned to the trailing edge.

states.name: selectable
states.description: With onSelect each row is a plain button with a 44-point touch target.

states.name: not converted
states.description: An active or past-due row whose monthly figure could not be converted shows "Not converted" with a spoken hint; other rows show a dash.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState at the small size: "No subscriptions" and "Subscriptions appear here once they are created.".

appearance: Names use the strong body style in the default text colour, or the link colour when rows open subscriptions in the table; plan, renewal, headings and period suffixes use the caption style in the muted text colour; rows are separated by dividers in the subtle border colour. Statuses are status badges with their tone's subtle fill. Every colour is a theme role, so the table reads in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web SubscriptionsTable is an HTML table with container queries and link rendering. On iOS rows are a stack at compact width and a Grid at regular width rather than SwiftUI Table, because Table is a scrolling container that cannot sit inside a screen's ScrollView with other content and collapses to one column on iPhone; the plan named List rows and Table, and this was changed for the same reason. Links (href, renderLink) become onSelect, which the app uses for navigation. Amounts are Decimal in major units; minorUnits is not offered. Dates are Date values written in the locale and the environment's time zone; there is no timeZone parameter. The relative-time dependency of the plan is not used: renewal dates are absolute, as on the web. The caption is the table's spoken name only (labels.caption). Android ships the same MonarchSubscriptionsTable.
accessibility: The table is a container named "Subscriptions".

Each subscription is one element read as its name, plan line, customer, status, spoken price ("$49.00 per month"), monthly figure and renewal, in both layouts; the column headings are hidden because each row names its values.
With onSelect each row is a button; activating it calls onSelect.
"Not converted" rows have a hint that explains why the figure is missing.
Statuses are read by their words and drawn with an icon, so they never depend on colour.
A missing amount is read as "No amount".
Rows wrap at every Dynamic Type size and switch to stacked rows at the accessibility sizes; selectable rows keep a 44-point touch target.
edgeCases: An unknown status key shows the neutral unknown look with a label made from the key.
A quantity of 1 or less is not shown.
An intervalCount below 1 is treated as 1; 3 months is written as "quarter".
Nothing is converted between currencies or summed.
The billing period words are English singular and plural strings; languages with other plural rules replace them with labels.interval.

wrapsNative: Toggle with a private switch ToggleStyle (a narrow track and round thumb, as the web draws it) and accessibilityRepresentation in each MonarchSwitchSettingsRow, ProgressView while saving, MonarchButton to retry
summary: A group of on/off settings that each save on their own, with saving, saved and failed states and retry on the row.
whenToUse: For preferences where every switch is saved at once with its own request, such as notification or privacy settings, and a failed save must show on the setting that did not stick.
whenNotToUse: For switches submitted together with other fields and a Save button, use a Form with plain Toggles, or MonarchFormField with the row layout. For one setting with no group, use a Toggle.
api: MonarchSwitchSettingsList.init(_ title: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, labels: MonarchSwitchSettingsListLabels = MonarchSwitchSettingsListLabels(), savedDuration: Duration = .seconds(2), @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)

MonarchSwitchSettingsRow.init(_ label: String, isOn: Binding<Bool>, description: String? = nil, labels: MonarchSwitchSettingsListLabels? = nil, onStatusChange: (@MainActor (MonarchSwitchSettingsStatus) -> Void)? = nil, save: @escaping @MainActor (Bool) async throws -> Void)
enum MonarchSwitchSettingsStatus { case idle, saving, saved, error }

struct MonarchSwitchSettingsListLabels { init(saving: String? = nil, saved: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, retry: String? = nil, retryLabel: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, errorMessage: (@Sendable (any Error) -> String?)? = nil) }

options.name: title
options.description: List: the heading of the group, a header for VoiceOver.

options.name: description
options.description: List: a sentence under the heading.

options.name: labels
options.description: List: replacements for "Saving", "Saved", "Couldn't save.", "Retry", the spoken retry name and the error message, for every row.

options.name: savedDuration
options.description: List: how long "Saved" stays after a save.

options.name: content
options.description: List: the rows.

options.name: label
options.description: Row: the name of the setting; labels the switch.

options.name: isOn
options.description: Row: the saved value. The row writes the new value when save returns.

options.name: description
options.description: Row: what the setting does, under the label and part of the switch's label.

options.name: labels
options.description: Row: replacements for this row; nil properties keep the list's.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Row: runs when the save status changes.

options.name: save
options.description: Row: saves the new value. Throwing rolls the switch back and shows the error with Retry.

states.name: idle
states.description: The switch shows the saved value; no status line.

states.name: saving
states.description: The switch already shows the new value; a small spinner and "Saving" in the muted colour. Further toggles are ignored.

states.name: saved
states.description: A check mark and "Saved" in the strong success colour for savedDuration, announced.

states.name: error
states.description: The switch returns to the saved value; an icon and "Couldn't save." with the error's message in the strong danger colour, and a Retry button that saves the failed value again. Announced. Toggling the switch again also retries.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Set with disabled(_:) on a row or the list. The switch cannot be toggled; label and description take the disabled text colour.

appearance: The list is a bordered group on the surface colour with the default border, 12-point corners and a subtle line between rows. Labels use the body style in the default text colour, descriptions the caption style in the muted colour. The switch is drawn from the theme: a narrow track in the accent when on and the strong neutral when off, with a round thumb; VoiceOver is given a standard Toggle. Status colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web has SwitchSettingsList and SwitchSettingsItem; on iOS the row is MonarchSwitchSettingsRow so it can also be placed in a system Form section without the list's frame. On the web, a handler that does not return a promise skips "Saved"; on iOS save is always async, so every successful save shows "Saved". The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent (the title is a header) and uncontrolled defaultChecked is replaced by the binding. The status line sits under the label rather than beside the switch, so it can wrap at large text sizes. Android builds the same component. The parity map lists inline-error-retry as a dependency; it is not used, because its retry button cannot be given a per-row spoken name, so the row draws the same icon-and-text message with a MonarchButton.
accessibility: Each switch is the standard Toggle, labelled by the row's label and description, so VoiceOver reads its name, its on or off value and its switch role.
While a save has failed, the error text is the hint of the switch.
"Saved" and the error are posted as announcements when the status changes; "Saving" is not announced, and the spinner is one element labelled "Saving".
The retry button is named "Retry" and the row label ("Retry Weekly summary") and is a MonarchButton with a 44-point touch target.
The status line has an icon and text, so saved and failed do not depend on colour.
The list title has the header trait.
edgeCases: A save that throws an error without a LocalizedError description shows only "Couldn't save."; pass labels.errorMessage to turn other errors into text.
Leaving the screen while a save runs does not cancel it; the binding is still written when it returns.
A late "Saved" timer never clears the status of a newer save.
Long labels and descriptions wrap; the error and Retry stack when they do not fit on one line.

name: MonarchTableBlock
title: TableBlock
wrapsNative: Grid inside ScrollView(.horizontal); TextField(axis: .vertical) per editable cell; Menu for the controls
summary: A small table of text inside a document: a read-only form that scrolls sideways, and an editable form with a text field per cell and a menu to add and delete rows and columns.
whenToUse: For a few rows and columns of text in a document or a note: a comparison, a schedule, a glossary.
whenNotToUse: For app data that people sort, filter or select, use the system Table or List. For side-by-side prose, use two columns of text.
api: init(_ caption: String? = nil, data: MonarchTableBlockData, label: String? = nil)
init(_ caption: String? = nil, data: Binding<MonarchTableBlockData>, label: String? = nil, labels: MonarchTableBlockLabels = MonarchTableBlockLabels(), onDelete: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchTableBlockData: Sendable, Hashable
MonarchTableBlockData.init(rows: [[String]], hasHeaderRow: Bool = true)
MonarchTableBlockData.init(rowCount: Int = 3, columnCount: Int = 3, hasHeaderRow: Bool = true)

MonarchTableBlockData: static let maximumRowCount = 50, static let maximumColumnCount = 20, private(set) var rows: [[String]], var hasHeaderRow: Bool, var rowCount: Int, var columnCount: Int, var canAddRow: Bool, var canAddColumn: Bool, var canDeleteRow: Bool, var canDeleteColumn: Bool, subscript(row: Int, column: Int) -> String, func isHeader(row: Int) -> Bool
MonarchTableBlockData: mutating func addRow(after row: Int) -> Bool, addColumn(after column: Int) -> Bool, deleteRow(at row: Int) -> Bool, deleteColumn(at column: Int) -> Bool

struct MonarchTableBlockLabels: Sendable { init(controls: String? = nil, addRow: String? = nil, addColumn: String? = nil, deleteRow: String? = nil, deleteColumn: String? = nil, headerRow: String? = nil, deleteTable: String? = nil, emptyCell: String? = nil, cellPosition: (@Sendable (_ row: Int, _ column: Int) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: caption
options.description: Text above the table. Also the spoken name of the table.

options.name: data
options.description: The cells. A value gives a read-only table; a binding gives an editable one.

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the table when the caption is not the right one.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings. Editable form only.

options.name: onDelete
options.description: Adds "Delete table" to the menu. The app removes the table. Editable form only.

states.name: read-only
states.description: Cells are text. Columns are between 96 and 240 points wide before Dynamic Type and text wraps inside them.

states.name: editable
states.description: Every cell is a text field in a 144-point column, at least 44 points high, and a "Table" menu button sits above the table.

states.name: header row
states.description: The first row has a subtle fill, stronger text and the header trait. Switched in the menu or with hasHeaderRow.

states.name: at a limit
states.description: Add row is disabled at 50 rows, add column at 20 columns, delete row and delete column at one.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With disabled(_:) the text uses the disabled colour and the fields and the menu do not respond.

appearance: Cells sit on the surface colour, header cells on the subtle background, with default-border hairlines between cells and around the table and 8-point outer corners. The caption is caption text in the muted colour. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web component is two things: a scrolling frame for a static table, and a Tiptap node with prosemirror-tables. There is no block editor on iOS yet, so the editable form is a self-contained view over a MonarchTableBlockData binding that a block editor can host later; the data type has the web's commands (add row and column after, delete row and column, header row) and limits (50 by 20). Not offered: cell selection across several cells, merged cells (colspan and rowspan), rich text inside a cell, and Tab to move between cells (the keyboard's own field navigation applies). The web shows the controls only while the caret is in the table; here the menu is always shown above an editable table and acts on the cell that last had focus, or on the last row and column when none had. The built-in strings are replaced through one MonarchTableBlockLabels value instead of one parameter each, because there are nine.
accessibility: The scrolling table is a container named by label, else the caption, else "Table"; a caption that is the spoken name is hidden so it is not read twice.
A read-only cell is one element: its text, or "Empty", as the label and "Row 2, column 1" as the value.
An editable cell is a text field whose label is its position.
Header cells have the header trait and stronger text, so the header does not depend on its fill.
The controls are a standard Menu; the header row item is a Toggle with a check mark; "Delete table" has the destructive role.
Editable cells are at least 44 points high and text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Ragged rows are padded with empty cells; an empty input becomes one empty cell; rows past 50 and columns past 20 are dropped.
Reading a cell outside the table gives an empty string and writing one does nothing.
After a row or column is added the new row or column takes focus.
At the largest text size columns are wider and the table scrolls sooner.
The grid is not lazy: it is meant for small tables, which the limits enforce.
