name: MonarchTableOfContents
title: TableOfContents
wrapsNative: VStack of Button entries; monarchTableOfContentsTarget sets id(_:) for ScrollViewReader.scrollTo and reports the heading with onGeometryChange; monarchTableOfContentsSpy reads them in a named coordinateSpace
summary: In-page navigation built from the page's headings: a list of entries that marks the section being read and scrolls to the one chosen, with a scroll spy for the scroll view.
whenToUse: On a long document, help article or settings page with several titled sections. On a phone show it in a sheet from a Contents button; on an iPad it can sit in a sidebar or an inspector.
whenNotToUse: For moving between screens use a NavigationStack or a List of NavigationLinks. For two to five sections that fit on one screen, use MonarchTabs or let people scroll.
api: MonarchTableOfContents.init(_ items: [MonarchTableOfContentsItem<ID>], selection: Binding<ID?>, title: String? = nil, showsTitle: Bool = true, currentLabel: String? = nil, action: @escaping @MainActor (ID) -> Void)
MonarchTableOfContentsItem.init(_ title: String, id: ID, level: Int = 2)
func monarchTableOfContentsTarget<ID: Hashable & Sendable>(_ id: ID) -> some View
func monarchTableOfContentsSpy<ID: Hashable>(selection: Binding<ID?>, offset: CGFloat = 0) -> some View

options.name: items
options.description: The entries in page order, each with a title, the id of its section and a heading level (2 by default).

options.name: selection
options.description: The section being read. Choosing an entry sets it; monarchTableOfContentsSpy keeps it in step with scrolling.

options.name: title
options.description: Replaces the built-in title "On this page".

options.name: showsTitle
options.description: Whether the title is shown. When hidden it still names the list for VoiceOver.

options.name: currentLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Current section", read as the value of the current entry.

options.name: action
options.description: Scrolls to the chosen section, usually ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(id, anchor: .top), and closes the sheet.

options.name: offset (spy)
options.description: The height of anything covering the top of the scroll view. A heading becomes current once it passes this line.

states.name: current
states.description: The entry's text is in the default colour and a semibold weight, with an accent line beside it.

states.name: other
states.description: Muted text with a subtle line beside it.

states.name: nested
states.description: An entry with a deeper level than the one before is indented one step per level of nesting.

states.name: no current section
states.description: With selection nil, no entry is marked, as before the first heading reaches the top.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the list makes every entry use the disabled text colour and ignore taps.

appearance: The title uses the default text colour; entries use the muted text colour and the current one the default text colour. The marker lines use the subtle border role, and the accent strong role for the current entry. All roles come from the theme in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web TableOfContents reads h2 and h3 elements from the DOM, spies with IntersectionObserver and writes #id to the URL. SwiftUI has no DOM, so the app passes the entries and marks each heading with monarchTableOfContentsTarget; the spy measures headings with onGeometryChange instead of IntersectionObserver, using the same rule (first heading in the top 40%, else the last scrolled past). There is no URL hash; the app can store the selection itself. The web's controlled activeId and onActiveChange are the selection binding. The web moves focus to the heading after scrolling; on iOS the app can do this with AccessibilityFocusState. Android builds the same component.
accessibility: The list is a container named by its title ("On this page" by default), and the visible title has the header trait.
Each entry is a button with its title as the name; the current entry's value is "Current section".
The current entry is marked by an accent line and a heavier weight as well as by colour.
Entries wrap instead of truncating at large text sizes, and each has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points.
The entry indent is a leading padding, so nesting follows the reading direction in right-to-left languages.
Scrolling to a section is the app's call to scrollTo; it does not move VoiceOver focus. Give headings the header trait so VoiceOver's headings rotor also reaches them.
edgeCases: Ids must be unique; the list and the spy identify entries by id.
A heading in a lazy stack that has not been created yet is not measured, so the spy only knows headings that have appeared.
When every heading is below the zone (the top of the page), the selection keeps its previous value; set it to the first entry's id if a section should be marked from the start.
Levels may skip (2 then 4); the entry nests one step, as on the web.

name: MonarchTableToolbar
title: TableToolbar
wrapsNative: ViewThatFits of an HStack (one line) or a VStack (two lines) holding the app's filter and control views, Text for the result count and MonarchBulkActionBar; search is the app's searchable(text:placement:prompt:)
summary: The bar above a table or list: the filters, the result count and the app's controls (view switcher, column menu, actions); while rows are selected the filters give way to the bulk selection bar.
whenToUse: Above a list or table that can be filtered, counted, switched between views or acted on in bulk, placed with safeAreaInset(edge: .top) or as the first view above the rows.
whenNotToUse: Not for navigation-bar items alone (use .toolbar) and not for search alone (use searchable). For a selection bar without filters use MonarchBulkActionBar.
api: init(resultCount: Int? = nil, selectedCount: Int = 0, totalCount: Int? = nil, bulkActions: [MonarchBulkAction] = [], labels: MonarchTableToolbarLabels = MonarchTableToolbarLabels(), onClearSelection: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder filters: () -> Filters, @ViewBuilder controls: () -> Controls)

init(resultCount: Int? = nil, selectedCount: Int = 0, totalCount: Int? = nil, bulkActions: [MonarchBulkAction] = [], labels: MonarchTableToolbarLabels = MonarchTableToolbarLabels(), onClearSelection: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder controls: () -> Controls) where Filters == EmptyView
struct MonarchTableToolbarLabels { init(toolbar: String? = nil, results: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: resultCount
options.description: Rows that match the search and filters, shown as "N results" and announced when it changes. nil hides the count.

options.name: selectedCount
options.description: Selected rows. While it is above zero (and onClearSelection is set) the bulk selection bar replaces the filters.

options.name: totalCount
options.description: Rows that could be selected, for "3 of 120 selected".

options.name: bulkActions
options.description: Actions on the selected rows, shown in the bulk selection bar.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken name of the bar and the result count text.

options.name: onClearSelection
options.description: Clears the selection. Without it there is no bulk selection bar.

options.name: filters
options.description: Filter controls, laid out in a row that scrolls sideways when it does not fit.

options.name: controls
options.description: Trailing controls: a segmented Picker as the view switcher, a Menu of Toggle items as the column menu, and actions.

states.name: wide
states.description: Filters, then the count and the controls at the trailing edge, on one line.

states.name: narrow
states.description: When one line does not fit, the filters (or the bulk bar) take the first line and the count and controls the second.

states.name: selecting
states.description: With onClearSelection and a selection, MonarchBulkActionBar with the count, the bulk actions and Clear selection replaces the filters; the count and controls stay.

appearance: The bar has no fill of its own and sits on the screen's background. The result count uses the muted text colour with tabular digits; the controls and the bulk bar keep their own Monarch styling in every theme.
platformNotes: The web toolbar contains its own SearchInput. On iOS search belongs to the navigation bar: the app adds searchable(text:placement:prompt:) to the list, which the plan's ".searchable slot" refers to, and the toolbar does not draw a field. The web builds the ViewSwitcher and ColumnMenu from props; on iOS both are native controls (a segmented Picker and a Menu of Toggle items, see view-switcher and column-menu) that the app passes in controls. The web has sm and md sizes; on iOS the controls keep their own sizes. The web keeps focus in the bulk area after Clear selection; on iOS focus follows the system. Android uses the same name and options.
accessibility: The bar is a container named "Table controls" (labels.toolbar).
A change of the result count is announced, for example "12 results".
The bulk selection bar is MonarchBulkActionBar, which announces its own count and reads each action as a button.
The count text scales with Dynamic Type; the layout moves to two lines when one does not fit.
edgeCases: A selection without onClearSelection keeps the filters, as on the web.
Filters wider than the screen scroll sideways instead of wrapping.
A result count of exactly one reads "1 result"; other counts are formatted for the locale ("1,204 results").

    onClearSelection: { selection.removeAll() },
    filters: { MonarchTag("Open only", isSelected: $onlyOpen) },
    controls: { MonarchButton("New", systemImage: "plus", variant: .primary, size: .sm) {} }
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web preview is 686 px wide, so the results count, view switch and actions share one row and the four columns fit. A phone is 400 pt wide, so the count and the actions wrap and the table scrolls sideways; the data, tones and order are the same.
parityExceptions.convention: adaptive layout: a phone wraps a toolbar and scrolls a wide table (HIG: Layout)

name: MonarchTabs
title: Tabs
wrapsNative: Button per tab, ViewThatFits, ScrollView with ScrollViewReader, matchedGeometryEffect, AccessibilityTraits.isTabBar and .isSelected
summary: A strip of tabs for the top of a screen or a section, with a line or a pill on the selected tab, optional counts and sideways scrolling. SwiftUI has no such control.
whenToUse: To switch between views of related content in the same place: the sections of a record, filtered lists with counts. The app shows the content for the selection below the strip.
whenNotToUse: For two to four short, equal choices use Picker with pickerStyle(.segmented). For the top-level destinations of an app use TabView (see bottom-tab-bar).
api: MonarchTabs.init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<Value>, items: [MonarchTabsItem<Value>], variant: MonarchTabsVariant = .line)
MonarchTabsItem.init(_ title: String, value: Value, count: String? = nil, countTone: MonarchTone = .neutral, isDisabled: Bool = false)
enum MonarchTabsVariant { case line, pill }

options.name: label
options.description: The spoken name of the strip, for example "Project sections". It is not shown.

options.name: selection
options.description: The value of the selected tab. Value is any Hashable type.

options.name: items
options.description: The tabs, in order. Each has a title, a unique value, and optionally a count, a count tone and isDisabled.

options.name: variant
options.description: line: a line under the selected tab and a hairline under the strip. pill: a raised pill on a muted track.

states.name: selected
states.description: The label takes the default text colour, with a 2-point accent line under it (line) or a bordered surface pill behind it (pill).

states.name: unselected
states.description: The label uses the muted text colour.

states.name: disabled tab
states.description: The label uses the disabled text colour and the tab cannot be chosen. Set per item with isDisabled, or for the strip with disabled(_:).

states.name: with a count
states.description: A subtle MonarchBadge in the count tone follows the label.

states.name: selection changes
states.description: The line or pill moves to the new tab over the fast duration, or at once with Reduce Motion.

states.name: tabs do not fit
states.description: The strip scrolls sideways, without indicators, and a newly selected tab is scrolled into view.

appearance: Labels use the label type role in the muted text role, the default text role when selected and the disabled text role when disabled. The line variant has a hairline in the default border role under the strip and a 2-point line in the strong accent role under the selected tab. The pill variant has a track in the muted background role and a selected pill in the surface role with a default border. Counts are subtle badges in the tone roles.
platformNotes: The parity map lists Tabs as build on iOS and as a theme on Material's tab row on Android. The web composes Tabs, TabsList, TabsTrigger and TabsContent; here one view takes the items and the selection, and the content is the app's own switch on the selection, as with Picker. Not offered: the web's link tabs (TabsNav, TabsLink), which are tab-styled links between pages (on iOS switching screens is navigation, not tabs), TabsFilter, which is this component with a selection that can be cleared, the accent count tone (MonarchTone has no accent), and arbitrary content in a trigger. The web's arrow-key movement between tabs is the system's Full Keyboard Access here. The web's scrollable flag is not a parameter: labels always stay on one line, and the strip scrolls by itself when the tabs do not fit the width. The pill track is 44 points high instead of the web's 36, so each tab meets the touch target.
accessibility: The strip is a container with the tab bar trait, named by label.
Each tab is a Button with the selected trait when it is the selection, so VoiceOver reads the name, "selected" and the position.
The count is part of the tab's name, after the title: "Open, 12". The visible badge is not read a second time.
The selection is marked by a line or a bordered pill, not by colour alone.
Each tab has a touch target at least 44 points high and wide.
Labels scale with Dynamic Type and stay on one line; when the tabs do not fit, the strip scrolls sideways.
The indicator moves without animation when Reduce Motion is on.
The order of the tabs follows the layout direction.
edgeCases: A selection that matches no item shows no indicator; every tab is unselected.
Values must be unique in the strip; they identify the tabs.
An empty count string shows no badge.
In the pill variant a neutral count has the same muted background as the track, so it shows as plain text. The web uses a darker fill there.
A scrolling strip gives no visible sign that more tabs follow, other than a tab cut off at the edge. Keep the number of tabs small.
A single label wider than the screen is not wrapped; it scrolls. Keep labels to one or two words.
With an empty items array the strip has no height apart from the line or the track padding.

name: MonarchTabularNumberStyle
title: TabularNumber
wrapsNative: Text with .monospacedDigit(), numbers formatted by a FormatStyle (.number, .percent, .currency(code:))
summary: Fixed-width digits for text, so that columns of figures line up and changing values do not jitter: a modifier for text that is already formatted, and a Text initialiser that formats a number or shows a dash when there is none.
whenToUse: For figures in tables and lists, totals, counters and timers. Use Text(monarchTabular:format:) for a number that may be missing and monarchTabularNumber() for text that is already formatted or that counts by itself.
whenNotToUse: Not for numbers inside a sentence, where proportional digits read better. For a number that is never missing, Text(value, format:) with monospacedDigit() is the same thing.
api: struct MonarchTabularNumberStyle: ViewModifier { init() }
func monarchTabularNumber() -> some View
Text.init<F: FormatStyle>(monarchTabular value: F.FormatInput?, format: F, emptyText: String? = nil, emptyLabel: String? = nil) where F.FormatOutput == String

options.name: value
options.description: The number, or nil when there is none. A floating-point number that is not finite counts as missing.

options.name: format
options.description: How the number is written: .number, .percent, .currency(code:) and their options. It uses the user's locale unless it names one.

options.name: emptyText
options.description: Shown in place of a missing number. Built in: an em dash.

options.name: emptyLabel
options.description: Read by VoiceOver in place of a missing number. Built in: "No value".

states.name: value
states.description: The formatted number in fixed-width digits.

states.name: missing
states.description: The value is nil or not finite: an em dash is shown and VoiceOver reads "No value".

appearance: Only the digit widths change. Size, weight and colour come from the type role and the foreground style applied to the text, in every theme. The dash for a missing value takes the colour of the text around it; the web draws it in the subtle text colour, which is foregroundStyle(theme.colors.textSubtle).
platformNotes: The web TabularNumber formats with Intl.NumberFormat; iOS uses the FormatStyle passed in, so every option of the platform is available and nothing is re-implemented. The modifier is the system monospacedDigit() under a Monarch name. The web never breaks a line inside a number; on iOS a number that does not fit wraps, and lineLimit(1) or fixedSize() is the app's choice. Android covers this with a text style in MonarchTypography.
accessibility: A formatted number is read by VoiceOver as its text.
A missing value is read as "No value" (or emptyLabel), not as a dash.
The text scales with Dynamic Type through the type role applied to it.
Number formatting follows the user's locale, including digits, grouping and decimal separators.
edgeCases: NaN and infinity are shown as missing, like nil.
Only digits get one width. Separators, signs and currency symbols keep their own widths, so align columns to the trailing edge.
A custom font family without fixed-width digits is not changed by the style.
The Text initialiser returns a Text, so it can be placed inside other text by interpolation; the VoiceOver label of the dash then applies to that fragment.

    .monarchTextStyle(.title)
    .monarchTabularNumber()

name: MonarchTagInput
title: TagInput
wrapsNative: TextField with .onSubmit and .submitLabel(.done), MonarchTag chips in MonarchFlowLayout, MonarchButton suggestions
summary: A field that edits a list of short values as removable tags, with validation, paste splitting and optional suggestions.
whenToUse: When people type several short free-form values into one field: skills, labels, keywords, email recipients, perhaps with known values suggested.
whenNotToUse: For values from a fixed list, use a multi-selection List or MonarchTag filters. For one value, use MonarchTextField. For values with several properties each, use a list with an add row.
api: init(_ label: String, tags: Binding<[String]>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, error: String? = nil, suggestions: [String] = [], separators: Set<Character> = [","], maxCount: Int? = nil, allowsDuplicates: Bool = false, isReadOnly: Bool = false, labels: MonarchTagInputLabels = MonarchTagInputLabels(), normalize: ((String) -> String)? = nil, validate: ((String, [String]) -> String?)? = nil)

struct MonarchTagInputLabels { init(duplicate: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, maximum: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, added: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, removed: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, remove: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, addSuggestion: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label; also the VoiceOver label of the text field.

options.name: tags
options.description: The tags, in order.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder text in the empty text field.

options.name: helper
options.description: Help text under the field, such as how values are separated.

options.name: error
options.description: An error from the app. A rejected tag's message replaces it while shown.

options.name: suggestions
options.description: Values offered as buttons under the field while the typed text matches them (ignoring case). Already added values are left out; at most 8 are shown.

options.name: separators
options.description: Characters that add the typed text, besides Return. New lines and tabs also split pasted text.

options.name: maxCount
options.description: The most tags. Further additions are rejected with "You can add up to N."

options.name: allowsDuplicates
options.description: Whether the same tag may appear twice. Duplicates are compared without case.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the tags without remove buttons and without the text field.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the duplicate and maximum messages, the announcements and the spoken names of the remove and suggestion buttons.

options.name: normalize
options.description: Cleans typed text before it is checked and added. Trims white space by default.

options.name: validate
options.description: Returns a message to reject a tag, or nil to accept it. Runs after the duplicate and maximum checks.

states.name: empty
states.description: Only the text field, with its prompt.

states.name: with tags
states.description: Small neutral tags wrap above the text field and the box grows; each has a remove button.

states.name: rejected entry
states.description: The rejected text stays in the field, the border and the message under the box take the danger colour with an icon; the message is announced and clears when the person types.

states.name: error
states.description: The app's error, shown like a rejection while no tag is rejected.

states.name: suggestions
states.description: Matching suggestions appear as ghost buttons with a plus under the box while text is typed.

states.name: read only
states.description: Tags without remove buttons; no text field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Set with disabled(_:). Tags without remove buttons, the text field disabled, the subtle fill and border and the disabled text colour.

appearance: The box repeats MonarchTextField: the surface fill, the input border (danger when there is a message), 8-point corners and the focus ring. Tags are small neutral MonarchTags. The label uses the label style, the help text the caption style in the muted colour, messages the strong danger colour. All are theme roles.
platformNotes: The web's keyboard shortcuts (Backspace in the empty field to reach the last tag, arrow keys between tags) are not offered: SwiftUI's TextField does not report Backspace in an empty field, and every remove button is a real button VoiceOver reaches. Suggestions are buttons under the field instead of a combobox listbox, and there is no addOnBlur or name for hidden form inputs. The web's sizes are not offered because the field and remove buttons keep the 44-point touch target at every size; tags are drawn at the small tag size. A paste is told apart from typing by the number of characters inserted at once: typing a separator commits what comes before it, and inserting several characters that contain separators commits every part. Android builds the same component. Several closures are optional (normalize, validate). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is normalize.
accessibility: The text field is labelled with the label; its hint is the rejection or error (read as "Error: …"), otherwise the help text. The visible label and supporting text are hidden from VoiceOver.
Each tag is read as its text; its remove button is a separate element named "Remove" and the tag, with a 44-point touch target, and can be renamed with labels.remove.
Additions ("Added Research."), removals ("Removed Research.") and rejection messages are posted as announcements.
After a tag is removed or a suggestion added, focus returns to the text field.
Suggestion buttons are named "Add" and the suggestion.
Messages have an icon and text, not colour alone.
edgeCases: Pasting "a, b, c" adds three tags; parts that are rejected stay in the field joined by commas.
Tags are compared without case for duplicates, so "research" is rejected when "Research" is there.
A long tag takes a row of its own in the flow layout.
Tags are identified by position, so duplicate tags (with allowsDuplicates) can each be removed.

name: MonarchTag
title: Tag
wrapsNative: Text, Button, Capsule
summary: A chip people act on: a label that can be removed, selected, or both.
whenToUse: For labels a person adds and removes, and for filters that toggle.
whenNotToUse: For a status that is never acted on, use MonarchBadge. For a choice of one among several, use a Picker.
api: init(_ text: String, systemImage: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, size: MonarchTagSize = .md, removeLabel: String? = nil, onRemove: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

init(_ text: String, isSelected: Binding<Bool>, systemImage: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, size: MonarchTagSize = .md, removeLabel: String? = nil, onRemove: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
enum MonarchTagSize { case sm, md }

options.name: text
options.description: The label.

options.name: isSelected
options.description: Whether the tag is on. Giving it makes the label a button that toggles it.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: An SF Symbol before the text. Decorative.

options.name: tone
options.description: Selects the colours while the tag is not selected.

options.name: size
options.description: sm is 24 points high, md is 28.

options.name: removeLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in spoken name of the remove button, "Remove" and the text.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Runs when the remove button is activated. No remove button without it.

states.name: selected
states.description: Accent fill, border and text, with a check mark before the text.

states.name: removable
states.description: A remove button follows the text.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Muted fill and disabled text colour, with disabled(_:). The buttons do not respond.

appearance: A capsule with the subtle fill, the border and the strong text colour of its tone; the neutral tone uses the muted background and the default text colour. A selected tag uses the accent subtle fill, accent border and accent strong text in every theme.
platformNotes: The web Tag also has an accent tone, which MonarchTone does not have; a selected tag uses the accent. The web TagGroup (arrow-key movement between tags and focus hand-over after a removal) is not offered: lay tags out yourself. Backspace and Delete do not remove a tag. The selection is always a binding; there is no uncontrolled form. The tag is a capsule here and has 8-point corners on the web. Android covers Tag by theming the Material 3 chips.
accessibility: A selectable tag is a button with the selected trait while it is on, and shows a check mark, so the state does not depend on colour.
The remove button is a separate element named "Remove" and the text of the tag; removeLabel replaces the name.
A selectable or removable tag is at least 44 points high; the visible capsule stays 24 or 28 points and the touch target extends above and below it.
The touch target of the remove button is at least 44 points wide and reaches 12 points back over the end of the label.
A tag with no binding and no remove action is read as its text. The icon is hidden from VoiceOver.
edgeCases: Long text wraps inside the capsule.
On a tag that is both selectable and removable, the last 12 points of the label belong to the remove button.
A plain tag is 24 or 28 points high, so tags of different kinds in one row have different layout heights.

name: MonarchTeamCalendar
title: TeamCalendar
wrapsNative: ScrollView(.vertical) holding a fixed people column and one ScrollView(.horizontal) for the days of every row, with ScrollViewReader to open at the day before today; the header pinned with visualEffect; bars are Buttons drawn with UnevenRoundedRectangle; details in a popover with presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover); MonarchAvatar, MonarchEmptyState, MonarchBanner, MonarchLoadingState; Date.FormatStyle and Date.IntervalFormatStyle
summary: Who is away when: people down the leading side, the days of a month or a custom range across, absences as bars that span their days, half days as half bars, pending entries faded, weekends and holidays shaded and today ringed.
whenToUse: For a team's leave or availability overview, where a manager scans who is out on which day and taps an absence to open it or an empty day to add one. Put a MonarchCalendarToolbar above it to move between months.
whenNotToUse: For one person's events day by day use MonarchAgendaList. For choosing a date use MonarchMiniMonth or DatePicker. For meetings with times use an agenda or a time grid; this grid has whole and half days only.

MonarchTeamCalendarMember.init(_ name: String, id: String, url: URL? = nil, description: String? = nil)
MonarchTeamCalendarMember.init(_ name: String, id: String, image: Image?, description: String? = nil)

MonarchTeamCalendarEntry.init(_ label: String, id: String, memberID: String, start: Date, end: Date? = nil, color: Color? = nil, portion: MonarchTeamCalendarPortion = .full, portions: [Date: MonarchTeamCalendarPortion] = [:], isPending: Bool = false)
MonarchTeamCalendarHoliday.init(_ name: String, date: Date)
enum MonarchTeamCalendarPortion { case full, firstHalf, secondHalf }

MonarchTeamCalendarLabels.init(person: String? = nil, grid: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, today: String? = nil, holiday: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, range: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, firstHalf: String? = nil, secondHalf: String? = nil, pending: String? = nil, emptyTitle: String? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, legend: String? = nil, loading: String? = nil)

options.name: members
options.description: The rows in display order, each with an id, a name, an optional photo (Image or URL) and an optional second line.

options.name: entries
options.description: The absences, each with a member id, a first and last day, a label, a colour, a portion, per-day portions and isPending. Days outside the range are left out; entries of unknown members are ignored.

options.name: month
options.description: Any day of the month shown. nil is the month of today. Ignored when from and to are both set.

options.name: from
options.description: The first day of a custom range, used with to.

options.name: to
options.description: The last day of a custom range, inclusive. A day before from gives one day; at most 366 days are shown.

options.name: holidays
options.description: Non-working days for everyone: shaded, named in what VoiceOver reads for the day, and shown in a popover when the day's header is tapped.

options.name: weekendDays
options.description: The shaded days of the week as Calendar weekday numbers, 1 for Sunday to 7 for Saturday. nil uses the calendar's own weekend (Calendar.isDateInWeekend).

options.name: today
options.description: Today's date: ringed in the header, read as Today, and where the days start scrolled to. Pass a fixed date in tests and previews.

options.name: calendar
options.description: The calendar and time zone days are read and named in. The locale for names comes from the environment.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows MonarchLoadingState with placeholder rows, named "Loading team calendar", instead of the grid.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Shows this message in a danger MonarchBanner instead of the grid, and announces it.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Shows the line under the grid that explains shading, half bars and faded bars.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for "Person", the grid name, "Today", the holiday and range phrases, "first half", "second half", "pending", the empty state, the legend and the loading name.

options.name: onEntryTap
options.description: Called when a bar is tapped. Without it a tap on a bar shows its label, person and days in a popover.

options.name: onCellTap
options.description: Called with the member and the start of the day when an empty day is tapped, for example to add time away. Without it empty days take no taps and are not VoiceOver elements.

states.name: bars
states.description: Consecutive whole days of one entry are one bar with the label inside, a solid leading stripe in the entry colour and a light tint of it; a bar cut by the range has no rounded corner and no stripe on that side.

states.name: half day
states.description: A half bar at the leading side (first half) or the trailing side (second half) of the day, without a label; the whole day is still the touch target.

states.name: pending
states.description: A faded bar, and "pending" in what VoiceOver reads.

states.name: weekend and holiday
states.description: The day's column is shaded in the muted fill; a holiday's header is a button that shows its name in a popover, and the name is read with the day.

states.name: today
states.description: The day number is bold in the strong accent inside an accent ring, "Today" is read with it, and the days start scrolled to the day before today.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchLoadingState with placeholder rows instead of the grid.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger MonarchBanner with the message instead of the grid.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState "Nobody to show" when there are no members.

appearance: The grid sits on the surface colour inside a default border with large corners; rows are separated by subtle lines, and the header and the people column by default ones. Weekend and holiday columns use the muted fill. Bars lay the entry colour (the solid accent by default) over the surface colour with a solid stripe at the start; labels keep the default text colour, and day letters and descriptions the muted text colour. Dark and high-contrast themes use their own surface, text, border and accent roles.
platformNotes: The web TeamCalendar is a table of square day cells with the label in a hover title and a roving tab stop moved with arrow, Home, End and Page keys. On iOS the people column stays fixed, the day header stays pinned while rows scroll, and the days are fitted beside the people column as on the web (14 days of November on a phone); only a range too long for the smallest readable day width scrolls sideways in one horizontal ScrollView, opening at the day before today. Consecutive days of an entry are one spanning bar, one VoiceOver element and one target, so onEntryTap passes the entry and member but not the day (the web passes the day too). The hover title and Android's long-press tooltip become a tap: without onEntryTap a bar is a button that shows its details in a popover, and a holiday's header shows its name the same way; iOS has no touch tooltip (see tooltip). Pending entries are faded, as on the web. Days are Date values read in the calendar's time zone, as in MonarchAgendaList, instead of ISO strings (web) or UTC milliseconds (Android); weekendDays use Calendar weekday numbers, the same numbers as Android's Calendar constants, and default to the calendar's weekend instead of a fixed Saturday and Sunday. errorMessage is a String, not a node. Android's empty slot is not offered: an app that needs its own empty state checks members.isEmpty. The accent tone is used through the accent roles directly, because MonarchTone has no accent case. Hardware keyboard navigation uses the system focus between buttons, not the web's key map. Marked experimental as a domain composite until a Rook app adopts it. Several closures are optional (onEntryTap, onCellTap). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onEntryTap.
accessibility: The people column's header is one heading element named for the grid, "Team calendar, November 2026" (or the custom range).
Each person is one heading element, "Alex Kim, Design", so the headings rotor moves from person to person.
Each day header is one element read as its full date, with "Today" before today's and "Holiday: name" after a holiday's; a holiday's header is a button that shows the name.
Each bar is one button read as "Annual leave, Alex Kim, Monday, November 2 to Thursday, November 5", with "first half" or "second half" for a half day and "pending" for a pending entry.
With onCellTap each empty day is a button read as "Sam Lee, Wednesday, November 4"; without it empty days are not elements.
Days are at least 44 points wide and rows at least 44 points tall, and both scale with Dynamic Type, so bars, half-day bars and empty days have 44-point targets.
Half days, pending entries, today and holidays are drawn with shape (half bar, outline, ring, shading) and said in words, not shown by colour alone.
Names and descriptions wrap at the largest text sizes and the row grows to fit; the people column takes at most 40 percent of the width.
The error message is posted as a VoiceOver announcement when it appears; the loading placeholder is named "Loading team calendar".
VoiceOver reads the people column first, then the day headers, then the bars row by row; every bar names its person, so it is understood out of row order.
Right to left, the people column is on the right, earlier days are further right, and half bars and rounded corners are mirrored.
edgeCases: Give the calendar a height, as for a List; inside another vertical scroll view it needs .frame(height:).
One entry per person per day: when two entries cover the same day, the later one in entries is shown, as on the web.
An end before the start is treated as the start; an entry for an unknown member id is ignored.
A one-day or half-day bar has no visible label; it is read by VoiceOver and shown in the popover (or the app's screen after onEntryTap).
Very long labels are cut with an ellipsis inside their bar; the full label is read and shown in the popover.
A custom range is capped at 366 days. Every day is a view, so very long ranges with many members cost more to lay out.
today defaults to now; pass a fixed date for previews and tests.
Bar colours are the app's: the fill is a tint of the colour over the surface and the label keeps the default text colour, so any colour stays readable.

name: MonarchTemplatePicker
title: TemplatePicker
wrapsNative: LazyVGrid of Buttons with a custom ButtonStyle; MonarchTag toggles for categories; search through searchable(text:prompt:) on the containing screen
summary: A gallery of templates to start from, with category filters, search through the system search field, and an optional "start from scratch" card first.
whenToUse: When people create a document, project or workspace and can start from one of several templates or from scratch.
whenNotToUse: Not for a few plain options without previews (use MonarchRadioCardGroup or a Picker) and not for choosing many items (use a List with selection).
api: init(_ label: String, selection: Binding<String?>, templates: [MonarchTemplatePickerItem], categories: [MonarchTemplatePickerCategory] = [], query: String = "", blank: MonarchTemplatePickerItem? = nil, initialCategory: String? = nil, labels: MonarchTemplatePickerLabels = MonarchTemplatePickerLabels())

struct MonarchTemplatePickerItem: Identifiable { init(id: String, name: String, description: String? = nil, category: String? = nil, badge: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, image: Image? = nil, keywords: [String] = [], isDisabled: Bool = false); static func blank(name: String? = nil, description: String? = nil, id: String = "blank") -> Self }
struct MonarchTemplatePickerCategory: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String) }
struct MonarchTemplatePickerLabels { init(categories: String? = nil, allCategories: String? = nil, results: (@Sendable (Int) -> String)? = nil, noResults: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: label
options.description: The name of the gallery, read by VoiceOver. It is not shown; a sheet's navigation title usually says it.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the chosen template or of the blank card, or nil for none yet.

options.name: templates
options.description: The templates in order, each with a name, an optional description, category, badge, preview symbol or image, search keywords and disabled flag.

options.name: categories
options.description: Category filters, shown as a scrolling row of toggle tags with "All" first when given.

options.name: query
options.description: The search text from searchable(text:) on the screen that shows the picker. Every word must appear in the name, description or keywords.

options.name: blank
options.description: A "start from scratch" card shown first whatever the filters, usually .blank() or .blank(description:).

options.name: initialCategory
options.description: The category filter selected at first. All by default.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the filter names, the announced result count and the no-results message.

states.name: selected
states.description: The chosen card has the accent subtle background, a heavier accent border and a check mark.

states.name: pressed
states.description: The card darkens to the emphasis background with a strong border.

states.name: disabled template
states.description: Subtle background with disabled text; it cannot be chosen.

states.name: no results
states.description: A filtered MonarchEmptyState saying no templates match the search, under the blank card.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) every card and filter is disabled.

appearance: Cards share the radio card colours: surface background with the default border, accent subtle and accent strong when chosen. The preview is a subtle tile with a large symbol or the app's image. Names use the label style, descriptions the muted caption style, badges are info MonarchBadges. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web picker has its own search box; on iOS search is the system search field from searchable on the containing screen, passed in as query, so it sits in the navigation bar and keyboard like every other iOS search. The web's renderPreview pane is not offered: on a phone the app shows a preview after the choice, for example in the next step. Previews are an SF Symbol or an Image instead of free content. The web's arrow-key grid navigation is replaced by VoiceOver and Full Keyboard Access moving through the buttons.
accessibility: The grid is a container named by label.
Each card is one standard button: the template name as its label, the badge and description as its value, the selected trait when chosen, and at least 44 points high.
Selection is also shown by a check mark and a heavier border, not colour alone.
Category filters are MonarchTag toggles in a container named "Categories".
When the category or search changes, the number of templates shown is announced.
Previews are hidden from VoiceOver.
edgeCases: The blank card is never hidden by the filters.
Search ignores case and accents and matches the words in any order.
Cards are at least 144 points wide, scaled with Dynamic Type, so the largest text sizes show one column.
A selected template hidden by a filter stays selected.

name: MonarchTermsAcceptance
title: TermsAcceptance
wrapsNative: Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox), and a Link per document
summary: The required "I agree to the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" checkbox for sign-up, with a link to each document and the versions that were accepted.
whenToUse: In sign-up and checkout forms where agreeing to the terms is required to continue, and in any form that must record which version of a document the person agreed to.
whenNotToUse: Not for optional choices such as marketing messages (use MonarchMarketingConsentCheckbox) and not for storage or tracking choices (use MonarchConsentPreferences).
api: init(isAccepted: Binding<Bool>, documents: [MonarchTermsDocument], isRequired: Bool = true, showsRequiredError: Bool = false, labels: MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels = MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels(), onChange: (@MainActor (Bool, MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails) -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchTermsDocument: Identifiable { init(_ title: String, url: URL, version: String? = nil, id: String? = nil); static func versions(of documents: [MonarchTermsDocument]) -> [String: String] }
struct MonarchTermsAcceptanceDetails { let versions: [String: String]; let date: Date }
struct MonarchTermsAcceptanceLabels { init(label: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, requiredMessage: String? = nil, requiredHint: String? = nil) }

options.name: isAccepted
options.description: Whether the box is ticked. Start it false for sign-up so the agreement is an active choice.

options.name: documents
options.description: The documents. Their titles are joined into the label in the locale's list format and each is a link under it.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Whether the box must be ticked to continue. Adds the VoiceOver hint "Required" and allows the error.

options.name: showsRequiredError
options.description: Shows "Accept the terms to continue" while the box is required and not ticked. Set it when the person tries to continue; the error clears once the box is ticked.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the label sentence (built from the joined titles), the error and the hint.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Runs when the box changes, with the new state, the version of each document keyed by its id, and the time.

states.name: unticked
states.description: The empty checkbox with the sentence and the document links under it.

states.name: accepted
states.description: The checkbox is filled with a check mark.

states.name: invalid
states.description: With showsRequiredError while unticked: an error icon and "Accept the terms to continue" under the links in the danger strong colour, announced when it appears.

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true): the box, the label and the links use the disabled text colour and cannot be used.

appearance: The checkbox is MonarchCheckboxToggleStyle. The links are underlined in the link text role and indented to line up with the label; the error uses the danger strong role. All colours are theme roles, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: On the web the document links sit inside the checkbox label. On iOS a link inside a toggle's label cannot be activated on its own, so the label is the plain sentence and the documents are separate links under it. There is no form submission on iOS, so the app sets showsRequiredError when the person tries to continue instead of the web's native required attribute, and there are no name, value or versionsName form fields: the app records the details from onChange. The web's target option has no equivalent; links open the system's handler for the URL. Disabling the view also disables the links, unlike the web where the links stay usable.
accessibility: The box is a standard Toggle with the Monarch checkbox style, so VoiceOver reads its label, its on and off value and the activation gesture of the system.
A required box has the hint "Required".
Each document is a separate standard Link with a 44-point touch target, underlined so it is not shown by colour alone.
The error has an icon and text, is read as one element and is announced when it appears.
Text scales with Dynamic Type and the links wrap onto further rows.
edgeCases: One document gives "I agree to the Terms of Service"; three give "A, B, and C" in English, joined by the locale's list format.
Documents without a version are left out of the reported versions.
Two documents with the same URL need an explicit id, because the id is the key of the versions.

title: TermsUpdateDialog
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) with interactiveDismissDisabled for the blocking form, holding a ScrollView with Text, Text(date, format:), Link with buttonStyle(.monarchLink(.standalone, isExternal: true)), MonarchInlineNotice for an error and MonarchButton for accept and decline
summary: A recipe, not a component: a sheet that tells people the terms have changed, with a summary, the effective date and links to the documents, which in its blocking form cannot be dismissed until they accept or decline.
whenToUse: When updated terms or a privacy policy must be shown at sign-in or on launch, either to be accepted (blocking) or only to inform.
whenNotToUse: For consent to optional processing such as analytics use the consent recipes (see cookie-consent-banner). For a minor wording change, a banner (MonarchBanner) is enough.
api: func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> some View) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View
Link(_ title: String, destination: URL).buttonStyle(.monarchLink(.standalone, isExternal: true))

MonarchButton.init(_ title: String, systemImage: String? = nil, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, isLoading: Bool = false, loadingLabel: String? = nil, fullWidth: Bool = false, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)
MonarchInlineNotice.init(_ message: String, title: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .info, …)

states.name: blocking
states.description: Accept and continue, and Decline (for example Sign out); the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: informational
states.description: One Got it button; the sheet can be swiped away.

states.name: pending
states.description: The accept button shows its loading state and dismissal stays disabled while the acceptance is recorded.

states.name: error
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice above the buttons when recording the acceptance failed.

appearance: A system sheet on the theme's surface colour with the title in the heading style, body text in the default and muted text colours, links in the link colour with the external icon, a primary accept button and a ghost decline button.
platformNotes: The web TermsUpdateDialog is a component with mode, effectiveDate parsing, documents, version labels and pending and error props. On iOS it composes a sheet: the date is formatted with Text(date, format:) in the person's locale, links open in the browser through the environment's openURL, and blocking is interactiveDismissDisabled. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; VoiceOver focus moves into the sheet when it appears.
Each document is a Link, read with "opens in the browser" from the Monarch link style.
The accept button reads its loading state; an error is shown as text in a notice with an icon, not only colour.
In the blocking form the escape gesture does nothing, so decline must be offered as a button.
edgeCases: At the largest text sizes the summary and links scroll; keep the buttons under the ScrollView so they stay visible.
Show the sheet once per version: store the accepted version and compare on launch.
If declining signs the person out, say so on the decline button.

name: MonarchTextField
title: Input
wrapsNative: TextField, SecureField
summary: A labelled text field with placeholder, helper text, an error state, a required mark, read-only and multiline modes, accessories and a focus binding, over the standard TextField or SecureField.
whenToUse: For text input in a Monarch layout: single line, or multiline with axis: .vertical. Use labelVisibility: .hidden inside a Form row whose label already names the field.
whenNotToUse: For long documents with formatting use MonarchRichTextEditor (iOS 26 and later). For numbers use MonarchNumberInput.

options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: text
options.description: The text to edit.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

options.name: helper
options.description: Supporting text under the field.

options.name: error
options.description: Error message; replaces the helper while present.

options.name: isSecure
options.description: Hides the text, for passwords.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows a mark after the label and adds "Required" to the hint.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Shows the text, selectable, without letting it be edited; "Read only" is added to the hint.

options.description: .vertical for a multiline field that grows with its text.

options.name: lineLimit
options.description: The fewest and most lines of a multiline field; nil grows without a limit.

options.name: labelVisibility

options.name: focus
options.description: The app's focus binding for the field.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the spoken "Required", "Read only" and the form of an error.

options.name: leading / trailing
options.description: Views inside the field box before and after the text, such as a currency symbol or a clear button.

states.name: empty
states.description: Shows the prompt in the subtle text colour.

states.name: focused
states.description: Draws the theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: error
states.description: Danger border, and an icon and message under the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: A surface-coloured field with an input border and 8-point corners. The focus ring is 2 points wide in the accent, or 3 points in the text colour in the high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Android wraps Material 3 OutlinedTextField with a floating label; iOS keeps the label above the field, as iOS forms do. There is no MonarchTextFieldStyle, because SwiftUI's TextFieldStyle has no public requirement to implement. Keyboard type, content type and submit label are the standard SwiftUI modifiers.
accessibility: The field is one VoiceOver element: label, then value, then the error (spoken as "Error: …") or else the helper text as the hint.
A new error message is announced when it appears.
The error is shown with an icon and text, not colour alone.
The field is at least 44 points high and the whole field focuses the input when touched.
Text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: An empty error string counts as no error.
The built-in "Error:" prefix cannot be replaced by a parameter.
Single line only.

summary: Applies one of the nine Monarch type roles (size, weight, tracking, line spacing) to text.

name: MonarchThemeToggle
title: ThemeToggle
wrapsNative: Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented); Menu with an inline Picker and .menuStyle(.button), drawn with MonarchButtonStyle (ghost)
summary: Light, dark or system appearance, bound to the MonarchSchemePreference that the app passes to .monarchTheme(scheme:).
whenToUse: On a settings screen (segmented) or in a toolbar or account menu (menu) to let people choose the app's appearance.
whenNotToUse: Not for contrast or accent choices; use a standard Picker bound to MonarchContrastPreference or the accent. Not needed when the app always follows the device.
api: init(selection: Binding<MonarchSchemePreference>, variant: MonarchThemeToggleVariant = .segmented, size: MonarchThemeToggleSize = .md, showsLabel: Bool = true, labels: MonarchThemeToggleLabels = MonarchThemeToggleLabels())
static func storageValue(for preference: MonarchSchemePreference) -> String
static func preference(storageValue: String?) -> MonarchSchemePreference?
enum MonarchThemeToggleVariant { case segmented, menu }
enum MonarchThemeToggleSize { case sm, md }
struct MonarchThemeToggleLabels { var title, light, dark, system: String? }

options.name: selection
options.description: The chosen scheme: .light, .dark or .system. The app applies it with .monarchTheme(scheme:) and stores it.

options.name: variant
options.description: segmented shows three segments; menu shows one button that opens the three choices.

options.name: size
options.description: sm or md. Segmented: the regular or the large system control. Menu: the sm or md Monarch button.

options.name: showsLabel
options.description: menu only: whether the button shows the current choice's name beside its symbol. Without it the name is still spoken.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings Theme, Light, Dark and System.

states.name: light, dark, system
states.description: The selected segment, or the checked menu item and the symbol and name on the menu button (sun, moon, half-filled circle).

states.name: disabled
states.description: With .disabled(true) the system dims the segmented control; the menu button uses the disabled roles of the Monarch button style.

appearance: The segmented variant is the system segmented control, whose selected segment follows the system look in light, dark and increased contrast. The menu variant is a ghost Monarch button: default text colour on no fill, a subtle fill while pressed, and the system menu with a checkmark on the current choice.
platformNotes: The web toggle reads and writes the shared rook_theme cookie and applies the theme to the html element itself. On iOS there is no shared cookie: the toggle only changes its binding, and the app stores the choice (for example with @AppStorage) and applies it with .monarchTheme(scheme:). storageValue(for:) and preference(storageValue:) use the same light, dark and system values as the cookie. The web menu variant's side and align options have no meaning for a system menu, which the system places. Segments show names only, because a system segmented control shows either text or an image per segment.
accessibility: Both variants are standard Pickers, so VoiceOver reads the choices as items with the current one selected, and the menu's choices carry the system checkmark.
The menu button is named Theme (or labels.title) and its value is the current choice's name, also when showsLabel is false.
The choices are named in words; the symbols are not the only sign of the choice.
The menu button has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points; the segmented control keeps the system control height.
Names scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Long translated names are truncated by the system segmented control; use the menu variant when names are long.
preference(storageValue:) returns nil for a missing or unknown stored value, so the app chooses its own default.
The toggle can sit inside a view whose theme it changes; the change applies as soon as the binding changes.

summary: Installs a Monarch theme (colours, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion) in the SwiftUI environment and sets the tint.
whenToUse: Once, at the root of the app or of a screen that uses Monarch. Apply it again lower in the tree to give a subtree another scheme or accent.
whenNotToUse: Do not read MonarchTokens colours directly in views; read the theme from the environment so the view follows Dark Mode, Increase Contrast and the accent.

func monarchTheme(_ appearance: MonarchAppearance, typography: MonarchTypography = .system) -> some View
@Environment(\.monarchTheme) var theme: MonarchTheme
func MonarchThemeTokens.withAccent(_ accent: MonarchAccent) -> MonarchThemeTokens
func MonarchThemeTokens.withAI(_ ai: MonarchAccent) -> MonarchThemeTokens

options.name: scheme
options.description: Light, dark or the device setting.

options.name: contrast
options.description: Standard, high contrast or the Increase Contrast setting.

options.name: accent
options.description: One of the 21 generated accents.

options.name: typography
options.description: Optional custom font families. The system typeface by default.

states.name: light
states.description: Standard contrast on a light canvas.

states.name: dark
states.description: Standard contrast on a dark canvas.

states.name: hc-light
states.description: High contrast on a light canvas; focus ring 3 points wide in the text colour.

states.name: hc-dark
states.description: High contrast on a dark canvas; focus ring 3 points wide in the text colour.

appearance: Resolves to one of four themes. The accent replaces the accent roles, links, and (in the standard themes only) the focus ring. A custom AI colour (withAI, from MonarchBrandTheme.aiAccent) replaces the AI roles, thinking and citation.
platformNotes: Android wraps MaterialTheme and the web sets CSS custom properties; iOS puts a value in the SwiftUI environment and sets tint, so system controls take the accent without Monarch wrapping them. Only the subtree is themed: sheets and system chrome presented outside it follow the device.
accessibility: Follows Dark Mode unless a scheme is fixed.
Switches to the high-contrast themes when Increase Contrast is on, unless a contrast is fixed.
The high-contrast themes draw the focus ring 3 points wide in the text colour.
edgeCases: A component used outside monarchTheme() gets the light theme with the default accent.
Applying the modifier again inside a themed tree replaces the theme for that subtree only.
A custom font family that is not registered with the app falls back to the system font.

name: MonarchThreadPanel
title: ThreadPanel
wrapsNative: Screen content for a NavigationStack push, or a NavigationStack in .inspector or .sheet: MonarchVirtualMessageList (ScrollView with LazyVStack and .defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom)) for the replies with the root and reply count divider as its header, .safeAreaInset(edge: .bottom) for the typing indicator and reply box, .navigationTitle, and .toolbar with a Toggle using .toggleStyle(.button) to follow and a .cancellationAction Close button
summary: The replies to one message of a conversation: the message, a reply count divider, the replies pinned to the newest one, a Follow button, and the app's reply box pinned to the bottom.
whenToUse: When someone opens the replies to one message of a chat or channel: pushed onto the conversation's navigation stack on a phone, or in an inspector beside the conversation on iPad.
whenNotToUse: For the conversation itself, use MonarchVirtualMessageList with MonarchMessageRow (the message-timeline recipe). For discussions anchored to a document passage, use MonarchCommentThread or MonarchCommentsPanel.
api: init(_ replies: [Item], replyCount: Int? = nil, status: MonarchThreadPanelStatus = .ready, isFollowing: Bool = false, notice: String? = nil, seenDelay: Duration = .milliseconds(400), now: Date? = nil, labels: MonarchThreadPanelLabels = MonarchThreadPanelLabels(), onClose: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onFollowingChange: (@MainActor (Bool) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onRepliesSeen: (@MainActor (Int) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder root: () -> Root, @ViewBuilder typing: () -> Typing, @ViewBuilder composer: () -> Composer, @ViewBuilder headerActions: () -> Actions, @ViewBuilder reply: @escaping (Item, MonarchVirtualMessageListContext<Item>) -> Reply)

init(_ replies: [Item], …, onRepliesSeen: (@MainActor (Int) -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder root: () -> Root, @ViewBuilder composer: () -> Composer, @ViewBuilder reply: @escaping (Item, MonarchVirtualMessageListContext<Item>) -> Reply) where Typing == EmptyView, Actions == EmptyView
struct MonarchThreadPanel<Item: MonarchVirtualMessageListItem, Reply: View, Root: View, Typing: View, Composer: View, Actions: View>: View
enum MonarchThreadPanelStatus: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case ready, loading, error, deleted }

struct MonarchThreadPanelLabels: Sendable { init(title:close:follow:following:followedNotice:unfollowedNotice:followFailed:replyCount:replies:loading:error:deleted:list:), every parameter optional; list: MonarchVirtualMessageListLabels? }

options.name: replies
options.description: The loaded replies, oldest first. Item conforms to MonarchVirtualMessageListItem (id, time, authorID).

options.name: replyCount
options.description: The number of replies for the divider; can exceed the loaded replies. The loaded count when nil.

options.name: status
options.description: ready shows the replies; loading placeholder rows; error a failure with Try again; deleted a notice with Close.

options.name: isFollowing
options.description: The person follows the thread: the Follow toggle is on and reads Following with a filled bell.

options.name: notice
options.description: A note after the replies, such as Showing the first 500 replies.

options.name: seenDelay
options.description: How long the replies stay on screen in an active scene before onRepliesSeen.

options.name: now
options.description: Fixes now for the Today and Yesterday separators. The clock by default; the locale and calendar come from the environment.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, and optionally the list's (MonarchVirtualMessageListLabels), whose name defaults to Replies.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Adds Close in the cancellation position of the toolbar and under a deleted thread. Leave it out when the panel is pushed: the back button closes it.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Try again when the thread could not be loaded.

options.name: onFollowingChange
options.description: Follows (true) or unfollows. Adds the Follow toggle while ready; it is disabled until the function returns. Throw to announce a failure.

options.name: onRepliesSeen
options.description: Receives the reply count once the replies have been on screen for seenDelay in an active scene, and again when the count changes: mark the thread read here.

options.name: root
options.description: The message the thread answers, usually a MonarchMessageRow. EmptyView for none.

options.name: typing
options.description: Above the reply box, such as a MonarchTypingIndicator.

options.name: composer
options.description: The reply box, usually a MonarchMessageComposer, pinned under the replies. EmptyView for a read-only thread.

options.name: headerActions
options.description: Further toolbar buttons, after Follow in the primary action position.

options.name: reply
options.description: Draws one reply, usually a MonarchMessageRow with isGrouped: context.isGrouped.

states.name: ready
states.description: The root message, the reply count divider and the replies, newest at the bottom, with day separators and grouping; typing and the reply box at the bottom.

states.name: no replies
states.description: The root and the 0 replies divider.

states.name: following
states.description: The Follow toggle is on, reads Following with a filled bell, and is disabled while the change runs.

states.name: loading
states.description: A MonarchLoadingState with three rows, read as Loading thread; no Follow; the typing indicator and the reply box still show, as on the web.

states.name: error
states.description: This thread couldn’t be loaded., with Try again (MonarchInlineErrorRetry), or in the strong danger role without onRetry.

states.name: deleted
states.description: This thread was deleted., announced when it appears, with a Close button when onClose is given.

appearance: No fill of its own above the replies, so it takes the screen's, sheet's or inspector's surface; the bottom bar uses the surface role with a subtle border on top. The reply count, notice and deleted text use the muted text role, the divider lines the subtle border role, and the toolbar is the system navigation bar in the theme's tint. The same roles adapt to dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web's ThreadPanel is a side panel with its own header and takes the replies as children of a scrolling log. On iOS it is a screen: the title and buttons are in the navigation bar, it is pushed onto the conversation's NavigationStack on a phone (the back button and back swipe close it) or shown in .inspector at regular width, and the replies are a MonarchVirtualMessageList, so only rows near the screen are built, day separators are added and consecutive replies group. The web's follow button with aria-pressed is a Toggle with the button style, read with its on or off value. The web's close icon button is a Close text button in the cancellation position. The web reports replies seen while the page is visible; here the delay runs while the scene is active. Android draws an in-content header with a FilterChip; iOS uses the navigation bar. Android's key and time functions are the MonarchVirtualMessageListItem protocol here, and its LazyListState is not exposed. Status experimental: it is a product composite until a Rook app adopts it.
accessibility: The navigation title, Thread, is the screen's heading.
The replies are a container named Replies; MonarchVirtualMessageList announces arriving replies and makes day separators headers.
The reply count divider is a header, so the rotor moves from the message to its replies.
Follow is a Toggle with the button style: VoiceOver reads its title and on or off value; it is disabled while the change runs.
Following, unfollowing and a failure are announced; the deleted notice is announced when it appears.
Loading is one element read as Loading thread; Close and Try again have touch targets of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: replyCount can be larger than the loaded replies; use notice to say how many are shown.
The root and divider show above the first reply, as the list's header, once the start of the thread is loaded.
Follow is hidden while loading, after an error and for a deleted thread; the typing indicator and the reply box show in every state.
onRepliesSeen is called again after the delay when replyCount changes, and when the scene becomes active again.
A negative replyCount counts as 0.
The replies scroll themselves: give the panel the full screen or a bounded height and do not put it in a vertically scrolling parent.
