name: MonarchTimeGrid
title: TimeGrid
wrapsNative: ScrollView with ScrollViewReader, a custom Layout per day column (overlap columns), MonarchEventChip blocks and bars, LongPressGesture sequenced before DragGesture, onTapGesture(coordinateSpace:), accessibilityActions and sensoryFeedback
summary: The day and week view of a calendar: an hour gutter, an all-day row and one column per day, with overlapping events side by side, a now line, working-hours shading, unavailable blocks, tap to create and long press and drag to move.
whenToUse: For a calendar's day or week view, a booking schedule or a staff rota where the time of day matters. Put MonarchCalendarToolbar above it to change days and views.
whenNotToUse: For a list of upcoming events by day use MonarchAgendaList; to pick a day use MonarchMiniMonth or DatePicker. Do not put it inside another vertical ScrollView: the hours scroll themselves.
api: MonarchTimeGrid.init(days: [Date], events: [MonarchAgendaEvent] = [], now: Date? = Date(), startHour: Int = 0, endHour: Int = 24, hourHeight: CGFloat? = nil, snapMinutes: Int = 15, workingHours: [MonarchTimeGridWorkingHours]? = nil, unavailable: [MonarchTimeGridUnavailable] = [], scrollToMinutes: Int? = nil, showsAllDayRow: Bool = false, calendar: Calendar = .current, labels: MonarchTimeGridLabels = MonarchTimeGridLabels(), canMoveEvent: (@MainActor (MonarchAgendaEvent) -> Bool)? = nil, onSelectDay: (@MainActor (Date) -> Void)? = nil, onSelectSlot: (@MainActor (MonarchTimeGridSlot) -> Void)? = nil, onSelectEvent: (@MainActor (MonarchAgendaEvent) -> Void)? = nil, onMoveEvent: (@MainActor (MonarchTimeGridMove) -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchTimeGridSlot: Hashable, Sendable { let day: Date; let minutes: Int; let start: Date; init(day: Date, minutes: Int, start: Date) }
struct MonarchTimeGridMove: Hashable, Sendable { let event: MonarchAgendaEvent; let start: Date; let end: Date; init(event: MonarchAgendaEvent, start: Date, end: Date) }
struct MonarchTimeGridUnavailable: Identifiable, Hashable, Sendable { init(id: String, start: Date, end: Date, label: String? = nil) }
struct MonarchTimeGridWorkingHours: Hashable, Sendable { init(weekday: Int, start: Int, end: Int) }

struct MonarchTimeGridLabels: Sendable { init(allDay: String? = nil, createEvent: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, today: String? = nil, openDay: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, range: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, moveEarlier: String? = nil, moveLater: String? = nil, moveToPreviousDay: String? = nil, moveToNextDay: String? = nil) }

options.name: days
options.description: The day columns in order, any time on each day: one for a day view, seven for a week.

options.name: events
options.description: The events, the same model as MonarchAgendaList. Timed events are placed by start and end (exclusive); all-day events go in the all-day row of each day they cover.

options.name: now
options.description: The current time for the now line and today's heading; nil hides both. Pass it from TimelineView(.everyMinute) to keep the line moving.

options.name: startHour
options.description: The first visible hour, 0 to 23.

options.name: endHour
options.description: The end of the visible hours (exclusive), 1 to 24. At least one hour is shown.

options.name: hourHeight
options.description: The height of one hour. nil is 48 points scaled with Dynamic Type.

options.name: snapMinutes
options.description: Taps, drags and VoiceOver moves snap to this many minutes; also the shortest an event is drawn.

options.name: workingHours
options.description: Working hours per ISO weekday in minutes from midnight; time outside them is shaded. nil shades nothing.

options.name: unavailable
options.description: Blocks drawn hatched with an optional label, such as time off or a closure.

options.name: scrollToMinutes
options.description: Minutes from midnight to scroll to when the grid appears and when the first day or the number of days changes. nil is an hour before the earliest visible event, else 08:00.

options.name: showsAllDayRow
options.description: Shows the all-day row even when no all-day event is visible.

options.name: calendar
options.description: The calendar and time zone the grid is drawn in. Events are placed by wall-clock time in it.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: canMoveEvent
options.description: Which events may be moved. nil allows all, when onMoveEvent is set.

options.name: onSelectDay
options.description: Makes the headings of a multi-day grid buttons, for example to open the day view.

options.name: onSelectSlot
options.description: Called when an empty part of a column is tapped, with the time snapped down to snapMinutes. Also adds one VoiceOver button per hour.

options.name: onSelectEvent
options.description: Opens an event, for example in MonarchEventPopover. Without it events are not buttons.

options.name: onMoveEvent
options.description: Turns on moving events by long press and drag and by VoiceOver actions. The grid does not change the events; the app applies or confirms the move.

states.name: week
states.description: Seven columns with weekday and date headings; overlapping events share the column width side by side.

states.name: day
states.description: One column; headings are not buttons.

states.name: today
states.description: Today's date sits on a filled accent circle, its heading is read with "Today", and the now line crosses its column when now is inside the visible hours.

states.name: all-day row
states.description: Shown when an all-day event is visible or showsAllDayRow is on: an "All day" gutter label and bar chips per day.

states.name: working hours
states.description: Time outside the working hours of each weekday is shaded.

states.name: unavailable
states.description: A hatched block with its label; taps still reach the slot under it.

states.name: short event
states.description: Events under 45 minutes are one line, start time then title; events of 70 minutes or more also show their detail.

states.name: moving
states.description: After a press of 0.4 seconds the event fades, a dashed ghost shows the new time and title, scrolling pauses, and haptics mark the pick-up and each step. Releasing calls onMoveEvent when the start changed.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without callbacks the grid only shows events.

appearance: The grid sits on the surface background with subtle border lines for hours and columns and a default border under the heading. Hour labels, weekdays and the all-day label use the muted text colour; today's date is in the accent on-solid colour on an accent solid circle; the now line is the danger solid colour. Shading outside working hours is the muted background, and unavailable blocks are the muted background with strong-border hatching and a label, so the two differ by more than colour. Events are MonarchEventChip blocks in their own colour or the accent. Every role is the theme's, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web TimeGrid reads ISO days in an IANA zone, drags with a pointer only (touch keeps scrolling), moves focus between hour slots with the arrow keys, and takes a renderEvent wrapper. On iOS days are Date values in the given Calendar, moving is long press then drag as in Calendar, with system haptics, and VoiceOver gets named move actions instead of keyboard dragging. There is no renderEvent: onSelectEvent gives the app the event to show in MonarchEventPopover or a sheet. The web's hourCycle prop is the locale's choice on iOS (set the environment locale). Events reuse MonarchAgendaEvent rather than a separate CalendarEvent type. iOS has no system day or week grid (EventKitUI does not offer one), so this is a custom view. Android has no TimeGrid yet. Several closures are optional (canMoveEvent, onSelectDay, onSelectSlot, onSelectEvent, onMoveEvent). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canMoveEvent.
accessibility: Each day heading is one element read as "Wednesday 4 November", with ", Today" on today; it has the header trait, or is a button with the hint "Opens Wednesday 4 November" when onSelectDay is set in a multi-day grid.
Each event is a MonarchEventChip read as one element: title, time spoken in full ("9:30 to 11:00"), status and detail; with onSelectEvent it is a button.

A movable event has the VoiceOver actions Move earlier, Move later (by snapMinutes), Move to previous day and Move to next day, each offered only when the move is possible, so it can be rescheduled without dragging.
With onSelectSlot every hour of every column is a button read as "Create event, Wednesday 4 November, 09:00".
Each column is a container named with its long date; the all-day cell of each day is a container named "Wednesday 4 November, All day".
Unavailable blocks are read with their label and times; shading, the hour gutter, grid lines, the now line and the drag ghost are hidden.
Today is marked by a word and a filled shape, not by colour alone.
Hour height, gutter width and text scale with Dynamic Type; day headings that are buttons keep a 44-point touch target.
Haptics use the system's sensoryFeedback: impact when an event is picked up, selection at each step.
edgeCases: Daylight-saving days still show 24 rows: events are placed by wall-clock time, so a skipped hour leaves a gap and a repeated hour overlaps; a slot in a skipped hour starts at the next valid time.
An event that ends exactly at midnight does not appear on the next day; a multi-day timed event is clipped on each day it touches.
Events outside startHour to endHour are hidden; events crossing the edges are clipped.
An event with no end, or an end before its start, is drawn snapMinutes long.
A moved event keeps its duration; a move is clamped so the whole event stays in the visible hours, and a move that would not change the start is not reported.
Many overlapping events in a narrow week column become thin; open the day view for detail.
Event ids must be unique.

parityExceptions.reason: The web grid has 686 px for five days, so day names sit beside the number in capitals and event text has room. On a phone the day columns are about 60 pt wide, so the name sits above the number and event text is shortened; the events, times and tones are the same.
parityExceptions.convention: adaptive layout: day columns narrower on a phone (HIG: Layout)

name: MonarchTimeOffPanel
title: TimeOffPanel
wrapsNative: A VStack of rows with MonarchBadge, MonarchFlowLayout and MonarchDivider; Toggle with .toggleStyle(.monarchCheckbox) for Include past; sheet(isPresented:) holding a NavigationStack and Form with Picker, Toggle, DatePicker (.date, and date and time) and TextField(axis: .vertical) for the add form; confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:presenting:actions:message:) with Button(role: .destructive) to remove; MonarchBanner, MonarchEmptyState and MonarchLoadingState for the states; Date.FormatStyle in the panel's time zone
summary: Lists time off (holidays, sickness, training, closures) and adds or removes it: an Include past checkbox, an add form in a sheet and a destructive confirmation to remove; the app saves.
whenToUse: In a booking or staffing product, on the screen where people or a manager plan the periods when nobody can be booked.
whenNotToUse: For the calendar view of who is away, use MonarchTeamCalendar. For a single date range in a form, use MonarchDateRangePicker. For working hours, use the availability editor.
api: init(entries: [MonarchTimeOffEntry], timeZone: TimeZone? = nil, now: Date = Date(), people: [MonarchTimeOffOption] = [], allowsClosure: Bool = false, types: [MonarchTimeOffOption] = [], showsPast: Binding<Bool>? = nil, isLoading: Bool = false, errorMessage: String? = nil, notice: String? = nil, labels: MonarchTimeOffPanelLabels = MonarchTimeOffPanelLabels(), canRemove: ((MonarchTimeOffEntry) -> Bool)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onAdd: (@MainActor (MonarchTimeOffDraft) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onRemove: (@MainActor (MonarchTimeOffEntry) async throws -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchTimeOffEntry.init(id: String, personID: String?, personName: String? = nil, isAllDay: Bool, start: Date, end: Date, type: String? = nil, reason: String? = nil, status: String? = nil)
MonarchTimeOffOption.init(_ label: String, value: String)
MonarchTimeOffDraft.init(personID: String?, isAllDay: Bool, start: Date, end: Date, type: String? = nil, reason: String? = nil)

struct MonarchTimeOffPanelLabels { var title, message, add, includePast, closure, everyone, past, allDay, allDayToggle, removeTitle, removeMessage, removeConfirm, emptyTitle, emptyMessage, retry, loading, formTitle, formMessage, who, type, closureNotice, from, until, start, end, reason, reasonHelper, cancel, save, endBeforeStart, failed: String?; var remove: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? }

options.name: entries
options.description: The periods to list, in display order. A nil personID is a closure for everyone.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The time zone entries are shown and entered in; the add form's pickers use it. nil is the device's zone (.autoupdatingCurrent), read each time.

options.name: now
options.description: Now, to mark and hide past entries and to start the add form.

options.name: people
options.description: The people the add form offers in Who. With one person and no closure, Who is hidden.

options.name: allowsClosure
options.description: Adds Everyone to Who: a closure that blocks bookings for everyone.

options.name: types
options.description: The kinds of time off the add form offers in Type, such as leave types.

options.name: showsPast
options.description: Whether past entries are listed; load past entries when it turns on if the product pages them. nil keeps it inside the panel, off at first.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows placeholder rows instead of the list.

options.name: errorMessage
options.description: Shows a danger banner with this message instead of the list.

options.name: notice
options.description: An information banner above the list, such as "2 appointments fall in this period".

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: canRemove
options.description: Whether an entry can be removed. By default every entry, when onRemove is set.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Try again to the error banner.

options.name: onAdd
options.description: Adds time off from the form and shows the Add time off button. Throw to keep the form open with the error's description.

options.name: onRemove
options.description: Removes an entry after the confirmation. Throw to show the error above the list.

states.name: list
states.description: A row per entry: who (or Everyone) with badges for a closure (warning), the type (neutral), the status (info) and Past (neutral outline), then the dates and the reason, and a remove button.

states.name: past hidden
states.description: With Include past off, entries that ended (all-day ones before today, timed ones before now) are not listed.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchEmptyState "No time off planned" with its message.

states.name: loading
states.description: Placeholder rows named "Loading time off".

states.name: error
states.description: A danger MonarchBanner with the message and, with onRetry, Try again.

states.name: adding
states.description: A sheet with Who, a closure notice, Type, All day, From and Until (or Start and End with times), the time zone, and a reason of at most 200 characters. Add is disabled while the end is before the start; while onAdd runs it shows progress and the sheet cannot be dismissed; a failure is a danger banner in the form and is announced.

states.name: removing
states.description: The system confirmation dialog "Remove this time off?" with the entry, a destructive Remove and Cancel; while onRemove runs the row's button is a progress indicator; a failure is a danger banner above the list and is announced.

appearance: The title in the subheading style with a muted description, the primary add button, rows separated by dividers with the name in the default text role and the dates in the muted role, badges in their tone roles, and the remove symbol in the muted role. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and both high-contrast themes follow; the form and the dialog are the system's.
platformNotes: The web shows the add form in a Dialog; iOS uses a sheet with a Form and toolbar buttons, and removes with the system confirmation dialog instead of the web's ConfirmDialog. The panel is a column of rows rather than a List, so it can sit in a scroll view with other content, and removing is a button and a VoiceOver action rather than a swipe, which needs a List. Entries hold Date values instead of ISO strings: all-day entries are the first moment of the first and last day in timeZone. The web's hourCycle is not offered (the locale and the person's 24-hour setting decide), nor headingLevel (the title has the header trait). The web keeps the confirmation open while onRemove runs; on iOS the dialog closes and the row shows progress. Add is disabled while the dates are wrong instead of reporting it after a submit, and the web's "Fill in the dates." never applies because the pickers always hold a date. Android has no TimeOffPanel yet. Experimental until a Rook app adopts it. Several closures are optional (canRemove, onRetry, onAdd, onRemove). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canRemove.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.

Each entry is one element read as who, the badges and the dates, such as "Ana Lima, Annual leave, Pending, Mon, Nov 9, 2026 – Fri, Nov 13, 2026 (all day) · Family visit"; Closure and Past are words, not colour alone.
The remove button is named "Remove time off for Ana Lima, …", has a 44-point touch target, and is also a VoiceOver action on the entry.
Include past is a checkbox-styled Toggle, read as a switch with its value.
The add form uses system pickers, a switch and a text field, each with its label; the date problem is shown with an icon and text.
A failure to add or remove is announced.
edgeCases: An all-day entry that ends today is not past until tomorrow; a timed entry is past once its end has passed.
A timed entry that runs over midnight shows both days; the same entry can fall on another day in another time zone.
Moving From after Until moves Until with it.
The reason is trimmed, sent as nil when empty, and kept to 200 characters.
With no people and no closure, the draft's personID is nil; the app decides whose time off it is.
Long names, types and statuses wrap; badges flow onto the next line.

examples.title: Add and remove
examples.template:
MonarchTimeOffPanel(
    entries: entries,
    timeZone: TimeZone(identifier: {{timeZone}}),
    now: {{now|date}},
    people: [MonarchTimeOffOption({{people.0.label}}, value: {{people.0.value}}), MonarchTimeOffOption({{people.1.label}}, value: {{people.1.value}})],

                start: draft.start,
                end: draft.end,

name: MonarchTimesheetDiff
title: TimesheetDiff
wrapsNative: VStack of Text lines with strikethrough, MonarchIcon, Date.FormatStyle and Duration.UnitsFormatStyle
summary: What changed between two versions of a timesheet: added, removed and changed entries, each named in words with its effect on the time, and a totals line.
whenToUse: When a timesheet is resubmitted or corrected, and in approval review, so the approver sees exactly which entries changed and how the total moved.
whenNotToUse: Not for the timesheet itself; use a list or grid of entries. Not for the change history of any record; use an activity feed.
api: init(_ diff: MonarchTimesheetDiffResult, title: String? = nil, subtitle: String? = nil, showsTotals: Bool = true, showsBillable: Bool = true, labels: MonarchTimesheetDiffLabels = MonarchTimesheetDiffLabels())

init(before: [MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry], after: [MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry], title: String? = nil, subtitle: String? = nil, showsTotals: Bool = true, showsBillable: Bool = true, labels: MonarchTimesheetDiffLabels = MonarchTimesheetDiffLabels())

struct MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry: Identifiable { init(id: String, date: Date, minutes: Int, project: String? = nil, activity: String? = nil, task: String? = nil, isBillable: Bool? = nil, note: String? = nil) }

struct MonarchTimesheetDiffResult { init(added: [MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry] = [], removed: [MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry] = [], changed: [MonarchTimesheetDiffChange] = []); init(before: [MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry], after: [MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry]); var isEmpty: Bool; var totals: MonarchTimesheetDiffTotals }
struct MonarchTimesheetDiffChange: Identifiable { init(id: String, fields: [MonarchTimesheetDiffField], before: MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry, after: MonarchTimesheetDiffEntry) }
struct MonarchTimesheetDiffField: RawRepresentable { init(_ name: String); static let date, minutes, project, activity, task, billable, note, start, end }
struct MonarchTimesheetDiffTotals { init(total: Int, billable: Int) }
struct MonarchTimesheetDiffLabels { init(title:added:removed:changed:fields:before:after:noProject:nonBillable:noChanges:delta:totals:entry:), every parameter optional }

options.name: diff
options.description: The entries added, removed and changed, when the product computes the difference itself.

options.name: before, after
options.description: The two versions; entries are matched by id and compared on date, minutes, project, activity, task, isBillable and note.

options.name: title
options.description: The heading. Built in: "What changed".

options.name: subtitle
options.description: Quiet text after the heading, such as "since version 3".

options.name: showsTotals
options.description: Shows the totals line.

options.name: showsBillable
options.description: Adds the billable change to the totals line. Turn it off when billing does not apply.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, the field names, the delta and totals formats, and the line of an entry (the web's renderEntry, as text).

states.name: added
states.description: A success-tinted line with a success bar, a plus symbol and "Added"; the entry and the time gained.

states.name: removed
states.description: A danger-tinted line with a minus symbol and "Removed"; the entry struck through in the muted colour and the time lost.

states.name: changed
states.description: A warning-tinted line with a pencil symbol and "Changed time, project"; the old line struck through above the new one, and the change of time when there is one.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No changes." in the muted colour.

appearance: Each change is a rounded line on the subtle fill of its tone (success, danger or warning) with a bar in the tone's border colour at the leading edge; the kind is in the tone's strong colour with a symbol. Changes of time and the totals are captions in the muted colour with tabular digits. The heading is the label type role, semibold, with the subtitle muted. All colours are theme roles, so the dark and high-contrast themes need nothing else.
platformNotes: The web takes ISO date strings; here the day is a Date shown in the environment's time zone. The web's renderEntry returns any content; here labels.entry returns the line as text, which is also what VoiceOver reads. The web's open-ended field names are a MonarchTimesheetDiffField value, with the compared fields built in and room for a product's own. The web's headingLevel has no iOS equivalent; the title has the header trait. Durations ("1h 30m") follow the web's compact form and are not localised; replace them with labels.delta and labels.entry, or rely on VoiceOver, which reads durations in words in the user's locale. The parity map named the badge and tabular-number components; the kind is shown as text with a symbol, as on the web, and digits use monospacedDigit.
accessibility: The title is a heading.
Each change is one element: "Removed, minus 45 minutes, Mon, Jan 12, 45 minutes, Pulse, non-billable"; a changed entry adds "Before" and "After" before its two lines.
Durations are read in words in the user's locale ("1 hour, 30 minutes").
The kind is a word and a symbol as well as a colour; a removed entry and the old line of a changed one are struck through.
Text wraps and scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: An empty project is shown as "No project".
isBillable nil counts as billable in the totals, as on the web; only false is non-billable.
A changed entry whose time did not change shows no change of time.
A missing value and an empty one are different, so nil to "" is a change.
Field names the strings table does not know are shown by their raw name.
Order: added, then removed, then changed, each in the order of its version.

name: MonarchTimesheetGrid
title: TimesheetGrid
wrapsNative: Grid with GridRow inside a horizontal ScrollView at regular width; at compact width one day per page with MonarchDurationInput (TextField and Stepper) per row; Menu for row actions
summary: A period of time entry, usually a week: rows of projects or tasks against days, with typed durations, row, day and period totals, locked days and a daily limit.
whenToUse: For weekly time entry and review in time-tracking, payroll and project apps, where people log time per project per day and see the totals as they type.
whenNotToUse: Not for a single duration; use MonarchDurationInput. Not for showing what changed between versions of a timesheet; use MonarchTimesheetDiff. Not for general tabular data; use MonarchDataTable.
api: init(days: [MonarchTimesheetGridDay], rows: [MonarchTimesheetGridRow], summaryRows: [MonarchTimesheetGridSummaryRow] = [], maximumMinutesPerDay: Int = 1440, layout: MonarchTimesheetGridLayout = .automatic, isReadOnly: Bool = false, emptyMessage: String? = nil, labels: MonarchTimesheetGridLabels = MonarchTimesheetGridLabels(), rowActions: ((MonarchTimesheetGridRow) -> [MonarchDataTableRowAction])? = nil, onDayActivate: (@MainActor (Date) -> Void)? = nil, onCellActivate: (@MainActor (String, Date) -> Void)? = nil, onCellChange: (@MainActor (String, Date, Int) async throws -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchTimesheetGridDay: Identifiable { init(_ date: Date, label: String? = nil, isToday: Bool = false, isNonWorking: Bool = false, isLocked: Bool = false, lockReason: String? = nil, note: String? = nil, expectedMinutes: Int? = nil) }
struct MonarchTimesheetGridRow: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, cells: [Date: Int] = [:], isReadOnly: Bool = false); func minutes(on date: Date) -> Int }
struct MonarchTimesheetGridSummaryRow: Identifiable { init(id: String, label: String, cells: [Date: String], total: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchTimesheetGridLayout { case automatic, grid, day }

struct MonarchTimesheetGridLabels { init(caption:rowHeader:total:dayTotal:rowActions:cellLabel:locked:noTime:invalid:tooLong:saveFailed:expected:overLimit:empty:today:saving:previousDay:nextDay:rowTotal:duration:shortDay:longDay:), every parameter optional }

options.name: days
options.description: The days in order, usually a week. A day can be today, non-working, locked (with a reason), carry a note and an expected number of minutes.

options.name: rows
options.description: The rows with their minutes per day, keyed by the day's date. A read-only row never takes typing.

options.name: summaryRows
options.description: Display-only footer rows with text per day, such as attendance.

options.name: maximumMinutesPerDay
options.description: The largest value a cell accepts, and the day total above which a day is flagged.

options.name: layout
options.description: A grid at regular width and one day per page at compact width and the accessibility text sizes; .grid or .day forces one.

options.name: isReadOnly
options.description: Makes every cell read-only, for example after submission.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: Shown when there are no rows. Built in: "No time logged for this period."

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, the duration formatter and the day formatters.

options.name: rowActions
options.description: The actions of a row, in a menu beside its name, such as clearing the row.

options.name: onDayActivate
options.description: Makes day headings buttons, for example to open a day view.

options.name: onCellActivate
options.description: Makes read-only cells with time buttons, for example to open the entries behind them. Receives the row identifier and the day.

options.name: onCellChange
options.description: Saves a typed value: row identifier, day and minutes (0 clears). The cell is disabled while it runs; a thrown error is shown on the cell. Without it, every cell is read-only.

states.name: editable
states.description: Open cells are bordered fields; typing is read on Return or when focus leaves, and the value is passed to onCellChange.

states.name: saving
states.description: The cell is disabled, its text muted, and its hint reads "Saving" until onCellChange returns.

states.name: error
states.description: Text that cannot be read, a value above the daily maximum or a failed save gives the cell a danger border and shows the message with a warning symbol under the grid (in the day layout, under the field); the message is announced and the typed text is kept.

states.name: locked day
states.description: The day's heading shows a lock symbol and the reason; its cells are shaded, muted and read-only, and read with the reason.

states.name: read-only row or grid
states.description: Cells show the time as text (a dash when empty). With onCellActivate, cells with time are link-coloured buttons.

states.name: today
states.description: The heading is in the accent colour with an accent bar under it and is read with "Today".

states.name: non-working day
states.description: The column (or the day page header) is shaded; entry is still allowed.

states.name: over the daily limit
states.description: The day total is in the danger colour with a warning symbol and is read with "Over the daily limit".

states.name: empty
states.description: Without rows the grid shows the empty message in place of the rows; without days the day layout shows only the message.

appearance: The grid sits on the surface with subtle-border separators between rows; headings and the first column use the label style, with the muted text colour for the column headings, descriptions, notes and summary rows. Locked and non-working columns use the subtle background; today's heading uses the strong accent colour with a bar in the solid accent; errors and over-limit totals use the strong danger colour with a symbol. Fields use the input border on the surface, like MonarchTextField. All roles come from the theme, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web always renders a table that scrolls sideways; on a phone that is hard to use, so at compact width (and at the accessibility text sizes) this shows one day per page with previous and next buttons, a MonarchDurationInput with its system Stepper for each editable row, and the row's period total under its name. The web keys days and cells by ISO date strings; here the key is the day's Date, the same value in days and in each row's cells. The web's label, markers and summary cells accept any content; here they are text. The web's row-actions slot takes any content; here row actions are MonarchDataTableRowAction values in a Menu beside the row name, the same type MonarchDataTable uses, and they sit in the first column rather than a separate actions column. The web moves between cells with all four arrow keys; here, with a hardware keyboard, Return saves and moves down, up and down arrows move between cells, Tab follows the system order and left and right arrows move the text cursor. VoiceOver has no table navigation over a SwiftUI Grid; each cell is named by its row and day instead. Android uses the same name, MonarchTimesheetGrid. Several closures are optional (rowActions, onDayActivate, onCellActivate, onCellChange). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is rowActions.
accessibility: The grid is a container named "Time per row and day" (overridable with labels.caption).

Column headings, day headings and row names have the header trait; a day heading is one element read as the day, "Today", the lock reason and the note, such as "Mon, Jan 12, Approved, Payroll closed".
Each cell is named by its row and day, such as "Atlas, Tue, Jan 13"; a read-only cell's value is the time in words in the person's locale and the lock reason, such as "No time, Approved".
An editable cell is a text field whose hint is its error ("Error: …") or "Saving" while it is being saved.
Day totals are named "Day total, <day>" and read the time in words, the expected time and "Over the daily limit"; row totals are named "<row>, Total".
Errors are announced when they appear, and shown with a symbol and text, not colour alone. Locked days have a lock symbol, today a bar, over-limit totals a warning symbol.
In the day layout the day title is adjustable (swipe up or down to change day), and the previous and next buttons are labelled "Previous day" and "Next day" and disabled at the ends.
Day headings with onDayActivate and cells with onCellActivate have the button trait.
Cells, fields and buttons are at least 44 points high; text scales with Dynamic Type and the column widths scale with it.
edgeCases: Negative minutes in cells count as 0.
Cells keyed by a date that is not in days are ignored in every total.
Empty text clears the cell: onCellChange receives 0.
A value equal to the saved one is not passed to onCellChange.
If onCellChange succeeds but the app does not update rows, the typed text stays in the cell.
A lockReason locks the day even when isLocked is false.
The first day page is today, else the first day; the page stays where the person moved it.
Long row names and notes wrap; the grid scrolls sideways when the columns do not fit.
isReadOnly wins over onCellChange.

A zone the system does not know shows an offset of UTC+00:00 and no long name.

name: MonarchToast
title: Toast
wrapsNative: overlay(alignment:), Observation (@Observable), AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: Transient notifications: a MonarchToastCenter that holds them, a host modifier that draws them over the content at one edge, and the MonarchToast value.
whenToUse: To confirm something that just happened without interrupting, optionally with one action such as Undo.
whenNotToUse: For a message that must be read or answered, use the system alert modifier. For a status that should stay beside its content, use MonarchBanner. Do not put the only way to recover from an error in a toast, because it closes by itself.
api: struct MonarchToast { init(_ title: String, message: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, actionTitle: String? = nil, duration: TimeInterval? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) }
final class MonarchToastCenter { init(limit: Int = 3, durationScale: Double = 1) }
var toasts: [MonarchToast] { get }
let limit: Int
var durationScale: Double
func show(_ toast: MonarchToast) -> UUID

func show(_ title: String, message: String? = nil, tone: MonarchTone = .neutral, actionTitle: String? = nil, duration: TimeInterval? = nil, action: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onDismiss: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil) -> UUID
func dismiss(_ id: UUID)
func dismissAll()
func monarchToastHost(_ center: MonarchToastCenter, position: MonarchToastPosition = .bottom, dismissLabel: String? = nil) -> some View
enum MonarchToastPosition { case bottom, top }

options.name: title
options.description: A short headline.

options.name: message
options.description: One line of detail.

options.name: tone
options.description: Selects the icon and its colour.

options.name: actionTitle
options.description: Title of the action button. No button without it and action.

options.name: duration
options.description: Seconds before the toast closes itself. nil is 5, or 10 for the danger tone and for a toast with an action. .infinity keeps it until dismissed.

options.name: action
options.description: Runs when the action button is activated; the toast then closes.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Runs once when the toast closes for any reason (time, dismiss, swipe, a newer toast, the app). After the action button it runs after action.

options.name: limit
options.description: On the center: how many toasts are shown at once. Older ones close first.

options.name: durationScale
options.description: On the center: multiplies every duration. .infinity turns closing by time off.

options.name: position
options.description: On the host: the edge where toasts appear.

options.name: dismissLabel
options.description: On the host: replaces the built-in "Dismiss" spoken name of the close button.

states.name: shown
states.description: Slides in from its edge and fades in; appears at once when Reduce Motion is on.

states.name: closed
states.description: By its timer, the dismiss button, the action, a drag towards its edge, dismiss(_:), dismissAll(), or when newer toasts exceed the limit.

appearance: A raised surface with 12-point corners, the default border and the large elevation shadow. The icon is in the strong colour of the tone, the title in the default text colour and the message in the muted text colour. Toasts are at most 640 points wide and stack with the newest nearest the content.
platformNotes: iOS has no toast, so this is built. The host is a SwiftUI overlay inside the safe area of the view it is applied to. It does not sit above sheets and full-screen covers, which the plan asked for: that needs a separate UIWindow, which was not built because it could not be tested without a device. Until then, apply the host to the content of a sheet, with a center of its own. Being inside the safe area, the bottom position moves above the keyboard. Toasts are shown through a MonarchToastCenter from the environment, where the web has a global toast() function and a provider. Timers do not pause while a toast is touched or while VoiceOver focus is on it; set durationScale, or an infinite duration, where that matters. The web's hotkey, offsets and three positions become top and bottom. There is no altText for the action. Android themes the Material 3 SnackbarHost. Several closures are optional (action, onDismiss). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is action.
accessibility: Showing a toast posts an announcement with the tone name, the title and the message. The danger tone is announced with high priority, the others with the default priority.
The icon, title and message are one element, read as the tone name, the title, then the message, so the tone does not depend on colour.
The action and the dismiss button are separate buttons with touch targets of at least 44 points; the drag gesture is never the only way to close a toast.
The slide and fade are not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
The action moves under the text when both do not fit on one line.
A toast closes by time even while VoiceOver is reading it; durationScale lengthens or turns off the timers.
edgeCases: actionTitle without action, or action without actionTitle, shows no button, and the toast uses the short duration.
A negative duration closes the toast at once.
Changing durationScale affects toasts shown afterwards.
Without the host modifier above it, reading the center from the environment is a runtime error, as for any @Observable environment object.
A toast behind a sheet is not visible.

whenNotToUse: For a setting in a list, use a plain Toggle (a switch). For selecting items or agreeing to terms, use the checkbox style. For one choice from a set, use a segmented Picker.

name: MonarchToggleGroup
title: ToggleGroup
wrapsNative: Toggle with MonarchToggleButtonStyle (.toggleStyle(.monarchButton)), in MonarchFlowLayout or VStackLayout
summary: Related toggle buttons in one named group, with any number on (a Set binding) or at most one on (an optional binding).
whenToUse: For a formatting toolbar, list filters or view options where several on/off choices belong together, or a toolbar choice where at most one is on.
whenNotToUse: When exactly one of a few views is always chosen, use Picker with .pickerStyle(.segmented). For settings saved with a form, use Toggle or Picker in a Form. For more than about seven options, use a Menu or Picker.
api: init(_ title: String, selection: Binding<Set<Value>>, options: [MonarchToggleGroupOption<Value>], variant: MonarchToggleButtonVariant = .ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, axis: Axis = .horizontal)

init(_ title: String, selection: Binding<Value?>, options: [MonarchToggleGroupOption<Value>], variant: MonarchToggleButtonVariant = .ghost, size: MonarchButtonSize = .md, isRequired: Bool = false, axis: Axis = .horizontal)
MonarchToggleGroupOption.init(_ value: Value, label: String, systemImage: String? = nil, count: String? = nil, isIconOnly: Bool = false, isDisabled: Bool = false)

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the group, spoken by VoiceOver and not shown.

options.name: selection
options.description: The values that are on. A Set allows any number; an optional allows at most one.

options.name: options
options.description: The items in order: value, label, optional symbol, count, icon-only and disabled flags.

options.name: variant
options.description: ghost or outline: how items are drawn while off.

options.name: size
options.description: sm, md or lg for every item.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Single choice only: turning off the selected item is ignored, so one stays on.

options.name: axis
options.description: A row that wraps onto new rows, or a column.

states.name: off
states.description: An item is drawn as a toggle button that is off (no fill for ghost, a bordered surface for outline).

states.name: on
states.description: An item has the accent subtle fill, accent border and accent text; with Differentiate Without Colour it also shows a checkmark.

states.name: disabled
states.description: An item with isDisabled, or the whole group with disabled(_:), uses the disabled roles and does not respond.

appearance: Items are MonarchToggleButtonStyle toggles: on items use the accent subtle fill, accent border and strong accent text; off items use muted text, with the surface fill and default border for outline. Counts use the subtle text colour. Colours come from theme roles in every theme.
platformNotes: The web ToggleGroup has one Tab stop with arrow keys, Home and End, and a loop option; on iOS each item is a separate VoiceOver element and keyboard focus follows the system, so those options are not offered. The web value "" for nothing selected is nil here. The web xs size is not offered on touch. Android covers toggle-group with a style on its theme instead of a type; iOS ships this wrapper because a group needs one selection binding for single and multiple choice.
accessibility: The group is a container whose label is the title.
Each item is a standard Toggle given to VoiceOver through MonarchToggleButtonStyle, read with its label and its on or off value.
An item with a count is read as the label, a comma and the count, such as "Open, 12".
An icon-only item is read by its label; the symbol is decorative.
With Differentiate Without Colour an on item also shows a checkmark, so the state is not colour alone.
Every item has a touch target of at least 44 by 44 points and scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A horizontal group wraps onto new rows at large text sizes or with many items.
With isRequired and nothing selected, the first tap selects an item; after that one item stays on.
Values must be unique; they identify the items.
With a Set binding the order of the values is not kept; read them in the order of options.

title: Toolbar
wrapsNative: toolbar(content:) with ToolbarItem(placement: .primaryAction) and ToolbarItemGroup(placement: .secondaryAction or .bottomBar), with searchable(text:prompt:) for the search field and safeAreaInset(edge: .top) for a row of filters
summary: The controls above a list (search, view switch, density, export, filters) live in the system's navigation bar and bottom bar, not in a row drawn by Monarch.
whenToUse: For the tools of a list or a document screen: put the search field in searchable, the main tool in .primaryAction, less used tools in .secondaryAction (they collapse into an overflow menu), and filter chips in a safeAreaInset row under the bar.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a toolbar row inside the content; it scrolls away and repeats what the bars do. For a formatting bar inside an editor, an HStack of Toggles with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()) is enough. For a call, use MonarchCallControls.
api: func toolbar<Content: ToolbarContent>(content: () -> Content) -> some View
ToolbarItem(placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic, content: () -> Content)
ToolbarItemGroup(placement: ToolbarItemPlacement = .automatic, content: () -> Content)
func searchable(text: Binding<String>, placement: SearchFieldPlacement = .automatic, prompt: String) -> some View
func safeAreaInset(edge: VerticalEdge, alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, content: () -> some View) -> some View

states.name: compact width
states.description: Secondary actions collapse into the system's overflow menu; the primary action stays in the bar.

states.name: search active
states.description: The search field takes the top of the screen while it is focused (system behaviour).

states.name: disabled
states.description: A disabled item uses the system's disabled colour and is skipped by VoiceOver activation.

appearance: System bars. Items that are Buttons or Menus take the accent tint of the Monarch theme; filter chips in the inset row use the Monarch toggle button style. Correct in light, dark and both high-contrast themes because the system draws the bars.
platformNotes: The web Toolbar is a role="toolbar" row with search on the leading edge, grouped controls, trailing controls, a filters row and roving arrow-key focus. On iOS the navigation bar and the bottom bar are the toolbar: the system places, overflows and focuses the items, and a hardware keyboard moves between them with Tab. Monarch ships no toolbar type. .bottomBar and .topBarTrailing exist on iOS only; the compiled examples use the placements shared with the host build. Android uses its top app bar.
accessibility: Bar items are read as buttons with their titles; give icon-only items a title through Label or Button(_:systemImage:), which the bar shows as an icon and VoiceOver reads (system behaviour).
The search field is the system's, with its own label and clear button.
Filter chips with .toggleStyle(.monarchButton()) are read as toggles with their on or off value.
Bar items have the system's touch targets.
edgeCases: Too many primary items crowd the bar on a small phone; keep one or two and move the rest to .secondaryAction.
A safeAreaInset filter row with many chips scrolls horizontally; it does not wrap.
Items placed with .secondaryAction show in an overflow menu on iPhone and in the bar on iPad (system behaviour), not checked on an iPad.
The catalogue page places its items in the catalogue's own bar; the examples bring their own NavigationStack.

title: Tooltip
wrapsNative: help(_:), which sets the accessibility hint; accessibilityLabel(_:) for the name of the control
summary: iOS shows no tooltip. The help modifier carries the same supplementary text: on iOS and iPadOS it becomes the accessibility hint, and where the system has tooltips (an app running on a Mac, visionOS) it is shown as one. Monarch ships nothing, and nothing essential may live in help text.
whenToUse: To clarify what an icon-only control does, together with accessibilityLabel for its name. VoiceOver reads the name, then the help text as the hint.
whenNotToUse: Not for anything a person needs in order to use the screen: on a phone or tablet it is never seen. Put that text on screen, or in a popover opened by an info button.
api: func help(_ text: String) -> some View
func accessibilityLabel(_ label: String) -> some View
func accessibilityHint(_ hint: String) -> some View

states.name: touch
states.description: Nothing is shown.

states.name: VoiceOver
states.description: The help text is read as the hint, after the name and a pause.

states.name: pointer on a Mac or visionOS
states.description: The system shows the help text beside the control after a short delay.

appearance: Nothing is drawn on iOS and iPadOS. Where the system shows a tooltip it draws it itself; Monarch colours and type are not applied.
platformNotes: The web Tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus, with a side, an alignment and a delay. The parity map expected help(_:) to show on pointer and keyboard on iPad; according to the SwiftUI documentation it shows a help tag only on macOS and visionOS and otherwise configures the accessibility hint, so on iPadOS a pointer shows nothing. The web's content must become plain text. Android uses the Material 3 PlainTooltip, which opens on long press; iOS has no equivalent, so a control that needs explaining on touch gets a visible label, or an info button that opens a popover.
accessibility: An icon-only control needs accessibilityLabel for its name; help is not a name.
help(_:) configures the accessibility hint, so VoiceOver reads it after the name. accessibilityHint(_:) sets the hint directly when the spoken text should differ.
Write the hint as the result of the action ("Shows only unpaid invoices"), without the word button and without the name again.
People can turn hints off in VoiceOver settings, so a hint must not carry information the label lacks.
edgeCases: On an iPhone and an iPad the help text is never visible.
Keep the text to one short sentence; it is read aloud in full.
The reason a control is disabled belongs on screen, not in help text.

title: TopNav
wrapsNative: TabView with tabItem(_:); from iOS 18 also tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable), behind an availability check
summary: A row of top-level destinations is the app's TabView, which the system places for the device: the tab bar on iOS 17, and from iPadOS 18 a bar at the top that can become a sidebar. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For the few top-level areas of an app. Declare them once as tabs and let the system place them for the device and the OS version.
whenNotToUse: Do not draw a horizontal row of links at the top of a screen as app navigation. For views of one screen's content use MonarchTabs; for many destinations use a sidebar (see sidebar-nav).
api: TabView(selection: Binding<SelectionValue>?, content: () -> Content)
func tabItem(_ label: () -> some View) -> some View
func tabViewStyle(_ style: some TabViewStyle) -> some View
static var sidebarAdaptable: SidebarAdaptableTabViewStyle (iOS 18.0 and later)

states.name: iPhone, and iPad on iOS 17
states.description: The destinations are the tab bar at the bottom.

states.name: iPad on iPadOS 18 and later
states.description: The destinations are a bar at the top; with sidebarAdaptable the person can turn it into a sidebar.

states.name: selected
states.description: The selected destination takes the tint.

appearance: The system draws the bar or the sidebar. The selected destination takes the tint, which monarchTheme sets to the theme's accent.
platformNotes: The parity map named tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) alone. That style is iOS 18 API and does not compile against the iOS 17 deployment target, so the documented answer is TabView with tabItem, adding the style inside if #available(iOS 18.0, *). The web TopNav is a row of links in a header that moves the links that do not fit into a More menu, with start and end slots. On iOS overflow is the system's (the More tab, or the sidebar from iPadOS 18), the start and end slots are toolbar items of the navigation bar, and destinations are views, not links. Android uses the Material navigation suite, which also adapts to the window.
accessibility: System behaviour: the destinations are a tab bar; each is read with its title, position and selected state.
System behaviour: on iPadOS 18 the top bar and the sidebar expose the same items.
Give every destination a title as well as a symbol.
edgeCases: On iOS 17 an iPad shows the same bottom tab bar as an iPhone.
tabViewStyle(.sidebarAdaptable) without the availability check is a compile error for an iOS 17 target.
More than five destinations on a phone become a More tab.

title: TransferOwnershipFlow
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) with a NavigationStack(path:) and navigationDestination(for:) for the three steps, MonarchStepper at the top of each step, MonarchEntityPicker, two MonarchConsequenceLists, MonarchRolePicker and a danger MonarchButton, with interactiveDismissDisabled(_:) while transferring
summary: A recipe, not a component: hand a workspace to another member in three pushed steps (choose the new owner, see what changes for each side, confirm), then wait for them to accept.
whenToUse: When the owner of a workspace or organisation gives ownership to another member, for example before leaving or deleting their account.
whenNotToUse: For changing a member's role other than owner, use MonarchRolePicker in the member's row. For removing a member, use a confirmationDialog.
api: .sheet(isPresented: $isOpen) { NavigationStack(path: $path) { pick.navigationDestination(for: Step.self) { … } }.interactiveDismissDisabled(isTransferring) }
MonarchStepper([MonarchStepperStep(id:label:), …], current: index)
MonarchEntityPicker("New owner", selection: $owner, entities: [MonarchEntityPickerEntity(…, hint: "Only admins can become the owner", isDisabled: true)])
MonarchConsequenceList([MonarchConsequence(.changed, …)], heading: "For you")
MonarchRolePicker("Your role after the transfer", selection: $yourRole, roles:, layout: .compact)
MonarchButton("Transfer ownership", variant: .danger, isLoading: isTransferring, fullWidth: true)

states.name: choose
states.description: Step 1 of 3: the member picker, with members who cannot become the owner disabled and the reason as their hint; Continue is disabled until someone is chosen.

states.name: what changes
states.description: Step 2 of 3: what changes for you and for the new owner, and your role after the transfer.

states.name: confirm
states.description: Step 3 of 3: the danger button, which shows progress while the transfer starts; the sheet cannot be swiped away.

states.name: pending
states.description: The sheet closes and a banner says the app is waiting for the new owner to accept.

appearance: A system sheet with a navigation bar and the back button on later steps; Monarch's stepper, entity picker, consequence lists, role picker and danger button on the canvas background. Every colour is a theme role, so dark and high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web TransferOwnershipFlow is one component on a WizardDialog with eligibleRoles, a requiresAcceptance mode, a cancel-transfer screen and default consequence messages. On iOS it is a recipe: each step is a screen pushed on a NavigationStack inside the sheet, so the system back button and swipe-back move between steps, and MonarchStepper shows where the person is. Eligibility, the consequences' wording and the pending or immediate result are the app's. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: Each step's navigation title and the stepper's spoken progress (step 2 of 3) tell VoiceOver users where they are.
Members who cannot become the owner are disabled rows that read their reason.
MonarchConsequenceList reads each consequence with its kind, so nothing depends on the icon colour.
Announce the result with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when the sheet closes.
edgeCases: With no eligible member, show MonarchEmptyState on the first step with Invite someone instead of the picker.
Clear the chosen member and pop to the first step each time the sheet opens.
If the transfer fails, stay on the confirm step and show the error with MonarchInlineNotice.
Long member names wrap in the headings For <name>.

title: TreeView
wrapsNative: Buttons in a VStack: a leading chevron, the name over its detail and an edit button per row, nested by depth; List(_:children:selection:rowContent:) remains the choice for the system outline
summary: A hierarchical list with expand and collapse and optional selection is the standard SwiftUI List with a children key path. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For folders, an org chart, categories or a document outline that people expand level by level. Use List(_:children:) for a whole tree, OutlineGroup to mix a tree with other rows in one List, and a recursive DisclosureGroup when children load on demand.
whenNotToUse: For one folding section, use DisclosureGroup with .disclosureGroupStyle(.monarch) or MonarchToggleBlock. For drilling into a deep hierarchy on a phone, use NavigationStack with one list per level, which reads better than deep indentation.
api: List(_ data: Data, children: KeyPath<Data.Element, Data?>, selection: Binding<SelectionValue?>?, rowContent: (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
List(_ data: Data, children: KeyPath<Data.Element, Data?>, selection: Binding<Set<SelectionValue>>?, rowContent: (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
OutlineGroup(_ data: Data, children: KeyPath<Data.Element, Data?>, content: (Data.Element) -> Leaf)
DisclosureGroup(isExpanded: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> Content, label: () -> Label)

states.name: collapsed and expanded
states.description: System disclosure indicator on each parent row; children are indented under it.

states.name: selected
states.description: System row highlight with selection; multiple selection uses a Set binding and edit mode on iPhone.

states.name: loading children
states.description: With a recursive DisclosureGroup, show a ProgressView row while the app loads the children of an expanded node.

appearance: System list rows in every theme. Row content takes Monarch type through monarchTextStyle and colours from the theme; the disclosure indicator and the selection highlight are the system's, tinted by the theme's accent.
platformNotes: The web TreeView implements the APG tree pattern by hand: roving focus, arrow keys, typeahead, single or multiple selection, aria-current, lazy children with a spinner and row actions. On iOS the system list already gives expand and collapse, selection, VoiceOver navigation and hardware keyboard support, so Monarch does not re-implement it. Android builds MonarchTreeView because Compose has no tree list. Not covered natively: typeahead to a row and an outline variant with indentation guides. Row actions belong in swipeActions or contextMenu on the row.
accessibility: System behaviour: parent rows are read with their expanded or collapsed state and can be toggled with VoiceOver; children are announced at their level.
Selection is read as the selected trait.
Give each row a text label (Label or Text); icons in Label are read with the title.
edgeCases: A children array that is empty is a parent with nothing in it; nil is a leaf.
On iPhone, List selection is shown in edit mode or when the list drives a NavigationSplitView; outside them, use a NavigationLink or a button per row.
Deep trees indent further at each level; past three levels prefer drilling down with NavigationStack.

whenNotToUse: For a title that must stay on one line with no way to expand, use Text with lineLimit(1). For long documents, show the text in full on its own screen.

The web accepts inline elements (links, emphasis); this takes a plain String. Whether the text is cut is measured with two hidden copies of the text, because SwiftUI does not report truncation. The button is a standard button whose title changes between "Show more" and "Show less"; both titles can be replaced.
The button's touch target is at least 44 points high.
Expanding and collapsing is animated unless Reduce Motion is on.

With isExpandable false the cut text has no visible way to expand; use it only where the whole text is one tap away.
An empty string shows nothing and no button.
With a binding that is true and text that fits, the button still shows so the state can be turned off.

title: TwoFactorSetup
wrapsNative: VStack with MonarchStepper over three steps: MonarchButton that opens the otpauth URL with openURL, MonarchCopyField for the setup key and a QR code from Core Image's the CIQRCodeGenerator CIFilter as an Image; MonarchOtpPinInput (the .oneTimeCode content type); MonarchRecoveryCodes
summary: A recipe, not a component: turn on two-step verification in three steps: connect an authenticator app, enter a code from it, and save the recovery codes.
whenToUse: In account security settings, when a person turns on two-step verification with an authenticator app.
whenNotToUse: To ask for a code at sign-in, use MonarchOtpPinInput alone. To re-confirm a signed-in person, use MonarchStepUpAuthDialog. For passkeys, use MonarchPasskeyManager.
api: MonarchStepper(steps, current: step)
MonarchButton("Open in authenticator app", systemImage: "key", variant: .primary, fullWidth: true) { openURL(otpauthURL) }
MonarchCopyField("Setup key", value: secret, isLabelHidden: true)
CIFilter(name: "CIQRCodeGenerator") → CIContext().createCGImage → Image(decorative:scale:)
MonarchOtpPinInput("6-digit code", text: $code, error: codeError) { _ in verifyCode() }
MonarchRecoveryCodes(codes, onAcknowledge: { … })

states.name: connect
states.description: Open in authenticator app first, the setup key with a copy button, then the QR code for another device, and Next.

states.name: verify
states.description: A six-cell code field that fills from the keyboard's one-time code suggestion; an incomplete or rejected code shows the field's error.

states.name: verifying
states.description: Verify shows its spinner.

states.name: recovery
states.description: The recovery codes with copy, save to file and the "I have saved my recovery codes" acknowledgement, which finishes the setup.

appearance: Existing Monarch components in the theme: the stepper's markers, a primary button, the copy field's monospaced key, the code cells and the recovery codes grid. The QR code stays black on white in every theme so scanners can read it.
platformNotes: The web's TwoFactorSetup is a dialog component with its own steps and messages, and the QR code first. On a phone the QR code is secondary, since the camera cannot scan the screen it is on: the otpauth link opens the authenticator app on the same device, and the setup key can be copied. iOS has a first-party QR generator in Core Image (the CIQRCodeGenerator filter), so the recipe draws the code itself, or the app passes an Image from its server. Present the recipe in a sheet with presentationDetents([.large]) when it starts from a settings row. Android composes the same recipe and draws or receives the QR code, because Android has no first-party generator.
accessibility: Each step title has the header trait; the stepper reads each step's position and name, such as "Step 2 of 3, Enter a code".
The QR code is one image element named "QR code for your authenticator app"; the setup key beside it gives the same data as text.
The setup key is a copy field whose button announces the copy.
The code field is one element named "6-digit code" with the code as its value; errors are shown and read in words.
The recovery codes are a named group with their own acknowledgement toggle.
edgeCases: Group the setup key in fours for reading, but copy and encode it without spaces in the otpauth link.
If no authenticator app is installed, opening the otpauth link fails; the setup key still works.
A rejected code usually means the device clock is wrong; say so in the error.

title: useUndoToast
wrapsNative: MonarchToastCenter.show with actionTitle "Undo", and a Task that commits the change when the undo window ends
summary: A recipe, not a component: "Note deleted. Undo" for a reversible change the app has already applied, with a toast that offers Undo and a commit that runs when the window closes.
whenToUse: For low-stakes deletes and moves that are applied at once and can be put back: archive, delete a note, remove from a list.
whenNotToUse: For changes that cannot be undone, ask first with a confirmationDialog or MonarchTypeToConfirmInput. For a change that is not destructive, a plain toast or nothing.
api: MonarchToastCenter.show(_ title: String, message: String?, tone: MonarchTone, actionTitle: String?, duration: TimeInterval?, action: (() -> Void)?) -> UUID
Task { try? await Task.sleep(for:); guard !Task.isCancelled … }

states.name: offered
states.description: A neutral toast with the past-tense title and an Undo button, for 8 seconds (5 to 10 is the range the web uses).

states.name: undone
states.description: The action cancels the commit, puts the item back and shows a short success toast, "Restored".

states.name: committed
states.description: When the window ends without Undo, the deferred work (for example the server delete) runs.

appearance: The standard MonarchToast in the neutral tone with an action button, then a success toast after undoing.
platformNotes: The web useUndoToast is a hook that commits when the toast closes for any reason (timeout, dismiss, swipe, a newer toast pushing it out, the page hiding). MonarchToast has no callback when it closes, so the recipe commits on its own timer of the same length, scaled by the center's durationScale; dismissing the toast early does not commit early. A product that must commit when the app goes to the background should also commit from scenePhase. The plan for Android is a native snackbar; on iOS the recipe composes MonarchToast.
accessibility: The toast is announced when it appears (MonarchToastCenter), with its title and message.
The Undo button is a standard button in the toast; give the person enough time with durationScale if they need it.
The success toast after undoing is announced too.
edgeCases: Each delete gets its own commit task; undoing one does not affect the others.
Put the item back at its old index, limited to the current count, in case the list changed.
If the person deletes many items quickly, older toasts close when the center's limit is reached, but their commits still run on their own timers.

name: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard
title: UnsavedChangesGuard
wrapsNative: ViewModifier using interactiveDismissDisabled, navigationBarBackButtonHidden with a toolbar back button (iOS), confirmationDialog(_:isPresented:titleVisibility:actions:message:) and alert for a failed save
summary: A modifier that warns before leaving a screen or a sheet throws away unsaved changes, with Keep editing, Discard changes and an optional Save and leave.
whenToUse: On an editor or a form in a sheet or a pushed screen, while it has changes that are not saved and leaving would lose them.
whenNotToUse: When changes are saved as they are made (show MonarchSaveStatusIndicator instead), or when the draft is kept and restored later. For confirming a deletion use confirm-dialog.
api: func monarchUnsavedChangesGuard(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, hasChanges: Bool, labels: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels = MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels(), guardsBackButton: Bool = true, onSave: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onLeave: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLeaveReason) -> Void) -> some View

MonarchUnsavedChangesGuard.init(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, hasChanges: Bool, labels: MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels = MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels(), guardsBackButton: Bool = true, onSave: (@MainActor () async throws -> Void)? = nil, onLeave: @escaping @MainActor (MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLeaveReason) -> Void)
enum MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLeaveReason { case discard, save }

MonarchUnsavedChangesGuardLabels.init(title: String? = nil, message: String? = nil, keepEditing: String? = nil, discard: String? = nil, save: String? = nil, saveFailed: String? = nil, back: String? = nil, saving: String? = nil)

options.name: isPresented
options.description: Whether the question is shown. Set it to true from the app's own Cancel or Close button when there are changes; the guarding back button sets it too.

options.name: hasChanges
options.description: Whether there are unsaved changes. While false nothing is blocked and the system back button is kept.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the question, the message, the three choices, the save failure, the back button and "Saving".

options.name: guardsBackButton
options.description: Whether the navigation bar's back button is replaced, while there are changes, by one that asks first. iOS only.

options.name: onSave
options.description: Saves the changes. When given, Save and leave is offered. While it runs the screen cannot be left; a thrown error is shown in an alert and the person stays.

options.name: onLeave
options.description: Leaves the screen (dismiss or pop), called with .discard straight away or with .save after onSave succeeded.

states.name: no changes
states.description: Nothing changes: the sheet can be swiped away and the system back button works.

states.name: changes
states.description: The sheet cannot be swiped away, and on iOS the back button reads "Back" with a chevron and asks first; the back swipe is off.

states.name: asking
states.description: A confirmation dialog titled "Discard unsaved changes?" with Save and leave, Discard changes (destructive) and Keep editing (cancel).

states.name: saving
states.description: A "Saving" progress indicator on a raised surface over the content; leaving stays blocked.

states.name: save failed
states.description: An alert with the error's description, or "Your changes could not be saved. Try again.", and a Keep editing button.

appearance: The question and the failure are the system confirmation dialog and alert, drawn by the system in every theme; the destructive choice is the system's red. The saving indicator uses the raised background, the default text colour and a medium shadow from the theme.
platformNotes: The web UnsavedChangesGuard is a dialog plus a hook that blocks router navigation, intercepts same-origin links and asks the browser to warn before the tab closes. iOS has no links or tabs to close, so the guard blocks the two ways out a person can take without the app's code, the sheet swipe and the back button, and the app's own Cancel button sets isPresented. SwiftUI cannot tell when a blocked swipe was attempted, so a swipe does nothing instead of asking. The web keeps the dialog open with a pending state while saving; the system dialog closes when a button is tapped, so the guard shows a progress indicator over the screen and reports a failure in an alert. The web's children (extra content in the dialog) cannot go in a confirmation dialog. Android builds the same component with the same name.
accessibility: System behaviour: VoiceOver reads the dialog's title and message; the escape gesture chooses Keep editing, the cancel role.
The destructive choice is named "Discard changes", so it does not depend on its red colour.
The replacement back button is a labelled button with a backward chevron that follows the reading direction.
"Saving" is announced when the save starts and shown with a labelled progress indicator; a failure is shown in an alert, which VoiceOver reads.
While leaving is blocked, the back swipe and the sheet swipe are off, so a gesture cannot lose the changes.
edgeCases: Without onSave only Discard changes and Keep editing are offered.
Apply the modifier inside the sheet's content (for example on the root of its NavigationStack), so interactiveDismissDisabled reaches the sheet.
Errors are shown with their LocalizedError description when they have one; other errors show the built-in failure text.
The guard does not stop the app from dismissing in code; route every Cancel and Close through isPresented.

examples.title: Leaving with unsaved changes
A pushed screen whose back button asks first
examples.code:
TextField("Notes", text: $notes, axis: .vertical)
    .monarchTextStyle(.body)
    .navigationTitle("Notes")
    .monarchUnsavedChangesGuard(
        isPresented: $isAsking,
        hasChanges: !notes.isEmpty,
        onLeave: { _ in dismiss() }
    )

parityExceptions.reason: The question is the system confirmation dialog. Anchored to its button it is a bubble with the two actions; Keep editing is its cancel role, which the system does not draw as a button there (tapping outside or the escape gesture keeps editing). The destructive role takes the system red.
parityExceptions.convention: HIG: confirmation dialog; the cancel role is the dismissal

states.name: uploading

states.name: done

states.name: cancelled

appearance: A subheading title with a muted caption summary and a linear Monarch progress bar while files are active. Rows are separated by MonarchDivider; each has the file type icon, the name and size, and a caption status line whose colour and icon follow the status.
platformNotes: The web shows an image thumbnail when one is given; here each row shows MonarchFileTypeIcon. The web moves keyboard focus to the next row when a row is removed; iOS does not move VoiceOver focus. Transfers that must survive the app going to the background belong to a background URLSession in the app; the queue only shows them. Progress is a fraction from 0 to 1. Android shares the name and the statuses.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Each row is the file name read with its size and status as the value.
Progress bars are standard ProgressViews named "Upload progress of" and the file name; the total bar reads its percentage.
Cancel, retry and remove are separate buttons named with the file name, with 44-point touch targets.
Finished and failed files are announced ("a.pdf uploaded."), and when the last active upload of several ends, the result is announced.
Status is written in words with an icon, so colour is never the only signal.
edgeCases: Total progress leaves out failed and cancelled files, and is weighted by size only when every remaining file has a size.
Retry is not offered for items with isRetryable false.
Long names wrap to two lines and are then shortened in the middle.
The summary's English plural is fixed ("1 of 4 uploaded"); pass labels.summary for other languages.
