name: MonarchUptimeBar
title: UptimeBar
wrapsNative: HStack of RoundedRectangle segments in a GeometryReader with a SpatialTapGesture; popover(isPresented:) with presentationCompactAdaptation(.popover) for the details; accessibilityAdjustableAction and accessibilityChartDescriptor(_:) for VoiceOver
summary: A row of per-period status segments, usually one per day, with the details of a period one tap away and the overall uptime under it.
whenToUse: On status pages, monitor lists and service tiles, to show the state of each day (or hour) of a period at a glance.
whenNotToUse: For a trend of a measured value, such as response time, use MonarchLineChart. For the share of monitors in each state right now, use MonarchStackedProportionBar.
api: MonarchUptimeBar.init(_ label: String? = nil, segments: [MonarchUptimeBarSegment], description: String? = nil, overallUptime: Double? = nil, showsOverallUptime: Bool = true, startLabel: String? = nil, endLabel: String? = nil, thresholds: MonarchUptimeBarThresholds = MonarchUptimeBarThresholds(), size: MonarchUptimeBarSize = .md, showsLegend: Bool = false, uptimeDigits: Int = 2, activeIndex: Binding<Int?>? = nil, summary: String? = nil, labels: MonarchUptimeBarLabels = MonarchUptimeBarLabels(), onSegmentSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchUptimeBarSegment) -> Void)? = nil)
MonarchUptimeBarSegment.init(id: String, label: String, status: MonarchUptimeBarStatus? = nil, uptime: Double? = nil, details: [MonarchUptimeBarDetail] = [], note: String? = nil)
MonarchUptimeBarDetail.init(_ label: String, value: String)
MonarchUptimeBarThresholds.init(operational: Double = 99.9, degraded: Double = 99)
enum MonarchUptimeBarStatus { case operational, degraded, partial, down, maintenance, noData }
enum MonarchUptimeBarSize { case sm, md }

MonarchUptimeBarLabels.init(statusNames: [MonarchUptimeBarStatus: String] = [:], uptime: String? = nil, overall: (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, period: String? = nil, status: String? = nil, legend: String? = nil, summary: (@Sendable (Int, [MonarchUptimeBarStatus: Int], String?) -> String)? = nil)

options.name: label
options.description: What is monitored, such as a service name, shown above the bar and spoken first.

options.name: segments
options.description: The periods, oldest first. Each has an id, a label, and a status or an uptime (or neither, for no data), with optional details and a note.

options.name: description
options.description: A short line under the label, such as "Last 30 days".

options.name: overallUptime
options.description: The overall uptime in percent. The mean of the measured segments when nil.

options.name: showsOverallUptime
options.description: Whether the overall uptime is written under the bar.

options.name: startLabel
options.description: Text under the oldest segment, such as "30 days ago".

options.name: endLabel
options.description: Text under the newest segment, such as "Today".

options.name: thresholds
options.description: The cut points for segments with an uptime but no status: at or above operational is operational, at or above degraded is degraded, below is down.

options.name: size
options.description: The height of the segments: md 32 points for status pages, sm 20 points for tiles and rows. The touch area is at least 44 points high either way.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Lists the names of the colours under the bar. With several bars on a page, show it on one.

options.name: uptimeDigits
options.description: The decimal places of uptime percentages.

options.name: activeIndex
options.description: The inspected segment. Bind several bars to one value to inspect the same period on each. Kept inside when nil.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that VoiceOver reads.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings: state names, "Uptime", the overall line, axis names, "Legend" and the summary.

options.name: onSegmentSelect
options.description: Runs when a segment is tapped, or double-tapped with VoiceOver while inspected, such as to open that day's incidents.

states.name: default
states.description: Every segment in its state's colour; no data is a muted, outlined segment.

states.name: inspected
states.description: The inspected segment has a 2-point ring in the default text colour.

states.name: details open
states.description: After a tap, a popover over the segment shows the period, the state with its marker and uptime, the details and the note.

states.name: empty
states.description: No segments: an empty touch area, and a summary of zero periods.

appearance: Operational is the solid success colour, degraded the solid warning colour, partial outage the strong warning colour, down the solid danger colour and maintenance the solid info colour; no data is the muted background with the default border. The ring is the default text colour; labels are default and muted text. The roles follow the light, dark and high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: Touch replaces hover: the web shows a tooltip while the pointer moves and keyboard arrows move through the days; here a tap opens a popover (a popover on iPhone too, through presentationCompactAdaptation) and VoiceOver swipes move through the days. The web dims the other segments while one is inspected; here only the ring marks it, because Monarch does not dim colours with opacity. The web meta slot (a badge in the header) is not offered: put the bar in an HStack with the badge. The web exports a separate UptimeLegend; here showsLegend draws the same list. The web keeps a hidden data table; here VoiceOver gets the accessibility chart descriptor. The web locale option is the environment locale. Segments run from the leading edge, so the oldest day is on the right in right-to-left layouts. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The bar is one adjustable element. Its label is the label and the summary, such as "Search API, Periods: 30. Operational 28, Down 2. Uptime 99.83%." Only the states present are counted.

Swiping up or down inspects the next or previous period; the value is that period's details, such as "Mar 12: Degraded, Uptime 99.42%, Checks 1,440, Slow responses from the search index". The popover does not open for VoiceOver.
With onSegmentSelect, double-tapping selects the inspected period.
The periods are given as an accessibility chart descriptor: the uptime of each period on a 0 to 100 axis, with its state as a second, categorical value (Audio Graphs and the chart's data table).
Every state has a name in the details, the legend, the summary and the descriptor, so colour never carries it alone; no data is drawn hollow.
The touch area is at least 44 points high. The start, end and overall line under the bar are hidden, because the summary says the overall uptime.
The legend is a container named "Legend"; each entry is read as its state name.
edgeCases: A segment's own status wins over its uptime.
A segment with neither status nor a finite uptime is no data.
The overall uptime averages only the measured segments; with none it is not shown.
With many segments (90 days) each segment can be about 2 points wide; a tap still finds the nearest one from its position.
An activeIndex outside the segments is ignored.
Tapping outside the popover closes it and clears the inspected segment.

options.name: error

options.name: isRetrying

options.name: labels

states.name: normal
states.description: The meter is filled in the accent colour and the line under it reads "42% used".

states.name: near the limit
states.description: At or above warningAt: the warning colour, a warning icon and "Near the limit · 84% used".

states.name: over the limit

appearance: A muted track with a fill in the accent, warning or danger solid colour. The status line uses the matching strong colour and an icon; labels and descriptions are muted text, in every theme.
platformNotes: The web component lays items out in a grid or a list; on a phone they are a single column, so there is no layout option. Like the web, loading draws skeleton rows and the error uses MonarchInlineErrorRetry. The web has header actions, a heading level, compact notation and a per-item formatter; these are not offered: numbers use the locale of the environment with at most one fraction digit. The eight built-in strings are replaced through MonarchUsageMeterLabels rather than one parameter each. Android uses the same names.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Each item is one element: its label is the item's label and its value is the figures, the level and the percentage, for example "42 of 50 GB, Near the limit, 84% used".
Near and over the limit are written as text and have an icon, so they do not depend on the colour of the meter.
When the level of an item changes while the view is on screen, VoiceOver announces every item that is near or over its limit.
The placeholder rows are read as one Loading usage element.
The retry button is the one of MonarchInlineErrorRetry, with a 44-point touch target.
All text scales with Dynamic Type and wraps.
edgeCases: Used above the limit draws a full meter; the percentage shows the real share, such as 130%.
Exactly at the limit is near the limit, not over it.
A limit of zero, a negative limit or a limit that is not a number is treated as no limit.
The error takes precedence over loading.
The announcement is posted when levels change, not when the view first appears.
The unit is written after the figures with a space, in every locale.

name: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput
title: UsernameAvailabilityInput
wrapsNative: TextField with .task(id:) for the debounced check
summary: A labelled text field whose value is checked while the person types, with the status shown as an icon and a message and announced.
whenToUse: For handles, workspace addresses and slugs that must be unique.
whenNotToUse: For validation that needs no request, use MonarchTextField with its error parameter.
api: init(_ label: String, text: Binding<String>, prompt: String? = nil, helper: String? = nil, prefix: String? = nil, isRequired: Bool = false, debounce: Duration = .milliseconds(400), checkingLabel: String? = nil, validLabel: String? = nil, invalidLabel: String? = nil, errorLabel: String? = nil, retryLabel: String? = nil, transform: ((String) -> String)? = nil, onStatusChange: (@MainActor (MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus, String?) -> Void)? = nil, validate: @escaping @Sendable (String) async throws -> MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult?)
struct MonarchUsernameAvailabilityResult { init(isValid: Bool, message: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchUsernameAvailabilityStatus { case idle, checking, valid, invalid, error }

options.name: label
options.description: The visible label, already localised.

options.name: text
options.description: The text to edit and check.

options.name: prompt
options.description: Placeholder shown while the field is empty.

options.name: helper
options.description: Supporting text under the field, shown while there is no status message.

options.name: prefix
options.description: Fixed text before the value, such as a domain.

options.name: debounce
options.description: How long typing must pause before the check runs.

options.name: checkingLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Checking availability…".

options.name: validLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Available".

options.name: invalidLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Not available".

options.name: errorLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Couldn’t check availability."

options.name: retryLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Try again".

options.name: transform
options.description: Rewrites typed text before it is stored, such as lower-casing.

options.name: onStatusChange
options.description: Runs when the status or its message changes.

options.name: validate
options.description: The check. Return nil when there is nothing to check. Throwing sets the error status.

options.name: isRequired
options.description: Shows the required mark after the label.

states.name: idle
states.description: A plain field; the helper text shows.

states.name: checking
states.description: A progress indicator at the end of the field and "Checking availability…" under it.

states.name: valid
states.description: A success border, a check symbol and the message in the success colour.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A danger border, a warning symbol and the message in the danger colour.

states.name: error
states.description: An information symbol in the warning colour, the message and a "Try again" button.

states.name: focused
states.description: Draws the theme's focus ring around the field.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Subtle background and the disabled text colour, set with disabled(_:).

appearance: The same field as MonarchTextField, with the prefix in the muted text colour before the text and the status icon after it.
platformNotes: The web passes an AbortSignal to the check; here the check runs in a task that SwiftUI cancels when the text changes, which also cancels URLSession requests made in it. The web has sm, md and lg sizes; iOS has the one size of MonarchTextField. The web reports the first idle status on mount; onStatusChange runs on changes only. Monarch does no networking. Several closures are optional (transform, onStatusChange). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is transform.
accessibility: The field is one VoiceOver element: label, value, and a hint made of the prefix, the helper text and the status message.
Settled results ("Available", "Not available", a failure) are announced; "Checking" is not.
Each status has its own icon and message, not colour alone.
The "Try again" button is a separate element with a 44-point touch target.
The field is at least 44 points high and the whole field focuses the input.
Text scales with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Empty text is idle and is never checked.
A check cancelled by new typing never writes its result, so the status always describes the latest text.
"Try again" runs the check at once, without the wait.
The message returned by the check replaces the built-in and overridden texts.
Changing validate does not start a new check; the next edit does.

name: MonarchVersionHistoryPanel
title: VersionHistoryPanel
wrapsNative: NavigationStack(path:) with a List of NavigationLink rows and navigationDestination(for:), a segmented Picker, MonarchDiffViewer and confirmationDialog; presented by the app in .sheet or .inspector
summary: The version history of a document or record: the saved versions, what changed between a version and now, its full text, and restore behind a confirmation.
whenToUse: For a document, page or record whose versions are kept, when people need to see what changed and go back to an earlier version.
whenNotToUse: Not for a log of who did what (use MonarchActivityTimeline), and not for comparing two arbitrary texts (use MonarchDiffViewer).
api: init(_ title: String? = nil, versions: [MonarchVersionHistoryPanelVersion], selection: Binding<String?>, currentLines: [String], selectedLines: [String]? = nil, currentID: String? = nil, isLoading: Bool = false, labels: MonarchVersionHistoryPanelLabels = MonarchVersionHistoryPanelLabels(), onSaveVersion: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onRestore: (@MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)? = nil, onClose: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

struct MonarchVersionHistoryPanelVersion: Identifiable, Sendable { init(id: String, date: Date, authorName: String, authorImage: Image?, note: String? = nil, isAutomatic: Bool = false); init(id: String, date: Date, authorName: String, authorURL: URL? = nil, note: String? = nil, isAutomatic: Bool = false) }

struct MonarchVersionHistoryPanelLabels: Sendable { init(close:noteLabel:notePlaceholder:save:saved:saveFailed:empty:current:automatic:versions:changes:fullText:now:identical:restore:restoreTitle:restoreDescription:restoreConfirm:restored:restoreFailed:loading:view: String? = nil, diff: MonarchDiffViewerLabels = MonarchDiffViewerLabels()) }

options.name: title
options.description: The title of the list. "History" when nil.

options.name: versions
options.description: The saved versions, newest first: id, date, author name and picture, name and whether it was saved automatically.

options.name: selection
options.description: The id of the version on screen, or nil for the list. It is the navigation path; the back button and gesture set it to nil.

options.name: currentLines
options.description: The content now, one entry per block or paragraph.

options.name: selectedLines
options.description: The selected version's content. Load it when selection changes; a placeholder shows while it is nil.

options.name: currentID
options.description: The version that matches the content now, marked Current and without Restore. The newest when nil.

options.name: isLoading
options.description: Shows redacted placeholder rows while the list loads.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, and the diff's strings.

options.name: onSaveVersion
options.description: Shows a name field and Save version at the top of the list. Receives the trimmed name (at most 200 characters). Throw to show an error.

options.name: onRestore
options.description: Shows Restore this version on versions other than the current one, behind a confirmation. Throw to keep the screen with an error; on success the list shows again.

options.name: onClose
options.description: Shows a Close button in the navigation bar.

states.name: list
states.description: The versions, each with an avatar, a relative time, the author and the name; the current one has an info badge.

states.name: loading
states.description: Redacted placeholder rows, read as "Loading".

states.name: empty
states.description: An empty state: "No versions yet. Save one to mark this moment."

states.name: saving
states.description: Save version shows progress and the name field is disabled; an error shows under it.

states.name: version, loading
states.description: The version's screen shows redacted lines until selectedLines arrives.

states.name: changes
states.description: A diff of the version against now, with totals and folded unchanged runs, or "This version is identical to the current one."

states.name: full text
states.description: The version's paragraphs, selectable.

states.name: restoring
states.description: Restore shows progress after the confirmation; an error shows above it.

appearance: System list rows with the default and muted text roles, a subtle info badge for Current, and the diff's success and danger roles for added and removed lines. Dark and high-contrast themes resolve the same roles.
platformNotes: The web is an aside panel that swaps its list for a detail view with tabs; on iPhone it is a navigation stack with the system back button and swipe gesture, a segmented control for the two views and the system confirmation dialog for restore. The app presents it in a sheet, or in an inspector beside the document on iPad. Times are relative and refresh every minute through TimelineView; the absolute date is written on the version's screen instead of a tooltip. Android uses the same name.
accessibility: Each version is one navigation link read as the relative time, the author and the version's name or "Saved automatically"; the current version has the value "Current".
Avatars are decorative, because the author's name is written beside them.
On the version's screen the author line and the date are read as one element, and the navigation title is the relative time.
The diff is read as described for MonarchDiffViewer: each line after "Added" or "Removed".
Placeholders are read as "Loading".
"Version saved", "Version restored" and the save and restore errors are announced.
Restore is behind the system confirmation dialog with a destructive button and the system Cancel.
edgeCases: A selection that is not among versions shows an empty screen until the list contains it.
Long names and notes wrap in the rows.
Version names are cut to 200 characters, as on the web.
Restore is never offered on the current version.

name: MonarchVideoThumbnail
title: VideoThumbnail
wrapsNative: Image or AsyncImage for the poster, Button when it plays, MonarchBadge for the length, AVAssetImageGenerator for a captured frame
summary: A poster for a video with a round play mark and a badge that shows its length. With an action the whole thumbnail is a button.
whenToUse: In a list, a card or a message, as the still that stands for a video and opens the player.
whenNotToUse: To play the video, present VideoPlayer from AVKit. To show any other file, use Quick Look (see file-preview).
api: init(_ title: String, image: Image?, duration: TimeInterval? = nil, aspectRatio: CGFloat? = nil, contentMode: ContentMode = .fill, showsPlayIcon: Bool = true, playLabel: String? = nil, onPlay: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)

init(_ title: String, url: URL?, duration: TimeInterval? = nil, aspectRatio: CGFloat? = nil, contentMode: ContentMode = .fill, showsPlayIcon: Bool = true, playLabel: String? = nil, onPlay: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil)
nonisolated static func frame(of videoURL: URL, at time: TimeInterval? = nil) async throws -> Image

options.name: title
options.description: What the video shows, already localised. Read by VoiceOver; not drawn. Empty gives the built-in "Video".

options.name: image
options.description: The poster the app already has. First initialiser.

options.name: url
options.description: The URL of a poster image, loaded with AsyncImage. Second initialiser. Not the URL of the video.

options.name: duration
options.description: The length in seconds, shown as 1:05 or 1:01:05.

options.name: aspectRatio
options.description: Width divided by height. 16 to 9 when nil or not positive.

options.name: contentMode
options.description: .fill crops the poster to the frame; .fit letterboxes it.

options.name: showsPlayIcon
options.description: Draws the round play mark over the poster.

options.name: playLabel
options.description: Replaces the built-in "Play <title>" spoken name of the button.

options.name: onPlay
options.description: Makes the thumbnail a button that runs this.

states.name: poster
states.description: The image fills or fits the frame, with the play mark in the middle.

states.name: placeholder
states.description: While there is no image, while a URL loads and when it fails: an inverse fill with a muted play glyph. With no source at all the round play mark is not drawn.

states.name: button
states.description: With onPlay the thumbnail is a plain-style Button; disabled(_:) stops it.

appearance: The frame is filled with the inverse background and clipped to 12-point corners. The play mark is a surface-coloured disc with a glyph in the default text colour. The length is a solid neutral MonarchBadge in the trailing bottom corner. The same roles are used in light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web captures a frame from the video itself when no thumbnail is given. On iOS the view takes a poster by the image convention (an Image or a URL, nothing else), and frame capture is the separate async function frame(of:at:), which the app calls and whose result it passes as image, so the view never decodes video while it draws. The web's translucent play disc and badge are opaque here, because Monarch on iOS takes colours by role and does not dim. The web's onCaptureError is the error thrown by frame(of:at:). The spoken length is in words ("1 minute, 5 seconds"), not the digits of the badge.
accessibility: With onPlay it is one button whose label is "Play <title>", or playLabel.
Without onPlay it is one element with the image trait whose label is the title.
The length is the accessibility value, formatted in words for the locale of the environment.
The play mark and the badge are not separate elements.
The badge text and the play mark scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: A title of only spaces is read as "Video".
A negative length shows 0:00; an infinite or not-a-number length shows no badge.
The touch target is the whole thumbnail; a thumbnail narrower or shorter than 44 points is smaller than the minimum target.
At the largest text sizes the badge can cover much of a small thumbnail.
frame(of:at:) clamps the requested second to the length of the video and throws the AVFoundation error for a file it cannot open.

title: ViewSwitcher
wrapsNative: MonarchSegmentedControl, one titled segment with an SF Symbol per view (a SwiftUI segmented Picker draws a title or an image, never both)
summary: A recipe, not a component: a segmented Picker that switches one data set between table, board, calendar and gallery views.
whenToUse: Above a collection that can be shown in two to five layouts, when the choice applies at once and stays while the person works.
whenNotToUse: For more than five views, or views that are separate screens, use a Menu in the toolbar or a TabView. For filters, use MonarchTag with a selection.
api: Picker(_ title: String, selection: Binding<SelectionValue>, content: () -> Content).pickerStyle(.segmented)

states.name: selected
states.description: System segment highlight.

states.name: disabled
states.description: disabled(_:) on the Picker disables every segment; there is no per-segment disabled state in the segmented style.

appearance: The system segmented control in every theme. Text segments use the system font of the control; icon segments use SF Symbols chosen for each view.
platformNotes: The web ViewSwitcher is a SegmentedControl with built-in labels and icons for table, board, calendar, gallery, list and timeline, counts after the labels, sizes, and labels that hide on narrow screens. On iOS a segmented Picker already does the switching; each segment shows a text or an image, not both, so the recipe chooses text when the labels fit and icons named for VoiceOver when they do not. The app supplies the names and symbols, so Monarch ships no strings for them. Android shares the recipe approach.
accessibility: System behaviour: the control is read as a group of segments with the selected one marked.
Icon segments need accessibilityLabel on each Image, so VoiceOver reads the view's name instead of the symbol name.
The Picker's title ("View") names the group.
edgeCases: At the largest text sizes, long text segments are shortened by the system; switch to icons or a Menu when they no longer fit.
Keep the chosen view in the app's state (for example AppStorage) so it survives a relaunch.

title: VirtualList
wrapsNative: List, or LazyVStack inside a ScrollView, with ForEach over Identifiable data
summary: Long lists are virtualised by the platform: List and LazyVStack create a row only when it is about to appear. Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: For any list that can be long. Use List for rows with system behaviour (swipe actions, selection, separators) and LazyVStack in a ScrollView for free layout such as cards or a feed.
whenNotToUse: For a handful of rows, a plain VStack is enough. Do not put a lazy stack inside a non-lazy one that measures all of it, and do not give rows the index as identity when the data can be reordered or filtered.
api: List(_ data: Data, rowContent: (Data.Element) -> RowContent)
LazyVStack(alignment: HorizontalAlignment = .center, spacing: CGFloat? = nil, pinnedViews: PinnedScrollableViews = [], content: () -> Content)
ForEach(_ data: Data, id: KeyPath<Data.Element, ID>, content: (Data.Element) -> Content)
ScrollViewReader, ScrollViewProxy.scrollTo(_ id: ID, anchor: UnitPoint? = nil)

states.name: loading more
states.description: Add a row with a ProgressView after the last item and load the next page from its onAppear.

states.name: empty
states.description: Show MonarchEmptyState in place of the list.

appearance: System list appearance, with the theme's tint. In a LazyVStack the rows are your own views, drawn with theme colours.
platformNotes: The web VirtualList measures row heights, keeps a window of rows and exposes scrollToIndex; List and LazyVStack do all of that inside the framework. Item keys are the identity of the data: make the element Identifiable, or pass id:, with an id that is stable across reloads, as the web getItemKey must be. Heights are measured by the framework, so there is no estimated height or overscan to set. The web onEndReached is the onAppear of the last row or of a trailing loading row. The web scrollToKey is ScrollViewReader with scrollTo(_:anchor:). A LazyVStack keeps rows it has created; List reuses them. Android uses LazyColumn with keys and content types.
accessibility: System behaviour: List rows are exposed in order and VoiceOver scrolls the list as it moves through it.
In a LazyVStack, rows that have not been created are not in the accessibility tree until scrolling creates them.
A trailing loading row should have an accessibilityLabel that says more items are loading.
edgeCases: Identity by index (id: \.self on indices) loses row state and animations when the data is filtered or reordered.
A LazyVStack needs a scrolling ancestor; outside a ScrollView it creates every row.
Rows with @State keep it only while they exist: a LazyVStack row keeps its state once created, a List row that scrolls far away may be recreated.

name: MonarchVirtualMessageList
title: VirtualMessageList
wrapsNative: ScrollView with LazyVStack and .defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom), ScrollViewReader.scrollTo for Jump to latest and deep links, MonarchLoadMore with autoLoads at the top
summary: A conversation's messages pinned to the newest at the bottom, with day separators, a New messages divider, grouping of consecutive messages, Load older at the top and Jump to latest.
whenToUse: The message area of a chat channel, a direct conversation, a thread or a support conversation, with MonarchMessageRow rows and a MonarchMessageComposer under it.
whenNotToUse: For a top-to-bottom feed that grows downwards use a List with MonarchLoadMore (see virtual-list). For one discussion anchored to an item use MonarchCommentThread. For a log of system lines use MonarchLogViewer.

options.description: Replacements for every built-in string.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds a retry to the first-load failure.

options.name: onAtBottomChange
options.description: Called when the reader reaches or leaves the newest message, for example to mark the conversation read.

options.name: header
options.description: Above the first message once all history is loaded, such as the conversation intro; shown alone while empty.

options.name: footer
options.description: Under the last message, such as MonarchTypingIndicator or a read receipt.

options.name: row
options.description: Builds one message's row, usually MonarchMessageRow with isGrouped: context.isGrouped.

states.name: at the newest message
states.description: New messages scroll into view as they arrive (with the theme's motion, or at once under Reduce Motion) and are announced.

states.name: scrolled up
states.description: A secondary Jump to latest button shows at the bottom trailing corner; new messages keep the view still and the button reads "3 new messages".

states.name: older history
states.description: MonarchLoadMore at the top loads older messages when it comes into view, shows Loading older messages… and, on failure, a retry.

states.name: all history loaded
states.description: The header is shown above the first message.

states.name: first load
states.description: Redacted placeholder message rows, read as Loading messages.

states.name: first load failed
states.description: MonarchErrorState with the message and a retry.

states.name: empty
states.description: Only the header.

appearance: Rows are the app's (usually MonarchMessageRow). Day separators are caption text in the muted text colour between subtle border lines; the New messages divider uses the accent strong colour for text and the accent border colour for its lines, because Monarch has no accent tone. The Jump button is a small secondary MonarchButton.
platformNotes: The web list virtualises with measured row heights, an overscan and an imperative handle (scrollToBottom, scrollToItem); on iOS LazyVStack builds only nearby rows and defaultScrollAnchor(.bottom) keeps the view still when older messages are prepended, so there is no estimated height, overscan or initial render count, and scrolling to a message uses scrollToID. The web announces arrivals through a live region; iOS posts an announcement. The web refreshes Today and Yesterday on a timer; iOS recomputes them when the list redraws, or pass now. The web takes locale and time zone props; iOS reads locale and calendar (with its time zone) from the environment. Android has no message list yet.
accessibility: The list is a container named Messages.
Day separators and the New messages divider are headers, so the VoiceOver headings rotor moves between days.
Arriving messages are announced as "2 new messages"; scrolling older messages into view is silent.
The Jump button is a standard button of at least 44 points whose title includes the unseen count.
Placeholder rows are one element read as Loading messages.
Scrolling to the newest message is not animated when Reduce Motion is on.
edgeCases: A message with no authorID, or sent before the previous one, never groups.
Replacing items with a different conversation is not counted as arrivals.
An unknown firstUnreadID shows no divider; an unknown scrollToID does nothing until that message is loaded.
If the whole list fits on screen, the top load row is visible and keeps loading pages until hasOlder is false.
Whether the reader is at the bottom is decided by the bottom marker being built by the lazy stack, so it turns true slightly before the very end.

title: VisuallyHidden
wrapsNative: accessibilityLabel(_:), accessibilityValue(_:), accessibilityHint(_:) and accessibilityHidden(_:) on the element itself
summary: Text for VoiceOver only is set on the element with the accessibility modifiers. There is no hidden view, and Monarch ships nothing.
whenToUse: To name an icon-only control, to add context that a sighted person gets from the layout ("Save changes to the ticket"), to merge several texts into one spoken phrase, or to hide a decorative image.
whenNotToUse: Do not put a transparent or zero-size Text in the view tree to carry spoken text. Do not hide content that sighted people can see and use.
api: func accessibilityLabel(_ label: String) -> some View
func accessibilityValue(_ value: String) -> some View
func accessibilityHint(_ hint: String) -> some View
func accessibilityHidden(_ hidden: Bool) -> some View
func accessibilityElement(children: AccessibilityChildBehavior = .ignore) -> some View
appearance: Nothing is drawn. The modifiers change only what assistive technology reads.
platformNotes: The web hides a span off screen so a screen reader still finds it in the document. iOS has no document: each view is an accessibility element with a label, a value, a hint and traits, so the spoken text is set on the element. A label replaces the visible text for VoiceOver, so start it with the visible words, which Voice Control uses to find the control. Android sets contentDescription and semantics in the same way.
accessibility: accessibilityLabel replaces what VoiceOver reads for the element; accessibilityValue and accessibilityHint are read after it.
accessibilityHidden(true) removes the element and its children from VoiceOver, Switch Control and Voice Control.
accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) with a label makes several views one element with one phrase.
MonarchIcon applies the same rule: without a label it is hidden, with a label it is read.
edgeCases: A label that does not contain the visible text breaks Voice Control's "Tap <name>". Keep the visible words at the start.
accessibilityHidden on a control that can still be tapped leaves it unreachable for VoiceOver users.
Hints may be turned off by the person; do not put essential information in a hint.

name: MonarchWebhookDeliveries
title: WebhookDeliveries
wrapsNative: VStack of row Buttons with accessibilityActions and contextMenu, Picker with .pickerStyle(.menu) for the filters, sheet(item:) with presentationDetents([.medium, .large]), NavigationStack and LabeledContent for the details; MonarchStatusBadge, MonarchLoadMore, MonarchEmptyState, MonarchInlineErrorRetry, MonarchLoadingState and MonarchCopyButton
summary: The delivery log of a webhook endpoint or another outbound integration: status, event, response, attempts and time per delivery, with filters, paging, a details sheet and Redeliver.
whenToUse: On the screen of one webhook endpoint or integration, where a developer checks what was sent, why a delivery failed, and sends it again.
whenNotToUse: For a log of inbound API requests use MonarchLogViewer or a List with the log-drawer recipe. For a single delivery's record alone use the log-drawer recipe.

states.name: rows
states.description: Each delivery is a row: status badge and time, event type in code type, event ID, response and attempts, the error in the danger role, and a chevron.

states.name: filtered
states.description: The filters narrow the rows; Clear filters shows while any is set.

states.name: loading
states.description: MonarchLoadingState skeleton rows read as "Loading deliveries".

states.name: load error
states.description: MonarchInlineErrorRetry with the message and Try again.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No deliveries yet" with an optional action; filtered to nothing, "No deliveries match" with Clear filters.

states.name: details
states.description: A sheet at medium height with every fact, the event ID with a copy button, and Redeliver.

states.name: redelivering
states.description: The Redeliver button is busy; then "Redelivery queued." or "Could not redeliver. Try again." is shown in the sheet and announced.

states.name: paging
states.description: A MonarchLoadMore footer with loading, failure and end states.

appearance: Rows on the page background separated by hairlines in the subtle border role. Status badges keep their tones and symbols; secondary text uses the muted role and errors the danger strong role. The filters are system menu pickers and a field that reads the MonarchTextField tokens. The details sheet uses the Monarch labeled content style. All follow light, dark and both high-contrast themes.
platformNotes: The web shows a table with columns and a Redeliver button in each row. On iPhone each delivery is a row that opens a details sheet (the log-drawer recipe, built in) where Redeliver lives, with Redeliver also in the row's context menu and VoiceOver actions. The web's renderActions slot is not offered; use onSelect to open the app's own screen with extra actions. onRedeliver is async and throws instead of returning a promise. The web's error accepts rich content; here it is a String. Times are RelativeDateTimeFormatter text instead of RelativeTime with a tooltip. Android has no entry yet. Marked experimental as a product composite until a Rook app adopts it. Several closures are optional (canRedeliver, onRedeliver, onSelect, onRetry, onEmptyAction, onLoadMore). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is canRedeliver.
accessibility: Each row is one button read as a sentence: event type, event ID, status, response, error, attempts and time, with the hint "Shows the delivery details."
Redeliver is a custom VoiceOver action on rows that can be redelivered, and a context menu item.
The outcome of a redelivery is announced.
Statuses are words with distinct symbols, never colour alone.
The filter menus are named "Status" and "Event type" and the search field "Find by event ID"; the filter bar is a container named "Webhook deliveries".
The details sheet has Close in the confirmation slot; the event ID copy button reads "Copy event ID" and announces the copy.
Rows and controls have 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: An event ID filter matches only the whole ID, ignoring case; any other text matches part of the event type.
A delivery with only an error shows no response line; one never attempted shows "Not attempted yet".
The next attempt time shows only for pending and retrying deliveries.
The details sheet follows the delivery by id, so a status that changes while it is open is shown.
Long event names and IDs wrap at the largest text sizes.

title: WeeklyHoursEditor

summary: Edits weekly availability: each day switched on or off, one or more time intervals per day, copying a day to the whole week, and overlap checks.
whenToUse: Booking availability, business hours, support or on-call hours: any setting that is “these times on these weekdays”.
whenNotToUse: For one-off dates such as holidays or time off, use a list of dates with DatePicker (date-picker). For rotas that change week to week, use MonarchShiftRoster.

options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

states.description: The switch is on; each interval shows its start and end menus and a remove icon button; Add interval and Copy to all follow.

states.name: day off
states.description: The switch is off and reads Unavailable under the day's name in the muted colour.

states.name: invalid
states.description: A danger MonarchInlineNotice under the day says what is wrong: a time outside the day, an interval ending before it starts, or an overlap.

appearance: Days are separated by a hairline in the subtle border colour. The day switch is the standard Toggle; the time menus are standard menu pickers; the buttons are small ghost Monarch buttons. Unavailable, the time zone line and the read-only hours use the muted text colour, and problems use the danger tone with its icon. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from the colour roles.
platformNotes: Same value shape, validation and defaults as the web and Android (`{ day, start, end }` in minutes, ISO weekdays, 09:00 to 17:00, 15-minute steps, six intervals), and the same names (MonarchWeeklyHoursInterval, MonarchWeeklyHoursError, MonarchWeeklyHoursEditorLabels). Differences: value is a Binding; the first day follows the environment calendar by default (Android and the web default to Monday) and firstWeekday takes the Calendar weekday numbers; uses24HourClock replaces Android's is24Hour and the web's hourCycle; enabled is the SwiftUI .disabled modifier; the remove button is always the minus.circle symbol with the name Remove, so there is no removeIcon; labels add interval for the spoken name of an interval row. Times are menu Pickers, not DatePicker with .hourAndMinute (the planned date-time-picker dependency), because DatePicker has no minute step and no end-of-day 24:00. On a phone each interval is one line, start – end and the remove icon, and it stacks when the text is large. The web's hidden form input (name) has no meaning in SwiftUI.
accessibility: The heading has the header trait.
Each day is a container named by the weekday; its switch is the standard Toggle labelled with the weekday, and reads Unavailable while off.
Each interval is a container named such as “Monday interval 1” holding the Start and End menus and the remove button “Remove Monday interval 1”; the dash between the menus is hidden.
Add interval and Copy to all are named with the day (“Add interval to Monday”, “Copy to all days from Monday”) and keep the visible title in the name for Voice Control.
A problem is text with the danger icon, not only colour, and its message is announced when it appears or changes.
Copying a day is announced (“Monday hours copied to every day.”) with a success haptic.
The read-only view combines each day's name and hours into one element.
Switches, menus and buttons have touch targets of at least 44 points.
edgeCases: Switching a day off and on again restores its intervals while the editor stays on screen; it starts from the default interval after the editor leaves the view tree.
A stored time that is not on the step is kept and offered in the menu.
Intervals with a day outside 1 to 7 are dropped at the next change.
The end of the day is Midnight on a 12-hour clock and 24:00 on a 24-hour clock.
With a step of 1 each menu has over a thousand times; keep the step at 5 minutes or more.
The editor does not scroll on its own: put it in a ScrollView or a Form section.

name: MonarchWidget
title: Widget
wrapsNative: MonarchCard (or a plain VStack) with a header of Text, Button and Menu with .menuStyle(.button); MonarchEmptyState, MonarchInlineErrorRetry and MonarchInlineNotice for the states; TimelineView(.everyMinute) for the updated line
summary: The frame of a dashboard widget: a title with a period, header actions, an overflow menu, View all, and its own loading, empty and error states.
whenToUse: On a home or dashboard screen made of independent sections that load on their own, or when a section needs a period label, View all or an overflow menu (refresh, export, remove).
whenNotToUse: For a single figure inside another surface, use MonarchMetric. For a container with no data states, use MonarchCard. For a titled section without a box, use MonarchSectionHeader.
api: init(_ title: String, description: String? = nil, period: String? = nil, systemImage: String? = nil, variant: MonarchWidgetVariant = .card, state: MonarchWidgetState = .ready, isRetrying: Bool = false, updatedAt: Date? = nil, footer: String? = nil, labels: MonarchWidgetLabels = MonarchWidgetLabels(), onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onViewAll: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, @ViewBuilder actions: () -> Actions, @ViewBuilder menu: () -> MenuItems, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content)
init(… the same …, @ViewBuilder menu: () -> MenuItems, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where Actions == EmptyView
init(… the same …, @ViewBuilder content: () -> Content) where Actions == EmptyView, MenuItems == EmptyView
enum MonarchWidgetState { case ready, loading, empty(String? = nil), failed(String? = nil) }
enum MonarchWidgetVariant { case card, plain }
struct MonarchWidgetLabels { var menu, viewAllLabel, loading, updated: (@Sendable (String) -> String)?; var viewAll, error, empty: String? }

options.name: title
options.description: The widget's title. It has the header trait.

options.name: description
options.description: A caption line under the title.

options.name: period
options.description: The period the figures cover, muted beside the title.

options.name: systemImage
options.description: A decorative SF Symbol before the title.

options.name: variant
options.description: card draws a MonarchCard without a shadow; plain has no surface, for a widget inside another surface.

options.name: state
options.description: ready shows the content; loading three placeholder lines; empty a small MonarchEmptyState; failed the message, with Try again when onRetry is set.

options.name: isRetrying
options.description: With failed and onRetry: the Try again button is busy.

options.name: updatedAt
options.description: Shown in the footer as "Updated 5 minutes ago", refreshed every minute. Hidden while loading.

options.name: footer
options.description: A note under the body. Hidden while loading.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Adds Try again to the failed state.

options.name: onViewAll
options.description: Adds a View all button to the header; the app navigates.

options.name: actions
options.description: Controls in the header before the menu, such as a small segmented Picker.

options.name: menu
options.description: The overflow menu's items: Button, Toggle, Divider. A destructive item takes role: .destructive.

options.name: content
options.description: The body, shown in the ready state.

states.name: ready
states.description: The content is shown under the header.

states.name: loading
states.description: Three static placeholder lines in the muted background colour, one element read as "Loading" and the title. The footer is hidden.

states.name: empty
states.description: A small MonarchEmptyState with the given title or "Nothing to show yet".

states.name: failed
states.description: A MonarchInlineErrorRetry with Try again when onRetry is set, otherwise a plain danger MonarchInlineNotice. The failure is announced.

appearance: The card variant is a MonarchCard without a shadow: the surface background and the subtle border role. The title is label-size semibold text in the default text role; the period, description and footer use the muted text role. Header buttons are small ghost MonarchButtons. The placeholder lines use the muted background role. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes come from these roles.
platformNotes: The web Widget is a <section> landmark with a heading level, a link for View all and an items array for the menu. On iOS the title has the header trait (there are no landmarks or heading levels), View all is a button whose action the app uses to navigate, and the menu takes standard Menu items through a view builder. The web `span` belongs to its DashboardGrid and has no equivalent here. The web loading placeholder can be replaced with `skeleton`; on iOS pass state .ready with content redacted by .redacted(reason: .placeholder) instead. The web's Try again can wait on a promise; on iOS the app sets isRetrying. Android uses the same name and options. Several closures are optional (onRetry, onViewAll). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is onRetry.
accessibility: The title has the header trait, so the Headings rotor moves between widgets; the icon is hidden.
The menu button is icon-only and named "More actions for" and the title; View all is named "View all:" and the title, starting with its visible text.
The loading placeholder is one element named "Loading" and the title.
A change to the failed state is announced with the message; Try again is a separate button from MonarchInlineErrorRetry.
At the accessibility text sizes the header controls move under the title instead of squeezing it.
Header buttons keep 44-point touch targets through MonarchButtonStyle.
edgeCases: Long titles wrap; the header controls keep their size.
The updated line is relative to the current time and refreshes every minute.
The ready state with no content shows only the header.

title: WizardDialog
wrapsNative: sheet(isPresented:) holding a NavigationStack with MonarchStepper, the step's content and a bottom bar of MonarchButton Back and Continue; interactiveDismissDisabled once the person has started
summary: A recipe, not a component: a task of a few steps in a sheet, with a stepper showing progress, the current step's content, Back and Continue, and a danger last step.
whenToUse: For a short task with two to five ordered steps that belongs over the current screen: setting up an integration, moving a project, deleting a workspace with checks.
whenNotToUse: For one step use a sheet (see responsive-dialog). For a long onboarding flow use pushed screens in a NavigationStack. For a form whose steps are independent, use one scrolling form with sections.
api: MonarchStepper.init(_ steps: [MonarchStepperStep], current: Int, furthest: Int? = nil, orientation: MonarchStepperOrientation = .horizontal, compact: MonarchStepperCompactMode = .automatic, labels: MonarchStepperLabels = MonarchStepperLabels(), onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchStepperStep, Int) -> Void)? = nil)
func sheet(isPresented: Binding<Bool>, content: () -> some View) -> some View
func interactiveDismissDisabled(_ isDisabled: Bool = true) -> some View
MonarchButton.init(_ title: String, …, variant: MonarchButtonVariant = .secondary, …, action: @escaping @MainActor () -> Void)

states.name: step
states.description: The stepper marks the current step; the content shows the step's title (a header) and fields; Back and Continue are at the bottom.

states.name: blocked
states.description: Continue is disabled while the step is not valid, with the reason shown as caption text next to the buttons.

states.name: destructive last step
states.description: Continue is named after the action ("Delete workspace") and uses the danger variant.

states.name: started
states.description: After the first step the sheet cannot be swiped away; Cancel in the toolbar closes it.

appearance: A system sheet on the theme's surface colour with MonarchStepper (accent for the current step), Monarch text styles, a secondary Back button and a primary or danger Continue button.
platformNotes: The web WizardDialog is a component that takes steps with content, canContinue, blockedReason, a per-step async onContinue with pending and error states, and a done step. On iOS the app holds the step index and composes MonarchStepper and MonarchButton in a sheet; a step's async work uses the button's isLoading and shows failures with MonarchInlineNotice. The web moves focus to the step heading; on iOS post an AccessibilityNotification.Announcement of the new step or use AccessibilityFocusState. Android plans the same recipe.
accessibility: MonarchStepper reads "Step 2 of 4" and each step's state; the step title has the header trait.
Announce the new step with AccessibilityNotification.Announcement when Continue or Back changes it, since focus stays on the button.
A disabled Continue has its reason shown as text, not only a dimmed button.
Cancel is in the toolbar with the cancellationAction placement, so the escape gesture is not the only way out once dismissal is disabled.
edgeCases: At compact widths the stepper switches to its compact form by itself.
Keep the entered values in the parent's state so Back shows them again.
Reset the step to the first when the sheet is dismissed.

title: WorkspaceOnboardingForm
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchTextField, MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput, MonarchRadioCardGroup and MonarchButton, with @State for values and validation
summary: A recipe, not a component: the form that creates a workspace, with a name, a unique username checked for availability, and a workspace type, with inline validation and a pending submit.
whenToUse: In the first-run flow of a product that needs a workspace or organisation before anything else.
whenNotToUse: Not for editing an existing workspace's settings (use a Form with sections) and not for signing up a person (that is the account flow).
api: VStack { MonarchTextField("Workspace name", text: $name, error: nameError); MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput("Workspace username", text: $username, prefix: "@", onStatusChange: …, validate: …); MonarchRadioCardGroup("Type", selection: $type, options: …, columns: 2); MonarchButton("Continue", variant: .primary, isLoading: isCreating, fullWidth: true) { … } }

states.name: invalid name
states.description: MonarchTextField shows the error once the person has typed or submitted: at least 4 and at most 25 characters.

states.name: username checking, available, taken or failed
states.description: MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput checks the local rules and the product's lookup after typing pauses, and reports its status; Continue waits for valid.

states.name: type missing
states.description: After a submit without a type, an error label with an icon appears under the cards.

states.name: creating
states.description: The Continue button shows a progress indicator while the product creates the workspace.

appearance: Each part keeps its own Monarch look: the text field's input border, the radio cards' selected border and mark, the primary button. Errors use the danger strong role with an icon.
platformNotes: The web ships WorkspaceOnboardingForm as one pattern with onSubmit, checkUsername, rules and messages props. On iOS it is a recipe: the fields, rules and submit logic stay in the app's view, so the rules (4 to 25 characters for the name, 5 to 30 letters and digits for the username) and the default types (Creator and Business) are shown in the example and are not a Monarch API. The web's form error alert after a failed submit is left to the app, for example MonarchInlineNotice above the button.
accessibility: Each field keeps its own label, helper and error text, read by VoiceOver with the field.
The username status is announced by MonarchUsernameAvailabilityInput.
The type cards are buttons with the selected trait.
Errors have an icon and text, not colour alone.
The Continue button reports its loading state.
edgeCases: Submitting while the username is still being checked does nothing; tell the person to wait, as the catalogue page does.
At the accessibility text sizes the two type cards stack in one column.

whenNotToUse: To narrow a workspace to one of its Spaces use MonarchSpaceSwitcher. To pick a workspace inside a form use MonarchCombobox.

options.name: isIconOnly

options.name: manageURL

options.name: labels

options.name: onCreate
options.description: Adds Create workspace, which runs this (after closing the sheet).

states.name: menu
states.description: Up to five loaded workspaces: a system menu with the workspaces as an inline picker (the current one checked), then a divider and the actions.

states.name: sheet
states.description: More than five workspaces, or loading: a sheet with a searchable list of logos, names and handles, the current one checked.

states.name: nothing chosen
states.description: The button shows a building symbol and Choose a workspace.

states.name: searching
states.description: The sheet keeps the workspaces whose name, handle or keywords contain the text; with no match it reads No workspaces match.

states.name: loading

states.name: disabled

appearance: A ghost MonarchButtonStyle button: a small square MonarchAvatar (logo or initials), the name in the default text colour, the handle and an up-down chevron in the muted text colour. The menu is the system menu; the sheet is a system inset List with avatars, caption handles in the muted text colour and an accent check mark. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The popover is drawn by Monarch, as the web's, so the search field, the avatars and the @handle column are inside it; the system menu cannot hold them. On iPhone it stays a popover from the button (presentationCompactAdaptation) and the same view serves a long list: it filters as the person types and shows a loading row while the list loads. VoiceOver reads each row as the workspace name with its handle and whether it is current.
accessibility: The button is one element named "Workspace" whose value is the workspace's name and handle ("Acme, @acme"), built by a tested pure function, also when only the logo shows.
In the menu the workspaces are a system Picker, so VoiceOver reads the chosen one as selected.
In the sheet each row is a button named by the name and handle; the chosen row has the selected trait and a check mark.
Logos are decorative MonarchAvatar views.
Rows and actions keep a 44-point touch target.
Choosing the current workspace again changes nothing.
edgeCases: A selected id that is not in workspaces reads Choose a workspace.
A handle given with or without its @ is shown with one @.
Search also matches keywords, which are never shown, such as an old name.
With no workspaces and nothing loading the menu holds only the actions.

name: MonarchWorldMap
title: WorldMap
wrapsNative: Canvas with bundled simplified country outlines, SpatialTapGesture, inside MonarchChartFrame
summary: Values by country on a simplified world map: a choropleth in one data colour with a "Less … More" legend, or bubbles sized by value, with tiles for values that belong to no country and a data table.
whenToUse: For one metric by country where the geography matters: workspaces, revenue or traffic by country.
whenNotToUse: For exact comparison of a few countries, use MonarchBarList or MonarchBarChart. For places, routes or anything below country level, use MapKit's Map. For a matrix of two categories, use MonarchHeatmap.
api: init(_ title: String, data: [MonarchWorldMapDatum], description: String? = nil, status: MonarchChartFrameStatus = .ready, variant: MonarchWorldMapVariant = .choropleth, color: MonarchChartColor = .data1, thresholds: [Double]? = nil, extras: [MonarchWorldMapExtra] = [], showsLegend: Bool = true, summary: String? = nil, emptyMessage: String? = nil, footer: String? = nil, labels: MonarchWorldMapLabels = MonarchWorldMapLabels(), countryName: ((String) -> String)? = nil, formatValue: ((Double) -> String)? = nil, onRetry: (@MainActor () -> Void)? = nil, onSelect: (@MainActor (MonarchWorldMapDatum) -> Void)? = nil)
struct MonarchWorldMapDatum { init(_ country: String, value: Double, details: [MonarchWorldMapDetail] = []) }
struct MonarchWorldMapDetail { init(_ label: String, value: String) }
struct MonarchWorldMapExtra: Identifiable { init(_ label: String, value: Double, key: String? = nil) }
enum MonarchWorldMapVariant { case choropleth, bubble }

struct MonarchWorldMapLabels { init(frame: MonarchChartFrameLabels = MonarchChartFrameLabels(), country: String? = nil, value: String? = nil, extras: String? = nil, less: String? = nil, more: String? = nil, rangeBelow: String? = nil, range: String? = nil, rangeAbove: String? = nil, unplaced: (@Sendable (String, String) -> String)? = nil, summary: (@Sendable (Int, String) -> String)? = nil) }

options.name: title
options.description: The name of the chart, already localised.

options.name: data
options.description: One value per ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. Codes are trimmed and upper-cased; a later entry for the same code wins; values that are not finite are left out.

options.name: description
options.description: One line under the title, such as the period.

options.name: status
options.description: Map, loading placeholder, empty state or error. A ready map without values or extras shows the empty state.

options.name: variant
options.description: Filled countries, or bubbles whose area grows with the value on a neutral map.

options.name: color
options.description: The data colour of the steps or bubbles.

options.name: thresholds
options.description: Three ascending values where levels 2, 3 and 4 start. Quarters of the largest value when nil.

options.name: extras
options.description: Values that belong to no country ("Global", "EU"), shown as tiles under the map and as table rows.

options.name: showsLegend
options.description: Shows the "Less … More" legend under a choropleth.

options.name: summary
options.description: Replaces the generated summary that names the map for VoiceOver.

options.name: emptyMessage
options.description: The empty-state message.

options.name: footer
options.description: Notes under the chart, such as the source.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for the built-in strings, including the chart frame's.

options.name: countryName
options.description: Names a country from its code. The default is Locale.localizedString(forRegionCode:) in the environment's locale, then the code.

options.name: formatValue
options.description: Writes a value. The default is a number in the environment's locale.

options.name: onRetry
options.description: Shows Try again in the error status.

options.name: onSelect
options.description: Runs with a country's datum when it is tapped or selected with VoiceOver, for drill-in.

states.name: ready
states.description: Countries with a value are filled in one of five steps of the data colour mixed into the muted background; the rest are muted. Countries too small for an outline get a dot.

states.name: bubble
states.description: Every country is muted; each country with a value has a circle in the data colour, largest drawn first so small ones stay on top.

states.name: inspected
states.description: After a tap or a VoiceOver swipe, the country is outlined in the default text colour and its name, value and details are written under the map.

states.name: unplaced codes
states.description: A muted note under the map: "Not on the map: XX (5)". The codes are still in the table and the summary.

states.name: loading, empty, error
states.description: The chart frame's placeholder, empty state and error with optional retry, keeping the height.

states.name: table
states.description: "View as table" replaces the map with one row per country and extra, a value column and a column per detail label.

appearance: Countries are filled with the theme's muted background and up to four mixes of the chosen data colour, separated by hairlines in the surface colour; the inspected country is outlined in the default text colour. Bubbles mix the data colour into the surface with a solid edge. Every colour comes from the theme, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow it.
platformNotes: Uses the same Natural Earth 1:110m outline, centroids, levels, bubble sizes, summary and table as the web's WorldMap, converted into the package. The web shows a floating tooltip on hover and steps through countries with the arrow keys; on iOS a tap inspects a country and writes its details under the map, and VoiceOver swipes up and down through the countries by value. The controlled activeCountry and onActiveCountryChange props are not offered. A tap that misses a small country finds the nearest country with a value within 22 points, because many countries are smaller than a 44-point target at phone width. The table toggle and the chart descriptor for Audio Graphs come from the chart frame's pieces. The map is never mirrored in right-to-left languages. Android uses the same name. Several closures are optional (countryName, formatValue, onRetry, onSelect). Pass each one with its label: Swift gives a single unlabelled trailing closure to the first parameter that accepts it, which is countryName.
accessibility: The map is one adjustable element named by the generated summary, for example "5 countries. Highest: United States 1,200, Germany 300, India 150.".
Swiping up and down moves through the countries with a value, largest first, and reads each as "Germany: 300, Users 90".
With onSelect the map has the button trait and a double tap selects the current country.
The map carries an accessibility chart descriptor with each country's value, for Audio Graphs.
The legend is one element read as its steps; the tiles under the map are a group named "Other values", each read as its label and value.
"View as table" gives every value in rows and columns; nothing is shown by colour alone.
edgeCases: Codes the map cannot draw (unknown or very small territories without a centroid) are listed under the map with their total.
Values of zero or less are drawn as the muted background, like countries without a value; the table still shows them.
With only extras and no countries, the tiles show without the map.
Ties are ordered by code, so the order is stable.
The outline is simplified for showing values; it is not for navigation and takes no position on disputed borders. Kosovo is XK; N. Cyprus is drawn as CY and Somaliland as SO.
Russia and Fiji cross the 180th meridian; the part past it is cut off at the map's right edge, as on the web.
